declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_geometricallyConnected_strictHenselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F00.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat, and suppose that for every geometric
point `x̄` of `X` the morphism `Spec(O^sh_{X,x̄}) ⟶ Spec(O^sh_{S,f(x̄)})` of strict henselizations
has geometrically connected fibres. Then for every cartesian square

```
Y --h--> X
|e       |f
v        v
T --g--> S
```

with `g` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the canonical base change map
`f⁻¹ g_* F ⟶ h_* e⁻¹ F` is an isomorphism for every sheaf of sets `F` on `T_étale`.

The strict henselizations are those constructed inside a big étale site `B` containing `X` and
`S`; the base change map is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleSetBaseChange`, and the conclusion
is that it is an isomorphism of functors, that is, at every `F`. The flatness of the morphisms
of strict henselizations used by the proof is derived from `Flat f` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.flat_strictHenselizationSquareMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_geometricallyConnected_strictHenselization [Flat f]
    (hconn : ∀ x : GeometricPoint X,
      GeometricallyConnected (strictHenselizationSquareMap B hX hS f x))
    (sq : IsPullback h e f g) [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g] :
    IsIso (smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, 0} e h g f sq.w.symm)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.higherBaseChangeMapAb
declarations.doc:
**The base change map on higher direct images**, `(f')⁻¹ R^q g_* ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹`, for abelian
sheaves on the small étale sites of a commutative square. It is the degree-`q` cohomology of the
canonical derived base change comparison `smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb`, transported along the
canonical identifications `baseChangeSourceIso` and `baseChangeTargetIso` of the two sides with
cohomology of the bounded below derived composites.
declarations.comment: bc

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.BaseChangeHolds
declarations.doc:
**The condition `BC(f, n, q₀)` of Stacks 0F02.** For `f : X ⟶ S` a morphism of schemes and
`n` an integer, `BC(f, n, q₀)` holds if for every commutative diagram

```
X  ←--  X'  ←-h-  Y
|f      |f'       |e
S  ←--  S'  ←-g-  T
```

in which `X' = X ×_S S'` and `Y = X' ×_{S'} T` and `g` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated,
and every abelian sheaf `F` on the small étale site of `T` annihilated by `n`, the base change
map `(f')⁻¹ R^q g_* F ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹ F` is an isomorphism for every `q ≤ q₀`.

The two cartesian squares are the hypotheses `IsPullback p f' f s` and `IsPullback h e f' g`;
the map whose invertibility is asserted is `higherBaseChangeMapAb`, the base change map on
higher direct images. Annihilation by `n` is imposed on every section of `F`, which is the same
as annihilation of `F` itself.
declarations.statement: public abbrev BaseChangeHolds {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (n q₀ : ℤ) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.mono_cokernelDesc_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Part (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0F03].** In the situation of
`mono_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_injective`, with `F` annihilated by `n` contained in the
underlying abelian sheaf of an injective sheaf `I` of `ℤ/nℤ`-modules,

`Coker((f')⁻¹R^{q+1} g_* F ⟶ R^{q+1} h_* e⁻¹F) ⊂ R^{q+1} h_* e⁻¹I`,

the inclusion being the canonical map induced by `R^{q+1}h_* e⁻¹(F ⟶ I)`, which is defined
because `higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_comp_map_eq_zero_of_injective` vanishes. This is
`mono_cokernelDesc_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_shortExact` with its short exact sequence
constructed from `F ⊂ I`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mono_cokernelDesc_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_injective
    (hbc : BaseChangeHolds f n (q : ℤ))
    (sq₁ : IsPullback p f' f s) (sq : IsPullback h e f' g)
    [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    {F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1}}
    (hF : ∀ (U : T.Etale) (x : F.obj.obj (op U)), n • x = 0)
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (etaleZModRingSheaf T n)) [Injective I]
    (k : F ⟶ (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u + 1} (etaleZModRingSheaf T n)).obj I) (hk : Mono k) :
    Mono (cokernel.desc ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f' g h e sq.w (q + 1)).app F)
      ((higherBaseChangeTarget h e (q + 1)).map k)
      (higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_comp_map_eq_zero_of_injective n q f' g h e sq I k hk))
declarations.comment: part (3), the cokernel inside R^q h_* e⁻¹ of an injective ℤ/nℤ-module sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.mono_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_annihilated
declarations.doc:
**Part (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0F03].** With `f : X ⟶ S` and `n` as in [Stacks, Tag 0F02],
assume `BC(f, n, q)`, let

```
X  ←--  X'  ←-h-  Y
|f      |f'       |e
S  ←--  S'  ←-g-  T
```

be a commutative diagram with `X' = X ×_S S'` and `Y = X' ×_{S'} T` and `g` quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `T` annihilated
by `n`. Then the base change map `(f')⁻¹R^{q+1} g_* F ⟶ R^{q+1} h_* e⁻¹F` is injective.

This is `mono_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_injective` at the embedding
`torsionEtaleInjectiveEmbedding` of `F` into an injective sheaf of `ℤ/nℤ`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mono_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_annihilated
    (hbc : BaseChangeHolds f n (q : ℤ))
    (sq₁ : IsPullback p f' f s) (sq : IsPullback h e f' g)
    [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    {F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1}}
    (hF : ∀ (U : T.Etale) (x : F.obj.obj (op U)), n • x = 0) :
    Mono ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f' g h e sq.w (q + 1)).app F)
declarations.comment: part (1), injectivity of the base change map

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.mono_cokernelMap_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_annihilated
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0F03].** In the situation of
`mono_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_annihilated`, if `F ⊂ G` where `G` on the small étale site
of `T` is annihilated by `n`, then

`Coker((f')⁻¹R^{q+1}g_* F → R^{q+1}h_* e⁻¹F) ⊂ Coker((f')⁻¹R^{q+1}g_* G → R^{q+1}h_* e⁻¹G)`,

the inclusion being the map induced on cokernels by the naturality square of the base change
map. This is `mono_cokernelMap_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_injective` at the embedding
`torsionEtaleInjectiveEmbedding` of `G` into an injective sheaf of `ℤ/nℤ`-modules, which
realises the choice `F ⊂ G ⊂ I` of the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mono_cokernelMap_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_annihilated
    (hbc : BaseChangeHolds f n (q : ℤ))
    (sq₁ : IsPullback p f' f s) (sq : IsPullback h e f' g)
    [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    {F G : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1}} (i : F ⟶ G) (hi : Mono i)
    (hF : ∀ (U : T.Etale) (x : F.obj.obj (op U)), n • x = 0)
    (hG : ∀ (U : T.Etale) (x : G.obj.obj (op U)), n • x = 0) :
    Mono (cokernel.map ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f' g h e sq.w (q + 1)).app F)
      ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f' g h e sq.w (q + 1)).app G)
      ((higherBaseChangeSource f' g (q + 1)).map i)
      ((higherBaseChangeTarget h e (q + 1)).map i)
      ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f' g h e sq.w (q + 1)).naturality i).symm)
declarations.comment: part (2), the cokernel inclusion under F ⊂ G

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_isIso_integralSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F04.** With `f : X ⟶ S` and `n` as in [Stacks, Tag 0F02], assume
`BC(f, n, q)`. Consider the commutative diagrams

```
X  ←--  X'  ←-h-  Y  ←-π'-  Y'            X'  ←----h' = π' ≫ h----  Y'
|f      |f'       |e        |e'    and    |f'                       |e'
S  ←--  S'  ←-g-  T  ←-π-   T'            S'  ←----g' = π ≫ g-----  T'
```

with all squares cartesian, `g` quasi-compact and quasi-separated and `π` integral surjective,
and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `T` annihilated by `n`, with
`F' = π⁻¹F`. If the base change map
`(f')⁻¹ R^{q+1} g'_* F' ⟶ R^{q+1} h'_* (e')⁻¹ F'` of the pasted diagram is an isomorphism, then
so is the base change map `(f')⁻¹ R^{q+1} g_* F ⟶ R^{q+1} h_* e⁻¹ F` of the middle square.

The index convention is that of [Stacks, Tag 0F03] in this library: the source's `q ≥ 1` with
`BC(f, n, q - 1)` is read as degree `q + 1` with `BC(f, n, q)`.

The unit `F ⟶ π_*π⁻¹F` is a monomorphism because `π` is surjective
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.mono_smallEtaleUnitAb_of_surjective`) and `π_*π⁻¹F` is annihilated by
`n` (`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.zsmul_eq_zero_of_additive`), so by parts (1) and (2) of
[Stacks, Tag 0F03] it suffices that the base change map of the middle square at `π_*π⁻¹F` is an
isomorphism. That is the hypothesis, read through
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_pushforward_iff`, which is where
[Stacks, Tag 0EYP], [Stacks, Tag 04C2] and the relative Leray identification `Rπ_* = π_*` enter.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_isIso_integralSurjective
    {X S S' X' T Y T' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ)
    (hbc : BaseChangeHolds f n (q : ℤ))
    (s : S' ⟶ S) (p : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (sq₁ : IsPullback p f' f s)
    (g : T ⟶ S') (h : Y ⟶ X') (e : Y ⟶ T) (sq₂ : IsPullback h e f' g)
    [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    (π : T' ⟶ T) (π' : Y' ⟶ Y) (e' : Y' ⟶ T') (sq₃ : IsPullback π' e' e π)
    [IsIntegralHom π] [Surjective π]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1})
    (hF : ∀ (U : T.Etale) (y : F.obj.obj (op U)), n • y = 0)
    (hpaste : IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f' (π ≫ g) (π' ≫ h) e'
      (sq₃.paste_horiz sq₂).w (q + 1)).app ((smallEtalePullbackAb π).obj F))) :
    IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f' g h e sq₂.w (q + 1)).app F)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_integralSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F04.** With `f : X ⟶ S` and `n` as in [Stacks, Tag 0F02], assume
`BC(f, n, q)`. Consider the commutative diagrams

```
X  ←--  X'  ←-h-  Y  ←-π'-  Y'            X'  ←----h' = π' ≫ h----  Y'
|f      |f'       |e        |e'    and    |f'                       |e'
S  ←--  S'  ←-g-  T  ←-π-   T'            S'  ←----g' = π ≫ g-----  T'
```

with all squares cartesian, `g` quasi-compact and quasi-separated and `π` integral surjective,
and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `T` annihilated by `n`, with
`F' = π⁻¹F`. If the base change map `(f')⁻¹ R^{q+1} g'_* F' ⟶ R^{q+1} h'_* (e')⁻¹ F'` of the
pasted diagram is an isomorphism, then so is the base change map
`(f')⁻¹ R^{q+1} g_* F ⟶ R^{q+1} h_* e⁻¹ F` of the middle square.

The index convention is that of [Stacks, Tag 0F03] in this library: the source's `q ≥ 1` with
`BC(f, n, q - 1)` is read as degree `q + 1` with `BC(f, n, q)`.

Both base change maps are decided by the criterion
`isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_iff_map_eq_zero` of [Stacks, Tag 0F03]. Embed `F'` into an
injective sheaf `J'` of `ℤ/nℤ`-modules by `k'`; the hypothesis says `R^{q+1}h'_*(e')⁻¹k' = 0`.
The sheaf `π_*J'` is annihilated by `n` and receives `F` by the monomorphism
`F ⟶ π_*π⁻¹F ⟶ π_*J'`, the unit being injective because `π` is surjective; embedding `π_*J'`
into an injective sheaf of `ℤ/nℤ`-modules gives an embedding of `F` factoring through it. And
`R^{q+1}h_* e⁻¹(π_*k')` vanishes: through the base change transformation
`e⁻¹π_* ⟶ π'_*(e')⁻¹` of `exists_baseChange_isIso_of_baseChangeHolds`, invertible at `J'`, it is
carried to `R^{q+1}h_*(π'_*(e')⁻¹k')`, which is `R^{q+1}h'_*(e')⁻¹k'` read through
`integralCompRightDerivedIso π' h`, `π'` being integral.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_integralSurjective
    {X S S' X' T Y T' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ)
    (hbc : BaseChangeHolds f n (q : ℤ))
    (s : S' ⟶ S) (p : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (sq₁ : IsPullback p f' f s)
    (g : T ⟶ S') (h : Y ⟶ X') (e : Y ⟶ T) (sq₂ : IsPullback h e f' g)
    [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    (π : T' ⟶ T) (π' : Y' ⟶ Y) (e' : Y' ⟶ T') (sq₃ : IsPullback π' e' e π)
    [IsIntegralHom π] [Surjective π]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1})
    (hF : ∀ (U : T.Etale) (y : F.obj.obj (op U)), n • y = 0)
    (hcollapse : IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f' (π ≫ g) (π' ≫ h) e'
      (sq₃.paste_horiz sq₂).w (q + 1)).app ((smallEtalePullbackAb π).obj F))) :
    IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f' g h e sq₂.w (q + 1)).app F)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_iff_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F05.** With `f : X ⟶ S` and `n` as in [Stacks, Tag 0F02], let
`q ≥ 1` and assume `BC(f, n, q - 1)`. Consider the commutative diagrams

```
X  ←--  X'  ←-π'-  X''  ←-h'-  Y                X'  ←------h------  Y
|f      |f'        |f''        |e       and     |f'                 |e
S  ←--  S'  ←-π-   S''  ←-g'-  T                S'  ←------g------  T
```

with all squares cartesian, `g'` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `π` integral,
`h = h' ≫ π'` and `g = g' ≫ π`, and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `T`
annihilated by `n`. Then the base change map `(f')⁻¹ R^q g_* F ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹ F` of the
collapsed diagram is an isomorphism if and only if the base change map
`(f'')⁻¹ R^q g'_* F ⟶ R^q h'_* e⁻¹ F` of the right-hand square is. The source's statement is the
forward implication.

Both are decided by the criterion `isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_iff_map_eq_zero` at one
embedding `F ⊂ I` into an injective sheaf of `ℤ/nℤ`-modules, and the two morphisms it asks to
vanish correspond under `rightDerivedCompIntegralIso h' π'`, the faithful functor `π'_*`
carrying one to the other.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_iff_of_isIntegralHom
    {X S X' S' X'' S'' Y T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q)
    (hbc : BaseChangeHolds f n ((q : ℤ) - 1)) (s : S' ⟶ S) (p : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S')
    (sq₁ : IsPullback p f' f s) (π : S'' ⟶ S') (π' : X'' ⟶ X') (f'' : X'' ⟶ S'')
    (sq₂ : IsPullback π' f'' f' π) (g' : T ⟶ S'') (h' : Y ⟶ X'') (e : Y ⟶ T)
    (sq₃ : IsPullback h' e f'' g') [QuasiCompact g'] [QuasiSeparated g'] [IsIntegralHom π]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1})
    (hF : ∀ (U : T.Etale) (x : F.obj.obj (Opposite.op U)), n • x = 0) :
    IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f' (g' ≫ π) (h' ≫ π') e (sq₃.paste_horiz sq₂).w q).app F) ↔
      IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f'' g' h' e sq₃.w q).app F)
declarations.comment: as an equivalence; the source's statement is the forward implication

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_isIso_collapsed_of_bc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F05.** With `f : X ⟶ S` and `n` as in [Stacks, Tag 0F02], let
`q ≥ 1` and assume `BC(f, n, q - 1)`. Consider the commutative diagrams

```
X  ←--  X'  ←-π'-  X''  ←-h'-  Y                X'  ←------h------  Y
|f      |f'        |f''        |e       and     |f'                 |e
S  ←--  S'  ←-π-   S''  ←-g'-  T                S'  ←------g------  T
```

with all squares cartesian, `g'` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `π` integral,
`h = h' ≫ π'` and `g = g' ≫ π`, and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `T`
annihilated by `n`. If the base change map `(f')⁻¹ R^q g_* F ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹ F` of the collapsed
diagram is an isomorphism, then so is the base change map
`(f'')⁻¹ R^q g'_* F ⟶ R^q h'_* e⁻¹ F` of the right-hand square.

The two relative Leray identifications the source's proof uses are supplied, not assumed: they
are `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.integralLerayIso` for `g = g' ≫ π` and for `h = h' ≫ π'`, the
second along the base change `π'` of `π`, whose integrality is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIntegralHom_of_isPullback`.

The remaining identification, [Stacks, Tag 0EYP] for the middle square, is not assumed either:
it is needed only at the cohomology sheaves of `Rg'_* F`, which are annihilated by `n` because
`F` is, and there it is the source's own `BC(f, n, q - 1)` read in degree zero, which is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleBaseChangeAb_app_of_annihilated`. That only the
cohomology sheaves matter is
`Stacks.Cohomology.BaseChange.isIso_derived_app_iff_homology`, both legs of the middle square's
direct image being exact.

The pasting compatibility the source elides is *not* assumed: it is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb_eq_derivedVPaste_app`, the pasting law for
the derived base change comparison along the direct image legs, whose two leg comparisons
`Rg'_* ⋙ Rπ_* ≅ R(g' ≫ π)_*` and `Rh'_* ⋙ Rπ'_* ≅ R(h' ≫ π')_*` are the derived form of the
relative Leray identification for an integral morphism. Of the four factors of that pasting,
two are isomorphisms outright, the third is one by the preceding paragraph, and the fourth is
the direct image
along `π'` of the base change map of the right-hand square; the conclusion is then
`isIso_pushforward_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_iff` in the form carried by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtalePushforwardAb_map_iff_of_isIntegralHom`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_isIso_collapsed_of_bc
    {X S X' S' X'' S'' Y T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q)
    (hbc : BaseChangeHolds f n ((q : ℤ) - 1)) (s : S' ⟶ S) (p : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S')
    (sq₁ : IsPullback p f' f s) (π : S'' ⟶ S') (π' : X'' ⟶ X') (f'' : X'' ⟶ S'')
    (sq₂ : IsPullback π' f'' f' π) (g' : T ⟶ S'') (h' : Y ⟶ X'') (e : Y ⟶ T)
    (sq₃ : IsPullback h' e f'' g') [QuasiCompact g'] [QuasiSeparated g'] [IsIntegralHom π]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1})
    (hF : ∀ (U : T.Etale) (x : F.obj.obj (Opposite.op U)), n • x = 0)
    (hcollapse : IsIso
      ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f' (g' ≫ π) (h' ≫ π') e (sq₃.paste_horiz sq₂).w q).app F)) :
    IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f'' g' h' e sq₃.w q).app F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_field_point
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F06.** A property of quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes
over a nonempty base, invariant under thickenings and stable under affine-transition
inverse limits and passage to a closed subscheme or its quasi-compact open complement,
holds at some field-valued point.

The `[Nonempty T]` hypothesis is deliberate and necessary rather than a weakening. Without it the
statement is false: `T = Spec PUnit` is empty and affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated,
and for `P = fun _ _ ↦ True` all four remaining hypotheses hold, while the conclusion would supply
a morphism into `T` from the nonempty scheme `Spec K`. The Stacks statement leaves the condition
implicit; the proof below needs it to put `⊥` into the family of closed subschemes that are
nonempty and carry `P`, which is where Zorn's lemma is applied.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_field_point {T : Scheme.{u}} [Nonempty T] [CompactSpace T]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace T] (P : ∀ X : Scheme.{u}, (X ⟶ T) → Prop)
    (hThickening : ∀ {X X' : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
      [CompactSpace X'] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X'] (i : X ⟶ X') (f : X' ⟶ T),
      IsThickening i → (P X (i ≫ f) ↔ P X' f))
    (hLimit : ∀ {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I] [IsCofiltered I]
      (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
      [∀ {i j : I} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map a)]
      [∀ i, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
      (c : Cone D) (_ : IsLimit c)
      [CompactSpace c.pt] [QuasiSeparatedSpace c.pt]
      (f : c.pt ⟶ T) (fi : ∀ i, D.obj i ⟶ T),
      (∀ {i j : I} (a : i ⟶ j), D.map a ≫ fi j = fi i) →
      (∀ i, c.π.app i ≫ fi i = f) →
      (∀ i, P (D.obj i) (fi i)) → P c.pt f)
    (hClosedOrOpen : ∀ {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
      [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (f : X ⟶ T) (J : X.IdealSheafData)
      [CompactSpace J.subscheme] [QuasiSeparatedSpace J.subscheme]
      (V : X.Opens) (_hV : (V : Set X) = (J.support : Set X)ᶜ)
      [CompactSpace V.toScheme] [QuasiSeparatedSpace V.toScheme],
      P X f → (P V.toScheme (V.ι ≫ f) ∨
        P J.subscheme (J.subschemeι ≫ f)))
    (hP : P T (𝟙 T)) :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (g : Spec (.of K) ⟶ T),
      P (Spec (.of K)) g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_field_point_of_isDirected
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F06.** Let `T` be a nonempty quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and
`P` a property of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes over `T` such that

1. `P` is invariant under thickenings;
2. if `T'` is the limit of a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes
   `Tᵢ` over `T` with affine transition morphisms and `P(Tᵢ)` holds for all `i`, then `P(T')`
   holds;
3. if `P(T')` holds, `Z ⊂ T'` is a closed subscheme and its complement `U` is quasi-compact, then
   `P(U)` or `P(Z)` holds;

and such that `P(T)` holds. Then there are a field `K` and a morphism `Spec K ⟶ T` with
`P(Spec K)`.

The limit hypothesis is the source's, for directed inverse systems; it is reduced to the one of
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_field_point`, for small cofiltered diagrams, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.limit_property_of_isCofiltered`. The `[Nonempty T]` hypothesis is necessary,
as recorded at `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_field_point`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_field_point_of_isDirected {T : Scheme.{u}} [Nonempty T] [CompactSpace T]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace T] (P : ∀ X : Scheme.{u}, (X ⟶ T) → Prop)
    (hThickening : ∀ {X X' : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
      [CompactSpace X'] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X'] (i : X ⟶ X') (f : X' ⟶ T),
      IsThickening i → (P X (i ≫ f) ↔ P X' f))
    (hLimit : ∀ {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I]
      (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
      [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map a)]
      [∀ i, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
      (c : Cone D) (_ : IsLimit c)
      [CompactSpace c.pt] [QuasiSeparatedSpace c.pt]
      (f : c.pt ⟶ T) (fi : ∀ i, D.obj i ⟶ T),
      (∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), D.map a ≫ fi j = fi i) →
      (∀ i, c.π.app i ≫ fi i = f) →
      (∀ i, P (D.obj i) (fi i)) → P c.pt f)
    (hClosedOrOpen : ∀ {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
      [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (f : X ⟶ T) (J : X.IdealSheafData)
      [CompactSpace J.subscheme] [QuasiSeparatedSpace J.subscheme]
      (V : X.Opens) (_hV : (V : Set X) = (J.support : Set X)ᶜ)
      [CompactSpace V.toScheme] [QuasiSeparatedSpace V.toScheme],
      P X f → (P V.toScheme (V.ι ≫ f) ∨
        P J.subscheme (J.subschemeι ≫ f)))
    (hP : P T (𝟙 T)) :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (g : Spec (.of K) ⟶ T),
      P (Spec (.of K)) g
declarations.comment: the limit hypothesis for directed inverse systems, as in the source

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_affine_field_not_isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F07.** With `f : X ⟶ S` and `n` as in [Stacks, Tag 0F02], assume
`BC(f, n, q)` holds and `BC(f, n, q + 1)` does not. Then there are a commutative diagram

```
X  ←--  X'  ←-h-  Y
|f      |f'       |e
S  ←--  S'  ←-g-  Spec K
```

with `X' = X ×_S S'`, `Y = X' ×_{S'} Spec K`, `S'` affine and `K` a field, and an abelian sheaf
`F` on the small étale site of `Spec K` annihilated by `n`, such that
`(f')⁻¹ R^{q+1} g_* F ⟶ R^{q+1} h_* e⁻¹ F` is not an isomorphism.

The source's *"we may and do replace `S'` by an affine open of `S'`"* is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_forall_isAffine`. The dévissage
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_field_point_of_isDirected` of [Stacks, Tag 0F06] is applied to the
source's property `P`, which is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.ObstructionSurvives`; its three
hypotheses are `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.obstructionSurvives_iff_of_isThickening`,
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.obstructionSurvives_of_isLimit` and
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.obstructionSurvives_open_or_closed`.

Proved here: that the failure of `BC(f, n, q + 1)` under `BC(f, n, q)` is a failure in degree
exactly `q + 1`, that the shrunk base is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the choice of the
obstruction class and that `P` holds at the base, that `P` at a field-valued point is a failure
of base change, and that the sheaf the dévissage returns is annihilated by `n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_affine_field_not_isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hprev : BaseChangeHolds f n (q : ℤ))
    (hfail : ¬ BaseChangeHolds f n ((q : ℤ) + 1)) :
    ∃ (S' X' Y : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsAffine S') (s : S' ⟶ S) (p : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S')
      (_hp : IsPullback p f' f s) (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (g : Spec (.of K) ⟶ S')
      (h : Y ⟶ X') (e : Y ⟶ Spec (.of K)) (sq : IsPullback h e f' g)
      (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology (Spec (.of K))) Ab.{u + 1}),
      (∀ (U : (Spec (.of K)).Etale) (x : F.obj.obj (op U)), n • x = 0) ∧
        ¬ IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f' g h e sq.w (q + 1)).app F)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.FirstFailureDiagram.normalFailureDiagram_of_not_baseChangeHolds
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F08.** With `f : X ⟶ S` and `n` as in [Stacks, Tag 0F02], assume
`BC(f, n, q)` holds and `BC(f, n, q + 1)` does not (the source's `BC(f, n, q - 1)` and
`BC(f, n, q)` for `q ≥ 1`, indexed from `q + 1`). Then there are a commutative diagram

```
X  ←--  X'  ←-h-  Y
|f      |f'       |e
S  ←--  S'  ←-g-  Spec K
```

with both squares cartesian, in which `S'` is affine, integral and normal with algebraically
closed function field, `K` is algebraically closed and `g : Spec K ⟶ S'` is dominant, and an
integer `d ∣ n` for which `R^{q+1} h_*(ℤ/dℤ)` is nonzero; this is `NormalFailureDiagram`,
the sheaf `ℤ/dℤ` on `Y` being the inverse image along `e` of `constantZMod (Spec K) d`, the
constant sheaf `ℤ/dℤ` on `Spec K`. `BaseChangeHolds` is the condition `BC(f, n, q₀)` of
[Stacks, Tag 0F02].

The failure is first realised over the spectrum of a field `K` with `S'` affine by
[Stacks, Tag 0F07] (`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_affine_field_not_isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb`).
The field is replaced by an algebraic closure `K̄` by
[Stacks, Tag 0F04] (`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_integralSurjective`)
applied to the integral surjective `Spec K̄ ⟶ Spec K`, and the diagram is then normalized by
`normalFailureDiagram_of_isAlgClosed`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normalFailureDiagram_of_not_baseChangeHolds {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hprev : BaseChangeHolds f n (q : ℤ))
    (hfail : ¬ BaseChangeHolds f n ((q : ℤ) + 1)) :
    NormalFailureDiagram f n (q + 1)
declarations.comment: the base change condition BC(f, n, q) of 0F02 and its failure in degree q + 1, indexed as the source's BC(f, n, q - 1) and BC(f, n, q)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.FirstFailureDiagram.normalFailureDiagram_of_firstFailure
declarations.doc:
With `f : X ⟶ S` and `n` as in [Stacks, Tag 0F02], assume `BC(f, n, q)` holds and
`BC(f, n, q + 1)` does not. Then there is a diagram

```
X  ←--  X'  ←-h-  Y
|f      |         |
S  ←--  S'  ←---  Spec K
```

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb_app_of_smoothLimit
declarations.doc:
**Smooth base change along a limit of smooth schemes** ([Stacks, Tag 0F09]). Let `S` be a
scheme and let `S' = lim S_i` be a directed inverse limit of schemes `S_i` smooth over `S` with
affine transition morphisms: an inverse system `D` over a directed nonempty preorder `I`, with
structure morphisms `p_i : S_i ⟶ S` compatible with the transitions, a limit cone `c` with point
`S'`, and `g : S' ⟶ S` the composite of each leg of `c` with `p_i`. Let `f : X ⟶ S` be
quasi-compact and quasi-separated and let `X' = X ×_S S'` be a fibre product, with projections
`f' : X' ⟶ S'` and `g' : X' ⟶ X`. Then for every `E ∈ D⁺(X_étale)` whose cohomology sheaves
`H^q(E)` have stalks which are torsion of orders invertible on `S` (every element of the stalk at
every geometric point is killed by a positive integer which is a unit on `S`), the base change map
`g⁻¹ Rf_* E ⟶ Rf'_* (g')⁻¹ E` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb_app_of_smoothLimit
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (p : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj S) (hp : ∀ i, Smooth (p.app i))
    (haff : ∀ ⦃i j : Iᵒᵖ⦄ (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map a)) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    (g : c.pt ⟶ S) (hg : ∀ i, c.π.app i ≫ p.app i = g) {X X' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (f' : X' ⟶ c.pt) (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (sq : IsPullback f' g' g f) (E : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1}))
    (hE : ∀ (q : ℤ) (t : GeometricPoint X)
      (a : ↑((smallEtaleStalkAb t.hom).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor
          (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1}) q).obj E))),
      ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ IsUnit ((n : ℤ) : Γ(S, ⊤)) ∧ n • a = 0) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb g f f' g' sq.w).app E)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.bijective_etaleCohomology_pullback_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F0B] (1).** Let `K/k` be an extension of separably closed fields, `X` a
quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme over `k`, `p : X_K ⟶ X` its base change to `K` and `E` in
`D⁺(X_étale)` whose cohomology sheaves have stalks which are torsion of orders invertible in `k`.
Then for every `q` the restriction map `H^q_ét(X, E) ⟶ H^q_ét(X_K, E|_{X_K})` is bijective. Here
`H^q_ét(X, E)` is the group of morphisms in `D⁺(X_étale)` from the constant sheaf `ℤ` placed in
degree `-q` to `E`, and restriction is the derived pullback along `p` followed by the
identification of the pullback of `ℤ_X` with `ℤ_{X_K}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_etaleCohomology_pullback_of_isSepClosed
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsSepClosed k] [IsSepClosed K]
    {X XK : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (p : XK ⟶ X) (fK : XK ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    (sq : IsPullback p fK f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))
    (E : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1}))
    (hE : ∀ q : ℤ, HasTorsionOrdersInvertibleOn (Spec (.of k))
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1}) q).obj E))
    (q : ℤ) :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun φ : (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ (-q)).obj (constantZ X) ⟶ E ↦
        (singleConstantZPullbackIso p (-q)).hom ≫
          (smallEtalePullbackAb p).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.map φ)
declarations.comment: (1): H^q(X, E) ⟶ H^q(X_K, E|_{X_K}) is an isomorphism for K/k separably closed

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_derivedUnit_baseChange_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F0B] (2).** Let `K/k` be an extension of separably closed fields, `X` a scheme
over `k`, `p : X_K ⟶ X` its base change to `K` and `E` in `D⁺(X_étale)` whose cohomology sheaves
have stalks which are torsion of orders invertible in `k`. Then `E ⟶ Rp_*(E|_{X_K})`, the unit of
the derived adjunction `p⁻¹ ⊣ Rp_*` at `E`, is an isomorphism. The source assumes `X`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the statement holds without it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedUnit_baseChange_of_isSepClosed
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsSepClosed k] [IsSepClosed K]
    {X XK : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (p : XK ⟶ X) (fK : XK ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    (sq : IsPullback p fK f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))
    (E : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1}))
    (hE : ∀ q : ℤ, HasTorsionOrdersInvertibleOn (Spec (.of k))
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1}) q).obj E)) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleAdjunctionAb p).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.unit.app E)
declarations.comment: (2): E ⟶ R(X_K → X)_* E|_{X_K} is an isomorphism for K/k separably closed

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_etaleModuleDerivedBaseChangeUnbounded_app_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F0C.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes, `g : Y' ⟶ Y`
a morphism of schemes, and `X' = Y' ×_Y X`, given as a cartesian square `sq` with projections
`f' : X' ⟶ Y'` and `g' : X' ⟶ X`. Let `Λ` be a commutative ring in which some integer `n ≥ 1` is
zero — for instance `ℤ/nℤ`. Then for every object `E` of the unbounded derived category
`D(X_étale, Λ)` the base change map `g^{-1} Rf_* E ⟶ Rf'_* (g')^{-1} E` of [Stacks, Tag 0A2A]
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleModuleDerivedBaseChangeUnbounded`) is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_etaleModuleDerivedBaseChangeUnbounded_app_of_isProper (Λ : Type) [CommRing Λ]
    (hΛ : ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ (n : Λ) = 0) {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (E : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules Λ X)) :
    IsIso ((etaleModuleDerivedBaseChangeUnbounded Λ f g g' f' sq.w).app E)
declarations.comment:
for every commutative ring Λ with n = 0 in Λ for some n ≥ 1, which contains the
source's Λ = ℤ/nℤ

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesColimitsOfShape_etaleModuleDerivedDirectImageUnbounded_of_isProper

Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes and let `Λ` be a torsion ring, in any

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.DerivedTensorConstant.nonempty_derivedSections_tensor_derivedConstantSheaf_iso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F0E].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`E ∈ D⁺(X_étale)` and `K ∈ D⁺(ℤ)`. Then

> `RΓ(X, E ⊗_ℤ^L K̲) ≅ RΓ(X, E) ⊗_ℤ^L K`.

Here abelian sheaves are sheaves of modules over the integers lifted to the coefficient
universe, `E ⊗_ℤ^L K̲` is the derived tensor product of `E` with the derived constant sheaf on
`K`, `RΓ(X, -)` is any right derived functor of the global sections on the unbounded derived
category, and the right-hand side is the derived tensor product of `D(ℤ)`.

The isomorphism is the composite of the canonical identifications: `E` is represented by a
bounded below complex `I` of injective sheaves and `K` by a bounded below complex `P` of flat
modules (`ℤ` has global dimension one), so that `E ⊗_ℤ^L K̲ = I ⊗ P̲` and
`RΓ(X, E) ⊗_ℤ^L K = Γ(X, I) ⊗ P`; the comparison `Γ(X, I) ⊗ P ⟶ Γ(X, I ⊗ P̲)` is an isomorphism
of complexes (`totalTensorIso`), and `Γ(X, I ⊗ P̲) ⟶ RΓ(X, I ⊗ P̲)` is an isomorphism because
`I ⊗ P̲` is a bounded below complex of acyclic sheaves (`rightAcyclic_tensorObj_X`). Both use that
`X` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, through the commutation of étale cohomology with
filtered colimits (Stacks 03Q5): a flat module is the filtered colimit of free modules of finite
rank (Stacks 058G), for which `Hᵖ(X, F ⊗ M̲) = Hᵖ(X, F) ⊗ M` is additivity.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_derivedSections_tensor_derivedConstantSheaf_iso
    (RΓ : DerivedCategory (Sh X) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)))
    (α : (Γm X).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RΓ)
    [RΓ.IsRightDerivedFunctor α (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Sh X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (E : DerivedCategory (Sh X)) (a : ℤ) [E.IsGE a]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ))) (b : ℤ) [K.IsGE b] :
    letI := CochainComplex.KFlatMonoidal.derivedMonoidal (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ))
      (CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.OneSided.exists_kFlat_quasiIso (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ))
    Nonempty (RΓ.obj (E ⊗ (Stacks.ModuleSheaf.derivedConstantSheafComplexes.{t, t', u + 1, u, u + 1}
        X.smallEtaleTopology).obj K) ≅ RΓ.obj E ⊗ K)
declarations.comment:
abelian sheaves on `X_étale` are sheaves of `ULift ℤ`-modules, `RΓ(X, -)` is any
right derived functor of global sections on the unbounded derived category, and the identification
is stated as the existence of an isomorphism in `D(ℤ)`

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_etalePushforwardProjectionMap_of_isProper_of_isGE
declarations.doc:
**Projection formula for a proper morphism and a bounded below object with torsion
cohomology** [Stacks, Tag 0F0F]. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes, let
`E ∈ D^+(X_étale)` have torsion cohomology sheaves and let `K ∈ D^+(Y_étale)`. Then the projection
map `Rf_*E ⊗^L_ℤ K ⟶ Rf_*(E ⊗^L_ℤ f^{-1}K)` is an isomorphism in `D(Y_étale, ℤ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_etalePushforwardProjectionMap_of_isProper_of_isGE {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsProper f] (E : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} ℤ X)) (a : ℤ) (hE : E.IsGE a)
    (hT : ∀ n, IsTorsionEtaleModule.{u, 0} ℤ X ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj E))
    (K : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} ℤ Y)) (b : ℤ) (hK : K.IsGE b) :
    IsIso (etalePushforwardProjectionMap.{u, 0} ℤ f E K)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_etalePushforwardProjectionMap_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F0G].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes and `Λ` a torsion ring.
For `E ∈ D(X_étale, Λ)` and `K ∈ D(Y_étale, Λ)`, unbounded, the canonical map of

    (E : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X))
    (K : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ Y)) :
    IsIso (etalePushforwardProjectionMap.{u, 0} Λ f E K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigPHSite.exists_phEtaleCohomologyComparison
declarations.doc:
Consider the comparison of the ph topology of a big ph site `B` with the étale topology on
the same category of schemes. Let `𝒫` be the class of proper morphisms, and for `X` in the site
let `𝒜'_X ⊂ Ab((Sch/X)_étale)` be the full subcategory of sheaves of the form `π_X⁻¹F` with `F` a
torsion abelian sheaf on `X_étale`. Then `𝒜'_X` is a weak Serre subcategory and properties
(0EZ4)–(0EZ8) of the comparison situation of Stacks 0EZ3 hold: there is a comparison situation
with the ph topology as finer topology, the étale topology as coarser topology, `𝒫` as
distinguished class and the `𝒜'_X` as weak Serre classes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_phEtaleCohomologyComparison (B : BigPHSite.{u}) :
    ∃ S : Stacks.ComparingTopologies.CohomologyComparison (phAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).Scheme,
      S.fineCoverage = B.precoverage ∧
      S.coarseCoverage = (phAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).precoverage ∧
      S.morphismProperty = (fun _ _ f => IsProper ((phAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).inclusion.map f)) ∧
      ∀ X : (phAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).Scheme,
        HEq (S.weakSerre X)
          (smallEtaleTorsionPullbackClass (phAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X
            ((phAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).topology.over X))

declarations.name: henselizations_equiv_of_zeroLocus_eq
declarations.doc:
Henselization of a pair depends only on the radical of its ideal: two ideals with the same
vanishing locus give canonically isomorphic henselizations over the base ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselizations_equiv_of_zeroLocus_eq
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I J : Ideal A)
    (AI AJ : Type u) [CommRing AI] [CommRing AJ] [Algebra A AI] [Algebra A AJ]
    (hAI : HenselianPair AI (I.map (algebraMap A AI)))
    (hAJ : HenselianPair AJ (J.map (algebraMap A AJ)))
    (hI : ∀ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (K : Ideal B),
      HenselianPair B K →
        ∀ f : A →+* B, I ≤ K.comap f →
          ∃! g : AI →+* B,
            g.comp (algebraMap A AI) = f ∧ I.map (algebraMap A AI) ≤ K.comap g)
    (hJ : ∀ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (K : Ideal B),
      HenselianPair B K →
        ∀ f : A →+* B, J ≤ K.comap f →
          ∃! g : AJ →+* B,
            g.comp (algebraMap A AJ) = f ∧ J.map (algebraMap A AJ) ≤ K.comap g)
    (hIJ : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A)) :
    ∃! e : AI ≃+* AJ,
      e.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap A AI) = algebraMap A AJ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleAbelianSheaf_support_notMem_of_torsion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F0M (1).** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let `η` be a
generic point of an irreducible component of `X`. Let `ℱ` be a torsion abelian sheaf on `X_étale`
whose stalk at a geometric point `η̄` above `η` is zero. Then `ℱ` is a filtered colimit of
constructible abelian sheaves, each of whose supports is contained in a closed subset of `X` —
equivalently a closed subscheme of `X` — not containing `η`.

Torsion is `Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty`: every local section of `ℱ` is, locally on
`X_étale`, annihilated by a positive integer, that is `ℱ` is the union of its subsheaves `ℱ[n]`.
This is the notion of torsion abelian sheaf of the source (Stacks 0DD7, 03SA (2)), and it is
implied by asking every section over every étale `U → X` to be torsion. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleAbelianSheaf_support_notMem` with its
two inputs proved: Stacks 03SA (2) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleAbelianSheaf_of_qcqs`, and Stacks 095P
in the form the source uses is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_smallEtaleGeometricStalkFunctor_map_eq_zero`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleAbelianSheaf_support_notMem_of_torsion
    [CompactSpace X.obj] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X.obj]
    (η : X.obj) (hη : η ∈ genericPoints X.obj)
    (p : GeometricPoint X.obj) (hp : GeometricPoint.LiesOver p η)
    (ℱ : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (hℱ : Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) ℱ)
    (hstalk : IsZero ((smallEtaleGeometricStalkFunctor B X p).obj ℱ)) :
    ∃ (J : Type (u + 1)) (_ : SmallCategory J) (_ : IsFiltered J)
      (G : J ⥤ Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
      (κ : G ⟶ (Functor.const J).obj ℱ),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk ℱ κ)) ∧
        (∀ j, IsConstructibleAbelianSheaf B X (G.obj j)) ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ Z : Set X.obj, IsClosed Z ∧ η ∉ Z ∧
            supportSheaf.{u, u + 1} B X.obj X.property (G.obj j) ⊆ Z
declarations.comment: part (1), torsion abelian sheaves: every local section is locally annihilated by a positive integer

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleModuleSheaf_support_notMem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F0M (2).** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let `η` be a
generic point of an irreducible component of `X` and let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring. Let `ℱ` be a
sheaf of `Λ`-modules on `X_étale` whose stalk at a geometric point `η̄` above `η` is zero. Then
`ℱ` is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of `Λ`-modules, each of whose supports is
contained in a closed subset of `X` — equivalently a closed subscheme of `X` — not containing
`η`.

The proof is the source's proof of part (1), which it says carries over verbatim. Write
`ℱ = colim ℱᵢ` with `ℱᵢ` constructible by Stacks 03SA (3); out of every `i` choose a transition
map `ℱᵢ ⟶ ℱ_{i'(i)}` whose stalk at `η̄` vanishes, by Stacks 095P in the stalkwise form
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_smallEtaleGeometricStalkModuleFunctor_map_eq_zero`; the images of these
transition maps form a filtered system with colimit `ℱ`
(`CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitArrowImageCocone`), each image is constructible by Stacks 03RZ
and has vanishing stalk at `η̄`, its support is constructible by Stacks 09YS (3), and the closure
of a constructible set avoiding the generic point `η` avoids `η`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleModuleSheaf_support_notMem
    [CompactSpace X.obj] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X.obj]
    (η : X.obj) (hη : η ∈ genericPoints X.obj)
    (p : GeometricPoint X.obj) (hp : GeometricPoint.LiesOver p η)
    (ℱ : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (hstalk : IsZero (etaleStalk B X.obj X.property p ℱ.obj)) :
    ∃ (J : Type (u + 1)) (_ : SmallCategory J) (_ : IsFiltered J)
      (G : J ⥤ Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
      (κ : G ⟶ (Functor.const J).obj ℱ),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk ℱ κ)) ∧
        (∀ j, IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X Λ (G.obj j)) ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ Z : Set X.obj, IsClosed Z ∧ η ∉ Z ∧ supportModuleSheaf B X Λ (G.obj j) ⊆ Z
declarations.comment: part (2), sheaves of modules over a Noetherian ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleModuleSheaf_isClosed_support
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F0N, part (2).** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring and
let `E ⊆ X` be stable under specialization. A sheaf of `Λ`-modules `F` on the small étale site of
`X` whose support is contained in `E` is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of
`Λ`-modules, each of whose supports is contained in a closed subset of `E`.

The source says of this part only that it is "exactly the same" as part (1), and so it is: write
`F` as a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of `Λ`-modules by Stacks 03SA (3) — which is
in the library — replace each term by the image of its map to `F`, and run the same three steps,
with Stacks 09BH (3) in place of Stacks 09BH (2) and Stacks 09YS (3) in place of
Stacks 09YS (2).

Stacks 03SA (3) enters as the unconditional
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_qcqs`, so neither
Stacks 093C in the shriek spelling nor the sheaves-of-modules case of Stacks 03S8 has to be
supplied here. Stacks 09BH (3) enters through
`AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleModuleSheaf_forall_epi`, whose own geometric step is
`AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeLocallyConstantSubsheavesAreConstructible`. So this statement
assumes nothing.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleModuleSheaf_isClosed_support
    [IsNoetherian X.obj]
    (E : Set X.obj) (hE : StableUnderSpecialization E)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (hsupp : supportModuleSheaf B X Λ F ⊆ E) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : SmallCategory I) (_ : IsFiltered I)
      (D : I ⥤ Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
      (ι : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj F), Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk F ι)) ∧
        ∀ i, IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X Λ (D.obj i) ∧
          ∃ Z : Set X.obj, IsClosed Z ∧ Z ⊆ E ∧ supportModuleSheaf B X Λ (D.obj i) ⊆ Z
declarations.comment: part (2); Stacks 03SA (3), Stacks 093C, Stacks 03S8 for sheaves of modules, Stacks 09BH (3), Stacks 09YS (3), Stacks 0903, Stacks 095E, Stacks 09YR and Stacks 03RZ (3) are all discharged from the library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleAbelianSheaf_isClosed_support_of_torsion
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and let `E ⊆ X` be stable under specialization. A torsion
abelian sheaf `F` on the small étale site of `X` whose support is contained in `E` is a filtered
colimit of constructible abelian sheaves, each of whose supports is contained in a closed subset
of `E`. Here torsion is the local condition `Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleAbelianSheaf_isClosed_support_of_torsion
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme) [IsNoetherian X.obj]
    (E : Set X.obj) (hE : StableUnderSpecialization E)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (hF : Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) F)
    (hsupp : supportSheaf B X.obj X.property F ⊆ E) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : SmallCategory I) (_ : IsFiltered I)
      (D : I ⥤ Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
      (ι : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj F), Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk F ι)) ∧
        ∀ i, IsConstructibleAbelianSheaf B X (D.obj i) ∧
          ∃ Z : Set X.obj, IsClosed Z ∧ Z ⊆ E ∧
            supportSheaf B X.obj X.property (D.obj i) ⊆ Z
declarations.comment: part (1), torsion abelian sheaves, torsion in the local sense of Stacks 0DD7

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleCohomologicalDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F0Q.** The least degree above which the étale cohomology
of every torsion abelian sheaf on a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public def etaleCohomologicalDimension (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [HasSheafify X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]
    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})] : ℕ∞

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleCohomologicalDimension_le_iSup_of_isLimit_of_isDirected
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F0R** (Étale Cohomology, Lemma 59.95.2). Let `X = lim X_i` be a
directed limit of a system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with affine transition
morphisms. Then `cd(X) ≤ max cd(X_i)`.

The directed system is the diagram `D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme` over a directed set `I`, with affine
transition maps and quasi-compact quasi-separated values; the limit is the cone `c` with
`hc : IsLimit c`; the maximum over the index set is the supremum in the complete lattice `ℕ∞`,
attained because a directed set is nonempty. The instances on `c.pt` are what makes `cd(X)`
defined and are consequences of `hc`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.compactSpace_of_isLimit'`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.quasiSeparatedSpace_pt_of_isLimit`).
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleCohomologicalDimension_le_iSup_of_isLimit_of_isDirected
    [CompactSpace c.pt] [QuasiSeparatedSpace c.pt] (hc : IsLimit c) :
    etaleCohomologicalDimension c.pt ≤ ⨆ i : Iᵒᵖ, etaleCohomologicalDimension (D.obj i)
declarations.comment: cd(lim X_i) ≤ max cd(X_i) for a directed limit of qcqs schemes with affine transition morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleCohomologicalDimension_le_one_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F0S.** Let `K` be a field and `X` an affine scheme of finite type over
`K` of dimension at most one. Then `cd(X) ≤ 1 + cd(K)`.

The source's statement is for `X` of dimension one; dimension at most one is no harder, and
contains it.

The proof is the source's. Let `𝓕` be a torsion sheaf on `X_étale`. By the Leray spectral
sequence for `g : X ⟶ Spec K` (`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LerayVanishing`) it suffices that
`H^p(Spec K, R^qg_*𝓕) = 0` for `p + q > 1 + cd(K)`. For `q ≤ 1` this is the definition of
`cd(K)`, `R^qg_*𝓕` being torsion (Stacks 0DDD). For `q ≥ 2` the sheaf `R^qg_*𝓕` vanishes: its
stalk at a geometric point is the cohomology of the base change of `X` to the strict
henselization, which is a separable closure `Ω` of `K` (Stacks 03Q9), and `X_Ω` is an affine curve
over a separably closed field, of cohomological dimension at most one by
`etaleCohomologicalDimension_le_one_of_isSepClosed`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleCohomologicalDimension_le_one_add
    {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (hX : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) :
    etaleCohomologicalDimension X ≤ 1 + etaleCohomologicalDimension (Spec (.of K))
declarations.comment: for `X` of dimension at most one, which contains the source's dimension one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleCohomologicalDimension_spec_le_add_trdeg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F0T** (Étale Cohomology, Lemma 59.95.4). Let `L/K` be a field
extension. Then `cd(L) ≤ cd(K) + trdeg_K(L)`.

The cohomological dimension of a field is that of its spectrum (Tag 0F0Q: "if `X = Spec(A)` we
sometimes call this the cohomological dimension of `A`"), `etaleCohomologicalDimension`, valued in
`ℕ∞`; the transcendence degree is the cardinal `Algebra.trdeg K L` read in `ℕ∞` by
`Cardinal.toENat`, so that an infinite transcendence degree is `⊤` and the inequality is then
clear, as in the source.

The proof is the source's: a tower of transcendence degree one steps
(`etaleCohomologicalDimension_spec_le_add_trdeg_of_le_one_add`, which also treats the algebraic
case `r = 0`) reduces to `trdeg_K(L) ≤ 1`, which is
`etaleCohomologicalDimension_spec_le_one_add_of_trdeg_le_one` (Tags 0F0R and 0F0S).
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleCohomologicalDimension_spec_le_add_trdeg
    (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] :
    etaleCohomologicalDimension (Spec (.of L)) ≤
      etaleCohomologicalDimension (Spec (.of K)) + (Algebra.trdeg K L).toENat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_strictHenselization_map_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F0U.** At a point `x` of a finite-type `K`-scheme, a strict
henselization of the local ring admits a map from a separable closure of a rational function
field in `trdeg K κ(x)` variables. The induced residue-field extension is purely inseparable,
and the strict henselization is a filtered colimit of finite-type algebras of dimension at most
`dimₓ(X) - trdeg K κ(x)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_strictHenselization_map_of_finiteType
    (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (x : X) :
    letI := (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫
      X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x (by simp)).hom).toAlgebra
    letI := (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫
      (Spec (.of K)).presheaf.germ ⊤ (f x) trivial ≫
      (Spec (.of K)).residue (f x) ≫ f.residueFieldMap x).hom).toAlgebra
    ∃ (ι E Rsh L : Type u)
      (_ : Field E) (_ : Algebra K E) (_ : Algebra (MvRatFunc ι K) E)
      (_ : IsScalarTower K (MvRatFunc ι K) E)
      (_ : IsSepClosure (MvRatFunc ι K) E)
      (_ : CommRing Rsh) (_ : IsLocalRing Rsh)
      (_ : Algebra K Rsh) (_ : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) Rsh)
      (_ : IsScalarTower K (X.presheaf.stalk x) Rsh)
      (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) L)
      (_ : IsSepClosure (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) L),
      Cardinal.mk ι = Algebra.trdeg K (X.residueField x) ∧
      IsLocalRing.IsHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x) L Rsh ∧
      ∃ e : E →ₐ[K] Rsh,
        letI := ((residue Rsh).comp e.toRingHom).toAlgebra
        IsPurelyInseparable E (ResidueField Rsh) ∧
          letI := e.toAlgebra
          IsFilteredColimitOfFiniteTypeAlgebrasWithDimensionAddLE E Rsh
            (Cardinal.toENat (Cardinal.mk ι)) (topologicalKrullDimAt X x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleCohomologicalDimension_le_add_of_topologicalKrullDim_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F0V**, for every bound `n` on the dimension. Let `K` be a field and
let `X` be an affine scheme of finite type over `K` with `dim(X) ≤ n`. Then `cd(X) ≤ n + cd(K)`.

The proof is the source's induction on the dimension: dimension at most one is Stacks 0F0S, and
in dimension `d ≥ 2` Noether normalization reduces to `𝔸^d_K`, which is the inductive step
`etaleCohomologicalDimension_spec_polynomial_le`. This form holds for every `X`, the empty one
included; with `n = dim(X)` it is the source's `cd(X) ≤ dim(X) + cd(K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleCohomologicalDimension_le_add_of_topologicalKrullDim_le
    (K : Type u) [Field K] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [IsAffine X] (n : ℕ) (hX : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ n) :
    etaleCohomologicalDimension X ≤ n + etaleCohomologicalDimension (Spec (.of K))
declarations.comment: for every natural number n ≥ dim X, which also covers the empty scheme; the literal inequality cd(X) ≤ dim(X) + cd(K) for nonempty X is etaleCohomologicalDimension_le_topologicalKrullDim_add

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleCohomologicalDimension_le_topologicalKrullDim_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F0V.** Let `K` be a field and let `X` be a nonempty affine scheme of
finite type over `K`. Then `cd(X) ≤ dim(X) + cd(K)`.

The inequality is read in `WithBot ℕ∞`, where `dim(X)` lives. Nonemptiness is needed: for
`X = ∅` the dimension is `−∞` and `cd(∅) = 0`, so the inequality fails; the empty case is covered
by `etaleCohomologicalDimension_le_add_of_topologicalKrullDim_le`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleCohomologicalDimension_le_topologicalKrullDim_add
    (K : Type u) [Field K] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [IsAffine X] [Nonempty X] :
    (etaleCohomologicalDimension X : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤
      topologicalKrullDim X + (etaleCohomologicalDimension (Spec (.of K)) : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: verbatim, cd(X) ≤ dim(X) + cd(K) in WithBot ℕ∞, for nonempty X: for X = ∅ the source's inequality reads 0 ≤ −∞ and fails; etaleCohomologicalDimension_le_add_of_topologicalKrullDim_le covers every X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_H_of_smallEtaleSupport_subset_trdegLESet
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F0W.** Let `K` be a field and `X` an affine scheme of finite type over
`K`. Let `E_a ⊆ X` be the set of points `x` with `trdeg_K κ(x) ≤ a`, and let `𝓕` be an abelian
torsion sheaf on `X_ét` whose support is contained in `E_a`. Then `H^b_ét(X, 𝓕) = 0` for
`b > a + cd(K)`.

The scheme is of finite type over `K` through `f`, the residue fields are `K`-algebras through
`f`, `E_a` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.trdegLESet K f a`, the support is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleSupport` (the points over which some geometric stalk is nonzero),
torsion is `Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty` (Stacks 0DD7), `cd(K)` is the cohomological
dimension `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleCohomologicalDimension` of `Spec K` (Stacks 0F0Q), and the
vanishing of `H^b` is `Subsingleton`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_H_of_smallEtaleSupport_subset_trdegLESet (K : Type u) [Field K]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsAffine X] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (a : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (hF : Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty X.smallEtaleTopology F)
    (hsupp : Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleSupport F ⊆ Scheme.trdegLESet K f a)
    (b : ℕ) (hb : (a : ℕ∞) + Scheme.etaleCohomologicalDimension (Spec (.of K)) < b) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1} F b)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSupport_rightDerived_etaleAbelianDirectImage_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F0X.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an affine morphism of schemes locally of
finite type over a field `K` (the structure morphisms `gX`, `gY`, with `f ≫ gY = gX`), let
`E_a(X)` be the set of points `x ∈ X` with `trdeg_K κ(x) ≤ a`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.trdegLESet`), and let `𝓕` be an abelian torsion sheaf on `X_ét` whose
support is contained in `E_a(X)`. Then `R^q f_* 𝓕` has support contained in `E_{a - q}(Y)`: every
point `y` of its support has `trdeg_K κ(y) + q ≤ a` (so the support is empty when `q > a`).

The proof is the source's: Stacks 03Q9
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_stalk_rightDerived_iff_subsingleton_sheafH`) computes the stalk at a
geometric point over `y` as the cohomology of `X ×_Y Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{Y,y})`, which vanishes by
`AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_H_strictHenselizationBaseChange_of_trdeg` (Stacks 0F0U, 0F0W
over a separable closure of `K(t_1, …, t_b)`, and the vanishing form of Stacks 03Q6).
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtaleSupport_rightDerived_etaleAbelianDirectImage_subset
    (K : Type u) [Field K] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (gX : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) (gY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType gX] [LocallyOfFiniteType gY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f]
    (hfg : f ≫ gY = gX) (a : ℕ) (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (hF : Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty X.smallEtaleTopology F)
    (hsupp : smallEtaleSupport F ⊆ Scheme.trdegLESet K gX a) (q : ℕ) :
    smallEtaleSupport (((etaleAbelianDirectImage.{u, u + 1} f).rightDerived q).obj F) ⊆
      {y | letI : Algebra K (Y.residueField y) :=
          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ gY.appTop ≫ Y.Γevaluation y).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.trdeg K (Y.residueField y) + q ≤ a}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.etaleCohomologicalDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F0Z.** The cohomological dimension `cd(f)` of a quasi-compact,
quasi-separated morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y`: the smallest `d ∈ {0, 1, 2, …} ∪ {∞}` such
that `R^i f_* F = 0` for every abelian torsion sheaf `F` on `X_ét` and every `i > d`.
declarations.statement: public def etaleCohomologicalDimension [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] : ℕ∞

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.etaleCohomologicalDimension_lt_top_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F10, part (1).** A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes of finite type
over a field `K` has finite cohomological dimension: `cd(f) < ∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Hom.etaleCohomologicalDimension_lt_top_of_finiteType (K : Type u) [Field K]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (x : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [LocallyOfFiniteType x] [QuasiCompact x]
    (y : Y ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [LocallyOfFiniteType y] [QuasiCompact y] (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : f ≫ y = x) :
    haveI := quasiCompact_of_finiteType K x y f
    haveI := quasiSeparated_of_finiteType K x f
    f.etaleCohomologicalDimension < ⊤
declarations.comment: (1): cd(f) < ∞ for a morphism of schemes of finite type over a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleCohomologicalDimension_lt_top_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F10, part (2).** If the field `K` has finite cohomological dimension
`cd(K) = cd(Spec K) < ∞`, then every scheme `X` of finite type over `K` has finite cohomological
dimension: `cd(X) < ∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleCohomologicalDimension_lt_top_of_finiteType (K : Type u) [Field K]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (x : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [LocallyOfFiniteType x] [QuasiCompact x]
    (hK : etaleCohomologicalDimension (Spec (.of K)) < ⊤) :
    haveI : CompactSpace X := compactSpace_of_finiteType K x
    haveI : QuasiSeparatedSpace X := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_finiteType K x
    etaleCohomologicalDimension X < ⊤
declarations.comment: (2): cd(X) < ∞ for X of finite type over a field K with cd(K) < ∞

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedDirectImage_zmod
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F11] (1).** Let `n ≥ 1` and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated morphism of schemes with `cd(f) < ∞`. Then the unbounded derived direct image
`Rf_* : D(X_étale, ℤ/nℤ) ⟶ D(Y_étale, ℤ/nℤ)` commutes with direct sums.

Here `cd(f)` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.etaleCohomologicalDimension`, Tag 0F0Z, and
`Rf_*` is any unbounded right derived functor of the direct image of sheaves of `ℤ/nℤ`-modules.
The two inputs of the argument of the source are proved: the uniform vanishing of the higher
direct images on sheaves of `ℤ/nℤ`-modules is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_isZero_rightDerived_etaleModuleDirectImage_zmod`, and their
commuting with direct sums (Tag 09Z1 for a constant system) is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_rightDerived_etaleModuleDirectImage`.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedDirectImage_zmod
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (hcd : f.etaleCohomologicalDimension < ⊤) (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{z} (EtaleModules.{u, 0} (ZMod n) X)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{z} (EtaleModules.{u, 0} (ZMod n) Y)]
    (RF : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} (ZMod n) X) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} (ZMod n) Y))
    (α : (etaleModuleDirectImage.{u, 0} (ZMod n) f).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF)
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (EtaleModules.{u, 0} (ZMod n) X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (I : Type (u + 1)) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) RF
declarations.comment:
(1): Rf_* : D(X_étale, ℤ/nℤ) ⟶ D(Y_étale, ℤ/nℤ) commutes with direct sums for
f quasi-compact and quasi-separated with cd(f) < ∞, n ≥ 1

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedGlobalSections_zmod
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F11] (2).** Let `n ≥ 1` and let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
scheme with `cd(X) < ∞`. Then the unbounded derived global sections
`RΓ(X, -) : D(X_étale, ℤ/nℤ) ⟶ D(ℤ/nℤ)` commute with direct sums.

Here `cd(X)` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleCohomologicalDimension`, Tag 0F0Q, and

theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedGlobalSections_zmod

    [HasDerivedCategory.{z} (EtaleModules.{u, 0} (ZMod n) X)]

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.ProjectionFormulaConstant.isIso_projectionFormulaMap_toPoint
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme with `cd(X) < ∞` and let `Λ` be a
torsion ring. For `E ∈ D(X_étale, Λ)` and `K ∈ D(pt, Λ) = D(Λ)`, the
canonical map of Cohomology on Sites, Section 0943, for the structure morphism
`π : (X_étale, Λ̲) ⟶ (pt, Λ)`,

`RΓ(X, E) ⊗^L_Λ K = Rπ_*E ⊗^L_Λ K ⟶ Rπ_*(E ⊗^L_Λ Lπ^*K) = RΓ(X, E ⊗^L_Λ K̲)`,

is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_projectionFormulaMap_toPoint [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (hcd : Scheme.etaleCohomologicalDimension X < ⊤) (hΛ : IsAddTorsion Λ)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (ringedTopos Λ X).O)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (pointRingedTopos Λ).O))) :
    IsIso (projectionFormulaMap (toPoint Λ X) E K)
declarations.comment:
the canonical map of Section 0943 for the structure morphism of `(X_étale, Λ̲)` to
the point ringed by `Λ`, on the shared ringed topos `EtaleCoefficients.ringedTopos`; `D(pt, Λ)`
is `D(Λ)` through `EtaleCoefficients.pointDerivedEquivalence`

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_etaleKunnethCompositeMap_zmod_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F14] (2).** Let `k` be a separably closed field, `f : X ⟶ Spec k` proper,
`g : Y ⟶ Spec k` of finite type, and `n ≥ 1`. For `E ∈ D(X_étale, ℤ/nℤ)` and
`K ∈ D(Y_étale, ℤ/nℤ)`, unbounded, the Künneth map
`RΓ(X, E) ⊗^L_{ℤ/nℤ} RΓ(Y, K) = Rf_*E ⊗^L Rg_*K ⟶ R(pr₂ ≫ g)_*(pr₁⁻¹E ⊗^L pr₂⁻¹K)
= RΓ(X ×_k Y, pr₁⁻¹E ⊗^L pr₂⁻¹K)` in `D((Spec k)_étale, ℤ/nℤ) = D(ℤ/nℤ)` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_etaleKunnethCompositeMap_zmod_of_finiteType (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (k : Type u)
    [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g]
    (E : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} (ZMod n) X))
    (K : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} (ZMod n) Y)) :
    IsIso (etaleKunnethCompositeMap.{u, 0} (ZMod n) f g (pullback.fst f g) (pullback.snd f g)
      pullback.condition E K)
declarations.comment:
(2); on D((Spec k)_et, ℤ/nℤ), which global sections identify with D(ℤ/nℤ) for k
separably closed, so that the direct images to Spec k are the derived global sections

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_etaleKunnethCompositeMap_of_isGE_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F14] (1).** Let `k` be a separably closed field, `f : X ⟶ Spec k` proper and
`g : Y ⟶ Spec k` with `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let `E ∈ D⁺(X_étale)` have torsion
cohomology sheaves and `K ∈ D⁺(Y_étale)`. Then the Künneth map
`RΓ(X, E) ⊗^L_ℤ RΓ(Y, K) = Rf_*E ⊗^L_ℤ Rg_*K ⟶ R(pr₂ ≫ g)_*(pr₁⁻¹E ⊗^L_ℤ pr₂⁻¹K)
= RΓ(X ×_k Y, pr₁⁻¹E ⊗^L_ℤ pr₂⁻¹K)` in `D((Spec k)_étale, ℤ) = D(ℤ)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_etaleKunnethCompositeMap_of_isGE_of_isProper (k : Type u) [Field k]
    [IsSepClosed k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y]
    (E : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} ℤ X)) (a : ℤ) (hE : E.IsGE a)
    (hT : ∀ n, IsTorsionEtaleModule.{u, 0} ℤ X ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj E))
    (K : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} ℤ Y)) (b : ℤ) (hK : K.IsGE b) :
    IsIso (etaleKunnethCompositeMap.{u, 0} ℤ f g (pullback.fst f g) (pullback.snd f g)
      pullback.condition E K)
declarations.comment:
(1); on D((Spec k)_et, ℤ), which global sections identify with D(ℤ) for k
separably closed, so that the direct images to Spec k are the derived global sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Sheaf.exists_clopen_decomposition_of_isColimit_cofan_ulift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02WO and Stacks 0F15 for sheaves with values in a universe `max w u` independent of
the universe `u` of the schemes.** A section `x` of a coproduct `P = ∐ᵢ Fᵢ` of pointwise
`u`-small sheaves over an object `W` of the big fppf site of `S`, the index type being
`u`-small, decomposes `W` into a family of pairwise disjoint open subobjects `W' i`, covering
`W`, such that `x` restricted to `W' i` comes from `Fᵢ`; and each `W' i` is universal with that
property.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Sheaf.exists_clopen_decomposition_of_isColimit_cofan` with the value
universe of the sheaves decoupled from the universe of the morphisms of the site. The
decomposition machinery is not rebuilt: the sheaves are universe lifts of sheaves of `Type u`,
the coproduct cocone descends to those by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_shrink_isColimit_cofan_of_small`, and the conclusion, which speaks
of objects of the site and of sections, transports back along the lift.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sheaf.exists_clopen_decomposition_of_isColimit_cofan_ulift {I : Type v} [Small.{u} I]
    {F : I → Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max w u))}
    (hF : ∀ i, FunctorToTypes.Small.{u} (F i).obj)
    {P : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max w u))} (ι : ∀ i, F i ⟶ P)
    (hP : IsColimit (Cofan.mk P ι)) (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (x : P.obj.obj (op W)) :
    ∃ (W' : I → BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : ∀ i, W' i ⟶ W),
      (∀ i, IsOpenImmersion ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (p i))) ∧
      (∀ i, ∃ z : (F i).obj.obj (op (W' i)),
        (ι i).hom.app (op (W' i)) z = P.obj.map (p i).op x) ∧
      (∀ i i', i ≠ i' → ∀ (y : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (W' i))
        (y' : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (W' i')),
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (p i) y ≠
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (p i') y') ∧
      (∀ w : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W,
        ∃ i, w ∈ Set.range ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (p i))) ∧
      (∀ (i : I) (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (t : T ⟶ W),
        (∃ z : (F i).obj.obj (op T), (ι i).hom.app (op T) z = P.obj.map t.op x) →
        ∃ t' : T ⟶ W' i, t' ≫ p i = t)
declarations.comment: in an arbitrary value universe
