declarations.name: Stacks.MayerVietoris.CanonicalMapOfComplexes.cSquare_natural
declarations.doc: The chain-level canonical maps commute with chain maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem cSquare_natural {I I' : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{v} R) ℤ} (f : I ⟶ I') :
    (sectionsComplex R sq.X₄).map f ≫ cSquare sq I' =
      cSquare sq I ≫ mappingCoconeMap sq f
declarations.comment: functoriality on complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.MayerVietoris.CanonicalMapOfComplexes.cSquare_arrow_iso_of_isKInjective
declarations.doc:
Changing a K-injective representative gives an isomorphic arrow in `D(Ab)`.

Two K-injective representatives of the same derived object are homotopy equivalent, and
the chain-level canonical map is natural; the induced map of mapping cocones is inverted
by the localization functor because it is the third component of a morphism of
distinguished triangles whose other two components are inverted.
declarations.statement:
theorem cSquare_arrow_iso_of_isKInjective
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v} R))
    (I I' : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{v} R) ℤ)
    [I.IsKInjective] [I'.IsKInjective]
    (_ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj I ≅ K) (_ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj I' ≅ K) :
    Nonempty (Arrow.mk (DerivedCategory.Q.map (cSquare sq I)) ≅
      Arrow.mk (DerivedCategory.Q.map (cSquare sq I')))
declarations.comment: independence of the K-injective representative

declarations.name: Stacks.MayerVietoris.CanonicalMapOfComplexes.DerivedCSquareData.cSquareTriangle
declarations.doc: The triangle on derived sections, with boundary obtained using the inverse of `c`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cSquareTriangle (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v} R))
    [D.IsCSquareIso K] : Triangle (DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{v})
declarations.comment: the canonical triangle on derived objects

declarations.name: Stacks.MayerVietoris.CanonicalMapOfComplexes.DerivedCSquareData.isCSquareIso_iff_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical condition on a derived object can be tested on any K-injective
representative.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCSquareIso_iff_quasiIso (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v} R))
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{v} R) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective]
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj I ≅ K) :
    D.IsCSquareIso K ↔ QuasiIso (cSquare sq I)
declarations.comment: computation of the isomorphism condition

declarations.name: Stacks.MayerVietoris.CanonicalMapOfComplexes.DerivedCSquareData.cSquareTriangle_functorial
declarations.doc:
Every derived morphism induces a unique morphism of the derived triangles with the given
three components.
declarations.statement:
theorem cSquareTriangle_functorial {K K' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v} R)} (f : K ⟶ K')
    [D.IsCSquareIso K] [D.IsCSquareIso K'] :
    ∃! t : D.cSquareTriangle K ⟶ D.cSquareTriangle K',
      t.hom₁ = (D.derivedSections sq.X₄).map f ∧
        t.hom₂ = biprod.map ((D.derivedSections sq.X₃).map f)
          ((D.derivedSections sq.X₂).map f) ∧
        t.hom₃ = (D.derivedSections sq.X₁).map f
declarations.comment: functoriality of the triangle in the derived object

declarations.name: Stacks.MayerVietoris.CanonicalMapOfComplexes.derivedCSquareData
declarations.doc:
**The derived construction of the canonical map of a square**, under `UnivLE` between the
universes of the site, of its homs, of the rings and of the modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedCSquareData [UnivLE.{u, v}] [UnivLE.{w, v}] [UnivLE.{r, v}] :
    DerivedCSquareData.{u, v} (R := R) sq
declarations.comment: the functorial derived construction and its K-injective computation

declarations.name: Stacks.MayerVietoris.CanonicalMapOfComplexes.cSquareTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**The derived-section triangle is distinguished** at every derived object where the
canonical map is invertible, under `UnivLE` between the universes of the site, of its homs, of
the rings and of the modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem cSquareTriangle_distinguished [UnivLE.{u, v}] [UnivLE.{w, v}] [UnivLE.{r, v}]
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v} R))
    [(derivedCSquareData.{u, v} (R := R) sq).IsCSquareIso K] :
    (derivedCSquareData.{u, v} (R := R) sq).cSquareTriangle K ∈
      distTriang (DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{v})
declarations.comment: the triangle is distinguished

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MayerVietoris.essImage_iff_forall_isCSquareIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F18.** Let `C` carry two Grothendieck topologies `J' ≤ J` and let `𝒪` be a sheaf of
rings for `J`, so that the identity of `C` is a comparison of ringed sites
`ε : (C_J, 𝒪_J) ⟶ (C_{J'}, 𝒪_{J'})`. Let `A` be a type and for each `α : A` let

```
E α ⟶ Y α
  ↓      ↓
Z α ⟶ X α
```

be a commutative square in `C`. Assume

1. a `J'`-sheaf of sets `F'` is a `J`-sheaf whenever
   `F'(X α) = F'(Z α) ×_{F'(E α)} F'(Y α)` for all `α`, and
2. for every `K'` in `D(𝒪_{J'})` in the essential image of `Rε_*` the canonical comparison maps
   `c^{K'}_{X α, Z α, Y α, E α}` of [Stacks, Tag 0F16] are isomorphisms for all `α`.

Then an object `K'` of `D⁺(𝒪_{J'})` lies in the essential image of `Rε_*` if and only if the
maps `c^{K'}_{X α, Z α, Y α, E α}` are isomorphisms for all `α`.

`Rε_*` is any right derived functor of `ε_*` together with its unit; the hypothesis that it is a
right derived functor is what makes the essential image independent of the choice.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_iff_forall_isCSquareIso {A : Type*} (sq : A → Square S.C)
    (hdetect : ∀ F : Sheaf J' (Type max u w),
      (∀ a, ((sq a).op.map F.obj).IsPullback) → Presheaf.IsSheaf S.J F.obj)
    (Rε : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v} (ringSheafOfLe h
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O))))
    (η : letI := modulePushforward_additive.{u, v, w, r} h
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O);
      (modulePushforward.{u, v, w, r} h
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rε)
    [Rε.IsRightDerivedFunctor η
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{v}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (hcomparison : ∀ K' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v} (ringSheafOfLe h
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O))),
      Rε.essImage K' → ∀ a, (CanonicalMapOfComplexes.derivedCSquareData.{u, v}
        (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (S.ofLe h).O)) (sq a)).IsCSquareIso K')
    (K' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v} (ringSheafOfLe h
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O))))
    (hplus : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t
      (C := SheafOfModules.{v} (ringSheafOfLe h
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)))).plus K') :
    Rε.essImage K' ↔ ∀ a, (CanonicalMapOfComplexes.derivedCSquareData.{u, v}
      (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (S.ofLe h).O)) (sq a)).IsCSquareIso K'

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MayerVietoris.isCSquareIso_ofLe_of_isPushout
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F19.** Let `J' ≤ J` be two topologies on `C` and let `𝒪` be a sheaf of rings for
`J`, so that the identity of `C` is a comparison `ε : (C_J, 𝒪_J) ⟶ (C_{J'}, 𝒪_{J'})`. Let a
commutative square in `C` be given whose `J`-sheafified representables form a pushout square and
whose map `h_E^# ⟶ h_Y^#` is a monomorphism. Then for every object `K'` of `D(𝒪_{J'})` in the
essential image of the derived direct image `Rε_*`, the canonical map `c^{K'}_{X,Z,Y,E}` of
Stacks 0F16 for the coarser topology is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCSquareIso_ofLe_of_isPushout (sq : Square S.C)
    (hpushout : (sq.map (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda S.J)).IsPushout)
    (hmono : Mono ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda S.J).map sq.f₁₂))
    (Rε : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (S.ofLe h).O)))
    (η : letI := (modulePushforward_additive.{u, v, w, r} h
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O));
      (modulePushforward.{u, v, w, r} h
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rε)
    [Rε.IsRightDerivedFunctor η
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (K' : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (S.ofLe h).O)))
    (hK' : Rε.essImage K') :
    (CanonicalMapOfComplexes.derivedCSquareData.{u, v}
      (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (S.ofLe h).O)) sq).IsCSquareIso K'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isRestriction_iff_isSheafOnAffineBasis
declarations.doc:
A presheaf on the affine opens is (up to isomorphism) the restriction of a sheaf
if and only if it is a sheaf on the affine-open basis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRestriction_iff_isSheafOnAffineBasis (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : PresheafOnBasis X.affineOpens) :
    (∃ G : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) (TopCat.of X),
      Nonempty (F ≅ restrictOfSheaf X.affineOpens G)) ↔
      IsSheafOnBasis X.affineOpens F
declarations.comment: equivalence of (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isSheafOnAffineBasis_iff_standardPairs
declarations.doc:
A presheaf on the affine-open basis is a sheaf exactly when its section set on the
empty open is a singleton and compatible sections glue uniquely across every standard
two-open cover of an affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheafOnAffineBasis_iff_standardPairs (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : PresheafOnBasis X.affineOpens) :
    IsSheafOnBasis X.affineOpens F ↔
      ((∃! _s : F.obj (op (affineBasisOpen X ⟨⊥, isAffineOpen_bot X⟩)), True) ∧
      ∀ (U : X.affineOpens) (f g : Γ(X, U.1))
        (_hcov : U.1 = X.basicOpen f ⊔ X.basicOpen g)
        (s : F.obj (op (affineBasisOpen X (X.affineBasicOpen f))))
        (t : F.obj (op (affineBasisOpen X (X.affineBasicOpen g)))),
        (F.restrictMap X.affineOpens
            (show (affineBasisOpen X (X.affineBasicOpen (f * g))).obj ≤
                (affineBasisOpen X (X.affineBasicOpen f)).obj by
              change X.basicOpen (f * g) ≤ X.basicOpen f
              rw [X.basicOpen_mul]
              exact inf_le_left) s =
          F.restrictMap X.affineOpens
            (show (affineBasisOpen X (X.affineBasicOpen (f * g))).obj ≤
                (affineBasisOpen X (X.affineBasicOpen g)).obj by
              change X.basicOpen (f * g) ≤ X.basicOpen g
              rw [X.basicOpen_mul]
              exact inf_le_right) t) ↔
        ∃! r : F.obj (op (affineBasisOpen X U)),
          (F.restrictMap X.affineOpens (by exact (X.affineBasicOpen_le f)) r = s) ∧
          (F.restrictMap X.affineOpens (by exact (X.affineBasicOpen_le g)) r = t))
declarations.comment: equivalence of (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineZariski.inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F1B.** The inclusion of the small affine Zariski site of a scheme into its small
Zariski site is a special cocontinuous functor. Its dense-subsite component is the induced
equivalence of topoi `Sh(S_{affine, Zar}) ≌ Sh(S_Zar)`, given by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite.sheafEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem SmallAffineZariski.inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous
    (B : BigZariskiSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    IsSpecialCocontinuous (SmallAffineZariski.topology B S hS)
      (SmallZariski.topology B S hS) (SmallAffineZariski.inclusion B S hS)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.FieldExtensionBaseChange.isIso_smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb_of_stalks
declarations.doc:
**Direct images commute with extension of the base field** ([Stacks, Tag 0F1C]). Let `L/K`
be an extension of fields, let `g : T ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
schemes over `K`, and let `g_L : T_L ⟶ S_L` be its base change to `Spec L`, with
`S_L = Spec L ×_K S` and `T_L = Spec L ×_K T`. Let `E ∈ D⁺(T_étale)` have cohomology sheaves whose
stalks are torsion of orders invertible in `K`: every element of the stalk of `H^q(E)` at every
geometric point of `T` is killed by a positive integer invertible in `K`. Let `E_L` be the
pullback of `E` to `(T_L)_étale`. Then `Rg_{L,*} E_L` is the pullback of `Rg_* E` to `S_L`: the
base change map `(S_L ⟶ S)⁻¹ Rg_* E ⟶ Rg_{L,*} E_L` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb_of_stalks
    (E : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1}))
    (hE : ∀ (q : ℤ) (t : GeometricPoint T)
      (a : ↑((smallEtaleStalkAb t.hom).obj ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ q).obj E))),
      ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ IsUnit (n : K) ∧ n • a = 0) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb (pullback.snd _ sS) g
      (baseChangeMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) sS sT g hg)
      (pullback.snd _ sT) (baseChangeMap_snd _ sS sT g hg)).app E)
declarations.comment: the base change map `(S_L ⟶ S)⁻¹ Rg_* E ⟶ Rg_{L,*} E_L` is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.FirstFailureFunctionField.functionFieldFailure_of_not_baseChangeHolds
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F1D.** With `f : X ⟶ S` and `n` as in [Stacks, Tag 0F02], assume `n`
is invertible on `S`, `BC(f, n, q)` holds and `BC(f, n, q + 1)` does not. Then there are
cartesian squares

```
X  ←--  X'  ←-h-  Y
|f      |         |
S  ←--  S'  ←---  Spec K
```

where `S'` is affine, integral and normal with algebraically closed function field `K = K(S')`,
the bottom right arrow is the canonical morphism from the spectrum of the function field, and
there is an integer `d ∣ n` with `R^{q+1} h_*(ℤ/dℤ)` nonzero
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.FirstFailureFunctionField.FunctionFieldFailure`).

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.KunnethMapOnRingedTopoi.directImageMap
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `Rf_*E ⟶ Rc_*Lp^*E`** for a factorization `c = f ∘ p`: the adjoint
transpose, for `Lc^* ⊣ Rc_*`, of `pullbackDirectImageCounit`.
declarations.statement:
def directImageMap (hp : f.comp p = c)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    (derivedPushforward f).obj E ⟶
      (derivedPushforward c).obj ((derivedPullback p).obj E)
declarations.comment: the canonical map Rf_*E ⟶ Rc_*p⁻¹E

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.KunnethMapOnRingedTopoi.kunnethMapOfCupProduct
declarations.doc:
**The Künneth map, via the relative cup product.**  For morphisms of ringed topoi
`p : W ⟶ X`, `f : X ⟶ S`, `q : W ⟶ Y`, `g : Y ⟶ S` and `c : W ⟶ S` with `c = f ∘ p = g ∘ q`,
and for `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)`, `K ∈ D(𝒪_Y)`, the canonical map

`Rf_*E ⊗^L_{𝒪_S} Rg_*K ⟶ Rc_*(Lp^*E ⊗^L_{𝒪_W} Lq^*K)`.

It is the canonical maps `Rf_*E ⟶ Rc_*Lp^*E` and `Rg_*K ⟶ Rc_*Lq^*K` in the two tensor factors,
followed by the relative cup product of [Stacks, Tag 0B6C] for `c`.
declarations.statement:
def kunnethMapOfCupProduct :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor S.O).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj E)).obj
        ((derivedPushforward g).obj K) ⟶
      (derivedPushforward c).obj
        (((derivedTensorProductFunctor W.O).obj ((derivedPullback p).obj E)).obj
          ((derivedPullback q).obj K))
declarations.comment: the canonical map, via the relative cup product of Remark 0B6C

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.KunnethMapOnRingedTopoi.kunnethMapOfAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**The Künneth map, as an adjoint.**  The same canonical map

`Rf_*E ⊗^L_{𝒪_S} Rg_*K ⟶ Rc_*(Lp^*E ⊗^L_{𝒪_W} Lq^*K)`,

written as the adjoint, for `Lc^* ⊣ Rc_*`, of the compatibility of derived pullback with the
derived tensor product ([Stacks, Tag 07A4]) followed by the maps `Lc^*Rf_*E ⟶ Lp^*E` and
`Lc^*Rg_*K ⟶ Lq^*K` in the two factors.
declarations.statement:
def kunnethMapOfAdjoint :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor S.O).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj E)).obj
        ((derivedPushforward g).obj K) ⟶
      (derivedPushforward c).obj
        (((derivedTensorProductFunctor W.O).obj ((derivedPullback p).obj E)).obj
          ((derivedPullback q).obj K))
declarations.comment: the canonical map, as the adjoint of the map on inverse images

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.KunnethMapOnRingedTopoi.kunnethMapOfCupProduct_eq_kunnethMapOfAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**The two constructions of the Künneth map agree**: `kunnethMapOfCupProduct` equals
`kunnethMapOfAdjoint`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kunnethMapOfCupProduct_eq_kunnethMapOfAdjoint :
    kunnethMapOfCupProduct p f c hmosp hmosf hmosc q g hmosq hmosg hp hq E K =
      kunnethMapOfAdjoint p f c hmosp hmosf hmosc q g hmosq hmosg hp hq E K
declarations.comment: the two constructions of the remark agree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_sheafH_and_epi_counit_of_supportSheaf_subset_closedPoints
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be a separably closed field, let `X` be a scheme of finite type over `K` and let `F`
be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `X` whose support is contained in the set of
closed points of `X`. Then `H^q(X, F) = 0` for `q > 0`, and `F` is globally generated: the
constant sheaf on its group of global sections surjects onto it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem subsingleton_sheafH_and_epi_counit_of_supportSheaf_subset_closedPoints
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsSepClosed K] (X : B.Scheme)
    (f : X.obj ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (F : SmallEtaleAbelianSheaf B X)
    (hF : supportSheaf B X.obj X.property F ⊆ {x : X.obj | IsClosed ({x} : Set X.obj)}) :
    (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1} F q)) ∧
      Epi ((constantSheafΓAdj (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).counit.app F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_iff_forall_isZero_etaleHypercohomology_of_closedPointSupport
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F1G].** Let `K` be a separably closed field, `X` a scheme of finite type over
`K` and `Q` an object of the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on the small étale
site of `X` whose stalks vanish away from the closed points of `X`. Then `Q` is zero if and only
if all of its hypercohomology groups vanish.

One direction is formal. For the other, `Q` is zero exactly when every cohomology sheaf `H^q(Q)`
is zero; the stalk hypothesis says that each `H^q(Q)` is supported at closed points, so
[Stacks, Tag 0BKZ] identifies `H^q(X, Q)` with `Γ(X, H^q(Q))`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_hypercohomologyAbIsoΓHomology_of_supportSheaf_subset_closedPoints`),
and [Stacks, Tag 0F1F] makes a sheaf supported at closed points with no global sections zero
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_of_isZero_Γ_of_supportSheaf_subset_closedPoints`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_iff_forall_isZero_etaleHypercohomology_of_closedPointSupport
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsSepClosed K] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (Q : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X hX) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}))
    (hQ : ∀ (p : GeometricPoint X) (q : ℤ), ¬ IsClosed ({p.hom default} : Set X) →
      IsZero (etaleStalk B X hX p
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X hX) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) q).obj Q).obj)) :
    IsZero Q ↔
      ∀ q : ℤ, IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} q).obj
        ((smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSectionsAb.{u, u + 1} B X hX).obj Q))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.OpenImmersionProductSquare.isIso_baseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be a field, `j : U ⟶ X` an open immersion of schemes of finite type over `K` and `Y`
a scheme of finite type over `K`. For every abelian sheaf `𝓕` on `U_étale` whose stalks are
torsion of orders invertible in `K`, the base change map `q⁻¹Rj_*𝓕 ⟶ Rh_*p⁻¹𝓕` of the square
```
Y ×_K X  ←-h-  Y ×_K U
   |q              |p
   X     ←-j-      U
```
is an isomorphism (in `D⁺((Y ×_K X)_étale)`, `𝓕` placed in degree zero).
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_baseChangeMap {K : Type u} [Field K] {X U Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) (sU : U ⟶ Spec (.of K)) (sY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hj : j ≫ sX = sU) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] [QuasiCompact sX]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sU] [QuasiCompact sU] [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] [QuasiCompact sY]
    (𝓕 : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology U) Ab.{u + 1})
    (h𝓕 : ∀ (t : GeometricPoint U) (a : (smallEtaleStalkAb t.hom).obj 𝓕),
      ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ IsUnit ((n : ℤ) : K) ∧ n • a = 0) :
    IsIso (baseChangeMap sX sU sY j hj 𝓕)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.BaseChangeOverField.isIso_smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb_of_field
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F1I].** Let `K` be a field. For any commutative diagram

```
X  ←-p-  X'  ←-h-  Y
|        |f'       |e
Spec K ←-s- S' ←-g- T
```

of schemes over `K` with `X' = X ×_{Spec K} S'` and `Y = X' ×_{S'} T` and `g` quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and every abelian sheaf `𝓕` on `T_étale` whose stalks are torsion of orders
invertible in `K`, the base change map `(f')⁻¹Rg_*𝓕 ⟶ Rh_*e⁻¹𝓕` is an isomorphism (in
`D⁺(X'_étale)`, `𝓕` placed in degree zero).

`𝓕` is the filtered colimit of its subsheaves `𝓕[n]`, `n` invertible in `K`
(`isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_of_forall_annihilated`), and for those this is
`derivedBaseChangeHolds_of_isUnit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb_of_field (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (πX : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) {S' X' T Y : Scheme.{u}} (s : S' ⟶ Spec (.of K)) (p : X' ⟶ X)
    (f' : X' ⟶ S') (hp : IsPullback p f' πX s) (g : T ⟶ S') (h : Y ⟶ X') (e : Y ⟶ T)
    (sq : IsPullback h e f' g) [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    (𝓕 : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1})
    (h𝓕 : ∀ (t : GeometricPoint T) (a : (smallEtaleStalkAb t.hom).obj 𝓕),
      ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ IsUnit ((n : ℤ) : K) ∧ n • a = 0) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb f' g h e sq.w).app
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj 𝓕))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.EtaleCoefficients.isIso_tensorBaseChangeMap_of_isUnit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F1J].** Let `K` be a field and `n ≥ 1` an integer invertible in `K`. Consider
a commutative diagram
```
X <-p-- X' <-h-- Y
|       |f'      |e
v       v        v
Spec K <- S' <-g- T
```
of schemes with `X' = X ×_{Spec K} S'` and `Y = X' ×_{S'} T` and `g` quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. The canonical map

`p⁻¹E ⊗^L_{ℤ/nℤ} (f')⁻¹Rg_*F ⟶ Rh_*(h⁻¹p⁻¹E ⊗^L_{ℤ/nℤ} e⁻¹F)`

is an isomorphism if `E ∈ D⁺(X_étale, ℤ/nℤ)` has Tor amplitude in `[a, ∞]` for some `a ∈ ℤ` and
`F ∈ D⁺(T_étale, ℤ/nℤ)`.

This is `isIso_tensorBaseChangeMap_zmod_of_derivedBaseChangeHolds`, with derived base change over
`X` and over the schemes finite over the affine opens of `X` given by [Stacks, Tag 0F1I]
(`derivedBaseChangeHolds_of_isUnit`: `X` over `K` is arbitrary there). The lower bound on `E`
(`_hE`, `E ∈ D⁺`) is part of the source's statement; the proof does not need it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_tensorBaseChangeMap_of_isUnit (K : Type u) [Field K] (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (hn : IsUnit (n : K)) {X X' Y S' T : Scheme.{u}} (πX : X ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    (πS : S' ⟶ Spec (.of K)) (p : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (hX' : IsPullback p f' πX πS)
    (g : T ⟶ S') (h : Y ⟶ X') (e : Y ⟶ T) (hY : IsPullback h e f' g) [QuasiCompact g]
    [QuasiSeparated g] (E : DerivedModules (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) X) (_hE : ∃ b : ℤ, E.IsGE b)
    (a : ℤ) (hEa : HasTorAmplitudeGE (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) E a)
    (F : DerivedModules (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) T) (hF : ∃ b : ℤ, F.IsGE b) :
    IsIso (tensorBaseChangeMap (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) f' g h e hY.w
      ((pullback (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) p).obj E) F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineZariski.abelian_fullyFaithful_and_essImage_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F1L.** Let `S_affine` be the affine opens of the scheme `S` with the chaotic
topology, for which abelian sheaves are abelian presheaves, let `S_{affine,Zar}` be the same
category with the Zariski topology, and let `ε : S_{affine,Zar} ⟶ S_affine` be the comparison.
Then the derived direct image `Rε_* : D(S_{affine,Zar}) ⟶ D(S_affine)` is fully faithful, and an
object `K` of `D⁺(S_affine)` is in its essential image if and only if

1. `RΓ(∅, K)` is zero in `D(Ab)`, and
2. whenever `U = V ∪ W` with `U, V, W` affine opens of `S` and `V, W ⊆ U` standard opens, the map
   `c^K_{U,V,W,V ∩ W}` of Stacks 0F16 is a quasi-isomorphism.

`Rε_*` is any right derived functor of `ε_*`, given with its unit `η`; condition (1) is stated
for every affine open with empty underlying scheme, and condition (2) for every square of affine
opens exhibiting `U` as the union of two standard opens with intersection the fourth corner.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelian_fullyFaithful_and_essImage_iff :
    Nonempty Rε.FullyFaithful ∧
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (chaotic B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}),
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t
          (C := Sheaf (chaotic B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).plus K →
        (Rε.essImage K ↔
          (∀ U : SmallAffineZariski B S hS, IsEmpty ((toScheme B S hS).obj U) →
              IsZero ((chaoticDerivedSections B S hS U).obj K)) ∧
            ∀ sq : Square (SmallAffineZariski B S hS), IsStandardOpenCoverSquare B S hS sq →
              (chaoticCSquareData B S hS sq).IsCSquareIso K)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.hasTorAmplitudeGE_iff_exists_kFlatRepresentative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F1M.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site, `E` an object of `D(O)` and `a` an integer.
Then `E` has Tor amplitude in `[a, ∞]` for the derived tensor product of `D(O)` — that is,
`E ⊗^L_O F[0]` has no cohomology below `a` for every `O`-module `F` — if and only if `E` is
represented by a K-flat complex of flat `O`-modules vanishing in every degree below `a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitudeGE_iff_exists_kFlatRepresentative
    (E : RingedSite.DerivedModules.{u, u, u, d} X) (a : ℤ) :
    letI : X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u} := inferInstance
    DerivedTensorProduct.HasTorAmplitudeGE (canonicalDerivedTensorProduct.{u, u, d} X) E a ↔
      ∃ K : CochainComplex (RingedSite.Modules.{u, u, u} X) ℤ,
        IsKFlat X.O K ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X.O) (K.X i)) ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ, i < a → IsZero (K.X i)) ∧
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E)
declarations.comment: equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_pullbackStable_kFlatRepresentative_of_hasTorAmplitudeGE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F1M, the "moreover" clause.** An object `E` of `D(O)` with Tor amplitude in
`[a, ∞]` for the derived tensor product of `D(O)` is represented by a complex `K` which is
K-flat, has flat terms and vanishes in every degree below `a`, and which moreover stays K-flat
with flat terms under pullback: for every morphism `f` of ringed topoi into `(C, O)` presented
by a morphism of sites, the degreewise pullback `f^*K` is K-flat and each of its terms is
flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pullbackStable_kFlatRepresentative_of_hasTorAmplitudeGE
    (E : RingedSite.DerivedModules.{u, u, u, d} X) (a : ℤ)
    (hE :
      letI : X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u} := inferInstance
      DerivedTensorProduct.HasTorAmplitudeGE
        (canonicalDerivedTensorProduct.{u, u, d} X) E a) :
    letI : X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u} := inferInstance
    ∃ K : CochainComplex (RingedSite.Modules.{u, u, u} X) ℤ,
      IsKFlat X.O K ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X.O) (K.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, i < a → IsZero (K.X i)) ∧
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E) ∧
      ∀ X' : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.{u, u, u},
        letI : X'.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u} := inferInstance
        ∀ f : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom X' (RingedSite.ringedTopos X),
          f.u.IsMorphismOfSites (RingedSite.ringedTopos X).J X'.J →
            IsKFlat X'.O
                ((Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.KFlatPullback.pullbackComplex f).obj K) ∧
              ∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X'.O)
                (((Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.KFlatPullback.pullbackComplex f).obj K).X i)
declarations.comment:
the Moreover clause: the representative stays K-flat, and keeps flat terms, under
pullback

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.EtaleCoefficients.isIso_tensorBaseChangeMap_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F1N].** Let `K` be a field and `n ≥ 1` an integer invertible in `K`.
Consider a commutative diagram
```
X <-p-- X' <-h-- Y
|       |f'      |e
v       v        v
Spec K <- S' <-g- T
```
of schemes of finite type over `K` (through `πX`, `πS` and `g ≫ πS`) with `X' = X ×_K S'` and
`Y = X' ×_{S'} T`. Then the canonical map

`p⁻¹E ⊗^L_{ℤ/nℤ} (f')⁻¹Rg_*F ⟶ Rh_*(h⁻¹p⁻¹E ⊗^L_{ℤ/nℤ} e⁻¹F)`

is an isomorphism for all `E ∈ D(X_étale, ℤ/nℤ)` and `F ∈ D(T_étale, ℤ/nℤ)`.

The reduction to `E ∈ D⁺` of Tor amplitude bounded below and `F ∈ D⁺`, where the functors
commute with direct sums because `cd(g), cd(h) < ∞` ([Stacks, Tag 0F10]), is
`isIso_tensorBaseChangeMap_of_finiteType_of_isGE`; the bounded below case is [Stacks, Tag 0F1J]
(`isIso_tensorBaseChangeMap_of_isUnit`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_tensorBaseChangeMap_of_finiteType (K : Type u) [Field K] (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (hn : IsUnit (n : K)) {X X' Y S' T : Scheme.{u}} (πX : X ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    (πS : S' ⟶ Spec (.of K)) (p : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (h : Y ⟶ X') (e : Y ⟶ T)
    (g : T ⟶ S') [LocallyOfFiniteType πX] [QuasiCompact πX] [LocallyOfFiniteType πS]
    [QuasiCompact πS] [LocallyOfFiniteType (g ≫ πS)] [QuasiCompact (g ≫ πS)]
    (hX' : IsPullback p f' πX πS) (hY : IsPullback h e f' g)
    (E : DerivedModules (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) X)
    (F : DerivedModules (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) T) :
    IsIso (tensorBaseChangeMap (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) f' g h e hY.w
      ((pullback (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) p).obj E) F)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.EtaleCoefficients.isIso_kunnethMap_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F1P], as the Künneth map of [Stacks, Tag 0F1E].** Let `k` be a separably
closed field, `X` and `Y` schemes of finite type over `k` (through `f` and `g`), and `n ≥ 1` an
integer invertible in `k`. For `E ∈ D(X_étale, ℤ/nℤ)` and `K ∈ D(Y_étale, ℤ/nℤ)` the Künneth map

`RΓ(X, E) ⊗^L_{ℤ/nℤ} RΓ(Y, K) = Rf_*E ⊗^L Rg_*K ⟶ R(pr₁ ≫ f)_*(pr₁⁻¹E ⊗^L pr₂⁻¹K)
  = RΓ(X ×_k Y, pr₁⁻¹E ⊗^L pr₂⁻¹K)`

is an isomorphism in `D((Spec k)_étale, ℤ/nℤ) = D(ℤ/nℤ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_kunnethMap_of_isSepClosed (hn : IsUnit (n : k))
    (E : DerivedModules (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) X)
    (K : DerivedModules (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) Y) :
    IsIso (kunnethMap (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) (Limits.pullback.fst f g) f
      (Limits.pullback.snd f g) g Limits.pullback.condition E K)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.EtaleCoefficients.kunnethOverSepClosedIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F1P].** Let `k` be a separably closed field, `X` and `Y` schemes of finite
type over `k` (through `f` and `g`), and `n ≥ 1` an integer invertible in `k`. For
`E ∈ D(X_étale, ℤ/nℤ)` and `K ∈ D(Y_étale, ℤ/nℤ)`

`RΓ(X ×_k Y, pr₁⁻¹E ⊗^L_{ℤ/nℤ} pr₂⁻¹K) ≅ RΓ(X, E) ⊗^L_{ℤ/nℤ} RΓ(Y, K)`

in `D(ℤ/nℤ)`, where `RΓ(Z, -) = Γ ∘ R(Z ⟶ Spec k)_*` for the global sections equivalence
`Γ : D((Spec k)_étale, ℤ/nℤ) ≌ D(ℤ/nℤ)` (`derivedModulesEquivOfSepClosed`). It is the inverse of
`Γ` of the Künneth map of [Stacks, Tag 0F1E] (`isIso_kunnethMap_of_isSepClosed`), followed by the
compatibility of `Γ` with `⊗^L` (`kunnethOverSepClosedIso_inv`).
declarations.statement:
def kunnethOverSepClosedIso [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)))]
    (hn : IsUnit (n : k))
    (E : DerivedModules (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) X)
    (K : DerivedModules (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) Y) :
    (derivedModulesEquivOfSepClosed k (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n))).functor.obj
        ((pushforward (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) (Limits.pullback.fst f g ≫ f)).obj
          (((tensor (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) (Limits.pullback f g)).obj
            ((pullback (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) (Limits.pullback.fst f g)).obj E)).obj
              ((pullback (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) (Limits.pullback.snd f g)).obj K))) ≅
      ((CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct
          (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n))).tensor.obj
        ((derivedModulesEquivOfSepClosed k (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n))).functor.obj
          ((pushforward (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) f).obj E))).obj
        ((derivedModulesEquivOfSepClosed k (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n))).functor.obj
          ((pushforward (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) g).obj K))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.EtaleCoefficients.kunnethOverSepClosedIso_inv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F1P]: the isomorphism is the Künneth map of [Stacks, Tag 0F1E].** The inverse
of `kunnethOverSepClosedIso` is the compatibility of `Γ` with `⊗^L`,
`RΓ(X, E) ⊗^L RΓ(Y, K) ≅ Γ(Rf_*E ⊗^L Rg_*K)`, followed by `Γ` of the Künneth map
`Rf_*E ⊗^L Rg_*K ⟶ R(pr₁ ≫ f)_*(pr₁⁻¹E ⊗^L pr₂⁻¹K)` of Tag 0F1E.
declarations.statement:
theorem kunnethOverSepClosedIso_inv
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)))] (hn : IsUnit (n : k))
    (E : DerivedModules (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) X)
    (K : DerivedModules (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) Y) :
    (kunnethOverSepClosedIso k n f g hn E K).inv =
      (((derivedModulesEquivOfSepClosedTensorIso k (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n))).app
          ((pushforward (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) f).obj E)).app
          ((pushforward (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) g).obj K)).inv ≫
        (derivedModulesEquivOfSepClosed k (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n))).functor.map
          (kunnethMap (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)) (Limits.pullback.fst f g) f
            (Limits.pullback.snd f g) g Limits.pullback.condition E K)

The right-hand map is the difference of the two maps induced by localization.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence (f : R) :
    ShortComplex AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.exists_isOpen_adic_submodule_completionAlong
declarations.doc:
The completion of a module containing an open `I`-adic submodule again contains an open
submodule with the `I`-adic topology.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_isOpen_adic_submodule_completionAlong
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R] [IsTopologicalRing R]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    [IsTopologicalAddGroup M] [ContinuousSMul R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.FG) (N : Submodule R M) (_hN : IsOpen (N : Set M))
    (_hAdic : (𝓝 (0 : N)).HasBasis (fun _ : ℕ ↦ True)
      (fun n ↦ ((I ^ n • ⊤ : Submodule R N) : Set N))) :
    ∃ P : Submodule R (TopologicalRing.CompletionAlong I N),
      @IsOpen (TopologicalRing.CompletionAlong I N)
          (TopologicalRing.CompletionAlong.limitTopology I N) (P : Set _) ∧
        TopologicalSpace.induced
          (fun p : P => (p : TopologicalRing.CompletionAlong I N))
          (TopologicalRing.CompletionAlong.limitTopology I N) = I.adicModuleTopology P
declarations.comment: open_adic_completion

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.CompletionAlong.quotPowEquiv
declarations.doc:
The second conclusion of Tag 0F1S at the level of the filtration `I ^ n N`:
`M^ / I ^ n M^ = M / I ^ n M`.
declarations.comment: completion_mod_ideal_power

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.exists_isOpen_adic_submodule_completionOverOpen
declarations.doc:
Tag 0F1S, first conclusion, over the completion of `M` taken over all of its open
submodules: `M^` has an open submodule whose topology is `I`-adic.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_isOpen_adic_submodule_completionOverOpen (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.FG)
    (N : Submodule R M) (hN : IsOpen (N : Set M))
    (hAdic : (𝓝 (0 : N)).HasBasis (fun _ : ℕ ↦ True)
      (fun n ↦ ((I ^ n • ⊤ : Submodule R N) : Set N))) :
    ∃ P : Submodule R (CompletionOverOpen R M),
      @IsOpen (CompletionOverOpen R M) (CompletionOverOpen.limitTopology R M) (P : Set _) ∧
        TopologicalSpace.induced (fun p : P ↦ (p : CompletionOverOpen R M))
          (CompletionOverOpen.limitTopology R M) = I.adicModuleTopology P
declarations.comment: open_adic_completion

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.completionOverOpenQuotPowEquiv
declarations.doc:
Tag 0F1S, second conclusion, over the completion of `M` taken over all of its open
submodules: `M^ / I ^ n M^ = M / I ^ n M` for every `n`, in particular for every `n ≥ 1`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def completionOverOpenQuotPowEquiv (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.FG)
    (N : Submodule R M) (hN : IsOpen (N : Set M))
    (hAdic : (𝓝 (0 : N)).HasBasis (fun _ : ℕ ↦ True)
      (fun n ↦ ((I ^ n • ⊤ : Submodule R N) : Set N))) (n : ℕ) :
    ((CompletionOverOpen R M) ⧸ (I ^ n • ⊤ : Submodule R (CompletionOverOpen R M))) ≃ₗ[R]
      (M ⧸ (I ^ n • ⊤ : Submodule R M))
declarations.comment: completion_mod_ideal_power

declarations.name: isRegular_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
Given a short exact sequence `0 → M₁ →[α] M₂ →[β] M₃ → 0` of `R`-modules, if a sequence `rs` of
elements of `R` is both `M₁`-regular and `M₃`-regular, then it is `M₂`-regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegular_of_shortExact {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type*} [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁]
    [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂] [AddCommGroup M₃] [Module R M₃]
    (α : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂) (β : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃)
    (hα : Function.Injective α) (hβ : Function.Surjective β)
    (hexact : LinearMap.range α = LinearMap.ker β)
    (rs : List R)
    (h1 : IsRegular M₁ rs) (h3 : IsRegular M₃ rs) :
    IsRegular M₂ rs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIndQuasiAffineHom_tfae
declarations.doc:
Ind-quasi-affineness of a morphism of schemes can be tested on the quasi-compact open
subschemes above the affine opens of the target, above the members of one cover of the target by
quasi-compact quasi-separated opens, or above all quasi-compact quasi-separated opens of the
target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIndQuasiAffineHom_tfae {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsIndQuasiAffineHom f,
      ∀ (V : Y.Opens), IsAffineOpen V →
        ∀ (U : (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme.Opens), IsCompact (U : Set (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme) →
          IsQuasiAffineHom (U.ι ≫ f ∣_ V),
      ∃ (ι : Type u) (V : ι → Y.Opens),
        (iSup V = ⊤) ∧
          (∀ j, IsCompact (V j : Set Y)) ∧
          (∀ j, IsQuasiSeparated (V j : Set Y)) ∧
          (∀ j (U : (f ⁻¹ᵁ V j).toScheme.Opens),
              IsCompact (U : Set (f ⁻¹ᵁ V j).toScheme) →
                IsQuasiAffineHom (U.ι ≫ f ∣_ (V j))),
      ∀ (V : Y.Opens), IsCompact (V : Set Y) → IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set Y) →
        ∀ (U : (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme.Opens), IsCompact (U : Set (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme) →
          IsQuasiAffineHom (U.ι ≫ f ∣_ V)]
declarations.comment: equivalent characterizations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIndQuasiAffineHom_isZariskiLocalAtTarget
declarations.doc: Being an ind-quasi-affine morphism is Zariski local on the base.
declarations.statement:
instance isIndQuasiAffineHom_isZariskiLocalAtTarget :
    IsZariskiLocalAtTarget (@IsIndQuasiAffineHom : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
declarations.comment: Zariski locality on the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIndQuasiAffineHom_isStableUnderComposition
declarations.doc: Being an ind-quasi-affine morphism of schemes is stable under composition.

      (@IsIndQuasiAffineHom : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.normal_iff_isCompletelyNormal_of_powerSeries_flat
declarations.doc:
A domain whose power series ring is flat over its polynomial ring is normal
if and only if it is completely normal.
declarations.statement:
theorem normal_iff_isCompletelyNormal_of_powerSeries_flat
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    (hflat : Module.Flat (Polynomial R) (PowerSeries R)) :
    IsIntegrallyClosed R ↔ IsCompletelyNormal R

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.instFlatPowerSeriesOfValuationRing
declarations.doc: The power series ring over a valuation ring is flat over its coefficient ring.
declarations.statement:
instance instFlatPowerSeriesOfValuationRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [ValuationRing R] : Module.Flat R (PowerSeries R)
declarations.comment: flat over the coefficient ring

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.not_flat_powerSeries_over_polynomial_of_dim_gt_one

In dimension greater than one, the power series ring over a valuation ring is not
flat over its polynomial ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_flat_powerSeries_over_polynomial_of_dim_gt_one (R : Type*)
    [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [ValuationRing R] (hdim : 1 < ringKrullDim R) :
    ¬ Module.Flat (Polynomial R) (PowerSeries R)
declarations.comment: not flat over the polynomial ring

declarations.name: Stacks.QuasiAffineGlobalGeneration.exists_affine_nonvanishingOpen_containing_finite_sections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0F20, at the ringed-space spelling**: over `L.sections`, with the
ringed-space nonvanishing open of Stacks Tag 01CY. Transported from
`Stacks.QuasiAffineGlobalGeneration.exists_affine_nonvanishingOpen_containing_finite` along
`Stacks.NonvanishingSpelling.nonvanishingOpen_symm_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_nonvanishingOpen_containing_finite_sections [X.IsQuasiAffine]
    (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] {E : Set X} (hE : E.Finite) (W : X.Opens)
    (hEW : E ⊆ (W : Set X)) :
    ∃ s : (toSheafOfModules X L).sections,
      IsAffineOpen (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X.toRingedSpace
        (toSheafOfModules X L) s) ∧
      E ⊆ (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X.toRingedSpace
        (toSheafOfModules X L) s : Set X) ∧
      Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X.toRingedSpace
        (toSheafOfModules X L) s ≤ W

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GlueingNearPoint.moduleRestrictionFunctorAtPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F21**, the canonical functor.  A module of finite presentation on `S` goes to its
restriction to `U`, its restriction to `Spec 𝒪_{S, s}`, and the canonical identification of the
two restrictions to the punctured local scheme.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def moduleRestrictionFunctorAtPoint (S : Scheme.{u}) (U : S.Opens) (s : S) :
    FinitePresentationModules S ⥤ moduleGlueingDataNearPoint S U s
declarations.comment: the canonical functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GlueingNearPoint.moduleGlueingEquivalenceNearClosedPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F21.** Let `s` be a closed point of a scheme `S` whose open complement
`U = S \ {s}` has quasi-compact inclusion, and let `V = Spec 𝒪_{S, s} ∖ {s}`.  Restricting a
module of finite presentation on `S` to `U` and to `Spec 𝒪_{S, s}`, together with the canonical
identification `α` of the two induced restrictions to `V`, is an equivalence onto the category
of triples `(𝒢, ℋ, α)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def moduleGlueingEquivalenceNearClosedPoint (S : Scheme.{u}) (s : S)
    (hs : IsClosed ({s} : Set S)) (hqc : QuasiCompact (puncturedOpen hs).ι) :
    FinitePresentationModules S ≌ moduleGlueingDataNearPoint S (puncturedOpen hs) s

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.nonempty_preparedExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F23.** Every coherent triple admits a prepared extension: a coherent
module on `Spec A` on which `f` acts regularly, isomorphic to the triple's punctured-spectrum
member over the punctured spectrum, and mapping compatibly to its closed-fibre member.

The module is `𝔪ⁿ G` for a coherent extension `G ⟶ j_*F` of the punctured-spectrum member of the
triple and a suitable power `n`; the three steps are described in the implementation notes of
this file.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_preparedExtension (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (f : A) (T : CoherentTriple A f) :
    Nonempty (PreparedExtension A f T)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.CoherentTriple.eulerCharacteristic
declarations.doc:
**The Euler characteristic of a coherent triple**: the length of the cokernel minus the
length of the kernel of the closed-fibre map of a prepared extension. Prepared extensions exist
by `Stacks.Algebraization.nonempty_preparedExtension`, and the number does not depend on the one
chosen by `Stacks.Algebraization.PreparedExtension.eulerCharacteristic_eq`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def CoherentTriple.eulerCharacteristic {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {f : A} (T : CoherentTriple A f) : ℤ
declarations.comment: the Euler characteristic of the triple itself

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.kernel_finiteLength
declarations.doc: **The kernel of the closed-fibre map of a prepared extension has finite length over `A`.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem kernel_finiteLength
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (f : A)
    (T : CoherentTriple A f) (P : PreparedExtension A f T) :
    IsFiniteLength A (kernel P.closedFibreMap).carrier
declarations.comment: finite length of the kernel

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.cokernel_finiteLength
declarations.doc:
**The cokernel of the closed-fibre map of a prepared extension has finite length over
`A`.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem cokernel_finiteLength
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (f : A)
    (T : CoherentTriple A f) (P : PreparedExtension A f T) :
    IsFiniteLength A (cokernel P.closedFibreMap).carrier
declarations.comment: finite length of the cokernel

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.PreparedExtension.eulerCharacteristic_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F25.** The Euler characteristic of a coherent triple does not depend
on the prepared extension used to compute it: any two prepared extensions of the same triple have
the same Euler characteristic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem PreparedExtension.eulerCharacteristic_eq
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (f : A) (hf : f ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
    (T : CoherentTriple A f) (P Q : PreparedExtension A f T) :
    P.eulerCharacteristic = Q.eulerCharacteristic

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.eulerCharacteristic_add_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F26.** The Euler characteristic of a coherent triple is additive
along a short exact sequence of coherent triples: for any prepared extensions `P`, `Q` and `N`
of the three terms, the Euler characteristic of `Q` is the sum of those of `P` and `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eulerCharacteristic_add_of_shortExact
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (f : A)
    (hf : f ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
    {T S R : CoherentTriple A f} {φ : T.Hom S} {ψ : S.Hom R}
    (hT : CoherentTriple.ShortExact φ ψ)
    (P : PreparedExtension A f T) (Q : PreparedExtension A f S)
    (N : PreparedExtension A f R) :
    Q.eulerCharacteristic = P.eulerCharacteristic + N.eulerCharacteristic

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.CoherentTriple.eulerCharacteristic_add_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F26 for the triples themselves.** The Euler characteristic of a
coherent triple is additive along a short exact sequence of coherent triples.
declarations.statement:
public theorem CoherentTriple.eulerCharacteristic_add_of_shortExact {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {f : A} (hf : f ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
    {T S R : CoherentTriple A f} {φ : CoherentTriple.Hom T S}
    {ψ : CoherentTriple.Hom S R} (hse : CoherentTriple.ShortExact φ ψ) :
    S.eulerCharacteristic = T.eulerCharacteristic + R.eulerCharacteristic
declarations.comment: additivity for the Euler characteristics of the triples themselves

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_polynomial_natDegree_le_dim_supp
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian local ring, `f ∈ 𝔪` a nonzerodivisor, and `(L, L₀, λ)` an invertible
coherent triple. For every coherent triple `T = (F, F₀, α)` there is a polynomial `P ∈ ℚ[t]` with

`χ(T ⊗ (L, L₀, λ)^{⊗ n}) = P(n)` for every `n ∈ ℤ`,

and `deg P ≤ dim(Supp F)`, the dimension being truncated at `0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_polynomial_natDegree_le_dim_supp (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal A)
    (L : CoherentTriple A f) (hL : IsInvertibleTriple L) (T : CoherentTriple A f) :
    ∃ P : Polynomial ℚ,
      (P.natDegree : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ max 0 (topologicalKrullDim ↥(SheafOfModules.supp T.F)) ∧
        ∀ n : ℤ, (((T.twistZ L hL n).eulerCharacteristic : ℤ) : ℚ) = P.eval (n : ℚ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_polynomial_natDegree_le_of_forall_sub_eq
declarations.doc:
**A function on all of `ℤ` whose first difference is a polynomial is a polynomial.** If
`g : ℤ → ℤ` satisfies `g (n + 1) - g n = Q(n)` at every integer `n`, with `Q` a rational
polynomial of degree at most `d`, then `g` agrees at every integer with a rational polynomial of
degree at most `d + 1`.

This is the variant of [Stacks, Tag 00JZ] for functions defined on all integers with which the
proof of [Stacks, Tag 0F27] concludes, and unlike `IsNumericalPolynomial` it constrains the
function at every integer rather than only at large ones.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_polynomial_natDegree_le_of_forall_sub_eq {g : ℤ → ℤ} {d : ℕ}
    {Q : Polynomial ℚ} (hQ : Q.natDegree ≤ d)
    (hg : ∀ n : ℤ, (g (n + 1) : ℚ) - (g n : ℚ) = Q.eval (n : ℚ)) :
    ∃ P : Polynomial ℚ, P.natDegree ≤ d + 1 ∧ ∀ n : ℤ, (g n : ℚ) = P.eval (n : ℚ)
declarations.comment: the concluding step: polynomiality on ℤ from the first difference

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.CoherentTriple.twistPow
declarations.doc:
**The twists of a coherent triple by the nonnegative tensor powers of an invertible coherent
triple.** The zeroth twist is the triple itself and each further one is the tensor product of the
previous one with the invertible triple, so the `n`-th is `(F ⊗ L^{⊗ n}, F₀ ⊗ L₀^{⊗ n}, α ⊗ λ^{⊗
n})` up to the associativity of the tensor product. This is the family whose Euler
characteristics [Stacks, Tag 0F27] asserts to be given by a polynomial.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def CoherentTriple.twistPow {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {f : A} (T L : CoherentTriple A f) (hL : IsInvertibleTriple L) : ℕ → CoherentTriple A f
declarations.comment: the twist of a coherent triple by the nonnegative powers of an invertible triple

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.CoherentTriple.twistZ
declarations.doc:
**The twist of a coherent triple by the `n`-th tensor power of an invertible coherent
triple**, for `n : ℤ`. Its members are the tensor products of the members of the triple with the
`n`-th tensor powers of the members of the invertible triple, and its identification over the
punctured closed fibre is the tensor product of the two identifications, the second taken in its
`n`-th tensor power.

This is the family whose Euler characteristics [Stacks, Tag 0F27] asserts to be given by a
polynomial.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def CoherentTriple.twistZ {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] {f : A}
    (T L : CoherentTriple A f) (hL : IsInvertibleTriple L) (n : ℤ) : CoherentTriple A f
declarations.comment: the integer twists of a coherent triple by an invertible coherent triple

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.CoherentTriple.eulerCharacteristic_eq_length_cokernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F28.** For an invertible coherent triple over a Noetherian local ring
of depth at least three, the Euler characteristic of the triple is the length of the cokernel of
the canonical map on global sections.

The prepared extension taken is the direct image of the triple's punctured-spectrum member; its
closed-fibre map has a cokernel of the same length as that of the canonical map on global
sections, and its kernel vanishes because the global sections of that direct image have depth at
least two over `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem CoherentTriple.eulerCharacteristic_eq_length_cokernel (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (f : A) (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal A) (hreg : IsRegular f)
    (T : CoherentTriple A f)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
      (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme.presheaf
      (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2 T.F]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (closedFibre A f).presheaf
      (closedFibre A f).ringCatSheaf.2 T.F₀]
    (hdepth : 3 ≤ Module.depth A (maximalIdeal A) A) :
    letI := puncturedSectionsModule A T.F
    letI := puncturedClosedFibreSectionsModule A f
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (puncturedClosedFibre A f).ι).obj T.F₀)
    T.eulerCharacteristic =
      ((Module.length A
        (Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (puncturedClosedFibre A f).ι).obj T.F₀, ⊤) ⧸
          LinearMap.range (globalSectionsMap A f T))).toNat : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the Euler characteristic formula

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.CoherentTriple.eulerCharacteristic_nonneg
declarations.doc:
**The Euler characteristic of an invertible coherent triple is nonnegative**, being the
length of a cokernel.
declarations.statement:
public theorem CoherentTriple.eulerCharacteristic_nonneg (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (f : A) (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal A) (hreg : IsRegular f)
    (T : CoherentTriple A f)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
      (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme.presheaf
      (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2 T.F]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (closedFibre A f).presheaf
      (closedFibre A f).ringCatSheaf.2 T.F₀]
    (hdepth : 3 ≤ Module.depth A (maximalIdeal A) A) :
    0 ≤ T.eulerCharacteristic
declarations.comment: nonnegativity

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.globalSectionsMap
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map on global sections of a coherent triple.** It carries a section of the
module on the punctured spectrum to its restriction to the punctured closed fibre, read through
the triple's identification as a section of the module on the closed fibre. It is linear over
`A`, which acts on both sides through the structure morphisms.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def globalSectionsMap (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (f : A)
    (T : CoherentTriple A f) :
    letI := puncturedSectionsModule A T.F
    letI := puncturedClosedFibreSectionsModule A f
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (puncturedClosedFibre A f).ι).obj T.F₀)
    Γ(T.F, ⊤) →ₗ[A] Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (puncturedClosedFibre A f).ι).obj T.F₀, ⊤)
declarations.comment: the canonical map on global sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.finiteLength_cokernel_globalSectionsMap
declarations.doc:
**The cokernel of the canonical map on global sections has finite length.** The restriction
map from the closed fibre to the punctured closed fibre is surjective, by Hartogs extension on
`A / fA`, and restriction along the closed immersion is surjective on global sections, so the
cokernel is a quotient of the cokernel of the closed-fibre map of any prepared extension of the
triple, which has finite length.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteLength_cokernel_globalSectionsMap (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (f : A) (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal A) (hreg : IsRegular f)
    (T : CoherentTriple A f)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (closedFibre A f).presheaf
      (closedFibre A f).ringCatSheaf.2 T.F₀]
    (hdepth : 3 ≤ Module.depth A (maximalIdeal A) A) :
    letI := puncturedSectionsModule A T.F
    letI := puncturedClosedFibreSectionsModule A f
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (puncturedClosedFibre A f).ι).obj T.F₀)
    IsFiniteLength A
      (Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (puncturedClosedFibre A f).ι).obj T.F₀, ⊤) ⧸
        LinearMap.range (globalSectionsMap A f T))
declarations.comment: finite length of the cokernel

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.CoherentTriple.eulerCharacteristic_eq_zero_iff_isTrivial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F28.** For an invertible coherent triple over a Noetherian local ring
of depth at least three, the Euler characteristic of the triple vanishes exactly when the member
on the punctured spectrum is trivial.

By the Euler-characteristic formula the vanishing is the surjectivity of the canonical map on
global sections, which for the prepared extension given by the direct image of the
punctured-spectrum member is the surjectivity of the closed-fibre map; that map is injective by
`Stacks.Algebraization.injective_closedFibreMap_of_pushforward`, and the two halves of the
criterion are
`Stacks.Algebraization.isTrivial_of_bijective_closedFibreMap` and
`Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_closedFibreMap_of_isTrivial`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem CoherentTriple.eulerCharacteristic_eq_zero_iff_isTrivial (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (f : A) (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal A) (hreg : IsRegular f)
    (T : CoherentTriple A f)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
      (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme.presheaf
      (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2 T.F]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (closedFibre A f).presheaf
      (closedFibre A f).ringCatSheaf.2 T.F₀]
    (hdepth : 3 ≤ Module.depth A (maximalIdeal A) A) :
    T.eulerCharacteristic = 0 ↔
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsTrivial (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme.presheaf
        (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2 T.F
declarations.comment: vanishing criterion

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.picRestrictionInjOnTorsion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F2A.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and let `f ∈ 𝔪` be a
nonzerodivisor with `depth(A/fA) ≥ 2`. Let `U` be the punctured spectrum of `A` and `U₀` the
punctured spectrum of `A/fA`. Then `Pic(U) → Pic(U₀)` is injective on torsion.

Two classes of finite order with the same restriction have a difference of finite order
restricting to zero, and such a difference is zero by
`Stacks.Algebraization.eq_zero_of_schemePullbackClass_eq_zero_of_isOfFinAddOrder`.

The Euler-characteristic polynomiality the argument rests on is [Stacks, Tag 0F27], proved as
`Stacks.Algebraization.exists_polynomial_natDegree_le_dim_supp`, and the `f`-torsion-freeness of
`𝒪_U` is proved, from `f` being a nonzerodivisor, by
`Stacks.Algebraization.isFTorsionFree_unitModule`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem picRestrictionInjOnTorsion (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (f : A) (hfm : f ∈ maximalIdeal A) (hreg : IsRegular f)
    (hb : 2 ≤ Module.depth A (maximalIdeal A) (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f})) :
    Set.InjOn (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClass (puncturedClosedFibreRestriction A f))
      {x : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme |
        IsOfFinAddOrder x}

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.puncturedClosedFibreRestriction_injOn_torsion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F2A.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and let `f ∈ 𝔪` be a
nonzerodivisor with `depth(A/fA) ≥ 2`. Let `U` be the punctured spectrum of `A` and `U₀` the
punctured spectrum of `A/fA`. Then `Pic(U) → Pic(U₀)` is injective on torsion.

The map is pullback of invertible modules along the restriction `U₀ ⟶ U` of the closed immersion
`Spec(A/fA) ⟶ Spec A`. This is an alias of `Stacks.Algebraization.picRestrictionInjOnTorsion`.
declarations.statement: alias puncturedClosedFibreRestriction_injOn_torsion

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.kollar_picRestrictionInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F2B** (Kollár). Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and `f ∈ 𝔪`.
Assume

1. `A` has a dualizing complex,
2. `f` is a nonzerodivisor,
3. `depth(A/fA) ≥ 2`, and
4. every prime `𝔭 ∋ f` with `dim(A/𝔭) = 2` has `depth(A_𝔭) ≥ 2`.

Let `U`, resp. `U₀`, be the punctured spectrum of `A`, resp. of `A/fA`. Then `Pic(U) → Pic(U₀)`
is injective. Finally, if (1), (2), (3) hold, `A` satisfies Serre's condition `(S₂)` and
`dim(A) ≥ 4`, then (4) holds.

This is the proposition's own conclusion, under the source's four hypotheses and nothing else:
`Stacks.Algebraization.picRestrictionInjective_kollar`, after translating hypothesis (3) into
`depth(A) ≥ 3` by `Stacks.Algebraization.le_depth_quotient_span_singleton_iff` and replacing the
dualizing complex by the unique shift of it that is normalized
(`Dualizing.exists_isNormalizedDualizingComplex_shift`).

The source's closing sentence — that (1), (2), (3) together with `(S₂)` and `dim(A) ≥ 4` imply
(4) — is the other half of the tag, and is
`Stacks.Serre.LocalizationDepth.two_le_ringDepth_localization_of_isDualizingComplex`, which
carries the tag's attribute for that assertion. The two attribute strings partition the
proposition, so this one claims only the injectivity.
declarations.statement:
public theorem kollar_picRestrictionInjective (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (f : A) (hfm : f ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) :
    ∀ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K →
      IsSMulRegular A f →
      2 ≤ Module.depth A (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f}) →
      (∀ p : Ideal A, ∀ _ : p.IsPrime, f ∈ p → ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p) = 2 →
        2 ≤ Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p)) (Localization.AtPrime p)) →
      Function.Injective
        (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClass (puncturedClosedFibreRestriction A f))
declarations.comment: the proposition: Pic(U) → Pic(U₀) is injective

declarations.name: Stacks.Serre.LocalizationDepth.two_le_ringDepth_localization_of_isDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**The last assertion of [Stacks, Tag 0F2B].** Let `A` be a Noetherian local ring admitting a
dualizing complex, satisfying Serre's condition `(S₂)` and of dimension at least four. Then the
localization of `A` at a prime whose quotient has dimension two has depth at least two, which is
the fourth hypothesis of that source's proposition.

A ring with a dualizing complex is universally catenary, hence catenary, so this is the
preceding statement. The source restricts the primes to those containing an element `f` which it
assumes to be a nonzerodivisor with `depth(A ⧸ fA) ≥ 2`; neither `f` nor those two hypotheses
enter the argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem two_le_ringDepth_localization_of_isDualizingComplex (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] {K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)}
    (hK : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K) (hS₂ : PropertySkRing A 2)
    (hdim : 4 ≤ ringKrullDim A) :
    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p.asIdeal) = 2 →
      2 ≤ ringDepth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
declarations.comment: the last assertion: (S₂) and dimension at least four give hypothesis (4)

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.picardColimitSurjective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F2D].** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and `f ∈ 𝔪`. Assume

1. `A` is `f`-adically complete,
2. `f` is a nonzerodivisor,
3. `H¹_𝔪(A/fA)` and `H²_𝔪(A/fA)` are finite `A`-modules, and
4. `H³_𝔪(A/fA) = 0`.

Let `U`, resp. `U₀`, be the punctured spectrum of `A`, resp. of `A/fA`. Then
`colim_{U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U open} Pic(U') ⟶ Pic(U₀)` is surjective: every invertible module on `U₀` is
the restriction of an invertible module on an open `U'` of `U` containing `U₀`. The conclusion is
`Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.PicardColimitSurjective`, the elementwise form of surjectivity
out of the filtered colimit.

The proof is the source's. A class on `U₀` extends to a compatible family along the
infinitesimal neighbourhoods `Uₙ = V((f𝒪_U)ⁿ⁺¹)` by [Stacks, Tag 0C6R] and
`H²(U₀, 𝒪_{U₀}) = H³_𝔪(A/fA) = 0` (`exists_compatible_idealPowerStages`); the representing
invertible modules, pushed forward to `U`, form a finite locally free object of `Coh(U, f𝒪_U)`
(`Stacks.Coherent.IdealPowerStageModules`); by [Stacks, Tag 0EKZ] it is the completion of a
finite locally free `𝒢` on an open `V ⊇ U₀` (`exists_completion_iso_of_eq_situation`); `𝒢`
restricts to the given module on `U₀`
(`Stacks.Coherent.IdealPowerStageModules.exists_pullback_iso_of_completion_iso`) and is
therefore invertible on an open `U' ⊇ U₀` (`exists_opens_isInvertible_of_pullback_iso`).
declarations.statement:
theorem picardColimitSurjective [IsNoetherianRing A] (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal A)
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) A) (hreg : IsSMulRegular A f)
    (hH1 : Module.Finite A (Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, u} A
      {closedPoint A} ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f}))) 1))
    (hH2 : Module.Finite A (Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, u} A
      {closedPoint A} ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f}))) 2))
    (hvanish3 : IsZero (Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, u} A
      {closedPoint A} ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f}))) 3)) :
    PicardColimitSurjective A f

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.exists_isCompatible
declarations.doc:
**The first half of the proof of [Stacks, Tag 0F2D].**  Let `X₀ ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ ⋯` be a tower of
first-order thickenings in which the ideal sheaf of every stage has vanishing second cohomology.
Then every Picard class on the bottom stage extends to a compatible family of Picard classes
along the whole tower.

This is the step the source writes as "this gives an exact sequence
`Pic(U_{n+1}) → Pic(U_n) → H²(U₀, 𝒪_{U₀}) = H³_𝔪(A/fA) = 0`.  Therefore each invertible
`𝒪_{U₀}`-module is restricted from an invertible object of `Coh(U, f𝒪_U)`."  Each single lift is
`surjective_picardRestriction_of_forall_eq_zero`, and the family is assembled by recursion on the
stage, choosing a lift at each step.

What remains of the tag after this is [Stacks, Tag 0EKZ], which descends the formal object so
obtained to an invertible module on an open `U'` with `U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U`; see
`Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.PicardColimitSurjective` for the conclusion that needs it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCompatible
    (h2 : ∀ n, ∀ x : CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H.{u}
      (Stacks.Thickenings.idealAddSheafOnSub (T.hom n)) 2, x = 0)
    (c₀ : Pic (T.obj 0)) :
    ∃ c : (n : ℕ) → Pic (T.obj n), c 0 = c₀ ∧ IsCompatible T c
declarations.comment: the first half of the source's proof, in the generality the argument has: for a tower of first-order thickenings whose ideal sheaves have vanishing H², every Picard class on the bottom stage extends to a compatible family along the whole tower. That is the source's step `Pic(U_{n+1}) → Pic(U_n) → H²(U₀,𝒪_{U₀}) = H³_𝔪(A/fA) = 0, therefore each invertible 𝒪_{U₀}-module is restricted from an invertible object of Coh(U,f𝒪_U)`, and the single-stage lift is Stacks 0C6R, Stacks.Thickenings.exact_picardRestriction in StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Thickenings.PicardSequence. The vanishing of H² is a condition on the tower, not every tower satisfying it; for the same half at the punctured spectrum, with that vanishing derived from the source's own hypotheses (2) f a nonzerodivisor and (4) H³_𝔪(A/fA) = 0, see Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.exists_isCompatiblePullback_puncturedSpectrum. NOT covered by this declaration: the tag's own conclusion, surjectivity of colim_{U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U} Pic(U') → Pic(U₀), written as Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.PicardColimitSurjective, which needs Stacks 0EKZ and through it Stacks 0EIR part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.exists_isCompatiblePullback_puncturedSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**The first half of the proof of [Stacks, Tag 0F2D].** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local
ring and let `f ∈ 𝔪` be a nonzerodivisor with `H³_𝔪(A/fA) = 0`. Then every Picard class on the
bottom stage of the tower of infinitesimal neighbourhoods of `U₀` in the punctured spectrum `U`
extends to a family of classes along the whole tower, each the pullback of the next.

Only hypotheses (2) and (4) of the tag are used. The tower is
`Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.infinitesimalTower` of
`Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.puncturedPrincipalImmersion`, the layers are all `𝒪_{U₀}` because
`f` is a nonzerodivisor generating the ideal sheaf on every chart, and the single-stage lift is
the exact sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0C6R].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCompatiblePullback_puncturedSpectrum [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal A) (hreg : IsSMulRegular A f)
    (hvanish3 : IsZero (Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, u} A
      {closedPoint A} ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f}))) 3))
    (c₀ : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme
      (nthOrderInfinitesimalNeighbourhood (puncturedPrincipalImmersion A f) 0)) :
    ∃ c : (n : ℕ) → Stacks.Picard.ofScheme
        ((infinitesimalTower (puncturedPrincipalImmersion A f)).obj n),
      c 0 = c₀ ∧
        IsCompatiblePullback (infinitesimalTower (puncturedPrincipalImmersion A f)) c
declarations.comment: the first half of the source's proof at the punctured spectrum itself, under the source's own hypotheses (2) f a nonzerodivisor and (4) H³_𝔪(A/fA) = 0 and nothing else: every Picard class on U₀ extends to a family along the tower of infinitesimal neighbourhoods of U₀ in U, each the pullback of the next. The per-stage vanishing H²(U_n's ideal sheaf) = 0 is proved here, not assumed: the layers are identified with 𝒪_{U₀} by multiplication by f^{n+1} (Stacks.Thickenings.idealSheafIsoStructureSheafNthOrderBottom, which is where (2) enters) and H²(U₀,𝒪_{U₀}) = 0 is derived from (4). NOT covered: the tag's own conclusion, surjectivity of colim_{U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U} Pic(U') → Pic(U₀), which is the second half and needs Stacks 0EKZ, hence Stacks 0EIR part (2); hypotheses (1) f-adic completeness and (3) finiteness of H¹_𝔪(A/fA), H²_𝔪(A/fA) are inputs of that half alone and do not appear here

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.picardColimitSurjective_of_isDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F2E].** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and `f ∈ 𝔪`. Assume

1. `A` has a dualizing complex,
2. `A` is `f`-adically complete,
3. `f` is a nonzerodivisor,
4. one of the following is true
   * (a) `A_f` is `(S₂)` and for `𝔭 ⊂ A`, `f ∉ 𝔭` minimal we have `dim(A/𝔭) ≥ 4`, or
   * (b) if `𝔭 ∉ V(f)` and `V(𝔭) ∩ V(f) ≠ {𝔪}`, then `depth(A_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > 3`,
5. `H³_𝔪(A/fA) = 0`.

Then the conclusion of [Stacks, Tag 0F2D] holds: with `U`, resp. `U₀`, the punctured spectrum of
`A`, resp. of `A/fA`, the map `colim_{U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U open} Pic(U') ⟶ Pic(U₀)` is surjective. As
for [Stacks, Tag 0F2D] (`Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.picardColimitSurjective`), the conclusion
is `Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.PicardColimitSurjective`, the elementwise form of surjectivity
out of the filtered colimit: every invertible module on `U₀` is the restriction of an invertible
module on an open `U'` of `U` containing `U₀`.

Hypothesis (4a) reads "`A_f` is `(S₂)`" as `PropertySkRing (Localization.Away f) 2`, Serre's
condition of [Stacks, Tag 031P] for the ring `A_f`; in (4b), `V(f)` is the set of primes
containing `f`. Hypothesis (1) is read in any model `[HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat A)]` of the
derived category; whether a dualizing complex exists does not depend on the model. These are the
spellings of [Stacks, Tag 0EKY]
(`Stacks.Algebraization.completionEquivalence_local_principal_finiteLocallyFree`). Hypothesis (5)
is written, as in [Stacks, Tag 0F2D], in the library's default model, before the model of (1) is
introduced, so that the two do not interfere.

The proof is the source's: that of [Stacks, Tag 0F2D] with [Stacks, Tag 0EKY] in place of
[Stacks, Tag 0EKZ]. A class on `U₀` extends along the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of `U₀` by
[Stacks, Tag 0C6R] and `H²(U₀, 𝒪_{U₀}) = H³_𝔪(A/fA) = 0`, giving an invertible object of
`Coh(U, f𝒪_U)`; by the essential surjectivity of [Stacks, Tag 0EKY] it is the completion of a
finite locally free module on an open `V ⊇ U₀`, which is invertible near `U₀`
(`Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.picardColimitSurjective_of_forall_isCompletionNearClosed`).
declarations.statement:
theorem picardColimitSurjective_of_isDualizingComplex [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal A)
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) A) (hreg : IsSMulRegular A f)
    (hvanish3 : IsZero (Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, u} A
      {closedPoint A} ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f}))) 3))
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} A)]
    (hdual : ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K)
    (hcond :
      (PropertySkRing (Localization.Away f) 2 ∧
        ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, IsMinimalPrime p.asIdeal → f ∉ p.asIdeal →
          (4 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p.asIdeal)) ∨
      (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
        ({q : PrimeSpectrum A | p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal} ∩
          {q : PrimeSpectrum A | f ∈ q.asIdeal}) ≠
          {⟨maximalIdeal A, (maximalIdeal.isMaximal A).isPrime⟩} →
        (3 : WithBot ℕ∞) <
          (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
            (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
            (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) : WithBot ℕ∞) +
            ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p.asIdeal))) :
    PicardColimitSurjective A f
declarations.comment: the whole remark: under (1)-(5) the conclusion of 0F2D holds; points (a) and (b) are commentary with no mathematical claim

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.surjective_schemePullbackClass_puncturedClosedFibre_of_localCohomology
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F2F].**  Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and `f ∈ 𝔪`.  Assume
(1) the conditions of [Stacks, Tag 0F2D]: `A` is `f`-adically complete, `f` is a nonzerodivisor,
`H¹_𝔪(A/fA)` and `H²_𝔪(A/fA)` are finite `A`-modules and `H³_𝔪(A/fA) = 0`; and (2) for every
maximal ideal `𝔓` of `A_f` the punctured spectrum of `(A_f)_𝔓` has trivial Picard group.  Let `U`,
resp. `U₀`, be the punctured spectrum of `A`, resp. `A/fA`.  Then `Pic(U) → Pic(U₀)` is
surjective.

A class on `U₀` comes from a class on an open `U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U` by [Stacks, Tag 0F2D]
(`picardColimitSurjective`); the complement `U ∖ U'` is a finite set of points that are maximal
ideals of `A_f`, and the class extends across each of them by [Stacks, Tag 0F21]
(`surjective_schemePullbackClass_puncturedClosedFibre_of_isNoetherianRing`), hypothesis (2)
being read at those points by `subsingleton_picard_localizationAtPrime_of_away`.

`U₀` is `Stacks.Algebraization.puncturedClosedFibre A f`, the part of `Spec(A/fA)` over `U`,
which is the punctured spectrum of `A/fA`
(`Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.puncturedClosedFibre_eq_puncturedSpectrum_quotient`).
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_schemePullbackClass_puncturedClosedFibre_of_localCohomology
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal A)
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) A) (hreg : IsSMulRegular A f)
    (hH1 : Module.Finite A (Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, u} A
      {closedPoint A} ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f}))) 1))
    (hH2 : Module.Finite A (Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, u} A
      {closedPoint A} ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f}))) 2))
    (hvanish3 : IsZero (Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, u} A
      {closedPoint A} ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f}))) 3))
    (h2 : ∀ (P : Ideal (Localization.Away f)) [P.IsMaximal],
      Subsingleton (Stacks.Picard.ofScheme
        (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum (Localization.AtPrime P)).toScheme)) :
    Function.Surjective (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClass
      (morphismRestrict (Stacks.Algebraization.closedImmersion A f)
        (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A)))
declarations.comment: the full statement: for a Noetherian local ring (A, m) and f in m, under the four conditions of Stacks 0F2D (f-adic completeness, f a nonzerodivisor, finiteness of H^1_m(A/fA) and H^2_m(A/fA), vanishing of H^3_m(A/fA)) and triviality of Pic of the punctured spectrum of (A_f)_P for every maximal ideal P of A_f, restriction Pic(U) -> Pic(U_0) from the punctured spectrum U of A to the punctured spectrum U_0 of A/fA is surjective

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PicardBaseChange.injective_schemePullbackClass_puncturedSpectrumCompletionMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F2G.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring of depth at least two,
let `A^` be its completion and let `U`, resp. `U^`, be the punctured spectrum of `A`, resp. `A^`.
Then `Pic(U) ⟶ Pic(U^)` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_schemePullbackClass_puncturedSpectrumCompletionMap
    (hdepth : 2 ≤ Module.depth A (maximalIdeal A) A) :
    Function.Injective
      (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClass (puncturedSpectrumCompletionMap A))

declarations.name: Stacks.PicardUFD.subsingleton_picardGroup_puncturedSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F2H.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a regular local ring. Then the Picard group of
the punctured spectrum `Spec A ∖ {𝔪}` of `A` is trivial.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_picardGroup_puncturedSpectrum (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] :
    Subsingleton (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme.picardGroup

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.subsingleton_picardGroup_puncturedSpectrum_of_completeIntersection
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F2I]** (Grothendieck). Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring. If `A` is a
complete intersection of dimension at least four — its `𝔪`-adic completion is the quotient of a
regular local ring by an ideal generated by a regular sequence — then the Picard group of the
punctured spectrum `U = Spec A ∖ {𝔪}` of `A` is trivial.

The proof is the source's. The induction on the length of the regular sequence, through
[Stacks, Tag 0F2G], [Stacks, Tag 0F2H] and [Stacks, Tag 0F2F], is
`subsingleton_picardGroup_puncturedSpectrum_of_isCompleteIntersectionRing`, which takes the
conclusion of [Stacks, Tag 0F2D] as an input; that input is supplied here by the library's proof
of [Stacks, Tag 0F2D], `picardColimitSurjective`. Its conditions are discharged as in the
source: `f`-adic completeness follows from `𝔪`-adic completeness, the element is a
nonzerodivisor, and `depth(A') ≥ 5` gives `depth(A'/fA') ≥ 4`, so that `H^i_𝔪(A'/fA') = 0` for
`i < 4` (`isZero_localCohomology_quotient_of_five_le_depth`).
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_picardGroup_puncturedSpectrum_of_completeIntersection
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hA : LocalCompleteIntersection.IsCompleteIntersectionRing A)
    (hdim : 4 ≤ ringKrullDim A) :
    Subsingleton (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme.picardGroup
declarations.comment: proved in full: Stacks 0F2D is supplied by its proof picardColimitSurjective

    ¬ Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsTrivial
