        (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum (hypersurface k)).toScheme.presheaf
        (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum (hypersurface k)).toScheme.ringCatIsSheaf
        (Stacks.Divisors.negativeTwist' (cartierDivisor k))
declarations.comment: nontrivial line bundle

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.QuadricCone.picardGroup_not_subsingleton'
declarations.doc:
The Picard group `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.picardGroup` of the punctured spectrum
`U = Spec A ∖ {𝔪}` of `A = k⟦x,y,z,w⟧/(xy - zw)` is nontrivial.
declarations.comment: the conclusion: Pic(U) is nontrivial, at the same Scheme.picardGroup that Stacks 0F2I is stated at, so this is literally the negation of that proposition's conclusion for this A

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.QuadricCone.dimension_bound_isSharp
declarations.doc:
*The dimension bound in [Stacks, Tag 0F2I] is sharp.*  For every
field `k` the ring `A = k⟦x,y,z,w⟧/(xy - zw)` is a Noetherian local complete intersection of
dimension exactly three — so it satisfies every hypothesis of [Stacks, Tag 0F2I] except
`dim A ≥ 4` — and the Picard group of its punctured spectrum is nontrivial.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dimension_bound_isSharp (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    IsNoetherianRing (hypersurface k) ∧ IsLocalRing (hypersurface k) ∧
      LocalCompleteIntersection.IsCompleteIntersectionRing (hypersurface k) ∧
      ringKrullDim (hypersurface k) = 3 ∧
      ¬ Subsingleton
        (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum (hypersurface k)).toScheme.picardGroup

declarations.name: main_theorem0F2K
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F2K**.
In a quasi-compact space having a basis of quasi-compact opens closed under pairwise
intersections, a locally closed subset `T ⊆ X` that is quasi-compact and whose complement
`Tᶜ` is retrocompact in `X` is constructible in `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem0F2K
    [CompactSpace X]
    (B : Set (Set X))
    (hB : TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis B)
    (_hBcompact : ∀ U ∈ B, IsCompact U)
    (hBinter : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ V ∈ B, IsCompact (U ∩ V))
    (T : Set X)
    (hTlc : IsLocallyClosed T)
    (hTqc : IsCompact T)
    (hTcRetro : IsRetrocompact Tᶜ) :
    IsConstructibleStratified T

declarations.name: Stacks.ZariskiAndSeparation.ReducedInducedLocallyClosed.reducedInducedIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
The defining ideal sheaf of the reduced induced scheme structure on a locally
closed subset.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def reducedInducedIdealSheaf {X : Scheme.{u}} (T : Set X)
    (hT : IsLocallyClosed T) : (reducedInducedOpen T hT).toScheme.IdealSheafData
declarations.comment: reduced_induced_scheme_structure_on_a_locally_closed_subset

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyFinite_iff_parts_isLocallyConstructible
declarations.doc:
A partition of a scheme into retrocompact parts is locally finite if and only if all its
parts are locally constructible.
declarations.statement:
public lemma locallyFinite_iff_parts_isLocallyConstructible
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {P : Set (Set X)} (hP : IsTopologicalPartition P)
    (hP_retrocompact : ∀ S ∈ P, IsRetrocompact S) :
    LocallyFinite (fun S : P ↦ (S : Set X)) ↔
      ∀ S ∈ P, Topology.IsLocallyConstructible S

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteFactorization.exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinite_finitePresentation_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Zariski's Main Theorem with finite presentation (Stacks Project, Tag 0F2N).**  Let
`f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-finite separated morphism onto a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme,
and assume in addition that `f` is locally of finite presentation.  Then the factorization of
[Stacks, Tag 05K0] into a quasi-compact open immersion `j : X ⟶ T` followed by a finite
morphism `π : T ⟶ S` may be chosen with `π` of finite presentation as well.

Quasi-finiteness is Stacks 02NG, as for Tag 05K0: `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType` and `AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact` together.  Finite
presentation of `π` is `AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation`, part (3) of [Stacks, Tag 01TP];
for a finite, hence affine, morphism it is the same as being locally of finite presentation,
so this is the tag's "finite and of finite presentation over `S`".
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinite_finitePresentation_factorization
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] :
    ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (j : X ⟶ T) (π : T ⟶ S),
      IsOpenImmersion j ∧ QuasiCompact j ∧ IsFinite π ∧ FinitePresentation π ∧ f = j ≫ π

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineStratification
declarations.doc:
A locally finite stratification of `X` with affine reduced induced strata
and affine inclusions into `X`.
declarations.statement: structure AffineStratification (X : Scheme.{u}) (I : Type v) [PartialOrder I]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineStratification_fin
declarations.doc:
A finite affine stratification can be reindexed by the interval from zero
to the length of its indexing poset.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineStratification_fin {X : Scheme.{u}}
    {I : Type v} [PartialOrder I] [Finite I]
    (s : AffineStratification X I) (n : ℕ)
    (hn : (Order.krullDim I = n) ∨ (IsEmpty I ∧ n = 0)) :
    Nonempty (AffineStratification X (Fin (n + 1)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasFiniteAffineStratification_iff
declarations.doc:
A scheme has an affine stratification indexed by a finite poset if and only if it is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFiniteAffineStratification_iff (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    HasFiniteAffineStratification.{u, v} X ↔ (CompactSpace X ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineStratificationNumber
declarations.doc:
The least `n` admitting an affine stratification of `X` with strata
indexed by `0, …, n`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def affineStratificationNumber (X : Scheme.{u}) : ℕ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineStratificationNumber_le_of_isOpenCover
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F2W].** A separated scheme with an open covering by `n + 1` affine opens
has affine stratification number at most `n`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineStratificationNumber_le_of_topologicalKrullDim
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F2X].** A Noetherian scheme of finite dimension `d` has affine
stratification number at most `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineStratificationNumber_le_of_topologicalKrullDim (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (d : ℕ) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    affineStratificationNumber X ≤ d

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_affineStratification_of_topologicalKrullDim_le
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian scheme of dimension at most `d` has an affine stratification indexed by
`0, …, d`; that is, its affine stratification number is at most `d` in the sense of
[Stacks, Tag 0F2V].
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_affineStratification_of_topologicalKrullDim_le (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsNoetherian X] (d : ℕ) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    Nonempty (AffineStratification X (Fin (d + 1)))
declarations.comment: an affine stratification indexed by 0, …, d exists

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_cohomology_of_affineStratificationNumber
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F2Y].** Let `X` be a nonempty quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme with
affine stratification number `n`. Then `Hᵖ(X, F) = 0` for every `p > n` and every quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_cohomology_of_affineStratificationNumber (X : Scheme.{u}) [Nonempty X]
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (p : ℕ)
    (hp : affineStratificationNumber X < p) :
    IsZero (Hgroup X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ p F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineStratificationNumber_proj_le
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F2Z], the upper bound.** The affine stratification number of `ℙⁿ_k` is at
most `n`: projective space is separated and the `n + 1` standard coordinate charts are an affine
open covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineStratificationNumber_proj_le (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) :
    affineStratificationNumber (Proj (polyGrading k n)) ≤ n
declarations.comment: the upper bound

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.le_affineStratificationNumber_proj
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F2Z], the lower bound.** The affine stratification number of `ℙⁿ_k` is at
least `n`: `Hⁿ(ℙⁿ_k, 𝒪(-n-1))` is nonzero, while [Stacks, Tag 0F2Y] makes the cohomology of a
quasi-coherent module vanish above the affine stratification number.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_affineStratificationNumber_proj (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) :
    n ≤ affineStratificationNumber (Proj (polyGrading k n))
declarations.comment: the lower bound

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineStratificationNumber_proj
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F2Z].** The affine stratification number of `n`-dimensional projective space
over a field is exactly `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineStratificationNumber_proj (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) :
    affineStratificationNumber (Proj (polyGrading k n)) = n
declarations.comment: the equality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyOpen_iff_forall_isOpenMap_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is universally open if and only if its base change along every
morphism locally of finite presentation is an open map.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyOpen_iff_forall_isOpenMap_pullback_snd {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    UniversallyOpen f ↔
      ∀ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (g : S' ⟶ S),
        LocallyOfFinitePresentation g → IsOpenMap (pullback.snd f g)
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyOpen_iff_forall_isOpenMap_affineSpaceMap
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is universally open if and only if the induced morphism of affine
`n`-spaces is an open map for every `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyOpen_iff_forall_isOpenMap_affineSpaceMap {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    UniversallyOpen f ↔
      ∀ n : ℕ, IsOpenMap (AffineSpace.map (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) f)
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyOpen_of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_dominant_components
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F32.** A locally quasi-finite morphism to a geometrically unibranch,
locally Noetherian scheme is universally open as soon as every irreducible component of its
source dominates an irreducible component of its target.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyOpen_of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_dominant_components
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (hY : IsGeometricallyUnibranch Y)
    (hcomponents : ∀ C : irreducibleComponents X,
      ∃ D : irreducibleComponents Y, closure (f '' (C : Set X)) = (D : Set Y)) :
    UniversallyOpen f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyOpen_iff_isOpen_image_basicOpen_linearCombination
declarations.doc:
Universal openness of a finite algebra is detected by the image of the
principal open defined by a universal linear combination of module generators.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyOpen_iff_isOpen_image_basicOpen_linearCombination
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (d : ℕ) (b : Fin d → B) (hb : Submodule.span A (Set.range b) = ⊤) :
    UniversallyOpen (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B))) ↔
      IsOpen (PrimeSpectrum.comap (MvPolynomial.map (σ := Fin d) (algebraMap A B)) ''
        (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen
          (∑ i : Fin d, MvPolynomial.C (b i) * MvPolynomial.X i) :
            Set (PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin d) B))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_locallyQuasiFinite_universallyOpen_baseChange_of_limitBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be the limit of a cofiltered system of schemes with affine transition morphisms and
`f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀` a locally finitely presented morphism over a quasi-compact quasi-separated stage
`S i₀`, with `X₀`, `Y₀` quasi-compact and quasi-separated. If the base change of `f₀` to the limit
is locally of finite type, locally quasi-finite and universally open, then so is its base change
to some stage `S i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_locallyQuasiFinite_universallyOpen_baseChange_of_limitBaseChange
    {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I] [IsCofiltered I]
    (S : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (S.map g)]
    (c : Cone S) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (S.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [CompactSpace (S.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (S.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left]
    [UniversallyOpen ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ (i : I) (g : i ⟶ i₀),
      (LocallyOfFiniteType ((Over.pullback (S.map g)).map f₀).left ∧
        LocallyQuasiFinite ((Over.pullback (S.map g)).map f₀).left) ∧
          UniversallyOpen ((Over.pullback (S.map g)).map f₀).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_eq_numGeometricConnectedComponents
declarations.doc:
For a locally quasi-finite morphism, the functions counting geometrically irreducible and
geometrically connected components of its fibres agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_eq_numGeometricConnectedComponents
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyQuasiFinite f] :
    geometricIrreducibleComponentCount f =
      numGeometricConnectedComponents f
declarations.comment: agreement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_forall_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_le
declarations.doc:
The geometric fibre count of a locally quasi-finite morphism whose source is quasi-compact
is bounded by a natural number.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_forall_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_le {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [CompactSpace X] :
    ∃ d : ℕ, ∀ y : Y, geometricIrreducibleComponentCount f y ≤ (d : ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: boundedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isGreatest_range_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount
declarations.doc:
The geometric fibre count of a locally quasi-finite morphism whose source is quasi-compact
and whose target is nonempty attains a finite maximum: its set of values has a greatest element.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGreatest_range_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [CompactSpace X] [Nonempty Y] :
    ∃ d : ℕ, IsGreatest (Set.range (geometricIrreducibleComponentCount f)) (d : ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: maximum, the target is assumed nonempty

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_ge
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F36.** For a separated, locally quasi-finite and universally open
morphism of schemes, the locus where the number of geometric components of the fibre is at least
a fixed natural number is open.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_maxLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F37.** For a separated, locally quasi-finite and universally open
morphism whose geometric fibre count attains the finite maximum `d`, the locus where the count
equals `d` is open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_maxLocus
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [UniversallyOpen f] (d : ℕ)
    (hmax : IsGreatest (Set.range (geometricIrreducibleComponentCount f)) (d : ℕ∞)) :
    IsOpen {y : Y | geometricIrreducibleComponentCount f y = (d : ℕ∞)}
declarations.comment: openness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_restrict_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_maxLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F37.** The morphism is finite over the open locus where its geometric
fibre count attains the finite maximum.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_restrict_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_maxLocus
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [UniversallyOpen f] (d : ℕ)
    (hmax : IsGreatest (Set.range (geometricIrreducibleComponentCount f)) (d : ℕ∞)) :
    IsFinite (f ∣_ ⟨{y : Y | geometricIrreducibleComponentCount f y = (d : ℕ∞)},
      isOpen_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_maxLocus f d hmax⟩)
declarations.comment: finiteness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum_comp_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
Weighted fibre sums by separable residue degrees commute with cartesian
base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum_comp_of_isPullback
    {U U' V V' : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ V) (h : U' ⟶ U)
    (f' : U' ⟶ V') (g : V' ⟶ V) (sq : IsPullback h f' f g)
    [LocallyQuasiFinite f] (hfinite : ∀ v, (f ⁻¹' {v}).Finite) (w : U → ℤ) :
    separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum f w ∘ g =
      separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum f' (w ∘ h)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeighting
declarations.doc:
An integer-valued function `w` on `X` is a weighting of `f : X ⟶ Y` if its
separable-degree weighted fibre sum is locally constant on every finite open
piece of every étale base change of `f`.
declarations.statement: def IsWeighting {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (w : X → ℤ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeighting.comp_of_isPullback
declarations.doc: A weighting pulls back to a weighting along an arbitrary base change.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyOpen_of_positive_weighting
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3C.** A locally quasi-finite morphism carrying an everywhere
positive weighting is universally open.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyOpen_of_positive_weighting {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f]
    {w : X → ℤ} (hw : IsWeighting f w) (hpositive : ∀ x : X, 0 < w x) :
    UniversallyOpen f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flatQuasiFiniteWeight
declarations.doc:
The local-fibre length times the inseparable degree of the residue-field
extension at a point of a scheme morphism.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def flatQuasiFiniteWeight {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : X → ℤ
declarations.comment: the formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flatQuasiFiniteWeight_pos
declarations.doc: The canonical local-fibre weighting is strictly positive.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatQuasiFiniteWeight_pos {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [Flat f]
    (x : X) : 0 < flatQuasiFiniteWeight f x
declarations.comment: positivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flatQuasiFiniteWeight_isWeighting
declarations.doc: The canonical local-fibre function is a weighting.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatQuasiFiniteWeight_isWeighting {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [Flat f] :
    IsWeighting f (flatQuasiFiniteWeight f)
declarations.comment: weighting

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flatQuasiFiniteWeight_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Example 0GKI, final claim.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be flat, locally quasi-finite
and locally of finite presentation and let `f' : X' ⟶ Y'` be a base change of `f` along
`g : Y' ⟶ Y`, with `p : X' ⟶ X` the projection. Then the canonical weighting of `f'` is the
restriction along `p` of the canonical weighting of `f`.

The weight at a point is the length of the local ring of the scheme-theoretic fibre through it
times the inseparable degree of the residue field extension. The comparison morphism of fibres
`N` is flat, so Tag `02M1` splits the length upstairs as the length downstairs times the length
of the local ring of the fibre of `N`, and
`Stacks.Chow.length_fiberStalk_mul_finInsepDegree_of_isPullback` trades that last length against
the two inseparable degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatQuasiFiniteWeight_of_isPullback {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    {p : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback p f' f g)
    [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [Flat f] :
    flatQuasiFiniteWeight f' = flatQuasiFiniteWeight f ∘ p
declarations.comment: base-change invariance of the function of the formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_weighting_genericSeparableDegree
declarations.doc:
**The generic-separable-degree weighting.** For `f : X ⟶ Y` locally quasi-finite and locally of
finite type over a geometrically unibranch locally Noetherian scheme `Y`, there is a weighting
`w` of `f` whose value at `x` is, for all compatible strict henselizations `Rsh` of `𝒪_{Y,f(x)}`
and `Ssh` of `𝒪_{X,x}`, every minimal prime `p` of `Rsh` and every algebraic closure `Kbar` of
`κ(p)`, the number of `κ(p)`-algebra maps `κ(p) ⊗[Rsh] Ssh → Kbar`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_weighting_genericSeparableDegree
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    (hY : IsGeometricallyUnibranch Y) :
    ∃ w : X → ℕ,
      IsWeighting f (fun x ↦ (w x : ℤ)) ∧
      ∀ (x : X)
        (κY : Type u) [Field κY]
        [Algebra (maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x))).ResidueField κY]
        [IsSepClosure (maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x))).ResidueField κY]
        (Rsh : Type u) [CommRing Rsh] [IsLocalRing Rsh]
        [Algebra (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) Rsh]
        (_hRsh : Stacks.StrictHenselization.IsStrictHenselization
          (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) κY Rsh)
        (κX : Type u) [Field κX]
        [Algebra (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)).ResidueField κX]
        [IsSepClosure (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)).ResidueField κX]
        (Ssh : Type u) [CommRing Ssh] [IsLocalRing Ssh]
        [Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ssh] [Algebra Rsh Ssh]
        [Algebra (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) Ssh]
        [IsScalarTower (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) Rsh Ssh]
        (_hSsh : Stacks.StrictHenselization.IsStrictHenselization
          (X.presheaf.stalk x) κX Ssh)
        (_hcomp : (algebraMap (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) Ssh) =
          (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ssh).comp (f.stalkMap x).hom)
        (p : Ideal Rsh) [p.IsPrime] (_hp : p ∈ minimalPrimes Rsh)
        (Kbar : Type u) [Field Kbar]
        [Algebra p.ResidueField Kbar] [IsAlgClosure p.ResidueField Kbar],
        w x = Nat.card (AlgHom p.ResidueField
          (TensorProduct Rsh p.ResidueField Ssh) Kbar)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyConstructible_weighting_levelSet
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3G.** The level sets of a weighting of a locally quasi-finite
morphism are locally constructible in the source.

Quasi-finiteness being local, the hypothesis is `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite` together
with `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType`, which is Stacks 01TD's pointwise characterization
of a locally quasi-finite morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyConstructible_weighting_levelSet
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f]
    {w : X → ℤ} (hw : IsWeighting f w) (n : ℤ) :
    IsLocallyConstructible {x : X | w x = n}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyConstructible_separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum_levelSet
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3H.** Each level set of the weighted fibre sum of a weighting of a
locally quasi-finite morphism of finite presentation is locally constructible on the target.

The statement is local on the target, so one restricts to an affine open of it; the restricted
morphism is again locally quasi-finite of finite presentation and the restricted weight is again
a weighting, by [Stacks, Tag 0F3B], while the weighted fibre sum commutes with the restriction by
[Stacks, Tag 0F39].
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyConstructible_separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum_levelSet
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyQuasiFinite f] (hf : FinitePresentation f)
    (w : X → ℤ) (hw : IsWeighting f w) (n : ℤ) :
    Topology.IsLocallyConstructible
      {y : Y | separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum f w y = n}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeighting.upperSemicontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3I.** A positive weighting of a locally quasi-finite morphism is
upper semicontinuous on its source.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsWeighting.upperSemicontinuous
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite f] {w : X → ℤ}
    (hw : IsWeighting f w) (hpos : ∀ x, 0 < w x) :
    UpperSemicontinuous w

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerSemicontinuous_separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3J.** The weighted fibre sum of a positive weighting of a
separated, locally quasi-finite morphism with finite fibres is lower semicontinuous.
declarations.statement:
theorem lowerSemicontinuous_separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f]
    (hfinite : ∀ y, (f ⁻¹' {y}).Finite) (w : X → ℤ)
    (hw : IsWeighting f w) (hpos : ∀ x, 0 < w x) :
    LowerSemicontinuous (separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum f w)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isGreatest_range_separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3K.** The weighted fibre sum of a weighting of a locally quasi-finite
morphism with quasi-compact source attains its maximum: its set of values has a greatest
element.

The target is assumed nonempty, which the source does not say and without which the set of
values is empty and has no greatest element.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isGreatest_range_separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f]
    [CompactSpace X] [Nonempty Y] {w : X → ℤ} (hw : IsWeighting f w) :
    ∃ d : ℤ, IsGreatest (Set.range (separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum f w)) d
declarations.comment: the target is assumed nonempty

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_restrict_separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum_maxLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3L.** A separated locally quasi-finite morphism with finite fibres
and a positive weighting is finite over the open locus where its weighted fibre sum attains its
global maximum.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFinite_restrict_separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum_maxLocus
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [IsSeparated f]
    (hfinite : ∀ y : Y, (f ⁻¹' {y}).Finite)
    (w : X → ℤ) (hw : IsWeighting f w)
    (hpositive : ∀ x : X, 0 < w x)
    (d : ℤ)
    (hmax : IsGreatest (Set.range (separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum f w)) d) :
    ∃ U : Y.Opens,
      (U : Set Y) = {y | separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum f w y = d} ∧
        IsFinite (f ∣_ U)

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_finitePresentation_algebra_universal_for_idempotents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3M.** A finite, finitely presented algebra has a finitely
presented weakly universal base change equipped with an idempotent: every idempotent after an
arbitrary base change is the image of the universal one under some specialization.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.exists_finitePresentation_algebra_universal_for_idempotents
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Module.Finite A B] [Algebra.FinitePresentation A B] :
    ∃ (Auniv : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing Auniv) (_ : Algebra A Auniv)
      (_ : Algebra.FinitePresentation A Auniv)
      (euniv : B ⊗[A] Auniv),
      IsIdempotentElem euniv ∧
        ∀ (A' : Type w) [CommRing A'] [Algebra A A'] (e : B ⊗[A] A'),
          IsIdempotentElem e →
            ∃ f : Auniv →ₐ[A] A',
              Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A B) f euniv = e

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_universal_finite_open_subscheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3N.** A quasi-finite morphism of finite presentation between affine
schemes admits a base change of finite presentation carrying a universal finite open subscheme:
every open subscheme of a base change along a morphism of affine schemes that is finite over the
new base is the inverse image of this one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_universal_finite_open_subscheme
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y] (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyQuasiFinite f] (hfp : FinitePresentation f) :
    ∃ (Yuniv : Scheme.{u}) (g : Yuniv ⟶ Y)
      (Uuniv : (pullback f g).Opens),
      FinitePresentation g ∧
        IsFinite (Uuniv.ι ≫ pullback.snd f g) ∧
      ∀ (Y' : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y'] (g' : Y' ⟶ Y)
          (U' : (pullback f g').Opens),
          IsFinite (U'.ι ≫ pullback.snd f g') →
            ∃ (h : Y' ⟶ Yuniv) (hh : h ≫ g = g'),
              (pullback.lift (pullback.fst f g')
                (pullback.snd f g' ≫ h)
                (by rw [Category.assoc, hh]; exact pullback.condition)) ⁻¹ᵁ Uuniv = U'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_exists_weighting_baseChange
declarations.doc:
A weighting on the limit base change of a quasi-finite finitely presented
morphism of affine schemes comes from a weighting at every sufficiently late
stage of the directed inverse system.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_exists_weighting_baseChange
    {I : Type v} [Small.{u} I] [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [∀ i : I, IsAffine (D.obj (op i))]
    (i₀ : I) (X₀ : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X₀]
    (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ D.obj (op i₀))
    (hfp : FinitePresentation f₀)
    [LocallyQuasiFinite f₀]
    (w : (pullback f₀ (c.π.app (op i₀)) : Scheme.{u}) → ℤ)
    (hw : IsWeighting
      (pullback.snd f₀ (c.π.app (op i₀))) w) :
    ∀ᶠ i in Filter.atTop, ∀ hi : i₀ ≤ i,
      ∃ wᵢ : (pullback f₀ (D.map (homOfLE hi).op) : Scheme.{u}) → ℤ,
        IsWeighting
          (pullback.snd f₀ (D.map (homOfLE hi).op)) wᵢ ∧
        w = wᵢ ∘ pullback.lift
          (pullback.fst f₀ (c.π.app (op i₀)))
          (pullback.snd f₀ (c.π.app (op i₀)) ≫ c.π.app (op i))
          (by
            rw [Category.assoc, c.w (homOfLE hi).op]
            exact pullback.condition)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum_eq_max
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3R.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-finite morphism of finite
presentation between affine schemes and let `w` be an everywhere positive weighting of `f`.
If the weighted fibre sum of `w` attains a greatest value `d`, then the locus in `Y` where
that value is attained is an affine open subscheme of `Y`.

Quasi-finiteness is expressed, as in Tag 01TD, by `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType`
together with `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite`; the maximum value exists by Tag 0F3K, and
the locus is produced together with its openness rather than assumed open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffineOpen_separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum_eq_max
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y] (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f] (hfp : FinitePresentation f)
    (w : X → ℤ) (hw : IsWeighting f w) (hpositive : ∀ x, 0 < w x) (d : ℤ)
    (hd : IsGreatest (Set.range (separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum f w)) d) :
    ∃ U : Y.Opens,
      (U : Set Y) = {y | separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum f w y = d} ∧ IsAffineOpen U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineStratificationNumber_le_ncard_separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a surjective quasi-finite morphism of
schemes and let `w : X → ℤ_{>0}` be a positive weighting of `f`. If `X` is affine and `Y` is
separated, then the affine stratification number of `Y` is at most the number of distinct values
of the weighted fibre integral `∫_f w`.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineStratificationNumber_le_ncard_separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [Y.IsSeparated] (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Surjective f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f]
    (w : X → ℤ) (hw : IsWeighting f w) (hpositive : ∀ x, 0 < w x) :
    affineStratificationNumber Y ≤
      (Set.range (separableDegreeWeightedFiberSum f w)).ncard
declarations.comment: quasi-finite as LocallyOfFiniteType and LocallyQuasiFinite; bound as in source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_of_sup_eq_top_of_isClosedImmersion_mapDesc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3U.** Two separated open subschemes covering the source, whose
overlap is closed in their fibre product over the base, give a separated morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_sup_eq_top_of_isClosedImmersion_mapDesc
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (U V : X.Opens)
    (hcover : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    [IsSeparated (U.ι ≫ f)] [IsSeparated (V.ι ≫ f)]
    (hUV : IsClosedImmersion (pullback.mapDesc U.ι V.ι f)) :
    IsSeparated f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_disjoint_strictTransforms
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3V, part (1).** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme
and `U ⊆ X` an open. Let `Z₁ = V(ℐ₁)` and `Z₂ = V(ℐ₂)` be closed subschemes of finite
presentation which do not meet inside `U`. Then there is a centre of finite presentation disjoint
from `U` — so that the blowup of `X` in it is a `U`-admissible blowup — on which the strict
transforms of `Z₁` and `Z₂` are disjoint.

Quasi-compactness of `U` is not needed; see the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_disjoint_strictTransforms [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (U : X.Opens) (I₁ I₂ : X.IdealSheafData)
    (h₁ : FinitePresentation I₁.subschemeι) (h₂ : FinitePresentation I₂.subschemeι)
    (hdisj : Disjoint ((U : Set X) ∩ (I₁.support : Set X)) (I₂.support : Set X)) :
    ∃ I : X.IdealSheafData, Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U (blowUpToBase I) ∧
      Disjoint (U : Set X) (I.support : Set X) ∧
        Disjoint (Set.range (strictTransformToBlowUp I₁.subschemeι I).base)
          (Set.range (strictTransformToBlowUp I₂.subschemeι I).base)
declarations.comment: separate_strict_transforms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_disjoint_closures
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3V, part (2).** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme,
let `U ⊆ X` be a quasi-compact open and let `T₁, T₂ ⊆ U` be disjoint constructible closed subsets.
Then there is a `U`-admissible blowup `X' ⟶ X` in which the closures of `T₁` and `T₂` are
disjoint.

This is part (1) applied to closed subschemes of `X` cutting out `T₁` and `T₂` on `U`: the closure
of the preimage of `Tᵢ` is contained in the strict transform of the `i`-th subscheme, which is
closed because the subscheme is a closed subscheme of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_disjoint_closures [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) (T₁ T₂ : Set U.toScheme)
    (hT₁ : IsClosed T₁) (hT₂ : IsClosed T₂) (hc₁ : Topology.IsConstructible T₁)
    (hc₂ : Topology.IsConstructible T₂) (hdisj : Disjoint T₁ T₂) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (f : X' ⟶ X), Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U f ∧
      Disjoint (closure (f.base ⁻¹' (U.ι.base '' T₁)))
        (closure (f.base ⁻¹' (U.ι.base '' T₂)))
declarations.comment: separate_constructible_closures

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_strictTransform_isIso_near_closure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3W.** A proper morphism which is an isomorphism over an open
containing a subset `T` closed in a quasi-compact open `V` becomes, after a `V`-admissible
blowup, a morphism whose strict transform is an isomorphism over an open neighbourhood of the
closure of the inverse image of `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_strictTransform_isIso_near_closure
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y]
    (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsCompact (V : Set Y))
    (T : Set Y) (hTV : T ⊆ (V : Set Y))
    (hT : IsClosed (V.ι.base ⁻¹' T))
    (hiso : ∃ W : Y.Opens, W ≤ V ∧ T ⊆ (W : Set Y) ∧ IsIso (f ∣_ W)) :
    ∃ I : Y.IdealSheafData,
      FinitePresentation I.subschemeι ∧
      Disjoint (V : Set Y) (I.support : Set Y) ∧
      ∃ W : (blowUp I).Opens,
        closure ((blowUpToBase I).base ⁻¹' T) ⊆ (W : Set (blowUp I)) ∧
        IsIso (strictTransformToBlowUp f I ∣_ W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_common_isAdmissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3X.** Let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let
`u₁ : U ⟶ X₁` and `u₂ : U ⟶ X₂` be open immersions of schemes over `S`, with `U`, `X₁` and `X₂`
of finite type and separated over `S`. Then there is a commutative diagram of schemes over `S`
in which `Xᵢ' ⟶ Xᵢ` is a `U`-admissible blowup, `Xᵢ' ⟶ X` is an open immersion, and `X` is
separated and of finite type over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_common_isAdmissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion {S U X₁ X₂ : Scheme.{u}}
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (fU : U ⟶ S) (f₁ : X₁ ⟶ S) (f₂ : X₂ ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType fU] [QuasiCompact fU] [IsSeparated fU]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f₁] [QuasiCompact f₁] [IsSeparated f₁]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f₂] [QuasiCompact f₂] [IsSeparated f₂]
    (u₁ : U ⟶ X₁) (u₂ : U ⟶ X₂) [IsOpenImmersion u₁] [IsOpenImmersion u₂]
    (hu₁ : u₁ ≫ f₁ = fU) (hu₂ : u₂ ≫ f₂ = fU) :
    ∃ (X₁' X₂' X : Scheme.{u}) (b₁ : X₁' ⟶ X₁) (b₂ : X₂' ⟶ X₂)
      (j₁ : X₁' ⟶ X) (j₂ : X₂' ⟶ X)
      (v₁ : U ⟶ X₁') (v₂ : U ⟶ X₂') (v : U ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S),
      Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup u₁.opensRange b₁ ∧
        Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup u₂.opensRange b₂ ∧
          IsOpenImmersion j₁ ∧ IsOpenImmersion j₂ ∧
            LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ QuasiCompact f ∧ IsSeparated f ∧
              (v₁ ≫ b₁ = u₁) ∧ (v₂ ≫ b₂ = u₂) ∧
                (v₁ ≫ j₁ = v) ∧ (v₂ ≫ j₂ = v) ∧
                  (b₁ ≫ f₁ = j₁ ≫ f) ∧ (b₂ ≫ f₂ = j₂ ≫ f) ∧ (v ≫ f = fU)

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.exists_iso_image_strictTransform
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3Y.** For `f : V ⟶ X ×_S Y` quasi-compact with first projection landing
in an open `U ⊆ X`, a `U`-admissible blowup `b : X' ⟶ X` and a lift `g : V ⟶ X' ×_S Y` of `f`, the
scheme-theoretic image of `g` is the strict transform along `b` of that of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_image_strictTransform
    {X Y S V X' : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ S) (q : Y ⟶ S)
    (U : X.Opens) (b : X' ⟶ X)
    (f : V ⟶ pullback p q) [QuasiCompact f]
    (g : V ⟶ pullback (b ≫ p) q)
    (hfU : Set.range (f ≫ pullback.fst p q).base ⊆ (U : Set X))
    (hbgX : g ≫ pullback.fst (b ≫ p) q ≫ b = f ≫ pullback.fst p q)
    (hbgY : g ≫ pullback.snd (b ≫ p) q = f ≫ pullback.snd p q)
    (hb : IsAdmissibleBlowup U b) :
    ∃ I : X.IdealSheafData,
      ∃ e : X' ≅ blowUp I,
        e.hom ≫ blowUpToBase I = b ∧
        Disjoint (U : Set X) (I.support : Set X) ∧
        ∃ (j : strictTransform (f.imageι ≫ pullback.fst p q) I ⟶ pullback (b ≫ p) q)
          (a : g.image ≅ strictTransform (f.imageι ≫ pullback.fst p q) I),
          j ≫ pullback.fst (b ≫ p) q ≫ e.hom =
            strictTransformι (f.imageι ≫ pullback.fst p q) I ≫
              pullback.snd (f.imageι ≫ pullback.fst p q) (blowUpToBase I) ∧
          j ≫ pullback.snd (b ≫ p) q =
            strictTransformι (f.imageι ≫ pullback.fst p q) I ≫
              pullback.fst (f.imageι ≫ pullback.fst p q) (blowUpToBase I) ≫
                f.imageι ≫ pullback.snd p q ∧
          a.hom ≫ j = g.imageι

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_properExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F3Z.** After a `V`-admissible blowup `b : Y' ⟶ Y` of a
compactification `j` of a quasi-compact open subscheme `V` of `U`, the blowup contains an open
subscheme `V'` which maps properly to `U`, extending the inclusion of `V`, and whose copy of `V`
is exactly the inverse image of the interior of the compactification.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_properExtension
    {S U : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ S)
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f]
    (V : U.Opens) [QuasiCompact V.ι]
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (V.ι ≫ f))) :
    ∃ (Y' : Scheme.{u}) (b : Y' ⟶ j.space) (V' : Y'.Opens)
      (e : V.toScheme ⟶ V'.toScheme) (p : V'.toScheme ⟶ U),
      Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup j.immersion.opensRange b ∧
        IsOpenImmersion e ∧
        Set.range (e ≫ V'.ι).base =
          (b ⁻¹ᵁ j.immersion.opensRange : Y'.Opens) ∧
        e ≫ V'.ι ≫ b = j.immersion ∧
        IsProper p ∧
        e ≫ p = V.ι ∧ p ≫ f = V'.ι ≫ b ≫ j.toBase

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasCompactification_of_two_opens
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F40.** A separated finite-type scheme over a Noetherian base has a
compactification as soon as it is covered by two compactifiable open subschemes whose
intersection is dense.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCompactification_of_two_opens
    {S U : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ S)
    [IsNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f]
    (U₁ U₂ : U.Opens) (hcover : U₁ ⊔ U₂ = ⊤)
    (hdense : Dense ((U₁ ⊓ U₂ : U.Opens) : Set U))
    (h₁ : HasCompactification (U₁.ι ≫ f)) (h₂ : HasCompactification (U₂.ι ≫ f)) :
    HasCompactification f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_quasiCompact_compactificationOf_of_isQuasiAffine
declarations.doc:
**Nagata compactification for a quasi-affine source (Stacks Project, Tag 0F41).** A
separated morphism of finite type from a quasi-affine scheme to a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme admits a compactification: a quasi-compact open immersion into a scheme
proper over the base.

The source statement has no quasi-affineness hypothesis; this is the case of its proof in which
the source immerses into relative projective space directly, with no gluing along a covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quasiCompact_compactificationOf_of_isQuasiAffine
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [X.IsQuasiAffine] :
    ∃ j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f), QuasiCompact j.immersion
declarations.comment: the case of a quasi-affine source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasCompactification_of_compactSpace_quasiSeparatedSpace
declarations.doc:
**Nagata compactification (Stacks Project, Tag 0F41).** Let `S` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme and let `f : X ⟶ S` be a separated morphism of finite type. Then `X` has a
compactification over `S`: `f` factors as a quasi-compact open immersion of `X` into a scheme
proper over `S`.

[Stacks, Tag 01ZJ] factors `f` through a closed immersion into a separated morphism of finite
presentation, and compactifiability descends along a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCompactification_of_compactSpace_quasiSeparatedSpace {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [QuasiCompact f] : HasCompactification f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparatedFiniteType
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is separated and of finite type when it is separated, locally of
finite type and quasi-compact.
declarations.statement: abbrev isSeparatedFiniteType : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}
declarations.comment: the condition on the objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FTS
declarations.doc:
The category of schemes separated and of finite type over `S`: its objects are the
schemes over `S` whose structure morphism is separated and of finite type, and its
morphisms are the morphisms of schemes over `S` between them.
declarations.statement: abbrev FTS (S : Scheme.{u}) : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the category

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_elementaryDistinguishedSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F45.** A morphism of algebraic spaces `g : X ⟶ Y` over `S` is separated once an
elementary distinguished square `(U ⊆ X, f : V ⟶ X)` has `U ⟶ Y` and `V ⟶ Y` separated and
has the comparison maps `U ×_X V ⟶ U ×_Y V` and `V ×_X V ⟶ V ×_Y V` closed.

The second comparison map is **not** among the source's hypotheses: Lemma 81.14.1 asks only for
`U ×_X V ⟶ U ×_Y V` to be closed, and its proof asserts that
`(V ×_Y V) ×_{X ×_Y X, Δ} X = V`, which is false — that base change is `V ×_X V`. The source's
hypothesis list is insufficient, and the counterexample in this module's docstring shows the
extra hypothesis cannot be dropped. This statement is therefore the repaired one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSeparated_of_elementaryDistinguishedSquare
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X V Y : (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (g : X ⟶ Y) (U : Subfunctor X) (f : V ⟶ X)
    (hsq : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsElementaryDistinguishedSquare B S hS hX U f)
    (hU : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated B S hS (U.ι ≫ g))
    (hV : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hUV : IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.mapDesc U.ι f g))
    (hVV : IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.mapDesc f f g)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated B S hS g
declarations.comment: with the additional hypothesis that V ×_X V ⟶ V ×_Y V is closed; the source's hypothesis list is insufficient, see the counterexample in the module docstring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isSeparated_of_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F45 as published is false.** It is not true that a morphism `g : X ⟶ Y` of
algebraic spaces over `S` is separated as soon as an elementary distinguished square
`(U ⊆ X, f : V ⟶ X)` has `U ⟶ Y` and `V ⟶ Y` separated and `U ×_X V ⟶ U ×_Y V` closed. The
counterexample is
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.exists_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare_not_isSeparated`,
over the field `ℚ`. The statement with the further hypothesis that `V ×_X V ⟶ V ×_Y V` is closed
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_elementaryDistinguishedSquare`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isSeparated_of_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare :
    ¬ ∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
      {X V Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
      (_hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (g : X ⟶ Y) (U : Subfunctor X) (f : V ⟶ X),
      IsElementaryDistinguishedSquare B S hS hX U f →
      IsSeparated B S hS (U.ι ≫ g) → IsSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g) →
      IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.mapDesc U.ι f g) → IsSeparated B S hS g
declarations.comment: counterexample: the statement as published is false; the corrected statement, with V ×_X V ⟶ V ×_Y V also closed, is isSeparated_of_elementaryDistinguishedSquare

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_separating_strictTransforms_and_closures
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F46.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
algebraic space over `S` and let `U ⊆ X` be a quasi-compact open subspace.

1. If `Z₁, Z₂ ⊆ X` are closed subspaces of finite presentation with `Z₁ ∩ Z₂ ∩ U = ∅`, then
   there is a `U`-admissible blowup `b : X' ⟶ X` such that the strict transforms of `Z₁` and
   `Z₂` are disjoint.  The blowup is recorded with its centre `Y`, a finitely presented closed
   subspace of `X` disjoint from `U` in which `b` is the blowup, and the strict transforms are
   taken relative to the exceptional divisor `b⁻¹Y`.
2. If `T₁, T₂ ⊆ |U|` are disjoint constructible closed subsets, then there is a `U`-admissible
   blowup `b : X' ⟶ X` such that the closures of `T₁` and `T₂` in `|X'|` are disjoint, `Tᵢ`
   being read in `|X'|` through `b`, which is an isomorphism over `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_separating_strictTransforms_and_closures
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1) (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1) (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.toFunctor) :
    (∀ Z₁ Z₂ : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1,
      IsFinitePresentation B S hS Z₁.1.ι → IsFinitePresentation B S hS Z₂.1.ι →
        Disjoint (subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 U.1 ∩ subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 Z₁.1)
          (subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 Z₂.1) →
        ∃ (X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : X' ⟶ X) (Y : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1),
          IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U b ∧ IsFinitePresentation B S hS Y.1.ι ∧
            Disjoint (subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 U.1) (subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 Y.1) ∧
              IsBlowupAlong B S hS Y b ∧
                Disjoint (strictTransformPointSet (closedSubspaceSpaceι X Z₁) b
                    (preimageClosedSubspace b Y).1)
                  (strictTransformPointSet (closedSubspaceSpaceι X Z₂) b
                    (preimageClosedSubspace b Y).1)) ∧
      ∀ T₁ T₂ : Set (points B S hS U.1.toFunctor), IsClosed T₁ → IsClosed T₂ →
        Topology.IsConstructible T₁ → Topology.IsConstructible T₂ → Disjoint T₁ T₂ →
        ∃ (X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : X' ⟶ X), IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U b ∧
          Disjoint (closure (pointsMap B S hS _ b.hom ⁻¹' (pointsMap B S hS _ U.1.ι '' T₁)))
            (closure (pointsMap B S hS _ b.hom ⁻¹' (pointsMap B S hS _ U.1.ι '' T₂)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isBlowupAlong_isIso_strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp_over_closure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F47.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` with `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let `V ⊆ Y` be a quasi-compact open
subspace and let `T ⊆ |V|` be a closed subset such that `f|_{f⁻¹(V)} : f⁻¹(V) ⟶ V` is an
isomorphism over an open neighbourhood `W` of `T` in `V`.  Then there is a `V`-admissible blowup
`b : Y' ⟶ Y`, the blowup of `Y` in a closed subspace `Yc` of finite presentation whose points
avoid those of `V`, such that the strict transform `f' : X' ⟶ Y'` of `f` is an isomorphism over
an open neighbourhood `W'` of the closure of `T` in `|Y'|`.

An open subspace of `V` is an open subspace `W` of `Y` with `W ≤ V`, and `f|_{f⁻¹(V)}` is an
isomorphism over it exactly when `f` is, i.e. when `f⁻¹(W) ⟶ W` is an isomorphism.  The centre
`Yc` is recorded, since the strict transform is taken relative to it.  The closure of `T` in
`|Y'|` is the closure of the set of points of `Y'` mapping into the image of `T` in `|Y|`, as in
Stacks 0F46 (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_disjoint_closure`).  The source
also asks `X` to be quasi-compact and quasi-separated; this follows from properness of `f` over
the quasi-compact and quasi-separated `Y`, is not used, and is omitted.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isBlowupAlong_isIso_strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp_over_closure
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.1)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (V : OpenSubspaces B S hS Y.1) (hVqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS V.1.toFunctor)
    (T : Set (points B S hS V.1.toFunctor)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (W : OpenSubspaces B S hS Y.1) (hWV : W.1 ≤ V.1)
    (hTW : pointsMap B S hS _ V.1.ι '' T ⊆ subspacePointSet B S hS Y.1 W.1)
    (hWiso : IsIso (pullback.snd f.hom W.1.ι)) :
    ∃ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : Y' ⟶ Y) (Yc : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Y.1),
      IsFinitePresentation B S hS Yc.1.ι ∧
        Disjoint (subspacePointSet B S hS Y.1 V.1) (subspacePointSet B S hS Y.1 Yc.1) ∧
          IsBlowupAlong B S hS Yc b ∧
            ∃ W' : OpenSubspaces B S hS Y'.1,
              closure (pointsMap B S hS _ b.hom ⁻¹' (pointsMap B S hS _ V.1.ι '' T)) ⊆
                  subspacePointSet B S hS Y'.1 W'.1 ∧
                IsIso (pullback.snd
                  (strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp B S hS f b (Yc.1.preimage b.hom)).hom
                  W'.1.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_surjective_finite_flat_etaleLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F48.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of quasi-compact
and quasi-separated algebraic spaces over `S`, let `V ⊆ Y` be a quasi-compact open subspace with
inverse image `U = f⁻¹(V)`, let `A ⊆ U` and `Bc ⊆ V` be closed subspaces such that `f`
restricts to an isomorphism `e : A ≅ Bc`, and assume `f` is étale at every point of `A`.  Then
there is a `V`-admissible blowup `b : Y' ⟶ Y`, with centre `Yc`, such that the strict transform
`f' : X' ⟶ Y'` of `f` satisfies: for every geometric point `ā` of `X'` lying in the closure of
the inverse image of `|A|` in `|X'|` there is a quotient `φ : 𝒪_{X', ā} ⟶ 𝒪`, a surjection onto
a local ring, such that `φ ∘ (𝒪_{Y', f'(ā)} ⟶ 𝒪_{X', ā})` is finite and flat.

The ring `𝒪` is the étale local ring of the strict transform `E` of a quasi-compact open `X₁₀`
of a `U`-admissible blowup of `X`, at a geometric point over `ā`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isFlat_cover_closure`), chosen so that the
part of `X₁₀` over `Bc` lies over `A`.  As `A` is open in `f⁻¹(Bc)`, being the image of a section
of `f⁻¹(Bc) ⟶ Bc` near which that morphism is étale, `E ×_{Y'} Bc ⟶ Bc` is a monomorphism, and
`E ⟶ Y'` is étale at every point over the closure of `|Bc|`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtaleAt_of_mono_pullback_snd`), which contains `f'(ā)`.  So the map
`𝒪_{Y', f'(ā)} ⟶ 𝒪` is bijective
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_etaleLocalRingMap_of_isEtaleAt`) and `φ` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_surjective_finite_flat_etaleLocalRing
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1) (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1) (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y.1)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (V : OpenSubspaces B S hS Y.1) (hVqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS V.1.toFunctor)
    (A : ClosedSubspaces B S hS (V.1.preimage f.hom).toFunctor)
    (Bc : ClosedSubspaces B S hS V.1.toFunctor) (e : A.1.toFunctor ≅ Bc.1.toFunctor)
    (he : e.hom ≫ Bc.1.ι = A.1.ι ≫ V.1.fromPreimage f.hom)
    (het : ∀ a : points B S hS A.1.toFunctor,
      IsEtaleAt B S hS f.hom (pointsMap B S hS _ (A.1.ι ≫ (V.1.preimage f.hom).ι) a)) :
    ∃ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : Y' ⟶ Y) (Yc : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Y.1),
      IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS V b ∧ IsFinitePresentation B S hS Yc.1.ι ∧
        Disjoint (subspacePointSet B S hS Y.1 V.1) (subspacePointSet B S hS Y.1 Yc.1) ∧
          IsBlowupAlong B S hS Yc b ∧
            ∀ abar : GeometricPoint B S hS
                (strictTransformSpace B S hS f b (Yc.1.preimage b.hom)).1,
              abar.image ∈ closure (pointsMap B S hS _
                  (strictTransformSpaceι B S hS f b (Yc.1.preimage b.hom) ≫
                    strictTransformPullbackToSource B S hS f b).hom ⁻¹'
                  Set.range (pointsMap B S hS _ (A.1.ι ≫ (V.1.preimage f.hom).ι))) →
              ∃ (O : CommRingCat.{u + 1})
                (φ : etaleLocalRing B S hS
                  (strictTransformSpace B S hS f b (Yc.1.preimage b.hom)).1 abar →+* O),
                IsLocalRing O ∧ Function.Surjective φ ∧
                  (φ.comp (etaleLocalRingMap
                    (strictTransformSpace B S hS f b (Yc.1.preimage b.hom)).2
                    (strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp B S hS f b (Yc.1.preimage b.hom)).hom
                    abar)).Finite ∧
                  (φ.comp (etaleLocalRingMap
                    (strictTransformSpace B S hS f b (Yc.1.preimage b.hom)).2
                    (strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp B S hS f b (Yc.1.preimage b.hom)).hom
                    abar)).Flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_le_strictTransformInAmbient
declarations.doc:
**One inclusion of Stacks 0F49, with Stacks 085T and 0863 as explicit hypotheses.**  Let
`X ⟶ T` and `Y ⟶ T` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `U ⊆ X` be an open subspace,
let `v : V ⟶ X ×_T Y` be a morphism whose composite with the first projection factors through
`U`, and let `Z` be the scheme-theoretic image of `v`.  Let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowup of `X` in
a closed subspace `Zc` of finite presentation whose points are disjoint from those of `U` — that
is, a `U`-admissible blowup of Stacks 086B.  Then the scheme-theoretic image of the lift
`v' : V ⟶ X' ×_T Y` is **contained in** the strict transform of `Z` with respect to `b`.

Here `X' ×_T Y` is spelled `(X ×_T Y) ×_X X'`, the strict transform of Stacks 0862 is taken of
`Z` viewed as an algebraic space over `X`, and its image in the ambient space is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformInAmbient`.

Stacks 0F49 asserts that the two are equal.  This is the inclusion of the scheme-theoretic image
in the strict transform, and only that; it is not the tag's equality, and the clause string of
the attribute says which inclusion it is.  The reverse inclusion is the content the library
cannot reach; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_eq_strictTransformInAmbient`.

Two hypotheses stand for inputs the library does not have, and both are *upstream* of this
conclusion — each is the conclusion of a tag that is missing, and neither mentions the
scheme-theoretic image of the lift:

* `hfac` is the source's morphism `V ⟶ Z'`, which comes from Stacks 085T part (1): the blowup is
  an isomorphism away from its centre, and `V` lies over `U`, which is disjoint from the centre;
* `himm` is step (1) of the source's proof, that the strict transform is a closed subspace of
  `X' ×_X Z`, which is Stacks 0863 part (2).

Given those, the inclusion is the minimality of the scheme-theoretic image, Stacks 082X in the
form `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_le`: the strict transform is a
closed subspace through which the lift factors.  Quasi-compactness of `v` is not needed for this
half and so is not carried; the source uses it only in the reverse inclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_le_strictTransformInAmbient (p : X ⟶ T) (q : Y ⟶ T)
    (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1) (Zc : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (b : X' ⟶ X)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS Zc.1.ι)
    (hdisj : Disjoint (subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 U.1)
      (subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 Zc.1))
    (hbl : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Zc b)
    (v : V ⟶ AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS p q)
    (v' : V.1 ⟶ (strictTransformPullback B S hS (fiberProductFirst B S hS p q) b).1)
    (hvU : Subfunctor.range (v.hom ≫ (fiberProductFirst B S hS p q).hom) ≤ U.1)
    (hfac : IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U b →
      Subfunctor.range (v.hom ≫ (fiberProductFirst B S hS p q).hom) ≤ U.1 →
      Subfunctor.range v' ≤ strictTransformInAmbient B S hS p q b Zc
        (schemeTheoreticImage B S hS v.hom
          (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS p q).property))
    (himm : IsClosedSubspace B S hS (strictTransformInAmbient B S hS p q b Zc
      (schemeTheoreticImage B S hS v.hom
        (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS p q).property))) :
    schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS v' ≤
      strictTransformInAmbient B S hS p q b Zc
        (schemeTheoreticImage B S hS v.hom
          (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS p q).property)
declarations.comment: the inclusion of the scheme-theoretic image in the strict transform

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_eq_strictTransformInAmbient_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F49.**  Let
`X ⟶ T` and `Y ⟶ T` be
morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `U ⊆ X` be an open subspace, let `v : V ⟶ X ×_T Y` be
a *quasi-compact* morphism whose composite with the first projection factors through `U`, and let
`Z` be the scheme-theoretic image of `v`.  Let `b : X' ⟶ X` be a `U`-admissible blowup, that is,
the blowup of `X` in a closed subspace `Zc` of finite presentation whose points are disjoint from
those of `U`.  Then the scheme-theoretic image of the lift `v' : V ⟶ X' ×_T Y` **equals** the
strict transform of `Z` with respect to `b`.

This is the assertion of Stacks 0F49.  Both inclusions are proved:

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_le_strictTransformInAmbient_of_lift`
  is steps (1) and (2) of the source's proof — the strict transform is a closed subspace of
  `X' ×_T Y` through which the lift factors;
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformInAmbient_le_schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor` is steps
  (4) and (5) — `V` is scheme-theoretically dense in the part of `Z ×_X X'` lying over the
  complement of the centre, by part (3) of Stacks 082Z, and the strict transform is cut out by
  the ideal of sections supported on the exceptional divisor, which is the ideal-theoretic form
  of "there are no nonzero sections of `𝒪_{Z'}` supported on `E`".

Step (3) of the source's proof, the quasi-compactness of the lift, is supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompact_of_comp_fiberProductFirst_unconditional`, which needs
the properness of the admissible blowup, Stacks 085Z.  That is now *proved*, in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_of_isBlowupAlong_of_isFinitePresentation`, and carries no side
condition, so **nothing is assumed here beyond the source's own hypotheses**.  In particular the
density statement, part of the tag's own conclusion, is the theorem
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformInAmbient_le_schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor`, and neither
the existence of a proper blowup nor a surjective étale chart of `X` with the size conditions of
Stacks 085Q is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_eq_strictTransformInAmbient_unconditional
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)] (p : X ⟶ T) (q : Y ⟶ T)
    (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1) (Zc : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (b : X' ⟶ X)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS Zc.1.ι)
    (hdisj : Disjoint (subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 U.1)
      (subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 Zc.1))
    (hbl : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Zc b)
    (v : V ⟶ AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS p q)
    (hv : IsQuasiCompact B S hS v.hom)
    (v' : V.1 ⟶ (strictTransformPullback B S hS (fiberProductFirst B S hS p q) b).1)
    (hv' : v' ≫ pullback.fst (fiberProductFirst B S hS p q).hom b.hom = v.hom)
    (hvU : Subfunctor.range (v.hom ≫ (fiberProductFirst B S hS p q).hom) ≤ U.1) :
    schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS v' =
      strictTransformInAmbient B S hS p q b Zc
        (schemeTheoreticImage B S hS v.hom
          (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS p q).property)
declarations.comment: the equality of the scheme-theoretic image of the lift with the strict transform, at the source's hypotheses and with NO side condition and no part of the conclusion assumed. The properness of the admissible blowup, Stacks 085Z, is proved rather than assumed, by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_of_isBlowupAlong_of_isFinitePresentation, which itself carries no side condition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isProper_extension_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
Let `T` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, let `g : U ⟶ T` be
separated and of finite type, and let `f : V ⟶ U` be étale. Suppose `V` has a compactification
over `T`: a quasi-compact open immersion `j : V ⟶ Y` into an algebraic space `Y` with
`p : Y ⟶ T` proper and `j ≫ p = f ≫ g`. Then there are a `V`-admissible blowup `b : Y' ⟶ Y` and
an open subspace `V' ⊆ Y'` containing `V` — a morphism `e : V ⟶ V'` lying over `j` whose image
in `Y'` is the inverse image of `V` — such that `f` extends to a proper morphism `q : V' ⟶ U`
over `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isProper_extension_of_isEtale
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) {T U V Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (hTqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS T.1) (hTqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ T.1)
    (g : U.1 ⟶ T.1) (hgft : IsFiniteType B S hS g) (hgsep : IsSeparated B S hS g)
    (f : V.1 ⟶ U.1) (_hf : IsEtale B S hS f)
    (j : V.1 ⟶ Y.1) (p : Y.1 ⟶ T.1) (hj : IsOpenImmersion B S hS j)
    (hjqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS j) (hp : IsProper B S hS p) (hcomm : j ≫ p = f ≫ g) :
    ∃ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : Y' ⟶ Y),
      IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS
        ⟨Subfunctor.range j, isOpenSubspace_subfunctorRange B S hS V.2 hj⟩ b ∧
      ∃ (V' : OpenSubspaces B S hS Y'.1) (e : V.1 ⟶ V'.1.toFunctor) (q : V'.1.toFunctor ⟶ U.1),
        Subfunctor.range (e ≫ V'.1.ι) = (Subfunctor.range j).preimage b.hom ∧
          e ≫ V'.1.ι ≫ b.hom = j ∧ IsProper B S hS q ∧ e ≫ q = f ∧
            q ≫ g = V'.1.ι ≫ b.hom ≫ p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasCompactification_of_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare
declarations.doc:
**Compactifications glue across an elementary distinguished square** (Stacks 0F4B). Over a
quasi-compact, quasi-separated algebraic space `Y` of finite type over `Spec ℤ`, let `U` be
separated and of finite type over `Y` and `(U₂ ⊆ U, f : U₁ ⟶ U)` an elementary distinguished
square such that `U₁` and `U₂` have compactifications over `Y` and `U₁ ×_U U₂ ⟶ U` has dense
image. Then `U` has a compactification over `Y`.

The proof is the repaired one of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.NagataCompactification.EtaleSquareGluing`; the density of
`U₁ ×_U U₂` in `U` is not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCompactification_of_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) :
    Stmt0F4B (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) hZ
declarations.comment: proof corrected: the source's W₁ = U ⊔_{U₁} (X₁ ∖ (Z̄₁₂ ∪ T̄)) need not be separated; X₁ is modified by three more admissible blowups (0F46 twice, and a blowup in I + J^M from the Nullstellensatz on the closure of the off-diagonal of U₁ ×_U U₁), and W₁ is glued from the chart N = X₁ ∖ (closure (V₁ ∖ U₁) ∪ closure (∂ ∖ Q))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_etale_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F4C.** Let `U` be a dense open subspace of a Noetherian algebraic space `X`
over `S` with `U ≠ X`. There is an affine scheme `V` and an étale morphism `V ⟶ X` such that
the open subspace `W` whose points are those of `U` together with the image of `V` strictly
contains `U`, the pair `(U ⊆ W, V ⟶ W)` is an elementary distinguished square, and
`U ×_X V ⟶ U` has dense image.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_etale_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXnoeth : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X)
    (U : Subfunctor X) (hU : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsOpenSubspace B S hS U)
    (hUproper : U ≠ ⊤)
    (_hUdense : letI : TopologicalSpace (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.points B S hS X) :=
        AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointTopology B S hS X
      DenseRange (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap B S hS U.toFunctor U.ι)) :
    ∃ (V : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (W : Subfunctor X)
      (hW : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsOpenSubspace B S hS W)
      (hUW : U < W)
      (f : yoneda.obj V ⟶ W.toFunctor),
      IsAffine ((AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtale B S hS (f ≫ W.ι) ∧
      (Set.range (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor W.ι) =
        Set.range (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap B S hS U.toFunctor U.ι) ∪
          Set.range (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) (f ≫ W.ι))) ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsElementaryDistinguishedSquare B S hS hW.1
        (Subfunctor.range (Subfunctor.homOfLe hUW.le)) f ∧
      (letI : TopologicalSpace (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.points B S hS U.toFunctor) :=
        AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointTopology B S hS U.toFunctor
       DenseRange (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap B S hS (pullback U.ι (f ≫ W.ι))
         (pullback.fst U.ι (f ≫ W.ι))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasCompactification_of_isSeparated_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Nagata's compactification theorem for algebraic spaces.** Let `Y` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a separated morphism of finite
type. Then `X` has a compactification over `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCompactification_of_isSeparated_of_isFiniteType (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) : HasCompactification B S hS f

declarations.name: preservesFiniteLimits_sheafToPresheaf_comp_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F4E.** Let `(C, J)` be a site and `u : C ⥤ Type u` a functor whose category of
neighbourhoods `u.Elements` (pairs `(U, x)` with `x ∈ u(U)`) is cofiltered. Then the stalk functor
`Sh(C) ⥤ Set`, sending a sheaf `𝓕` to `colim_{(U, x) ∈ u.Elementsᵒᵖ} 𝓕(U)` (Stacks 04EH), is left
exact, i.e. it preserves finite limits. Exactly the Stacks hypotheses: `u` is an arbitrary functor
with cofiltered category of neighbourhoods, and no covering condition on `u` is required.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteLimits_sheafToPresheaf_comp_stalk
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (u : C ⥤ Type u) [IsCofiltered u.Elements] :
    Limits.PreservesFiniteLimits (sheafToPresheaf J (Type u) ⋙
      (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ (Type u)).obj (CategoryOfElements.π u).op ⋙ Limits.colim)
declarations.comment:
The stalk functor is written as `sheafToPresheaf` followed by the colimit over the
opposite of the category of neighbourhoods `u.Elements`; `u` is any functor with
`IsCofiltered u.Elements`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Stalk.presheafPushforward_stalk_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F4F**, packaged as the existence of the natural isomorphism
`(u_p F)_v ≅ F_{v ∘ u}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafPushforward_stalk_iso (u : C ⥤ D) (v : D ⥤ Type u) :
    Nonempty (u.op.lan ⋙ presheafStalk v ≅ presheafStalk (u ⋙ v))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isMorphismOfSites_of_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F4G.** Let `u : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor of sites. Let `{(q_i, v_i)}`
be a conservative family of points of `D`. If each functor `u_i = v_i ∘ u` defines a point
of `C`, then `u` defines a morphism of sites `f : D → C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMorphismOfSites_of_points
    (hP : P.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints)
    (Ψ : P.FullSubcategory → Point.{u} J)
    (hΨ : ∀ Φ : P.FullSubcategory, (Ψ Φ).fiber = u ⋙ Φ.obj.fiber) :
    u.IsMorphismOfSites J K

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.ringHom_dpow_of_finiteVariableStage
declarations.doc:
Compatibility with divided powers propagates from the coefficients and the adjoined variables
to a whole finite variable stage. The argument is that the graph of the homomorphism is a subring
of the product containing the images of the generators, and that finite variable stages of the
product are stable under its divided powers.

This supersedes the `private` `map_dpow_of_finiteVariableStage` of
`StacksFrontier/RingTheory/DividedPowers/TateResolution/SetVariableExtension/Construction.lean`,
generalized from an algebra homomorphism to a ring homomorphism commuting with the structure
maps.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringHom_dpow_of_finiteVariableStage
    {R : Type u} {P : Type v} {C : Type z} {D : Type*} {J : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [Ring P] [Ring C] [Ring D]
    [Algebra R P] [Algebra R C] [Algebra R D]
    (Pᵢ : ℕ → Submodule R P) [GradedAlgebra Pᵢ]
    (Cᵢ : ℕ → Submodule R C) [GradedAlgebra Cᵢ] [IsStrictlyGradedComm Cᵢ]
    (Dᵢ : ℕ → Submodule R D) [GradedAlgebra Dᵢ] [IsStrictlyGradedComm Dᵢ]
    (δ : DividedPowerStructure Cᵢ) (ε : DividedPowerStructure Dᵢ)
    (ι : P →ₐ[R] C) (T : J → C) (S : Finset J) (d : ℕ)
    (hgrade : ∀ (m : ℕ) (a : P), a ∈ Pᵢ m → ι a ∈ Cᵢ m)
    (hT : ∀ j : J, T j ∈ Cᵢ d)
    (hclosed : ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : P), ι a ∈ positiveEvenPart Cᵢ →
      δ.dpow n (ι a) ∈ Set.range ι)
    (f : C →+* D) (hf : ∀ (m : ℕ) (x : C), x ∈ Cᵢ m → f x ∈ Dᵢ m)
    (hfalg : ∀ r : R, f (algebraMap R C r) = algebraMap R D r)
    (hcoeff : ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : P), ι a ∈ positiveEvenPart Cᵢ →
      ε.dpow n (f (ι a)) = f (δ.dpow n (ι a)))
    (hgen : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : J), T j ∈ positiveEvenPart Cᵢ →
      ε.dpow n (f (T j)) = f (δ.dpow n (T j)))
    {x : C} (hx : x ∈ finiteVariableStage δ ι T S)
    (hp : x ∈ positiveEvenPart Cᵢ) (n : ℕ) :
    ε.dpow n (f x) = f (δ.dpow n x)
declarations.comment: divided powers on a finite stage

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.finiteVariableStages_directedColimit_addHom
declarations.doc:
The additive analogue of `finiteVariableStages_directedColimit`: if the finite variable stages
cover the extension, a family of additive maps out of them which agree wherever their arguments
agree extends uniquely to an additive map out of the whole extension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteVariableStages_directedColimit_addHom
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} {C : Type z} {D : Type w} {J : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [Ring A] [Ring C] [AddCommGroup D] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R C]
    (Cᵢ : ℕ → Submodule R C) [GradedAlgebra Cᵢ]
    [IsStrictlyGradedComm Cᵢ] (δ : DividedPowerStructure Cᵢ)
    (ι : A →ₐ[R] C) (T : J → C)
    (hfinite : ∀ x : C, ∃ S : Finset J, x ∈ finiteVariableStage δ ι T S)
    (f : (S : Finset J) → finiteVariableStage δ ι T S →+ D)
    (hcompat : ∀ (S U : Finset J)
      (x : finiteVariableStage δ ι T S)
      (y : finiteVariableStage δ ι T U),
      (x : C) = (y : C) → f S x = f U y) :
    ∃! g : C →+ D,
      ∀ (S : Finset J) (x : finiteVariableStage δ ι T S),
        g (x : C) = f S x
declarations.comment: directed colimit of finite stages, additively

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.exists_gradedDividedPowerColimit
declarations.doc:
The colimit of a directed system of strictly graded-commutative nonnegatively graded
algebras with divided powers on their positive even parts, indexed by an arbitrary nonempty
directed preorder.

The colimit is graded by the elements coming from a homogeneous element of some stage, carries
the unique divided power structure for which every stage map preserves divided powers, and has
both the algebra and the module universal property: the first produces maps of graded algebras
with divided powers, the second — which is what a colimit of differentials needs, a differential
being linear and not multiplicative — produces `R`-linear maps.  Every element of the colimit,
homogeneous or not, comes from a stage, and two stage elements with the same image in the
colimit already agree at a later stage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_gradedDividedPowerColimit
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {I : Type w}
    [Preorder I] [IsDirectedOrder I] [Nonempty I]
    (B : I → Type v) [stageRing : ∀ S, Ring (B S)] [stageAlgebra : ∀ S, Algebra R (B S)]
    (Bᵢ : (S : I) → ℕ → Submodule R (B S))
    [stageGraded : ∀ S, GradedAlgebra (Bᵢ S)]
    [stageComm : ∀ S, IsStrictlyGradedComm (Bᵢ S)]
    (γ : (S : I) → DividedPowerStructure (Bᵢ S))
    (transition : ∀ {S T : I}, S ≤ T → B S →ₐ[R] B T)
    (htransition_self : ∀ (S : I) (x : B S), transition (le_refl S) x = x)
    (htransition_comp : ∀ {S T U : I} (h : S ≤ T) (h' : T ≤ U) (x : B S),
      transition h' (transition h x) = transition (h.trans h') x)
    (htransition_grade : ∀ {S T : I} (h : S ≤ T) (m : ℕ) (x : B S),
      x ∈ Bᵢ S m → transition h x ∈ Bᵢ T m)
    (htransition_dpow : ∀ {S T : I} (h : S ≤ T) (n : ℕ) (x : B S),
      x ∈ positiveEvenPart (Bᵢ S) →
        transition h ((γ S).dpow n x) = (γ T).dpow n (transition h x)) :
    ∃ (C : Type (max v w)) (ringC : Ring C),
      letI : Ring C := ringC
      ∃ algebraC : Algebra R C,
        letI : Algebra R C := algebraC
        ∃ (Cᵢ : ℕ → Submodule R C) (gradedC : GradedAlgebra Cᵢ),
          letI : GradedAlgebra Cᵢ := gradedC
          ∃ strictC : IsStrictlyGradedComm Cᵢ,
            letI : IsStrictlyGradedComm Cᵢ := strictC
            ∃ (δ : DividedPowerStructure Cᵢ) (incl : (S : I) → B S →ₐ[R] C),
              (∀ {S T : I} (h : S ≤ T) (x : B S), incl T (transition h x) = incl S x) ∧
              (∀ (S : I) (m : ℕ) (x : B S), x ∈ Bᵢ S m → incl S x ∈ Cᵢ m) ∧
              (∀ (m : ℕ) (x : C), x ∈ Cᵢ m →
                ∃ (S : I) (y : B S), y ∈ Bᵢ S m ∧ incl S y = x) ∧
              (∀ x : C, ∃ (S : I) (y : B S), incl S y = x) ∧
              (∀ (S : I) (n : ℕ) (x : B S), x ∈ positiveEvenPart (Bᵢ S) →
                δ.dpow n (incl S x) = incl S ((γ S).dpow n x)) ∧
              (∀ (S T : I) (x : B S) (y : B T), incl S x = incl T y →
                ∃ U : I, ∃ (hS : S ≤ U) (hT : T ≤ U),
                  transition hS x = transition hT y) ∧
              (∀ {D : Type z} [Ring D] [Algebra R D] (Dᵢ : ℕ → Submodule R D)
                  [GradedAlgebra Dᵢ] [IsStrictlyGradedComm Dᵢ]
                  (ε : DividedPowerStructure Dᵢ) (g : (S : I) → B S →ₐ[R] D),
                  (∀ {S T : I} (h : S ≤ T) (x : B S), g T (transition h x) = g S x) →
                  (∀ (S : I) (m : ℕ) (x : B S), x ∈ Bᵢ S m → g S x ∈ Dᵢ m) →
                  (∀ (S : I) (n : ℕ) (x : B S), x ∈ positiveEvenPart (Bᵢ S) →
                    ε.dpow n (g S x) = g S ((γ S).dpow n x)) →
                  ∃! F : C →ₐ[R] D,
                    (∀ (S : I) (x : B S), F (incl S x) = g S x) ∧
                    (∀ (m : ℕ) (x : C), x ∈ Cᵢ m → F x ∈ Dᵢ m) ∧
                    (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : C), x ∈ positiveEvenPart Cᵢ →
                      ε.dpow n (F x) = F (δ.dpow n x))) ∧
              ∀ {M : Type y} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (g : (S : I) → B S →ₗ[R] M),
                  (∀ {S T : I} (h : S ≤ T) (x : B S), g T (transition h x) = g S x) →
                  ∃! F : C →ₗ[R] M, ∀ (S : I) (x : B S), F (incl S x) = g S x
declarations.comment: directed colimit of graded algebras with divided powers

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.exists_setVariableDividedPowerExtension
declarations.doc:
A set of positive-degree variables has a free strictly graded-commutative algebra with
divided powers over a graded divided-power algebra. Every element involves only finitely many
variables (including their divided powers). The universal property fixes the coefficient and
generator maps, and requires target maps to preserve grading and divided powers.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_setVariableDividedPowerExtension
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [CommRing R] [Ring A] [Algebra R A]
    (Aᵢ : ℕ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra Aᵢ]
    [IsStrictlyGradedComm Aᵢ] (γ : DividedPowerStructure Aᵢ)
    (J : Type w) (deg : J → ℕ) (hdeg : ∀ j, 0 < deg j) :
    ∃ (C : Type (max u v w)) (ringC : Ring C),
      letI : Ring C := ringC
      ∃ (algebraC : Algebra R C),
        letI : Algebra R C := algebraC
