          (etaleModuleLift B Λ (fShriekFunctor.{u, u} B h)).mapDerivedCategory).hom ≫
        Functor.whiskerLeft
          (etaleModuleLift B Λ (fShriekFunctor.{u, u} B g')).mapDerivedCategory
          (properBaseChangeMap B Λ g f' f h w₂ RF' αF' RF αF) ≫
        (Functor.associator
          (etaleModuleLift B Λ (fShriekFunctor.{u, u} B g')).mapDerivedCategory
          (etaleModuleLift B Λ (fShriekFunctor.{u, u} B g)).mapDerivedCategory RF).inv ≫
        Functor.whiskerRight
          (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIsoOfCompIso
            (etaleModuleLiftFShriekCompIso B Λ g' g (g' ≫ g) rfl)).hom RF

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.properBaseChangeMap_interchange
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F7E], for the maps of the four squares.** Consider a commutative diagram of a
big étale site
```
X'' --k'--> X' --k--> X
 |          |         |
 f''        f'        f
 v          v         v
Y'' --l'--> Y' --l--> Y
 |          |         |
 g''        g'        g
 v          v         v
Z'' --m'--> Z' --m--> Z
```
whose vertical arrows are proper and whose horizontal arrows are separated and locally
quasi-finite, label its squares `A B / C D`, and let `Λ` be a ring. With `γ_A, γ_B, γ_C, γ_D`
the maps of [Stacks, Tag 0F7B] for the squares
(`γ_A : l'_! ∘ Rf''_* ⟶ Rf'_* ∘ k'_!`, `γ_B : l_! ∘ Rf'_* ⟶ Rf_* ∘ k_!`,
`γ_C : m'_! ∘ Rg''_* ⟶ Rg'_* ∘ l'_!`, `γ_D : m_! ∘ Rg'_* ⟶ Rg_* ∘ l_!`), the two transformations
`m_! ∘ m'_! ∘ Rg''_* ∘ Rf''_* ⟶ Rg_* ∘ Rf_* ∘ k_! ∘ k'_!`
```
γ_B ∘ γ_D ∘ γ_A ∘ γ_C   and   γ_B ∘ γ_A ∘ γ_D ∘ γ_C
```
(composites of whiskerings, as in Categories, Section 003D) agree, here at every object `K` of
`D(X''_étale, Λ)`. The squares `A` and `D` meet in a single point, and the identity is the
naturality of `γ_D` with respect to `γ_A` (Categories, Lemma 003F). It holds for every choice of
the six right derived functors of the direct images.

    [LocallyOfFiniteType (B.inclusion.map m')]
    [IsSeparated (B.inclusion.map m)] [LocallyQuasiFinite (B.inclusion.map m)]

    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X'' Λ)]

        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF')
    (RF : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X Λ) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Y Λ))
    (αF : (etaleModuleLift B Λ (etalePushforward.{u, u + 1} B f)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF)
    (RG'' : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Y'' Λ) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Z'' Λ))

        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RG'')

      DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Z' Λ))

        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RG')

    [RF''.IsRightDerivedFunctor αF''
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X'' Λ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RF'.IsRightDerivedFunctor αF'
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X' Λ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RG''.IsRightDerivedFunctor αG''
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Y'' Λ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RG'.IsRightDerivedFunctor αG'
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Y' Λ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X'' Λ)) :
    (etaleModuleLift B Λ (fShriekFunctor.{u, u} B m)).mapDerivedCategory.map
        ((properBaseChangeMap B Λ l' g'' g' m' wC RG'' αG'' RG' αG').app (RF''.obj K)) ≫
      (etaleModuleLift B Λ (fShriekFunctor.{u, u} B m)).mapDerivedCategory.map
        (RG'.map ((properBaseChangeMap B Λ k' f'' f' l' wA RF'' αF'' RF' αF').app K)) ≫

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.properBaseChangeMap_rectangle_interchange
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F7E], for the maps of the rectangles.** In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.properBaseChangeMap_interchange`, consider moreover right derived
functors `R(g'' ∘ f'')_*`, `R(g' ∘ f')_*`, `R(g ∘ f)_*` of the direct images along the vertical
composites, and the maps of [Stacks, Tag 0F7B] for the four rectangles
```
γ_{A+B} : (l ∘ l')_! ∘ Rf''_* ⟶ Rf_* ∘ (k ∘ k')_!
γ_{C+D} : (m ∘ m')_! ∘ Rg''_* ⟶ Rg_* ∘ (l ∘ l')_!
γ_{A+C} : m'_! ∘ R(g'' ∘ f'')_* ⟶ R(g' ∘ f')_* ∘ k'_!
γ_{B+D} : m_! ∘ R(g' ∘ f')_* ⟶ R(g ∘ f)_* ∘ k_!
```
written, as the source does, through `R(g ∘ f)_* = Rg_* ∘ Rf_*` (the canonical comparisons of
[Stacks, Tag 05T2], isomorphisms by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isIso_compComparison_etalePushforwardMod`) and
`(l ∘ l')_! = l_! ∘ l'_!` (Stacks 0F50,
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.etaleModuleLiftFShriekCompIso`, on derived categories by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIsoOfCompIso`). Then the two transformations
`m_! ∘ m'_! ∘ Rg''_* ∘ Rf''_* ⟶ Rg_* ∘ Rf_* ∘ k_! ∘ k'_!`
```
γ_{B+D} ∘ γ_{A+C}   and   γ_{A+B} ∘ γ_{C+D}
```
agree, here at every object `K` of `D(X''_étale, Λ)`. By [Stacks, Tag 0F7C]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.properBaseChangeMap_rectangle_eq_comp`) and [Stacks, Tag 0F7D]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.properBaseChangeMap_horizontal_paste`) these are
`γ_B ∘ γ_D ∘ γ_A ∘ γ_C` and `γ_B ∘ γ_A ∘ γ_D ∘ γ_C`, which agree by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.properBaseChangeMap_interchange`. It holds for every choice of the
nine right derived functors.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.properBaseChangeMap_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F7F]: the base change maps of Tag 0F7B are compatible with change of base.**
Let `b : Y₁ ⟶ Y` be a morphism of a big étale site and `k ≫ f = f' ≫ l` a commutative square
```
X' --k--> X
|         |
f'        f
v         v
Y' --l--> Y
```
with `f`, `f'` proper and `k`, `l` separated and locally quasi-finite. Let its base change by `b`
be given by cartesian squares `X₁ = X ×_Y Y₁` (projections `a : X₁ ⟶ X`, `f₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁`),
`Y'₁ = Y' ×_Y Y₁` (projections `b' : Y'₁ ⟶ Y'`, `l₁ : Y'₁ ⟶ Y₁`), `X'₁ = X' ×_{Y'} Y'₁`
(projections `a' : X'₁ ⟶ X'`, `f'₁ : X'₁ ⟶ Y'₁`), and `k₁ : X'₁ ⟶ X₁` the induced morphism
(`k₁ ≫ a = a' ≫ k`, `k₁ ≫ f₁ = f'₁ ≫ l₁`); the base-changed square inherits the hypotheses.
For a ring `Λ`, right derived functors `Rf'_*`, `Rf_*`, `Rf'₁_*`, `Rf₁_*` of the direct images
(with their units), and `K` in `D(X'_étale, Λ)`, the diagram
```
b⁻¹ l_! Rf'_* K ⟶ l₁_! b'⁻¹ Rf'_* K ⟶ l₁_! Rf'₁_* a'⁻¹ K
      |                                        |
b⁻¹ Rf_* k_! K ⟶ Rf₁_* a⁻¹ k_! K  ⟶ Rf₁_* k₁_! a'⁻¹ K
```
in `D(Y₁_étale, Λ)` commutes, where the vertical maps are those of [Stacks, Tag 0F7B]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.properBaseChangeMap`), and the horizontal maps are the base change
maps of Étale Cohomology, Section 0EZQ (`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.etaleDerivedBaseChangeMap`)
and the isomorphisms of [Stacks, Tag 0F55]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.derivedFShriekBaseChangeIso`). The original square is not required
to be cartesian, and `Rf₁_*` may be any functor with a transformation from `f₁_*`.

theorem properBaseChangeMap_baseChange {X' X Y' Y X'₁ X₁ Y'₁ Y₁ : B.Scheme}
    (k : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (f : X ⟶ Y) (l : Y' ⟶ Y) (w : k ≫ f = f' ≫ l)
    (b : Y₁ ⟶ Y) (a : X₁ ⟶ X) (f₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (sqX : IsPullback a f₁ f b)
    (b' : Y'₁ ⟶ Y') (l₁ : Y'₁ ⟶ Y₁) (sqY : IsPullback b' l₁ l b)
    (a' : X'₁ ⟶ X') (f'₁ : X'₁ ⟶ Y'₁) (sqX' : IsPullback a' f'₁ f' b')
    (k₁ : X'₁ ⟶ X₁) (hk₁ : k₁ ≫ a = a' ≫ k) (w₁ : k₁ ≫ f₁ = f'₁ ≫ l₁)
    [IsProper (B.inclusion.map f')] [IsProper (B.inclusion.map f)]
    [IsSeparated (B.inclusion.map k)] [LocallyQuasiFinite (B.inclusion.map k)]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (B.inclusion.map k)]
    [IsSeparated (B.inclusion.map l)] [LocallyQuasiFinite (B.inclusion.map l)]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (B.inclusion.map l)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X' Λ)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X Λ)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Y' Λ)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Y Λ)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X'₁ Λ)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X₁ Λ)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Y'₁ Λ)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Y₁ Λ)]
    (RF' : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X' Λ) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Y' Λ))
    (αF' : (etaleModuleLift B Λ (etalePushforward.{u, u + 1} B f')).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF')
    (RF : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X Λ) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Y Λ))
    (αF : (etaleModuleLift B Λ (etalePushforward.{u, u + 1} B f)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF)
    (RF'₁ : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X'₁ Λ) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Y'₁ Λ))
    (αF'₁ : (etaleModuleLift B Λ (etalePushforward.{u, u + 1} B f'₁)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF'₁)
    (RF₁ : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X₁ Λ) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B Y₁ Λ))
    (αF₁ : (etaleModuleLift B Λ (etalePushforward.{u, u + 1} B f₁)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF₁)
    [RF'.IsRightDerivedFunctor αF'
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X' Λ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor αF
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X Λ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RF'₁.IsRightDerivedFunctor αF'₁
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X'₁ Λ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X' Λ)) :
    haveI := isProper_of_isPullback B a f₁ f b sqX
    haveI := isProper_of_isPullback B a' f'₁ f' b' sqX'
    haveI := isSeparated_of_isPullback B b' l₁ l b sqY
    haveI := locallyQuasiFinite_of_isPullback B b' l₁ l b sqY
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isPullback B b' l₁ l b sqY
    haveI := isSeparated_of_isPullback B a' k₁ k a
      (isPullback_baseChange_left B w sqX sqY sqX' hk₁ w₁)
    haveI := locallyQuasiFinite_of_isPullback B a' k₁ k a
      (isPullback_baseChange_left B w sqX sqY sqX' hk₁ w₁)
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isPullback B a' k₁ k a
      (isPullback_baseChange_left B w sqX sqY sqX' hk₁ w₁)
    (etaleModuleLift B Λ (abPullback.{u, u} B b)).mapDerivedCategory.map
        ((properBaseChangeMap B Λ k f' f l w RF' αF' RF αF).app K) ≫
      (etaleDerivedBaseChangeMap B Λ a f₁ f b sqX RF αF RF₁ αF₁).app
        ((etaleModuleLift B Λ (fShriekFunctor.{u, u} B k)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K) ≫
      RF₁.map ((derivedFShriekBaseChangeIso B Λ a' k₁ k a
        (isPullback_baseChange_left B w sqX sqY sqX' hk₁ w₁)).hom.app K) =
    (derivedFShriekBaseChangeIso B Λ b' l₁ l b sqY).hom.app (RF'.obj K) ≫
      (etaleModuleLift B Λ (fShriekFunctor.{u, u} B l₁)).mapDerivedCategory.map
        ((etaleDerivedBaseChangeMap B Λ a' f'₁ f' b' sqX' RF' αF' RF'₁ αF'₁).app K) ≫
      (properBaseChangeMap B Λ k₁ f'₁ f₁ l₁ w₁ RF'₁ αF'₁ RF₁ αF₁).app
        ((etaleModuleLift B Λ (abPullback.{u, u} B a')).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isIso_lowerShriekProperDirectImageMap_app
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F7G].** Consider a commutative diagram of schemes `f ≫ h = g` (that is,
`g = h ∘ f`, with `f : X ⟶ Y`, `h : Y ⟶ Z` and `g : X ⟶ Z`) with `f` and `g` locally
quasi-finite and `h` proper. Let `Λ` be a ring. Functorially in `K ∈ D(X_étale, Λ)` there is a
canonical map `g_! K ⟶ Rh_*(f_! K)` in `D(Z_étale, Λ)`, namely
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.lowerShriekProperDirectImageMap` (a natural transformation, for
any right derived functor `Rh_*` of the direct image). This map is an isomorphism if

* (a) `K` is bounded below and has torsion cohomology sheaves, or
* (b) `Λ` is a torsion ring.

Case (a) is `isIso_lowerShriekProperDirectImageMap_app_of_isGE`, case (b)
`isIso_lowerShriekProperDirectImageMap_of_natCast_eq_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_lowerShriekProperDirectImageMap_app
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} B X Λ))
    (hK : (∃ n : ℤ, K.IsGE n ∧ moduleTorsionCohomologyProperty.{u, u, w, u} B X Λ K) ∨
      ∃ m : ℕ, 0 < m ∧ (m : Λ) = 0) :
    IsIso ((lowerShriekProperDirectImageMap B Λ f h g w RH αH).app K)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriek_independent_of_compactification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F7I**, for `Rf_! : D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ) ⥤ D⁺_tors(Y_étale, Λ)` and an
arbitrary ring `Λ`. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite type separated morphism of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes. Then `X` has a compactification over `Y`, and the functors `Rf_!`
built from the compactifications are, up to canonical isomorphism, independent of the
compactification: the isomorphisms `derivedLowerShriekCompactificationIso f j k Λ` between them
compose, and along every morphism `g : j ⟶ k` of compactifications they are the isomorphism
built from the map of [Stacks, Tag 0F7G] and the composition of derived direct images.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedLowerShriek_independent_of_compactification :
    (∃ j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f), QuasiCompact j.immersion) ∧
      (∀ j k l : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f),
        derivedLowerShriekCompactificationIso f j k Λ ≪≫
            derivedLowerShriekCompactificationIso f k l Λ =
          derivedLowerShriekCompactificationIso f j l Λ) ∧
      ∀ {j k : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)} (g : j ⟶ k),
        derivedLowerShriekCompactificationIso f k j Λ = derivedLowerShriekHomIso Λ g
declarations.comment: bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology sheaves, arbitrary ring Λ

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekCompIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F7J.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be separated morphisms of
finite type of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, and let `Λ` be a ring. Then
`R(g ∘ f)_! ≅ Rg_! ∘ Rf_!` as functors on `D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ)`, where `Rf_!`, `Rg_!` and
`R(g ∘ f)_!` are computed through arbitrary compactifications `jf`, `jg` and `j`.

The isomorphism is that of the source: through a compactification `X ⟶ X̄` of `X` over `Ȳ`
(Nagata's theorem, [Stacks, Tag 0F41]) it is
`R(ḡ ∘ f̄)_* (j' ∘ j)_! ≅ Rḡ_* Rf̄_* j'_! j_! ≅ Rḡ_* i_! Rf'_* j_!`
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekCompOverIso`, which uses [Stacks, Tag 0F7B] for the
open immersion `i`), and it is transported to the given compactifications by
[Stacks, Tag 0F7I] (`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekCompactificationIso`), which is the
independence of the choices made. `Rf_!` carries `D⁺_tors` into `D⁺_tors` by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isTorsionPlus_derivedLowerShriek_obj`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedLowerShriekCompIso [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace Y]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] [CompactSpace Z] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Z] [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (jf : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (jg : CompactificationOf (Over.mk g))
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (f ≫ g))) :
    (isTorsionPlus.{u, 0} Λ X).ι ⋙ derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} (f ≫ g) j Λ ≅
      (isTorsionPlus.{u, 0} Λ X).ι ⋙ derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} f jf Λ ⋙
        derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} g jg Λ

and let `Λ` be a ring. Then `R(g ∘ f)_! ≅ Rg_! ∘ Rf_!` as functors on `D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ)`,
where `Rf_!`, `Rg_!` and `R(g ∘ f)_!` are computed through arbitrary compactifications `jf`, `jg`
and `j`.

Through a compactification `X ⟶ X̄` of `X` over `Ȳ` (Nagata's theorem, [Stacks, Tag 0F41]) the
isomorphism is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekCompOverIsoUniv`, which uses
[Stacks, Tag 0F7B] for the open immersion `Y ⟶ Ȳ`; it is transported to the given

(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekCompactificationIsoUniv`).
declarations.statement:
def derivedLowerShriekCompIsoUniv [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace Y]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] [CompactSpace Z] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Z] [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (jf : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (jg : CompactificationOf (Over.mk g))
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (f ≫ g))) :
    (isTorsionPlus.{u, w} Λ X).ι ⋙ derivedLowerShriek.{u, w} (f ≫ g) j Λ ≅
      (isTorsionPlus.{u, w} Λ X).ι ⋙ derivedLowerShriek.{u, w} f jf Λ ⋙

declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F7J**, on unbounded derived categories. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and
`g : Y ⟶ Z` be separated morphisms of finite type of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, and
let `Λ` be a torsion ring, in any universe. Then `R(g ∘ f)_! ≅ Rg_! ∘ Rf_!` as functors
`D(X_étale, Λ) ⥤ D(Z_étale, Λ)`, where `Rf_!`, `Rg_!` and `R(g ∘ f)_!` are computed through
arbitrary compactifications `jf`, `jg` and `j`.

The isomorphism is that of the source: through a compactification `X ⟶ X̄` of `X` over `Ȳ`
(Nagata's theorem, [Stacks, Tag 0F41]) it is
`R(ḡ ∘ f̄)_* (j' ∘ j)_! ≅ Rḡ_* Rf̄_* j'_! j_! ≅ Rḡ_* i_! Rf'_* j_!`
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekUnboundedCompOverIso`, which uses

compactifications by [Stacks, Tag 0F7I]
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekUnboundedCompactificationIsoUniv`). The case of

`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekCompIsoUniv`.

def derivedLowerShriekUnboundedCompIso [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace Y]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] [CompactSpace Z] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Z] [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]

      derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, w} f jf Λ ⋙ derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, w} g jg Λ

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekCompIso_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F7K.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y`, `g : Y ⟶ Z` and `h : Z ⟶ T` be separated
morphisms of finite type of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, and let `Λ` be a ring. Then
the two isomorphisms `R(h ∘ g ∘ f)_! ≅ Rh_! ∘ Rg_! ∘ Rf_!` on `D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ)` built from the
isomorphisms of [Stacks, Tag 0F7J] (`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekCompIso`) agree:
through `R(h ∘ g)_! ∘ Rf_!` and through `Rh_! ∘ R(g ∘ f)_!`. Each of `Rf_!`, `Rg_!`, `Rh_!`,
`R(g ∘ f)_!`, `R(h ∘ g)_!` and `R(h ∘ g ∘ f)_!` is computed through an arbitrary compactification.

The proof follows [Stacks, Tag 0F7K]: choosing a compactification `Ȳ` of `Y` over the
compactification `Z̄` of `Z` (and of `X` over `Ȳ`) the statement is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekCompIso_assoc_of_tower`, and the isomorphisms of
[Stacks, Tag 0F7J] do not depend on the compactifications
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekCompIso_hom_app_second` and its first and third slot
companions). The statement on the unbounded derived categories `D(X_étale, Λ)`, for a torsion
ring `Λ`, is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekUnboundedCompIso_assoc`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedLowerShriekCompIso_assoc (jf : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f))
    (jg : CompactificationOf (Over.mk g)) (jh : CompactificationOf (Over.mk h))
    (jfg : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (f ≫ g))) (jgh : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (g ≫ h)))
    (jfgh : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (f ≫ g ≫ h)))
    (K : (isTorsionPlus.{u, 0} Λ X).FullSubcategory) :
    (derivedLowerShriekCompIso Λ f (g ≫ h) jf jgh jfgh).hom.app K ≫
        (derivedLowerShriekCompIso Λ g h jg jh jgh).hom.app
          ⟨(derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} f jf Λ).obj K.obj,
            isTorsionPlus_derivedLowerShriek_obj Λ f jf K.obj K.property⟩ =
      (derivedLowerShriekCompIso Λ (f ≫ g) h jfg jh jfgh).hom.app K ≫
        (derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} h jh Λ).map
          ((derivedLowerShriekCompIso Λ f g jf jg jfg).hom.app K)
declarations.comment: D⁺_tors(X_et, Λ)

`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekCompIso_assoc`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedLowerShriekUnboundedCompIso_assoc (jf : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f))
    (jg : CompactificationOf (Over.mk g)) (jh : CompactificationOf (Over.mk h))
    (jfg : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (f ≫ g))) (jgh : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (g ≫ h)))
    (jfgh : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (f ≫ g ≫ h)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X)) :
    (derivedLowerShriekUnboundedCompIso Λ hΛ f (g ≫ h) jf jgh jfgh).hom.app K ≫
        (derivedLowerShriekUnboundedCompIso Λ hΛ g h jg jh jgh).hom.app
          ((derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, 0} f jf Λ).obj K) =
      (derivedLowerShriekUnboundedCompIso Λ hΛ (f ≫ g) h jfg jh jfgh).hom.app K ≫
        (derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, 0} h jh Λ).map
          ((derivedLowerShriekUnboundedCompIso Λ hΛ f g jf jg jfg).hom.app K)
declarations.comment: unbounded D(X_et, Λ), Λ torsion

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F7L.** For a cartesian square of schemes `f' ≫ g = g' ≫ f` and a
compactification `j` of `X` over `Y`, the canonical isomorphism `g⁻¹ ∘ Rf_! ≅ Rf'_! ∘ (g')⁻¹` of
functors on `D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ)`, the bounded below complexes with torsion cohomology sheaves,
`Rf'_!` being computed with the base change of `j`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.CompactificationOf.baseChange`). Its components are
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekBaseChange`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedLowerShriekBaseChangeIso :
    (isTorsionPlus.{u, 0} Λ X).ι ⋙ derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} f j Λ ⋙
        etaleModuleDerivedInverseImagePlus.{u, 0} Λ g ≅
      (isTorsionPlus.{u, 0} Λ X).ι ⋙ etaleModuleDerivedInverseImagePlus.{u, 0} Λ g' ⋙
        derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} f' (j.baseChange sq) Λ
declarations.comment: the isomorphism g⁻¹ ∘ Rf_! ≅ Rf'_! ∘ (g')⁻¹ on D⁺_tors

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekBaseChange_compIso
declarations.doc:
For cartesian squares of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes
```
X' --hX--> X
|f'        |f
Y' --hY--> Y
|g'        |g
Z' --h-->  Z
```
with `f` and `g` separated of finite type, the base change isomorphisms
`h⁻¹ ∘ R(g ∘ f)_! ≅ R(g' ∘ f')_! ∘ hX⁻¹`, `h⁻¹ ∘ Rg_! ≅ Rg'_! ∘ hY⁻¹` and
`hY⁻¹ ∘ Rf_! ≅ Rf'_! ∘ hX⁻¹` (`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekBaseChange`) are
compatible with the isomorphisms `R(g ∘ f)_! ≅ Rg_! ∘ Rf_!`
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekCompIso`) on `D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ)`, for arbitrary
compactifications.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedLowerShriekBaseChange_compIso (sqg : IsPullback hY g' g h)
    (sqf : IsPullback hX f' f hY) (jf : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f))
    (jg : CompactificationOf (Over.mk g)) (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (f ≫ g)))
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X)) (hK : isTorsionPlus.{u, 0} Λ X K) :
    haveI : IsSeparated f' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sqf inferInstance
    haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType f' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sqf inferInstance
    haveI : IsSeparated g' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sqg inferInstance
    haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType g' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sqg inferInstance
    (etaleModuleDerivedInverseImagePlus.{u, 0} Λ h).map
        ((derivedLowerShriekCompIso Λ f g jf jg j).hom.app ⟨K, hK⟩) ≫
      (derivedLowerShriekBaseChange.{u, 0} Λ sqg jg).app
        ((derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} f jf Λ).obj K) ≫
      (derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} g' (jg.baseChange sqg) Λ).map
        ((derivedLowerShriekBaseChange.{u, 0} Λ sqf jf).app K) =
    (derivedLowerShriekBaseChange.{u, 0} Λ (sqf.paste_vert sqg) j).app K ≫
      (derivedLowerShriekCompIso Λ f' g' (jf.baseChange sqf) (jg.baseChange sqg)
        (j.baseChange (sqf.paste_vert sqg))).hom.app
          ⟨(etaleModuleDerivedInverseImagePlus.{u, 0} Λ hX).obj K,
            isTorsionPlus_etaleModuleDerivedInverseImagePlus_obj Λ hX K hK⟩
declarations.comment: compatibility with the isomorphisms of Lemma 0F7J, on D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekUnboundedBaseChange_compIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F7L, the compatibility with Tag 0F7J, on `D(X_étale, Λ)`.** For
cartesian squares of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes
```
X' --hX--> X
|f'        |f
Y' --hY--> Y
|g'        |g
Z' --h-->  Z
```
with `f` and `g` separated of finite type and a torsion ring `Λ`, the base change isomorphisms
`h⁻¹ ∘ R(g ∘ f)_! ≅ R(g' ∘ f')_! ∘ hX⁻¹`, `h⁻¹ ∘ Rg_! ≅ Rg'_! ∘ hY⁻¹` and
`hY⁻¹ ∘ Rf_! ≅ Rf'_! ∘ hX⁻¹` of `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekUnboundedBaseChangeIso`
(whose components are `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekUnboundedBaseChange`) are
compatible with the isomorphisms `R(g ∘ f)_! ≅ Rg_! ∘ Rf_!` and `R(g' ∘ f')_! ≅ Rg'_! ∘ Rf'_!` of
[Stacks, Tag 0F7J] (`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekUnboundedCompIso`) on the unbounded
derived category `D(X_étale, Λ)`, for arbitrary compactifications `jf`, `jg`, `j` of `f`, `g`,
`g ∘ f`, the primed functors being computed through their base changes. The case of
`D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ)` for an arbitrary ring is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekBaseChange_compIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedLowerShriekUnboundedBaseChange_compIso (sqg : IsPullback hY g' g h)
    (sqf : IsPullback hX f' f hY) (jf : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f))
    (jg : CompactificationOf (Over.mk g)) (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (f ≫ g)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X)) :
    haveI : IsSeparated f' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sqf inferInstance
    haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType f' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sqf inferInstance
    haveI : IsSeparated g' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sqg inferInstance
    haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType g' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sqg inferInstance
    (etaleModuleDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} Λ h).map
        ((derivedLowerShriekUnboundedCompIso Λ hΛ f g jf jg j).hom.app K) ≫
      (derivedLowerShriekUnboundedBaseChange.{u, 0} Λ sqg jg).app
        ((derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, 0} f jf Λ).obj K) ≫
      (derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, 0} g' (jg.baseChange sqg) Λ).map
        ((derivedLowerShriekUnboundedBaseChange.{u, 0} Λ sqf jf).app K) =
    (derivedLowerShriekUnboundedBaseChange.{u, 0} Λ (sqf.paste_vert sqg) j).app K ≫
      (derivedLowerShriekUnboundedCompIso Λ hΛ f' g' (jf.baseChange sqf) (jg.baseChange sqg)
        (j.baseChange (sqf.paste_vert sqg))).hom.app
          ((etaleModuleDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} Λ hX).obj K)
declarations.comment: compatibility with the isomorphisms of 0F7J, on unbounded D(X_étale, Λ), Λ torsion

registrations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekUnboundedBaseChangeIso
registrations.comment: the isomorphism g⁻¹ ∘ Rf_! ≅ Rf'_! ∘ (g')⁻¹ on unbounded D(X_étale, Λ), Λ a torsion ring

declarations.name: hasProjectiveDimensionLE_one_and_split_of_fittingIdeal_eq_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F7M.** Let `M` be a finitely presented module. If its `k`th Fitting ideal is
generated by a nonzerodivisor `f` and its `(k - 1)`st Fitting ideal vanishes, then `M` and its
`f`-power torsion submodule have projective dimension at most one, the quotient is finite locally
free of rank `k`, and `M` is the direct sum of the quotient and the torsion submodule.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasProjectiveDimensionLE_one_and_split_of_fittingIdeal_eq_span_singleton
    {R : Type uR} {M : Type uU} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.FinitePresentation R M] (k : ℕ) (f : R) (hf : IsRegular f)
    (hk : fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (k : ℤ) = Ideal.span {f})
    (hkm1 : fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) ((k : ℤ) - 1) = ⊥) :
    let T := LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lsmul R M f)
    let Q := M ⧸ T
    HasProjectiveDimensionLE (ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{uR} M)) 1 ∧
      T = Submodule.torsion' R M (Submonoid.powers f) ∧
      HasProjectiveDimensionLE (ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{uR} T)) 1 ∧
      (∃ hfin : Module.Finite R Q,
        letI := hfin
        ∃ hproj : Module.Projective R Q,
          letI := hproj
          Module.rankAtStalk (R := R) Q = fun _ => k) ∧
      Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] Q × T)

declarations.name: Stacks.Decalage.Cohomology.bijective_etaCohomologyTorsionMap
declarations.doc:
**The canonical isomorphism of Tag 0F7P.** For a complex `M^•` of `f`-torsion free
`A`-modules, the map `H^{j+1}(M^•) / H^{j+1}(M^•)[f] → H^{j+1}(η_f M^•)` (with
`H^{j+1}(M^•)[f] = ker (ξ ↦ f • ξ)` the `f`-torsion) sending the class of a
cocycle `z` to the class of `f^{j+1} z` is bijective, i.e. an isomorphism of `A`-modules.  The
source's index `i` is `j + 1` here, and every `i ∈ ℤ` arises.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_etaCohomologyTorsionMap (j : ℤ) :
    Function.Bijective (etaCohomologyTorsionMap C j) ∧
      ∀ z : Zc C j,
        etaCohomologyTorsionMap C j (Submodule.Quotient.mk (Submodule.Quotient.mk z)) =
          Submodule.Quotient.mk (⟨fpowZ C j z, fpowZ_mem_Zeta C j z⟩ : Zeta C j)
declarations.comment: the map H^i(M)/H^i(M)[f] → H^i(η_f M), [z] ↦ [f^i z], is bijective, for every complex of f-torsion free modules; i = j + 1, and f need not be a nonzerodivisor on A

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.QuasiIsoPreservation.quasiIso_etaPow_of_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F7Q.** The Berthelot--Ogus décalage of a quasi-isomorphism of
complexes of `f`-torsion-free modules is a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_etaPow_of_quasiIso
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {f : A} (_hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)
    (E : EtaFunctor.{u, v} f)
    {M N : CochainComplex (FTorsionFreeModule.{u, v} f) ℤ} (g : M ⟶ N)
    (hg : QuasiIso ((underlyingComplex f).map g)) :
    QuasiIso ((underlyingComplex f).map (E.functor.map g))

The décalage `EtaComplex.etaMap f φ` of a quasi-isomorphism `φ` between complexes of

theorem quasiIso_etaMap (f : A) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.DerivedDescent.exists_additive_derived_eta
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F7R.** For a nonzerodivisor `f`, the Berthelot--Ogus décalage
descends to an additive endofunctor of the derived category. On every complex
of `f`-torsion-free modules it is naturally isomorphic, on objects and
morphisms, to the chain-level décalage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_additive_derived_eta
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)]
    (f : A) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) :
    ∃ (Leta : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)),
      Leta.Additive ∧
        ∃ E : EtaFunctor.{u, v} f,
          Nonempty (underlyingComplex f ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ Leta ≅
            E.functor ⋙ underlyingComplex f ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.Reduction.exists_boundary_subcomplex_of_etaQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F7S.** Modulo a nonzerodivisor `f`, the eta complex has an acyclic
subcomplex with degree-`i` term `B^(i+1) ⊕ B^i`, and the quotient complex has the
cohomology modules of `M/fM` as its terms, with the induced differential transported
along the equivalences `e`. The final three clauses give the
representative formulas for the maps `t`, `s`, and `s'` from the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundary_subcomplex_of_etaQuotient
    (f : A) (_hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)
    (C : EtaComplex.Complex.{u, v} A) (hC : EtaComplex.IsTorsionFree f C) :
    let barTerm : ℤ → Type (max u v) := fun i =>
      (C.X i) ⧸ LinearMap.range (EtaComplex.scalarMap f (C.X i))
    ∃ barD : ∀ i j, barTerm i →ₗ[A] barTerm j,
      (∀ i (x : C.X i),
        barD i (i + 1) (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) =
          Submodule.Quotient.mk ((C.d i (i + 1)).hom x)) ∧
      (∀ i j, i + 1 ≠ j → barD i j = 0) ∧
      (∀ i (x : barTerm i), barD (i + 1) (i + 1 + 1) (barD i (i + 1) x) = 0) ∧
      let B : ∀ i, Submodule A (barTerm i) := fun i =>
        LinearMap.range (barD (i - 1) i)
      let Z : ∀ i, Submodule A (barTerm i) := fun i => LinearMap.ker (barD i (i + 1))
      let H : ℤ → Type (max u v) := fun i =>
        (Z i) ⧸ (B i).comap (Z i).subtype
      let Q : ℤ → Type (max u v) := fun i => EtaComplex.QuotientTerm f C i
      ∃ (hBZ : ∀ i, B i ≤ Z i)
        (s : ∀ i, B (i + 1) →ₗ[A] Q i)
        (s' : ∀ i, B i →ₗ[A] Q i)
        (t : ∀ i, Q i →ₗ[A] Z i)
        (e : ∀ i,
          (Q i ⧸ LinearMap.range (LinearMap.coprod (s i) (s' i))) ≃ₗ[A] H i),
        (∀ i, Function.Injective (LinearMap.coprod (s i) (s' i))) ∧
        (∀ i, Function.Injective (s i)) ∧
        (∀ i, Function.Surjective (t i)) ∧
        (∀ i, Function.Exact (s i) (t i)) ∧
        (∀ i (bNext : B (i + 1)) (b : B i),
          t i (s i bNext + s' i b) = ⟨b, hBZ i b.2⟩) ∧
        (∀ i (bNext : B (i + 1)) (b : B i),
          EtaComplex.quotientDifferential f C i (s i bNext + s' i b) =
            s' (i + 1) bNext) ∧
        (∀ i, Function.Exact
          (fun p : B i × B (i - 1) => ((0 : B (i + 1)), p.1))
          (fun p : B (i + 1) × B i => ((0 : B (i + 1 + 1)), p.1))) ∧
        (∀ i (q : Q i),
          e i (Submodule.Quotient.mk q) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (t i q)) ∧
        (∃ dH : ∀ i, H i →ₗ[A] H (i + 1),
          (∀ i (q : Q i),
            e (i + 1) (Submodule.Quotient.mk
              (EtaComplex.quotientDifferential f C i q)) =
                dH i (e i (Submodule.Quotient.mk q))) ∧
          (∀ i (h : H i), dH (i + 1) (dH i h) = 0)) ∧
        (∀ i (x : C.X i)
            (hx : EtaPow.fpowMap f (C.X i) i x ∈ EtaComplex.term f C i),
          ∃ hz : Submodule.Quotient.mk x ∈ Z i,
            t i (Submodule.Quotient.mk
              (⟨EtaPow.fpowMap f (C.X i) i x, hx⟩ : EtaComplex.term f C i)) =
                ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk x, hz⟩) ∧
        (∀ i (y : C.X (i + 1)) (hy : Submodule.Quotient.mk y ∈ B (i + 1))
            (y' : C.X (i + 1)) (x : C.X i)
            (_heq : y = f • y' + (C.d i (i + 1)).hom x),
          ∃ heta : EtaPow.fpowMap f (C.X i) (i + 1) x ∈ EtaComplex.term f C i,
            s i ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk y, hy⟩ =
              Submodule.Quotient.mk
                (⟨EtaPow.fpowMap f (C.X i) (i + 1) x, heta⟩ :
                  EtaComplex.term f C i)) ∧
        (∀ i (x : C.X i) (hx : Submodule.Quotient.mk x ∈ B i)
            (x' : C.X i) (z : C.X (i - 1))
            (_heq : x = f • x' + (C.d (i - 1) i).hom z),
          ∃ heta : EtaPow.fpowMap f (C.X i) i ((C.d (i - 1) i).hom z) ∈
              EtaComplex.term f C i,
            s' i ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk x, hx⟩ =
              Submodule.Quotient.mk
                (⟨EtaPow.fpowMap f (C.X i) i ((C.d (i - 1) i).hom z), heta⟩ :
                  EtaComplex.term f C i))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaComplex.ModNonzerodivisor.etaTensorMod_to_bockstein_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F7T.** If `f` is a nonzerodivisor and every term of `M` is
`f`-torsion-free, the canonical map from `η_f M ⊗_A A/fA` to the Bockstein
complex of `M/f` is a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaTensorMod_to_bockstein_quasiIso
    (f : A) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (hM : ∀ i, IsSMulRegular (M.X i) f) :
    QuasiIso
      ((etaTensorQuotientIso f hf M hM).hom ≫ etaQuotientToBockstein f hf M hM)

declarations.name: EtaDecalage.etaFetaG_eq_etaFG_cochainComplex
declarations.doc:
For a cochain complex `M^•` of `A`-modules, the cochain complexes `η_f (η_g M^•)` and
`η_{fg} M^•` in `CochainComplex (ModuleCat A) ℤ` are equal.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaFetaG_eq_etaFG_cochainComplex (hdd : ∀ i, (d (i + 1)).comp (d i) = 0)
    (preserve : ∀ i, ((etaFetaG (f := f) (g := g) (d := d)) i).map (dLoc f g M d i)
      ≤ (etaFetaG (f := f) (g := g) (d := d)) (i + 1)) :
    (etaFetaG (f := f) (g := g) (d := d)).toCochainComplex preserve hdd
      = (etaFG (f := f) (g := g) (d := d)).toCochainComplex
          (by rw [← etaFetaG_eq_etaFG hdd]; exact preserve) hdd

declarations.name: EtaPow.LocallyFree.etaTerm_finite_projective_and_split_of_idealI_isPrincipal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F7W.** Let `f` be a nonzerodivisor and let `C` be a bounded complex of finite
free modules. If the ideal generated by the maximal minors of `(f, dⁱ)` is principal, then the
degree-`i` eta term is finite locally free of rank `rank C i`. Its natural map `x ↦ (x, dⁱx)`
into `fⁱ Cⁱ × fⁱ⁺¹ Cⁱ⁺¹` admits a linear retraction, and hence includes it as a direct
summand.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaTerm_finite_projective_and_split_of_idealI_isPrincipal
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (C : BoundedComplex A) (f : A) (hf : IsRegular f) (i : ℤ)
    (hI : (idealI C f i).IsPrincipal) :
    let d := (C.d i).mulVecLin
    let E := fetaTerm f d i
    let P := fpowSub f (Fin (C.rank i) → A) i
    let Q := fpowSub f (Fin (C.rank (i + 1)) → A) (i + 1)
    let inclusion : E →ₗ[A] P × Q := LinearMap.prod
      (LinearMap.codRestrict P E.subtype (fun x => x.2.1))
      (LinearMap.codRestrict Q ((fLoc f d).comp E.subtype) (fun x => x.2.2))
    (∃ hfin : Module.Finite A E,
      letI := hfin
      ∃ hproj : Module.Projective A E,
        letI := hproj
        Module.rankAtStalk (R := A) E = fun _ => C.rank i) ∧
      ∃ retraction : P × Q →ₗ[A] E,
        retraction.comp inclusion = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.GoodBaseChange.isIso_etaBaseChangeMap_toCochainComplex
declarations.doc:
For a bounded complex `C` of finite free `A`-modules all of whose determinantal ideals
`I_i(C, f)` are principal, the canonical base-change comparison `B ⊗_A (η_f C) ⟶ η_g (B ⊗_A C)` is
an isomorphism of complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_etaBaseChangeMap_toCochainComplex (C : BoundedComplex A) (f : A) (hf : IsRegular f)
    (hg : IsRegular (algebraMap A B f)) (hI : ∀ i : ℤ, (idealI C f i).IsPrincipal) :
    IsIso (etaBaseChangeMap (B := B) f C.toCochainComplex)
declarations.comment: the comparison chain map of this file is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.LocallyFreeTerms.eta_baseChange_of_idealI_isPrincipal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F7X.** Let `A → B` be a ring map, let `f` be a nonzerodivisor of `A` whose image
is a nonzerodivisor of `B`, and let `C` be a bounded complex of finite free `A`-modules. If
every determinantal ideal `Iᵢ(C, f)` is principal, then base change of the eta construction
agrees in every degree with the eta construction of the base-changed complex. The equality
takes place inside the localization of the finite free `B`-module after applying the canonical
localization--base-change and finite-free base-change identifications.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eta_baseChange_of_idealI_isPrincipal
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (C : BoundedComplex A) (f : A) (hf : IsRegular f)
    (hg : IsRegular (algebraMap A B f))
    (hI : ∀ i : ℤ, (idealI C f i).IsPrincipal) :
    ∀ i : ℤ,
      let freeBaseChange := TensorProduct.piScalarRight A B B (Fin (C.rank i))
      let ambientMap :=
        ((LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers (algebraMap A B f))
            freeBaseChange.toLinearMap).restrictScalars B).comp
          (Stacks.Eta.BaseChange.psiEquiv f (Fin (C.rank i) → A)).toLinearMap
      Submodule.map ambientMap
          (Submodule.baseChange B (fetaTerm f (C.d i).mulVecLin i)) =
        fetaTerm (algebraMap A B f)
          ((C.baseChange (algebraMap A B)).d i).mulVecLin i

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.LocallyFreeTerms.etaTermBaseChangeEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F7X] in degree `i`, as an isomorphism.** For a ring map `A → B` under which
the nonzerodivisor `f` stays a nonzerodivisor, and a bounded complex `M^•` of finite free
`A`-modules all of whose determinantal ideals `I_i(M^•, f)` are principal, the canonical map
`(η_f M^•)^i ⊗_A B ⟶ (η_g (M^• ⊗_A B))^i` of
`Stacks.Eta.LocallyFreeTerms.etaTermBaseChangeMap` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def etaTermBaseChangeEquiv (C : BoundedComplex A) (f : A) (hf : IsRegular f)
    (hg : IsRegular (algebraMap A B f)) (hI : ∀ i : ℤ, (idealI C f i).IsPrincipal) (i : ℤ) :
    (B ⊗[A] (fetaTerm f (C.d i).mulVecLin i)) ≃ₗ[B]
      fetaTerm (algebraMap A B f) ((C.d i).map (algebraMap A B)).mulVecLin i
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism, degreewise: the comparison map etaTermBaseChangeMap, induced by the ambient comparison, is bijective in every degree. That these degreewise isomorphisms are compatible with the two differentials is ambientBaseChangeMap_comp_fLoc; they are not assembled into one isomorphism of cochain complexes here.

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.BocksteinVanishing.cyclesReduction_epi_iff_powerBocksteinOperator_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F7Y.** For a complex of `f`-torsion-free modules, reduction from cycles
modulo `f²` to cycles modulo `f` is surjective if and only if the corresponding Bockstein
operator is zero. Moreover, these equivalent conditions hold if multiplication by `f` is
injective on `Hⁱ⁺¹(M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cyclesReduction_epi_iff_powerBocksteinOperator_eq_zero
    (f : A) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} A) ℤ) (hM : ∀ n, IsSMulRegular (M.X n) f)
    (i : ℤ) :
    let K := commonUniverseComplex M
    let f' : ULift.{v} A := ULift.up f
    let hf' := ulift_mem_nonZeroDivisors f hf
    let hK := fun n => commonUniverseModules_regular (M.X n) f (hM n)
    let hLower := (powerIdealRows_shortExact f' hf' K hK i).2
    let cyclesReduction := HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap
      (literalPowerQuotientShortComplex K f').g i
    (Epi cyclesReduction ↔ powerBocksteinOperator K f' i i hLower = 0) ∧
      (IsSMulRegular (M.homology (i + 1)) f → Epi cyclesReduction)

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.ReductionDirectSum.etaQuotient_range_eq_prod_of_cyclesReduction_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F7Z.** If cycles modulo `f` lift to cycles modulo `f²`, the canonical
map `(1, dⁱ)` embeds the degree-`i` eta term modulo `f` as a product of a submodule
of `fⁱCⁱ/fⁱ⁺¹Cⁱ` and a submodule of `fⁱ⁺¹Cⁱ⁺¹/fⁱ⁺²Cⁱ⁺¹`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaQuotient_range_eq_prod_of_cyclesReduction_surjective
    (f : A) (_hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)
    (C : EtaComplex.Complex.{u, v} A) (hC : EtaComplex.IsTorsionFree f C)
    (i : ℤ) :
    let mul : ∀ _n : ℕ, ∀ j : ℤ, C.X j →ₗ[A] C.X j := fun n j =>
      { toFun := fun x => (f ^ n) • x
        map_add' := fun x y => smul_add (f ^ n) x y
        map_smul' := fun a x => by simp only [RingHom.id_apply, smul_comm a (f ^ n)] }
    let modTerm : ℕ → ℤ → Type (max u v) := fun n j =>
      (C.X j) ⧸ LinearMap.range (mul n j)
    let dMod : ∀ n j, modTerm n j →ₗ[A] modTerm n (j + 1) := fun n j =>
      Submodule.mapQ _ _ (C.d j (j + 1)).hom (by
        rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
        exact ⟨(C.d j (j + 1)).hom x, by
          exact (map_smul (C.d j (j + 1)).hom (f ^ n) x).symm⟩)
    let reduction : ∀ j, modTerm 2 j →ₗ[A] modTerm 1 j := fun j =>
      Submodule.mapQ _ _ LinearMap.id (by
        rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
        refine ⟨f • x, ?_⟩
        change f ^ 1 • (f • x) = f ^ 2 • x
        simp only [pow_one, pow_two, mul_smul])
    (∀ x : modTerm 1 i, dMod 1 i x = 0 →
      ∃ y : modTerm 2 i, dMod 2 i y = 0 ∧ reduction i y = x) →
    let P₀ := EtaPow.fpowSub f (C.X i) i
    let P₁ := EtaPow.fpowSub f (C.X i) (i + 1)
    let Q₀ := EtaPow.fpowSub f (C.X (i + 1)) (i + 1)
    let Q₁ := EtaPow.fpowSub f (C.X (i + 1)) (i + 2)
    let leftPowerQuotient := P₀ ⧸ P₁.comap P₀.subtype
    let rightPowerQuotient := Q₀ ⧸ Q₁.comap Q₀.subtype
    ∃ (canonical : EtaComplex.QuotientTerm f C i →ₗ[A]
          leftPowerQuotient × rightPowerQuotient)
      (Z : Submodule A leftPowerQuotient) (B : Submodule A rightPowerQuotient),
      (∀ x : EtaComplex.term f C i,
        canonical (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) =
          (Submodule.Quotient.mk (⟨x.1, x.2.1⟩ : P₀),
            Submodule.Quotient.mk
              (⟨EtaPow.fLoc f (C.d i (i + 1)).hom x.1, x.2.2⟩ : Q₀))) ∧
      Function.Injective canonical ∧ LinearMap.range canonical = Z.prod B

declarations.name: Stacks.SplitInjectionDirectSum.main_theorem_0f80
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Tag 0F80, Lemma 15.98.7).**
Let `A` be a commutative ring, let `M`, `N₁`, `N₂` be finite projective
`A`-modules, and let `s : M → N₁ × N₂` be a split injection. Then there exists
a finitely generated ideal `J ⊆ A` such that, for every commutative ring `B`
and every ring map `A → B`, the map `A → B` factors through `A/J`
(`J ≤ ker(A → B)`) if and only if the base-changed map `s_B` identifies `M_B`
with a direct sum of submodules of `N_{1,B} ⊕ N_{2,B}` (Definition 4).
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_0f80
    [Module.Finite A M] [Module.Projective A M]
    [Module.Finite A N₁] [Module.Projective A N₁]
    [Module.Finite A N₂] [Module.Projective A N₂]
    (s : M →ₗ[A] (N₁ × N₂)) (hs : IsSplitInjective s) :
    ∃ J : Ideal A, J.FG ∧
      ∀ (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B],
        (J ≤ RingHom.ker (algebraMap A B)) ↔ IdentifiesDirectSum s B

declarations.name: Stacks.Decalage.ObstructionIdeal.exists_fg_obstructionIdeal_with_finiteProjective_etaHomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F81.** The sum of the degreewise direct-sum obstruction ideals is finitely
generated.  Its quotient is a finitely presented closed immersion, the ideal vanishes at primes
where cycles lift (equivalently, where the localized Bockstein operators vanish), primes where
all localized cohomology modules are free belong to this locus, and after quotienting by the
obstruction ideal all cohomology modules of the eta complex are finite projective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_fg_obstructionIdeal_with_finiteProjective_etaHomology
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (C : BoundedComplex A) (f : A) (hf : IsRegular f)
    (hI : ∀ i : ℤ, (idealI C f i).IsPrincipal) :
    let R := A ⧸ Ideal.span {f}
    let M := associatedComplex C
    ∃ (Jᵢ : ℤ → Ideal R) (J : Ideal R),
      (∀ i, (Jᵢ i).FG) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, ∀ (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra R B],
        Jᵢ i ≤ RingHom.ker (algebraMap R B) ↔
          Stacks.SplitInjectionDirectSum.IdentifiesDirectSum (etaReductionMap C f i) B) ∧
      (∀ i, C.rank i = 0 → C.rank (i + 1) = 0 → Jᵢ i = ⊥) ∧
      (J = ⨆ i, Jᵢ i) ∧
      J.FG ∧
      Function.Surjective (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) ∧
      RingHom.FinitePresentation (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) ∧
      ({p : Ideal A | ∃ hp : p.IsPrime, CyclesLiftAt C f p hp} =
        {p : Ideal A | ∃ hp : p.IsPrime, BocksteinVanishesAt C f p hp}) ∧
      (∀ (p : Ideal A) [hp : p.IsPrime], CyclesLiftAt C f p hp →
        Subsingleton (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl J)) ∧
      (∀ (p : Ideal A) [hp : p.IsPrime], f ∈ p →
        (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime p)
          ((associatedComplex (C.baseChange
            (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime p)))).homology i)) →
        CyclesLiftAt C f p hp) ∧
      let S := R ⧸ J
      let φ : A →+* S := (Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {f}))
      let ηM := ((ModuleCat.extendScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (EtaComplex.etaObject f M)
      ∀ i : ℤ,
        ∃ hfin : Module.Finite S (ηM.homology i),
          letI := hfin
          Module.Projective S (ηM.homology i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affine_pullback_iso_affineSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F82.** A quasi-affine scheme `X` admits an integer `n`, an affine
scheme `T` and a morphism `T ⟶ X` such that for every morphism `X' ⟶ X` with `X'` affine the
fibre product `X' ×_X T` is isomorphic to affine `n`-space over `X'`, as a scheme over `X'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_pullback_iso_affineSpace (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.IsQuasiAffine] :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (T : Scheme.{u}), IsAffine T ∧
      ∃ f : T ⟶ X, ∀ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsAffine X') (g : X' ⟶ X),
        Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.fst g f) ≅
          Over.mk (AffineSpace.over (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) X').hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_contains_affine_pullback_iso_affineSpace
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-affine scheme `X` satisfying the size cutoff of a big fppf site `B`, the
affine-space bundle of Stacks 0F82 over `X` can be chosen with its total space satisfying the
cutoff too, and its structure morphism is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_contains_affine_pullback_iso_affineSpace (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.IsQuasiAffine] (hX : B.Contains X) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (T : Scheme.{u}), IsAffine T ∧ B.Contains T ∧
      ∃ f : T ⟶ X, LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧
        ∀ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsAffine X') (g : X' ⟶ X),
          Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.fst g f) ≅
            Over.mk (AffineSpace.over (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) X').hom)
declarations.comment: the bundle chosen inside a big fppf site

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineFromVanishing.isAffineHom_of_forall_isZero_rightDerived_ideal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F83.** A quasi-compact morphism between quasi-separated schemes is
affine as soon as the first higher direct image of every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals on the
source vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_of_forall_isZero_rightDerived_ideal
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y]
    (hR₁ : ∀ I : Subobject (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf),
      (Subobject.underlying.obj I).IsQuasicoherent →
        IsZero (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived 1).obj
          (Subobject.underlying.obj I))) :
    IsAffineHom f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HasResolutionProperty
declarations.doc:
A scheme has the resolution property if every finite type quasi-coherent module on it is a
quotient of a finite locally free module.
declarations.statement: class HasResolutionProperty (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
A scheme carrying an ample invertible module has the resolution property: every finite type
quasi-coherent module on it is a quotient of a finite locally free module.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_of_isAmple {X : Scheme.{u}} (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : IsAmple X L) : HasResolutionProperty X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**The affine case of [Stacks, Tag 0F88].** The source of an affine morphism onto a
quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme with the resolution property has the resolution property.

The quasi-affine case is
`AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_of_isQuasiAffineHom`, by way of [Stacks, Tag 0FDD] — so
the tag below carries the clause string naming the case that is.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_of_isAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f]
    [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] [HasResolutionProperty Y] :
    HasResolutionProperty X
declarations.comment: the affine case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_of_isAffineHom_or_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F88**. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an affine or quasi-affine morphism of schemes with `Y`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. If `Y` has the resolution property, so does `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_of_isAffineHom_or_isQuasiAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsAffineHom f ∨ IsQuasiAffineHom f) [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y]
    [HasResolutionProperty Y] : HasResolutionProperty X
declarations.comment: affine or quasi-affine f; the whole statement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_epi_of_isIdealAffineCovering
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a scheme with a finite affine open covering `U` and finite type quasi-coherent
sheaves of ideals `I j` whose vanishing loci are the complements of the `U j`.  If `X` has the
resolution property then each `I j` is the quotient of a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_epi_of_isIdealAffineCovering [HasResolutionProperty X] {m : ℕ}
    {U : Fin m → X.Opens} {I : Fin m → X.IdealSheafData} (h : IsIdealAffineCovering X U I)
    (j : Fin m) :
    ∃ (E : X.Modules)
      (_ : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (R := X.ringCatSheaf) E)
      (q : E ⟶ idealPow (I j) 1), Epi q
declarations.comment: the direction that is immediate: resolution property implies each ideal is a finite-locally-free quotient

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_iff_forall_exists_epi_idealPow_of_isIdealAffineCovering
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F89].** Let `X` be a scheme with
1. a finite affine open covering `X = U 0 ∪ ⋯ ∪ U (m - 1)`, and
2. finite type quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals `I j` with `V(I j) = X ∖ U j`.

Then `X` has the resolution property if and only if each `I j` is the quotient of a finite
locally free `𝒪_X`-module.

The forward direction is `exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_epi_of_isIdealAffineCovering`, the
converse `hasResolutionProperty_of_isIdealAffineCovering`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_iff_forall_exists_epi_idealPow_of_isIdealAffineCovering {m : ℕ}
    {U : Fin m → X.Opens} {I : Fin m → X.IdealSheafData} (h : IsIdealAffineCovering X U I) :
    HasResolutionProperty X ↔
      ∀ j, ∃ (E : X.Modules)
        (_ : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (R := X.ringCatSheaf) E)
        (q : E ⟶ idealPow (I j) 1), Epi q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_of_isIdealAffineCovering
declarations.doc:
**The substantial direction of [Stacks, Tag 0F89].**  Let `X` be a scheme with a finite
affine open covering `U` and finite type quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals `I j` whose vanishing
loci are the complements of the `U j`.  If each `I j` is the quotient of a finite locally free
`𝒪_X`-module then `X` has the resolution property.

`X` need not be Noetherian: this is the tag at the generality the source states it.  Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_epi_of_isIdealAffineCovering`, which is the
direction the source calls trivial, it is the equivalence the tag asserts.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_of_isIdealAffineCovering {X : Scheme.{u}} {m : ℕ}
    {U : Fin m → X.Opens} {I : Fin m → X.IdealSheafData} (h : IsIdealAffineCovering X U I)
    (E : Fin m → X.Modules)
    (hE : ∀ j, SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (E j))
    (q : ∀ j, E j ⟶ idealPow (I j) 1) (hq : ∀ j, Epi (q j)) :
    HasResolutionProperty X
declarations.comment: the substantial direction, at the source's generality: finite-locally-free quotients of the ideals give the resolution property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular.hasResolutionProperty
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F8A].** A quasi-compact regular scheme with affine diagonal has the resolution
property.

Quasi-compactness is `CompactSpace X`, the affine diagonal is
`IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from X))`, and regularity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular` ([Stacks, Tag 02IS]); these are exactly the conditions of the
source.

The proof is the one of `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfect/ResolutionPropertyRegular.lean`:
regularity gives Noetherianness and unique
factorization in the local rings, a regular scheme is normal so every point lies in a dense affine
open, [Stacks, Tag 0EGJ] cuts out the complement of each of those by an effective Cartier divisor,
quasi-compactness makes the covering finite, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_of_isNoetherian_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor` concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsRegular.hasResolutionProperty (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [IsAffineHom
      (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal (CategoryTheory.Limits.terminal.from X))]
    (hX : IsRegular X) : HasResolutionProperty X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
Let `c` be a limit cone over a cofiltered diagram `D` of quasi-compact, quasi-separated
schemes with affine transition morphisms.  If some stage `D.obj i` has the resolution property,
then so does the limit `c.pt`.

The projection `c.π.app i : c.pt ⟶ D.obj i` is affine, so this is the affine case of
[Stacks, Tag 0F88]; it is one direction of [Stacks, Tag 0F8B]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_iff_exists_of_isLimit`).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_of_isLimit [IsCofiltered I]
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)] (hc : IsLimit c)
    [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    (i : I) [HasResolutionProperty (D.obj i)] :
    HasResolutionProperty c.pt
declarations.comment: the direction that is immediate: if a stage of the diagram has the resolution property then so does the limit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_iff_exists_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F8B].**  Let `c` be a limit cone over a cofiltered diagram `D` of
quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms.  The limit `c.pt` has
the resolution property if and only if some stage `D.obj i` has it.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_iff_exists_of_isLimit (hc : IsLimit c) :
    HasResolutionProperty c.pt ↔ ∃ i, HasResolutionProperty (D.obj i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HasResolutionProperty.isAffineHom_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F8C.** A quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme with the resolution
property has affine diagonal.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_diagonal_of_exists_isAffineHom_isNoetherian_hasResolutionProperty`
composed with `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineHom_isNoetherian_hasResolutionProperty`, which
supplies the required affine morphism from the converse of
`AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_of_isLimit` at Noetherian stages
(`AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_stage`).
declarations.statement:
theorem HasResolutionProperty.isAffineHom_diagonal (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [HasResolutionProperty X] :
    IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from X))

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.exists_boundedFiniteLocallyFree_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F8E.** On a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme with the
resolution property, a bounded below complex of quasi-coherent modules representing a perfect
object of the derived category receives a quasi-isomorphism from a bounded complex of finite
locally free modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedFiniteLocallyFree_quasiIso (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [AlgebraicGeometry.HasResolutionProperty X]
    (F : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    (hFplus : CochainComplex.plus X.Modules F)
    (hFqc : ∀ i : ℤ, (F.X i).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hFperf : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F)) :
    ∃ (E : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (f : E ⟶ F),
      boundedFiniteLocallyFreeComplex X E ∧ QuasiIso f

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.exists_boundedFiniteLocallyFree_iso_of_hasResolutionProperty
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F8F].**  Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme with the
resolution property.  Every perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` is isomorphic to the image of a bounded
complex of finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules.

The three assumptions on `X` are exactly the source's.  The affine diagonal used in the proof
comes
from [Stacks, Tag 0F8C], `AlgebraicGeometry.HasResolutionProperty.isAffineHom_diagonal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedFiniteLocallyFree_iso_of_hasResolutionProperty (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [HasResolutionProperty X]
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K) :
    ∃ E : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ, boundedFiniteLocallyFreeComplex X E ∧
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ≅ K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.exists_boundedFiniteLocallyFree_roof_of_hasResolutionProperty
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F8G].**  Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme with the
resolution property and let `ℰ^•`, `ℱ^•` be finite complexes of finite locally free
`𝒪_X`-modules.  Every morphism `α : ℰ^• ⟶ ℱ^•` of `D(𝒪_X)` is represented by a diagram
`ℰ^• ← 𝒢^• → ℱ^•` with `𝒢^•` a bounded complex of finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules and
`𝒢^• → ℰ^•` a quasi-isomorphism.

The assumptions on `X` are exactly the source's.  The affine diagonal used in the proof comes
from [Stacks, Tag 0F8C], `AlgebraicGeometry.HasResolutionProperty.isAffineHom_diagonal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedFiniteLocallyFree_roof_of_hasResolutionProperty (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [HasResolutionProperty X]
    (E F : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    (hE : boundedFiniteLocallyFreeComplex X E) (hF : boundedFiniteLocallyFreeComplex X F)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) :
    ∃ (G : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (p : G ⟶ E) (_ : QuasiIso p) (q : G ⟶ F),
      boundedFiniteLocallyFreeComplex X G ∧
        inv (DerivedCategory.Q.map p) ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map q = α

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.exists_boundedFiniteLocallyFree_homotopy_of_hasResolutionProperty
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme with the resolution property and let
`ℰ^•`, `ℱ^•` be finite complexes of finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules.  If two maps of complexes
`α^•, β^• : ℰ^• ⟶ ℱ^•` define the same morphism of `D(𝒪_X)`, then there is a
quasi-isomorphism `γ^• : 𝒢^• ⟶ ℰ^•` with `𝒢^•` a bounded complex of finite locally free
`𝒪_X`-modules such that `α^• ∘ γ^•` and `β^• ∘ γ^•` are homotopic.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedFiniteLocallyFree_homotopy_of_hasResolutionProperty (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [HasResolutionProperty X]
    (E F : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    (hE : boundedFiniteLocallyFreeComplex X E) (hF : boundedFiniteLocallyFreeComplex X F)
    (α β : E ⟶ F) (h : DerivedCategory.Q.map α = DerivedCategory.Q.map β) :
    ∃ (G : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (γ : G ⟶ E) (_ : QuasiIso γ),
      boundedFiniteLocallyFreeComplex X G ∧ Nonempty (Homotopy (γ ≫ α) (γ ≫ β))

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.perfectDerivedProperty_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Perfect objects form a triangulated subcategory of `D(O_X)`.** This is the ringed-space
statement `Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectTriangulatedSubcategory.isTriangulated_isPerfect`, read on the
ringed space underlying `X`.
declarations.statement:
instance perfectDerivedProperty_isTriangulated (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (show ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory X.Modules) from
      fun K => IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: perfect objects form a triangulated subcategory

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.perfectComplexFunctor_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**The canonical functor `K^b(A) ⥤ D_perf(O_X)` is exact.** The composite
`K^b(A) ⥤ K(O_X) ⥤ D(O_X)` is exact, being the inclusion of a triangulated subcategory
followed by the localization functor of the derived category, and the canonical functor is its
lift along the perfectness of its values, which is exact because `D_perf(O_X)` is a
triangulated subcategory.
declarations.statement:
instance perfectComplexFunctor_isTriangulated (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (perfectComplexFunctor X).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: exactness of the canonical functor

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.BoundedFiniteLocallyFreeHomotopyCategory
declarations.doc: The homotopy category `K^b(A)` of bounded complexes of finite locally free modules.
declarations.statement: abbrev BoundedFiniteLocallyFreeHomotopyCategory (X : Scheme.{u})
declarations.comment: the category K^b(A)

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.PerfectDerivedCategory
declarations.doc: The full subcategory `D_perf(O_X)` of perfect objects of the derived category.
declarations.statement: abbrev PerfectDerivedCategory (X : Scheme.{u})
declarations.comment: the category of perfect objects

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.quasiIsomorphisms
declarations.doc: The system `S` of quasi-isomorphisms of `K^b(A)`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev quasiIsomorphisms (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    MorphismProperty (BoundedFiniteLocallyFreeHomotopyCategory X)
declarations.comment: the system S of quasi-isomorphisms

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.perfectDerivedProperty_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms
declarations.doc: **Perfect objects form a strictly full subcategory of `D(O_X)`.**
declarations.statement:
instance perfectDerivedProperty_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms
      (fun K : DerivedCategory X.Modules => IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
declarations.comment: perfect objects are closed under isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.quasiIsomorphisms_isInvertedBy_perfectComplexFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The canonical functor `K^b(A) ⥤ D_perf(O_X)` inverts the quasi-isomorphisms of `K^b(A)`.**
A morphism of `K^b(A)` is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when its image in `K(O_X)` is one, so
`CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.Qh` sends it to an isomorphism; that image is the image of the
morphism under the fully faithful inclusion of `D_perf(O_X)`, which therefore reflects the
invertibility.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIsomorphisms_isInvertedBy_perfectComplexFunctor (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (quasiIsomorphisms X).IsInvertedBy (perfectComplexFunctor X)
declarations.comment: the canonical functor inverts the system `S` of quasi-isomorphisms, so that it factors through `S⁻¹K^b(A)`; this is the first field of `Functor.IsLocalization`, for every scheme X

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.perfectComplexFunctor_isLocalization_of_hasResolutionProperty
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence clause of [Stacks, Tag 0F8I].**  On a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
scheme with the resolution property, the canonical functor `K^b(A) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_X)` presents
`D_perf(𝒪_X)` as the localization of `K^b(A)` at the quasi-isomorphisms.

The three assumptions on `X` are exactly the source's.  The affine diagonal is supplied
by [Stacks, Tag 0F8C] (`AlgebraicGeometry.HasResolutionProperty.isAffineHom_diagonal`), which
rests on the converse of [Stacks, Tag 0F8B] at Noetherian stages
(`AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_stage`).
declarations.statement:
theorem perfectComplexFunctor_isLocalization_of_hasResolutionProperty (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [HasResolutionProperty X] :
    (perfectComplexFunctor X).IsLocalization (quasiIsomorphisms X)
declarations.comment: the canonical functor presents the perfect derived category as the localization of the bounded homotopy category at the quasi-isomorphisms

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.perfect_of_boundedFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**`K^b(A)` lands in `D_perf(O_X)`.** A bounded complex of finite locally free modules is
strictly perfect on a small enough neighbourhood of each point of `X`, so it is perfect in the
sense of Tag 08CM with the identity as the local quasi-isomorphism, and it represents its own
image in the derived category.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfect_of_boundedFiniteLocallyFree (X : Scheme.{u})
    (E : BoundedFiniteLocallyFreeHomotopyCategory X) :
    IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj E.obj)
declarations.comment: the functor lands in perfect objects

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.isSaturated_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Perfectness is a saturated property of objects of `D(O_X)` on a ringed space.**  Both
summands of a perfect biproduct are perfect by [Stacks, Tag 08CS], and perfectness is closed
under isomorphism, so the isomorphism closure in the definition of saturation is the property
itself.  For a scheme `X`, whose `X.Modules` is `OXMod` of `X.toRingedSpace`, this is the
saturation clause of Tag 0F8I: a direct summand of a perfect object of `D(O_X)` is perfect.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSaturated_isPerfect {X : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)] :
    ObjectProperty.IsSaturated
      (fun K : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X) => IsPerfect K)
declarations.comment: `D_perf(O_X)` is a saturated subcategory of `D(O_X)` -- the adjective `saturated` of the source's item (3), which is closure under direct summands, on any ringed space

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.boundedFiniteLocallyFreeHomotopyProperty_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**`K^b(A)` is a triangulated subcategory of `K(O_X)`.** The property of being a bounded
complex with finite locally free terms holds of the zero complex, is stable under shift, and is
stable under mapping cones; the last because `(mappingCone f).X i` is `K.X (i + 1) ⊞ L.X i`.
declarations.statement:
instance boundedFiniteLocallyFreeHomotopyProperty_isTriangulated
    (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (boundedFiniteLocallyFreeHomotopyProperty X).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the homotopy subcategory is triangulated

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.perfectComplexFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The canonical functor `K^b(A) ⥤ D_perf(O_X)`.** It is `DerivedCategory.Qh` restricted to
`K^b(A)`, lifted to the full subcategory of perfect objects along
`Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.perfect_of_boundedFiniteLocallyFree`.
declarations.statement:
def perfectComplexFunctor (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    BoundedFiniteLocallyFreeHomotopyCategory X ⥤ PerfectDerivedCategory X
declarations.comment: the canonical functor

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.quasiIsomorphisms_isSaturated
declarations.doc: **The system `S` of quasi-isomorphisms of `K^b(A)` is saturated.**
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIsomorphisms_isSaturated (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (quasiIsomorphisms X).IsSaturated
declarations.comment: saturation of the quasi-isomorphism system

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.quasiIsomorphisms_isCompatibleWithTriangulation
declarations.doc:
**The system `S` of quasi-isomorphisms of `K^b(A)` is compatible with the triangulated
structure.**
declarations.statement:
instance quasiIsomorphisms_isCompatibleWithTriangulation (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (quasiIsomorphisms X).IsCompatibleWithTriangulation
declarations.comment: compatibility of quasi-isomorphisms with triangulation

declarations.name: CochainComplex.nonempty_truncLE_truncLE_iso
declarations.doc:
**The first row of the display of Stacks 0F8J.** Truncating `K` above degree `n` and then
above a degree `m ≤ n` returns the truncation of `K` above degree `m`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_truncLE_truncLE_iso (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) {m n : ℤ} (h : m ≤ n) :
    Nonempty ((K.truncLE n).truncLE m ≅ K.truncLE m)
declarations.comment: the left-hand row of the display is the preceding truncation

declarations.name: CochainComplex.nonempty_Q_shortComplexTruncLE_X₃_iso
declarations.doc:
**The right-hand row of the display of Stacks 0F8J.** The quotient of the truncation of `K`
above degree `k - 1` inside the truncation of `K` above degree `k` is the cohomology object
`H^k(K)` placed in degree `k`.
declarations.comment: the right-hand row of the display is the shifted cohomology object

declarations.name: CochainComplex.nonempty_triangleOfSES_truncLE_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F8J.** The canonical truncation triangle
`τ_{≤k-1}K ⟶ τ_{≤k}K ⟶ H^k(K)[-k] ⟶ (τ_{≤k-1}K)[1]` is the triangle of the short exact sequence
of complexes `0 ⟶ τ_{≤k-1}(τ_{≤k}K) ⟶ τ_{≤k}K ⟶ Q ⟶ 0`, morphisms included.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_triangleOfSES_truncLE_iso (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (k : ℤ) :
    Nonempty (DerivedCategory.triangleOfSES
      ((K.truncLE k).shortComplexTruncLE_shortExact (k - 1)) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.triangleLEGT (k - 1)).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (K.truncLE k)))
declarations.comment: the truncation triangle is the triangle of the displayed short exact sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.isFiniteLocallyFree_cycles
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F8J], the kernels.**  Let `ℰ` be a complex of finite locally free
`𝒪_X`-modules vanishing above degree `b`, each of whose cohomology sheaves is a perfect
`𝒪_X`-module of tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.  Then `Ker(d^n)` is finite locally free for every
`n`.

Boundedness below is not needed for this: the induction descends from `b`, and each step consumes
only the degree above.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_cycles
    (hterm : ∀ n : ℤ, IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (P.X n))
    (hperf : ∀ n : ℤ, IsPerfect.{u, u, u + 1}
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (P.homology n)))
    (htor : ∀ n : ℤ, HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (P.homology n)) (-1) 0)
    (b : ℤ) [P.IsStrictlyLE b] (n : ℤ) :
    IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (P.cycles n)
declarations.comment:
the kernels of the differentials, for a complex of finite locally free modules on
a scheme vanishing above a degree, with the cohomology sheaves perfect of tor amplitude in
[-1, 0]

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.isFiniteLocallyFree_kernel_homologyπ
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F8J], the images.**  Under the hypotheses of
`Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.isFiniteLocallyFree_cycles`, the image `Im(d^{n-1})` of the
differential into degree `n` is finite locally free.

That image is written here as `kernel (P.homologyπ n)`, the kernel of the projection from the
cocycles in degree `n` onto the cohomology there — the presentation
`StacksDraft.CartanEilenbergResolutions.cochainGluingData` uses, and the one that is indexed by `n`
with no subtraction.  It is the image in the categorical sense too:
`StacksDraft.CartanEilenbergResolutions.exists_imageIso_of_cochainGluingData` exhibits an
isomorphism
`CategoryTheory.Limits.image (P.dFrom (n - 1)) ≅ kernel (P.homologyπ n)` compatible with the
factorisation of the differential through it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_kernel_homologyπ
    (hterm : ∀ n : ℤ, IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (P.X n))
    (hperf : ∀ n : ℤ, IsPerfect.{u, u, u + 1}
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (P.homology n)))
    (htor : ∀ n : ℤ, HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (P.homology n)) (-1) 0)
    (b : ℤ) [P.IsStrictlyLE b] (n : ℤ) :
    IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (kernel (P.homologyπ n))
declarations.comment:
the images of the differentials, presented as the kernels of the projections from
the cocycles onto the cohomology, for a complex of finite locally free modules on a scheme
vanishing above a degree, with the cohomology sheaves perfect of tor amplitude in [-1, 0]

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.boundedComplexSplitting
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F8J] assembled: the degreewise exactness datum of a bounded complex of finite
locally free `𝒪_X`-modules with perfect cohomology of tor dimension at most one.**

This is the source's conclusion in the form its consumers need.  `Stacks.Chow` defines the Chern
classes, the power sums and the Chern character of a complex against a
`Stacks.Chow.BoundedComplexSplitting` — the family of short exact sequences
`0 ⟶ Ker(d^n) ⟶ ℰ^n ⟶ Im(d^n) ⟶ 0` together with finite local freeness of every kernel and every
image — and before this nothing produced one.  The finite local freeness of the kernels and of
the images is precisely what the source takes from this tag; the rest of the datum is the
degreewise presentation of the complex, supplied by
`StacksDraft.CartanEilenbergResolutions.cochainGluingData`.

The two vanishing conditions at the ends of the range are the boundedness of the complex: nothing
enters degree `a` because `ℰ^{a-1}` vanishes, and nothing leaves degree `a + k` because
`ℰ^{a+k+1}` does.
declarations.statement:
def boundedComplexSplitting (a : ℤ) (k : ℕ)
    [P.IsStrictlyGE a] [P.IsStrictlyLE (a + (k : ℤ))]
    (hterm : ∀ n : ℤ, IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (P.X n))
    (hperf : ∀ n : ℤ, IsPerfect.{u, u, u + 1}
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (G.H n)))
    (htor : ∀ n : ℤ, HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (G.H n)) (-1) 0) :
    Stacks.Chow.BoundedComplexSplitting X P a k
declarations.comment:
the degreewise exactness datum of a bounded complex of finite locally free modules
on a scheme, assembled from the two displayed short exact sequences, with the cohomology sheaves
perfect of tor amplitude in [-1, 0]

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isFiniteLocallyFree_range_and_ker_of_torDimensionLE_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F8J.** Let `X` be a scheme and let `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` be such that every cohomology module
`H^i(E)` is a perfect `𝒪_X`-module of Tor dimension at most one, that is, `H^i(E)` placed in degree
zero is a perfect object with Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`. Let `ℰ^•` be a complex of finite locally
free `𝒪_X`-modules which vanishes above degree `b` and represents `E`. Then `Im(d^i)` and
`Ker(d^i)` are finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules for every `i`.

The source takes `E` perfect and `ℰ^•` bounded; neither the perfectness of `E` nor a lower bound
on `ℰ^•` is used.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_range_and_ker_of_torDimensionLE_one
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (K : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E) (b : ℤ) [K.IsStrictlyLE b]
    (hterm : ∀ i : ℤ,
      Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (K.X i))
    (hH : ∀ i : ℤ,
      IsPerfect.{u, u, u + 1} ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj E)) ∧
      HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj E)) (-1) 0)
    (i : ℤ) :
    Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf)
        (image (K.d i (i + 1)) : X.Modules) ∧
      Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf)
        (kernel (K.d i (i + 1)) : X.Modules)
declarations.comment: the images and kernels of the differentials

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isFiniteLocallyFree_truncLE_X_of_torDimensionLE_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F8J, the truncation rows.** Under the hypotheses of
`StacksDraft.Perfect.isFiniteLocallyFree_range_and_ker_of_torDimensionLE_one`, fix `k` and let
`0 ⟶ τ_{≤k-1}(τ_{≤k}ℰ^•) ⟶ τ_{≤k}ℰ^• ⟶ Q ⟶ 0` be the short exact sequence of successive canonical
truncations. Every term of each of its three rows is a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module.

The rows are `ℰ^a → ⋯ → ℰ^{k-2} → Ker(d^{k-1})`, `ℰ^a → ⋯ → ℰ^{k-1} → Ker(d^k)` and
`Im(d^{k-1}) → Ker(d^k)`, as displayed in the source. This short exact sequence represents the
distinguished triangle `τ_{≤k-1}E ⟶ τ_{≤k}E ⟶ H^k(E)[-k] ⟶ (τ_{≤k-1}E)[1]`, which is
`CochainComplex.nonempty_triangleOfSES_truncLE_iso`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_truncLE_X_of_torDimensionLE_one
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (K : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E) (b : ℤ) [K.IsStrictlyLE b]
    (hterm : ∀ i : ℤ,
      Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (K.X i))
    (hH : ∀ i : ℤ,
      IsPerfect.{u, u, u + 1} ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj E)) ∧
      HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj E)) (-1) 0)
    (k i : ℤ) :
    Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf)
