immersions `j₁ : X₁ ⟶ X` and `j₂ : X₂ ⟶ X` cover `X`, every class of `k`-cycles on `X` is the sum
of the pushforwards of a class on `X₁` and a class on `X₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion_coprod
    (hcover : Set.range j₁ ∪ Set.range j₂ = Set.univ) :
    Function.Surjective ((chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion C sX₁ sX j₁ hj₁ k).coprod
      (chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion C sX₂ sX j₂ hj₂ k))
declarations.comment: surjectivity, for two arbitrary closed immersions

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exact_chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion_prod_coprod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F94, exactness in the middle, for two closed immersions.** If the images of two
closed immersions `j₁ : X₁ ⟶ X` and `j₂ : X₂ ⟶ X` cover `X`, a pair of classes of `k`-cycles on
`X₁` and `X₂` has vanishing sum of pushforwards exactly when it is the pair of pushforwards of a
class on the fibre product `X₁ ×_X X₂`, the second one negated.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion_prod_coprod
    (hcover : Set.range j₁ ∪ Set.range j₂ = Set.univ) :
    Function.Exact
      ((chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion C (pullback.fst j₁ j₂ ≫ sX₁) sX₁
          (pullback.fst j₁ j₂) rfl k).prod
        (-chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion C (pullback.fst j₁ j₂ ≫ sX₁) sX₂
          (pullback.snd j₁ j₂)
          (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq_fst C sX j₁ j₂ sX₁ sX₂ hj₁ hj₂)
          k))
      ((chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion C sX₁ sX j₁ hj₁ k).coprod
        (chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion C sX₂ sX j₂ hj₂ k))
declarations.comment: exactness in the middle, for two arbitrary closed immersions

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_properPushforward_subschemeι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F95.** For the Gysin map of the zero scheme of a global section of an invertible
module `L`, the composite with the pushforward along `i` is intersection with the first Chern
class of the restriction `L|_D`: `i^* i_* α = c₁(L|_D) ∩ α` in `A_k(D)`.

Both operations are functions of `L` and `s` alone: the Gysin map is
`Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible` and the right hand side is the cap product
`Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible` of the restricted module, which is invertible by
Stacks 0B8L. No hypothesis is carried: the two first Chern class component rules agree up to
rational equivalence on the integral components of `D`. The statement is exactly
`Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_properPushforward_zeroSchemeι`, of which this is an
alias.
declarations.statement: alias gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_properPushforward_subschemeι
declarations.comment: the identity i^* i_* α = c₁(L|_D) ∩ α in A_k(D), with i_* taken on cycles as in the source's proof, with no hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOnChowOfInvertible_properChowPushforward_subschemeι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F95, on Chow groups.** The composite
`i^* i_* : A_{k+1}(D) ⟶ A_k(D)` of the two descended operations of an invertible module `L` and a
section `s` is intersection with the first Chern class of `L|_D`.

The descended Gysin map is that of Stacks 02TO and the descended cap product that of Stacks 02TI,
at descent data `h` and `hchernD`. Both are propositions proved in this repository, as
`Stacks.Chow.gysinOfInvertibleFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence` and
`Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_firstChernComponentCycleRule`, so
the identity holds outright; with those proofs supplied it is
`Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible_properChowPushforward_zeroSchemeι`. The instance of Stacks 02S2
needed for `i_*` on Chow groups is discharged, `i` being a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHomomorphismOnChowOfInvertible_properChowPushforward_subschemeι
    (h : GysinOfInvertibleFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C p k L s)
    (hchernD : FirstChernClassCapFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
      ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) k
      (firstChernComponentCycleRule C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) k
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).obj L)))
    (α : chowGroup C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) (k + 1)) :
    gysinHomomorphismOnChowOfInvertible C p k L s h
        (properChowPushforward C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) p
          (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι rfl (k + 1)
          (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion
            (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι C
            ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) p rfl (k + 1)) α) =
      firstChernClassCapOnChow C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) k
        (firstChernComponentCycleRule C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) k
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).obj L))
        hchernD α
declarations.comment: the composite A_{k+1}(D) ⟶ A_k(D) of the descended operations, at any descent data h and hchernD; each is discharged by a theorem of this repository (Stacks 02TO and 02TI), so nothing is assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible_comp_properChowPushforward_zeroSchemeι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F95.** The composite of the proper pushforward along the zero scheme
`i : D = Z(s) ⟶ X` of a global section of an invertible module with the Gysin map of that zero
scheme is intersection with the first Chern class of the restriction `L|_D`:

  `i^* i_* α = c₁(L|_D) ∩ α`  in  `\CH_k(D)`,  for `α ∈ \CH_{k+1}(D)`.

All three maps are the operations on Chow groups: `i_*` is Tag 0GU8, whose vanishing hypothesis
of Tag 02S2 is discharged by
`Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion`, `i^*` is
the descended Gysin map `Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible` of Tag 02TO and the right hand side
is the descended cap product `Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapChow` of Tag 02TI, both of which are
unconditional in this repository. No hypothesis is carried.

Every class is the class of a cycle, and on a cycle the identity is
`Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_properPushforward_zeroSchemeι`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinChowOfInvertible_comp_properChowPushforward_zeroSchemeι :
    (gysinChowOfInvertible C p k L s).comp
        (properChowPushforward C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) p
          (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι rfl (k + 1)
          (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion
            (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι C
            ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) p rfl (k + 1))) =
      firstChernClassCapChow C k ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible_properChowPushforward_zeroSchemeι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F95**, read on a class. This is
`Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible_comp_properChowPushforward_zeroSchemeι` evaluated at `α`, the
source's "sends `α` to `c₁(L|_D) ∩ α`".
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinChowOfInvertible_properChowPushforward_zeroSchemeι
    (α : chowGroup C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) (k + 1)) :
    gysinChowOfInvertible C p k L s
        (properChowPushforward C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) p
          (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι rfl (k + 1)
          (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion
            (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι C
            ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) p rfl (k + 1)) α) =
      firstChernClassCapChow C k ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).obj L) α

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_properPushforward_zeroSchemeι
declarations.doc:
**The self-intersection formula.** For the Gysin map of the zero scheme `i : D = Z(s) ⟶ X` of
a global section of an invertible module `L`, the composite with the pushforward along `i` is
intersection with the first Chern class of the restriction `L|_D`:

  `i^* i_* α = c₁(L|_D) ∩ α`  in  `A_k(D)`,  for `α ∈ Z_{k+1}(D)`.

Both operations are functions of `L` and `s` alone: the Gysin map is
`Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible` (Tag 02T8) and the right hand side is the cap product
`Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassCapOfInvertible` (Tag 02SO) of the restricted module, which is
invertible by Tag 0B8L. No hypothesis is carried; see the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.Gysin42.SelfIntersectionFormula`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_properPushforward_zeroSchemeι
    (α : CycleGroup C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) (k + 1)) :
    gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L s
        (properPushforward C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) p
          (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι rfl (k + 1) α) =
      firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) k
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).obj L) α
declarations.comment: the identity i^* i_* α = c₁(L|_D) ∩ α in A_k(D), with i_* taken on cycles as in the source's proof

declarations.name: Stacks.LineBundle.Situation.isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_ker_zeroSection
declarations.doc:
**The image of the zero section of a line bundle is a relative effective Cartier divisor**,
part of clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0F96]. The projection of the total space is smooth of relative
dimension one, and the closed subscheme cut out by the zero section is finite locally free over
the base because the projection restricts on it to the comparison isomorphism with the base; so
[Stacks, Tag 0B9D] applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem Situation.isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_ker_zeroSection (D : Situation.{u}) :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor D.totalSpaceToBase
      D.zeroSection.ker
declarations.comment: (1), the zero section is a relative effective Cartier divisor

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionGysinChow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F96, clause (3).** The image `o(X)` of the zero section of a line bundle
`p : L ⟶ X` is an effective Cartier divisor on `L`, so it has a Gysin map; composed with the
identification of `o(X)` with `X` it is

  `o^* : \CH_{k + 1}(L) ⟶ \CH_k(X)`.

The divisor is presented as clause (1) presents it, the zero scheme of the tautological global
section of `p^*(ℒ^{⊗ -1})`, and the Gysin map of a zero scheme is the unconditional
[Stacks, Tag 02TO] on Chow groups. That the divisor is an effective Cartier divisor — the
clause's justification — is
`Stacks.LineBundle.Situation.isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_zeroScheme_tautologicalSectionBase`;
it is a theorem here and so is not taken as a hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
def zeroSectionGysinChow (k : ℤ) :
    chowGroup C (D.totalSpaceToBase ≫ sX) (k + 1) →+ chowGroup C sX k
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionGysinChow_comp_flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F96, clause (4).** The source's phrasing: the composite

  `o^* p^* : \CH_k(X) ⟶ \CH_k(X)`

*is* the identity map. This is
`Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionGysinChow_flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension` read as an equality of
homomorphisms; the two are interchangeable, both sides of the equality being determined by their
values.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroSectionGysinChow_comp_flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension (k : ℤ) :
    (zeroSectionGysinChow C D sX k).comp
        (flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C (D.totalSpaceToBase ≫ sX) sX D.totalSpaceToBase
          rfl 1 D.relativeDimension_totalSpaceToBase k) =
      AddMonoidHom.id (chowGroup C sX k)
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionChowPushforward_eq_neg_flatPullbackChow_firstChernClassCapChow
declarations.doc:
Let `(S, δ)` be the base situation of chapter 42, let `X` be locally of finite type over `S`,
let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module and let `p : L ⟶ X` be the associated line bundle with
zero section `o : X ⟶ L`. Then

  `o_* α = - p^*(c₁(ℒ) ∩ α)`  in  `A_{k+1}(L)`  for every  `α ∈ A_{k+1}(X)`.

Here `c₁(ℒ) ∩ -` on `A_{k+1}(X)` is `firstChernClassCapChow C k`, and the flat pullback, which
lands in `A_{k + ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)}(L)`, is transported to `A_{k+1}(L)` by
`Stacks.Chow.chowGroupCast`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroSectionChowPushforward_eq_neg_flatPullbackChow_firstChernClassCapChow (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup C sX (k + 1)) :
    zeroSectionChowPushforward C D sX (k + 1) α =
      -chowGroupCast C (D.totalSpaceToBase ≫ sX)
        (show k + ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = k + 1 from by simp)
        (flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C (D.totalSpaceToBase ≫ sX) sX D.totalSpaceToBase
          rfl 1 D.relativeDimension_totalSpaceToBase k (firstChernClassCapChow C k sX D.L α))
declarations.comment: part (5)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionChowPushforward
declarations.doc:
The proper pushforward on Chow groups along the zero section `o : X ⟶ L` of a line bundle,

`o_* : \CH_k(X) ⟶ \CH_k(L)`.
declarations.statement:
def zeroSectionChowPushforward (k : ℤ) :
    chowGroup C sX k →+ chowGroup C (D.totalSpaceToBase ≫ sX) k
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionGysinChow_zeroSectionChowPushforward_mk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F96, clause (6).** The Gysin map of the zero section of a line bundle `p : L ⟶ X`
composed with the pushforward along it is intersection with the first Chern class of `ℒ`, with a
minus sign:

  `o^* o_* α = - c₁(ℒ) ∩ α`,

a map `\CH_{k+1}(X) ⟶ \CH_k(X)`.

Both maps of the composite are the maps of clauses (2) and (3),
`Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionChowPushforward` and `Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionGysinChow`, and the only
hypothesis is theirs, that `X` be locally of finite type over `S`. The right hand side is the cap
product of [Stacks, Tag 02SO] on a cycle representative, which is what makes it unconditional;
see the module documentation.

The proof is the source's: the self-intersection formula [Stacks, Tag 0F95] for the divisor
`o(X)` on `L`, whose module is `p^*(ℒ^{⊗ -1})` by clause (1), followed by the identification of
the restriction of that module with `ℒ^{⊗ -1}` and by [Stacks, Tag 02SP] in the form
`c₁(ℒ^{⊗ -1}) ∩ α = -(c₁(ℒ) ∩ α)`, which is where the sign comes from.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroSectionGysinChow_zeroSectionChowPushforward_mk (k : ℤ)
    (α : CycleGroup C sX (k + 1)) :
    zeroSectionGysinChow C D sX k
        (zeroSectionChowPushforward C D sX (k + 1)
          (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C sX (k + 1)) α)) =
      -firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C sX k D.L α
declarations.comment: part (6)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionGysinChow_comp_zeroSectionChowPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F96, clause (6).** The source's phrasing: the composite

  `o^* o_* : \CH_{k+1}(X) ⟶ \CH_k(X)`

*is* the map `α ↦ - c₁(ℒ) ∩ α`, as an equality of homomorphisms read on cycle representatives.
Every Chow class is the class of a cycle, so this and
`Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionGysinChow_zeroSectionChowPushforward_mk` are interchangeable.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroSectionGysinChow_comp_zeroSectionChowPushforward (k : ℤ) :
    ((zeroSectionGysinChow C D sX k).comp
          (zeroSectionChowPushforward C D sX (k + 1))).comp
        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C sX (k + 1))) =
      -firstChernClassCapOfInvertible C sX k D.L
declarations.comment: part (6)

declarations.name: Stacks.LineBundle.Situation.isRegularSection_tautologicalSectionBase
declarations.doc:
The tautological global section of `p^*(L^{⊗ -1})` is a regular section, that is,
multiplication by it is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem Situation.isRegularSection_tautologicalSectionBase :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection D.totalSpace.sheaf.obj
      D.totalSpace.ringCatSheaf.property D.tautologicalSectionBaseSections
declarations.comment: part (1), the section is regular

declarations.name: Stacks.LineBundle.Situation.zeroScheme_tautologicalSectionBase_eq_ker_zeroSection
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0F96], the zero scheme.** Let `L` be an invertible module on a
scheme `X`, let `p : Tot(L) ⟶ X` be the associated line bundle and let `o : X ⟶ Tot(L)` be its
zero section. Then the closed subscheme `o(X)` of `Tot(L)` is the zero scheme of the tautological
global section of `p^*(L^{⊗ -1})`.

The hypotheses of [Stacks, Tag 0B74] that `X` be locally of finite type over a base scheme with
a dimension function are not needed and are omitted: clause (1) is a statement about the line
bundle alone.
declarations.statement:
theorem Situation.zeroScheme_tautologicalSectionBase_eq_ker_zeroSection :
    Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme D.totalSpace D.basePullbackInverse D.tautologicalSectionBase =
      D.zeroSection.ker
declarations.comment: part (1), the zero scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.LineBundle.Situation.isRegularSection_tautologicalSection
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0F96], regularity of the section.** The tautological global
section of `p^*(L^{⊗ -1})` is a regular section, that is, multiplication by it is injective:
its zero scheme is the image of the zero section, which is an effective Cartier divisor on the
total space by [Stacks, Tag 0B9D].
declarations.statement:
theorem Situation.isRegularSection_tautologicalSection :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection D.totalSpace.sheaf.obj
      D.totalSpace.ringCatSheaf.property
      (SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv D.pullbackInverse D.tautologicalSectionHom)
declarations.comment: part (1), the section is regular

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.TensorZeroScheme.pullbackTensorSection_proj
declarations.doc:
The pullback `p^*s` of the section to the zero scheme `L` of `z₁ ⊗ z₂ - q^*s`, read in
`p^*L₁ ⊗ p^*L₂`, is the product `s₁ ⊗ s₂` of the two restricted fibre coordinates.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackTensorSection_proj :
    pullbackTensorSection (proj Y L₁ L₂ s) L₁ L₂ s =
      tensorSectionsAt (spaceIdeal Y L₁ L₂ s).subscheme.sheaf.obj
        (spaceIdeal Y L₁ L₂ s).subscheme.ringCatSheaf.property (op ⊤)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (proj Y L₁ L₂ s)).obj L₁)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (proj Y L₁ L₂ s)).obj L₂)
        (section₁ Y L₁ L₂ s) (section₂ Y L₁ L₂ s)
declarations.comment: the construction and conditions (1), (3); (2) and (4)-(7) not proved here

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.TensorZeroScheme.exists_decomposition
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F97].** Let `Y` be a scheme, `L₁`, `L₂` invertible `𝒪_Y`-modules, `s` a
global section of `L₁ ⊗ L₂` and `i : D → Y` its zero scheme. There is a commutative diagram
`D₁ → L ← D₂` over `D → Y ← D`, with `p : L ⟶ Y`, and sections `sᵢ` of `p^*Lᵢ` such that
`p^*s = s₁ ⊗ s₂`; `p` is of finite type and flat of relative dimension `1`; `Dᵢ` is the zero
scheme of `sᵢ`; `Dᵢ ≅ \underline{\Spec}(\Sym^*(L_{3-i}^{⊗ -1})|_D)` over `D`;
`p^{-1}D = D₁ ∪ D₂`; `D₁ ∩ D₂ ⟶ D` is an isomorphism; and `D₁ ∩ D₂ ⟶ Dᵢ` is the zero section of
the line bundle `Dᵢ ⟶ D` (the record `Stacks.Chow.TensorZeroScheme.Decomposition`). Moreover the
formation of the diagram and of the sections commutes with arbitrary base change
(`Stacks.Chow.TensorZeroScheme.Decomposition.IsStableUnderBaseChange`).
declarations.statement: theorem exists_decomposition : ∃ R : Decomposition Y L₁ L₂ s, R.IsStableUnderBaseChange

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.TensorZeroScheme.gysinChowBranch₁_flatPullbackChowProj
declarations.doc:
In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0F97],

`i₁^* p^* α = p₁^* i^* α`  in  `A_{k+1}(D₁)`  for every  `α ∈ A_{k+1}(Y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinChowBranch₁_flatPullbackChowProj (α : Stacks.Chow.chowGroup C sY (k + 1)) :
    gysinChowBranch₁ C Y L₁ L₂ s R sY (k + 1)
        (flatPullbackChowProj C Y L₁ L₂ s R sY (k + 1) α) =
      flatPullbackChowProj₁ C Y L₁ L₂ s R sY k (gysinChowZeroIdeal C Y L₁ L₂ s sY k α)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.TensorZeroScheme.exists_principalReduction_isStableUnderBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F99].** For a scheme `X` locally of finite type over the base situation of
chapter 42 and a triple `(ℒ, s, i : D ⟶ X)` as in [Stacks, Tag 02T8] there is a commutative
square

  `D' --i'--> X'`
  `|p         |g`
  `D --i-->   X`

such that `p` and `g` are of finite type and flat of relative dimension `1`,
`p^* : A_k(D) ⟶ A_{k+1}(D')` is injective for all `k`, `D' ⊆ X'` is the zero scheme of a
global section of `𝒪_{X'}`, and `p^*i^* = (i')^*g^*`; and these properties remain true after
arbitrary base change by morphisms `Y ⟶ X` locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_principalReduction_isStableUnderBaseChange :
    ∃ R : PrincipalReduction C sX L s, R.IsStableUnderBaseChange

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.WeakCapRule.toBivariantClass
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F9A], a weak form of Fulton's Theorem 17.1.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation
02QL, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over `S` and let `p ∈ ℤ`.
A rule assigning to every morphism `Y' ⟶ Y` locally of finite type and every `k` a map
`c ∩ - : A_k(Y') ⟶ A_{k-p}(Y' ×_Y X)`, satisfying conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 0B76 and
condition (3) whenever `ℒ'|_{D'} ≅ 𝒪_{D'}` — a `Stacks.Chow.WeakCapRule` read against the
canonical Gysin system — is a bivariant class: an element of `A^p(X ⟶ Y)` with the same cap
operation (`Stacks.Chow.WeakCapRule.toBivariantClass_cap`).
declarations.statement:
def WeakCapRule.toBivariantClass (w : WeakCapRule C (canonicalGysinSystem C) sX sY f hf p) :
    CanonicalBivariantClass C sX sY f hf p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.degreeZeroPowerSum
declarations.doc: The zeroth power-sum polynomial is the rank variable `r`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev degreeZeroPowerSum : ChernPolynomial
declarations.comment: degree_zero_power_sum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coe_powerSumPolynomial_one
declarations.doc: The first power-sum polynomial is `c₁`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coe_powerSumPolynomial_one :
    (powerSumPolynomial 1 : MvPolynomial ℕ+ ℤ) = X (1 : ℕ+)
declarations.comment: first_four_power_sums

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coe_powerSumPolynomial_two
declarations.doc: The second power-sum polynomial is `c₁² - 2c₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coe_powerSumPolynomial_two :
    (powerSumPolynomial 2 : MvPolynomial ℕ+ ℤ) =
      X (1 : ℕ+) ^ 2 - 2 * X (2 : ℕ+)
declarations.comment: first_four_power_sums

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coe_powerSumPolynomial_three
declarations.doc: The third power-sum polynomial is `c₁³ - 3c₁c₂ + 3c₃`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coe_powerSumPolynomial_three :
    (powerSumPolynomial 3 : MvPolynomial ℕ+ ℤ) =
      X (1 : ℕ+) ^ 3 - 3 * X (1 : ℕ+) * X (2 : ℕ+) + 3 * X (3 : ℕ+)
declarations.comment: first_four_power_sums

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coe_powerSumPolynomial_four
declarations.doc: The fourth power-sum polynomial is `c₁⁴ - 4c₁²c₂ + 4c₁c₃ + 2c₂² - 4c₄`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coe_powerSumPolynomial_four :
    (powerSumPolynomial 4 : MvPolynomial ℕ+ ℤ) =
      X (1 : ℕ+) ^ 4 - 4 * X (1 : ℕ+) ^ 2 * X (2 : ℕ+) +
        4 * X (1 : ℕ+) * X (3 : ℕ+) + 2 * X (2 : ℕ+) ^ 2 - 4 * X (4 : ℕ+)
declarations.comment: first_four_power_sums

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.log_one_add_universalChernClassSum
declarations.doc:
In the completed rational graded ring, the logarithm of the universal total Chern class
is the signed generating series of the universal power-sum polynomials.
declarations.statement:
public theorem log_one_add_universalChernClassSum :
    PowerSeries.subst universalChernClassSum (PowerSeries.log ℚ) = powerSumSeries
declarations.comment: logarithmic_identity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eq_powerSumPolynomial_iff_eval_esymm
declarations.doc:
A weighted-homogeneous integral polynomial of positive degree `p` is the universal
power-sum polynomial precisely when substituting elementary symmetric polynomials in any
`n ≥ p` variables gives the sum of their `p`th powers.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eq_powerSumPolynomial_iff_eval_esymm
    (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p)
    (Q : weightedHomogeneousSubmodule ℤ (fun i : ℕ+ => (i : ℕ)) p) :
    Q = powerSumPolynomial p ↔
      ∀ n : ℕ, p ≤ n →
        eval₂Hom C (fun i : ℕ+ => esymm (Fin n) ℤ (i : ℕ))
            (Q : MvPolynomial ℕ+ ℤ) =
          psum (Fin n) ℤ p
declarations.comment: power_sum_characterization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.powerSumPolynomial
declarations.doc:
The universal power-sum polynomial `Pₚ` in the Chern-class variables `cᵢ`.

The variable indexed by `i : ℕ+` has weight `i`. Thus the value is packaged as a
weighted-homogeneous polynomial of degree `p`. For `p + 1`, the displayed recursion is
Newton's formula
`Pₚ₊₁ = ∑ᵢ₌₁ᵖ (-1)ⁱ⁻¹ cᵢ Pₚ₊₁₋ᵢ + (-1)ᵖ (p + 1) cₚ₊₁`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def powerSumPolynomial (p : ℕ) :
    weightedHomogeneousSubmodule ℤ (fun i : ℕ+ => (i : ℕ)) p
declarations.comment: power_sum_polynomials

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumComponentArbitraryRank_eq_add_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL, let `X` be locally of finite type over `S` and let
`0 ⟶ ℰ₁ ⟶ ℰ ⟶ ℰ₂ ⟶ 0` be a short exact sequence of finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules. Then for
every `p`

  `P_p(ℰ) = P_p(ℰ₁) + P_p(ℰ₂)`  in  `A^p(X)`,

where `P_p` is the universal power-sum polynomial of Stacks 0F9B evaluated at the Chern classes.
No constancy of the ranks is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePowerSumComponentArbitraryRank_eq_add_of_shortExact (p : ℕ) :
    modulePowerSumComponentArbitraryRank C sX S.X₂ p =
      modulePowerSumComponentArbitraryRank C sX S.X₁ p +
        modulePowerSumComponentArbitraryRank C sX S.X₃ p
declarations.comment: the source's more precise equality P_p(E) = P_p(E_1) + P_p(E_2), stated where the source states it: IN A^p(X), the degree-p Chow cohomology of Tag 0B7E at the Gysin system of the first Chern class of an invertible module (Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyComponent). A^*(X) = prod_{q >= 0} A^q(X) is the RING Stacks.Chow.TotalChowClass, whose product is the Cauchy product of the compositions A^i(X) x A^j(X) -> A^{i+j}(X) of Tag 0B75 (Stacks.Chow.TotalChowClass.instRing), so a polynomial in the Chern classes of a module is itself a bivariant class here; the Chern classes are the bivariant classes of Tag 0B7H, Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernClass, assembled into Stacks.Chow.totalChern. P_p is CONSTRUCTED, by the Newton recurrence of Tag 0F9B (AlgebraicGeometry.newtonPowerSum) applied to the homogeneous components of the total Chern class with the rank as degree-zero term, so P_0(E) is the rank as in the source's recursion. THE RANKS ARE ARBITRARY, exactly as in the source: only that the three terms are finite locally free is assumed, no rank is named, and the rank of a finite locally free module is locally constant, so X is decomposed into the open and closed loci where each rank is constant (Stacks.Chow.rankLocus) and the class is assembled over them by Tag 0FDZ as Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumArbitraryRank; Stacks.Chow.res_modulePowerSumArbitraryRank_of_constantRank identifies its restriction along any morphism of constant rank with the constant-rank power sum there, and the identity is read on a decomposition refining the rank decompositions of E_1 and of E_2. No filtration and no splitting of the sequence is supposed: the pulled-back sequence stays short exact with no flatness, a short exact sequence with finite locally free quotient being locally split. The splitting principle of the source is used only through the two results of the chapter it proves, both available here with no extra hypotheses: Tag 02UI on total classes (Stacks.Chow.totalChern_shortExact) and the commutativity of Chern classes of Tag 02UA (Stacks.Chow.commute_homComponent_totalChern). PROVED HERE: that those two give the additivity of every power sum, which is Newton's identities read as the single equation c . nu(c) = D(c) for the derivation D multiplying the index-m component by m

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.moduleChernCharacter_eq_add_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL, let `X` be locally of finite type over `S` and let
`0 ⟶ ℰ₁ ⟶ ℰ ⟶ ℰ₂ ⟶ 0` be a short exact sequence of finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules. Then

  `ch(ℰ) = ch(ℰ₁) + ch(ℰ₂)`.

Both sides lie in `∏_{p ≥ 0} (A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐)`, the rational Chow cohomology of `X` in which
Stacks 0ESX places the Chern character.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleChernCharacter_eq_add_of_shortExact :
    moduleChernCharacter C sX S.X₂ =
      moduleChernCharacter C sX S.X₁ + moduleChernCharacter C sX S.X₃
declarations.comment: the headline equality ch(E) = ch(E_1) + ch(E_2) for a short exact sequence 0 -> E_1 -> E -> E_2 -> 0 of finite locally free O_X-modules over X locally of finite type over the base of Situation 02QL. THE RANKS ARE ARBITRARY, exactly as in the source: only that the three terms are finite locally free is assumed and no rank is named. ch_p(F) = P_p(F)/p! is Stacks.Chow.moduleChernCharacterComponent, an element of A^p(X) tensor Q (Stacks.Chow.rationalChowCohomologyComponent) where A^p(X) is the degree-p Chow cohomology of Tag 0B7E -- the RATIONAL BIVARIANT group, not a ring of cap operators; the integral identity it is divided by holds in A^p(X) itself, in the bivariant ring A^*(X) = Stacks.Chow.TotalChowClass. ch(F) itself is Stacks.Chow.moduleChernCharacter, the family (ch_0(F), ch_1(F), ...) in the product prod_{p >= 0} (A^p(X) tensor Q), which is the home Tag 0ESX gives the Chern character, the degree in which it is concentrated being governed by a rank that is unbounded in general; addition there is degreewise, so an equality of two such families is an equality of Chern characters read in every degree at once, and Stacks.Chow.moduleChernCharacterComponent_eq_add_of_shortExact is that reading. It is derived from the source's more precise equality, Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumComponentArbitraryRank_eq_add_of_shortExact, by dividing by p!: the division of a sum by a scalar is term by term, so unlike Tag 0F9D no binomial coefficient intervenes. The splitting principle is NOT redone here; it enters only through Tag 02UI on total classes (Stacks.Chow.totalChern_shortExact) and the commutativity of Chern classes of Tag 02UA

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree_eq_add_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9C.** For a short exact sequence `0 ⟶ ℰ₁ ⟶ ℰ ⟶ ℰ₂ ⟶ 0` of finite locally free
`𝒪_X`-modules, of ranks that need not be constant, `P_p(ℰ) = P_p(ℰ₁) + P_p(ℰ₂)` for every `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree_eq_add_of_shortExact (S : ShortComplex X.Modules)
    (hS : S.ShortExact) [h₁ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} S.X₁]
    [h₃ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} S.X₃] (p : ℕ) :
    haveI := GenuineChern.isFiniteLocallyFree_of_shortExact S hS h₁ h₃
    powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree C sX S.X₂ p =
      powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree C sX S.X₁ p + powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree C sX S.X₃ p
declarations.comment: the precise form: P_p(E) = P_p(E_1) + P_p(E_2) in A^p(X), for every p >= 0, for a short exact sequence of finite locally free modules of arbitrary ranks; P_p is the polynomial of Stacks 0F9B in the Chern classes of Stacks 0B7H, assembled over the rank loci (Stacks 0ESW, 0FA7)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterOfFiniteLocallyFree_eq_add_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9C for the Chern character**: `ch(ℰ) = ch(ℰ₁) + ch(ℰ₂)`, degree by degree, for a
short exact sequence of finite locally free modules of arbitrary ranks.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernCharacterOfFiniteLocallyFree_eq_add_of_shortExact (S : ShortComplex X.Modules)
    (hS : S.ShortExact) [h₁ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} S.X₁]
    [h₃ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} S.X₃] (p : ℕ) :
    haveI := GenuineChern.isFiniteLocallyFree_of_shortExact S hS h₁ h₃
    chernCharacterOfFiniteLocallyFree C sX S.X₂ p =
      chernCharacterOfFiniteLocallyFree C sX S.X₁ p +
        chernCharacterOfFiniteLocallyFree C sX S.X₃ p
declarations.comment: ch(E) = ch(E_1) + ch(E_2), read in every degree p as ch_p = P_p/p! in A^p(X) ⊗ Q, for a short exact sequence of finite locally free modules of arbitrary ranks

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.powerSumCap_append
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9C, componentwise on cap products.** Let `0 → ℰ₁ → ℰ → ℰ₂ → 0` be a short exact
sequence of finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules, `ℰ₁` of rank `r` with a filtration whose
successive quotients are the invertible modules `ℒ_i = L i`, `ℰ₂` of rank `s` with quotients
`𝒩_j = N j`, and `ℰ` of rank `r + s` with the filtration obtained by juxtaposing them, whose
quotients `ℳ_k` are the `ℒ_i` followed by the `𝒩_j`. Then for every `n`-cycle `α` and every
`p ≥ 0`

  `P_p(ℰ) ∩ α = P_p(ℰ₁) ∩ α + P_p(ℰ₂) ∩ α`

in `A_{n-p}(X)`, which is the identity `P_p(ℰ) = P_p(ℰ₁) + P_p(ℰ₂)` of the source read against
`α`, and `ch(ℰ) = ch(ℰ₁) + ch(ℰ₂)` after dividing by `p!`. In degree one it is
`c₁(ℰ) ∩ α = c₁(ℰ₁) ∩ α + c₁(ℰ₂) ∩ α`, which is
`Stacks.Chow.chernClassCapExt_one_append`; in degree zero it is `r + s = r + s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem powerSumCap_append (hsub : ∀ i : Fin r, M (Fin.castAdd s i) ≅ L i)
    (hquot : ∀ j : Fin s, M (Fin.natAdd r j) ≅ N j) (k : ℕ) (α : chowGroup C p n) :
    powerSumCap C p n M hfacM k α
      = powerSumCap C p n L hfacL k α + powerSumCap C p n N hfacN k α
declarations.comment: componentwise on cap products, and conditional.  CORRECTION OF FORM: the source states P_p(E) = P_p(E_1) + P_p(E_2) in A^p(X) for a short exact sequence 0 -> E_1 -> E -> E_2 -> 0 of finite locally free O_X-modules, and ch(E) = ch(E_1) + ch(E_2) after dividing by p!. There is no bivariant ring here, so the identity is read degree by degree against a fixed cycle: for every n, every alpha in CycleGroup C p n and every p >= 0, P_p(E) cap alpha = P_p(E_1) cap alpha + P_p(E_2) cap alpha in A_{n-p}(X), each product of Chern classes being a COMPOSITE of operations on Chow groups, as Stacks 0FA6 reads c_1(F)^2. The module documentation gives both reasons. The division by p! is omitted only because it is a scalar. CARRIED: the three filtrations with invertible quotients L_i, N_j, M_k, Stacks 02TI for each quotient (hfacL, hfacN, hfacM), and hsub, hquot identifying the M_k with the L_i followed by the N_j -- the source's reduction of the short exact sequence, which it gets from Stacks 02UL and the injectivity of pi^* and which cannot be performed here. The Stacks 02UJ data needed to read the operator as P_p of the Chern classes of the module itself is carried not here but by Stacks.Chow.powerSumCap_one_eq_chernClassCapExt and Stacks.Chow.chernClassCapExt_one_append. PROVED HERE: the formal computation the source omits, in every degree and for every pair of ranks, as Stacks.Chow.powerSumRec_append; no commutativity is used, so Stacks 02TJ is not carried

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chernClassCapExt_one_append
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9C in degree one, entirely in Chern class cap products.** In the situation of
`Stacks.Chow.powerSumCap_append`, with `ℰ₁ = Q₁ r`, `ℰ₂ = Q₂ s` and `ℰ = Q (r + s)` the tops of
the three filtrations, for every `n`-cycle `α`

  `c₁(ℰ) ∩ α = c₁(ℰ₁) ∩ α + c₁(ℰ₂) ∩ α`

in `A_{n-1}(X)`. This is the degree-one case of Stacks 0F9C, `P_1` being `c_1`, with no
power-sum operator left in the statement: the three terms are the Chern class cap products of
Stacks 02U5 on the three modules themselves.

Each of the three sides is rewritten into its power-sum form by
`Stacks.Chow.powerSumCap_one_eq_chernClassCapExt`, which is Stacks 02UJ in degree one, and the
identity is then `Stacks.Chow.powerSumCap_append` in degree one.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernClassCapExt_one_append (hsub : ∀ i : Fin r, M (Fin.castAdd s i) ≅ L i)
    (hquot : ∀ j : Fin s, M (Fin.natAdd r j) ≅ N j)
    (QE : ℕ → X.Modules) (subE : ∀ k : Fin (r + s), M k ⟶ QE ((k : ℕ) + 1))
    (projE : ∀ k : Fin (r + s), QE ((k : ℕ) + 1) ⟶ QE (k : ℕ))
    (hzeroE : ∀ k : Fin (r + s), subE k ≫ projE k = 0)
    (hexactE : ∀ k : Fin (r + s), (ShortComplex.mk (subE k) (projE k) (hzeroE k)).ShortExact)
    (hrankE : ∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ r + s → PullbackPreservesRank (QE m) m)
    (chernE : ∀ m : ℕ, ChernClassCycleRule C m)
    (Q₁ : ℕ → X.Modules) (sub₁ : ∀ i : Fin r, L i ⟶ Q₁ ((i : ℕ) + 1))
    (proj₁ : ∀ i : Fin r, Q₁ ((i : ℕ) + 1) ⟶ Q₁ (i : ℕ))
    (hzero₁ : ∀ i : Fin r, sub₁ i ≫ proj₁ i = 0)
    (hexact₁ : ∀ i : Fin r, (ShortComplex.mk (sub₁ i) (proj₁ i) (hzero₁ i)).ShortExact)
    (hrank₁ : ∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ r → PullbackPreservesRank (Q₁ m) m)
    (chern₁ : ∀ m : ℕ, ChernClassCycleRule C m)
    (Q₂ : ℕ → X.Modules) (sub₂ : ∀ j : Fin s, N j ⟶ Q₂ ((j : ℕ) + 1))
    (proj₂ : ∀ j : Fin s, Q₂ ((j : ℕ) + 1) ⟶ Q₂ (j : ℕ))
    (hzero₂ : ∀ j : Fin s, sub₂ j ≫ proj₂ j = 0)
    (hexact₂ : ∀ j : Fin s, (ShortComplex.mk (sub₂ j) (proj₂ j) (hzero₂ j)).ShortExact)
    (hrank₂ : ∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ s → PullbackPreservesRank (Q₂ m) m)
    (chern₂ : ∀ m : ℕ, ChernClassCycleRule C m) (α : CycleGroup C p n)
    (hnormE : ∀ (m : ℕ) (hm : m ≤ r + s),
      chernClassCapExt C p n (QE m) m (hrankE m hm) (chernE m) 0 α =
        cycleClassDegreeZero C p n α)
    (hbinomE : ∀ k : Fin (r + s), ∀ i ≤ (k : ℕ) + 1,
      binomialTransform (inverseFirstChernCapStep C p n (M k) (hfacM k)) ((k : ℕ) + 1)
          (chernCapFamily C p n (QE ((k : ℕ) + 1)) ((k : ℕ) + 1) (hrankE ((k : ℕ) + 1) k.isLt)
            (chernE ((k : ℕ) + 1)) α) i =
        binomialTransform (inverseFirstChernCapStep C p n (M k) (hfacM k)) (k : ℕ)
          (chernCapFamily C p n (QE (k : ℕ)) (k : ℕ) (hrankE (k : ℕ) k.isLt.le)
            (chernE (k : ℕ)) α) i)
    (hnorm₁ : ∀ (m : ℕ) (hm : m ≤ r),
      chernClassCapExt C p n (Q₁ m) m (hrank₁ m hm) (chern₁ m) 0 α =
        cycleClassDegreeZero C p n α)
    (hbinom₁ : ∀ i : Fin r, ∀ t ≤ (i : ℕ) + 1,
      binomialTransform (inverseFirstChernCapStep C p n (L i) (hfacL i)) ((i : ℕ) + 1)
          (chernCapFamily C p n (Q₁ ((i : ℕ) + 1)) ((i : ℕ) + 1) (hrank₁ ((i : ℕ) + 1) i.isLt)
            (chern₁ ((i : ℕ) + 1)) α) t =
        binomialTransform (inverseFirstChernCapStep C p n (L i) (hfacL i)) (i : ℕ)
          (chernCapFamily C p n (Q₁ (i : ℕ)) (i : ℕ) (hrank₁ (i : ℕ) i.isLt.le)
            (chern₁ (i : ℕ)) α) t)
    (hnorm₂ : ∀ (m : ℕ) (hm : m ≤ s),
      chernClassCapExt C p n (Q₂ m) m (hrank₂ m hm) (chern₂ m) 0 α =
        cycleClassDegreeZero C p n α)
    (hbinom₂ : ∀ j : Fin s, ∀ t ≤ (j : ℕ) + 1,
      binomialTransform (inverseFirstChernCapStep C p n (N j) (hfacN j)) ((j : ℕ) + 1)
          (chernCapFamily C p n (Q₂ ((j : ℕ) + 1)) ((j : ℕ) + 1) (hrank₂ ((j : ℕ) + 1) j.isLt)
            (chern₂ ((j : ℕ) + 1)) α) t =
        binomialTransform (inverseFirstChernCapStep C p n (N j) (hfacN j)) (j : ℕ)
          (chernCapFamily C p n (Q₂ (j : ℕ)) (j : ℕ) (hrank₂ (j : ℕ) j.isLt.le)
            (chern₂ (j : ℕ)) α) t) :
    chernClassCapExt C p n (QE (r + s)) (r + s) (hrankE (r + s) le_rfl) (chernE (r + s)) 1 α
      = chernClassCapExt C p n (Q₁ r) r (hrank₁ r le_rfl) (chern₁ r) 1 α
        + chernClassCapExt C p n (Q₂ s) s (hrank₂ s le_rfl) (chern₂ s) 1 α
declarations.comment: the degree-one case, entirely in Chern class cap products, and conditional.  P_1 being c_1 (AlgebraicGeometry.coe_powerSumPolynomial_one), the identity P_p(E) = P_p(E_1) + P_p(E_2) reads c_1(E) cap alpha = c_1(E_1) cap alpha + c_1(E_2) cap alpha in A_{n-1}(X), for every n and every alpha in CycleGroup C p n, where E_1, E, E_2 are the tops of the three filtrations and the three terms are the cap products of Stacks 02U5 on those modules themselves. Read degree by degree for the reason given on Stacks.Chow.powerSumCap_append, of which this is the degree-one case and whose reduction it carries: the three filtrations as the towers Stacks 02UJ consumes, with hsub and hquot. ALSO CARRIED, each an input of Stacks 02UJ itself: chernE, chern1, chern2, the Stacks 02U0 component data; hnormE, hnorm1, hnorm2, the Stacks 02U0 normalisation c_0 = 1 along each tower; hbinomE, hbinom1, hbinom2, the equality of binomial transforms that Stacks 02UD gives once Stacks 02UG is applied; and hfacL, hfacN, hfacM, Stacks 02TI for c_1 of each quotient. Stacks 02TJ is NOT carried: the degree-one computation needs no commutativity

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.totalChernCharacterArbitraryRank_tensorObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9D, the headline identity.** Let `(S, δ)` be the situation of Stacks 02QL, let `X`
be locally of finite type over `S` and let `ℰ₁` and `ℰ₂` be finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules, of
no assumed rank. Then

  `ch(ℰ₁ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℰ₂) = ch(ℰ₁) ch(ℰ₂)`.

Both sides are power series over the rational bivariant ring `A^*(X) ⊗ 𝐐` whose degree-`p`
coefficient is `ch_p = P_p/p!`; multiplying two such series convolves their coefficients, so this
single identity is `Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterComponentArbitraryRank_tensorObj` in every degree at
once, and that in turn is `Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumArbitraryRank_tensorObj` divided by `p!`.
declarations.statement:
theorem totalChernCharacterArbitraryRank_tensorObj :
    totalChernCharacterArbitraryRank C sX (Scheme.Modules.tensorObj E₁ E₂)
      = totalChernCharacterArbitraryRank C sX E₁ * totalChernCharacterArbitraryRank C sX E₂
declarations.comment: the headline equality ch(E_1 tensor E_2) = ch(E_1) ch(E_2), with hypotheses EXACTLY the source's: Situation 02QL as the ChowSituation C, X locally of finite type over its base, and E_1, E_2 finite locally free O_X-modules -- NO rank is assumed, the predicate being AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree and not ...OfRank. The equality IS read in A^*(X) tensor Q: Stacks.Chow.rationalTotalChowClass is the ring Stacks.Chow.TotalChowClass of total Chow cohomology classes -- the product over q >= 0 of the groups A^q(X) of Stacks 0B7E, whose multiplication is the Cauchy product of the compositions of bivariant classes of Stacks 0B75 -- tensored over Z with Q so that p! is invertible, so each product ch_{p_1}(E_1) ch_{p_2}(E_2) is a composition of bivariant classes with rational coefficients. ch_p(F) = P_p(F)/p! is Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterComponentArbitraryRank and ch(F) itself is Stacks.Chow.totalChernCharacterArbitraryRank, the formal power series whose degree-p coefficient is ch_p(F): PowerSeries A is the product over p of copies of A under convolution, which is the home Stacks 0ESX gives the Chern character, the rank of F being unbounded, so an equality of these series is an equality of Chern characters in every degree at once and Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterComponentArbitraryRank_tensorObj is that reading. It is derived from the source's more precise equality, Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumArbitraryRank_tensorObj, by dividing by p!: the binomial coefficient disappears because C(p, p_1)/p! = 1/(p_1! p_2!) when p_1 + p_2 = p, which is Nat.add_choose_mul_factorial_mul_factorial. The rank decomposition and the splitting principle are PERFORMED by the cited theorem, not supposed; see its note

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumArbitraryRank_tensorObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9D, the source's more precise identity, in the bivariant ring.** Let `(S, δ)` be
the situation of Stacks 02QL, let `X` be locally of finite type over `S` and let `ℰ₁` and `ℰ₂` be
finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules, of no assumed rank. Then for every `p ≥ 0`

  `P_p(ℰ₁ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℰ₂) = ∑_{p₁ + p₂ = p} C(p, p₁) P_{p₁}(ℰ₁) P_{p₂}(ℰ₂)`

in `∏_{q ≥ 0} A^q(X)`, the bivariant ring of `X`, whose multiplication is the composition of
bivariant classes of Stacks 0B75. In degree zero the identity reads `rk(ℰ₁ ⊗ ℰ₂) = rk(ℰ₁) rk(ℰ₂)`
and in degree one `c₁(ℰ₁ ⊗ ℰ₂) = rk(ℰ₂) c₁(ℰ₁) + rk(ℰ₁) c₁(ℰ₂)`, both as locally constant
functions on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePowerSumArbitraryRank_tensorObj (p : ℕ) :
    modulePowerSumArbitraryRank C sX (Scheme.Modules.tensorObj E₁ E₂) p
      = ∑ q ∈ Finset.HasAntidiagonal.antidiagonal p,
          (p.choose q.1 : TotalChowClass C sX) *
            (modulePowerSumArbitraryRank C sX E₁ q.1 *
              modulePowerSumArbitraryRank C sX E₂ q.2)
declarations.comment: the source's more precise identity P_p(E_1 tensor E_2) = sum over p_1 + p_2 = p of binom(p, p_1) P_{p_1}(E_1) P_{p_2}(E_2), with hypotheses EXACTLY the source's: Situation 02QL as the ChowSituation C, X locally of finite type over its base, and E_1, E_2 finite locally free O_X-modules -- NO rank is assumed, the predicate being AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree and not ...OfRank. The identity is read IN THE BIVARIANT RING: Stacks.Chow.TotalChowClass is the product over q >= 0 of the Chow cohomology groups A^q(X) of Stacks 0B7E, whose multiplication is the Cauchy product of the composites of bivariant classes of Stacks 0B75 and whose unit is the identity class of Stacks 0FBS, so each product P_{p_1}(E_1) P_{p_2}(E_2) is a composition of bivariant classes and not a composite of cap operators; Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumComponentArbitraryRank_tensorObj reads the same identity in the single group A^p(X). P_p(F) is Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumArbitraryRank, Newton's recursion of Stacks 0F9B (AlgebraicGeometry.newtonPowerSum, which is the universal power-sum polynomial of that tag by AlgebraicGeometry.newtonPowerSum_eq_powerSumOfChernClasses) applied to the bivariant Chern classes c_i(F) of Stacks 0B7H, Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernClass, assembled over the rank loci of F by Stacks 0FDZ. THE RANK DECOMPOSITION IS PERFORMED, not assumed: the rank of a finite locally free module is locally constant (Stacks.Chow.moduleRank), its loci are open and closed and cover X (Stacks.Chow.isClopenDecomposition_rankLociFamily), the identity for two modules is read on the common refinement of their two decompositions (Stacks.Chow.eq_of_res_eq_of_constantModuleRanks), on a member of which E_1 tensor E_2 has constant rank r * s by Stacks 02U9, and restriction of total classes is a ring homomorphism. The constant-rank case is Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSum_tensorObj, obtained from Stacks.Chow.powerSumChernElem_tensorObj -- where the splitting principle of Stacks 02UL is performed -- read on EVERY test scheme g : T -> X for the pullbacks g^*E_1, g^*E_2 at once, which is what Stacks 0B76 needs for a bivariant class. The division by p! is omitted only because it is a scalar; Stacks.Chow.totalChernCharacterArbitraryRank_tensorObj performs it

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumComponentArbitraryRank_tensorObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9D, the source's more precise identity, read in `A^p(X)`.** An equality of two
elements of the Chow cohomology group `A^p(X)` of Stacks 0B7E: the class `P_p(ℰ₁ ⊗ ℰ₂)` is the
sum over `p₁ + p₂ = p` of the classes `C(p, p₁) P_{p₁}(ℰ₁) P_{p₂}(ℰ₂)` of `A^p(X)`, each formed
by the composition of bivariant classes of Stacks 0B75 inside the bivariant ring and read in
degree `p`. This is `Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumArbitraryRank_tensorObj` in degree `p`, the
components of a finite sum of total classes being the sum of their components.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePowerSumComponentArbitraryRank_tensorObj (p : ℕ) :
    modulePowerSumComponentArbitraryRank C sX (Scheme.Modules.tensorObj E₁ E₂) p
      = ∑ q ∈ Finset.HasAntidiagonal.antidiagonal p,
          ((p.choose q.1 : TotalChowClass C sX) *
            (modulePowerSumArbitraryRank C sX E₁ q.1 *
              modulePowerSumArbitraryRank C sX E₂ q.2)) p
declarations.comment: the same identity P_p(E_1 tensor E_2) = sum over p_1 + p_2 = p of binom(p, p_1) P_{p_1}(E_1) P_{p_2}(E_2) read as an equality of two elements of the SINGLE GROUP A^p(X) = Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyComponent of Stacks 0B7E at the Gysin system Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible of the genuine first Chern class, which is where the source states it. Hypotheses EXACTLY the source's: Situation 02QL as C, X locally of finite type over its base, E_1 and E_2 finite locally free with NO rank assumed. Each product on the right is formed in the bivariant ring Stacks.Chow.TotalChowClass, i.e. is a Cauchy product of the compositions of bivariant classes of Stacks 0B75, read in degree p, so the right-hand side is a sum over the antidiagonal of p of elements of A^p(X), which is the shape the source displays; the degree-p component of Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumArbitraryRank is Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumComponentArbitraryRank by definition. See Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSumArbitraryRank_tensorObj for the same identity in every degree at once and for how the rank decomposition and the splitting principle are performed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree_sheafTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9D.** For finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules `ℰ` and `ℱ`, of arbitrary ranks,

  `P_p(ℰ ⊗ ℱ) = ∑_{p₁ + p₂ = p} C(p, p₁) · P_{p₁}(ℰ) · P_{p₂}(ℱ)`

in the ring of total Chow cohomology classes of `X`, for every `p ≥ 0`. Along a morphism over
which both modules have constant rank this is `Stacks.Chow.powerSumTotal_sheafTensor`, and such
morphisms detect total classes (`Stacks.Chow.TotalChowClass.eq_of_res_eq_of_constantRank₂`).
declarations.statement:
theorem powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree_sheafTensor (p : ℕ) :
    haveI : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
        (R := X.ringCatSheaf) _ :=
        isFiniteLocallyFree_tensor hE hF
    powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree C sX (((sheafTensor X.sheaf).obj E).obj F) p =
      ∑ q ∈ antidiagonal p, (p.choose q.1 : ℤ) •
        (powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree C sX E q.1 * powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree C sX F q.2)
declarations.comment: the lemma as stated, for finite locally free E_1, E_2 of arbitrary ranks and every p >= 0, with no further hypothesis: P_p(E_1 tensor E_2) = sum over p_1 + p_2 = p of C(p, p_1) P_{p_1}(E_1) P_{p_2}(E_2), in the ring TotalChowClass C sX of total Chow cohomology classes (whose degree-p component is A^p(X)); P_p is the power sum of Stacks 0F9B assembled over the rank loci, powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree. The form ch(E_1 tensor E_2) = ch(E_1) ch(E_2) is Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterOfModule_sheafTensor

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalTotalChernCharacter_sheafTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9D for the Chern character**: `ch(ℰ ⊗ ℱ) = ch(ℰ) · ch(ℱ)` in
`∏_{p ≥ 0} A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐`, for finite locally free modules of arbitrary ranks.

In degree `m` both sides are computed on the lifts `∑_{p ≤ m} P_p/p!` of the two Chern characters
to `𝐐 ⊗ ∏_q A^q(X)` (`Stacks.Chow.RationalTotalChowClass.mul_apply_eq`); `P_p(ℰ) P_q(ℱ)` is
homogeneous of degree `p + q`, and the identity is
`Stacks.Chow.powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree_sheafTensor` divided by `m!`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalTotalChernCharacter_sheafTensor :
    haveI : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
        (R := X.ringCatSheaf) _ :=
        isFiniteLocallyFree_tensor hE hF
    rationalTotalChernCharacter C sX (((sheafTensor X.sheaf).obj E).obj F) =
      rationalTotalChernCharacter C sX E * rationalTotalChernCharacter C sX F
declarations.comment: the Chern character form ch(E_1 tensor E_2) = ch(E_1) ch(E_2), for finite locally free E_1, E_2 of arbitrary ranks, with no further hypothesis, in the ring Stacks.Chow.RationalTotalChowClass C sX = prod over p >= 0 of A^p(X) tensor Q with its Cauchy product; ch(E) is the family of the ch_p(E) = P_p(E)/p!

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.powerSumCap_lexFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9D, componentwise on cap products.** Let `ℰ₁` be finite locally free of rank `r`
with a filtration whose successive quotients are the invertible modules `ℒ_i = L i`, let `ℰ₂` be
finite locally free of rank `s` with quotients `𝒩_j = N j`, and let the filtration of
`ℰ₁ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℰ₂` be the lexicographic one of the source, of length `r·s`, whose `(i·s+j)`-th
quotient is `ℒ_i ⊗ 𝒩_j`. Then for every `n`-cycle `α` and every `p ≥ 0`

  `P_p(ℰ₁ ⊗ ℰ₂) ∩ α = ∑_{p₁ + p₂ = p} C(p, p₁) · (P_{p₁}(ℰ₁) ∘ P_{p₂}(ℰ₂)) ∩ α`

in `A_{n-p}(X)`, which is the identity
`P_p(ℰ₁ ⊗ ℰ₂) = ∑_{p₁+p₂=p} C(p,p₁) P_{p₁}(ℰ₁) P_{p₂}(ℰ₂)` of the source read against `α`, and
`ch(ℰ₁ ⊗ ℰ₂) = ch(ℰ₁) · ch(ℰ₂)` after dividing by `p!`, the binomial coefficients being what
`p! = p₁! · p₂! · C(p, p₁)` absorbs. Each product `P_{p₁}(ℰ₁) · P_{p₂}(ℰ₂)` is a composite of
operations on Chow groups, as `c₁(ℱ)²` is in Stacks 0FA6. In degree one, `P_0` being the rank,
the identity is `s·(c₁(ℰ₁) ∩ α) + r·(c₁(ℰ₂) ∩ α)`, the first displayed identity of
Stacks 0FA6.
declarations.statement:
theorem powerSumCap_lexFamily
    (hquot : ∀ (i : Fin r) (j : Fin s),
      M (finLexIndex i j) ≅ Scheme.Modules.tensorObj (L i) (N j))
    (hcommLN : ∀ (a : Fin r) (b : Fin s),
      FirstChernCapStepsCommute C p n (L a) (N b) (hfacL a) (hfacN b))
    (k : ℕ) (α : chowGroup C p n) :
    powerSumCap C p n M hfacM k α
      = ∑ q ∈ Finset.antidiagonal k, k.choose q.1 •
          evalChowGraded C p n α k
            (powerSumShift C p n L hfacL q.1 * powerSumShift C p n N hfacN q.2)
declarations.comment: componentwise on cap products, and conditional.  CORRECTION OF FORM: the source states P_p(E_1 tensor E_2) = sum over p_1 + p_2 = p of C(p, p_1) P_{p_1}(E_1) P_{p_2}(E_2) in A^p(X), and ch(E_1 tensor E_2) = ch(E_1) ch(E_2) after dividing by p!. There is no bivariant ring here, so the identity is read degree by degree against a fixed cycle, in A_{n-p}(X) for every n, every alpha in CycleGroup C p n and every p >= 0; every product of classes -- P_{p_1}(E_1) P_{p_2}(E_2) and the products inside each P_p -- is a COMPOSITE of operations on Chow groups, as Stacks 0FA6 reads c_1(F)^2. The module documentation gives both reasons. The division by p! is omitted only because it is a scalar. CARRIED: the three filtrations with invertible quotients, Stacks 02TI for each quotient (hfacL, hfacN, hfacM), and hquot, the source's lexicographic identification M_{i*s+j} iso L_i tensor N_j, which the source gets from Stacks 02UL and the injectivity of pi^* and which cannot be performed here; and Stacks 02TJ as hcommLN, genuinely needed because the binomial theorem applies to x_i + y_j only when those commute -- the members of one family need NOT commute among themselves, so hcommLL and hcommNN are not carried. Reading the operator as P_p of the Chern classes of the module itself uses the Stacks 02UJ data, carried by Stacks.Chow.powerSumCap_one_eq_chernClassCapExt. PROVED HERE: the formal computation the source omits, in every degree and for every pair of ranks, as Stacks.Chow.powerSumRec_lexFamily

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.HasDefinedChernClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9E (1).** The Chern classes of an object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` are **defined** when
some envelope `f : Y ⟶ X` has `Lf^*E` isomorphic to a locally bounded complex of finite locally
free `𝒪_Y`-modules.
declarations.statement: def HasDefinedChernClasses {X : Scheme.{u}} (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) : Prop
declarations.comment: clause (1): the condition under which the Chern classes of a perfect object are defined

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.perfectPowerSumComponent
declarations.doc:
**The class `P_p(E) ∈ A^p(X)`** of Stacks 0F9E (2), the degree-`p` component of
`Stacks.Chow.perfectPowerSum`.
declarations.statement:
def perfectPowerSumComponent (hE : HasDefinedChernClasses E) (p : ℕ) :
    chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (p : ℤ)
declarations.comment: clause (2), the class P_p(E) in A^p(X): the universal power sum of Tag 0F9B applied to c(E), with the alternating rank class r(E) as its degree-zero member. It restricts to P_p(E^bullet) along the envelope of every presentation, which is the property Tag 0GUD defines it by (Stacks.Chow.res_perfectPowerSumComponent)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.perfectChernCharacter
declarations.doc:
**The Chern character `ch(E) ∈ ∏_{p ≥ 0} (A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐)` of a perfect object whose Chern
classes are defined**, Stacks 0F9E (2), the family of its components.
declarations.statement:
def perfectChernCharacter (hE : HasDefinedChernClasses E) :
    fullRationalChowCohomology C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX
declarations.comment: clause (2), the class ch(E) in prod_{p >= 0} (A^p(X) tensor Q), componentwise as ch_p(E) = P_p(E)/p! as the source reads it

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.perfectChernClass
declarations.doc:
**The total Chern class `c(E)` of an object whose Chern classes are defined**, Stacks 0F9E
(2): the class of Stacks 0GUD, the unique total class of `X` whose restriction along the envelope
of a presentation of `E` is the total Chern class of the presenting complex. Its degree-`p`
component is `c_p(E)`.
declarations.statement: def perfectChernClass (hE : HasDefinedChernClasses E) : TotalChowClass C sX
declarations.comment: clause (2) for c(E): the class c(E) in prod_{p >= 0} A^p(X), carrying c_p(E) in degree p, for an object of D(O_X) whose Chern classes are defined in the sense of clause (1). Stacks.Chow.res_perfectChernClass pins it down at every envelope presentation, which is how Lemma 0GUD characterizes it. The two further classes clause (2) names are ch(E) (Stacks.Chow.perfectChernCharacter) and P_p(E) (Stacks.Chow.perfectPowerSumComponent)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.hasDefinedChernClasses_triangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9F, definedness.** Let `E₁ ⟶ E₂ ⟶ E₃ ⟶ E₁[1]` be a distinguished triangle of
perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)` satisfying one of the conditions of Stacks 0F9F. Then the Chern
classes of `E₁`, `E₂` and `E₃` are defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasDefinedChernClasses_triangle :
    HasDefinedChernClasses T.obj₁ ∧ HasDefinedChernClasses T.obj₂ ∧
      HasDefinedChernClasses T.obj₃
declarations.comment: the Chern classes of E₁, E₂, E₃ are defined

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.perfectChernClass_triangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9F, the total Chern class.** Under the hypotheses of Stacks 0F9F,
`c(E₂) = c(E₁) c(E₃)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfectChernClass_triangle (d₁ : HasDefinedChernClasses T.obj₁)
    (d₂ : HasDefinedChernClasses T.obj₂) (d₃ : HasDefinedChernClasses T.obj₃) :
    perfectChernClass C sX d₂ = perfectChernClass C sX d₁ * perfectChernClass C sX d₃
declarations.comment: c(E₂) = c(E₁) c(E₃)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.perfectChernCharacter_triangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9F, the Chern character.** Under the hypotheses of Stacks 0F9F,
`ch(E₂) = ch(E₁) + ch(E₃)`, in every degree `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfectChernCharacter_triangle (d₁ : HasDefinedChernClasses T.obj₁)
    (d₂ : HasDefinedChernClasses T.obj₂) (d₃ : HasDefinedChernClasses T.obj₃) (p : ℕ) :
    perfectChernCharacterComponent C sX d₂ p =
      perfectChernCharacterComponent C sX d₁ p + perfectChernCharacterComponent C sX d₃ p
declarations.comment: ch(E₂) = ch(E₁) + ch(E₃), in every degree

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.perfectPowerSum_triangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9F, the power sums.** Under the hypotheses of Stacks 0F9F,
`P_p(E₂) = P_p(E₁) + P_p(E₃)` for every `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfectPowerSum_triangle (d₁ : HasDefinedChernClasses T.obj₁)
    (d₂ : HasDefinedChernClasses T.obj₂) (d₃ : HasDefinedChernClasses T.obj₃) (p : ℕ) :
    perfectPowerSum C sX d₂ p = perfectPowerSum C sX d₁ p + perfectPowerSum C sX d₃ p
declarations.comment: P_p(E₂) = P_p(E₁) + P_p(E₃)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.hasDefinedChernClasses_and_additive_of_envelope
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9F under condition (1) of the source.** Let `T` be a distinguished triangle of
`D(𝒪_X)`. If there is an envelope `f : Y ⟶ X` such that `Lf^*T.mor₁ : Lf^*E₁ ⟶ Lf^*E₂` is
represented by a map `α : 𝓔₁^• ⟶ 𝓔₂^•` of locally bounded complexes of finite locally free
`𝒪_Y`-modules, then the Chern classes of `E₁`, `E₂`, `E₃` are defined and

  `c(E₂) = c(E₁) c(E₃)`,  `ch_p(E₂) = ch_p(E₁) + ch_p(E₃)`,  `P_p(E₂) = P_p(E₁) + P_p(E₃)`.

The cone of `α` is a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules representing
`Lf^*E₃`, so `f` together with `𝓔₁^•`, `𝓔₂^•` and `C(α)^•` presents all three objects, and each
identity is the corresponding identity for those complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasDefinedChernClasses_and_additive_of_envelope
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules))
    (hT : T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory X.Modules))
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : IsEnvelope f)
    {P₁ P₂ : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℤ} (α : P₁ ⟶ P₂)
    (h₁ : IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree P₁) (h₂ : IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree P₂)
    (e₁ : (Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj T.obj₁ ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P₁)
    (e₂ : (Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj T.obj₂ ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P₂)
    (hα : e₁.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map α =
      (Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        f.toLRSHom.toShHom).map T.mor₁ ≫ e₂.hom) :
    TriangleChernAdditive C sX T
declarations.comment: condition (1): there is an envelope f : Y -> X such that Lf^*E_1 -> Lf^*E_2 is represented by a map of locally bounded complexes of finite locally free O_Y-modules. The conclusion is the whole one: the Chern classes of E_1, E_2 and E_3 are defined, c(E_2) = c(E_1)c(E_3), ch(E_2) = ch(E_1) + ch(E_3) and P_p(E_2) = P_p(E_1) + P_p(E_3), the last two read componentwise in A^p(X) tensor Q and in A^p(X) as the source reads them. Perfectness of the three objects is a standing hypothesis of the source that no step of this proof uses, so it is omitted, exactly as for the criteria of Tag 0GUE

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.hasDefinedChernClasses_and_additive_of_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9F under condition (2) of the source.** If the first map `T.mor₁ : E₁ ⟶ E₂` of a
distinguished triangle of `D(𝒪_X)` is itself represented by a map `α : 𝓔₁^• ⟶ 𝓔₂^•` of locally
bounded complexes of finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules, then the Chern classes of `E₁`, `E₂`,
`E₃` are defined and

  `c(E₂) = c(E₁) c(E₃)`,  `ch_p(E₂) = ch_p(E₁) + ch_p(E₃)`,  `P_p(E₂) = P_p(E₁) + P_p(E₃)`.

This is condition (1) for the envelope `𝟙 X`, which is proper and completely decomposed; the
square identifying `α` with `T.mor₁` transports along the naturality of `L(𝟙 X)^* ≅ 𝟭`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasDefinedChernClasses_and_additive_of_map
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules))
    (hT : T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory X.Modules))
    {P₁ P₂ : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ} (α : P₁ ⟶ P₂)
    (h₁ : IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree P₁) (h₂ : IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree P₂)
    (i₁ : T.obj₁ ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P₁) (i₂ : T.obj₂ ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P₂)
    (hα : i₁.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map α = T.mor₁ ≫ i₂.hom) :
    TriangleChernAdditive C sX T
declarations.comment: condition (2): E_1 -> E_2 is represented by a map of locally bounded complexes of finite locally free O_X-modules. The conclusion is the whole one: the Chern classes of E_1, E_2 and E_3 are defined, c(E_2) = c(E_1)c(E_3), ch(E_2) = ch(E_1) + ch(E_3) and P_p(E_2) = P_p(E_1) + P_p(E_3), the last two read componentwise in A^p(X) tensor Q and in A^p(X) as the source reads them. Perfectness of the three objects is a standing hypothesis of the source that no step of this proof uses, so it is omitted, exactly as for the criteria of Tag 0GUE

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.triangleChernAdditive_of_isCompact_irreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F9F] under condition (3) of the source.** Let `T` be a distinguished triangle
of `D(𝒪_X)` whose first two objects are perfect and let the irreducible components of `X`, which
is locally of finite type over the base of the Chow situation, be quasi-compact. Then the Chern
classes of `E₁`, `E₂`, `E₃` are defined and

  `c(E₂) = c(E₁) c(E₃)`,  `ch_p(E₂) = ch_p(E₁) + ch_p(E₃)`,  `P_p(E₂) = P_p(E₁) + P_p(E₃)`.

`X` is locally Noetherian, the base being locally Noetherian and `X` locally of finite type over
it, so `Stacks.Chow.exists_isEnvelope_sigma_of_isCompact_irreducibleComponents` supplies an
envelope `∐ W ⟶ X` whose summands are Noetherian — hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated —
with the resolution property and affine diagonal. On such a source
`Stacks.Chow.exists_boundedFiniteLocallyFree_sigma_of_isPerfect` presents `Lf^*E₁` and `Lf^*E₂`
by complexes whose summandwise restrictions are bounded complexes of finite locally free
modules, and `Stacks.Chow.exists_isLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree_square_sigma` represents
`Lf^*E₁ ⟶ Lf^*E₂` by a map of locally bounded complexes of finite locally free modules together
with the commuting square. That is condition (1) of the source, in the shape
`Stacks.Chow.hasDefinedChernClasses_and_additive_of_envelope` asks for.

Every hypothesis is a hypothesis of the source: the Chow situation, `X` locally of finite type
over its base, the distinguished triangle, perfectness of `E₁` and `E₂`, and quasi-compactness
of the irreducible components of `X`. Local Noetherianity, the envelope, the summands'
resolution property and affine diagonal, the two complexes and the map between them are all
derived. Perfectness of `E₃` is a standing hypothesis of the source that no step of this proof
uses, so it is omitted.
declarations.statement:
theorem triangleChernAdditive_of_isCompact_irreducibleComponents
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules)) (hT : T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory X.Modules))
    (h₁ : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) T.obj₁)
    (h₂ : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) T.obj₂)
    (hqc : ∀ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X, IsCompact Z) :
    TriangleChernAdditive C sX T
declarations.comment: condition (3): the irreducible components of X are quasi-compact.  The conclusion is the whole one: the Chern classes of E_1, E_2 and E_3 are defined, c(E_2) = c(E_1)c(E_3), ch(E_2) = ch(E_1) + ch(E_3) and P_p(E_2) = P_p(E_1) + P_p(E_3), the last two read componentwise in A^p(X) tensor Q and in A^p(X) as the source reads them. The hypotheses are exactly the source's: the base situation of Tag 02QL, X locally of finite type over its base, the distinguished triangle, perfectness of E_1 and E_2, and the irreducible components of X quasi-compact. Perfectness of E_3 is a standing hypothesis of the source that no step of this proof uses, so it is omitted, exactly as for conditions (1), (2) and (4)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.triangleChernAdditive_of_compactSpace
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F9F] under condition (4) of the source.** Let `T` be a
distinguished triangle of `D(𝒪_X)` whose first two objects are perfect and let `X`, which is
locally of finite type over the base of the Chow situation, be quasi-compact. Then the Chern
classes of `E₁`, `E₂`, `E₃` are defined and

  `c(E₂) = c(E₁) c(E₃)`,  `ch_p(E₂) = ch_p(E₁) + ch_p(E₃)`,  `P_p(E₂) = P_p(E₁) + P_p(E₃)`.

`X` is Noetherian, the base being locally Noetherian, hence quasi-separated, so
[Stacks, Tag 0GTU] gives an envelope `f : Y ⟶ X` with `Y` carrying an ample family of invertible
modules; `Y` is Noetherian because `f` is proper, has the resolution property by
`Stacks.Chow.hasResolutionProperty_of_isAmpleFamily_of_isNoetherian`, and therefore has affine
diagonal by the Noetherian case of [Stacks, Tag 0F8C]. That is condition (1) of the source, in
the shape `Stacks.Chow.triangleChernAdditive_of_resolutionProperty_envelope` asks for.

Every hypothesis is a hypothesis of the source: the Chow situation, `X` locally of finite type
over its base, the distinguished triangle, perfectness of `E₁` and `E₂`, and quasi-compactness
of `X`. Quasi-separatedness, Noetherianity, the envelope, the ample family, the resolution
property and the affine diagonal are all derived. Perfectness of `E₃` is a standing hypothesis
of the source that no step of this proof uses, so it is omitted.
declarations.statement:
theorem triangleChernAdditive_of_compactSpace
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    [CompactSpace X]
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules)) (hT : T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory X.Modules))
    (h₁ : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) T.obj₁)
    (h₂ : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) T.obj₂) :
    TriangleChernAdditive C sX T
declarations.comment: condition (4): X is quasi-compact.  The conclusion is the whole one: the Chern classes of E_1, E_2 and E_3 are defined, c(E_2) = c(E_1)c(E_3), ch(E_2) = ch(E_1) + ch(E_3) and P_p(E_2) = P_p(E_1) + P_p(E_3), the last two read componentwise in A^p(X) tensor Q and in A^p(X) as the source reads them. Perfectness of E_3 is a standing hypothesis of the source that no step of this proof uses, so it is omitted, exactly as for conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.existsUnique_localizedChernClassOfClosedCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9H, for the Chern classes.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over `S`, let
`i_j : X_j ⟶ X` be closed immersions with `X = X₁ ∪ X₂` set theoretically, and let `E₂` be a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_{X₂})` whose Chern classes are defined and such that `E₂|_{X₁ ∩ X₂}` is
isomorphic to a finite locally free `𝒪_{X₁ ∩ X₂}`-module of rank `< p` sitting in cohomological
degree `0`. Then there is a unique bivariant class `c'_p(E₂) ∈ A^p(X₂ ⟶ X)` such that, on every
test scheme `g : X' ⟶ X` locally of finite type, with `i'_j : X'_j = X_j ×_X X' ⟶ X'`,

  `c'_p(E₂) ∩ i'_{2,*} α₂ = c_p(E₂) ∩ α₂`  and  `c'_p(E₂) ∩ i'_{1,*} α₁ = 0`

for all `α_j ∈ CH_k(X'_j)`; it is `Stacks.Chow.localizedChernClassOfClosedCover`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_localizedChernClassOfClosedCover
    (_perfect : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} (X := X₂.toRingedSpace) E₂)
    (hres : ∃ M : (pullback i₁ i₂).Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M p ∧
      Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
          (pullback.snd i₁ i₂).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E₂ ≅
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (pullback i₁ i₂).Modules 0).obj M)) :
    ∃! c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (i₂ ≫ sX) sX i₂ rfl (p : ℤ),
      (∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (α : chowGroup C (pullback.fst i₂ g ≫ i₂ ≫ sX) k),
        c.cap g k (chowPush C (pullback.fst i₂ g ≫ i₂ ≫ sX) (g ≫ sX) (pullback.snd i₂ g)
            (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (i₂ ≫ sX) sX i₂ rfl g) k α) =
          (perfectChernClass C (i₂ ≫ sX) hE₂ p).idRule C (i₂ ≫ sX) (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
            (pullback.fst i₂ g) k α) ∧
      (∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (α : chowGroup C (pullback.fst i₁ g ≫ i₁ ≫ sX) k),
        c.cap g k (chowPush C (pullback.fst i₁ g ≫ i₁ ≫ sX) (g ≫ sX) (pullback.snd i₁ g)
            (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (i₁ ≫ sX) sX i₁ rfl g) k α) = 0)
declarations.comment: the class c'_p(E₂) ∈ A^p(X₂ ⟶ X), existence and uniqueness of the bivariant class characterized by the two identities on every base change X' ⟶ X, for E₂|_{X₁ ∩ X₂} finite locally free of rank < p in degree 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.existsUnique_localizedPowerSumOfClosedCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9H, for the classes `P_p`.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over `S`, let
`i_j : X_j ⟶ X` be closed immersions with `X = X₁ ∪ X₂` set theoretically, and let `E₂` be a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_{X₂})` whose Chern classes are defined and whose restriction
`E₂|_{X₁ ∩ X₂}` is zero. Then there is a unique bivariant class `P'_p(E₂) ∈ A^p(X₂ ⟶ X)` such
that, on every test scheme `g : X' ⟶ X` locally of finite type, with
`i'_j : X'_j = X_j ×_X X' ⟶ X'`,

  `P'_p(E₂) ∩ i'_{2,*} α₂ = P_p(E₂) ∩ α₂`  and  `P'_p(E₂) ∩ i'_{1,*} α₁ = 0`

for all `α_j ∈ CH_k(X'_j)`; it is `Stacks.Chow.localizedPowerSumOfClosedCover`. Here `P_p(E₂)` is
the class of Definition 0F9E (2), `Stacks.Chow.perfectPowerSumComponent`: the class of Stacks 0GUD
which restricts along every envelope presentation `(f, 𝓔^•)` of `E₂` to `∑ (-1)^n P_p(𝓔^n)`
(`Stacks.Chow.existsUnique_perfectPowerSum`).
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_localizedPowerSumOfClosedCover
    (perfect : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} (X := X₂.toRingedSpace) E₂)
    (hzero : IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      (pullback.snd i₁ i₂).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E₂)) :
    ∃! c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (i₂ ≫ sX) sX i₂ rfl (p : ℤ),
      (∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (α : chowGroup C (pullback.fst i₂ g ≫ i₂ ≫ sX) k),
        c.cap g k (chowPush C (pullback.fst i₂ g ≫ i₂ ≫ sX) (g ≫ sX) (pullback.snd i₂ g)
            (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (i₂ ≫ sX) sX i₂ rfl g) k α) =
          (perfectPowerSumComponent C (i₂ ≫ sX) hE₂ p).idRule C (i₂ ≫ sX)
            (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.fst i₂ g) k α) ∧
      (∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (α : chowGroup C (pullback.fst i₁ g ≫ i₁ ≫ sX) k),
        c.cap g k (chowPush C (pullback.fst i₁ g ≫ i₁ ≫ sX) (g ≫ sX) (pullback.snd i₁ g)
            (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (i₁ ≫ sX) sX i₁ rfl g) k α) = 0)
declarations.comment: the class P'_p(E₂) ∈ A^p(X₂ ⟶ X), existence and uniqueness of the bivariant class characterized by the two identities on every base change X' ⟶ X, for E₂|_{X₁ ∩ X₂} zero

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.closedCoverPowerSum
declarations.doc:
Let `i₁ : X₁ ⟶ X` and `i₂ : X₂ ⟶ X` be closed immersions whose images cover `X`, and let
`E₂ ∈ D(𝒪_{X₂})` have defined Chern classes and restrict to zero on `X₁ ×_X X₂`. The class
`P'_p(E₂) ∈ A^p(X₂ ⟶ X)` is the extension of `P_p(E₂) ∈ A^p(X₂)` along the closed cover
(`Stacks.Chow.closedCoverExtension`): on a test scheme `T ⟶ X`, writing a class as
`j_{1,*} α₁ + j_{2,*} α₂` along the base-changed cover, `P'_p(E₂) ∩ α = P_p(E₂) ∩ α₂`.
declarations.statement:
def closedCoverPowerSum (hcover : Set.range i₁ ∪ Set.range i₂ = Set.univ)
    (hzero : IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      (pullback.snd i₁ i₂).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E₂)) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX₂ sX i₂ hi₂ p
declarations.comment: the class P'_p(E₂) in A^p(X₂ ⟶ X), for E₂ restricting to zero on X₁ ∩ X₂

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.closedCoverChernClass
declarations.doc:
Let `i₁ : X₁ ⟶ X` and `i₂ : X₂ ⟶ X` be closed immersions whose images cover `X`, and let
`E₂ ∈ D(𝒪_{X₂})` have defined Chern classes and restrict on `X₁ ×_X X₂` to a finite locally free
module of rank `< p` in degree `0`. The class `c'_p(E₂) ∈ A^p(X₂ ⟶ X)` is the extension of
`c_p(E₂) ∈ A^p(X₂)` along the closed cover (`Stacks.Chow.closedCoverExtension`): on a test scheme
`T ⟶ X`, writing a class as `j_{1,*} α₁ + j_{2,*} α₂` along the base-changed cover,
`c'_p(E₂) ∩ α = c_p(E₂) ∩ α₂`.
declarations.statement:
def closedCoverChernClass (hcover : Set.range i₁ ∪ Set.range i₂ = Set.univ)
    (hrank : ∃ M : (pullback i₁ i₂).Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M p ∧
      Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        (pullback.snd i₁ i₂).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E₂ ≅
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M)) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX₂ sX i₂ hi₂ p
declarations.comment: the class c'_p(E₂) in A^p(X₂ ⟶ X), for E₂ restricting on X₁ ∩ X₂ to a finite locally free module of rank < p in degree 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isClosedCoverExtension_closedCoverPowerSum
declarations.doc:
On every test scheme `g : T ⟶ X` locally of finite type, `P'_p(E₂)` caps the classes pushed
forward from `T ×_X X₂` as `P_p(E₂)` does, and kills the classes pushed forward from `T ×_X X₁`:
`P'_p(E₂) ∩ i_{2,*} α₂ = P_p(E₂) ∩ α₂` and `P'_p(E₂) ∩ i_{1,*} α₁ = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedCoverExtension_closedCoverPowerSum :
    IsClosedCoverExtension C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX i₁ i₂ sX₂ hi₂
      (perfectPowerSumComponent C sX₂ hE₂ p)
      (closedCoverPowerSum C sX i₁ i₂ sX₂ hi₂ hE₂ p hcover hzero)
declarations.comment: the two formulas P'_p(E₂) ∩ i_{2,*} α₂ = P_p(E₂) ∩ α₂ and P'_p(E₂) ∩ i_{1,*} α₁ = 0, after every base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.eq_closedCoverPowerSum_of_isClosedCoverExtension
declarations.doc:
A class of `A^p(X₂ ⟶ X)` satisfying the two formulas `c ∩ i_{2,*} α₂ = P_p(E₂) ∩ α₂` and
`c ∩ i_{1,*} α₁ = 0` after every base change is `P'_p(E₂)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_closedCoverPowerSum_of_isClosedCoverExtension
    {c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX₂ sX i₂ hi₂ p}
    (hc : IsClosedCoverExtension C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX i₁ i₂ sX₂ hi₂
      (perfectPowerSumComponent C sX₂ hE₂ p) c) :
    c = closedCoverPowerSum C sX i₁ i₂ sX₂ hi₂ hE₂ p hcover hzero
declarations.comment: uniqueness: P'_p(E₂) is the only class satisfying the two formulas after every base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isClosedCoverExtension_closedCoverChernClass
declarations.doc:
On every test scheme `g : T ⟶ X` locally of finite type, `c'_p(E₂)` caps the classes pushed
forward from `T ×_X X₂` as `c_p(E₂)` does, and kills the classes pushed forward from `T ×_X X₁`:
`c'_p(E₂) ∩ i_{2,*} α₂ = c_p(E₂) ∩ α₂` and `c'_p(E₂) ∩ i_{1,*} α₁ = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedCoverExtension_closedCoverChernClass :
    IsClosedCoverExtension C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX i₁ i₂ sX₂ hi₂
      (perfectChernClass C sX₂ hE₂ p)
      (closedCoverChernClass C sX i₁ i₂ sX₂ hi₂ hE₂ p hcover hrank)
declarations.comment: the two formulas c'_p(E₂) ∩ i_{2,*} α₂ = c_p(E₂) ∩ α₂ and c'_p(E₂) ∩ i_{1,*} α₁ = 0, after every base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.eq_closedCoverChernClass_of_isClosedCoverExtension
declarations.doc:
A class of `A^p(X₂ ⟶ X)` satisfying the two formulas `c ∩ i_{2,*} α₂ = c_p(E₂) ∩ α₂` and
`c ∩ i_{1,*} α₁ = 0` after every base change is `c'_p(E₂)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_closedCoverChernClass_of_isClosedCoverExtension
    {c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX₂ sX i₂ hi₂ p}
    (hc : IsClosedCoverExtension C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX i₁ i₂ sX₂ hi₂
      (perfectChernClass C sX₂ hE₂ p) c) :
    c = closedCoverChernClass C sX i₁ i₂ sX₂ hi₂ hE₂ p hcover hrank
declarations.comment: uniqueness: c'_p(E₂) is the only class satisfying the two formulas after every base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pushforward_localizedPowerSumOfClosedCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9I, for the classes `P_p`.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over `S`, let
`i_j : X_j ⟶ X` be closed immersions with `X = X₁ ∪ X₂` set theoretically, and let `E` be a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` whose Chern classes are defined and whose restriction `E|_{X₁}` is
zero. Then `E₂ = E|_{X₂}` satisfies the hypotheses of Stacks 0F9H with `E₂|_{X₁ ∩ X₂}` zero, and

  `i_{2,*} ∘ P'_p(E₂) = P_p(E)`   in   `A^p(X)`,

where `P'_p(E₂) ∈ A^p(X₂ ⟶ X)` is the class of Stacks 0F9H
(`Stacks.Chow.localizedPowerSumOfClosedCover`), `i_{2,*} ∘ -` is the pushforward of
Stacks 0EPK and `P_p(E)` is the class of Definition 0F9E (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforward_localizedPowerSumOfClosedCover
    (perfect : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (hzero : IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      i₁.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E)) :
    canonicalBivariantProperPushforward C (i₂ ≫ sX) sX sX i₂ (𝟙 X) rfl (Category.id_comp sX)
        (p : ℤ)
        (bivariantClassCongr C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (i₂ ≫ sX) sX
          (Category.comp_id i₂).symm rfl
          (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq rfl (Category.id_comp sX)) (p : ℤ)
