          (localizedPowerSumOfClosedCover C sX i₁ i₂ hcover
            (hasDefinedChernClasses_derivedPullback i₂ hE) p
            (isPerfect_restriction i₂ perfect)
            (isZero_restriction_intersection i₁ i₂ hzero))) =
      perfectPowerSumComponent C sX hE p
declarations.comment: the classes P'_p: i_{2,*} ∘ P'_p(E₂) = P_p(E) for E|_{X₁} zero

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pushforward_localizedChernClassOfClosedCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9I, for the Chern classes.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over `S`, let
`i_j : X_j ⟶ X` be closed immersions with `X = X₁ ∪ X₂` set theoretically, and let `E` be a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` whose Chern classes are defined and whose restriction `E|_{X₁}` is
isomorphic to a finite locally free `𝒪_{X₁}`-module of rank `< p` sitting in cohomological
degree `0`. Then `E₂ = E|_{X₂}` satisfies the hypotheses of Stacks 0F9H with `E₂|_{X₁ ∩ X₂}`
finite locally free of rank `< p` in degree `0`, and

  `i_{2,*} ∘ c'_p(E₂) = c_p(E)`   in   `A^p(X)`,

where `c'_p(E₂) ∈ A^p(X₂ ⟶ X)` is the class of Stacks 0F9H
(`Stacks.Chow.localizedChernClassOfClosedCover`), `i_{2,*} ∘ -` is the pushforward of
Stacks 0EPK and `c_p(E)` is the class of Definition 0F9E (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforward_localizedChernClassOfClosedCover
    (_perfect : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (hres : ∃ M : X₁.Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M p ∧
      Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
          i₁.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X₁.Modules 0).obj M)) :
    canonicalBivariantProperPushforward C (i₂ ≫ sX) sX sX i₂ (𝟙 X) rfl (Category.id_comp sX)
        (p : ℤ)
        (bivariantClassCongr C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (i₂ ≫ sX) sX
          (Category.comp_id i₂).symm rfl
          (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq rfl (Category.id_comp sX)) (p : ℤ)
          (localizedChernClassOfClosedCover C sX i₁ i₂ hcover
            (hasDefinedChernClasses_derivedPullback i₂ hE) p
            (exists_iso_single_restriction_intersection i₁ i₂ p hres))) =
      perfectChernClass C sX hE p
declarations.comment: the classes c'_p: i_{2,*} ∘ c'_p(E₂) = c_p(E) for E|_{X₁} finite locally free of rank < p in degree 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardChowCohomology_closedCoverPowerSum
declarations.doc:
Let `i₁ : X₁ ⟶ X` and `i₂ : X₂ ⟶ X` be closed immersions whose images cover `X`, and let
`E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` have defined Chern classes and restrict to zero on `X₁`. Let `E₂ = E|_{X₂}` be as in
Stacks 0F9H: it restricts to zero on `X₁ ×_X X₂`, and its Chern classes are defined by
`Stacks.Chow.HasDefinedChernClasses.derivedPullback`. Then `i_{2,*} ∘ P'_p(E₂) = P_p(E)` in
`A^p(X)`, with `i_{2,*} ∘ -` the pushforward of Stacks 0EPK.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforwardChowCohomology_closedCoverPowerSum
    (hcover : Set.range i₁ ∪ Set.range i₂ = Set.univ)
    (hzero : IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      i₁.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E))
    (hzero₂ : IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      (pullback.snd i₁ i₂).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
          i₂.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E))) :
    properPushforwardChowCohomology C sX (i₂ ≫ sX) i₂ rfl
        (closedCoverPowerSum C sX i₁ i₂ (i₂ ≫ sX) rfl (hE.derivedPullback i₂) p hcover
          hzero₂) =
      perfectPowerSumComponent C sX hE p
declarations.comment: the case of P'_p: i_{2,*} ∘ P'_p(E₂) = P_p(E) for E₂ = E|_{X₂} and E|_{X₁} zero

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardChowCohomology_closedCoverChernClass
declarations.doc:
Let `i₁ : X₁ ⟶ X` and `i₂ : X₂ ⟶ X` be closed immersions whose images cover `X`, and let
`E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` have defined Chern classes and restrict on `X₁` to a finite locally free module of rank
`< p` in degree `0`. Let `E₂ = E|_{X₂}` be as in Stacks 0F9H: it restricts on `X₁ ×_X X₂` to a
finite locally free module of rank `< p` in degree `0`, and its Chern classes are defined by
`Stacks.Chow.HasDefinedChernClasses.derivedPullback`. Then `i_{2,*} ∘ c'_p(E₂) = c_p(E)` in
`A^p(X)`, with `i_{2,*} ∘ -` the pushforward of Stacks 0EPK.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforwardChowCohomology_closedCoverChernClass
    (hcover : Set.range i₁ ∪ Set.range i₂ = Set.univ)
    (hrank : ∃ M : X₁.Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M p ∧
      Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        i₁.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M))
    (hrank₂ : ∃ M : (pullback i₁ i₂).Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M p ∧
      Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        (pullback.snd i₁ i₂).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
          ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
            i₂.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E) ≅
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M)) :
    properPushforwardChowCohomology C sX (i₂ ≫ sX) i₂ rfl
        (closedCoverChernClass C sX i₁ i₂ (i₂ ≫ sX) rfl (hE.derivedPullback i₂) p hcover
          hrank₂) =
      perfectChernClass C sX hE p
declarations.comment: the case of c'_p: i_{2,*} ∘ c'_p(E₂) = c_p(E) for E₂ = E|_{X₂} and E|_{X₁} finite locally free of rank < p in degree 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinCapOfLift
declarations.doc:
The cap operation `C ∩ - : A_k(T) ⟶ A_k(W_∞ ×_X T)` built
from a choice of lift: given a homomorphism `lift : A_k(T) ⟶ A_{k+1}(W ×_X T)` and a presentation
of the base-changed fibre at infinity as the zero scheme of a global section `s` of an invertible
module `L` on `W ×_X T`, it is `i_∞^* ∘ lift`, where `i_∞^*` is the Gysin map of `s` followed by
the identification `e` of that zero scheme with `W_∞ ×_X T`.
declarations.statement:
def gysinCapOfLift (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (G : GysinSystem C) {X W T : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (b : W ⟶ projectiveLineProduct f)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (modificationProjection f b)]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b)]
    (g : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
    (L : (modificationBaseChange f b g).Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (modificationBaseChange f b g).sheaf.obj
      (modificationBaseChange f b g).ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤))
    (e : (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme (modificationBaseChange f b g) L s).subscheme ≅
      pullback (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) g)
    (he : e.hom ≫ modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b g =
      modificationZeroSchemeOver C f b g L s)
    (lift : chowGroup C (g ≫ f) k →+ chowGroup C (modificationBaseChangeOver f b g) (k + 1)) :
    chowGroup C (g ≫ f) k →+ chowGroup C (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b g) k
declarations.comment: construction of the cap operation from a lift and a zero-scheme presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinCapOfLift_eq_of_gysin_pushforward_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Two lifts whose difference is pushed forward from the fibre at infinity give the same cap
operation, as soon as the Gysin map of `s` kills everything pushed forward from the fibre at
infinity.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinCapOfLift_eq_of_gysin_pushforward_eq_zero (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (G : GysinSystem C) {X W T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (b : W ⟶ projectiveLineProduct f) [LocallyOfFiniteType (modificationProjection f b)]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b)]
    (g : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [IsProper (modificationInfinityBaseChange f b g)]
    (k : ℤ) (L : (modificationBaseChange f b g).Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (modificationBaseChange f b g).sheaf.obj
      (modificationBaseChange f b g).ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤))
    (e : (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme (modificationBaseChange f b g) L s).subscheme ≅
      pullback (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) g)
    (he : e.hom ≫ modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b g =
      modificationZeroSchemeOver C f b g L s)
    (lift lift' : chowGroup C (g ≫ f) k →+
      chowGroup C (modificationBaseChangeOver f b g) (k + 1))
    (hfac : ProperPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
      (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b g) (modificationBaseChangeOver f b g)
      (modificationInfinityBaseChange f b g) (modificationInfinityBaseChange_over f b g) (k + 1))
    (hvanish : ∀ γ : chowGroup C (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b g) (k + 1),
      G.onChow (modificationBaseChangeOver f b g) L s k
        (properChowPushforward C (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b g)
          (modificationBaseChangeOver f b g) (modificationInfinityBaseChange f b g)
          (modificationInfinityBaseChange_over f b g) (k + 1) hfac γ) = 0)
    (hdiff : ∀ α : chowGroup C (g ≫ f) k,
      ∃ γ : chowGroup C (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b g) (k + 1),
        lift α - lift' α =
          properChowPushforward C (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b g)
            (modificationBaseChangeOver f b g) (modificationInfinityBaseChange f b g)
            (modificationInfinityBaseChange_over f b g) (k + 1) hfac γ) :
    gysinCapOfLift C G f b g k L s e he lift =
      gysinCapOfLift C G f b g k L s e he lift'
declarations.comment: independence of the chosen lift

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GysinAtInfinityData
declarations.doc:
The conclusion of the Gysin-at-infinity lemma, for a proper morphism
`b : W ⟶ 𝐏¹_X` which is an isomorphism over the standard affine chart `𝐀¹_X`: a degree-zero
bivariant class `C ∈ A⁰(W_∞ ⟶ X)` for the fibre at infinity, together with the identity
`i_{∞,*}(C ∩ α) = i_{0,*} α` on every test scheme locally of finite type over `X`.
declarations.comment: statement: the canonical class in A⁰(W_∞ ⟶ X) and its pushforward identity

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GysinAtInfinity.gysinAtInfinity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9J.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over the base of chapter 42 and let
`b : W ⟶ 𝐏¹_X` be proper and an isomorphism over `𝐀¹_X`, with fibre at infinity
`i_∞ : W_∞ ⟶ W`. The class `C = gysinAtInfinityClass ∈ A⁰(W_∞ ⟶ X)`

* is constructed as in the source: `C ∩ α = i_∞^* β` for every lift `β` of `α`;
* is canonical: it is the only class with that property;
* satisfies `i_{∞,*}(C ∩ α) = i_{0,*} α` on every test scheme `T ⟶ X` locally of finite type,
  that is, for `α ∈ A_k(X)` and similarly after any base change by `X' ⟶ X` locally of finite
  type; here `i_0` and `i_∞` are the base changes of the section at zero and of the inclusion of
  the fibre at infinity.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinAtInfinity :
    IsGysinAtInfinityCap C f b hA (gysinAtInfinityClass C f b hA) ∧
      (∀ c, IsGysinAtInfinityCap C f b hA c → c = gysinAtInfinityClass C f b hA) ∧
      haveI := hA
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ f) k),
        properChowPushforward C (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b g)
            (modificationBaseChangeOver f b g) (modificationInfinityBaseChange f b g)
            (modificationInfinityBaseChange_over f b g) k
            (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper C _ _ _ _ k)
            (Eq.mp (congrArg (chowGroup C (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b g))
              (sub_zero k)) ((gysinAtInfinityClass C f b hA).cap g k α)) =
          properChowPushforward C (g ≫ f) (modificationBaseChangeOver f b g)
            (modificationSectionAtZeroBaseChange f b inferInstance
              (modificationSectionAtZero_comp f b) g)
            (modificationSectionAtZeroBaseChange_over f b g inferInstance
              (modificationSectionAtZero_comp f b)) k
            (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper C _ _ _ _ k) α

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinAtInfinityClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9J, the class at infinity.** The degree-zero bivariant class
`C ∈ A⁰(W_∞ ⟶ X)` whose cap operation on a test scheme `T ⟶ X` is `α ↦ i_∞^* β` for a lift `β`
of `α` to `W ×_X T` (`Stacks.Chow.gysinCapAtInfinity`).
declarations.comment: the canonical bivariant class C in A⁰(W_∞ ⟶ X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinAtInfinityData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9J.** The class at infinity `C ∈ A⁰(W_∞ ⟶ X)` of `Stacks.Chow.gysinAtInfinityClass`
together with the identity `i_{∞,*}(C ∩ α) = i_{0,*} α` on every test scheme locally of finite
type over `X` (`Stacks.Chow.chowPushforward_gysinCapOfLift`).
declarations.statement: def gysinAtInfinityData : GysinAtInfinityData C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) f b hA
declarations.comment: the class C in A⁰(W_∞ ⟶ X) with i_{∞,*}(C ∩ α) = i_{0,*} α, built from the cap operation i_∞^* of a lift and its three bivariance laws

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinCapAtInfinity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9J, the cap operation.** `C ∩ - : A_k(T) ⟶ A_k(W_∞ ×_X T)`, `α ↦ i_∞^* β` for a
lift `β` of `α` (`Stacks.Chow.IsModificationLift`). A lift is chosen; by
`Stacks.Chow.gysinCapAtInfinity_eq_of_isModificationLift` the value is the same for every
lift, and that independence is what makes the operation additive.
declarations.statement:
def gysinCapAtInfinity :
    chowGroup C (g ≫ f) k →+ chowGroup C (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b g) k
declarations.comment: the cap operation of the class at infinity on a test scheme: i_∞^* of a lift

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinCapAtInfinity_eq_of_isModificationLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9J, independence of the chosen lift.** The cap operation is `i_∞^* β` for *every*
lift `β` of `α`: two lifts differ by a class supported on the fibre at infinity (Stacks 02RX), and
the Gysin map at infinity kills such classes because the normal bundle of the divisor at infinity
is trivial (Remark 0B6Z).
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinCapAtInfinity_eq_of_isModificationLift (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ f) k)
    (β : chowGroup C (modificationBaseChangeOver f b g) (k + 1))
    (hβ : IsModificationLift C f b hA g k α β) :
    gysinCapAtInfinity C f b hA g k α = modificationInfinityGysin C f b g k β
declarations.comment: independence of the chosen lift: C ∩ α = i_∞^* β for every lift β of α

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GysinAtInfinityCapPresentation
declarations.doc:
A presentation of the cap operation of the Gysin class at infinity `C ∈ A⁰(W_∞ ⟶ X)` as
the composite of a lift with the Gysin map of the divisor at infinity: on every test scheme
`g : T ⟶ X` locally of finite type and in every degree `k`, additive maps
`lift : CH_k(T) ⟶ CH_{k+1}(W ×_X T)` and `gysinStep : CH_{k+1}(W ×_X T) ⟶ CH_k(W_∞ ×_X T)`
with `C ∩ α = gysinStep (lift α)`.
declarations.statement:
structure GysinAtInfinityCapPresentation (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (G : GysinSystem C)
    {X W : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (b : W ⟶ projectiveLineProduct f) [IsProper b]
    (hA : IsIso (pullback.snd b (projectiveLineAffineChart f)))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (modificationProjection f b)]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b)]
    (D : GysinAtInfinityData C G f b hA)
declarations.comment: the construction of the class at infinity, as a presentation of its cap operation by a lift and a Gysin step

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowPushforward_gysinCapOfLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9J, the pushforward identity.** On every test scheme `g : T ⟶ X` locally of finite
type, `i_{∞,*}(C ∩ α) = i_{0,*} α` in `A_k(W ×_X T)`, for the cap operation
`Stacks.Chow.gysinCapAtInfinity` of the class at infinity.

For a lift `β` of `α`, `C ∩ α = i_∞^* β`; the Gysin images `i_∞^* β` and `i_0^* β` have the same
pushforward to `W ×_X T`, the divisors `D_0` and `D_∞` of `𝐏¹` being rationally equivalent
(`Stacks.Chow.modificationZeroGysin_eq_infinityGysin`); and `i_0^* β = α`
(`Stacks.Chow.chowPushforward_zeroGysin_of_isModificationLift`).
declarations.statement:
theorem chowPushforward_gysinCapOfLift
    (hA : IsIso (pullback.snd b (projectiveLineAffineChart f))) (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ f) k) :
    haveI := isClosedImmersion_modificationSectionAtZeroBaseChange f b g hA
    chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion C (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b g)
        (modificationBaseChangeOver f b g) (modificationInfinityBaseChange f b g)
        (modificationInfinityBaseChange_over f b g) k (gysinCapAtInfinity C f b hA g k α) =
      chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion C (g ≫ f) (modificationBaseChangeOver f b g)
        (modificationSectionAtZeroBaseChange f b (isIso_modificationFibreAtZeroProjection f b hA)
          (modificationSectionAtZero_comp_projection f b hA) g)
        (modificationSectionAtZeroBaseChange_over f b g _ _) k α
declarations.comment: the pushforward identity i_{∞,*}(C ∩ α) = i_{0,*} α on every test scheme locally of finite type over X

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GysinAtInfinity.properPushforward_localizedPowerSumClassAtInfinity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9K, for the classes `P'_p`.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over the base of
chapter 42, let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subscheme, let `b : W ⟶ 𝐏¹_X` be a proper morphism which is
an isomorphism over `𝐀¹_X` (assumption (A1)), and let `Q ∈ D(𝒪_W)` be a perfect object whose
Chern classes are defined (assumption (A0)). Let `T ⊆ W_∞` be a closed subscheme containing all
points of `W_∞` lying over `X \ Z` such that `Q|_T` is zero (assumption (A2)). Then the class
`P'_p(Q) = (E ⟶ Z)_* ∘ P'_p(Q|_E) ∘ C ∈ A^p(Z ⟶ X)` satisfies

  `(Z ⟶ X)_* ∘ P'_p(Q) = P_p(Q|_{X × {0}})`

in `A^p(X)`, where `X × {0}` is identified with `X` by the section at zero and `(Z ⟶ X)_* ∘ -` is
the pushforward of Stacks 0EPK.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_localizedPowerSumClassAtInfinity
    (hV : ∀ w, (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b).base w ∉ Set.range jZ.base →
      w ∈ Set.range iV.base)
    (hzero : IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      iV.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj (restrictionAtInfinity f b Q))) :
    properPushforwardLocalizedPowerSumClassAtInfinity C hA jZ hQ perfect hV hzero =
      powerSumAtZero C f b hA hQ p
declarations.comment: the classes P'_p: the class P'_p(Q) = (E ⟶ Z)_* ∘ P'_p(Q|_E) ∘ C in A^p(Z ⟶ X), for Q|_T zero, satisfies (Z ⟶ X)_* ∘ P'_p(Q) = P_p(Q|_{X × {0}})

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.modificationPowerSum
declarations.doc:
**The class `P'_p(Q)` of Stacks 0F9K.** Let `b : W ⟶ 𝐏¹_X` be proper and an isomorphism over
`𝐀¹_X`, let `Z ⊆ X` be closed, let `Q ∈ D(𝒪_W)` have defined Chern classes, and let `T ⊆ W_∞` be
closed, contain every point of `W_∞` over `X ∖ Z`, and be such that `Q|_T` is zero. The class is
`(E ⟶ Z)_* ∘ P'_p(Q|_E) ∘ C ∈ A^p(Z ⟶ X)`, where `E = W_∞ ×_X Z`, `P'_p(Q|_E)` is the extension
of `P_p(Q)|_E` along the closed cover `W_∞ = T ∪ E`, and `C` is the class of Stacks 0F9J
(`Stacks.Chow.gysinAtInfinityData`).
declarations.statement:
def modificationPowerSum
    (hT : ∀ w, modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b w ∉ Set.range z → w ∈ Set.range t)
    (hzero : IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      (t ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity f b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Q)) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (z ≫ f) f z rfl p
declarations.comment: the class P'_p(Q) in A^p(Z ⟶ X), for Q|_T zero

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.modificationChernClass
declarations.doc:
**The class `c'_p(Q)` of Stacks 0F9K.** Let `b : W ⟶ 𝐏¹_X` be proper and an isomorphism over
`𝐀¹_X`, let `Z ⊆ X` be closed, let `Q ∈ D(𝒪_W)` have defined Chern classes, and let `T ⊆ W_∞` be
closed, contain every point of `W_∞` over `X ∖ Z`, and be such that `Q|_T` is finite locally free
of rank `< p` in degree `0`. The class is `(E ⟶ Z)_* ∘ c'_p(Q|_E) ∘ C ∈ A^p(Z ⟶ X)`, where
`E = W_∞ ×_X Z`, `c'_p(Q|_E)` is the extension of `c_p(Q)|_E` along the closed cover
`W_∞ = T ∪ E`, and `C` is the class of Stacks 0F9J (`Stacks.Chow.gysinAtInfinityData`).
declarations.statement:
def modificationChernClass
    (hT : ∀ w, modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b w ∉ Set.range z → w ∈ Set.range t)
    (hrank : ∃ M : T.Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M p ∧
      Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        (t ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity f b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Q ≅
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M)) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (z ≫ f) f z rfl p
declarations.comment: the class c'_p(Q) in A^p(Z ⟶ X), for Q|_T finite locally free of rank < p in degree 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardChowCohomology_modificationPowerSum
declarations.doc:
In the situation of `Stacks.Chow.modificationPowerSum`,
`(Z ⟶ X)_* ∘ P'_p(Q) = P_p(Q|_{X × {0}})` in `A^p(X)`, where `(Z ⟶ X)_* ∘ -` is the pushforward
of Stacks 0EPK and `Q|_{X × {0}}` is the derived pullback of `Q` along the section at zero
`i_0 : X ⟶ W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforwardChowCohomology_modificationPowerSum
    (hT : ∀ w, modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b w ∉ Set.range z → w ∈ Set.range t)
    (hzero : IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      (t ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity f b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Q)) :
    properPushforwardChowCohomology C f (z ≫ f) z rfl
        (modificationPowerSum C f b hA z t hQ p hT hzero) =
      perfectPowerSumComponent C f (hQ.derivedPullback
        (modificationSectionAtZero f b (isIso_modificationFibreAtZeroProjection f b hA))) p
declarations.comment: the case of P'_p: (Z ⟶ X)_* ∘ P'_p(Q) = P_p(Q|_{X × {0}})

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardChowCohomology_modificationChernClass
declarations.doc:
In the situation of `Stacks.Chow.modificationChernClass`,
`(Z ⟶ X)_* ∘ c'_p(Q) = c_p(Q|_{X × {0}})` in `A^p(X)`, where `(Z ⟶ X)_* ∘ -` is the pushforward
of Stacks 0EPK and `Q|_{X × {0}}` is the derived pullback of `Q` along the section at zero
`i_0 : X ⟶ W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforwardChowCohomology_modificationChernClass
    (hT : ∀ w, modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b w ∉ Set.range z → w ∈ Set.range t)
    (hrank : ∃ M : T.Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M p ∧
      Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        (t ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity f b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Q ≅
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M)) :
    properPushforwardChowCohomology C f (z ≫ f) z rfl
        (modificationChernClass C f b hA z t hQ p hT hrank) =
      perfectChernClass C f (hQ.derivedPullback
        (modificationSectionAtZero f b (isIso_modificationFibreAtZeroProjection f b hA))) p
declarations.comment: the case of c'_p: (Z ⟶ X)_* ∘ c'_p(Q) = c_p(Q|_{X × {0}})

registrations.name: Stacks.Chow.GysinAtInfinity.properPushforward_localizedChernClassAtInfinity
registrations.comment: the classes c'_p: the class c'_p(Q) = (E ⟶ Z)_* ∘ c'_p(Q|_E) ∘ C in A^p(Z ⟶ X), for Q|_T finite locally free of rank < p in degree 0, satisfies (Z ⟶ X)_* ∘ c'_p(Q) = c_p(Q|_{X × {0}})

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.NonRegularSequence.exists_puncturedSpectrum_firstOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F9L], the punctured spectra.**  Reduction modulo `w` is a first-order
thickening `i : U₀ ⟶ U` of the punctured spectrum of `A₀` inside that of `A`, lying over
`Spec` of the reduction `q : A → A₀`; every invertible global function on `U₀` is the
restriction of one on `U`; and the ideal sheaf of `i`, pulled back to `U₀`, is the structure
sheaf of `U₀`.

These are the source's three geometric inputs.  The thickening is `A = A₀[w]/(w²)` read on
spectra and restricted to the punctured spectra; the lifting of units is the section `ι` of `q`
together with `Γ(U₀, 𝒪_{U₀}) = A₀`; and the identification of the ideal sheaf is multiplication
by `w`, which carries `A₀` isomorphically onto the kernel `wA` of `q`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_puncturedSpectrum_firstOrderThickening (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    ∃ (q : exampleRing k →+* intermediateRing k)
      (i : (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum (intermediateRing k)).toScheme ⟶
        (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum (exampleRing k)).toScheme)
      (_ : Stacks.Thickenings.IsFirstOrderThickening i),
      (∀ p : powerSeriesRing k 8,
        q (Ideal.Quotient.mk (eightVariableIdeal k) p) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (sevenVariableIdeal k) (MvPowerSeries.killCompl sevenToEight p)) ∧
      i ≫ (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum (exampleRing k)).ι =
        (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum (intermediateRing k)).ι ≫
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom q) ∧
      Function.Surjective (Stacks.Thickenings.unitsToSubCohomology i 0) ∧
      Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf
        (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum (intermediateRing k)).toScheme.ringCatSheaf).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit
            (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum (intermediateRing k)).toScheme.ringCatSheaf) ≅
        Stacks.Thickenings.idealAddSheafOnSub i)
declarations.comment: the punctured spectra: reduction modulo w is a first-order thickening U₀ ⟶ U over Spec of the reduction, invertible global functions lift along it, and its ideal sheaf pulled back to U₀ is the structure sheaf of U₀

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.NonRegularSequence.exampleRing_scheme_picardGroup_puncturedSpectrum_not_subsingleton
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F9L], the conclusion.** The Picard group of the punctured spectrum
`U = Spec A ∖ {𝔪}` of
`A = k⟦a,b,x,y,z,u,v,w⟧/(a³, b³, xa² + yab + zb², w²)`
is nontrivial.  Together with `powerSeriesRing_isRegularLocalRing` and
`powerSeriesRing_dimension` — the ambient ring `B = k⟦a,b,x,y,z,u,v,w⟧` is regular of
dimension `8`, and `A = B/(f₁, f₂, f₃, f₄)` with `r = 4`, so `dim B - r = 4 ≥ 4` — this is
the source's witness that [Stacks, Tag 0F2I] fails without the hypothesis that
`f₁, …, f_r` be a regular sequence.

The Picard group is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.picardGroup`, the same one [Stacks, Tag 0F2I]
and the companion example
`Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.QuadricCone.picardGroup_not_subsingleton'` are stated at, so
this is literally the negation of that proposition's conclusion for this `A`.

The argument itself runs in the universe-shrunk model of Tag 040B, where the exact sequence of
[Stacks, Tag 0C6R] lives: it is
`exampleRing_picardGroup_puncturedSpectrum_not_subsingleton'`, carried here across
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.picardGroupShrinkAddEquiv`, the isomorphism of abelian groups between
the two models.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exampleRing_scheme_picardGroup_puncturedSpectrum_not_subsingleton
    (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    ¬ Subsingleton
      (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum (exampleRing k)).toScheme.picardGroup
declarations.comment: the conclusion: the Picard group of the punctured spectrum is nontrivial, at the same Scheme.picardGroup that Stacks 0F2I is stated at, so this is literally the negation of that proposition's conclusion for this A

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.NonRegularSequence.socleElement_mul_variable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9L** (socle element annihilated by all five variables).
The class of `a²b²` in `A₁ = k⟦a,b,x,y,z⟧/(a³, b³, xa² + yab + zb²)` is killed by each of
the five variables `a, b, x, y, z`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem socleElement_mul_variable (k : Type u) [Field k] (i : Fin 5) :

declarations.comment: socle element annihilated by all five variables

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.NonRegularSequence.exampleRing_equiv_truncatedPolynomial
declarations.doc:
The square-zero description, with the inclusion of `A₀` identified with constant
polynomials and the chosen eighth variable identified with `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exampleRing_equiv_truncatedPolynomial (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    ∃ (e : exampleRing k ≃+* truncatedPolynomialRing k)
      (ι : intermediateRing k →+* exampleRing k)
      (q : exampleRing k →+* intermediateRing k),
      (∀ p : powerSeriesRing k 7,
        ι (Ideal.Quotient.mk (sevenVariableIdeal k) p) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (eightVariableIdeal k) (MvPowerSeries.rename sevenToEight p)) ∧
      (∀ p : powerSeriesRing k 8,
        q (Ideal.Quotient.mk (eightVariableIdeal k) p) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (sevenVariableIdeal k) (MvPowerSeries.killCompl sevenToEight p)) ∧
      (∀ a : intermediateRing k,
        e (ι a) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (Polynomial.C a)) ∧
      e (squareZeroCoordinate k) =
        Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (Polynomial.X : Polynomial (intermediateRing k)) ∧
      (∀ a : intermediateRing k, q (ι a) = a) ∧
      q (squareZeroCoordinate k) = 0 ∧
      Function.Injective (fun a : intermediateRing k => squareZeroCoordinate k * ι a) ∧
      Function.Exact
        (fun a : intermediateRing k => squareZeroCoordinate k * ι a)
        q
declarations.comment: square-zero extension with its chosen coordinates

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces
declarations.doc:
The canonical functor from spaces over `X` to cartesian gluing triples, including its natural
comparison with all three base changes and the two induced arrows.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (U' U X' X : Scheme.{u}) (hU' : B.Contains U')
    (hU : B.Contains U) (hX' : B.Contains X') (hX : B.Contains X)
    (gU : B.obj hU' ⟶ B.obj hU)
    (gX' : B.obj hU' ⟶ B.obj hX')
    (jU : B.obj hU ⟶ B.obj hX)
    (jX' : B.obj hX' ⟶ B.obj hX)
    (hcomm : gU ≫ jU = gX' ≫ jX') :
    GlueingFunctorSpec B U' U X' X hU' hU hX' hX gU gX' jU jX' hcomm

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_etaleCovering_iff_isGlueable
declarations.doc:
Glueability of an algebraic space can be checked on all affine schemes
étale over it, or on one étale covering by affine schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleCovering_iff_isGlueable
  {R : Type u} {R' : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing R']
  (g : R →+* R') (f : R)
  (_hglue : BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair g f)
  (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
  (hX : B.Contains (Spec (.of R)))
  (Y : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of R)) hX) :
  (∃ (I : Type (u + 1))
      (W : I → BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of R)) hX)
      (p : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (W i) ⟶ Y.1),
      IsEtaleCovering B (Spec (.of R)) hX
        (fun i ↦ yoneda.obj (W i)) p ∧
        ∀ i, IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of R)) hX).obj (W i)) ∧
          IsGlueableGlobalSections g f B hX (W i)) ↔
    IsGlueableAlgebraicSpace g f B hX Y

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.isAffineSpace_components
declarations.doc:
**The gluing functor of Stacks 0F9N takes affine algebraic spaces to triples with affine
components.** All four schemes of the square are assumed affine, as they are in the
Beauville--Laszlo situation, where they are the spectra of `R`, `R_f`, `R'` and `R'_f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineSpace_components
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (U' U X' X : Scheme.{u}) (hU' : B.Contains U')
    (hU : B.Contains U) (hX' : B.Contains X') (hX : B.Contains X)
    [IsAffine U'] [IsAffine U] [IsAffine X'] [IsAffine X]
    (gU : B.obj hU' ⟶ B.obj hU)
    (gX' : B.obj hU' ⟶ B.obj hX')
    (jU : B.obj hU ⟶ B.obj hX)
    (jX' : B.obj hX' ⟶ B.obj hX)
    (hcomm : gU ≫ jU = gX' ≫ jX')
    (G : GlueingFunctorSpec B U' U X' X hU' hU hX' hX gU gX' jU jX' hcomm)
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B X hX)
    (hY : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAffineSpace B X hX Y.1) :
    affineComponents B U' U X' hU' hU hX' gU gX' (G.functor.obj Y)
declarations.comment: the functor restricts to the affine subcategories

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9Q.** For a Beauville--Laszlo glueing pair `(g : R → R', f)`, the glueing functor
of Stacks 0F9N restricts to an **equivalence** between the category of affine algebraic spaces
over `X = Spec R` which are glueable for `(g, f)` and the full subcategory of those glueing
triples `(V, V', Y')` over `U ← U' → X'` whose three components are affine.

The functor in question is `BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction`, which is by
definition the restriction of `BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces`, the glueing
functor of Stacks 0F9N, to those two full subcategories.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction_isEquivalence {R R' : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing R']
    (g : R →+* R') (f : R) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hU' : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))))
    (hU : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))))
    (hX' : B.Contains (Spec (.of R'))) (hX : B.Contains (Spec (.of R)))
    (hcomm : canGU g f B hU' hU ≫ canJU f B hU hX = canGX' g f B hU' hX' ≫ canJX' g B hX' hX)
    (hglue : _root_.BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair g f) :
    (canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction g f B hU' hU hX' hX hcomm).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.beauvilleLaszloAffineEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9Q.** The glueing functor of Stacks 0F9N restricts to an equivalence between the
affine algebraic spaces over `X = Spec R` which are glueable for the pair `(R → R', f)` and the
cartesian glueing triples `(V, V', Y')` over `U ← U' → X'` whose three components are affine —
together with the identification of the forward functor of that equivalence with the restriction
of the glueing functor itself, which is what the statement of the tag asserts.

Faithfulness is Stacks 0F9S, fullness is
`BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.full_comp_glueingFunctor` and essential surjectivity is
`BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.essSurj_affineGlueableRestriction`; the equivalence is the one Mathlib
builds out of the three, so its forward functor *is* the restricted glueing functor and the
identification is `BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.affineGlueableRestrictionCompIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def beauvilleLaszloAffineEquivalence (f : R)
    (hpair : _root_.BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair (algebraMap R R') f)
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hX : B.Contains (Spec (.of R)))
    (hU : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))))
    (hX' : B.Contains (Spec (.of R')))
    (hU' : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away ((algebraMap R R') f))))) :
    AffineGlueingEquivalenceSpec (algebraMap R R') f B
      (Spec (.of (Localization.Away ((algebraMap R R') f))))
      (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))) (Spec (.of R')) hU' hU hX' hX
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hU hU').hom
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hX' hU').hom
      (beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away ((algebraMap R R') f))))
        (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))) (Spec (.of R')) (Spec (.of R)) hU' hU hX' hX
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hU hU').hom
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hX' hU').hom
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hX hU).hom
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hX hX').hom
        (specSite_square_comm f B hU' hU hX' hX)).functor

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.essSurj_affineGlueableRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9Q, the essential surjectivity clause.** The restriction of a glueing functor of
Stacks 0F9N to the affine algebraic spaces over `Spec R` which are glueable for the pair is
essentially surjective onto the cartesian glueing triples with affine components.
declarations.statement:
theorem essSurj_affineGlueableRestriction {R R' : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing R']
    [Algebra R R'] (f : R)
    (hpair : _root_.BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair (algebraMap R R') f)
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hX : B.Contains (Spec (.of R)))
    (hU : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))))
    (hX' : B.Contains (Spec (.of R')))
    (hU' : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away ((algebraMap R R') f)))))
    (hcomm : (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hU hU').hom ≫
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hX hU).hom =
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hX' hU').hom ≫
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hX hX').hom)
    (G : GlueingFunctorSpec B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away ((algebraMap R R') f))))
      (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))) (Spec (.of R')) (Spec (.of R)) hU' hU hX' hX
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hU hU').hom
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hX' hU').hom
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hX hU).hom
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.specSite B hX hX').hom hcomm) :
    (affineGlueableRestriction (g := algebraMap R R') (f := f) G).EssSurj
declarations.comment: the restricted functor is essentially surjective

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.isFinite_iff_canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9R for `P` finite, on the glueing functor.** Let `(g : R → R', f)` be a glueing pair
and let `F` be the glueing functor of Stacks 0F9N restricted, as in Stacks 0F9Q, to the affine
algebraic spaces over `X = Spec R` which are glueable for `(g, f)`. A morphism `φ` of such
spaces is finite if and only if the three components of the morphism of triples `F.map φ`, over
`U = Spec R_f`, `U' = Spec R'_{g f}` and `X' = Spec R'`, are finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_iff_canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction_map
    {R R' : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] (g : R →+* R') (f : R)
    (hglue : _root_.BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair g f) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hU' : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))))
    (hU : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))))
    (hX' : B.Contains (Spec (.of R'))) (hX : B.Contains (Spec (.of R)))
    (hcomm : canGU g f B hU' hU ≫ canJU f B hU hX = canGX' g f B hU' hX' ≫ canJX' g B hX' hX)
    {Y Z : (affineGlueableSpaces g f B hX).FullSubcategory} (φ : Y ⟶ Z) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFinite B (Spec (.of R)) hX φ.hom.hom ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFinite B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))) hU
          ((overU B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map
            ((canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction g f B hU' hU hX' hX hcomm).map
              φ).hom).hom ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFinite B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))) hU'
            ((overU' B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map
              ((canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction g f B hU' hU hX' hX hcomm).map
                φ).hom).hom ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFinite B (Spec (.of R')) hX'
              ((overX' B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map
                ((canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction g f B hU' hU hX' hX hcomm).map
                  φ).hom).hom
declarations.comment: P = finite; morphisms of affine glueable spaces

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.isFinite_affineGlueingEquivalence_inverse_map_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9R for `P` finite, on the inverse equivalence.** Let `(g : R → R', f)` be a glueing
pair. For every morphism `β` of glueing triples over `U ← U' → X'` with affine components, the
morphism of affine glueable algebraic spaces over `X = Spec R` corresponding to `β` under the
equivalence of Stacks 0F9Q is finite if and only if the three components of `β` are finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_affineGlueingEquivalence_inverse_map_iff
    {R R' : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] (g : R →+* R') (f : R)
    (hglue : _root_.BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair g f) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hU' : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))))
    (hU : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))))
    (hX' : B.Contains (Spec (.of R'))) (hX : B.Contains (Spec (.of R)))
    (hcomm : canGU g f B hU' hU ≫ canJU f B hU hX = canGX' g f B hU' hX' ≫ canJX' g B hX' hX)
    {T₁ T₂ : (affineComponents B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' (canGU g f B hU' hU)
      (canGX' g f B hU' hX')).FullSubcategory} (β : T₁ ⟶ T₂) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFinite B (Spec (.of R)) hX
        ((affineGlueingEquivalence g f B hU' hU hX' hX hcomm hglue).equivalence.inverse.map
          β).hom.hom ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFinite B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))) hU
          ((overU B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map β.hom).hom ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFinite B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))) hU'
            ((overU' B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map β.hom).hom ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFinite B (Spec (.of R')) hX'
              ((overX' B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map β.hom).hom
declarations.comment: P = finite; morphisms of triples with affine components

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.isClosedImmersion_iff_canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9R for `P` closed immersion, on the glueing functor.** Let `(g : R → R', f)` be a
glueing pair and let `F` be the glueing functor of Stacks 0F9N restricted, as in Stacks 0F9Q, to
the affine algebraic spaces over `X = Spec R` which are glueable for `(g, f)`. A morphism `φ` of
such spaces is a closed immersion if and only if the three components of the morphism of triples
`F.map φ`, over `U = Spec R_f`, `U' = Spec R'_{g f}` and `X' = Spec R'`, are closed immersions.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_iff_canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction_map
    {R R' : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] (g : R →+* R') (f : R)
    (hglue : _root_.BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair g f) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hU' : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))))
    (hU : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))))
    (hX' : B.Contains (Spec (.of R'))) (hX : B.Contains (Spec (.of R)))
    (hcomm : canGU g f B hU' hU ≫ canJU f B hU hX = canGX' g f B hU' hX' ≫ canJX' g B hX' hX)
    {Y Z : (affineGlueableSpaces g f B hX).FullSubcategory} (φ : Y ⟶ Z) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedImmersion B (Spec (.of R)) hX φ.hom.hom ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedImmersion B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))) hU
          ((overU B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map
            ((canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction g f B hU' hU hX' hX hcomm).map
              φ).hom).hom ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedImmersion B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))) hU'
            ((overU' B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map
              ((canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction g f B hU' hU hX' hX hcomm).map
                φ).hom).hom ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedImmersion B (Spec (.of R')) hX'
              ((overX' B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map
                ((canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction g f B hU' hU hX' hX hcomm).map
                  φ).hom).hom
declarations.comment: P = closed immersion; morphisms of affine glueable spaces

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.isClosedImmersion_affineGlueingEquivalence_inverse_map_iff
declarations.doc:
Let `(g : R → R', f)` be a glueing pair. For every morphism `β` of glueing triples over
`U ← U' → X'` with affine components, the morphism of affine glueable algebraic spaces over
`X = Spec R` corresponding to `β` under the inverse of the glueing equivalence is a closed
immersion if and only if the three components of `β` are closed immersions.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_affineGlueingEquivalence_inverse_map_iff
    {R R' : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] (g : R →+* R') (f : R)
    (hglue : _root_.BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair g f) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hU' : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))))
    (hU : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))))
    (hX' : B.Contains (Spec (.of R'))) (hX : B.Contains (Spec (.of R)))
    (hcomm : canGU g f B hU' hU ≫ canJU f B hU hX = canGX' g f B hU' hX' ≫ canJX' g B hX' hX)
    {T₁ T₂ : (affineComponents B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' (canGU g f B hU' hU)
      (canGX' g f B hU' hX')).FullSubcategory} (β : T₁ ⟶ T₂) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedImmersion B (Spec (.of R)) hX
        ((affineGlueingEquivalence g f B hU' hU hX' hX hcomm hglue).equivalence.inverse.map
          β).hom.hom ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedImmersion B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))) hU
          ((overU B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map β.hom).hom ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedImmersion B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))) hU'
            ((overU' B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map β.hom).hom ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedImmersion B (Spec (.of R')) hX'
              ((overX' B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map β.hom).hom
declarations.comment: P = closed immersion; morphisms of triples with affine components

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.isFlat_iff_canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9R for `P` flat, on the glueing functor.** Let `(g : R → R', f)` be a glueing pair
and let `F` be the glueing functor of Stacks 0F9N restricted, as in Stacks 0F9Q, to the affine
algebraic spaces over `X = Spec R` which are glueable for `(g, f)`. A morphism `φ` of such
spaces is flat if and only if the three components of the morphism of triples `F.map φ`, over
`U = Spec R_f`, `U' = Spec R'_{g f}` and `X' = Spec R'`, are flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_iff_canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction_map
    {R R' : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] (g : R →+* R') (f : R)
    (hglue : _root_.BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair g f) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hU' : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))))
    (hU : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))))
    (hX' : B.Contains (Spec (.of R'))) (hX : B.Contains (Spec (.of R)))
    (hcomm : canGU g f B hU' hU ≫ canJU f B hU hX = canGX' g f B hU' hX' ≫ canJX' g B hX' hX)
    {Y Z : (affineGlueableSpaces g f B hX).FullSubcategory} (φ : Y ⟶ Z) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlat B (Spec (.of R)) hX φ.hom.hom ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlat B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))) hU
          ((overU B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map
            ((canonicalAffineGlueableRestriction g f B hU' hU hX' hX hcomm).map
              φ).hom).hom ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlat B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))) hU'
            ((overU' B _ _ _ hU' hU hX' _ _).map

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.isFinite_iff_baseChange
declarations.doc:

`X = Spec R` is finite if and only if its base changes to `U = Spec R_f`, `U' = Spec R'_f` and
`X' = Spec R'`, the three components of its image under the glueing functor of Stacks 0F9N, are
finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_iff_baseChange (f : R) (hglue : IsGlueingPair (algebraMap R R') f)
    (h : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R B))) ⟶
      Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)))) :
    IsFinite h.left ↔
      IsFinite ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f))))).map h).left ∧
        IsFinite ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
            (algebraMap R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' f)))))).map h).left ∧
          IsFinite ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
            (algebraMap R R')))).map h).left
declarations.comment: P = finite

          (algebraMap R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' f)))))).map h).left ∧
        LocallyOfFinitePresentation ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' f)))))).map h).left) ∧
      (Flat ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap R R')))).map h).left ∧
        LocallyOfFinitePresentation ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap R R')))).map h).left)
declarations.comment: P = flat and finite presentation

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.etale_iff_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `(R → R', f)` be a glueing pair and let the `R`-algebra `A` be glueable for it. A morphism
`h : Spec B → Spec A` of schemes over `X = Spec R` is étale if and only if its base changes to
`U = Spec R_f`, `U' = Spec R'_f` and `X' = Spec R'`, the three components of its image under the
glueing functor of Stacks 0F9N, are étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_iff_baseChange (f : R) (hglue : IsGlueingPair (algebraMap R R') f)
    (hA : (beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence (S := R') A f).ShortExact)
    (h : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R B))) ⟶
      Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)))) :
    Etale h.left ↔
      Etale ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f))))).map h).left ∧
        Etale ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
            (algebraMap R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' f)))))).map h).left ∧
          Etale ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
            (algebraMap R R')))).map h).left
declarations.comment: P = étale

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces_map_injective_of_isGlueable
declarations.doc: The Beauville--Laszlo gluing functor is faithful on glueable algebraic spaces over `Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces_map_injective_of_isGlueable
    (R R' : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing R']
    (g : R →+* R') (f : R)
    (hglue : _root_.BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair g f)
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hU' : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))))
    (hU : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))))
    (hX' : B.Contains (Spec (.of R')))
    (hX : B.Contains (Spec (.of R))) :
    let U' : Scheme.{u} := Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))
    let U : Scheme.{u} := Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))
    let X' : Scheme.{u} := Spec (.of R')
    let X : Scheme.{u} := Spec (.of R)
    let gU : B.obj hU' ⟶ B.obj hU :=
      ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Localization.awayMap g f))⟩
    let gX' : B.obj hU' ⟶ B.obj hX' :=
      ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R' (Localization.Away (g f))))⟩
    let jU : B.obj hU ⟶ B.obj hX :=
      ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f)))⟩
    let jX' : B.obj hX' ⟶ B.obj hX :=
      ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom g)⟩
    ∀ (hcomm : gU ≫ jU = gX' ≫ jX')
      (Y Z : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces B X hX),
      _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGlueableAlgebraicSpace g f B hX Y →
      _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGlueableAlgebraicSpace g f B hX Z →
      Function.Injective (fun (φ : Y ⟶ Z) ↦
        (BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces
          B U' U X' X hU' hU hX' hX gU gX' jU jX' hcomm).functor.map φ)

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces_map_surjective_of_isGlueable_of_isAffineHom_diag
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9T, fullness.** For a Beauville--Laszlo glueing pair `(g : R → R', f)`, a
morphism of glueing triples between the images of two algebraic spaces over `Spec R` which are
glueable for `(g, f)` comes from a morphism of algebraic spaces, provided the target has affine
diagonal.

Nothing beyond the glueing pair and these two conditions is assumed: the equivalence of the
affine case is `BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.affineGlueingEquivalence` (Stacks 0F9Q) and étaleness of a
morphism of affine glueable spaces in terms of its components is
`BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.isEtale_iff_isEtale_glueingComponents` (Stacks 0F9R for the property
"étale"); both are supplied to
`beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces_map_surjective_of_isGlueable_of_affineDiagonal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces_map_surjective_of_isGlueable_of_isAffineHom_diag
    (R R' : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] (g : R →+* R') (f : R)
    (hglue : _root_.BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair g f) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hU' : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))))
    (hU : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))))
    (hX' : B.Contains (Spec (.of R'))) (hX : B.Contains (Spec (.of R))) :
    let U' : Scheme.{u} := Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))
    let U : Scheme.{u} := Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))
    let X' : Scheme.{u} := Spec (.of R')
    let X : Scheme.{u} := Spec (.of R)
    let gU : B.obj hU' ⟶ B.obj hU :=
      ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Localization.awayMap g f))⟩
    let gX' : B.obj hU' ⟶ B.obj hX' :=
      ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R' (Localization.Away (g f))))⟩
    let jU : B.obj hU ⟶ B.obj hX :=
      ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f)))⟩
    let jX' : B.obj hX' ⟶ B.obj hX := ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom g)⟩
    ∀ (hcomm : gU ≫ jU = gX' ≫ jX') (Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B X hX),
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGlueableAlgebraicSpace g f B hX Y →
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGlueableAlgebraicSpace g f B hX Z →
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAffineHom B X hX (diag Z.1) →
      Function.Surjective (fun (φ : Y ⟶ Z) ↦
        (beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces
          B U' U X' X hU' hU hX' hX gU gX' jU jX' hcomm).functor.map φ)
declarations.comment: fullness

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces_map_bijective_of_isGlueable_of_isAffineHom_diag
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9T.** For a Beauville--Laszlo glueing pair `(g : R → R', f)`, the glueing functor
of Stacks 0F9N is fully faithful on the full subcategory of algebraic spaces `Y/X` which are
glueable for `(g, f)` and have affine diagonal `Y → Y ×_X Y`: the map it induces on each hom-set
between two such objects is bijective.

Injectivity is Stacks 0F9S, which needs glueability alone; surjectivity needs affineness of the
diagonal of the target alone, and is
`beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces_map_surjective_of_isGlueable_of_isAffineHom_diag`.
declarations.statement:
theorem beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces_map_bijective_of_isGlueable_of_isAffineHom_diag
    (R R' : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] (g : R →+* R') (f : R)
    (hglue : _root_.BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair g f) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hU' : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))))
    (hU : B.Contains (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))))
    (hX' : B.Contains (Spec (.of R'))) (hX : B.Contains (Spec (.of R))) :
    let U' : Scheme.{u} := Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f)))
    let U : Scheme.{u} := Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))
    let X' : Scheme.{u} := Spec (.of R')
    let X : Scheme.{u} := Spec (.of R)
    let gU : B.obj hU' ⟶ B.obj hU :=
      ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Localization.awayMap g f))⟩
    let gX' : B.obj hU' ⟶ B.obj hX' :=
      ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R' (Localization.Away (g f))))⟩
    let jU : B.obj hU ⟶ B.obj hX :=
      ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f)))⟩
    let jX' : B.obj hX' ⟶ B.obj hX := ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom g)⟩
    ∀ (hcomm : gU ≫ jU = gX' ≫ jX') (Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B X hX),
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGlueableAlgebraicSpace g f B hX Y →
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGlueableAlgebraicSpace g f B hX Z →
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAffineHom B X hX (diag Y.1) →
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAffineHom B X hX (diag Z.1) →
      Function.Bijective (fun (φ : Y ⟶ Z) ↦
        (beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces
          B U' U X' X hU' hU hX' hX gU gX' jU jX' hcomm).functor.map φ)

registrations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces_map_injective_of_isGlueable
registrations.comment: faithfulness

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.Space.exists_isSeparatedOver_iso_of_isQuasiAffineComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9U.** Let `(g : R → R', f)` be a glueing pair, and let `X = Spec R`,
`U = Spec R_f`, `X' = Spec R'` and `U' = Spec R'_{g f}` be the four corners of its square, all in
the big fppf site `B`. Any cartesian triple `(V, V', Y')` of algebraic spaces over `U ← U' → X'`
whose three components are quasi-affine is isomorphic to the image, under the gluing functor of
Stacks 0F9N, of an algebraic space `Y` over `X` which is separated over `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSeparatedOver_iso_of_isQuasiAffineComponents
    (hglue : _root_.BeauvilleLaszlo.IsGlueingPair g f)
    (Z : GlueingData B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f))))
      (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))) (Spec (.of R')) hU' hU hX'
      (canGU g f B hU' hU) (canGX' g f B hU' hX'))
    (hZ : quasiAffineComponents B (Spec (.of (Localization.Away (g f))))
      (Spec (.of (Localization.Away f))) (Spec (.of R')) hU' hU hX'
      (canGU g f B hU' hU) (canGX' g f B hU' hX') Z) :
    ∃ Y : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of R)) hX,
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparatedOver B (Spec (.of R)) hX Y.obj ∧
        Nonempty ((beauvilleLaszloGlueingSpaces B _ _ _ _ hU' hU hX' hX
          (canGU g f B hU' hU) (canGX' g f B hU' hX') (canJU f B hU hX) (canJX' g B hX' hX)
          (canonical_comm g f B hU' hU hX' hX)).functor.obj Y ≅ Z)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.exists_away_iso_biprod_trivial_complexes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9V.** Two bounded complexes of finite projective modules representing
isomorphic derived objects become isomorphic as complexes over some principal localization,
after adjoining finite direct sums of trivial two-term complexes on both sides.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_away_iso_biprod_trivial_complexes
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (M N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) ℤ)
    (hMbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, M.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hNbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, N.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ N.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hMterms : ∀ i, Module.Finite R (M.X i) ∧ Projective (M.X i))
    (hNterms : ∀ i, Module.Finite R (N.X i) ∧ Projective (N.X i))
    (hMN : Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj M ≅ (DerivedCategory.Q).obj N)) :
    ∃ f : R, f ∉ p ∧
      let S := Localization.Away f
      let F := (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u} (algebraMap R S)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
      let IsTrivialSum := fun P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} S) ℤ =>
        ∃ (n : ℕ) (degree : Fin n → ℤ),
          Nonempty (P ≅ ∏ᶜ fun j => CochainComplex.mappingCone
            (𝟙 ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} S) (degree j)).obj
              (ModuleCat.of S (ULift.{v} S)))))
      ∃ P Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} S) ℤ,
        IsTrivialSum P ∧ IsTrivialSum Q ∧ Nonempty (F.obj M ⊞ P ≅ F.obj N ⊞ Q)

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.IdealPowerTensorComparison.map_eq
declarations.doc:
Any two such comparisons agree in **every** integer degree, negative ones included: the
degree-`0` normalization starts the recursion, and the recursion runs downwards as well as
upwards because tensoring by `I` is an equivalence, hence faithful.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IdealPowerTensorComparison.map_eq (I L : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ)
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf (Oₓ).property I]
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf (Oₓ).property L]
    (c d : IdealPowerTensorComparison X I L) (n : ℤ) (M : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) :
    c.map n M = d.map n M
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the degreewise interchange

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.etaTensorInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0F9W.** Décalage by an invertible ideal commutes with tensoring by an
invertible module: the décalage of `F ⊗ L` is canonically isomorphic to the décalage of `F`
tensored by `L`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def etaTensorInvertible (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono ι]
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf (Oₓ).property I]
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ)
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf (Oₓ).property L]
    (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ n : ℤ, IsIdealTorsionFree X ι (F.X n)) :
    etaObj X I ι
          ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{_, _, u, u, u} X.sheaf).flip.obj
            L).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj F)
          (fun n => idealTorsionFree_tensorInvertible X I ι L (F.X n) (hF n)) ≅
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{_, _, u, u, u} X.sheaf).flip.obj
          L).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (etaObj X I ι F hF)

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.etaTensorInvertible_fst
declarations.doc:
On the first projection of the defining fibre product, the comparison of Tag 0F9W is the
interchange of the `n`-th ideal power with the invertible tensor factor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaTensorInvertible_fst (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono ι]
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf (Oₓ).property I]
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ)
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf (Oₓ).property L]
    (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ n : ℤ, IsIdealTorsionFree X ι (F.X n)) (n : ℤ) :
    (etaTensorInvertible X I ι L F hF).hom.f n ≫
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{_, _, u, u, u} X.sheaf).flip.obj L).map
          (X := etaTerm X I ι F n) (Y := idealPowerTerm X I n (F.X n))
          (pullback.fst (idealPowerMap X I n (F.d n (n + 1)))
            (idealPowerIncl X I ι n (F.X (n + 1)))) =
      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ (idealPowerTensorIso X I L (F.X n) n).hom
declarations.comment: first degreewise projection

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.etaTensorInvertible_snd
declarations.doc:
On the second projection of the defining fibre product, the comparison of Tag 0F9W is the
interchange of the `(n+1)`-st ideal power with the invertible tensor factor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaTensorInvertible_snd (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono ι]
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf (Oₓ).property I]
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ)
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf (Oₓ).property L]
    (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ n : ℤ, IsIdealTorsionFree X ι (F.X n)) (n : ℤ) :
    (etaTensorInvertible X I ι L F hF).hom.f n ≫
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{_, _, u, u, u} X.sheaf).flip.obj L).map
          (X := etaTerm X I ι F n) (Y := idealPowerTerm X I (n + 1) (F.X (n + 1)))
          (pullback.snd (idealPowerMap X I n (F.d n (n + 1)))
            (idealPowerIncl X I ι n (F.X (n + 1)))) =
      pullback.snd _ _ ≫ (idealPowerTensorIso X I L (F.X (n + 1)) (n + 1)).hom
declarations.comment: second degreewise projection

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.Eta.isIso_derivedEtaPullbackComparison
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F9X] for a flat morphism.**  Let `X` be a scheme, let `D ⊆ X` be an effective
Cartier divisor with ideal sheaf `I = ℐ_D`, let `h : Y ⟶ X` be a flat morphism of schemes and
suppose the pullback `E = h^{-1}D` is defined, with ideal sheaf `J = ℐ_E`.  Then for every object
`M = [G^•]` of `D(𝒪_X)` presented by a complex of `I`-torsion-free modules, the canonical
comparison `Lh^*(Lη_I M) ⟶ Lη_J(Lh^* M)` is an isomorphism.

Two of the three constituents of `Stacks.Divisors.Eta.derivedEtaPullbackComparison` are
components of the natural isomorphism identifying `Lh^*` with the functor induced by `h^*`,
hence isomorphisms; the remaining one is an isomorphism by
`Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.isIso_transportedPullbackDerivedEtaMap`, which is where flatness is
used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedEtaPullbackComparison
    (hflat : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlat h.toLRSHom.toShHom)
    (K : CochainComplex
      (Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.TorsionFreeModule X.toRingedSpace (idealSheafι D)) ℤ) :
    IsIso (derivedEtaPullbackComparison h D hflat K)
declarations.comment: the case of a flat h, which neither implies nor is implied by the source's statement: flatness replaces goodness of the triple, and no goodness is used. the general case, for an arbitrary h and a good triple, is AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.nonempty_derivedPullback_derivedEta_iso

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.Eta.nonempty_derivedPullback_derivedEta_iso_of_forall_stalk_good
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F9X] with goodness in place of flatness.**  Let `X` be a scheme, let
`D ⊆ X` be an effective Cartier divisor with ideal sheaf `I = ℐ_D`, let `h : Y ⟶ X` be an
**arbitrary** morphism of schemes such that the inverse image `E = h^{-1}D` is defined, and let
`J = ℐ_E`.  Let `M` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` presented by a K-flat complex `𝒦` of flat
`𝒪_X`-modules, and suppose that at every point `z` of `Y` the stalk complex of `𝒦` at `h(z)` is
**good**: there are a generator `a` of `I_{h(z)}` whose germ generates `J_z` and a bounded
complex `C` of finite free `𝒪_{X,h(z)}`-modules representing `𝒦_{h(z)}` in `D(𝒪_{X,h(z)})` all
of whose determinantal ideals `I_i(C, a)` are principal.  Then

`Lh^*(Lη_I M) ≅ Lη_J(Lh^* M)`

in `D(𝒪_Y)`.

**No flatness of `h` is used**, which is what separates this from
`Stacks.Divisors.Eta.isIso_derivedEtaPullbackComparison`.  Presenting `M` by a K-flat complex of
flat modules is no restriction: `Stacks.Divisors.Eta.exists_kFlat_isFlat_rep'` produces one for
every object of `D(𝒪_X)`.  The auxiliary K-flat presentation of `η_I 𝒦` that the reduction
consumes is supplied here by the K-flat resolution of Stacks 06YF, so it is not a hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_derivedPullback_derivedEta_iso_of_forall_stalk_good
    (h𝒦 : Stacks.Cohomology.KFlatDerivedPullback.KFlatComplex X.toRingedSpace 𝒦)
    (hgood : ∀ z : Y, ∃ (a : ringStalk X.toRingedSpace (h.toLRSHom.toShHom.hom.base z))
        (_ : GeneratesStalkIdeal X.toRingedSpace (idealSheafι D)
          (h.toLRSHom.toShHom.hom.base z) a)
        (_ : GeneratesStalkIdeal Y.toRingedSpace
          (pullbackIdealIncl h.toLRSHom.toShHom (idealSheaf D) (idealSheafι D)) z
          (commStalkGermMap h.toLRSHom.toShHom z a))
        (C : BoundedComplex (ringStalk X.toRingedSpace (h.toLRSHom.toShHom.hom.base z))),
        (∀ i : ℤ, (idealI C a i).IsPrincipal) ∧
          Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj C.toCochainComplex ≅
            DerivedCategory.Q.obj
              (stalkComplex X.toRingedSpace (h.toLRSHom.toShHom.hom.base z) 𝒦)))
    (M : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj 𝒦 ≅ M) :
    Nonempty ((derivedPullback h.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ((derivedEtaData D).functor.obj M) ≅
      (derivedEtaData (D.comap h)).functor.obj
        ((derivedPullback h.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj M))
declarations.comment: the general case --- goodness in place of flatness, with goodness of the triple (Situation 0F8S) read at the stalks: at every point z of Y the stalk complex of the chosen representative is represented in the derived category of the local ring O_{X,h(z)} by a bounded complex C of finite free modules whose determinantal ideals I_i(C, a) are all principal, a being a generator of the stalk of the ideal sheaf. The passage from AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.IsGoodTriple to that stalkwise reading is AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.exists_affineOpen_stalk_goodModel, and the statement of the tag at a good triple is AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.nonempty_derivedPullback_derivedEta_iso. The case of a flat h, which neither implies nor is implied by this one, is Stacks.Divisors.Eta.isIso_derivedEtaPullbackComparison

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.derivedEtaPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F9X] for a flat morphism.**  Let `X`, `D`, `I`, `M` be as in Situation 0F8S,
let `h : Y ⟶ X` be a flat morphism of schemes such that the pullback `E = h^{-1}D` is defined,
and let `J = ℐ_E`.  Then

`Lh^*(Lη_I M) ≅ Lη_J(Lh^* M)`

in `D(𝒪_Y)`, where the right-hand side is the object of the pulled-back triple
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.pullback`.

The isomorphism is `Stacks.Divisors.Eta.derivedEtaPullbackIso`, conjugated by the presentation
`hKM` of `M` by a complex of `I`-torsion-free modules on each side.

The source's hypothesis that `(X, D, M)` is a good triple is **not** needed by this route and is
therefore not carried: the statement below is the flat case of tag 0F9X *without* goodness, which
is strictly stronger than the flat case of the source's statement.  Flatness, which the source
does not assume, is named in the attribute.
declarations.statement:
def derivedEtaPullbackIso (S : ComplexAndDivisorSituation.{u, d}) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (h : Y ⟶ S.X) [AlgebraicGeometry.Flat h]
    [hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsPullbackDefined h S.D]
    (K : CochainComplex
      (Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.TorsionFreeModule S.X.toRingedSpace (idealSheafι S.D)) ℤ)
    (hKM : DerivedCategory.Q.obj
      ((Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.torsionFreeComplex S.X.toRingedSpace
        (idealSheafι S.D)).obj K) ≅ S.standardObject) :
    (derivedPullback h.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        ((@Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.derivedEta S.X.toRingedSpace (idealSheaf S.D)
          (idealSheafι S.D) (Stacks.Divisors.Eta.mono_idealSheafι S.D)
          (Stacks.Divisors.Eta.isInvertible_idealSheaf S.D)
          (hasTorsionFreeResolutions S.D)).obj S.standardObject) ≅
      (@Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.derivedEta Y.toRingedSpace (idealSheaf (S.D.comap h))
          (idealSheafι (S.D.comap h)) (Stacks.Divisors.Eta.mono_idealSheafι (S.D.comap h))
          (Stacks.Divisors.Eta.isInvertible_idealSheaf (S.D.comap h))
          (hasTorsionFreeResolutions (S.D.comap h))).obj
        (S.derivedPullbackObject h)
declarations.comment: the case of a flat h, with no goodness hypothesis, which is therefore neither weaker nor stronger than the source's statement. the general case, for an arbitrary h and a good triple, is AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.nonempty_derivedPullback_derivedEta_iso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.nonempty_derivedPullback_derivedEta_iso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0F9X].**  Let `(X, D, M)` be a triple as in Situation 0F8S, with `ℐ` the ideal
sheaf of `D`, and let `h : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of schemes such that the inverse image
`E = h^{-1}D` is defined, with ideal sheaf `𝒥`.  If `(X, D, M)` is a good triple then

`Lh^*(Lη_ℐ M) ≅ Lη_𝒥(Lh^* M)`

in `D(𝒪_Y)`, the right-hand side being the décalage by the ideal sheaf of `E` of the object of
the pulled-back triple, i.e.
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.etaDerivedPullbackObject`.

No flatness of `h` is assumed.  The object is presented by a K-flat complex of flat modules —
which every object admits — and goodness is read at the stalks by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.exists_affineOpen_stalk_goodModel`, which also
supplies the generator of the stalk ideal whose germ generates the stalk ideal of `h^*ℐ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_derivedPullback_derivedEta_iso (hgood : S.IsGoodTriple) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (h : Y ⟶ S.X) (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsPullbackDefined h S.D) :
    Nonempty ((derivedPullback h.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        ((derivedEtaData S.D).functor.obj S.standardObject) ≅
      (derivedEtaData (S.D.comap h)).functor.obj (S.derivedPullbackObject h))
declarations.comment: the whole statement: for a good triple and an arbitrary morphism `h` along which the inverse image of the divisor is defined, `Lh^*(Lη_I M) ≅ Lη_J(Lh^* M)`. Goodness enters through its reading at the stalks, AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.exists_affineOpen_stalk_goodModel, and the ring-level input is Stacks 0F7X in the form Stacks.Eta.GoodBaseChange.quasiIso_baseChangeMap_comp_etaBaseChangeMap_of_kFlat. The case of a flat h without goodness is Stacks.Divisors.Eta.isIso_derivedEtaPullbackComparison

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.goodBlowupToBase_modification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0F9Y.**  Let `(X, D, M)` be as in Situation 0F8S, `W ⊆ X` the maximal open over
which the cohomology sheaves of `M` are locally free, `b : X' ⟶ X` the morphism of tag 0GTY,
`D' = b⁻¹D` with ideal sheaf `ℐ'`, and `Q = Lη_{ℐ'}Lb^*M`.  Then `b` is proper and

1. `b` is an isomorphism over `X ∖ D`,
2. `b` is an isomorphism over `W`,
3. `D'` is an effective Cartier divisor,
4. `Q = Lη_{ℐ'}Lb^*M`,
5. `Q` is perfect,
6. there is a closed immersion `i : T ⟶ D'` of finite presentation with (a) `D' ∩ b⁻¹(W) ⊆ T`
   scheme theoretically, (b) `H^n(Li^*Q)` finite locally free, and (c) for `t ∈ T` over
   `x ∈ W`, `H^n(Li^*Q)_t` free of the rank of `H^n(M)_x`,
7. over an affine chart `(U, A, f, M^•)` of `(X, D, M)`, `b⁻¹U ⟶ U` is the blowing up of `U` in
   `∏ᵢ I_i(M^•, f)`,
8. over an affine chart `(V, B, g, N^•)` of `(X', D', Lb^*M)` with every `I_i(N^•, g)`
   principal, (a) `Q|_V` is the sheaf attached to `η_g N^•`, and (b) `T ∩ V ⊆ D' ∩ V` is cut
   out by `J(N^•, g)`,
9. if `M` is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules, so is `Q`.

Clause (9) is printed with "bounded"; see the module docstring for why that is false and
"locally bounded" is the correct form.
declarations.statement:
theorem goodBlowupToBase_modification :
    IsProper S.goodBlowupToBase ∧
    IsIso (S.goodBlowupToBase ∣_ S.divisorComplement) ∧
    IsIso (S.goodBlowupToBase ∣_ S.locallyFreeLocus) ∧
    Stacks.Divisors.IsPullbackDefined S.goodBlowupToBase S.D ∧
    S.etaDerivedPullbackObject S.goodBlowupToBase S.isPullbackDefined_goodBlowupToBase =
      (Stacks.Divisors.Eta.derivedEtaData (S.D.comap S.goodBlowupToBase)).functor.obj
          (S.derivedPullbackObject S.goodBlowupToBase) ∧
    RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := S.goodBlowup.toRingedSpace)
      (S.etaDerivedPullbackObject S.goodBlowupToBase S.isPullbackDefined_goodBlowupToBase) ∧
    (∃ T : (S.D.comap S.goodBlowupToBase).subscheme.IdealSheafData,
      IsClosedImmersion T.subschemeι ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation T.subschemeι ∧
      T.comap ((S.D.comap S.goodBlowupToBase).subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ
          (S.goodBlowupToBase ⁻¹ᵁ S.locallyFreeLocus)).ι = ⊥ ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
        (S.etaDerivedPullbackRestrictHomology S.goodBlowupToBase
          S.isPullbackDefined_goodBlowupToBase
          (T.subschemeι ≫ (S.D.comap S.goodBlowupToBase).subschemeι) n)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℤ) (t : T.subscheme)
        (_ : ((T.subschemeι ≫ (S.D.comap S.goodBlowupToBase).subschemeι) ≫
          S.goodBlowupToBase).base t ∈ S.locallyFreeLocus),
        letI F := S.etaDerivedPullbackRestrictHomology S.goodBlowupToBase
          S.isPullbackDefined_goodBlowupToBase
          (T.subschemeι ≫ (S.D.comap S.goodBlowupToBase).subschemeι) n
        letI x := ((T.subschemeι ≫ (S.D.comap S.goodBlowupToBase).subschemeι) ≫
          S.goodBlowupToBase).base t
        letI : Module (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk T.subscheme.presheaf t))
            (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk F.val.presheaf t)) :=
          RingedSpace.moduleStalk (X := T.subscheme.toRingedSpace) F t
        letI : Module (ToType (S.X.presheaf.stalk x))
            (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (S.cohomologySheaf n).val.presheaf x)) :=
          RingedSpace.moduleStalk (X := S.X.toRingedSpace) (S.cohomologySheaf n) x
        Module.Free (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk T.subscheme.presheaf t))
            (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk F.val.presheaf t)) ∧
          Module.finrank (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk T.subscheme.presheaf t))
              (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk F.val.presheaf t)) =
            Module.finrank (ToType (S.X.presheaf.stalk x))
              (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (S.cohomologySheaf n).val.presheaf x))) ∧
      (∀ C : AffineChart (S.pullback S.goodBlowupToBase S.isPullbackDefined_goodBlowupToBase),
        (∀ i : ℤ, (C.determinantalIdeal i).IsPrincipal) →
          Nonempty ((RingedSpace.PseudoCoherence.restrictModules (S.pullback S.goodBlowupToBase
              S.isPullbackDefined_goodBlowupToBase).X.toRingedSpace C.U.1).mapDerivedCategory.obj
                (S.etaDerivedPullbackObject S.goodBlowupToBase
                  S.isPullbackDefined_goodBlowupToBase) ≅
            DerivedCategory.Q.obj C.specEtaComplex) ∧
          T.ideal C.divisorAffineOpen = C.obstructionIdeal)) ∧
    (∀ C : AffineChart S,
      ∃! e : (S.goodBlowupToBase ⁻¹ᵁ (C.U : S.X.Opens)).toScheme ≅
          AlgebraicGeometry.blowUp C.blowupCentreIdealSheaf,
        e.hom ≫ AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase C.blowupCentreIdealSheaf =
          S.goodBlowupToBase ∣_ (C.U : S.X.Opens)) ∧
    ((∃ ℳ : CochainComplex (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} S.X.toRingedSpace) ℤ,
        Stacks.Chow.IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree ℳ ∧
          Nonempty ((@DerivedCategory.Q _ _ _ S.hasDerivedCategory).obj ℳ ≅ S.M)) →
      ∃ 𝒬 : CochainComplex S.goodBlowup.Modules ℤ,
        Stacks.Chow.IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree 𝒬 ∧
          Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj 𝒬 ≅
            S.etaDerivedPullbackObject S.goodBlowupToBase
              S.isPullbackDefined_goodBlowupToBase))
declarations.comment: the full statement, with the morphism b of tag 0GTY (AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.goodBlowupToBase) as the witness and Q = Lη_{I'} Lb^* M: b proper and clauses (1)--(9), with T the closed subscheme of D' glued from the obstruction ideals J(N^•, g) of tag 0F81. Clause (9) is stated in its corrected form, Q represented by a LOCALLY BOUNDED complex of finite locally free modules (as tag 0GU0 gives): the printed 'bounded' is false for X = ⊔ₙ A¹, D the origins, M = O[n] on the n-th copy; see errata.md, entry 0F9Y (last sentence), 2026-10-27

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.exists_isProper_modification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0F9Y.**  Let `X` be a scheme, `D ⊆ X` an effective Cartier divisor and `M` a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`, and let `W ⊆ X` be the maximal open over which the cohomology
sheaves of `M` are locally free.  There are a proper morphism `b : X' ⟶ X` and an object `Q` of
`D(𝒪_{X'})` such that

1. `b` is an isomorphism over `X ∖ D`;
2. `b` is an isomorphism over `W`;
3. `D' = b⁻¹D` is an effective Cartier divisor;
4. `Q = Lη_{ℐ'}Lb^*M`, with `ℐ'` the ideal sheaf of `D'`;
5. `Q` is perfect;
6. there is a closed immersion `i : T ⟶ D'` of finite presentation with `D' ∩ b⁻¹(W) ⊆ T`
   scheme-theoretically, such that the cohomology sheaves of `Li^*Q` are finite locally free,
   and at a point `t ∈ T` over `W` the rank of `H^n(Li^*Q)` is the rank of `H^n(M)` at the image
   of `t`;
7. for every affine chart `(U, A, f, M^•)` of `(X, D, M)`, the part of `b` over `U` is the
   blowing up of `U` in `∏ᵢ I_i(M^•, f)`;
8. for every affine chart `(V, B, g, N^•)` of `(X', D', Lb^*M)` with principal `I_i(N^•, g)`,
   `Q|_V` is isomorphic to the complex associated with `η_g N^•`, and `T ∩ V` is cut out in
   `D' ∩ V` by `J(N^•, g) = ∑ᵢ J_i(N^•, g)`;
9. if `M` is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules, then
   `Q` is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free `𝒪_{X'}`-modules.

Here `b` is `goodBlowupToBase` (tag 0GTY), properness is `isProper_goodBlowupToBase`, clause (1)
is `IsGoodBlowup.isIso_resLE_divisorComplement`, clause (2) is tag 0F8W, clause (5) is tag 0F8U,
clause (6) is tag 0F8X with the subscheme of tag 0GTZ for the pulled-back triple, clause (7) is
`exists_isPullback_blowUpToBase`, clause (8) is the second assertion of tag 0GTV for the
pulled-back triple together with the defining property of that subscheme, and clause (9) is tag
0GU0.  Clause (9) asks for a locally bounded rather than a bounded complex; see the module
docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isProper_modification (S : ComplexAndDivisorSituation.{u, d}) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (b : X' ⟶ S.X), IsProper b ∧
      IsIso (b.resLE S.divisorComplement (b ⁻¹ᵁ S.divisorComplement) le_rfl) ∧
      IsIso (b.resLE S.locallyFreeLocus (b ⁻¹ᵁ S.locallyFreeLocus) le_rfl) ∧
      ∃ (hD' : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (S.D.comap b))
        (Q : DerivedCategory X'.Modules),
        Q = S.etaDerivedPullbackObject b hD' ∧
        RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X'.toRingedSpace) Q ∧
        (∃ T : (S.pullback b hD').D.subscheme.IdealSheafData,
          LocallyOfFinitePresentation T.subschemeι ∧
          T.comap ((S.pullback b hD').D.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ (b ⁻¹ᵁ S.locallyFreeLocus)).ι = ⊥ ∧
          (∀ n : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor T.subscheme.Modules n).obj
              ((derivedPullback
                (T.subschemeι ≫ (S.pullback b hD').D.subschemeι).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Q))) ∧
          (∀ (n : ℤ) (t : T.subscheme),
            ((T.subschemeι ≫ (S.pullback b hD').D.subschemeι) ≫ b) t ∈ S.locallyFreeLocus →
            Scheme.Modules.fiberRank
