                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor T.subscheme.Modules n).obj
                  ((derivedPullback
                    (T.subschemeι ≫ (S.pullback b hD').D.subschemeι).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Q))
                t =
              Scheme.Modules.fiberRank (S.cohomologySheaf n)
                (((T.subschemeι ≫ (S.pullback b hD').D.subschemeι) ≫ b) t)) ∧
          ∀ C : AffineChart (S.pullback b hD'), (∀ i : ℤ, (C.determinantalIdeal i).IsPrincipal) →
            T.ideal C.divisorAffineOpen = C.obstructionIdeal) ∧
        (∀ C : AffineChart S, ∃ e : blowUp C.blowupCentreIdealSheaf ⟶ X',
          IsPullback e (blowUpToBase C.blowupCentreIdealSheaf) b (C.U : S.X.Opens).ι) ∧
        (∀ C : AffineChart (S.pullback b hD'), (∀ i : ℤ, (C.determinantalIdeal i).IsPrincipal) →
          Nonempty ((RingedSpace.PseudoCoherence.restrictModules (S.pullback b hD').X.toRingedSpace
              C.U.1).mapDerivedCategory.obj Q ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj C.specEtaComplex)) ∧
        ((∃ ℳ : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} S.X.toRingedSpace) ℤ,
            Stacks.Chow.IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree ℳ ∧
              Nonempty ((@DerivedCategory.Q _ _ _ S.hasDerivedCategory).obj ℳ ≅ S.M)) →
          ∃ 𝒬 : CochainComplex X'.Modules ℤ,
            Stacks.Chow.IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree 𝒬 ∧
              Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj 𝒬 ≅ Q))
declarations.comment: the full statement in existential form: a proper b : X' ⟶ X and Q with clauses (1)--(9). Clause (9) is stated in its corrected form, Q represented by a LOCALLY BOUNDED complex of finite locally free modules (as tag 0GU0 gives): the printed 'bounded' is false for an infinite disjoint union; see errata.md, entry 0F9Y (last sentence), 2026-10-27

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestriction_comp
declarations.doc:
The restriction map of Stacks 0B7F is compatible with composition: restricting a class on `X`
along `f : Y ⟶ X` and then along `a : W ⟶ Y` gives the restriction along `a ≫ f`,

  `a^*(f^*(c)) = (a ≫ f)^*(c)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyRestriction_comp (c : chowCohomologyComponent C G sX p) :
    chowCohomologyRestriction C G (f ≫ sX) a p hgys
        (chowCohomologyRestriction C G sX f p hgys c) =
      chowCohomologyRestriction C G sX (a ≫ f) p hgys c
declarations.comment: compatibility with compositions, for the restriction map on Chow cohomology of Tag 0B7F

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantChowClass.restrict
declarations.doc:
The restriction `res(c) ∈ A^p(X' ⟶ Y')`, `X' = Y' ×_Y X`, of a bivariant class `c ∈ A^p(X ⟶ Y)`
along `h : Y' ⟶ Y`: a scheme `Y''` locally of finite type over `Y'` is one over `Y`, and
`res(c) ∩ α'' = c ∩ α''` for `α'' ∈ CH_k(Y'')` (`Stacks.Chow.BivariantChowClass.restrict_cap`).
declarations.statement:
def restrict (c : BivariantChowClass C sX sY f hf p) :
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_structure sY h hh
    BivariantChowClass C (pullback.fst f h ≫ sX) sY' (pullback.snd f h)
      (restrict_structure_eq hf h hh) p
declarations.comment: the restriction map A^p(X → Y) → A^p(X' → Y'), c ↦ res(c)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantChowClass.restrict_cap
declarations.doc:
`res(c) ∩ α'' = c ∩ α''`: for `g : Y'' ⟶ Y'` and `α'' ∈ CH_k(Y'')`, the cap of the restriction
is the cap of `c` at `g ≫ h`, read on `(Y' ×_Y X) ×_{Y'} Y''` through the canonical isomorphism
with `Y'' ×_Y X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrict_cap (c : BivariantChowClass C sX sY f hf p) {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y')
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ sY') k) :
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_structure sY h hh
    (c.restrict h hh).cap g k α =
      chowPushforwardOfIso C (pullback.fst f (g ≫ h) ≫ sX)
        (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f h) g ≫ (pullback.fst f h ≫ sX))
        (pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso f h g).inv (by simp) (k - p)
        (c.cap (g ≫ h) k (chowGroupCongr C (by rw [Category.assoc, hh]) k α))
declarations.comment: res(c) ∩ α'' = c ∩ α''

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantChowClass.restrict_restrict
declarations.doc:
Restriction is compatible with compositions of base changes: restricting `c` along `h : Y' ⟶ Y`
and then along `h' : Y'' ⟶ Y'` is restricting `c` along `h' ≫ h`, the two classes agreeing after
the canonical identification `(X ×_Y Y') ×_{Y'} Y'' ≅ X ×_Y Y''` of their sources.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrict_restrict {Y'' : Scheme.{u}} {sY'' : Y'' ⟶ C.S} [LocallyOfFiniteType sY'']
    (h' : Y'' ⟶ Y') (hh' : h' ≫ sY' = sY'') (c : BivariantChowClass C sX sY f hf p) :
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_structure sY h hh
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_structure sY' h' hh'
    ((c.restrict h hh).restrict h' hh').transport
        (restrict_structure_eq hf (h' ≫ h) (by rw [Category.assoc, hh, hh']))
        (pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso f h h') (pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso_hom_snd f h h') =
      c.restrict (h' ≫ h) (by rw [Category.assoc, hh, hh'])
declarations.comment: compatibility with compositions: res along Y'' → Y' after res along Y' → Y is res along Y'' → Y

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantChowClass.restrict_comp
declarations.doc:
Restriction is compatible with the composition of bivariant classes. For `a ∈ A^p(X ⟶ Y)`,
`b ∈ A^q(Y ⟶ Z)` and `h : Z' ⟶ Z`, write `Y' = Y ×_Z Z'` and `X' = X ×_Y Y' = X ×_Z Z'`; then
`res(a ∘ b) = res(a) ∘ res(b)` in `A^{p+q}(X' ⟶ Z')`, where `res(a) ∈ A^p(X ×_Y Y' ⟶ Y')` is the
restriction along `Y' ⟶ Y` and `res(b) ∈ A^q(Y' ⟶ Z')` the restriction along `h`. The two sources
are identified by the canonical isomorphism `X ×_Y (Y ×_Z Z') ≅ X ×_Z Z'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrict_comp {Z' : Scheme.{u}} {sZ' : Z' ⟶ C.S} [LocallyOfFiniteType sZ'] (h : Z' ⟶ Z)
    (hh : h ≫ sZ = sZ') (a : BivariantChowClass C sX sY f hf p)
    (b : BivariantChowClass C sY sZ g hg q) :
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_structure sZ h hh
    ((a.restrict (pullback.fst g h) rfl).comp (b.restrict h hh)).transport
        (restrict_structure_eq (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hf hg) h hh)
        (pullbackRightPullbackFstIso g h f) (pullbackRightPullbackFstIso_hom_snd g h f) =
      (a.comp b).restrict h hh
declarations.comment: compatibility with compositions: res(a ∘ b) = res(a) ∘ res(b)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestrictionCap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9Z.** The cap operation `res(c) ∩ -` of the restriction of a bivariant class `c`
of degree `p` for `f : X ⟶ Y` along `h : Y' ⟶ Y`: on a test scheme `g : T ⟶ Y'` it is the cap
operation of `c` at `g ≫ h`, pushed forward along the canonical isomorphism
`T ×_Y X ≅ (Y' ×_Y X) ×_{Y'} T`.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantRestrictionCap (c : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p) {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y')
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ) :
    chowGroup C (g ≫ (h ≫ sY)) k →+
      chowGroup C (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f h) g ≫ (pullback.fst f h ≫ sX)) (k - p)
declarations.comment: the cap operation of the restriction

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9Z.** The restriction `res(c)` of a bivariant class `c` of degree `p` for
`f : X ⟶ Y` along `h : Y' ⟶ Y`: the bivariant class of degree `p` for the base change
`X ×_Y Y' ⟶ Y'` with `res(c) ∩ α = c ∩ α`. Together with
`Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestriction_add`, `_neg` and `_zero` this is the restriction map
`A^p(X ⟶ Y) ⟶ A^p(X' ⟶ Y')` of the tag.

The Gysin axiom of a restricted class is not a consequence of the axioms of `c`, so the
construction carries the isomorphism case of Stacks 02TA for the Gysin system; see the
implementation notes of `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.Bivariant.Restriction`.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantRestriction (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso)
    (c : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p) :
    BivariantClass C G (pullback.fst f h ≫ sX) (h ≫ sY) (pullback.snd f h)
      (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf h) p

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestrictionAddHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9Z.** The restriction map `A^p(X ⟶ Y) ⟶ A^p(X' ⟶ Y')` along `h : Y' ⟶ Y`, as a
homomorphism of groups.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantRestrictionAddHom (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso) :
    BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p →+
      BivariantClass C G (pullback.fst f h ≫ sX) (h ≫ sY) (pullback.snd f h)
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf h) p

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestrictionCap_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9Z.** Restriction of a bivariant class is compatible with composition of base
changes: if `c'` is the restriction of `c` along `h`, then the restriction of `c'` along `h'` caps
exactly as the restriction of `c` along `h' ≫ h`, after the canonical identification of the two
iterated fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantRestrictionCap_comp (c : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p)
    (c' : BivariantClass C G (pullback.fst f h ≫ sX) (h ≫ sY) (pullback.snd f h)
      (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf h) p)
    (hc' : IsBivariantRestriction C G sX sY f hf h p c c') {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y'')
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ (h' ≫ (h ≫ sY))) k) :
    chowPushforwardOfIso C
        (pullback.fst (pullback.snd (pullback.snd f h) h') g ≫
          (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f h) h' ≫ (pullback.fst f h ≫ sX)))
        (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f (h' ≫ h)) g ≫ (pullback.fst f (h' ≫ h) ≫ sX))
        (iteratedRestrictionIso f h h' g).hom
        (iteratedRestrictionIso_hom_comp C sX f h h' g) (k - p)
        (bivariantRestrictionCap C G (pullback.fst f h ≫ sX) (h ≫ sY) (pullback.snd f h)
          (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf h) h' p c' g k α) =
      bivariantRestrictionCap C G sX sY f hf (h' ≫ h) p c g k
        (chowGroupCongr C (congrArg (g ≫ ·) (Category.assoc h' h sY).symm) k α)
declarations.comment: compatibility with compositions, on cap operations

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestriction_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9Z.** Restriction is compatible with composition of base changes: restricting
along `h` and then along `h'` agrees with restricting along `h' ≫ h`, after the canonical
identification of the two iterated fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantRestriction_comp (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso)
    (c : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p) {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y'')
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ (h' ≫ (h ≫ sY))) k) :
    chowPushforwardOfIso C
        (pullback.fst (pullback.snd (pullback.snd f h) h') g ≫
          (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f h) h' ≫ (pullback.fst f h ≫ sX)))
        (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f (h' ≫ h)) g ≫ (pullback.fst f (h' ≫ h) ≫ sX))
        (iteratedRestrictionIso f h h' g).hom
        (iteratedRestrictionIso_hom_comp C sX f h h' g) (k - p)
        ((bivariantRestriction C G (pullback.fst f h ≫ sX) (h ≫ sY) (pullback.snd f h)
          (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf h) h' p hgys
          (bivariantRestriction C G sX sY f hf h p hgys c)).cap g k α) =
      (bivariantRestriction C G sX sY f hf (h' ≫ h) p hgys c).cap g k
        (chowGroupCongr C (congrArg (g ≫ ·) (Category.assoc h' h sY).symm) k α)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isBivariantTransport_bivariantComposite_bivariantRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9Z, compatibility with the composition of bivariant classes.** The restriction of
the composite `a ∘ b` of Stacks 0B75 along `h : W ⟶ Z` caps exactly as the composite of the
restriction of `a` along `pullback.fst g h` with the restriction of `b` along `h`, read through
the comparison isomorphism `X ×_Y (Y ×_Z W) ≅ X ×_Z W` of the two sources.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBivariantTransport_bivariantComposite_bivariantRestriction
    (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso)
    (hgysc : G.IsNaturalUnderPullbackCompPushforward) :
    IsBivariantTransport C G (pullback.fst f (pullback.fst g h) ≫ sX)
      (pullback.fst (f ≫ g) h ≫ sX) (h ≫ sZ)
      (pullback.snd f (pullback.fst g h) ≫ pullback.snd g h)
      (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf (pullback.fst g h))
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sY sZ g hg h))
      (pullback.snd (f ≫ g) h)
      (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sZ (f ≫ g)
        (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hf hg) h)
      (pullbackRightPullbackFstIso g h f)
      (pullbackRightPullbackFstIso_hom_comp_snd f g h) (p + q)
      (bivariantComposite C G (pullback.fst f (pullback.fst g h) ≫ sX)
        (pullback.fst g h ≫ sY) (h ≫ sZ) (pullback.snd f (pullback.fst g h))
        (pullback.snd g h)
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf (pullback.fst g h))
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sY sZ g hg h) p q
        (bivariantRestriction C G sX sY f hf (pullback.fst g h) p hgys a)
        (bivariantRestriction C G sY sZ g hg h q hgys b) hgys hgysc)
      (bivariantRestriction C G sX sZ (f ≫ g) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hf hg) h (p + q)
        hgys
        (bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a b hgys hgysc))
declarations.comment: the clause `res(a ∘ b) = res(a) ∘ res(b)`: restriction commutes with the composition of bivariant classes of Tag 0B75, on cap operations, read through the comparison isomorphism of the two readings of the source fibre product. The compatibility with the composition of BASE CHANGES is the separate Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestrictionCap_comp

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantTransport_bivariantComposite_bivariantRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9Z, compatibility with the composition of bivariant classes**, as an identity of
bivariant classes: the transport along `X ×_Y (Y ×_Z W) ≅ X ×_Z W` of the composite of the
restrictions is the restriction of the composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantTransport_bivariantComposite_bivariantRestriction
    (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso)
    (hgysc : G.IsNaturalUnderPullbackCompPushforward) :
    bivariantTransport C G (pullback.fst f (pullback.fst g h) ≫ sX)
        (pullback.fst (f ≫ g) h ≫ sX) (h ≫ sZ)
        (pullback.snd f (pullback.fst g h) ≫ pullback.snd g h)
        (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq
          (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf (pullback.fst g h))
          (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sY sZ g hg h))
        (pullback.snd (f ≫ g) h)
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sZ (f ≫ g)
          (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hf hg) h)
        (pullbackRightPullbackFstIso g h f)
        (pullbackRightPullbackFstIso_hom_comp_snd f g h) (p + q) hgys
        (bivariantComposite C G (pullback.fst f (pullback.fst g h) ≫ sX)
          (pullback.fst g h ≫ sY) (h ≫ sZ) (pullback.snd f (pullback.fst g h))
          (pullback.snd g h)
          (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf (pullback.fst g h))
          (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sY sZ g hg h) p q
          (bivariantRestriction C G sX sY f hf (pullback.fst g h) p hgys a)
          (bivariantRestriction C G sY sZ g hg h q hgys b) hgys hgysc) =
      bivariantRestriction C G sX sZ (f ≫ g) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hf hg) h (p + q)
        hgys (bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a b hgys hgysc)
declarations.comment: the clause `res(a ∘ b) = res(a) ∘ res(b)` as an equality of bivariant classes, the composition being that of Tag 0B75 and the transport the comparison isomorphism of the two readings of the source fibre product

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantRestrictionViaSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0F9Z on completions.** The restriction
`res : A^*(X ⟶ Y)^∧ ⟶ A^*(X ×_Y Y' ⟶ Y')^∧` of completed bivariant classes (Stacks 0FE0) along
`h : Y' ⟶ Y`, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule: reading an element of the
completed group as the tuple `(c_p)_p` of Stacks 0FE0, it is the tuple `(res(c_p))_p` of the
restrictions of Stacks 0F9Z, which again vanishes in almost all degrees on each connected
component.
declarations.statement:
def completedBivariantRestrictionViaSequence :
    completedBivariantGroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf →+
      completedBivariantGroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.fst f h ≫ sX) (h ≫ sY)
        (pullback.snd f h) (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf h)
declarations.comment: the restriction on the completed bivariant groups A^*(X → Y)^∧ → A^*(X' → Y')^∧

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The restriction `res(c)` of a bivariant class `c ∈ A^p(X ⟶ Y)` along a morphism
`b : Y' ⟶ Y`, for the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule of an invertible module: the
bivariant class of degree `p` for the base change `X ×_Y Y' ⟶ Y'` with `res(c) ∩ α = c ∩ α`.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible
    (c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf p) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.fst f b ≫ sX) (b ≫ sY)
      (pullback.snd f b) (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf b) p

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible_cap
declarations.doc:
The restriction caps by the cap operation of `c`: `res(c) ∩ α = c ∩ α`, after the canonical
identification of the two fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible_cap
    (c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf p) {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : T ⟶ Y') [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ (b ≫ sY)) k) :
    (bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible C sX sY f hf b p c).cap g k α =
      bivariantRestrictionCap C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf b p c g k α

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestrictionAddHomOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The restriction map `A^p(X ⟶ Y) ⟶ A^p(X' ⟶ Y')` along `b : Y' ⟶ Y`, as a homomorphism of
groups, for the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule of an invertible module.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantRestrictionAddHomOfInvertible :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf p →+
      BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.fst f b ≫ sX) (b ≫ sY)
        (pullback.snd f b) (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf b) p

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible_comp
declarations.doc:
Restriction is compatible with composition of base changes: restricting along `b` and then
along `b'` agrees with restricting along `b' ≫ b`, after the canonical identification of the two
iterated fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible_comp
    (c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf p) {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : T ⟶ Y'') [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ (b' ≫ (b ≫ sY))) k) :
    chowPushforwardOfIso C
        (pullback.fst (pullback.snd (pullback.snd f b) b') g ≫
          (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f b) b' ≫ (pullback.fst f b ≫ sX)))
        (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f (b' ≫ b)) g ≫ (pullback.fst f (b' ≫ b) ≫ sX))
        (iteratedRestrictionIso f b b' g).hom
        (iteratedRestrictionIso_hom_comp C sX f b b' g) (k - p)
        ((bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible C (pullback.fst f b ≫ sX) (b ≫ sY)
          (pullback.snd f b) (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf b) b' p
          (bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible C sX sY f hf b p c)).cap g k α) =
      (bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible C sX sY f hf (b' ≫ b) p c).cap g k
        (chowGroupCongr C (congrArg (g ≫ ·) (Category.assoc b' b sY).symm) k α)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGrading
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0.** The group `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` attached to a closed immersion `f : Z ⟶ X` of
schemes locally of finite type over the base: operational Chow classes on `X` in the degrees
below `p`, and bivariant classes for `f` in the degrees from `p` onward.
declarations.comment: localized_bivariant_grading

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMulHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0.** The multiplication
`A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X) × A⁽ᑫ⁾(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A⁽ʳ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` of the remark as a **biadditive map**, at every `p`, `q`
and every target `r`. This is the distributive law of the source's graded algebra, bundled: the
underlying function is `Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMul` and the additivity in each
argument is `Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMul_add_left` and `_add_right`.
declarations.statement:
def localizedBivariantGradingMulHom (p q r : ℕ) :
    localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p →+
      localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl q →+
        localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl r
declarations.comment: the multiplication of the remark's graded algebra as a biadditive map A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^(q)(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^(r)(Z ⟶ X), which is its distributive law, at every p, q and every target r

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMulMaxHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0.** The multiplication with the target `A⁽ᵐᵃˣ⁽ᵖ⁼ᑫ⁾⁾(Z ⟶ X)` the source displays,
as a biadditive map.
declarations.statement:
def localizedBivariantGradingMulMaxHom (p q : ℕ) :
    localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p →+
      localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl q →+
        localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl (max p q)
declarations.comment: the multiplication A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) × A^(q)(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^(max(p,q))(Z ⟶ X) displayed in the remark as a biadditive map, for every p and q

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0.** The multiplication internal to `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` — the product of the source's
graded algebra — as a biadditive map, for every `p ≥ 0`.
declarations.statement:
def localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulHom (p : ℕ) :
    localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p →+
      localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p →+
        localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p
declarations.comment: the multiplication internal to A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) of the remark's graded algebra as a biadditive map A^(p) ⟶ A^(p) ⟶ A^(p), which is its distributive law, for every p ≥ 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.eq_localizedBivariantGradingMulHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, uniqueness of the canonical multiplication as a biadditive map.** A biadditive
map whose components are the two finite convolutions of the source — the property
`Stacks.Chow.LocalizedGrading.IsMul` — is `Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMulHom`. This is
`Stacks.Chow.LocalizedGrading.IsMul.eq_localizedBivariantGradingMul` read through
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMulHom_apply`; additivity is not used in the uniqueness, the
component formulas already prescribing every value.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_localizedBivariantGradingMulHom (p q r : ℕ)
    (M : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p →+
      localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl q →+
        localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl r)
    (hM : LocalizedGrading.IsMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p q r fun a b ↦ M a b) :
    M = localizedBivariantGradingMulHom C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p q r
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the canonical multiplication as a biadditive map: a biadditive map satisfying the two finite-convolution formulas of the remark is the multiplication

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, the unit of the graded algebra on `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`:** the element whose degree `0`
component is the class `1 ∈ A⁰(X)` of Stacks 0FBS and whose components in the other degrees
vanish.

For `p ≥ 1` the degree `0` slot of `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` is `A⁰(X)` and this is the unit; for `p = 0` that
slot is `A⁰(Z ⟶ X)`, which holds no canonical class, and this element is zero there. Together with
`Stacks.Chow.localizedGrading_self_admissible_iff` that makes `p = 1` the one `p` at which the
source's graded algebra on `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` is unital.
declarations.statement:
def localizedBivariantGradingOne (p : ℕ) :
    localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p
declarations.comment: the unit of the remark's graded algebra on A^(p)(Z ⟶ X): the class 1 of A^0(X) in the degree 0 slot, which is a slot of A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) exactly for p ≥ 1

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_one_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, the unit law of the graded algebra on `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`, for every `p ≥ 1`:**
multiplying by `Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingOne` on the left returns the element. The
bound `1 ≤ p` is what puts the degree `0` slot, where the unit sits, in `A⁰(X)`; for `p = 0` that
slot is `A⁰(Z ⟶ X)` and holds no canonical class.

Degree by degree the product has a single surviving term, the one at `i = 0`: below the cutoff it
is `1 · bₙ` in `A^*(X)` (`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyComposite_identityClass_left`), and from the
cutoff on it is the source's second pairing at the unit
(`Stacks.Chow.localizedMulChowBivariant_identityClass_left`), which is `res(1) ∘ bₙ = bₙ`.

No hypothesis is imposed on `b`: the index range of the sums,
`Finset.Icc (min 0 n) (max 0 n)`, contains the one surviving index `i = 0` in every degree
(`Stacks.Chow.zero_mem_Icc_min_max`), so the law holds on all of `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` — which is the group
the source asserts the graded algebra on, negative-degree factors included. See the implementation
notes of this module.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_one_left (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p)
    (b : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p) :
    localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p
        (localizedBivariantGradingOne C G sX f hgysinX p) b = b
declarations.comment: the unit law of the remark's graded algebra on A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) for every p ≥ 1: the class 1 of A^0(X) placed in degree 0 is a left unit for the multiplication internal to A^(p)(Z ⟶ X), on all of A^(p)(Z ⟶ X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_one_right
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, the unit law of the graded algebra on `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` on the right, for every
`p ≥ 1`:** multiplying by `Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingOne` on the right returns the
element. Together with `Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_one_left` this makes
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingOne` a two-sided unit, and with the associativity of
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_assoc` it is what
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMonoid` is assembled from.

Here the surviving term of the degree `n` component is the one at `i = n`, and the pairing that
applies is the source's *first* one, `Stacks.Chow.localizedMulBivariantChow_identityClass_right`:
`bₙ ∘ 1 = bₙ`.

This law is the sharp test of the index range of the sums: the component of `b` it has to return
in degree `n` is carried by the term at `i = n` alone. The range
`Finset.Icc (min 0 n) (max 0 n)` contains `i = n` in every degree
(`Stacks.Chow.self_mem_Icc_min_max`), so the law needs no hypothesis on `b` and holds on all of
`A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`; under the narrower range `0 ≤ i ≤ n` it would fail in every negative degree in which
`b` has a nonzero component. See the implementation notes of this module.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_one_right (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p)
    (b : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p) :
    localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p b
        (localizedBivariantGradingOne C G sX f hgysinX p) = b
declarations.comment: the unit law of the remark's graded algebra on A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) on the right for every p ≥ 1: the class 1 of A^0(X) placed in degree 0 is a right unit for the multiplication internal to A^(p)(Z ⟶ X), on all of A^(p)(Z ⟶ X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulHomOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0.** The multiplication internal to `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` of the remark's graded algebra
as a biadditive map, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, where nothing is
assumed.
declarations.statement:
def localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulHomOfInvertible (p : ℕ) :
    localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p →+
      localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p →+
        localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p
declarations.comment: the multiplication internal to A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) of the remark's graded algebra as a biadditive map, which is its distributive law, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule with nothing assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingOneOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, the unit of the graded algebra** at the Gysin system of the first Chern class
rule, where nothing is assumed: its degree `0` component is
`Stacks.Chow.bivariantIdentityClassOfInvertible`.
declarations.statement:
def localizedBivariantGradingOneOfInvertible (p : ℕ) :
    localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p
declarations.comment: the unit of the remark's graded algebra on A^(p)(Z ⟶ X), at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule with nothing assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_one_left_ofInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, the unit law of the graded algebra on `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` for every `p ≥ 1`** at the
Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, where nothing at all is assumed: the law holds on all
of `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_one_left_ofInvertible (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p)
    (b : localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p) :
    localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulHomOfInvertible C sX f p
        (localizedBivariantGradingOneOfInvertible C sX f p) b = b
declarations.comment: the unit law of the remark's graded algebra on A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) for every p ≥ 1, on all of A^(p)(Z ⟶ X), at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule with NOTHING ASSUMED

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_one_right_ofInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, the unit law of the graded algebra on `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` on the right, for every
`p ≥ 1`** at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, where nothing at all is assumed: the
law holds on all of `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_one_right_ofInvertible (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p)
    (b : localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p) :
    localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulHomOfInvertible C sX f p b
        (localizedBivariantGradingOneOfInvertible C sX f p) = b
declarations.comment: the unit law of the remark's graded algebra on A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) on the right for every p ≥ 1: the class 1 of A^0(X) placed in degree 0 is a right unit for the multiplication internal to A^(p)(Z ⟶ X), on all of A^(p)(Z ⟶ X), at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule with NOTHING ASSUMED

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedMulBivariantChow
declarations.doc:
The first of the three pairings: `A^i(Z ⟶ X) × A^j(X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X)`, composition of
bivariant classes, read through the equality `f ≫ 𝟙 X = f`.
declarations.statement:
def localizedMulBivariantChow (i j : ℤ) (c : BivariantClass C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl i)
    (b : chowCohomologyComponent C G sX j) : BivariantClass C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl (i + j)
declarations.comment: the pairing A^i(Z ⟶ X) × A^j(X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X) of the remark, composition of bivariant classes

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedMulChowBivariant
declarations.doc:
The second of the three pairings: `A^i(X) × A^j(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X)`, the restriction
`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestriction : A^i(X) ⟶ A^i(Z)` followed by the composition
`A^i(Z) × A^j(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X)`.
declarations.comment: the pairing A^i(X) × A^j(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X) of the remark, the restriction A^i(X) ⟶ A^i(Z) of Stacks 0F9Z followed by composition

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedMulBivariant
declarations.doc:
The third of the three pairings: `A^i(Z ⟶ X) × A^j(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X)`, sending
`(c, c')` to `res(c) ∘ c'` for the restriction
`res = Stacks.Chow.closedImmersionChowCohomologyRestriction : A^i(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^i(Z)`.
declarations.comment: the pairing A^i(Z ⟶ X) × A^j(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X) of the remark, (c, c') ↦ res(c) ∘ c' for the restriction res of Stacks 0F9Z

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMul
declarations.doc:
The multiplication `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X) × A⁽ᑫ⁾(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A⁽ʳ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` attached to a closed immersion
`f : Z ⟶ X` of schemes locally of finite type over the base, at every `p`, `q` and every target
`r`. Its degree `n` component is the sum over `i ∈ Finset.Icc (min 0 n) (max 0 n)` of the
products of the degree `i` component of the first factor with the degree `n - i` component of the
second: for `n < r` the localized factors are pushed forward to `A^*(X)` and the product is taken
in `A^*(X)` (`Stacks.Chow.localizedGradingMulAmbientTerm`), and for `n ≥ r` the term is the one of
the three pairings `Stacks.Chow.localizedMulBivariantChow`,
`Stacks.Chow.localizedMulChowBivariant`, `Stacks.Chow.localizedMulBivariant` that applies, and
`0` on the pairs `i < p`, `n - i < q` (`Stacks.Chow.localizedGradingMulLocalizedTerm`).
declarations.statement:
def localizedBivariantGradingMul (p q r : ℕ)
    (a : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p)
    (b : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl q) :
    localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl r
declarations.comment: the canonical multiplication A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) × A^(q)(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^(r)(Z ⟶ X) of the remark at every p, q and every target r, assembled degreewise from the three pairings and the pushforward of Stacks 0EPK; its associativity, which the source omits, is localizedBivariantGradingMul_assoc

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMulMax
declarations.doc:
The multiplication `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X) × A⁽ᑫ⁾(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A⁽ᵐᵃˣ⁽ᵖ⁼ᑫ⁾⁾(Z ⟶ X)`, for every `p` and `q`:
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMul` at `r = max(p, q)`.
declarations.statement:
def localizedBivariantGradingMulMax (p q : ℕ)
    (a : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p)
    (b : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl q) :
    localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl (max p q)
declarations.comment: the multiplication A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) × A^(q)(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^(max(p,q))(Z ⟶ X) displayed in the remark, for every p and q

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul
declarations.doc:
The multiplication internal to `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`, for every `p ≥ 0`:
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMul` at `r = p = q`.
declarations.comment: the multiplication internal to A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) of the remark's graded algebra, for every p ≥ 0; it is graded, and additive in each argument by localizedBivariantGradingMul_add_left and _add_right

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMul_fst
declarations.doc:
**The component formula below the cutoff of the target.** For `n < r`, the degree `n`
component of a product is the finite convolution `∑ aᵢ · bₙ₋ᵢ` over
`i ∈ Finset.Icc (min 0 n) (max 0 n)`, taken in `A^*(X)`
(`Stacks.Chow.localizedGradingMulAmbientTerm`).
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedBivariantGradingMul_fst (p q r : ℕ)
    (a : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p)
    (b : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl q) (n : {n : ℤ // n < (r : ℤ)}) :
    (localizedBivariantGradingMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p q r a b).1 n =
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc (min 0 n.1) (max 0 n.1),
        localizedGradingMulAmbientTerm C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p q a b n.1 i
declarations.comment: the finite-convolution formula for the degree n part of a product in a degree n below the cutoff of the target: the sum over i + j = n of the products of the degree i and degree j parts of the factors, pushed into A^*(X) by Stacks 0EPK and multiplied there

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMul_snd
declarations.doc:
**The component formula from the cutoff of the target on.** For `n ≥ r`, the degree `n`
component of a product is the finite convolution `∑ aᵢ · bₙ₋ᵢ` over
`i ∈ Finset.Icc (min 0 n) (max 0 n)`, taken in `A^*(Z ⟶ X)`
(`Stacks.Chow.localizedGradingMulLocalizedTerm`).
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedBivariantGradingMul_snd (p q r : ℕ)
    (a : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p)
    (b : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl q) (n : {n : ℤ // (r : ℤ) ≤ n}) :
    (localizedBivariantGradingMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p q r a b).2 n =
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc (min 0 n.1) (max 0 n.1),
        localizedGradingMulLocalizedTerm C G sX f hgys hgysc p q a b n.1 i
declarations.comment: the finite-convolution formula for the degree n part of a product in a degree n at or above the cutoff of the target: the sum over i + j = n of the products of the degree i and degree j parts of the factors under the three pairings of the remark

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.LocalizedGrading.IsMul.eq
declarations.doc:
**Uniqueness of the multiplication.** Any two maps satisfying the two component formulas
`Stacks.Chow.LocalizedGrading.IsMul` are equal; nothing else, not even additivity, is assumed of
them.
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the canonical multiplication: the two finite-convolution formulas determine it degreewise, so any two maps satisfying them are equal

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedMulBivariantChowOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The first pairing `A^i(Z ⟶ X) × A^j(X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X)` at the Gysin system
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`, with no hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
def localizedMulBivariantChowOfInvertible (i j : ℤ)
    (c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl i)
    (b : chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX j) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl (i + j)
declarations.comment: the pairing A^i(Z ⟶ X) × A^j(X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X) of the remark, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with nothing assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedMulChowBivariantOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The second pairing `A^i(X) × A^j(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X)` at the Gysin system
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`, with no hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
def localizedMulChowBivariantOfInvertible (i j : ℤ)
    (a : chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX i)
    (c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl j) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl (i + j)
declarations.comment: the pairing A^i(X) × A^j(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X) of the remark, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with nothing assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedMulBivariantOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The third pairing `A^i(Z ⟶ X) × A^j(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X)`, `(c, c') ↦ res(c) ∘ c'`, at the
Gysin system `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`, with no hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
def localizedMulBivariantOfInvertible (i j : ℤ)
    (c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl i)
    (c' : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl j) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl (i + j)
declarations.comment: the pairing A^i(Z ⟶ X) × A^j(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^{i+j}(Z ⟶ X) of the remark, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with nothing assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMulOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The multiplication `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X) × A⁽ᑫ⁾(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A⁽ʳ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`, at every `p`, `q` and every
target `r`, at the Gysin system `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`, with no hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
def localizedBivariantGradingMulOfInvertible (p q r : ℕ)
    (a : localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p)
    (b : localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl q) :
    localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl r
declarations.comment: the canonical multiplication A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) × A^(q)(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^(r)(Z ⟶ X) of the remark at every p, q and every target r, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with NOTHING ASSUMED: every Gysin compatibility is discharged there and Stacks 02RG on Chow groups, which the pushforward of Stacks 0EPK costs, is a theorem of this repository; its associativity, which the source omits, is localizedBivariantGradingMulOfInvertible_assoc

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMulMaxOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The multiplication `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X) × A⁽ᑫ⁾(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A⁽ᵐᵃˣ⁽ᵖ⁼ᑫ⁾⁾(Z ⟶ X)`, for every `p` and `q`,
at the Gysin system `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`, with no hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
def localizedBivariantGradingMulMaxOfInvertible (p q : ℕ)
    (a : localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p)
    (b : localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl q) :
    localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl (max p q)
declarations.comment: the multiplication A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) × A^(q)(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^(max(p,q))(Z ⟶ X) displayed in the remark, for every p and q, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule with nothing assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The multiplication internal to `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`, for every `p ≥ 0`, at the Gysin system
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`, with no hypotheses.
declarations.comment: the multiplication internal to A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) of the remark's graded algebra for every p ≥ 0, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule with nothing assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMul_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, associativity of the canonical multiplication**
`A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X) × A⁽ᑫ⁾(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A⁽ʳ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`: for `a ∈ A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`, `b ∈ A⁽ᑫ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`,
`c ∈ A⁽ˢ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` the two groupings `(a · b) · c` and `a · (b · c)` of a triple product agree, at
every pair of intermediate targets `A⁽ʳ¹⁾(Z ⟶ X)`, `A⁽ʳ²⁾(Z ⟶ X)` and every common target
`A⁽ʳ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` whose cutoffs satisfy the four inequalities below, which together come to
`p + q + s ≤ r + 2`. This is "the verification that these multiplications are associative in a
suitable sense" that the source omits, carried out in the range where every term of every grouping
is one of the source's own three pairings — no pair of degrees the remark leaves unprescribed
occurs. That covers every product the chapter forms: `r₁ = max(p, q)`, the target the source
displays (`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMulMax`), qualifies for `min(p, q) ≤ 1`, and so
does `r₁ = p + q`, the target at which Stacks 0FAL and Stacks 0FAY state their products. The
product internal to `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` of the source's graded algebra, where all six targets are
`p ≤ 1`, is the corollary `Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_assoc`; what
associativity of that product would come to for `p ≥ 2` is
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_singleLow_eq_zero_of_assoc`.

It is an equality and not a heterogeneous equality because the common target `r` is a parameter;
the degrees of the intermediate products are the arguments `r₁`, `r₂`, which the two groupings
bracket differently. Degreewise the two sides are the same double convolution of the three
factors' components written in the two decompositions `(m, i - m, n - i)` and `(m, j, n - m - j)`
of the total degree `n`, and the proof is exactly the two pieces the implementation notes name:
the reindexing `Stacks.Chow.sum_Icc_diag_flip` of that double convolution, and — term by term —
the three instances of the associativity of Stacks 0B75 for the pairings, read through the
transports the pairings carry by `Stacks.Chow.bivariantClassDegreeCongr_eq_of_heq`. Below the
cutoff of the target both sides are the double convolution in `A^*(X)`
(`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMul_isAmbientConvolution`) and the input is the
associativity of the multiplication of `A^*(X)`,
`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyComposite_assoc`; at or above it one of the three pairings applies to
each term, and where an intermediate product was read in `A^*(X)` the comparison also needs
`Stacks.Chow.localizedMulChowBivariant_localizedGradingPushforward_eq`, that a localized factor
may be pushed forward by Stacks 0EPK before it is multiplied on the left.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedBivariantGradingMul_assoc (p q s r₁ r₂ r : ℕ) (h₁ : p + q ≤ r₁ + 1)
    (h₂ : r₁ + s ≤ r + 1) (h₃ : q + s ≤ r₂ + 1) (h₄ : p + r₂ ≤ r + 1)
    (a : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p)
    (b : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl q)
    (c : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl s) :
    localizedBivariantGradingMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc r₁ s r
        (localizedBivariantGradingMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p q r₁ a b) c =
      localizedBivariantGradingMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p r₂ r a
        (localizedBivariantGradingMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc q s r₂ b c)
declarations.comment: associativity of the canonical multiplication A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) × A^(q)(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^(r)(Z ⟶ X) of the remark -- the verification the source omits -- for every triple of factors and every choice of intermediate targets r₁, r₂ and common target r with p + q + s ≤ r + 2, where every term of a triple product is one of the remark's three pairings; this covers the displayed target max(p,q) and the product internal to A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) of the graded algebra

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, associativity of the multiplication internal to `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`**, which is the
associativity the source's "`A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` canonically comes equipped with the structure of a
graded algebra" asks for, for `p ≤ 1` — the `p` at which a triple product of the internal
multiplication (`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul`, defined for every `p ≥ 0`)
meets no pair of degrees the remark leaves unprescribed,
`Stacks.Chow.localizedGrading_self_admissible_iff`. With
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMul_add_left`,
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMul_add_right` and the two unit laws
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_one_left` and `_one_right` this completes the
graded-algebra axioms for that product. For `p ≥ 2` the content of associativity is
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_singleLow_eq_zero_of_assoc`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_assoc (p : ℕ) (hp : p ≤ 1)
    (a b c : localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p) :
    localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p
        (localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p a b) c =
      localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p a
        (localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul C G sX f hRG hgysP hgys hgysc p b c)
declarations.comment: associativity of the multiplication internal to A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) of the remark's graded algebra, for p ≤ 1, where no pair of degrees the remark leaves unprescribed occurs in a triple product

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingSemigroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, the multiplicative structure of the remark's graded algebra on `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)`
as a bundled `Semigroup`**, on all of `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` for `p ≤ 1`, which is where associativity of
the internal product is proved. Nothing beyond the Gysin compatibilities of the product itself is
assumed: the multiplication is `Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul`, which is defined
for every `p ≥ 0`, and the associativity is
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_assoc`.

The unit of the algebra needs `p ≥ 1`, so the bundled `Monoid` is at `p = 1`:
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMonoid`.
declarations.statement:
def localizedBivariantGradingSemigroup (p : ℕ) (hp : p ≤ 1) :
    Semigroup (localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p)
declarations.comment: the multiplicative structure of the remark's graded algebra on A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) as a bundled Semigroup, on all of A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) for p ≤ 1, where associativity of the internal product is proved: the multiplication of the remark together with its associativity, with no hypothesis beyond the Gysin compatibilities the product itself carries

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMonoid
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, the remark's graded algebra on `A⁽¹⁾(Z ⟶ X)` as a bundled `Monoid`:** the
multiplication internal to `A⁽¹⁾(Z ⟶ X)`, its unit, and the three laws. This is the structure the
source's "`A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` canonically comes equipped with the structure of a graded algebra" asserts
on the multiplicative side. Its fields are
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul`,
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingOne`,
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_assoc`,
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_one_left` and
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_one_right`; the additive side of the algebra is
the `AddCommGroup` the grading carries, with the distributive law
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulHom`.

`p = 1` is where the three laws meet. The multiplication internal to `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` is defined for
every `p ≥ 0` and the two unit laws hold for every `p ≥ 1`, the degree `0` slot where the unit sits
being `A⁰(X)` exactly then; associativity is proved for `p ≤ 1`
(`Stacks.Chow.localizedGrading_self_admissible_iff`), and what it would come to for `p ≥ 2` is
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMul_singleLow_eq_zero_of_assoc`.

The carrier is **all** of `A⁽¹⁾(Z ⟶ X)`, the group the source asserts the algebra on. That rests
on the index range of the sums the product is formed from: a degree `n` component is the sum over
`Finset.Icc (min 0 n) (max 0 n)`, the pairs `i + j = n` whose two degrees both have the sign of
`n`, and that range contains `i = 0` and `i = n` in every degree
(`Stacks.Chow.zero_mem_Icc_min_max`, `Stacks.Chow.self_mem_Icc_min_max`) — the two indices
carrying the surviving term of a product with the unit on the left and on the right. The range is a
reading of the source's `∑_{i + j = n}`, which runs over an infinite index set; the reading and the
witness that the index set is infinite with independent summands are in the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.BivariantLemmas.LocalizedGradingMultiplication`.
declarations.statement:
def localizedBivariantGradingMonoid :
    Monoid (localizedBivariantGrading C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl 1)
declarations.comment: the remark's graded algebra on A^(1)(Z ⟶ X) as a bundled Monoid -- the multiplication internal to A^(1)(Z ⟶ X), the class 1 of A^0(X) in degree 0 as its unit, associativity and the two unit laws -- at p = 1, where the unit's degree 0 slot is A^0(X) and associativity is proved, on all of A^(1)(Z ⟶ X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMulOfInvertible_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, associativity of the canonical multiplication at the Gysin system of the first
Chern class rule, with nothing assumed:** there every Gysin compatibility that Stacks 0F9Z,
Stacks 0B75 and Stacks 0EPK carry for an arbitrary Gysin system is a theorem, and so is Stacks
02RG on Chow groups, which the pushforward of Stacks 0EPK costs. See
`Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingMul_assoc`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedBivariantGradingMulOfInvertible_assoc (p q s r₁ r₂ r : ℕ) (h₁ : p + q ≤ r₁ + 1)
    (h₂ : r₁ + s ≤ r + 1) (h₃ : q + s ≤ r₂ + 1) (h₄ : p + r₂ ≤ r + 1)
    (a : localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p)
    (b : localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl q)
    (c : localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl s) :
    localizedBivariantGradingMulOfInvertible C sX f r₁ s r
        (localizedBivariantGradingMulOfInvertible C sX f p q r₁ a b) c =
      localizedBivariantGradingMulOfInvertible C sX f p r₂ r a
        (localizedBivariantGradingMulOfInvertible C sX f q s r₂ b c)
declarations.comment: associativity of the canonical multiplication of the remark -- the verification the source omits -- at every choice of intermediate and common targets with p + q + s ≤ r + 2, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with NOTHING ASSUMED

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulOfInvertible_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA0, associativity of the multiplication internal to `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` at the Gysin
system of the first Chern class rule, with nothing assumed.** This is the associativity of the
source's graded algebra on `A⁽ᵖ⁾(Z ⟶ X)` for `p ≤ 1`, with no hypothesis of any kind beyond that
bound.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulOfInvertible_assoc (p : ℕ) (hp : p ≤ 1)
    (a b c : localizedBivariantGrading C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p) :
    localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulOfInvertible C sX f p
        (localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulOfInvertible C sX f p a b) c =
      localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulOfInvertible C sX f p a
        (localizedBivariantGradingInternalMulOfInvertible C sX f p b c)
declarations.comment: associativity of the multiplication internal to A^(p)(Z ⟶ X) of the remark's graded algebra, for p ≤ 1, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule with NOTHING ASSUMED

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestrictionCap_id_eq_cap_properChowPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA1.** For a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of schemes locally of finite type over
the base and a bivariant class `c` of degree `p` for `i`, the restriction `res(c)` of `c` along
`i` — a class of degree `p` for `Z ×_X Z ⟶ Z`, whose cap operation at the test scheme `𝟙 Z` is
read on `Z` through the canonical identification `(Z ×_X Z) ×_Z Z ≅ Z` — satisfies

  `res(c) ∩ α = c ∩ i_*α`

in `CH_{k-p}(Z)` for every `α ∈ CH_k(Z)`, the right-hand side being read on `Z` through the
canonical identification `X ×_X Z ≅ Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantRestrictionCap_id_eq_cap_properChowPushforward
    (c : BivariantClass C G sZ sX i hi p) (k : ℤ)
    (hfac : ProperPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C sZ sX i hi k)
    (α : chowGroup C sZ k) :
    chowPushforwardOfIso C (pullback.fst (pullback.snd i i) (𝟙 Z) ≫ (pullback.fst i i ≫ sZ)) sZ
        (selfPullbackIdIso i).inv (selfPullbackIdIso_inv_comp i sZ) (k - p)
        (bivariantRestrictionCap C G sZ sX i hi i p c (𝟙 Z) k
          (chowGroupCongr C (id_comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sZ sX i hi) k α)) =
      chowPushforwardOfIso C (pullback.fst i (𝟙 X) ≫ sZ) sZ (pullbackIdIso i).inv
        (pullbackIdIso_inv_comp i sZ) (k - p)
        (c.cap (𝟙 X) k (chowGroupCongr C (Category.id_comp sX).symm k
          (properChowPushforward C sZ sX i hi k hfac α)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestriction_cap_id_eq_cap_properChowPushforward
declarations.doc:

`Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestriction` of `c` along the closed immersion `i`, read at the test scheme

declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantRestriction_cap_id_eq_cap_properChowPushforward
    (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso) (c : BivariantClass C G sZ sX i hi p) (k : ℤ)
    (hfac : ProperPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C sZ sX i hi k)
    (α : chowGroup C sZ k) :
    chowPushforwardOfIso C (pullback.fst (pullback.snd i i) (𝟙 Z) ≫ (pullback.fst i i ≫ sZ)) sZ
        (selfPullbackIdIso i).inv (selfPullbackIdIso_inv_comp i sZ) (k - p)
        ((bivariantRestriction C G sZ sX i hi i p hgys c).cap (𝟙 Z) k
          (chowGroupCongr C (id_comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sZ sX i hi) k α)) =
      chowPushforwardOfIso C (pullback.fst i (𝟙 X) ≫ sZ) sZ (pullbackIdIso i).inv
        (pullbackIdIso_inv_comp i sZ) (k - p)
        (c.cap (𝟙 X) k (chowGroupCongr C (Category.id_comp sX).symm k
          (properChowPushforward C sZ sX i hi k hfac α)))
declarations.comment: for the restricted bivariant class

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.closedImmersionChowCohomologyRestriction_cap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA1.** The restriction map `res : A^p(Z ⟶ X) ⟶ A^p(Z)` of a closed immersion
satisfies `res(c) ∩ α = c ∩ i_*α` in `CH_{k-p}(Z)` for every `α ∈ CH_k(Z)`, both sides being read

declarations.statement:

        ((closedImmersionChowCohomologyRestriction C G sZ sX i hi p hgys c).cap (𝟙 Z) k

        (pullbackIdIso_inv_comp i sZ) (k - p)
        (c.cap (𝟙 X) k (chowGroupCongr C (Category.id_comp sX).symm k
          (properChowPushforward C sZ sX i hi k hfac α)))
declarations.comment: the cap formula for the restriction map to A^p(Z)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantCommute
declarations.doc:
Two bivariant classes `c₁ ∈ A^{p₁}(Z₁ ⟶ X)` and `c₂ ∈ A^{p₂}(Z₂ ⟶ X)` *commute* when

  `c₁ ∩ c₂ ∩ α = c₂ ∩ c₁ ∩ α`

for every morphism `t : T ⟶ X` locally of finite type and every `α ∈ CH_k(T)`; this is the
identity for every `α ∈ CH_k(X)` and after every base change `X' ⟶ X` locally of finite type.

The two sides live on the two iterated fibre products `Z₁ ×_X (Z₂ ×_X T)` and `Z₂ ×_X (Z₁ ×_X T)`
and in the two degrees `(k - p₂) - p₁` and `(k - p₁) - p₂`; they are compared by pushing the
first forward along `Stacks.Chow.commuteComparisonHom` and transporting the second along the
equality of degrees.
declarations.statement: def BivariantCommute : Prop
declarations.comment: the definition of commuting bivariant classes

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCommute_iff_commuteCompositeCap_eq
declarations.doc:
Two bivariant classes commute if and only if the cap operations of the two
composites `res(c₁) ∘ c₂` and `res(c₂) ∘ c₁` agree, under the canonical identification
`Z₁ ×_X Z₂ ≅ Z₂ ×_X Z₁` of their sources and the equality `p₁ + p₂ = p₂ + p₁` of their degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantCommute_iff_commuteCompositeCap_eq :
    BivariantCommute C G sX f₁ f₂ p₁ p₂ c₁ c₂ ↔
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (t : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType t] (k : ℤ)
        (α : chowGroup C (t ≫ sX) k),
        chowPushforwardOfIso C
            (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f₁ f₂ ≫ f₂) t ≫ (pullback.fst f₁ f₂ ≫ (f₁ ≫ sX)))
            (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f₂ f₁ ≫ f₁) t ≫ (pullback.fst f₂ f₁ ≫ (f₂ ≫ sX)))
            (compositeComparisonHom f₁ f₂ t)
            (compositeComparisonHom_comp_structureMorphism C sX f₁ f₂ t) ((k - p₂) - p₁)
            (commuteCompositeCap C G sX f₁ f₂ p₁ p₂ c₁ c₂ hgys hpp t k α) =
          chowGroupDegreeEquiv C
            (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f₂ f₁ ≫ f₁) t ≫ (pullback.fst f₂ f₁ ≫ (f₂ ≫ sX)))
            (by ring : (k - p₁) - p₂ = (k - p₂) - p₁)
            (commuteCompositeCap C G sX f₂ f₁ p₂ p₁ c₂ c₁ hgys hpp t k α)
declarations.comment: commuting is the equality of the two composites

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCommute_iff_cap_eq_of_isBivariantClassComposition
declarations.doc:
If `d₁` is the composite `res(c₁) ∘ c₂` and `d₂` is the composite `res(c₂) ∘ c₁` in the sense
of Stacks 0FE0, then `c₁` and `c₂` commute exactly when `d₁` and `d₂` agree under the canonical
identification `Z₁ ×_X Z₂ ≅ Z₂ ×_X Z₁`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantCommute_iff_cap_eq_of_isBivariantClassComposition
    (d₁ : BivariantClass C G (pullback.fst f₁ f₂ ≫ (f₁ ≫ sX)) sX (pullback.snd f₁ f₂ ≫ f₂)
      (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (f₁ ≫ sX) sX f₁ rfl f₂) rfl) (p₁ + p₂))
    (d₂ : BivariantClass C G (pullback.fst f₂ f₁ ≫ (f₂ ≫ sX)) sX (pullback.snd f₂ f₁ ≫ f₁)
      (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (f₂ ≫ sX) sX f₂ rfl f₁) rfl) (p₂ + p₁))
    (h₁ : IsBivariantClassComposition C G (pullback.fst f₁ f₂ ≫ (f₁ ≫ sX)) (f₂ ≫ sX) sX
      (pullback.snd f₁ f₂) f₂
      (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (f₁ ≫ sX) sX f₁ rfl f₂) rfl hpp p₁ p₂
      (bivariantRestriction C G (f₁ ≫ sX) sX f₁ rfl f₂ p₁ hgys c₁) c₂ d₁)
    (h₂ : IsBivariantClassComposition C G (pullback.fst f₂ f₁ ≫ (f₂ ≫ sX)) (f₁ ≫ sX) sX
      (pullback.snd f₂ f₁) f₁
      (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (f₂ ≫ sX) sX f₂ rfl f₁) rfl hpp p₂ p₁
      (bivariantRestriction C G (f₂ ≫ sX) sX f₂ rfl f₁ p₂ hgys c₂) c₁ d₂) :
    BivariantCommute C G sX f₁ f₂ p₁ p₂ c₁ c₂ ↔
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (t : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType t] (k : ℤ)
        (α : chowGroup C (t ≫ sX) k),
        chowPushforwardOfIso C
            (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f₁ f₂ ≫ f₂) t ≫ (pullback.fst f₁ f₂ ≫ (f₁ ≫ sX)))
            (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f₂ f₁ ≫ f₁) t ≫ (pullback.fst f₂ f₁ ≫ (f₂ ≫ sX)))
            (compositeComparisonHom f₁ f₂ t)
            (compositeComparisonHom_comp_structureMorphism C sX f₁ f₂ t) ((k - p₂) - p₁)
            (chowGroupDegreeEquiv C
              (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f₁ f₂ ≫ f₂) t ≫ (pullback.fst f₁ f₂ ≫ (f₁ ≫ sX)))
              (by ring : k - (p₁ + p₂) = (k - p₂) - p₁) (d₁.cap t k α)) =
          chowGroupDegreeEquiv C
            (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f₂ f₁ ≫ f₁) t ≫ (pullback.fst f₂ f₁ ≫ (f₂ ≫ sX)))
            (by ring : k - (p₂ + p₁) = (k - p₂) - p₁) (d₂.cap t k α)
declarations.comment: commuting is the equality of the two composite classes

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCommute_iff_commuteCompositeOfInvertible_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA2.** Two bivariant classes `c₁ ∈ A^{p₁}(Z₁ ⟶ X)` and `c₂ ∈ A^{p₂}(Z₂ ⟶ X)` at
the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule commute if and only if

  `res(c₁) ∘ c₂ = res(c₂) ∘ c₁`   in   `A^{p₁ + p₂}(Z₁ ×_X Z₂ ⟶ X)`,

where `res(cᵢ)` is the restriction of Stacks 0F9Z and `∘` the composition of Stacks 0B75. The
right-hand side, a class in `A^{p₂ + p₁}(Z₂ ×_X Z₁ ⟶ X)`, is read in `A^{p₁ + p₂}(Z₁ ×_X Z₂ ⟶ X)`
through the symmetry of the fibre product and the equality of degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantCommute_iff_commuteCompositeOfInvertible_eq
    (c₁ : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f₁ ≫ sX) sX f₁ rfl p₁)
    (c₂ : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (f₂ ≫ sX) sX f₂ rfl p₂) :
    BivariantCommute C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX f₁ f₂ p₁ p₂ c₁ c₂ ↔
      commuteCompositeOfInvertible C sX f₁ f₂ p₁ p₂ c₁ c₂ =
        bivariantClassDegreeCongr C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
          (pullback.fst f₁ f₂ ≫ (f₁ ≫ sX)) sX (pullback.snd f₁ f₂ ≫ f₂)
          (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq
            (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (f₁ ≫ sX) sX f₁ rfl f₂) rfl)
          (add_comm p₂ p₁)
          (bivariantTransport C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.fst f₂ f₁ ≫ (f₂ ≫ sX))
            (pullback.fst f₁ f₂ ≫ (f₁ ≫ sX)) sX (pullback.snd f₂ f₁ ≫ f₁)
            (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq
              (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (f₂ ≫ sX) sX f₂ rfl f₁) rfl)
            (pullback.snd f₁ f₂ ≫ f₂)
            (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq
              (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (f₁ ≫ sX) sX f₁ rfl f₂) rfl)
            (pullbackSymmetry f₂ f₁)
            (by rw [pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_snd_assoc, pullback.condition]) (p₂ + p₁)
            (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C)
            (commuteCompositeOfInvertible C sX f₂ f₁ p₂ p₁ c₂ c₁))
declarations.comment: commuting is the equality res(c₁) ∘ c₂ = res(c₂) ∘ c₁ of bivariant classes, at the canonical Gysin system, with nothing assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinBivariantClass_bivariantCommute
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA3.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL, let `X` be locally of finite type over
`S`, let `(𝓛, s, i : D ⟶ X)` be a triple as in Definition 02T8, let `f : Z ⟶ X` be locally of
finite type and let `c ∈ A^p(Z ⟶ X)` be a bivariant class of Definition 0B76. Then the bivariant
Gysin class `i^* ∈ A^1(D ⟶ X)` of Stacks 0B79 commutes with `c` in the sense of Remark 0FA2:
`i^* ∩ (c ∩ α) = c ∩ (i^* ∩ α)` for every `α ∈ CH_k(T)` and every `T ⟶ X` locally of finite
type, the two sides compared by the canonical isomorphism `D ×_X (Z ×_X T) ≅ Z ×_X (D ×_X T)`.

This is a restatement of condition (3) of Definition 0B76 for `c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinBivariantClass_bivariantCommute
    (c : BivariantChowClass C (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p) :
    BivariantCommute C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (gysinTripleInclusion L s) f 1 p
      (gysinBivariantClass C sX L s).1 (BivariantChowClass.equivBivariantClass c)
declarations.comment: the Gysin class i^* of Stacks 0B79 commutes with every c ∈ A^p(Z → X), in the sense of Remark 0FA2

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinBivariantClass_comp_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA3, on composites.** In the situation of
`Stacks.Chow.gysinBivariantClass_bivariantCommute`, with `i^* ∈ A^1(D ⟶ X)` the bivariant Gysin
class of Stacks 0B79 and `c ∈ A^p(Z ⟶ X)`,

  `res(i^*) ∘ c = res(c) ∘ i^*`   in   `A^{1+p}(D ×_X Z ⟶ X)`,

which Remark 0FA2 identifies with the commutation of `i^*` and `c`. Here
`res(i^*) ∈ A^1(D ×_X Z ⟶ Z)` and `res(c) ∈ A^p(Z ×_X D ⟶ D)` are the restrictions of
Remark 0F9Z; the second composite lives on `Z ×_X D` and in degree `p + 1`, and is read on
`D ×_X Z` through the canonical isomorphism and in degree `1 + p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinBivariantClass_comp_comm {sZ : Z ⟶ C.S} [LocallyOfFiniteType sZ]
    (hZ : f ≫ sX = sZ) (c : BivariantChowClass C sZ sX f hZ p) :
    ((BivariantChowClass.equivBivariantClass.symm (gysinBivariantClass C sX L s).1).restrict f
        hZ).comp c =
      (((c.restrict (gysinTripleInclusion L s) rfl).comp
          (BivariantChowClass.equivBivariantClass.symm
            (gysinBivariantClass C sX L s).1)).degreeCongr (add_comm p 1)).transport
        (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq (BivariantChowClass.restrict_structure_eq rfl f hZ) hZ)
        (pullbackSymmetry f (gysinTripleInclusion L s))
        (pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_snd_comp (gysinTripleInclusion L s) f)
declarations.comment: res(i^*) ∘ c = res(c) ∘ i^* in A^{1+p}(D ×_X Z → X), the form of Remark 0FA2 on composites

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinBivariantCommute
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA3.** Let `(𝓛, s, i : D ⟶ X)` be a triple as in Definition 02T8, let
`f : Z ⟶ X` be locally of finite type and let `c ∈ A^p(Z ⟶ X)` be a bivariant class. Then the
bivariant Gysin class `c' ∈ A^1(D ⟶ X)` of Stacks 0B79 commutes with `c` in the sense of
Stacks 0FA2.

This is a restatement of condition (3) of Definition 0B76: the two iterated cap operations are
the two sides of `Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass.gysin_naturality` for `c` at the divisor pulled
back to the test scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinBivariantCommute (hG : G.IsNaturalUnderPullbackCompPushforward)
    (c : BivariantClass C G (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl p)
    (c' : BivariantClass C G (gysinTripleInclusion L s ≫ sX) sX (gysinTripleInclusion L s) rfl 1)
    (hc' : IsGysinBivariantClass C G sX L s c') :
    BivariantCommute C G sX (gysinTripleInclusion L s) f 1 p c' c

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.topChernClassCompleted
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA4**, general case. The top Chern class
`c_top(ℰ) = ∏_r c_r(ℰ|_{X_r}) ∈ ∏_r A^r(X_r) ⊂ A^*(X)^∧` of a finite locally free module `ℰ` on
`X`, for the decomposition `X = ∐ X_r` by the rank of `ℰ`: the element of the completed bivariant
group of Stacks 0FE0 whose image `(c_p)_p ∈ ∏_p A^p(X)` has, under `A^p(X) = ∏_r A^p(X_r)` of
Stacks 0FDZ, the component `c_r(ℰ|_{X_r})` in `A^r(X_r)` and zero in `A^p(X_r)` for `p ≠ r`.
declarations.statement:
def topChernClassCompleted :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    {c : completedBivariantGroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX) //
      (∀ r : ℕ, rankLocusRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX E
          (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion C) (r : ℤ)
          (completedBivariantSequenceOfInvertible C sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX) c r) r =
        rankLocusTopChernClass C sX E r) ∧
      ∀ (p : ℤ) (r : ℕ), (r : ℤ) ≠ p →
        rankLocusRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX E
          (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion C) p
          (completedBivariantSequenceOfInvertible C sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX) c p) r =
        0}
declarations.comment: general case: c_top(E) = ∏ c_r(E|_{X_r}) ∈ ∏ A^r(X_r) ⊂ A^*(X)^∧

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.topChernClassOfFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA4**, finite case. If only finitely many of the rank loci `X_r` are nonempty, the
top Chern class `c_top(ℰ) = Σ_r c_r(ℰ|_{X_r}) ∈ A^*(X) = ⊕ A^*(X_r)`: the element of the graded
group `A^*(X) = ⊕_p A^p(X)` that is the sum, over the ranks `r` that occur, of a class of degree
`r`, and whose degree `p` part has, under `A^p(X) = ∏_r A^p(X_r)` of Stacks 0FDZ, the component
`c_r(ℰ|_{X_r})` in `A^r(X_r)` and zero in `A^p(X_r)` for `p ≠ r`.
declarations.statement:
def topChernClassOfFinite (hfin : {r : ℕ | (rankLocus E r : Set X).Nonempty}.Finite) :
    {c : nonhomogeneousBivariantGroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sX (𝟙 X)
        (Category.id_comp sX) //
      c = ∑ r ∈ hfin.toFinset, DirectSum.of _ (r : ℤ) (c r) ∧
      (∀ r : ℕ, rankLocusRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX E
          (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion C) (r : ℤ) (c r) r =
        rankLocusTopChernClass C sX E r) ∧
      ∀ (p : ℤ) (r : ℕ), (r : ℤ) ≠ p →
        rankLocusRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX E
          (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion C) p (c p) r = 0}
declarations.comment: finite case: c_top(E) = Σ_r c_r(E|_{X_r}) ∈ A^*(X) = ⊕ A^*(X_r)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.topChernTotalClass
declarations.doc:
The top Chern class `c_top(E) = Σ_r c_r(E|_{X_r})` of a finite locally free module `E` on `X`,
as an element of `∏_{p ≥ 0} A^p(X)`: its degree-`p` component is the class equal, on the locus
`X_p` where `E` has rank `p`, to the `p`-th Chern class of Stacks 0ESW, and to zero on every other
rank locus. It is assembled along the rank decomposition by Stacks 0FDZ.
declarations.statement: def topChernTotalClass : TotalChowClass C sX
declarations.comment: top Chern class in the product of the Chow cohomology groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.topChernClassOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The top Chern class `c_top(E) = Σ_r c_r(E|_{X_r})` of a finite locally free module `E` on `X`,
as an element of the completed bivariant group `A^*(X)^∧`: on a connected component `X_i` of `X`
the rank of `E` is a constant `r`, and there the class is the restriction to `X_i` of the
degree-`r` component of `c_top(E)` — that is, of the `r`-th Chern class of Stacks 0ESW, by
`Stacks.Chow.topChernClassOfInvertible_rankStratum` — placed in degree `r`.
declarations.statement:
def topChernClassOfInvertible :
    completedBivariantGroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX)
declarations.comment: completed top Chern class

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.topChernClassOfInvertible_rankStratum
declarations.doc:
On the locus where `E` has rank `r` the top Chern class is the `r`-th Chern class, in degree
`r`: a connected component `X_i` lies in the locus of the rank `r` of `E` on it, and the degree-`r`
part of `c_top(E)` there is the restriction to `X_i` of the Chern class `c_r(E)` of Stacks 0ESW,
that is `c_r(E|_{X_i})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topChernClassOfInvertible_rankStratum (i : _root_.ConnectedComponents X) :
    X.connectedComponentOpens i ≤
        Scheme.Modules.rankStratum E (Scheme.Modules.rankOnConnectedComponent E i) ∧
      topChernClassOfInvertible C sX E i (Scheme.Modules.rankOnConnectedComponent E i : ℤ) =
        bivariantConnectedComponentRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sX (𝟙 X)
          (Category.id_comp sX) _ (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion C)
          (totalChernOfFiniteLocallyFree C sX E (Scheme.Modules.rankOnConnectedComponent E i))
          i
declarations.comment: rank-locus Chern component

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.topChernClassOfInvertible_of_ne_rank
declarations.doc:
The top Chern class has no component in a degree other than the rank: on a connected component
on which `E` has rank `r`, the degree-`p` part of `c_top(E)` vanishes for every `p ≠ r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topChernClassOfInvertible_of_ne_rank (i : _root_.ConnectedComponents X) (p : ℤ)
    (h : p ≠ (Scheme.Modules.rankOnConnectedComponent E i : ℤ)) :
    topChernClassOfInvertible C sX E i p = 0
declarations.comment: off-rank vanishing

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.finite_degrees_topChernClassOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
If only finitely many of the loci `X_r` are nonempty, then only finitely many degrees occur in
the top Chern class, so it lies in the ordinary graded group `A^*(X)` inside its completion.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_degrees_topChernClassOfInvertible
    (hfin : {r : ℕ | (Scheme.Modules.rankStratum E r : Set X).Nonempty}.Finite) :
    {p : ℤ | ∃ i : _root_.ConnectedComponents X,
      topChernClassOfInvertible C sX E i p ≠ 0}.Finite
declarations.comment: finite-rank-locus case

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.topChernClassFiniteOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The top Chern class `c_top(E) = Σ_r c_r(E|_{X_r})` as an ordinary nonhomogeneous bivariant
class on `X`, when only finitely many of the loci `X_r` are nonempty: the sum, over the ranks `r`
that occur, of the degree-`r` part of the top Chern class.
declarations.statement:
def topChernClassFiniteOfInvertible
    (hfin : {r : ℕ | (Scheme.Modules.rankStratum E r : Set X).Nonempty}.Finite) :
    nonhomogeneousBivariantGroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sX (𝟙 X)
      (Category.id_comp sX)
declarations.comment: ordinary finite top Chern class

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.topChernClassFiniteOfInvertible_component
declarations.doc:
The finite sum `Σ_r c_r(E|_{X_r})` has the completed top Chern class as its image under the
identification of Stacks 0FDZ: in every degree and on every connected component, its restriction is
the corresponding part of `c_top(E)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topChernClassFiniteOfInvertible_component
    (hfin : {r : ℕ | (Scheme.Modules.rankStratum E r : Set X).Nonempty}.Finite) (p : ℤ)
    (i : _root_.ConnectedComponents X) :
    bivariantConnectedComponentRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sX (𝟙 X)
        (Category.id_comp sX) p (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion C)
        (topChernClassFiniteOfInvertible C sX E hfin p) i =
      topChernClassOfInvertible C sX E i p
declarations.comment: finite-class canonical image

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.topChernClassFiniteOfInvertible_rankStratum
declarations.doc:
On the locus where `E` has rank `r`, the component of the finite sum `Σ_r c_r(E|_{X_r})` in
degree `r` is the `r`-th Chern class: a connected component `X_i` lies in the locus of the rank `r`
of `E` on it, and the degree-`r` component of the sum there is the restriction of `c_r(E)`, that is
`c_r(E|_{X_i})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topChernClassFiniteOfInvertible_rankStratum
    (hfin : {r : ℕ | (Scheme.Modules.rankStratum E r : Set X).Nonempty}.Finite)
    (i : _root_.ConnectedComponents X) :
    X.connectedComponentOpens i ≤
        Scheme.Modules.rankStratum E (Scheme.Modules.rankOnConnectedComponent E i) ∧
      bivariantConnectedComponentRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sX (𝟙 X)
          (Category.id_comp sX) _ (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion C)
          (topChernClassFiniteOfInvertible C sX E hfin
            (Scheme.Modules.rankOnConnectedComponent E i : ℤ)) i =
        bivariantConnectedComponentRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sX (𝟙 X)
          (Category.id_comp sX) _ (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion C)
          (totalChernOfFiniteLocallyFree C sX E (Scheme.Modules.rankOnConnectedComponent E i))
          i
declarations.comment: finite-sum rank component

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.topChernClassFiniteOfInvertible_of_ne_rank
declarations.doc:
The finite sum `Σ_r c_r(E|_{X_r})` has no component in a degree other than the rank: on a
connected component on which `E` has rank `r`, its degree-`p` component vanishes for every
`p ≠ r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topChernClassFiniteOfInvertible_of_ne_rank
    (hfin : {r : ℕ | (Scheme.Modules.rankStratum E r : Set X).Nonempty}.Finite)
    (i : _root_.ConnectedComponents X) (p : ℤ)
    (h : p ≠ (Scheme.Modules.rankOnConnectedComponent E i : ℤ)) :
    bivariantConnectedComponentRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sX (𝟙 X)
        (Category.id_comp sX) p (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion C)
        (topChernClassFiniteOfInvertible C sX E hfin p) i = 0
declarations.comment: finite-sum off-rank component

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernClass_dualSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FA5, bivariantly and unconditionally.** For a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module `ℰ`
of rank `r` on a scheme `X` locally of finite type over the base and every `0 ≤ i ≤ r`,

  `c_i(ℰ^∨) = (-1)^i c_i(ℰ)`

in `A^i(X)`, the group of bivariant classes of degree `i` for `𝟙 X` of Stacks 0B76, for the Chern
classes `Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernClass` of Stacks 0B7H.

A bivariant class satisfying the characterization of Stacks 0B7H is unique
(`Stacks.Chow.eq_of_isChernClassBivariant`), so it suffices to check that `(-1)^i c_i(ℰ)` caps by
`c_i(g^*(ℰ^∨)) ∩ -` on every test scheme `g : T ⟶ X`. Integer multiples of bivariant classes are
pointwise on cap products, so the left side is `(-1)^i (c_i(g^*ℰ) ∩ -)`, and that is
`c_i(g^*(ℰ^∨)) ∩ -` by `Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernCap_dualSheaf` applied to `g^*ℰ`, once the
base-change isomorphism of Tag 0GMX identifies `g^*(ℰ^∨)` with `(g^*ℰ)^∨`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernClass_dualSheaf {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (E : X.Modules) (r : ℕ)
    [hE : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r]
    (j : Fin (r + 1)) :
    haveI := Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_dualSheaf E r hE
    chernClass C sX (dualSheaf E) r j = ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ)) • chernClass C sX E r j
declarations.comment: THE BIVARIANT AND UNCONDITIONAL FORM, an ADDITIONAL carrier -- the registration that already stood, Stacks.Chow.chernClassCapExt_eq_zsmul_of_dualFiltration, states the rule in the cycle vocabulary and carries two complete filtrations plus six further hypotheses, and Stacks.Chow.HasDualChernSignRule (which carries no attribute) states it as an assumed Prop on a carried total Chern class series; neither is superseded, because the three speak about three different renderings of c_i in this repository. WHAT IS PROVED HERE: for every scheme X locally of finite type over the base of chapter 42, every finite locally free O_X-module E of rank r, and every i with 0 <= i <= r, the equality c_i(E^dual) = (-1)^i c_i(E) of BIVARIANT CLASSES in A^i(X) -- the group of bivariant classes of degree i for the identity of X, Tag 0B76 -- at the Chern classes Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernClass of Tag 0B7H. HYPOTHESES: exactly the rank, i.e. E is finite locally free of rank r, plus X locally of finite type over the base. NOTHING ELSE IS CARRIED: no filtration of E and no filtration of E^dual, no splitting datum, no normalisation c_0 = 1, no binomial-transform equality, and no assumed compatibility of the cap products with flat pullback -- the last of these is now proved in this repository (Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.intertwines_chernFamily, Tag 02U8), which is what makes the source's reduction performable.
