theorem commutesExteriorProductCapAt_fundamentalChowClass
    (c : BivariantClass C G sY sZ u hu p)
    (hfr : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension sX d)
    (hd : relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction sX (genericPoint X) = (d : ℤ))
    (hRG : ProperPushforwardFlatPullbackBaseChange C) (h71 : G.FlatPullbackNaturality d) :
    CommutesExteriorProductCapAt C hδ G sX sY sZ u hu p c (d : ℤ) m
      (fundamentalChowClass C sX (d : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the equation α × (c ∩ β) = c ∩ (α × β) of the tag, for α the fundamental class of an integral scheme X flat of relative dimension d over the base — NOT for a general α ∈ CH_n(X), for which the missing inputs are recorded in the module notes; carries Stacks 02S1 as hfp, Stacks 02RG on Chow groups as hRG, and Stacks 0B71 with the identification of Stacks 0B6Y as h71, these being exactly the hypotheses of Stacks 0B78 in this repository

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.commutesExteriorProductCap_of_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FBY over a field.** Let `k` be a field, `X` locally of finite type over `k`,
`u : Y ⟶ Z` a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over `k`, and `c ∈ A^p(Y ⟶ Z)`. Then

  `α × (c ∩ β) = c ∩ (α × β)`   in   `CH_{n + (m - p)}(X ×_k Y)`

for every `α ∈ CH_n(X)` and every `β ∈ CH_m(Z)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem commutesExteriorProductCap_of_field (n m : ℤ) :
    CommutesExteriorProductCap (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl)
      (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) sX sY sZ u hu p c n m
declarations.comment: the bivariant classes are those of the Gysin system of invertible modules, `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.commutesExteriorProductCap_of_subsingleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FBY over a point.** Let the base be a point with dimension function zero, for
instance the spectrum of a field, let `X` be locally of finite type over it, let `u : Y ⟶ Z` be a
morphism of schemes locally of finite type over it and let `c ∈ A^p(Y ⟶ Z)` be a bivariant class
for any Gysin system. Then for all `α ∈ CH_n(X)` and `β ∈ CH_m(Z)`

  `α × (c ∩ β) = c ∩ (α × β)`   in   `CH_{n + (m - p)}(X ×_S Y)`.

Write `α = ∑ₓ nₓ [closure {x}]`. Then `α × β` is the locally finite sum over the points `x` of the
support of `α` of the pushforwards along `closure {x} ×_S Z ⟶ X ×_S Z` of the flat pullbacks of
`nₓ β` along the flat projections `closure {x} ×_S Z ⟶ Z`. Capping with `c` commutes with each of
these flat pullbacks by the flat-pullback axiom of Stacks 0B76, and with the locally finite sum by
`Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass.cap_chowGroupCongr_mk_eq_mk_of_locallyFinite`; the result is the
corresponding decomposition of `α × (c ∩ β)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem commutesExteriorProductCap_of_subsingleton (c : BivariantClass C G sY sZ u hu p)
    (n m : ℤ) : CommutesExteriorProductCap C hδ G sX sY sZ u hu p c n m
declarations.comment: α × (c ∩ β) = c ∩ (α × β) in CH_*(X ×_S Y), over a base which is a point with dimension function zero (in particular Spec k), for bivariant classes at any Gysin system

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exteriorProductCap_eq_capExteriorProduct_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FBY.** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a scheme locally of finite type over `k`, let
`u : Y ⟶ Z` be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over `k` and let
`c' ∈ A^q(Y ⟶ Z)`. Then for `α ∈ CH_n(X)` and `β ∈ CH_m(Z)`

  `α × (c' ∩ β) = c' ∩ (α × β)`   in   `CH_{n + (m - q)}(X ×_k Y)`.

Here `A^q(Y ⟶ Z)` is the group of bivariant classes of Stacks 0B76, the exterior product is that
of Stacks 0FBV, and the two sides are those of `Stacks.Chow.exteriorProductCap` and
`Stacks.Chow.capExteriorProduct`: `c' ∩ β` is read on `Y ≅ Y ×_Z Z`, and `c' ∩ (α × β)` is the
cap at the test scheme `X ×_k Z ⟶ Z`, read on `X ×_k Y ≅ Y ×_Z (X ×_k Z)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorProductCap_eq_capExteriorProduct_field
    (c' : BivariantChowClass (fieldChowSituation k) sY sZ u hu q) (n m : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sX n) (β : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sZ m) :
    haveI := BivariantChowClass.locallyOfFiniteType_of_structure sZ u hu
    exteriorProductCap (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl)
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) sX sY sZ u hu q
        (BivariantChowClass.equivBivariantClass c') n m α β =
      capExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl)
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) sX sY sZ u hu q
        (BivariantChowClass.equivBivariantClass c') n m α β
declarations.comment: α × (c' ∩ β) = c' ∩ (α × β) in CH_*(X ×_k Y), for k a field and c' ∈ A^q(Y → Z) of Stacks 0B76

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowExteriorProduct_assoc_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FBZ.** The exterior product on Chow groups is associative. Let `k` be a field, let
`X`, `Y` and `Z` be schemes locally of finite type over `k` and let `a ∈ CH_n(X)`,
`b ∈ CH_m(Y)`, `c ∈ CH_l(Z)`. Then

  `(a × b) × c = a × (b × c)`

in `CH_{n + m + l}(X ×_k Y ×_k Z)`.

The two sides are formed on the two bracketings of the triple product and in the two bracketings
of the degree, so the left-hand side is carried into the group of the right-hand side by
pushforward along the associator `Stacks.Chow.tripleProductAssoc`, which is an isomorphism over
the base by `Stacks.Chow.tripleProductAssoc_hom_comp_base`, followed by
`Stacks.Chow.chowGroupDegreeEquiv` for the degrees `(n + m) + l` and `n + (m + l)`. Both of those
transports are the identity on cycle coefficients, so what is asserted is the source's identity.

On classes of cycles it is `Stacks.Chow.exteriorProduct_assoc`, the cycle-level identity, read
modulo rational equivalence. Nothing is assumed beyond the base being the spectrum of a field:
the exterior product on Chow groups, `Stacks.Chow.chowExteriorProduct`, is itself unconditional
over such a base, the instances of Stacks 02S1 that make it well defined being discharged inside
it by `Stacks.Chow.flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalenceOnPointClosureFibres_holds`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowExteriorProduct_assoc_unconditional (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (g : Y ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (h : Z ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [LocallyOfFiniteType h] (n m l : ℤ)
    (a : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) f n)
    (b : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) g m)
    (c : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) h l) :
    chowGroupDegreeEquiv (fieldChowSituation k)
        (pullback.fst f (pullback.fst g h ≫ g) ≫ f) (add_assoc n m l)
        (chowPushforwardOfIso (fieldChowSituation k)
          (pullback.fst (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) h ≫ pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
          (pullback.fst f (pullback.fst g h ≫ g) ≫ f) (tripleProductAssoc f g h).hom
          (tripleProductAssoc_hom_comp_base f g h) (n + m + l)
          (chowExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl)
            (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) h (n + m) l
            (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ
              (chowExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl) f g n m
                (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ a b)) c))) =
      chowExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl) f (pullback.fst g h ≫ g) n
        (m + l)
        (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ a
          (chowExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl) g h m l
            (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ b c)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowExteriorProduct_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FBZ.** The exterior product on Chow groups is associative. Let `k` be a field, let
`X`, `Y` and `Z` be schemes locally of finite type over `k` and let `a ∈ CH_n(X)`,
`b ∈ CH_m(Y)`, `c ∈ CH_l(Z)`. Then

  `(a × b) × c = a × (b × c)`

in `CH_{n + m + l}(X ×_k Y ×_k Z)`.

The two sides are formed on the two bracketings of the triple product and in the two bracketings
of the degree, so the left-hand side is carried into the group of the right-hand side by
pushforward along the associator `Stacks.Chow.tripleProductAssoc`, which is an isomorphism over
the base by `Stacks.Chow.tripleProductAssoc_hom_comp_base`, followed by
`Stacks.Chow.chowGroupDegreeEquiv` for the degrees `(n + m) + l` and `n + (m + l)`. Both of those
transports are the identity on cycle coefficients, so what is asserted is the source's identity.

On classes of cycles it is `Stacks.Chow.exteriorProduct_assoc`, the cycle-level identity, read
modulo rational equivalence. Nothing is assumed: it is
`Stacks.Chow.chowExteriorProduct_assoc_unconditional`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowExteriorProduct_assoc (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (g : Y ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (h : Z ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [LocallyOfFiniteType h] (n m l : ℤ)
    (a : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) f n)
    (b : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) g m)
    (c : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) h l) :
    chowGroupDegreeEquiv (fieldChowSituation k)
        (pullback.fst f (pullback.fst g h ≫ g) ≫ f) (add_assoc n m l)
        (chowPushforwardOfIso (fieldChowSituation k)
          (pullback.fst (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) h ≫ pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
          (pullback.fst f (pullback.fst g h ≫ g) ≫ f) (tripleProductAssoc f g h).hom
          (tripleProductAssoc_hom_comp_base f g h) (n + m + l)
          (chowExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl)
            (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) h (n + m) l
            (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ
              (chowExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl) f g n m
                (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ a b)) c))) =
      chowExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl) f (pullback.fst g h ≫ g) n
        (m + l)
        (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ a
          (chowExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl) g h m l
            (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ b c)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.totalChowExteriorProduct_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FBZ.** Exterior product is associative. Let `k` be a field, let `X`, `Y`, `Z` be
schemes locally of finite type over `k`, and let `α ∈ CH_*(X)`, `β ∈ CH_*(Y)`, `γ ∈ CH_*(Z)`.
Then `(α × β) × γ = α × (β × γ)` in `CH_*(X ×_k Y ×_k Z)`, the left-hand side being carried
from `(X ×_k Y) ×_k Z` to `X ×_k (Y ×_k Z)` by pushforward along the associator of the fibre
product.
declarations.statement:
theorem totalChowExteriorProduct_assoc (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (g : Y ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (h : Z ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [LocallyOfFiniteType h]
    (α : DirectSum ℤ fun n : ℤ ↦ chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) f n)
    (β : DirectSum ℤ fun m : ℤ ↦ chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) g m)
    (γ : DirectSum ℤ fun l : ℤ ↦ chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) h l) :
    totalChowPushforwardOfIso (fieldChowSituation k)
        (pullback.fst (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) h ≫ pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
        (pullback.fst f (pullback.fst g h ≫ g) ≫ f) (tripleProductAssoc f g h).hom
        (tripleProductAssoc_hom_comp_base f g h)
        (totalChowExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (dimensionFunction_eq_zero_of_isClosed k)
          (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) h
          (totalChowExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k)
            (dimensionFunction_eq_zero_of_isClosed k) f g α β) γ) =
      totalChowExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (dimensionFunction_eq_zero_of_isClosed k) f
        (pullback.fst g h ≫ g) α
        (totalChowExteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k)
          (dimensionFunction_eq_zero_of_isClosed k) g h β γ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.smoothIntersectionProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FC0.** The intersection product

`· : CH_n(Y) ⊗_ℤ CH_m(Z) ⟶ CH_{n+m-d}(Y ×_X Z)`,   `α · β = Δ^!(α × β)`,

for `X` smooth over the base of relative dimension `d` (equidimensional of dimension `d`) and
`Y ⟶ X`, `Z ⟶ X` locally of finite type: the exterior product of Stacks 0FBV followed by the
Gysin map `Δ^!` of the diagonal of Stacks 0FBR (`Stacks.Chow.diagonalGysinClass`), read on
`Y ×_X Z = (Y ×_k Z) ×_{X ×_k X} X`. No bivariant class is a parameter.
declarations.comment: X equidimensional of dimension d: α · β = Δ^!(α × β) in CH_{n+m-d}(Y ×_X Z), with Δ^! the Gysin map of the diagonal of Stacks 0FBR, Stacks.Chow.diagonalGysinClass, and × the exterior product of Stacks 0FBV

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.smoothIntersectionProduct_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FC0.** The defining formula `α · β = Δ^!(α × β)` of
`Stacks.Chow.smoothIntersectionProduct`: it is `Stacks.Chow.intersectionProduct` at the Gysin
class of the diagonal.
declarations.statement:
theorem smoothIntersectionProduct_apply (n m : ℤ)
    (t : TensorProduct ℤ (chowGroup C (a ≫ sX) n) (chowGroup C (b ≫ sX) m)) :
    smoothIntersectionProduct C hδ sX hd a b n m t =
      intersectionProduct C hδ (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX a b (d : ℤ)
        (smoothDiagonalGysinClass C sX hd) n m t
declarations.comment: the defining formula α · β = Δ^!(α × β), with Δ^! the Gysin map of the diagonal

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.smoothIntersectionProductBilin
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FC0.** The intersection product as a `ℤ`-bilinear map
`CH_n(Y) → CH_m(Z) → CH_{n+m-d}(Y ×_X Z)`, `α ↦ β ↦ α · β`, for `X` smooth of relative
dimension `d`.
declarations.comment: the product α ↦ β ↦ α · β as a bilinear map, X equidimensional of dimension d

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.smoothIntersectionProductParts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FC0, for `X` of arbitrary dimension.** Let `X` be smooth over the base,
not necessarily equidimensional, with open and closed parts `X_d` of relative dimension `d`
(`Stacks.WeilCohomology.dimPart`, Stacks 02NM), and let `Y_d = a⁻¹(X_d)`, `Z_d = b⁻¹(X_d)` be the
parts of `Y` and `Z` over `X_d`. The intersection product `α · β = Δ^!(α × β)` "decomposes into
the parts lying over the open and closed subschemes of `X` where `X` has a given dimension": its
part over `X_d` is

`α|_{Y_d} · β|_{Z_d} = Δ_d^!(α|_{Y_d} × β|_{Z_d}) ∈ CH_{n+m-d}(Y_d ×_{X_d} Z_d)`,

`Stacks.Chow.smoothIntersectionProduct` over `X_d` with the Gysin map of the diagonal of `X_d`
(Stacks 0FBR). The product is the family of these parts. No bivariant class is a parameter.
declarations.statement:
def smoothIntersectionProductParts (n m : ℤ) :
    TensorProduct ℤ (chowGroup C (a ≫ sX) n) (chowGroup C (b ≫ sX) m) →+
      ∀ d : ℕ, chowGroup C
        (pullback.fst (dimPartOverHom sX a d) (dimPartOverHom sX b d) ≫
          (dimPartOverHom sX a d ≫ partBase sX d)) (n + m - d)
declarations.comment: X smooth of arbitrary dimension: α · β = Δ^!(α × β) in CH_*(Y ×_X Z), as the family over d of its parts in CH_{n+m-d}(Y_d ×_{X_d} Z_d) over the open and closed parts X_d of X of dimension d, each formed with the Gysin map of the diagonal of Stacks 0FBR

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isAssociativeIntersectionProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FC1.** Associativity of the intersection product of Stacks 0FC0: for
`X` a scheme over a field `k` whose diagonal carries a Gysin class `Δ^!` of degree `d`, and `Y`,
`Z`, `W` locally of finite type over `X`,

`(α · β) · γ = α · (β · γ)`   in   `CH_*(Y ×_X Z ×_X W)`,

read through the associator of the triple fibre product over `X` and the matching of the two
degrees, which is `Stacks.Chow.IsAssociativeIntersectionProduct`.

This is the source's chain of five equalities. The two instances of Stacks 0FBY are carried, as
`Stacks.Chow.CommutesDiagonalCapExteriorFirst` and
`Stacks.Chow.CommutesDiagonalCapExteriorSecond` — the repository's one carrier of that tag is the
fundamental-class case and does not cover either of them — and Stacks 0FBP is carried as
`Stacks.Chow.DiagonalGysinCommuteOnTripleProduct`, whose carriers here would apply but for the
class half of Stacks 0FBJ. The docstrings of those three say exactly what they assume and why
none of them is this conclusion. Stacks 0FBZ, associativity of the exterior
product, is **proved** in this repository and is consumed here as
`Stacks.Chow.chowExteriorProduct_assoc`; Stacks 0F9Z is free, the cap operation of
`Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass` being indexed by an arbitrary test morphism, so that `Δ₁₂^!` and
`Δ₂₃^!` are cap operations of `Δ^!` itself and no triple self-product of `X` is needed; and the
fibre-product identification the chain runs on is **proved** above, as
`Stacks.Chow.pullbackDiagonalExteriorTestIso` with its two instances
`Stacks.Chow.firstPartialDiagonalPullbackIso` and
`Stacks.Chow.secondPartialDiagonalPullbackIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAssociativeIntersectionProduct
    (hfirst : CommutesDiagonalCapExteriorFirst k G hpp sX a b g d Dc n m l)
    (hsecond : CommutesDiagonalCapExteriorSecond k G hpp sX a b g d Dc n m l)
    (hcommute : DiagonalGysinCommuteOnTripleProduct k G hpp sX a b g d Dc n m l) :
    IsAssociativeIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl) G sX a b g d Dc
      n m l hpp
declarations.comment: associativity (α·β)·γ = α·(β·γ) of the Stacks 0FC0 product over a field, via the source's five-step chain; 0FBZ comes from this repository and the chain's fibre-product identification is proved here; carried are 0FBY in both variables (only its fundamental-class case is carried here) and 0FBP (needs the class half of 0FBJ), plus 02S1 and 02S2

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isAssociativeIntersectionProduct_canonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC1.** Let `k` be a field, `X` smooth over `k` of arbitrary, not necessarily
constant, dimension, and `Y`, `Z`, `W` locally of finite type over `X`. The intersection product
`α · β = Δ^!(α × β)` of Stacks 0FC0 is formed with the Gysin class of the diagonal of Stacks 0FBR
part by part, over the open and closed parts `X_d` of `X` of dimension `d`
(`Stacks.Chow.dimPartOverIntersectionProduct`): for `α ∈ CH_n(Y)` and `β ∈ CH_m(Z)`, `α · β` has
component `α|_{Y_d} · β|_{Z_d} ∈ CH_{n+m-d}(Y_d ×_{X_d} Z_d)` over `X_d`, where
`Y_d = a⁻¹(X_d)`, `Z_d = b⁻¹(X_d)` are the parts of `Y` and `Z` over `X_d`. Then for
`γ ∈ CH_l(W)`

`(α · β) · γ = α · (β · γ)`   in   `CH_*(Y ×_X Z ×_X W)`,

component by component, read through the associator of the triple fibre product over `X_d` and
the matching of the degrees `(n + m - d) + l - d = n + (m + l - d) - d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAssociativeIntersectionProduct_canonical
    (α : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) (a ≫ sX) n)
    (β : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) (b ≫ sX) m)
    (γ : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k) (g ≫ sX) l) :
    (fun d : ℕ ↦ chowGroupDegreeEquiv (fieldChowSituation k)
        (pullback.fst (dimPartOverHom sX a d)
            (pullback.fst (dimPartOverHom sX b d) (dimPartOverHom sX g d) ≫
              dimPartOverHom sX b d) ≫
          (dimPartOverHom sX a d ≫ partBase sX d))
        (intersectionProductAssocDegree n m l d)
        (properChowPushforward (fieldChowSituation k)
          (pullback.fst (pullback.fst (dimPartOverHom sX a d) (dimPartOverHom sX b d) ≫
              dimPartOverHom sX a d) (dimPartOverHom sX g d) ≫
            ((pullback.fst (dimPartOverHom sX a d) (dimPartOverHom sX b d) ≫
              dimPartOverHom sX a d) ≫ partBase sX d))
          (pullback.fst (dimPartOverHom sX a d)
              (pullback.fst (dimPartOverHom sX b d) (dimPartOverHom sX g d) ≫
                dimPartOverHom sX b d) ≫
            (dimPartOverHom sX a d ≫ partBase sX d))
          (tripleProductAssoc (dimPartOverHom sX a d) (dimPartOverHom sX b d)
            (dimPartOverHom sX g d)).hom
          (tripleProductAssoc_hom_comp_structureMorphism (fieldChowSituation k) (partBase sX d)
            (dimPartOverHom sX a d) (dimPartOverHom sX b d) (dimPartOverHom sX g d))
          ((n + m - d) + l - d) (properPushforwardDescends (fieldChowSituation k) _ _ _ _ _)
          (μ (fun d ↦ pullback.fst (dimPartOverHom sX a d) (dimPartOverHom sX b d) ≫
              dimPartOverHom sX a d) (fun d ↦ dimPartOverHom sX g d)
            (fun d : ℕ ↦ n + m - d) (fun _ ↦ l)
            (fun d ↦ chowGroupCongr (fieldChowSituation k)
              (Category.assoc (pullback.fst (dimPartOverHom sX a d) (dimPartOverHom sX b d))
                (dimPartOverHom sX a d) (partBase sX d)).symm (n + m - d)
              (μ (fun d ↦ dimPartOverHom sX a d) (fun d ↦ dimPartOverHom sX b d) (fun _ ↦ n)
                (fun _ ↦ m) res[a, n, α] res[b, m, β] d))
            res[g, l, γ] d))) =
      μ (fun d ↦ dimPartOverHom sX a d)
        (fun d ↦ pullback.fst (dimPartOverHom sX b d) (dimPartOverHom sX g d) ≫
          dimPartOverHom sX b d) (fun _ ↦ n) (fun d : ℕ ↦ m + l - d) res[a, n, α]
        (fun d ↦ chowGroupCongr (fieldChowSituation k)
          (Category.assoc (pullback.fst (dimPartOverHom sX b d) (dimPartOverHom sX g d))
            (dimPartOverHom sX b d) (partBase sX d)).symm (m + l - d)
          (μ (fun d ↦ dimPartOverHom sX b d) (fun d ↦ dimPartOverHom sX g d) (fun _ ↦ m)
            (fun _ ↦ l) res[b, m, β] res[g, l, γ] d))
declarations.comment: the whole statement: associativity (α·β)·γ = α·(β·γ) in CH_*(Y ×_X Z ×_X W) of the Stacks 0FC0 product for X smooth over a field of arbitrary dimension, Y, Z, W locally of finite type over X and arbitrary α, β, γ, the product Δ^!(α × β) formed with the Gysin class of the diagonal on the open and closed parts of X of constant dimension, as in Section 0FC0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC2.** The map `A^p(X) ⟶ CH_{d-p}(X)` of Stacks 0FC2: cap product of a bivariant
class for the identity of `X` with the fundamental class `[X]_d`, read through the collapse of
`X ×_X X` onto `X` along its first projection.

For `X` smooth over a field and equidimensional of dimension `d` the source asserts that this map
is an isomorphism. Neither that assertion nor the compatibility of composition with the
intersection product is proved here; what is proved is the reduction of injectivity in
`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_injective_iff`. See the implementation notes of
this module.
declarations.statement:
def chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass :
    chowCohomologyComponent C G sX p →+ chowGroup C sX (d - p)
declarations.comment: the map A^p(X) → CH_{d-p}(X), c ↦ c ∩ [X]_d, for an arbitrary degree d over a general Chow situation; neither its bijectivity nor the compatibility of composition with the intersection product is covered

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_injective_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC2, injectivity reduced to Stacks 02UC.** The map `A^p(X) ⟶ CH_{d-p}(X)` of
Stacks 0FC2 is injective exactly when every bivariant class killing the fundamental class `[X]_d`
kills the fundamental class of every integral scheme locally of finite type over `X`.

This is the whole of what Stacks 02UC contributes to the injectivity half of Stacks 0FC2, and the
right-hand side is the statement that remains: in the source it is obtained by factoring the map
through `A^{p-d}(X ⟶ Spec k)` using Stacks 0FBT, which is not available here. The equivalence is
not vacuous in either direction — the forward implication uses that the zero class kills every
fundamental class, the backward one uses Stacks 02UC proper.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_injective_iff :
    Function.Injective (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass C G sX d p) ↔
      ∀ c : chowCohomologyComponent C G sX p,
        c.cap (𝟙 X) d (selfFundamentalClass C sX d) = 0 →
          c.CapsIntegralFundamentalClassesToZero C G sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX) p
declarations.comment: injectivity of the map c ↦ c ∩ [X]_d, reduced by Stacks 02UC to the statement that a class killing [X]_d kills the fundamental class of every integral scheme locally of finite type over X; the surjectivity of the map and the compatibility of composition with the intersection product are not covered

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_injective_iff_hasBirationalModification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC2, injectivity reduced to clause (3) of Stacks 02UC.** The same reduction as
`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_injective_iff`, with the criterion read through
the birational form of Stacks 02UC: it is enough that every integral scheme locally of finite
type over `X` admit a proper birational modification whose fundamental class the class kills.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_injective_iff_hasBirationalModification :
    Function.Injective (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass C G sX d p) ↔
      ∀ c : chowCohomologyComponent C G sX p,
        c.cap (𝟙 X) d (selfFundamentalClass C sX d) = 0 →
          c.HasBirationalModificationCappingToZero C G sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX) p
declarations.comment: injectivity of the map c ↦ c ∩ [X]_d, reduced by clause (3) of Stacks 02UC to the existence of proper birational modifications capping to zero; the surjectivity of the map and the compatibility of composition with the intersection product are not covered

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_bijective_of_smooth_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC2, first clause.** Let `X` be smooth over a field `k`, of constant relative
dimension `d`, that is equidimensional of dimension `d`. Then

  `A^p(X) ⟶ CH_{d-p}(X)`,  `c ↦ c ∩ [X]_d`

is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_bijective_of_smooth_field (p : ℤ) :
    Function.Bijective (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass (fieldChowSituation k)
      (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) sX d p)
declarations.comment: first clause; equidimensional of dimension d read as of constant relative dimension d over k; bivariant classes are those of the Gysin system of invertible modules

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_mulId_of_smooth_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC2, second clause.** Let `X` be smooth over a field `k`, of constant relative
dimension `d`. Via `Θ : A^p(X) ⟶ CH_{d-p}(X)`, `c ↦ c ∩ [X]_d`, composition of bivariant classes
becomes the intersection product of Stacks 0FC0 formed with the Gysin class `Δ^!` of the
diagonal (Stacks 0FBR):

  `Θ(a · b) = Θ(a) · Θ(b)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_mulId_of_smooth_field (p q : ℤ)
    (a : chowCohomologyComponent (fieldChowSituation k)
      (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) sX p)
    (b : chowCohomologyComponent (fieldChowSituation k)
      (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) sX q) :
    chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass (fieldChowSituation k)
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) sX d (p + q)
        (a.mulId (fieldChowSituation k) sX b) =
      chowGroupDegreeEquiv (fieldChowSituation k) sX
        (by ring : ((d : ℤ) - p) + (d - q) - d = d - (p + q))
        (chowGroupSelfProductUnitCollapse (fieldChowSituation k) sX
          (((d : ℤ) - p) + (d - q) - d)
          (intersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl)
            (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) sX (𝟙 X) (𝟙 X) d
            (bivariantClassCongrBase (fieldChowSituation k)
              (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) (pullback.diagonal sX)
              (diagonal_comp_selfProductStructure (fieldChowSituation k) sX) rfl d
              (diagonalGysinClass (fieldChowSituation k) sX sX hd))
            ((d : ℤ) - p) ((d : ℤ) - q)
            (chowGroupCongr (fieldChowSituation k) (Category.id_comp sX).symm ((d : ℤ) - p)
              (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass (fieldChowSituation k)
                (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) sX d p a) ⊗ₜ[ℤ]
              chowGroupCongr (fieldChowSituation k) (Category.id_comp sX).symm ((d : ℤ) - q)
                (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass (fieldChowSituation k)
                  (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) sX d q b))))
declarations.comment: second clause, with the intersection product of Stacks 0FC0 formed with the Gysin class Δ^! of the diagonal; equidimensional of dimension d read as of constant relative dimension d over k

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exteriorProductDedekindTensor
declarations.doc:
The exterior product over a Dedekind base as a map out of the tensor product,

  `× : CH_n(X) ⊗_ℤ CH_m(Y) ⟶ CH_{n+m-1}(X ×_S Y)`,

determined by `[X'] ⊗ [Y'] ↦ [X' ×_S Y']_{n+m-1}` on integral closed subschemes `X' ⊆ X` and
`Y' ⊆ Y` of delta-dimensions `n` and `m` with one of them dominating an irreducible component of
the base, and by `[X'] ⊗ [Y'] ↦ 0` when neither does, given that the cycle-level exterior
product respects rational equivalence in each variable (`hfac`).
declarations.comment: the map CH_n(X) ⊗_ℤ CH_m(Y) → CH_{n+m-1}(X ×_S Y) is well defined, given that the cycle-level exterior product carries rational equivalences to rational equivalences in each variable (the step the source proves with the bivariant classes of Stacks 0B78, 0B79 and 0B75, none of which is in this repository)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.existsUnique_exteriorProductDedekindChowTensor
declarations.doc:
Let `(S, δ)` be as in Stacks section 42.63 — locally the spectrum of a Dedekind domain, with
`δ = 0` at closed points and `δ = 1` elsewhere — and let `X`, `Y` be locally of finite type over
`S`. The map `× : CH_n(X) ⊗_ℤ CH_m(Y) ⟶ CH_{n+m-1}(X ×_S Y)` is well defined: there is exactly
one additive map out of the tensor product sending `[α] ⊗ [β]` to the class of the exterior
product `α × β` of the two cycles.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_exteriorProductDedekindChowTensor (hC : IsDedekindChowBase C) :
    ∃! F : TensorProduct ℤ (chowGroup C f n) (chowGroup C g m) →+
        chowGroup C (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) (n + m - 1),
      ∀ (α : CycleGroup C f n) (β : CycleGroup C g m),
        F (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C f n) α)
            (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C g m) β)) =
          QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) (n + m - 1))
            (exteriorProductDedekindCycles C f g n m α β)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.IsDedekindChowBase.exteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC4.** Over a Dedekind base the exterior product of cycles carries rational
equivalences to rational equivalences in each variable, for all `X`, `Y` locally of finite type
over the base and all `n`, `m`. This discharges the hypothesis of
`Stacks.Chow.exteriorProductDedekindTensor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsDedekindChowBase.exteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence
    (hS : IsDedekindChowBase C) : ExteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C f g n m
declarations.comment: the exterior product of cycles over a Dedekind base is compatible with rational equivalence in each variable; the source's bivariant classes `i_* ∘ (p')^*` and `i_* ∘ (p')^* ∘ c` are read on cycles as a flat pullback and a flat pullback of the Gysin map of a principal divisor with trivial normal bundle

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.IsDedekindChowBase.exteriorProductChow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC4.** The exterior product on Chow groups over a Dedekind base,

  `× : CH_n(X) ⊗_ℤ CH_m(Y) ⟶ CH_{n+m-1}(X ×_S Y)`,

well defined with no hypothesis beyond the base being as in Stacks section 42.63. It is
`Stacks.Chow.exteriorProductDedekindTensor` with its compatibility with rational equivalence
supplied by `Stacks.Chow.IsDedekindChowBase.exteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence`; on
a pure tensor of the classes of integral closed subschemes `X'` and `Y'` of delta-dimensions `n`
and `m` it is the class of `[X' ×_S Y']_{n+m-1}` when one of them dominates an irreducible
component of the base and zero otherwise.
declarations.comment: the map CH_n(X) ⊗_ℤ CH_m(Y) → CH_{n+m-1}(X ×_S Y) is well defined, unconditionally

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantChowClassCapBaseFundamentalClass_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Bivariant classes towards a Dedekind base are Chow classes.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Stacks
section 42.63 — locally the spectrum of a Dedekind domain, with `δ = 0` at the closed points and
`δ = 1` elsewhere — every irreducible component of `S` being of dimension one, and let `X` be a
scheme locally of finite type over `S`. For every `p ∈ ℤ` the canonical map
`A^p(X ⟶ S) ⟶ CH_{1-p}(X)`, `c ↦ c ∩ [S]₁`, is bijective. Here `A^p(X ⟶ S)` is the group of
bivariant classes of Stacks 0B76 for the structure morphism of `X`, and `c ∩ [S]₁` is read on `X`
through `X ×_S S ≅ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantChowClassCapBaseFundamentalClass_bijective :
    Function.Bijective (bivariantChowClassCapBaseFundamentalClass sX p)
declarations.comment: the canonical map A^p(X → S) → CH_{1-p}(X), c ↦ c ∩ [S]₁, is bijective; the components of S are curves, as in Example 02QN (for S the spectrum of a field the statement fails)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyDedekindEquiv
declarations.doc:
The canonical identification `A^p(X ⟶ S) = CH_{1-p}(X)` over a Dedekind base whose
irreducible components are curves, as an isomorphism of groups: `c ↦ c ∩ [S]₁`. Its inverse
sends `α` to the class `c_α` with `c_α ∩ α' = α × α'` (`chowCohomologyDedekindEquiv_symm`).
declarations.comment: the canonical identification A^p(X → S) = CH_{1-p}(X) as an isomorphism of groups, c ↦ c ∩ [S]₁, with inverse α ↦ c_α; the components of S are curves, as in Example 02QN

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCapBaseFundamentalClass_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC5**, corrected form. Let `(S, δ)` be a base as in section 42.63 of the Stacks
Project with no zero-dimensional component, and let `X` be locally of finite type over `S`. Then
`c ↦ c ∩ [S]₁` is a bijection `A^p(X → S) → CH_{1-p}(X)` for every `p ∈ ℤ`.

The hypothesis `hS1` is the correction. A field is a Dedekind domain, so the source's statement
also admits a component `Spec k` of `S` with `δ ≡ 0`, and there it fails: `[S]₁` restricts to
`[Spec k]₁ = 0`, so the map kills the nonzero class `1 ∈ A^0(Spec k → S)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantCapBaseFundamentalClass_bijective (hS : IsDedekindChowBase C)
    (hS1 : HasNoZeroDimensionalComponent C) :
    Function.Bijective
      (bivariantCapBaseFundamentalClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX p)
declarations.comment: corrected form: the base is assumed to have no zero-dimensional component (`Stacks.Chow.HasNoZeroDimensionalComponent`, every closed point a proper specialization); the source admits such components, a field being a Dedekind domain, and for `S = Spec k` the map `c ↦ c ∩ [S]₁` is zero while `A^0(S → S)` contains `1`. Bivariant classes are those of the Gysin system of invertible modules, `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCapBaseFundamentalClassEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC5**, corrected form, as an isomorphism of groups: over a base as in section 42.63
with no zero-dimensional component, `A^p(X → S) ≃+ CH_{1-p}(X)`, `c ↦ c ∩ [S]₁`.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantCapBaseFundamentalClassEquiv (hS : IsDedekindChowBase C)
    (hS1 : HasNoZeroDimensionalComponent C) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (𝟙 C.S) sX (Category.comp_id sX) p ≃+
      chowGroup C sX (1 - p)
declarations.comment: corrected form: the base is assumed to have no zero-dimensional component (`Stacks.Chow.HasNoZeroDimensionalComponent`); the identification A^p(X → S) = CH_{1-p}(X) as an isomorphism of groups, at the Gysin system of invertible modules

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_isExteriorProductOverBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC5, the inverse map**, corrected form. Over a base as in section 42.63 with no
zero-dimensional component, every `α ∈ CH_{1-p}(X)` is `c_α ∩ [S]₁` for a bivariant class
`c_α ∈ A^p(X → S)` acting by exterior product with `α`, `c_α ∩ α' = α × α'`; by
`Stacks.Chow.bivariantCapBaseFundamentalClass_injective` it is unique.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isExteriorProductOverBase (hS : IsDedekindChowBase C)
    (hS1 : HasNoZeroDimensionalComponent C) (α : chowGroup C sX (1 - p)) :
    ∃ c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (𝟙 C.S) sX (Category.comp_id sX) p,
      IsExteriorProductOverBase C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (1 - p) p α c ∧
        bivariantCapBaseFundamentalClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX p c = α
declarations.comment: corrected form: the inverse α ↦ c_α acts by exterior product, c_α ∩ α' = α × α'

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCommuteOverBase_of_isChowOperationGenerated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC6.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Stacks section 42.63, let `X` be a scheme locally of
finite type over `S` and let `c ∈ A^p(X ⟶ S)`. Let `Y ⟶ Z` be a morphism of schemes locally of
finite type over `S` and let `c' ∈ A^q(Y ⟶ Z)`. Then `c ∘ c' = c' ∘ c`: capping with `c` and
capping with `c'` may be performed in either order, the two results being read on the two
iterated fibre products `X ×_S (Y ×_Z T)` and `Y ×_Z (X ×_S T)` of a test scheme through the
canonical comparison isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantCommuteOverBase_of_isChowOperationGenerated
    (hfd : ∀ {A B : Scheme.{u}} (sA : A ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sA]
      (sB : B ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sB] (v : A ⟶ B) [LocallyOfFiniteType v] [Flat v]
      (hv : v ≫ sB = sA) (r : ℕ) (hr : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension v r) (k : ℤ),
      FlatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C sA sB v hv r hr k)
    (hgen : IsChowOperationGenerated C G sX p c) :
    BivariantCommuteOverBase C G sX sZ w p q c c'
declarations.comment: the commutation c ∘ c' = c' ∘ c, read on the cap operations of the two composites, for c an integral combination of flat pullbacks towards the base, the generators of the presentation in the proof of Stacks 0FC5 other than proper pushforwards and Gysin maps; given Stacks 02S1 for every flat morphism over the base

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCommuteOverBase_of_isDedekindChowBase_general
declarations.doc:
Let `(S, δ)` be as in section 42.63 of the Stacks Project, let `X` be a scheme locally of
finite type over `S` and let `c ∈ A^p(X ⟶ S)`. Let `Y ⟶ Z` be a morphism of schemes locally of
finite type over `S` and let `c' ∈ A^q(Y ⟶ Z)`. Then `c ∘ c' = c' ∘ c`:
capping with `c` and capping with `c'` may be performed in either order, the two results being
read on `X ×_S (Y ×_Z T)` and `Y ×_Z (X ×_S T)` through the canonical comparison isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantCommuteOverBase_of_isDedekindChowBase_general (hS : IsDedekindChowBase C)
    {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (sZ : Z ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sZ] (w : Y ⟶ Z)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType w] (q : ℤ)
    (c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (𝟙 C.S) sX (Category.comp_id sX) p)
    (c' : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (w ≫ sZ) sZ w rfl q) :
    BivariantCommuteOverBase C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sZ w p q c c'
declarations.comment: the commutation c ∘ c' = c' ∘ c read on the cap operations of the two composites (`Stacks.Chow.BivariantCommuteOverBase`), for the bivariant classes of the Gysin system of invertible modules `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCommuteOverBase_of_isChowOperationProperGenerated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC6.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Stacks section 42.63, let `X` be a scheme locally of
finite type over `S` and let `c ∈ A^p(X ⟶ S)`. Let `Y ⟶ Z` be a morphism of schemes locally of
finite type over `S` and let `c' ∈ A^q(Y ⟶ Z)`. Then `c ∘ c' = c' ∘ c`: capping with `c` and
capping with `c'` may be performed in either order, the two results being read on the two
iterated fibre products `X ×_S (Y ×_Z T)` and `Y ×_Z (X ×_S T)` of a test scheme through the
canonical comparison isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantCommuteOverBase_of_isChowOperationProperGenerated
    (hfd : ∀ {A B : Scheme.{u}} (sA : A ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sA]
      (sB : B ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sB] (v : A ⟶ B) [LocallyOfFiniteType v] [Flat v]
      (hv : v ≫ sB = sA) (r : ℕ) (hr : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension v r) (k : ℤ),
      FlatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C sA sB v hv r hr k)
    (hgen : IsChowOperationProperGenerated C G hpp sX p c) :
    BivariantCommuteOverBase C G sX sZ w p q c c'
declarations.comment: the commutation c ∘ c' = c' ∘ c, read on the cap operations of the two composites, for a c in the subgroup of A^p(X ⟶ S) generated by the flat pullbacks towards the base and by their proper pushforwards: of the generators the proof of Stacks 0FC5 exhibits this covers flat pullback, proper pushforward and integral combinations and not the Gysin maps; given Stacks 02S1 for flat and 02S2 for proper maps over the base

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantChowClass.comp_comm_of_isDedekindChowBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC6.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Stacks section 42.63 — locally the spectrum of a
Dedekind domain, with `δ = 0` at the closed points and `δ = 1` elsewhere. Let `X` be a scheme
locally of finite type over `S` and `c ∈ A^p(X ⟶ S)`. Let `f : Y ⟶ Z` be a morphism of schemes
locally of finite type over `S` and `c' ∈ A^q(Y ⟶ Z)`. Then `c ∘ c' = c' ∘ c` in
`A^{p+q}(X ×_S Y ⟶ Z)`.

Here `c ∘ c' = res(c) ∘ c'` with `res(c) ∈ A^p(X ×_S Y ⟶ Y)` the restriction of `c` along
`Y ⟶ S`, and `c' ∘ c = res(c') ∘ res(c)` with `res(c) ∈ A^p(X ×_S Z ⟶ Z)` the restriction of `c`
along `Z ⟶ S` and `res(c') ∈ A^q(Y ×_Z (X ×_S Z) ⟶ X ×_S Z)` the restriction of `c'` along
`X ×_S Z ⟶ Z` (Stacks 0F9Z, 0FA2). The second composite lives on `Y ×_Z (X ×_S Z)` and in degree
`q + p`; it is read on `X ×_S Y` through the canonical isomorphism and in degree `p + q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem BivariantChowClass.comp_comm_of_isDedekindChowBase (hC : IsDedekindChowBase C)
    (c : BivariantChowClass C sX (𝟙 C.S) sX (Category.comp_id sX) p)
    (c' : BivariantChowClass C sY sZ f hf q) :
    (c.restrict sY (Category.comp_id sY)).comp c' =
      (((c'.restrict (pullback.snd sX sZ)
          (BivariantChowClass.restrict_structure_eq (Category.comp_id sX) sZ
            (Category.comp_id sZ))).comp
        (c.restrict sZ (Category.comp_id sZ))).degreeCongr (add_comm q p)).transport
        (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq
          (BivariantChowClass.restrict_structure_eq (Category.comp_id sX) sY
            (Category.comp_id sY)) hf)
        (pointClassCompositeIso C sX sZ f hf) (pointClassCompositeIso_hom_comp C sX sZ f hf)
declarations.comment: c ∘ c' = c' ∘ c in A^{p+q}(X ×_S Y → Z) for c ∈ A^p(X → S) and c' ∈ A^q(Y → Z), the composites read as in Stacks 0FA2

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exteriorProductDedekindChowTensor_cap_comm
declarations.doc:
**The exterior product over a Dedekind base commutes with capping.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in
Stacks section 42.63 — locally the spectrum of a Dedekind domain, with `δ = 0` at the closed points
and `δ = 1` elsewhere — let `X` be locally of finite type over `S`, let `Y ⟶ Z` be a morphism of
schemes locally of finite type over `S` and let `c' ∈ A^q(Y ⟶ Z)`. Then for `α ∈ CH_n(X)` and
`β ∈ CH_m(T)`, `t : T ⟶ Z` a test scheme,

  `α × (c' ∩ β) = c' ∩ (α × β)`,

the left hand side living on `X ×_S (Y ×_Z T)` and the right hand side on `Y ×_Z (X ×_S T)`,
compared through the canonical isomorphism `Stacks.Chow.mixedCommuteHom`, and in the degrees
`n + (m - q) - 1` and `(n + m - 1) - q`. The source's statement is the case `T = Z`. The exterior
product is the map of Stacks 0FC4 and `c'` ranges over the whole group `A^q(Y ⟶ Z)` of
Stacks 0B76.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorProductDedekindChowTensor_cap_comm {T : Scheme.{u}} (t : T ⟶ Z)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType t] (α : chowGroup C sX n) (β : chowGroup C (t ≫ sZ) m) :
    chowPushforwardOfIso C (pullback.fst sX (pullback.fst w t ≫ (w ≫ sZ)) ≫ sX)
        (pullback.fst w (pullback.snd sX (t ≫ sZ) ≫ t) ≫ (w ≫ sZ))
        (mixedCommuteHom sX sZ w t) (mixedCommuteHom_comp_structureMorphism sX sZ w t)
        (n + (m - q) - 1)
        (exteriorProductDedekindChowTensor C sX (pullback.fst w t ≫ (w ≫ sZ)) n (m - q) hC
          (α ⊗ₜ[ℤ] c'.cap t m β)) =
      chowGroupDegreeEquiv C (pullback.fst w (pullback.snd sX (t ≫ sZ) ≫ t) ≫ (w ≫ sZ))
        (by ring : (n + m - 1) - q = n + (m - q) - 1)
        (c'.cap (pullback.snd sX (t ≫ sZ) ≫ t) (n + m - 1)
          (chowGroupCongr C
            (by rw [Category.assoc]; exact pullback.condition (f := sX) (g := t ≫ sZ))
            (n + m - 1)
            (exteriorProductDedekindChowTensor C sX (t ≫ sZ) n m hC (α ⊗ₜ[ℤ] β))))
declarations.comment: α × (c' ∩ β) = c' ∩ (α × β) for every c' ∈ A^q(Y → Z) and every test scheme T → Z (the remark is the case T = Z), over every base as in Section 42.63, with the exterior product of Stacks 0FC4 on the tensor product of Chow groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exteriorProductDedekindChow_cap_comm_of_isDedekindChowBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC7.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in section 42.63 of the Stacks Project, let `X` be locally
of finite type over `S` and `α ∈ CH_n(X)`, let `Y ⟶ Z` be a morphism of schemes locally of finite
type over `S` and `c' ∈ A^q(Y ⟶ Z)`. Then for every test scheme `t : T ⟶ Z` and `β ∈ CH_m(T)`,

  `α × (c' ∩ β) = c' ∩ (α × β)`

on `X ×_S Y ×_Z T`, the two iterated fibre products being compared through
`Stacks.Chow.mixedCommuteHom`, the exterior product being that of Stacks 0FC4.

Write `α = c ∩ [S]₁ + [a₀]` with `c ∩ [S₀]₀ = 0` and `a₀` supported over the zero-dimensional
locus (`Stacks.Chow.exists_bivariantCapBaseFundamentalClass_add_mk_eq`). The exterior product with
`[a₀]` vanishes, `c` acts by exterior product with `c ∩ [S]₁`, and `c` commutes with `c'` by
Stacks 0FC6 (`Stacks.Chow.bivariantCommuteOverBase_of_isDedekindChowBase_general`), so
`Stacks.Chow.exteriorProductDedekindChow_cap_comm` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorProductDedekindChow_cap_comm_of_isDedekindChowBase (hS : IsDedekindChowBase C)
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sZ : Z ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sZ] (w : Y ⟶ Z) [LocallyOfFiniteType w] (n q : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C sX n)
    (c' : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (w ≫ sZ) sZ w rfl q)
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (t : T ⟶ Z) [LocallyOfFiniteType t] (m : ℤ) (β : chowGroup C (t ≫ sZ) m) :
    chowPushforwardOfIso C (pullback.fst sX (pullback.fst w t ≫ (w ≫ sZ)) ≫ sX)
        (pullback.fst w (pullback.snd sX (t ≫ sZ) ≫ t) ≫ (w ≫ sZ))
        (mixedCommuteHom sX sZ w t) (mixedCommuteHom_comp_structureMorphism sX sZ w t)
        (n + (m - q) - 1)
        (exteriorProductDedekindChow C sX (pullback.fst w t ≫ (w ≫ sZ)) n (m - q)
          (hS.exteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence sX _ n (m - q)) α
          (c'.cap t m β)) =
      chowGroupDegreeEquiv C (pullback.fst w (pullback.snd sX (t ≫ sZ) ≫ t) ≫ (w ≫ sZ))
        (by ring : (n + m - 1) - q = n + (m - q) - 1)
        (c'.cap (pullback.snd sX (t ≫ sZ) ≫ t) (n + m - 1)
          (chowGroupCongr C
            (by rw [Category.assoc]; exact pullback.condition (f := sX) (g := t ≫ sZ))
            (n + m - 1) (exteriorProductDedekindChow C sX (t ≫ sZ) n m
              (hS.exteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence sX (t ≫ sZ) n m) α β)))
declarations.comment: α × (c' ∩ β) = c' ∩ (α × β) for every bivariant class c' ∈ A^q(Y → Z) and every test scheme T → Z (the remark is the case T = Z), over every base as in Section 42.63, including bases with zero-dimensional components; the exterior product is that of Stacks 0FC4

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exteriorProductDedekindChow_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FC8.** Associativity of the exterior product over a Dedekind base, on Chow
groups: for Chow classes `a`, `b`, `c` the two iterated exterior products agree after transport
along the associator of the triple fibre product and along the equality of the two iterated
delta-dimensions.

Proved from the cycle-level identity `hassoc`, which is the step the source leaves to
"associativity of fibre product of schemes"; see the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.ExteriorProductDedekind.Associativity` for why that step is
not formal. The remaining hypotheses are the Stacks 0FC4 descent conditions for the three
exterior products involved and the Stacks 02S2 condition for the pushforward along the
associator, exactly as everywhere else in this repository.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorProductDedekindChow_assoc
    (hXY : ExteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C f' g' n m)
    (hXYZ : ExteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
      (pullback.fst f' g' ≫ f') h' (n + m - 1) l)
    (hYZ : ExteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C g' h' m l)
    (hXYZ' : ExteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C f'
      (pullback.fst g' h' ≫ g') n (m + l - 1))
    (hpf : ProperPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
      (pullback.fst (pullback.fst f' g' ≫ f') h' ≫ (pullback.fst f' g' ≫ f'))
      (pullback.fst f' (pullback.fst g' h' ≫ g') ≫ f')
      (tripleFibreProductAssoc f' g' h').hom
      (tripleFibreProductAssoc_hom_structureMorphism f' g' h')
      (n + m - 1 + l - 1))
    (hassoc : IsExteriorProductDedekindAssociative C f' g' h' n m l)
    (α : CycleGroup C f' n) (β : CycleGroup C g' m) (γ : CycleGroup C h' l) :
    exteriorProductDedekind_degree_assoc n m l ▸
        properChowPushforward C
          (pullback.fst (pullback.fst f' g' ≫ f') h' ≫ (pullback.fst f' g' ≫ f'))
          (pullback.fst f' (pullback.fst g' h' ≫ g') ≫ f')
          (tripleFibreProductAssoc f' g' h').hom
          (tripleFibreProductAssoc_hom_structureMorphism f' g' h')
          (n + m - 1 + l - 1) hpf
          (exteriorProductDedekindChow C (pullback.fst f' g' ≫ f') h' (n + m - 1) l hXYZ
            (exteriorProductDedekindChow C f' g' n m hXY
              (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C f' n) α)
              (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C g' m) β))
            (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C h' l) γ)) =
      exteriorProductDedekindChow C f' (pullback.fst g' h' ≫ g') n (m + l - 1) hXYZ'
        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C f' n) α)
        (exteriorProductDedekindChow C g' h' m l hYZ
          (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C g' m) β)
          (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C h' l) γ))
declarations.comment: associativity on Chow groups, together with the associator of the triple fibre product over the base and the agreement of the two iterated delta-dimensions; the cycle-level identity is a hypothesis, since it needs the multiplicity of a point of a triple fibre product to factor through the two iterated double products, which this repository does not have

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exteriorProductDedekindChow_assoc_of_isDedekindChowBase
declarations.doc:
**Associativity of the exterior product.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Stacks section 42.63,
let `X`, `Y`, `Z` be locally of finite type over `S`, and let `a ∈ CH_n(X)`, `b ∈ CH_m(Y)`,
`c ∈ CH_l(Z)`. Then `(a × b) × c = a × (b × c)` in `CH_*(X ×_S Y ×_S Z)`.

The two sides live on the two bracketings `(X ×_S Y) ×_S Z` and `X ×_S (Y ×_S Z)` of the triple
fibre product and in the two spellings `(n + m - 1) + l - 1` and `n + (m + l - 1) - 1` of the same
delta-dimension, so the left side is carried across by proper pushforward along the associator of
the fibre product and by the equality of the two degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorProductDedekindChow_assoc_of_isDedekindChowBase (hC : IsDedekindChowBase C)
    (a : chowGroup C f n) (b : chowGroup C g m) (c : chowGroup C h l) :
    exteriorProductDedekind_degree_assoc n m l ▸
        properChowPushforward C
          (pullback.fst (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) h ≫ (pullback.fst f g ≫ f))
          (pullback.fst f (pullback.fst g h ≫ g) ≫ f)
          (tripleFibreProductAssoc f g h).hom
          (tripleFibreProductAssoc_hom_structureMorphism f g h)
          (n + m - 1 + l - 1)
          (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion
            (tripleFibreProductAssoc f g h).hom C _ _
            (tripleFibreProductAssoc_hom_structureMorphism f g h) (n + m - 1 + l - 1))
          (exteriorProductDedekindChow C (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) h (n + m - 1) l
            (exteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isDedekindChowBase C
              (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) h (n + m - 1) l hC)
            (exteriorProductDedekindChow C f g n m
              (exteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isDedekindChowBase C f g n m hC)
              a b) c) =
      exteriorProductDedekindChow C f (pullback.fst g h ≫ g) n (m + l - 1)
        (exteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isDedekindChowBase C f
          (pullback.fst g h ≫ g) n (m + l - 1) hC) a
        (exteriorProductDedekindChow C g h m l
          (exteriorProductFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isDedekindChowBase C g h m l hC)
          b c)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.IsDedekindChowBase.intersectionProduct_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FCA.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in section 42.63: `S` locally Noetherian with an open
covering by spectra of Dedekind domains, `δ = 0` at closed points and `δ = 1` elsewhere. Let `X`
be smooth over `S`, of arbitrary and not necessarily constant relative dimension, and let `Y`,
`Z`, `W` be locally of finite type over `X`. As section 42.64 prescribes, the intersection product
`α · β = Δ^!(α × β)` is formed over the open and closed parts `X_e` of `X` where `X ⟶ S` has
relative dimension `e` (`Stacks.WeilCohomology.dimPart`), with the Gysin class
`Δ^! ∈ A^e(X_e ⟶ X_e ×_S X_e)` of the diagonal of Stacks 0FBR: for `α ∈ CH_n(Y)` and
`β ∈ CH_m(Z)` its component over `X_e` is `α|_{Y_e} · β|_{Z_e} ∈ CH_{n+m-1-e}(Y_e ×_{X_e} Z_e)`,
where `Y_e = a⁻¹(X_e)` and `Z_e = b⁻¹(X_e)` are the parts of `Y` and `Z` over `X_e`
(`Stacks.Chow.chowGroupDimPartOver`). Then for `γ ∈ CH_l(W)`

  `(α · β) · γ = α · (β · γ)`   in   `CH_*(Y ×_X Z ×_X W)`,

component by component, read through the associator of the triple fibre product over `X_e` and
the matching of the degrees `(n + m - 1 - e) + l - 1 - e` and `n + (m + l - 1 - e) - 1 - e`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsDedekindChowBase.intersectionProduct_assoc [Smooth sX] (n m l : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup C (a ≫ sX) n) (β : chowGroup C (b ≫ sX) m) (γ : chowGroup C (g ≫ sX) l)
    (e : ℕ) :
    chowGroupDegreeEquiv C
        (pullback.fst π[a, e] (pullback.fst π[b, e] π[g, e] ≫ π[b, e]) ≫ (π[a, e] ≫ X[e]))
        (by ring : n + m - 1 - e + l - 1 - e = n + (m + l - 1 - e) - 1 - e)
        (properChowPushforward C
          (pullback.fst (pullback.fst π[a, e] π[b, e] ≫ π[a, e]) π[g, e] ≫
            ((pullback.fst π[a, e] π[b, e] ≫ π[a, e]) ≫ X[e]))
          (pullback.fst π[a, e] (pullback.fst π[b, e] π[g, e] ≫ π[b, e]) ≫ (π[a, e] ≫ X[e]))
          (tripleProductAssoc π[a, e] π[b, e] π[g, e]).hom
          (tripleProductAssoc_hom_comp_structureMorphism C X[e] π[a, e] π[b, e] π[g, e])
          (n + m - 1 - e + l - 1 - e) (properPushforwardDescends C _ _ _ _ _)
          (hS.intersectionProduct (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) X[e]
            (pullback.fst π[a, e] π[b, e] ≫ π[a, e]) π[g, e] e Δ[e] (n + m - 1 - e) l
            (chowGroupCongr C (Category.assoc (pullback.fst π[a, e] π[b, e]) π[a, e] X[e]).symm
              (n + m - 1 - e)
              (hS.intersectionProduct (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) X[e] π[a, e] π[b, e] e Δ[e] n m
                (res[a, e, n, α] ⊗ₜ[ℤ] res[b, e, m, β])) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] res[g, e, l, γ]))) =
      hS.intersectionProduct (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) X[e] π[a, e]
        (pullback.fst π[b, e] π[g, e] ≫ π[b, e]) e Δ[e] n (m + l - 1 - e)
        (res[a, e, n, α] ⊗ₜ[ℤ]
          chowGroupCongr C (Category.assoc (pullback.fst π[b, e] π[g, e]) π[b, e] X[e]).symm
            (m + l - 1 - e)
            (hS.intersectionProduct (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) X[e] π[b, e] π[g, e] e Δ[e] m l
              (res[b, e, m, β] ⊗ₜ[ℤ] res[g, e, l, γ])))
declarations.comment: the whole statement (α·β)·γ = α·(β·γ) in CH_*(Y ×_X Z ×_X W) for X smooth over a base as in section 42.63 (zero-dimensional components allowed), of arbitrary relative dimension, Y, Z, W locally of finite type over X and arbitrary α, β, γ; the product is Δ^!(α × β) with Δ^! the Gysin class of the diagonal of Stacks 0FBR and × the exterior product of Stacks 0FC4, formed on the open and closed parts of X of constant relative dimension as in section 42.64, bivariant classes those of `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.IsDedekindChowBase.chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_bijective_of_smooth_of_equidimensional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FCB, first clause.** Let `(S, δ)` be a base as in section 42.63 of the Stacks Project
(locally the spectrum of a Dedekind domain, fields allowed; `δ = 0` at closed points and `1`
elsewhere), and let `X` be smooth over `S`, equidimensional of dimension `d`: every irreducible
component of `X` has δ-dimension `d`. Then

  `A^p(X) ⟶ CH_{d-p}(X)`,   `c ↦ c ∩ [X]_d`,

is an isomorphism for every `p ∈ ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_bijective_of_smooth_of_equidimensional (d : ℕ)
    (hd : ∀ V : irreducibleComponents X,
      deltaDimension C sX ⟨V, V.2.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents _ V.2⟩ = d)
    (p : ℤ) :
    Function.Bijective
      (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX d p)
declarations.comment: first clause, in full: S as in section 42.63 with field components allowed, X smooth over S and equidimensional of dimension d (every irreducible component of δ-dimension d); bivariant classes are those of the Gysin system of invertible modules, `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.IsDedekindChowBase.chowGroupRestrict_chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_mulId
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FCB, second clause**, corrected form: over the one-dimensional part of the base. Let
`(S, δ)` be a base as in section 42.63 (field components allowed), and let `X` be smooth over `S`
and equidimensional of dimension `e + 1`. Write `X₁ ⊆ X` for the open and closed part over the
one-dimensional part `S₁` of `S`; it is smooth of relative dimension `e` over `S`. Then via
`Θ : c ↦ c ∩ [X]_{e+1}` composition of bivariant classes turns into the intersection product of
section 42.64 on `X₁`, formed with the Gysin class `Δ^!` of the diagonal of `X₁` (Stacks 0FBR):

  `Θ(a · b)|_{X₁} = Θ(a)|_{X₁} · Θ(b)|_{X₁}`.

When `S` has no zero-dimensional component, `X₁ = X`. Over the zero-dimensional part the clause is
false as stated, the exterior product of section 42.63 vanishing there identically
(`Stacks.Chow.not_chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_mulId_fieldChowSituation`); for `X`
equidimensional of dimension `0` the part `X₁` is empty.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowGroupRestrict_chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_mulId (e : ℕ)
    (hd : ∀ V : irreducibleComponents X,
      deltaDimension C sX ⟨V, V.2.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents _ V.2⟩ = e + 1)
    (p q : ℤ) (a : chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX p)
    (b : chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX q) :
    chowGroupRestrict C sX ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
        (hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι rfl ((e : ℤ) + 1 - (p + q))
        (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (e + 1) (p + q)
          (a.mulId C sX b)) =
      chowGroupDegreeEquiv C ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
        (by ring : ((e : ℤ) + 1 - p) + ((e : ℤ) + 1 - q) - 1 - e = (e + 1) - (p + q))
        (chowGroupSelfProductUnitCollapse C ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
          (((e : ℤ) + 1 - p) + ((e : ℤ) + 1 - q) - 1 - e)
          (hS.intersectionProduct (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
            ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX) (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) e
            (bivariantClassCongrBase C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
              (pullback.diagonal ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX))
              (diagonal_comp_selfProductStructure C ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX))
              rfl e (diagonalGysinClass C ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
                ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
                (hS.relativeDimension_oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX e hd)))
            ((e : ℤ) + 1 - p) ((e : ℤ) + 1 - q)
            (chowGroupCongr C (Category.id_comp _).symm ((e : ℤ) + 1 - p)
              (chowGroupRestrict C sX ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
                (hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι rfl ((e : ℤ) + 1 - p)
                (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (e + 1) p a))
              ⊗ₜ[ℤ] chowGroupCongr C (Category.id_comp _).symm ((e : ℤ) + 1 - q)
                (chowGroupRestrict C sX ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
                  (hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι rfl ((e : ℤ) + 1 - q)
                  (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (e + 1) q
                    b)))))
declarations.comment: second clause, corrected form: Θ(a · b) = Θ(a) · Θ(b) on the part X₁ of X over the one-dimensional part of S (all of X when S has no zero-dimensional component), with the intersection product of section 42.64 formed with the Gysin class Δ^! of the diagonal; over a zero-dimensional component the clause is false as stated, see `Stacks.Chow.not_chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_mulId_fieldChowSituation`; S as in section 42.63 with field components allowed, X smooth and equidimensional of dimension e + 1

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.IsDedekindChowBase.chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_bijective_and_mulId
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FCB.** Let `(S, δ)` be a base as in section 42.63 of the Stacks Project (locally the
spectrum of a Dedekind domain, a field being one; `δ = 0` at closed points and `1` elsewhere), and
let `X` be smooth over `S`, equidimensional of dimension `d`: every irreducible component of `X`
has δ-dimension `d`. Write `Θ : c ↦ c ∩ [X]_d`. Then

1. `Θ : A^p(X) ⟶ CH_{d-p}(X)` is bijective for every `p ∈ ℤ`;
2. if `d = e + 1`, then `Θ(a · b)|_{X₁} = Θ(a)|_{X₁} · Θ(b)|_{X₁}` on the open and closed part
   `X₁` of `X` over the one-dimensional part of `S`, the intersection product of section 42.64
   being formed with the Gysin class `Δ^!` of the diagonal of `X₁` (Stacks 0FBR); `X₁ = X` when
   `S` has no zero-dimensional component;
3. the second clause as printed fails over a field `k`: for `S = X = Spec k`, `d = 0`, one has
   `Θ(1 · 1) ≠ 0`, whereas the intersection product of section 42.64 vanishes on
   `CH_0(X) ⊗ CH_0(X)` for every class of the diagonal.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_bijective_and_mulId (d : ℕ)
    (hd : ∀ V : irreducibleComponents X,
      deltaDimension C sX ⟨V, V.2.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents _ V.2⟩ = d) :
    (∀ p : ℤ, Function.Bijective
      (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX d p)) ∧
    (∀ (e : ℕ) (hde : d = e + 1) (p q : ℤ)
      (a : chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX p)
      (b : chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX q),
      chowGroupRestrict C sX ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
          (hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι rfl ((e : ℤ) + 1 - (p + q))
          (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (e + 1) (p + q)
            (a.mulId C sX b)) =
        chowGroupDegreeEquiv C ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
          (by ring : ((e : ℤ) + 1 - p) + ((e : ℤ) + 1 - q) - 1 - e = (e + 1) - (p + q))
          (chowGroupSelfProductUnitCollapse C ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
            (((e : ℤ) + 1 - p) + ((e : ℤ) + 1 - q) - 1 - e)
            (hS.intersectionProduct (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
              ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX) (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) e
              (bivariantClassCongrBase C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
                (pullback.diagonal ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX))
                (diagonal_comp_selfProductStructure C ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX))
                rfl e (diagonalGysinClass C ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
                  ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
                  (hS.relativeDimension_oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX e
                    (fun V ↦ (hd V).trans (by exact_mod_cast hde)))))
              ((e : ℤ) + 1 - p) ((e : ℤ) + 1 - q)
              (chowGroupCongr C (Category.id_comp _).symm ((e : ℤ) + 1 - p)
                (chowGroupRestrict C sX ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
                  (hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι rfl ((e : ℤ) + 1 - p)
                  (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (e + 1) p a))
                ⊗ₜ[ℤ] chowGroupCongr C (Category.id_comp _).symm ((e : ℤ) + 1 - q)
                  (chowGroupRestrict C sX ((hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι ≫ sX)
                    (hS.oneDimensionalPartPreimage sX).ι rfl ((e : ℤ) + 1 - q)
                    (chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (e + 1) q
                      b)))))) ∧
    (∀ (k : Type u) [Field k],
      chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass (fieldChowSituation k)
          (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S) 0 (0 + 0)
          ((bivariantIdentityClassOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)
            (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S)).mulId (fieldChowSituation k)
            (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S)
            (bivariantIdentityClassOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)
              (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S))) ≠ 0 ∧
        ∀ (c : BivariantClass (fieldChowSituation k)
            (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S)
            (selfProductStructure (fieldChowSituation k) (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S))
            (pullback.diagonal (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S))
            (diagonal_comp_selfProductStructure (fieldChowSituation k)
              (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S)) 0)
          (t : TensorProduct ℤ
            (chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k)
              (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S ≫ 𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S) 0)
            (chowGroup (fieldChowSituation k)
              (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S ≫ 𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S) 0)),
          (isDedekindChowBase_fieldChowSituation k).intersectionProduct
            (gysinSystemOfInvertible (fieldChowSituation k)) (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S)
            (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S) (𝟙 (fieldChowSituation k).S) 0 c 0 0 t = 0)
declarations.comment: the whole tag: Θ is bijective in every degree, for S as in section 42.63 (a field is a Dedekind domain, so field components are part of the source's hypothesis) and X smooth and equidimensional of dimension d (δ-dimension of every irreducible component); the second clause in corrected form, Θ(a · b) = Θ(a) · Θ(b) on the part X₁ of X over the one-dimensional part of S (all of X when S has no zero-dimensional component), with the product Δ^!(α × β) of section 42.64; and the formal counterexample to the second clause as printed, S = X = Spec k, where the exterior product of section 42.63 vanishes, also stated as `Stacks.Chow.not_chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_mulId_fieldChowSituation`

declarations.name: Module.depth_le_depth_localized_add_ringKrullDim_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Depth drops by at most `dim(R/𝔭)` under localization.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian
local ring, `M` a finite `R`-module and `𝔭 ⊆ R` a prime ideal. Then
`depth_𝔪(M) ≤ depth_{𝔭R_𝔭}(M_𝔭) + dim(R/𝔭)`. The localization is presented abstractly: `Rₚ`
is any localization of `R` at `𝔭` and `f : M →ₗ[R] Mₚ` any localization of `M` at `𝔭`. The
inequality is read in `WithBot ℕ∞`, where `ringKrullDim` lives.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depth_le_depth_localized_add_ringKrullDim_quotient {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (Rₚ : Type*) [CommRing Rₚ] [Algebra R Rₚ]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime Rₚ p] [IsLocalRing Rₚ] (Mₚ : Type*) [AddCommGroup Mₚ]
    [Module R Mₚ] [Module Rₚ Mₚ] [IsScalarTower R Rₚ Mₚ] (f : M →ₗ[R] Mₚ)
    [IsLocalizedModule p.primeCompl f] :
    (depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) M : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤
      (depth Rₚ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal Rₚ) Mₚ : WithBot ℕ∞) + ringKrullDim (R ⧸ p)
declarations.comment:
Stated in `WithBot ℕ∞` with the smaller side on the left, for `Module.depth`
(Tag 00LI) along the maximal ideals of `R` and of `Rₚ`, and with the localizations presented by
`IsLocalization.AtPrime` and `IsLocalizedModule`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.IsArtinianCategory
declarations.doc:
An abelian category is *Artinian* if every object is Artinian, i.e. satisfies the
descending chain condition on subobjects. Unlike mathlib's `Artinian`, no smallness
condition is imposed.
declarations.statement: class IsArtinianCategory [Abelian C] : Prop
declarations.comment:
part (2): an abelian category is Artinian if every object is Artinian; part (1) is
mathlib's `IsArtinianObject`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.IsNoetherianAbelianCategory
declarations.doc:
An abelian category is Noetherian if every object of it is Noetherian, i.e. satisfies the
ascending chain condition on subobjects. Unlike Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Noetherian`, no
smallness of the category is required.
declarations.statement: class IsNoetherianAbelianCategory [Abelian C] : Prop
declarations.comment: (2): an abelian category is Noetherian if every object is Noetherian.

declarations.statement: instance : CategoryTheory.isArtinianObject.IsClosedUnderQuotients (C := C)
instance : CategoryTheory.isArtinianObject.IsClosedUnderExtensions (C := C)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isArtinianObject_iff_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FCH**: for a short exact sequence `0 ⟶ A₁ ⟶ A₂ ⟶ A₃ ⟶ 0` in an abelian
category, `A₂` is Artinian if and only if `A₁` and `A₃` are Artinian.
declarations.statement:
lemma isArtinianObject_iff_of_shortExact {S : ShortComplex C} (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    IsArtinianObject S.X₂ ↔ IsArtinianObject S.X₁ ∧ IsArtinianObject S.X₃
instance : CategoryTheory.isNoetherianObject.IsClosedUnderQuotients (C := C)
instance : CategoryTheory.isNoetherianObject.IsClosedUnderExtensions (C := C)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isNoetherianObject_iff_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FCI**: for a short exact sequence `0 ⟶ A₁ ⟶ A₂ ⟶ A₃ ⟶ 0` in an abelian
category, `A₂` is Noetherian if and only if `A₁` and `A₃` are Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
lemma isNoetherianObject_iff_of_shortExact {S : ShortComplex C} (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    IsNoetherianObject S.X₂ ↔ IsNoetherianObject S.X₁ ∧ IsNoetherianObject S.X₃

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isArtinianObject_and_isNoetherianObject_iff_exists_filtration
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FCJ**: an object of an abelian category is Artinian and Noetherian if and
only if it admits a finite filtration by subobjects with simple successive quotients.
declarations.statement:
lemma isArtinianObject_and_isNoetherianObject_iff_exists_filtration (X : C) :
    (IsArtinianObject X ∧ IsNoetherianObject X) ↔
      ∃ (a : ℕ → Subobject X) (n : ℕ) (hle : ∀ i, i < n → a i ≤ a (i + 1)),
        a 0 = ⊥ ∧ a n = ⊤ ∧
          ∀ i (hi : i < n), Simple (cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (hle i hi)))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Subobject.jordan_holder
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FCK (Jordan–Hölder).** Let `X` be an object of an abelian category with two
filtrations `0 = a 0 ⊆ a 1 ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ a n = X` and `0 = b 0 ⊆ b 1 ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ b m = X` by subobjects whose
successive quotients `a (i + 1) / a i` and `b (j + 1) / b j` are simple. Then `n = m`, and there
is a permutation `σ : Fin n ≃ Fin m` with `a (i + 1) / a i ≅ b (σ i + 1) / b (σ i)` for every `i`.

Stacks indexes the quotients `Sᵢ = Aᵢ/Aᵢ₋₁` by `1 ≤ i ≤ n`; here the quotient `a (i + 1) / a i`
is indexed by `i : Fin n`. Stacks assumes `X` satisfies the equivalent conditions of 0FCJ
(Artinian and Noetherian); by 0FCJ (`isArtinianObject_and_isNoetherianObject_iff_exists_filtration`)
this already follows from either filtration, so it is not assumed separately.
declarations.statement:
theorem jordan_holder (a : ℕ → Subobject X) (n : ℕ) (ha : ∀ i, i < n → a i ≤ a (i + 1))
    (ha0 : a 0 = ⊥) (han : a n = ⊤)
    (hsa : ∀ i (hi : i < n), Simple (cokernel (ofLE _ _ (ha i hi))))
    (b : ℕ → Subobject X) (m : ℕ) (hb : ∀ j, j < m → b j ≤ b (j + 1))
    (hb0 : b 0 = ⊥) (hbm : b m = ⊤)
    (hsb : ∀ j (hj : j < m), Simple (cokernel (ofLE _ _ (hb j hj)))) :
    n = m ∧ ∃ σ : Fin n ≃ Fin m, ∀ i : Fin n,
      Nonempty (cokernel (ofLE _ _ (ha i i.2)) ≅ cokernel (ofLE _ _ (hb (σ i) (σ i).2)))
declarations.comment: the quotient `a (i + 1) / a i` is indexed by `i : Fin n`; the Artinian and Noetherian hypothesis of Stacks follows from the filtrations by 0FCJ and is not assumed

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.full_faithful_essImage_minus_mapDerivedCategory
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an abelian category and `P` a Serre class in `A`, cutting out the Serre
subcategory `B = P.FullSubcategory`. Assume that for every epimorphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of `A` with
`Y ∈ B` there is an object `X'` of `B` and a morphism `g : X' ⟶ X` such that `g ≫ f` is again
epi (equivalently: some subobject of `X` belonging to `B` surjects onto `Y`). Then the
canonical functor `D⁻(B) ⥤ D⁻_B(A)` is an equivalence: the composite
`D⁻(B) ⥤ D(A)` is full and faithful and its essential image consists exactly of the bounded
above objects all of whose cohomology objects lie in `B`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem full_faithful_essImage_minus_mapDerivedCategory
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] (P : ObjectProperty A) [P.IsSerreClass]
    [P.IsClosedUnderFiniteProducts] [PreservesFiniteLimits P.ι] [PreservesFiniteColimits P.ι]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} P.FullSubcategory]
    (hP : ∀ ⦃X Y : A⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), Epi f → P Y → ∃ (X' : A) (g : X' ⟶ X), P X' ∧ Epi (g ≫ f)) :
    (Minus.ι ⋙ P.ι.mapDerivedCategory).Full ∧
      (Minus.ι ⋙ P.ι.mapDerivedCategory).Faithful ∧
      ∀ X : DerivedCategory A, (Minus.ι ⋙ P.ι.mapDerivedCategory).essImage X ↔
        ((∃ n : ℤ, X.IsLE n) ∧ ∀ i : ℤ, P ((homologyFunctor A i).obj X))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.K0
declarations.doc:
The **zeroth `K`-group** `K₀(C)` of a pretriangulated category `C`: the free abelian group
on the objects of `C` modulo the subgroup generated by the elements `[Y] - [X] - [Z]`, one for
each distinguished triangle `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z ⟶ X⟦1⟧` of `C`. The class of an object `X` is
`QuotientAddGroup.mk (FreeAbelianGroup.of X)`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev K0 (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] : Type u
declarations.comment: generalized from a triangulated to a pretriangulated category: the generators are the objects of `C` and there is one relation `[Y] - [X] - [Z] = 0` for each distinguished triangle `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z ⟶ X⟦1⟧`, as in Stacks

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.Bounded.exists_addEquiv_K0
declarations.doc:
**The zeroth `K`-group of `D^b(A)` is that of `A`**: for an abelian category `A` there is a
group isomorphism from the zeroth `K`-group of `A` (the free abelian group on the objects of `A`
modulo `[X₂] - [X₁] - [X₃]` for every short exact sequence `0 ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ 0`) to the zeroth
`K`-group of the bounded derived category of `A`, sending the class of `X` to the class of `X`
viewed as a complex in degree `0`. Such an isomorphism is unique, since the classes of objects
generate `K₀(A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem DerivedCategory.Bounded.exists_addEquiv_K0 {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A]
    [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] :
    ∃ e : KZero A ≃+ Pretriangulated.K0 (DerivedCategory.Bounded A),
      ∀ X : A, e (KZero.mk A X) =
        QuotientAddGroup.mk (FreeAbelianGroup.of
          (⟨(DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0).obj X,
            ⟨⟨0, inferInstance⟩, ⟨0, inferInstance⟩⟩⟩ : DerivedCategory.Bounded A))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.K0.map
declarations.doc:
The homomorphism `K₀(F) : K₀(C) → K₀(D)`, `[X] ↦ [F(X)]`, induced by an exact functor
`F : C ⥤ D`: the image under `F` of a distinguished triangle is distinguished, so the lift of
`X ↦ [F(X)]` to the free abelian group kills the defining relations.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def map (F : C ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] : K0 C →+ K0 D
declarations.comment:
the homomorphism itself; `map_cls` is its defining property and `map_unique` is
its uniqueness

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.K0.map_cls
declarations.doc: `K₀(F)` sends the class of an object `X` of `C` to the class of `F(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_cls (F : C ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] (X : C) :
    map F (cls X) = cls (F.obj X)
declarations.comment: the defining property of `map`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.K0.map_unique
declarations.doc:
`K₀(F)` is the only homomorphism `K₀(C) → K₀(D)` sending `[X]` to `[F(X)]` for every object
`X` of `C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_unique (F : C ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] (φ : K0 C →+ K0 D)
    (hφ : ∀ X : C, φ (cls X) = cls (F.obj X)) : φ = map F
declarations.comment: uniqueness of `map`

declarations.name: K0_homomorphism_of_homological
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 13.28.4 (tag `0FCR`).** Let `H : D → A` be a homological
functor from a triangulated category to an abelian category, such that for every
object `X` of `D` only finitely many of the objects `H(X[i])`, `i ∈ ℤ`, are
nonzero. Then there is a well-defined group homomorphism `K_0(D) → K_0(A)`
characterized by `[X] ↦ ∑_{i ∈ ℤ} (-1)^i [H(X[i])]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem K0_homomorphism_of_homological (H : D ⥤ A) (hH : H.IsHomological)
    (hfin : ∀ X : D, {i : ℤ | ¬ IsZero (H.obj ((shiftFunctor D i).obj X))}.Finite) :
    ∃ φ : K0 D →+ KZero A, ∀ X : D, φ (K0.cls X) = eulerClass D A H X

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.exists_addEquiv_K0_symm_eq_finsum_of_isWeakSerreClass
declarations.doc:
**The zeroth `K`-group of `D^b_B(A)` is that of `B`, with the inverse given by the Euler
characteristic**: for a weak Serre subcategory `B` of an abelian category `A` there is a group
isomorphism `e` from the zeroth `K`-group of `B` to the zeroth `K`-group of the triangulated
subcategory `D^b_B(A) ⊆ D(A)` of bounded objects with all cohomology objects in `B`, sending the
class `[X]` of an object of `B` to the class `[X[0]]` of `X` viewed as a complex in degree `0`,
and its inverse sends the class `[Y]` of an object of `D^b_B(A)` to the alternating sum
`∑ (-1)ⁱ [Hⁱ(Y)]` of the classes of its cohomology objects, a finite sum because `Y` is bounded.
declarations.statement:
theorem DerivedCategory.exists_addEquiv_K0_symm_eq_finsum_of_isWeakSerreClass
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    (B : ObjectProperty A) [B.IsWeakSerreClass]
    {P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory A)}
    (hP : P = (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := A)).bounded ⊓
      fun X ↦ ∀ n : ℤ, B ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A n).obj X))
    [P.IsTriangulated] :
    ∃ e : KZero B.FullSubcategory ≃+ Pretriangulated.K0 P.FullSubcategory,
      (∀ X : B.FullSubcategory, ∃ Y : P.FullSubcategory,
          Nonempty (P.ι.obj Y ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0).obj (B.ι.obj X))) ∧
        (∀ (X : B.FullSubcategory) (Y : P.FullSubcategory),
          (P.ι.obj Y ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0).obj (B.ι.obj X)) →
