            e (KZero.mk B.FullSubcategory X) =
              QuotientAddGroup.mk (FreeAbelianGroup.of Y)) ∧
        ∀ Y : P.FullSubcategory,
          e.symm (QuotientAddGroup.mk (FreeAbelianGroup.of Y)) =
            ∑ᶠ i : ℤ, (i.negOnePow : ℤ) • KZero.mk B.FullSubcategory
              ⟨(DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A i).obj Y.obj, (hP.le _ Y.property).2 i⟩
declarations.comment: isomorphism `[B] ↦ [B[0]]` with inverse `[X] ↦ ∑ (-1)ⁱ [Hⁱ(X)]`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.K0.exists_bilinear_of_bifunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0FCT (Lemma 13.28.6).**
Let `D`, `D'`, `D''` be triangulated categories and let `F : D ⥤ (D' ⥤ D'')` be a
(curried) bifunctor `⊗ : D × D' → D''`.  Assume that

1. for each object `X` of `D`, the partial functor `X ⊗ - = F.obj X : D' → D''`
   is an exact functor of triangulated categories (it admits a shift-commutation
   structure `csR X` and is triangulated for it), and
2. for each object `X'` of `D'`, the partial functor `- ⊗ X' = F.flip.obj X' : D → D''`
   is an exact functor of triangulated categories (it admits a shift-commutation
   structure `csL X'` and is triangulated for it).

Then `⊗` induces a bilinear map `K_0(D) × K_0(D') → K_0(D'')` sending the pair of
classes `([X], [X'])` to `[X ⊗ X']`.

The bilinear map is encoded as `b : K0 D →+ (K0 D' →+ K0 D'')`: additivity of `b`
in the second variable is built into the `AddMonoidHom` codomain, and additivity
in the first variable is built into `b` itself being an `AddMonoidHom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_bilinear_of_bifunctor
    (F : D ⥤ (D' ⥤ D''))
    (csR : ∀ X : D, (F.obj X).CommShift ℤ)
    (hR : ∀ X : D, letI := csR X; (F.obj X).IsTriangulated)
    (csL : ∀ X' : D', (F.flip.obj X').CommShift ℤ)
    (hL : ∀ X' : D', letI := csL X'; (F.flip.obj X').IsTriangulated) :
    ∃ b : K0 D →+ (K0 D' →+ K0 D''),
      ∀ (X : D) (X' : D'), b (cls X) (cls X') = cls ((F.obj X).obj X')

declarations.name: K0.exists_k0_perfectDerivedCategory_addEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FCU.** Euler characteristic induces an additive equivalence from the zeroth
K-group of the perfect derived category of `R` to the zeroth K-group of finite projective
`R`-modules. On a bounded finite-projective representative it is the alternating sum of the
classes of its terms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem K0.exists_k0_perfectDerivedCategory_addEquiv (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) :=
      (ObjectProperty.singleton
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of R R))).triangEnvelope
    ∃ e : CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.K0 P.FullSubcategory ≃+ K0 R,
      ∀ (K : P.FullSubcategory)
        (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (a b : ℤ),
        Q.IsStrictlyGE a → Q.IsStrictlyLE b →
        (hfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite R (Q.X i)) →
        (hprojective : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Projective R (Q.X i)) →
        Nonempty (K.obj ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q) →
        e (CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.K0.cls K) = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc a b,
          (i.negOnePow : ℤ) • K0.mk
            ({ carrier := Q.X i, finite := hfinite i, projective := hprojective i } : FGProj R)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Smooth.exists_smooth_isLocalization_of_hasProjectiveDimensionLT_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FCW.** Let `A → B` be a flat ring map, essentially of finite type, from a Noetherian
ring to a local ring. If `B` has finite projective dimension over `B ⊗[A] B`, then `B` is the
localization of a smooth `A`-algebra.

The source states this for a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings whose diagonal is
perfect; that form is `StacksDraft.Smooth.exists_smooth_isLocalization_of_isPerfect_diagonal`.
Finite projective dimension of the diagonal gives formal smoothness by
`StacksDraft.Smooth.formallySmooth_of_hasProjectiveDimensionLT_diagonal`, and a formally smooth
local algebra essentially of finite type is a localization of a smooth algebra by
`StacksDraft.Smooth.exists_smooth_isLocalization_of_formallySmooth`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_smooth_isLocalization_of_hasProjectiveDimensionLT_diagonal
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Algebra A B] [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.EssFiniteType A B]
    (hpd : letI := (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' (R := A) (S := B)).toRingHom.toAlgebra
      ∃ n : ℕ, HasProjectiveDimensionLT (ModuleCat.of (TensorProduct A B B) B) n) :
    ∃ (C : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra A C) (_ : Algebra.Smooth A C)
      (M : Submonoid C) (_ : Algebra C B), IsScalarTower A C B ∧ IsLocalization M B

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Smooth.smooth_of_flat_of_hasProjectiveDimensionLT_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FCX.** Let `A → B` be a flat finite type ring map from a Noetherian ring. If `B` has
finite projective dimension over `B ⊗[A] B`, then `B` is a smooth `A`-algebra.

The source assumes that `B` is Noetherian and that the diagonal is perfect; that form is
`StacksDraft.Smooth.smooth_of_flat_of_isPerfect_diagonal`. Smoothness is local on `B`, and at a
prime `𝔮` of `B` over `𝔭` of `A` finite projective dimension of the diagonal passes to the
localized map `A_𝔭 → B_𝔮`, which is then formally smooth by
`StacksDraft.Smooth.formallySmooth_of_hasProjectiveDimensionLT_diagonal`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smooth_of_flat_of_hasProjectiveDimensionLT_diagonal
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    (hpd : letI := (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' (R := A) (S := B)).toRingHom.toAlgebra
      ∃ n : ℕ, HasProjectiveDimensionLT (ModuleCat.of (TensorProduct A B B) B) n) :
    Algebra.Smooth A B

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModuleStatement.coordinates_bundle_points_sections
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FCY].** Let `k` be a field and `V` a `k`-vector space, and let
`𝐏(V) = Proj(Sym_k V)` be the projective space of `V`, with its structure morphism to `Spec k`.
Then:

* if `dim V = n + 1` then `𝐏(V)` is isomorphic to `ℙⁿ_k` as a scheme over `Spec k`;
* `𝐏(V)` is the projective space bundle over `Spec k` of `V` read as a quasi-coherent module on
  `Spec k`, by an isomorphism carrying the bundle projection to the structure morphism;
* the `k`-valued points of `𝐏(V)`, that is the sections of its structure morphism, correspond
  to the one-dimensional quotients of `V`, a point going to the space of vectors whose
  degree-one forms vanish at it;
* for every scheme `X` over `k`, every invertible `𝒪_X`-module `ℒ` and every `k`-linear map
  `ψ : V → Γ(X, ℒ)` whose image generates `ℒ`, the morphism `φ_{ℒ,ψ} : X ⟶ 𝐏(V)` is a morphism
  over `Spec k`, and there is an isomorphism `θ : φ_{ℒ,ψ}^*𝒪_{𝐏(V)}(1) ≅ ℒ` through which each
  `v : V` is sent to `ψ v` by the universal degree-one section of `v`;
* for every basis `v₀, …, vₙ` of `V`, the composite of `φ_{ℒ,ψ}` with the coordinate
  isomorphism `𝐏(V) ≅ ℙⁿ_k` of that basis is the morphism `X ⟶ ℙⁿ_k` of [Stacks, Tag 01ND] for
  the sections `ψ(v₀), …, ψ(vₙ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coordinates_bundle_points_sections :
    (∀ n : ℕ, Module.finrank k V = n + 1 →
        Nonempty ((projectiveSpaceOfModule k V).asOver (Spec (.of k)) ≅
          (projectiveSpaceOverRing n (.of k)).asOver (Spec (.of k)))) ∧
      (∃ e : projectiveSpaceOfModule k V ≅
          Stacks.RelativeProj.projectiveBundle (Spec (.of k)) (tildeOfModule k V),
        e.hom ≫ Stacks.RelativeProj.projectiveBundleToBase (Spec (.of k)) (tildeOfModule k V) =
          projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V) ∧
      (∃ E : {p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ projectiveSpaceOfModule k V //
            p ≫ projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))} ≃
          {K : Submodule k V // Module.finrank k (V ⧸ K) = 1},
        ∀ p v, v ∈ (E p).val ↔
          SymmetricAlgebra.ι k V v ∈ (p.val.base default).asHomogeneousIdeal) ∧
      ∀ {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] (L : X.Modules)
          [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] (ψ : V →ₗ[k] Γ(L, ⊤))
          (hψ : ⨆ v : V, nonvanishingOpen X L (ψ v) = ⊤),
        morphismOfGeneratingSections k V L ψ hψ ≫ projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V =
            X ↘ Spec (.of k) ∧
          (∃ θ : pullbackTwistOne (grading k V) (morphismOfGeneratingSections k V L ψ hψ) ≅ L,
            ∀ v : V, θ.hom.app ⊤ (pullbackSectionOne (grading k V)
              (morphismOfGeneratingSections k V L ψ hψ) (degreeOneElement k V v)) = ψ v) ∧
          ∀ {n : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin (n + 1)) k V),
            morphismOfGeneratingSections k V L ψ hψ ≫
                (basisProjectiveSpaceOfModuleIso b).hom.left =
              Stacks.ProjectiveFromSections.toProjectiveSpaceOver (basisSections b ψ)
                (generatesStalks_basisSections b ψ hψ) (X ↘ Spec (.of k))
declarations.comment: the five assertions of the tag in one statement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_coherent_submodule_extension_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FD0.** Let `F` and `G` be coherent modules on a locally Noetherian
scheme `X`, and let `φ : F|_U ⟶ G|_U` be a morphism over an open subscheme `U`. Then there is a
coherent submodule `F' ⟶ F` agreeing with `F` over `U` and a morphism `φ' : F' ⟶ G` whose
restriction to `U` is `φ` under that agreement.

The submodule is presented as a monomorphism `i : F' ⟶ F` whose restriction to `U` is an
isomorphism `e`; the two equations say that `e` is that restriction and that `φ` is the
restriction of `φ'` read through `e`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coherent_submodule_extension_of_isLocallyNoetherian [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F G : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] [G.IsCoherent] (U : X.Opens)
    (φ : F.restrict U.ι ⟶ G.restrict U.ι) :
    ∃ (F' : X.Modules) (_ : F'.IsCoherent) (i : F' ⟶ F) (_ : Mono i)
      (φ' : F' ⟶ G) (e : F'.restrict U.ι ≅ F.restrict U.ι),
      (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).map i = e.hom ∧
        e.hom ≫ φ = (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).map φ'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_globalSections_iff_geometricallyConnected
declarations.doc:
A proper geometrically reduced scheme over a field has only constant global functions
exactly when it is geometrically connected.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_globalSections_iff_geometricallyConnected
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProper f] [GeometricallyReduced f] :
    IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop) ↔ GeometricallyConnected f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_globalSections_tfae_geometricallyConnected_irreducible_integral
declarations.doc:
For a proper geometrically normal scheme over a field, having only constant global
functions, geometric connectedness, geometric irreducibility, and geometric integrality are
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_globalSections_tfae_geometricallyConnected_irreducible_integral
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProper f] (hnormal : IsGeometricallyNormal f) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop),
      GeometricallyConnected f,
      GeometricallyIrreducible f,
      GeometricallyIntegral f]

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionsVanishingOnSubscheme.exists_bound_generatesOffSupport_and_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FD5].** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a proper scheme over `k`, let `ℒ` be an
ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module and let `Z ⊂ X` be the closed subscheme cut out by a quasi-coherent
sheaf of ideals `I`. Then there is an integer `n₀` such that for every `n ≥ n₀` the kernel `V_n`
of `Γ(X, ℒ ^⊗ n) ⟶ Γ(Z, ℒ ^⊗ n|_Z)` generates `ℒ ^⊗ n` on `X ∖ Z` and the canonical morphism

`X ∖ Z ⟶ 𝐏(V_n)`

of [Stacks, Tag 0FCY] is an immersion of schemes over `k`.

The generation is the hypothesis `h` the existential carries: `GeneratesOffSupport k f I L n` says
that the germs of the members of `V_n` span the stalk of `ℒ ^⊗ n` at every point of `X ∖ Z`, and
it is what makes the canonical morphism exist. That morphism is
`AlgebraicGeometry.toProjectiveSpaceOfModule`, the morphism of [Stacks, Tag 0FCY], applied to the
linear system `V_n` restricted to `X ∖ Z`: that is what
`Stacks.SectionsVanishingOnSubscheme.toProjectiveSpaceOfVanishingSections_eq` proves the morphism
named below to be. The source speaks of *the* canonical morphism, which is basis free, and the
conclusion is asserted for the morphism built in **every** basis of `V_n` — the presentation of
`𝐏(V_n)` as `ℙᴺ_k` that [Stacks, Tag 0FCY] is stated with needs one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_bound_generatesOffSupport_and_isImmersion [IsProper f]
    (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n₀ ≤ n → ∃ h : GeneratesOffSupport k f I L n,
      ∀ (N : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin (N + 1)) k (vanishingSections k f I L n)),
        IsImmersion (toProjectiveSpaceOfVanishingSections k f b h) ∧
        toProjectiveSpaceOfVanishingSections k f b h ≫
            projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k (vanishingSections k f I L n) =
          (openComplement I).ι ≫ f

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.forGeneral_smooth_specializedDivisor_of_isImmersion_canonicalMorphism
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FD6].** In the standing situation of [Stacks, Tag 0G47] — a field `k`, a
scheme `X` over `k`, an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L`, a finite dimensional `k`-vector space `V`
with a basis, and a `k`-linear map `ψ : V → Γ(X, L)` — assume that

1. `X` is smooth over `k`,
2. the image of `ψ` generates `L`,
3. the corresponding morphism `φ_{L,ψ} : X → 𝐏(V)` of [Stacks, Tag 0FCY] is an immersion.

Then for general `v ∈ V ⊗_k k'` the scheme `H_v` is smooth over `k'`: there is a nonempty open
`U ⊂ 𝔸^r_k` such that for every field extension `k'/k` and every `v ∈ V ⊗_k k'` whose coordinate
tuple is a `k'`-point of `U`, the zero scheme `H_v = Z(ψ(v)) ⊂ X_{k'}` is smooth over `k'`.

Hypothesis (1) is the instance `[Smooth D.toBase]`, (2) is `hgen`, and (3) is `himm`, stated on
the basis-free morphism `Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.canonicalMorphism`. The base field is
arbitrary, and `dim V` may be `0`. The proof transports (3) to every basis by
`Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.isImmersive_iff_isImmersion_canonicalMorphism` and applies
`Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.forGeneral_smooth_specializedDivisor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem forGeneral_smooth_specializedDivisor_of_isImmersion_canonicalMorphism [Smooth D.toBase]
    (hgen : D.Generates) (himm : IsImmersion (D.canonicalMorphism hgen)) :
    D.ForGeneral (fun K _ _ w =>
      ∀ a : Fin (Module.finrank D.k D.V) → K,
        w = ∑ i, TensorProduct.tmul D.k (D.basis i) (a i) →
          Smooth ((D.specializedDivisor K a).subschemeι ≫ D.baseChangeToSpec K))
declarations.comment: hypothesis (3) is stated on the canonical morphism phi_(L, psi) : X -> P(V) of Tag 0FCY; arbitrary base field, any dim V

declarations.doc: **[Stacks, Tag 0FD7] at the twisted-graded-module spelling, in degree-zero cohomology.**
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_forall_le_isZero_cohomologyOverField_zero_twistedGradedModuleTwist (k : Type u)
    [Field k] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X L)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hAss : ∀ x : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) → x ∉ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints F) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ n₀ →
      IsZero (cohomologyOverField k f
        (Stacks.Cohomology.TwistedGradedModule.twist X L F n) 0)
declarations.comment: the vanishing at the twisted-graded-module spelling, in degree-zero cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.EnriquesSeveriZariski.exists_forall_le_isZero_cohomologyOverField_one_twistedGradedModuleTwist
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FD8].**  Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a scheme proper over `k`, let `ℒ` be
an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module and let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module.  If the stalk of `ℱ` has
depth at least two at every closed point of `X`, then

`H¹(X, ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℒ^{⊗ m}) = 0`

for all `m ≪ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_forall_le_isZero_cohomologyOverField_one_twistedGradedModuleTwist (k : Type u)
    [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] (L : X.Modules)
    [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X L) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsCoherent]
    (hdepth : ∀ x : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) → (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
      (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x)) :
    ∃ m₀ : ℤ, ∀ m : ℤ, m ≤ m₀ →
      IsZero (AlgebraicGeometry.cohomologyOverField k f
        (Stacks.Cohomology.TwistedGradedModule.twist X L F m) 1)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleSectionConnected.connectedSpace_zeroScheme_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FD9].** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a proper scheme over `k`, let `ℒ` be
an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module and let `s ∈ Γ(X, ℒ)`. If `s` is a regular section
([Stacks, Tag 01WY]), if `depth(𝒪_{X,x}) ≥ 2` for every closed point `x ∈ X`, and if `X` is
connected, then the zero scheme `Z(s)` is connected.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectedSpace_zeroScheme_of_isAmple (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace))
    [inst : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L]
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L) (s : L.sections)
    (hs : Mono (L.unitHomEquiv.symm s))
    (hdepth : ∀ x : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) → (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    [ConnectedSpace X] :
    ConnectedSpace (zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))).subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentToQuasicoherentDerivedMinus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDA.** The canonical functor
`D⁻(Coh(𝒪_X)) ⥤ D⁻_Coh(QCoh(𝒪_X))` on a Noetherian scheme: the derived functor of the
inclusion `Coh(𝒪_X) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_X)`, restricted to the bounded above complexes and corestricted
to the bounded above complexes with coherent cohomology, where it lands.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentToQuasicoherentDerivedMinus_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDA.** On a Noetherian scheme the canonical functor
`D⁻(Coh(𝒪_X)) ⥤ D⁻_Coh(QCoh(𝒪_X))` is an equivalence: the bounded above derived category of
coherent modules is the full subcategory of the bounded above derived category of
quasi-coherent modules whose objects have coherent cohomology.
declarations.statement:
instance coherentToQuasicoherentDerivedMinus_isEquivalence [IsNoetherian X] :
    (coherentToQuasicoherentDerivedMinus X).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentToModulesDerivedMinus_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDB.** On a Noetherian scheme the canonical functor
`D⁻(Coh(𝒪_X)) ⥤ D⁻_Coh(𝒪_X)` is an equivalence: the bounded above derived category of the
coherent `𝒪_X`-modules is the full subcategory of `D(𝒪_X)` of the complexes which are
cohomologically bounded above with coherent cohomology sheaves.
declarations.statement:
instance coherentToModulesDerivedMinus_isEquivalence [IsNoetherian X] :
    (coherentToModulesDerivedMinus X).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: bounded above

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentToModulesDerivedBounded_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDB.** On a Noetherian scheme the canonical functor
`D^b(Coh(𝒪_X)) ⥤ D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)` is an equivalence: the bounded derived category of the coherent
`𝒪_X`-modules is the full subcategory of `D(𝒪_X)` of the complexes which are cohomologically
bounded with coherent cohomology sheaves.
declarations.statement:
instance coherentToModulesDerivedBounded_isEquivalence [IsNoetherian X] :
    (coherentToModulesDerivedBounded X).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: bounded

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectCohomology.isBoundedCoherent_of_isPerfect_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**The converse half of [Stacks, Tag 0FDC].** Let `X` be a regular scheme which is
quasi-compact — equivalently, Noetherian and regular. Then every perfect object of the derived
category of `𝒪_X`-modules lies in `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)`: it is bounded and all of its cohomology
sheaves are coherent.

Regularity enters only through local Noetherianity, so this is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectCohomology.isBoundedCoherent_of_isPerfect`
([Stacks, Tag 0FXU]) read at the hypotheses of [Stacks, Tag 0FDC].
declarations.statement:
theorem isBoundedCoherent_of_isPerfect_of_isRegular
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (hX : IsRegular X) [CompactSpace X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
      (fun M : StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace => M.IsCoherent) K
declarations.comment: converse direction only: a perfect object on a quasi-compact regular scheme is bounded with coherent cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectCohomology.isPerfect_of_isBoundedCoherent_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**The forward half of [Stacks, Tag 0FDC].** Let `X` be a regular scheme. Then every object of
`D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)` — every object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules which is bounded and all
of whose cohomology sheaves are coherent — is perfect.

Quasi-compactness of `X` is not assumed. The proof is an induction on the length of the interval
carrying the cohomology of the object, with
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfect_single_of_isCoherent_of_isRegular` as its base case; that statement
needs no quasi-compactness either.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_isBoundedCoherent_of_isRegular {X : Scheme.{u}} (hX : IsRegular X)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
      (fun M : StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace => M.IsCoherent) K) :
    RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K
declarations.comment: forward direction: a bounded object with coherent cohomology on a regular scheme is perfect

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectCohomology.isPerfect_iff_isBoundedCoherent_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDC].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact regular scheme — equivalently, a
Noetherian regular scheme. Then the perfect objects of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules are
exactly the objects of `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)`.

The forward implication is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectCohomology.isPerfect_of_isBoundedCoherent_of_isRegular`, which
does not use quasi-compactness; the converse is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectCohomology.isBoundedCoherent_of_isPerfect_of_isRegular`, which
does.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_iff_isBoundedCoherent_of_isRegular {X : Scheme.{u}} (hX : IsRegular X)
    [CompactSpace X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)) :
    RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K ↔
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
        (fun M : StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace => M.IsCoherent) K
declarations.comment: the equivalence, on a quasi-compact regular scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_of_isRelativelyAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0FDD.** If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a morphism of schemes, `Y` is quasi-compact,
quasi-separated and has the resolution property, and `L` is an invertible `𝒪_X`-module ample
relative to `f`, then `X` has the resolution property.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_of_isRelativelyAmple {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] [HasResolutionProperty Y]
    (L : X.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L) : HasResolutionProperty X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_addEquiv_coherentKZero_K0
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDF.** The Grothendieck group `K'₀(X)` of coherent sheaves on a scheme
`X` is the zeroth `K`-group of `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`, the bounded objects of `D(𝒪_X)` with coherent
cohomology sheaves, by an isomorphism sending the class of a coherent sheaf to the class of that
sheaf placed in degree `0`; and that property determines it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_addEquiv_coherentKZero_K0 (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)] :
    ∃ e : CoherentKZero X ≃+ Pretriangulated.K0 (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory,
      (∀ F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf,
          ∃ K : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory,
            Nonempty (K.obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) 0).obj F.obj)) ∧
        ∀ (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
          (K : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory),
          (K.obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) 0).obj F.obj) →
            e (KZero.mk _ F) = QuotientAddGroup.mk (FreeAbelianGroup.of K)
declarations.comment: the identification K₀(Coh(𝒪_X)) = K₀(D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)), the source's second equality. The source's middle group K₀(D^b(Coh(𝒪_X))) is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_addEquiv_coherentKZero_K0_bounded`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_addEquiv_coherentKZero_K0_bounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDF.** The Grothendieck group `K'₀(X)` of coherent sheaves on a scheme
`X` is the zeroth `K`-group of `D^b(Coh(𝒪_X))`, the bounded derived category of the abelian
category of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, by an isomorphism sending the class of a coherent sheaf to the
class of that sheaf placed in degree `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_addEquiv_coherentKZero_K0_bounded (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)] :
    ∃ e : CoherentKZero X ≃+ Pretriangulated.K0
        (DerivedCategory.Bounded (Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)),
      ∀ F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf,
        e (KZero.mk _ F) = QuotientAddGroup.mk (FreeAbelianGroup.of
          (⟨(DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
                (Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) 0).obj F,
            ⟨⟨0, inferInstance⟩, ⟨0, inferInstance⟩⟩⟩ :
            DerivedCategory.Bounded (Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)))
declarations.comment: the identification K₀(Coh(𝒪_X)) = K₀(D^b(Coh(𝒪_X))), the source's first equality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_addEquiv_K0_bounded_K0_boundedCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDF.** For a scheme `X` the two outer groups of the chain of Tag 0FDF
agree: the zeroth `K`-group of `D^b(Coh(𝒪_X))`, the bounded derived category of the abelian
category of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, is isomorphic to the zeroth `K`-group of `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`, the
bounded objects of `D(𝒪_X)` whose cohomology sheaves are coherent. The isomorphism matches the
classes of a coherent sheaf placed in degree `0` on the two sides: it carries the class of `F` in
`D^b(Coh(𝒪_X))` to the class of any object of `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)` isomorphic to `F` in degree `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_addEquiv_K0_bounded_K0_boundedCoherent (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d'} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)] :
    ∃ e : Pretriangulated.K0
        (DerivedCategory.Bounded (Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)) ≃+
      Pretriangulated.K0 (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory,
      ∀ (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
        (K : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory),
        (K.obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) 0).obj F.obj) →
          e (QuotientAddGroup.mk (FreeAbelianGroup.of
              (⟨(DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
                    (Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) 0).obj F,
                ⟨⟨0, inferInstance⟩, ⟨0, inferInstance⟩⟩⟩ :
                DerivedCategory.Bounded
                  (Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)))) =
            QuotientAddGroup.mk (FreeAbelianGroup.of K)
declarations.comment: the identification K₀(D^b(Coh(𝒪_X))) = K₀(D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)) of the source's two outer groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.perfectDerivedProperty_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Perfect objects form a triangulated subcategory of `D(O_X)`.** This is the ringed-space
statement `Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectTriangulatedSubcategory.isTriangulated_isPerfect`, read on the
ringed space underlying `X`.
declarations.statement:
instance perfectDerivedProperty_isTriangulated (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (show ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory X.Modules) from
      fun K => IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: (1) D_perf(𝒪_X) is TRIANGULATED in D(𝒪_X) — the adjective of Definition 0FDG (1) that makes `K₀` of the subcategory defined at all, `CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.K0` taking a `[Pretriangulated]` instance. The definitional clause itself is `AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectKZero`

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.perfectDerivedProperty_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms
declarations.doc: **Perfect objects form a strictly full subcategory of `D(O_X)`.**
declarations.statement:
instance perfectDerivedProperty_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms
      (fun K : DerivedCategory X.Modules => IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
declarations.comment: (1) D_perf(𝒪_X) is STRICTLY FULL in D(𝒪_X) — the first of the three adjectives Definition 0FDG (1) attaches to the subcategory whose K-group it names. The definitional clause itself is `AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectKZero`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentModulesAbelian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDG.** Coherent sheaves of modules on a scheme form an abelian
category.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance coherentModulesAbelian (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    Abelian (Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
declarations.comment: coherent_abelian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentKZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDG (2).** The Grothendieck group `K'₀(X)` of coherent sheaves on a
scheme `X`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev CoherentKZero (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type _
declarations.comment: coherent_k0

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.perfectDerivedProperty_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
**`D_perf(𝒪_X)` is a saturated subcategory of `D(𝒪_X)`**: both summands of a perfect
biproduct are perfect. This is Tag 08CS, read on the ringed space underlying `X` at the standard
derived-category universe, fed to
`Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.isSaturated_isPerfect_of_biprod`.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfectDerivedProperty_isSaturated (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (show ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory X.Modules) from
      fun K => IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K).IsSaturated
declarations.comment: (1) D_perf(𝒪_X) is SATURATED in D(𝒪_X) — the third of the three adjectives Definition 0FDG (1) attaches to the subcategory whose K-group it names, and the only one the definition does not consume as an instance. The definitional clause itself is `AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectKZero`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectKZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDG (1).** The *Grothendieck group* `K₀(X)` of a scheme `X`: the
zeroth `K`-group of the strictly full, saturated, triangulated subcategory `D_perf(𝒪_X)` of
`D(𝒪_X)` consisting of the perfect objects.
declarations.statement: abbrev PerfectKZero (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type _
declarations.comment: (1) the DEFINITIONAL clause: K₀(X) := K₀(D_perf(𝒪_X)). Being a definition this states nothing on its own; the three adjectives the source attaches to D_perf(𝒪_X) are the assertional part of (1) and are registered separately, on `perfectDerivedProperty_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms` (strictly full), `perfectDerivedProperty_isTriangulated` (triangulated) and `perfectDerivedProperty_isSaturated` (saturated)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckGroupAffine.affineCoherentKZeroEquiv
declarations.doc:
The coherent Grothendieck group of `Spec R` is canonically isomorphic to
the Grothendieck group of finite `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def affineCoherentKZeroEquiv (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentKZero (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) ≃+ KPrime0 R
declarations.comment: affine_k0_prime

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckGroupAffine.affineCoherentKZeroEquiv_mk
declarations.doc:
The affine comparison sends the class of a coherent sheaf associated to a
finite module to the class of that module.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineCoherentKZeroEquiv_mk (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M : FinModule R)
    (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).ringCatSheaf)
    (hF : Nonempty (F.obj ≅
      AlgebraicGeometry.tilde (ModuleCat.of (CommRingCat.of R) M.carrier))) :
    affineCoherentKZeroEquiv R (KZero.mk _ F) = M.cls
declarations.comment: affine_k0_prime

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckGroupAffine.exists_addEquiv_K0_perfectDerivedCategory_spec
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDH], the clause `K₀(Spec R) = K₀(R)`.** For a commutative ring `R` the
Grothendieck group `K₀(Spec R) = K₀(D_perf(𝒪_{Spec R}))` of the affine scheme `Spec R` is
isomorphic to the Grothendieck group `K₀(R)` of finite projective `R`-modules, by the
isomorphism taking the class of a perfect object `K` of `D(𝒪_{Spec R})` which is isomorphic to
`M̃` to the alternating sum of the classes of the terms of a bounded complex of finite projective
`R`-modules representing `M`.

`perfEquiv` identifies `D_perf(R)` with `D_perf(𝒪_{Spec R})`,
`CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.K0.mapEquiv` turns that into an isomorphism of `K`-groups, and
`K0.exists_k0_perfectDerivedCategory_addEquiv` ([Stacks, Tag 0FCU]) identifies `K₀(D_perf(R))`
with `K₀(R)` by the Euler characteristic, which is where the alternating sum comes from.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_addEquiv_K0_perfectDerivedCategory_spec :
    ∃ e : Pretriangulated.K0 (PerfectDerivedCategory (Spec R)) ≃+ K0 (R : Type u),
      ∀ (K : PerfectDerivedCategory (Spec R)) (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
        (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (R : Type u)) ℤ) (a b : ℤ),
        Q.IsStrictlyGE a → Q.IsStrictlyLE b →
        (hfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite (R : Type u) (Q.X i)) →
        (hprojective : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Projective (R : Type u) (Q.X i)) →
        Nonempty (M ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q) →
        Nonempty (K.obj ≅ (tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategory.obj M) →
        e (Pretriangulated.K0.cls K) = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc a b,
          (i.negOnePow : ℤ) • K0.mk
            ({ carrier := Q.X i, finite := hfinite i, projective := hprojective i } :
              FGProj (R : Type u))
declarations.comment: affine_k0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_addEquiv_K0_coherentKZero_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDI].** Let `X` be a Noetherian regular scheme. Then the canonical map
`K₀(X) ⟶ K'₀(X)` from the Grothendieck group of perfect complexes to the Grothendieck group of
coherent sheaves is an isomorphism.

Every coherent sheaf placed in degree zero is a perfect complex, the comparison map takes the
class of such a complex to the class of the sheaf, and it is the only additive homomorphism
`K₀(X) ⟶ K'₀(X)` which does so.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_addEquiv_K0_coherentKZero_of_isRegular (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (hX : IsRegular X) :
    ∃ e : Pretriangulated.K0 (PerfectDerivedCategory X) ≃+ CoherentKZero X,
      (∀ F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf,
          ∃ K : PerfectDerivedCategory X,
            Nonempty (K.obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F.obj)) ∧
        (∀ (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
            (K : PerfectDerivedCategory X),
            (K.obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F.obj) →
              e (Pretriangulated.K0.cls K) = KZero.mk _ F) ∧
          ∀ φ : Pretriangulated.K0 (PerfectDerivedCategory X) →+ CoherentKZero X,
            (∀ (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
                (K : PerfectDerivedCategory X),
                (K.obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F.obj) →
                  φ (Pretriangulated.K0.cls K) = KZero.mk _ F) → φ = e.toAddMonoidHom

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.bijective_comparisonAddHom_of_hasResolutionProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDJ.**  On a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme with the
resolution property the canonical homomorphism `K₀(Vect(X)) ⟶ K₀(X) = K₀(D_perf(𝒪_X))`, which
sends the class of a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module to the class of that module placed in
degree zero, is an isomorphism: it is bijective, and it is a homomorphism of abelian groups by
construction.

Surjectivity is
`Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.surjective_comparisonAddHom`, which reads off the
class of a bounded complex of finite locally free modules as the alternating sum of the classes
of its terms.  Injectivity is the source's inverse map, the Euler characteristic
`Σᵢ (-1)ⁱ [ℰⁱ]`; it is well defined because two bounded complexes of finite locally free modules
isomorphic in `D(𝒪_X)` are connected by a roof of such complexes ([Stacks, Tag 0F8G]) and because
the Euler characteristic of a bounded acyclic such complex vanishes, the modules of cycles being
finite locally free.

The affine diagonal that both halves need is [Stacks, Tag 0F8C] at these same three conditions,
`AlgebraicGeometry.HasResolutionProperty.isAffineHom_diagonal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_comparisonAddHom_of_hasResolutionProperty (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [HasResolutionProperty X] :
    Function.Bijective (comparisonAddHom X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.surjective_comparisonAddHom_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**The surjectivity half of [Stacks, Tag 0FDJ].** On a Noetherian, quasi-separated scheme with
the resolution property the canonical homomorphism `K₀(Vect(X)) ⟶ K₀(X) = K₀(D_perf(𝒪_X))`, which
sends the class of a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module to the class of that module placed in
degree zero, is surjective.

The scheme has affine diagonal by the Noetherian case of [Stacks, Tag 0F8C],
`AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_diagonal_of_hasResolutionProperty_of_isNoetherian`, so
`Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.exists_boundedFiniteLocallyFree_iso_of_affineDiagonal`
— [Stacks, Tag 0F8F] with the affine diagonal assumed rather than deduced — writes every perfect
object of `D(𝒪_X)` as the image of a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. That is the
hypothesis of `Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.surjective_comparisonAddHom`, which
reads off the class of such a complex as the alternating sum of the classes of its terms.

The whole tag, on a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme with the resolution property and
with the comparison homomorphism an isomorphism, is
`Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.bijective_comparisonAddHom_of_hasResolutionProperty`
of `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Perfect.VectorBundleComparisonBijectiveUnconditional`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_comparisonAddHom_of_isNoetherian (X : Scheme.{u})
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.HasResolutionProperty X] :
    Function.Surjective (comparisonAddHom X)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of `K₀(Vect(X)) ⟶ K₀(X)`, for a Noetherian scheme in place of an arbitrary quasi-compact one: the affine diagonal that the proof needs is deduced from the resolution property by the Noetherian case of Tag 0F8C

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedCategoryBBounded_coherentModules_derivedTensor_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDK.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme. The derived tensor product of a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` with an object of `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)` is an object of `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`: the
derived tensor product produces the bifunctor
`⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} : D_perf(𝒪_X) × D^b_Coh(𝒪_X) ⟶ D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryBBounded_coherentModules_derivedTensor_of_isPerfect
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
    (hL : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) L) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
      (((TorFormula.derivedTensor X).obj K).obj L)
declarations.comment: the bifunctor D_perf × D^b_Coh ⟶ D^b_Coh

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_derivedTensorProduct_module
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDK.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme. The zeroth `K`-group
`K₀(D^b_Coh(𝒪_X))` of the cohomologically bounded objects of `D(𝒪_X)` with coherent cohomology
sheaves carries a module structure over the Grothendieck ring `K₀(D_perf(𝒪_X))` of the perfect
objects for which the scalar multiple of the class of an object of `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)` by the class of
a perfect object is the class of their derived tensor product. In particular that scalar
multiplication is bilinear.

The ring acting is the commutative ring of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_derivedTensorProduct_commRing`
(`perfectTensorStructureScheme_eq`), and the group acted on is `K'₀(X)` by
[Stacks, Tag 0FDF].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedTensorProduct_module :
    letI := (perfectTensorStructureScheme X).commRing
    ∃ m : Module (K0 (perfectAtScheme X).FullSubcategory)
        (K0 (boundedCoherentAtScheme X).FullSubcategory),
      ∀ (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))
        (hK : perfectAtScheme X K) (hL : boundedCoherentAtScheme X L)
        (h : boundedCoherentAtScheme X (((TorFormula.derivedTensor X).obj K).obj L)),
        letI := m
        K0.cls (⟨K, hK⟩ : (perfectAtScheme X).FullSubcategory) •
            K0.cls (⟨L, hL⟩ : (boundedCoherentAtScheme X).FullSubcategory) =
          K0.cls (⟨((TorFormula.derivedTensor X).obj K).obj L, h⟩ :
            (boundedCoherentAtScheme X).FullSubcategory)
declarations.comment: K₀(D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)) is a module over the Grothendieck ring K₀(D_perf(𝒪_X))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_module_coherentKZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDK.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme. The Grothendieck group
`K'₀(X)` of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules is a module over the Grothendieck ring
`K₀(X) = K₀(D_perf(𝒪_X))`: there is a module structure on `K'₀(X)` and an isomorphism of abelian
groups `K'₀(X) ≅ K₀(D^b_Coh(𝒪_X))` which takes the class of a coherent module to the class of
that module placed in degree zero — the isomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 0FDF] — and which carries the
scalar multiple of the class of a coherent sheaf `ℱ` by the class of a perfect object `K` to the
class of their derived tensor product `K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} ℱ[0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_module_coherentKZero :
    letI := (perfectTensorStructureScheme X).commRing
    ∃ (m : Module (K0 (perfectAtScheme X).FullSubcategory) (CoherentKZero X))
      (e : CoherentKZero X ≃+ K0 (boundedCoherentAtScheme X).FullSubcategory),
      (∀ F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf,
          ∃ K : (boundedCoherentAtScheme X).FullSubcategory,
            Nonempty (K.obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) 0).obj F.obj)) ∧
      (∀ (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
          (K : (boundedCoherentAtScheme X).FullSubcategory),
          (K.obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) 0).obj F.obj) →
            e (KZero.mk _ F) = K0.cls K) ∧
      ∀ (K : (perfectAtScheme X).FullSubcategory)
        (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
        (L : (boundedCoherentAtScheme X).FullSubcategory)
        (_ : L.obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) 0).obj F.obj)
        (h : boundedCoherentAtScheme X (((TorFormula.derivedTensor X).obj K.obj).obj L.obj)),
        letI := m
        e (K0.cls K • KZero.mk _ F) =
          K0.cls (⟨((TorFormula.derivedTensor X).obj K.obj).obj L.obj, h⟩ :
            (boundedCoherentAtScheme X).FullSubcategory)
declarations.comment: K'₀(X) is a module over the Grothendieck ring K₀(X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_derivedTensorProduct_commRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDK.** The Grothendieck group `K₀(D_perf(𝒪_X))` of the perfect
objects of `D(𝒪_X)` carries a commutative ring structure whose additive group is the one it
already has, whose product of the classes of two perfect objects is the class of their derived
tensor product, and whose unit is the class of the structure sheaf in degree zero.

The source states this for a scheme; it holds for any ringed space, and for an arbitrary
derived tensor product of `𝒪_X`-modules, which is the generality Tag 09J5 is stated in.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedTensorProduct_commRing :
    ∃ r : CommRing (K0 (ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
        (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect.{u, u, d} (X := X)))),
      r.toAddCommGroup = (inferInstance : AddCommGroup (K0 (ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
        (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect.{u, u, d} (X := X))))) ∧
      (∀ (K L : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
            (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect.{u, u, d} (X := X)))
          (h : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X)
            ((T.tensor.obj K.obj).obj L.obj)),
        r.mul (K0.cls K) (K0.cls L) = K0.cls ⟨(T.tensor.obj K.obj).obj L.obj, h⟩) ∧
      (∀ h : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X)
          ((DerivedCategory.Q (C := Mod X.sheaf)).obj
            ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Mod X.sheaf) 0).obj
              (SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.sheaf)))),
        r.one = K0.cls ⟨_, h⟩)
declarations.comment: perfect_k_ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_comparisonRingHom
declarations.doc:
There is a unique ring homomorphism from the Grothendieck ring of vector bundles on a scheme
`X` to the Grothendieck ring of perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)` which sends the class of a finite
locally free module to the class of that module placed in degree zero.

The ring structure on the target is the one of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_derivedTensorProduct_commRing`, for the given derived
tensor product.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_comparisonRingHom :
    letI := (RingedSpace.perfectTensorStructure X.toRingedSpace T).commRing
    ∃! f : VectorBundleKZero X →+*
        K0 (ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
          (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect.{u, u, d} (X := X.toRingedSpace))),
      ∀ (M : X.Modules) (_ : IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) M)
        (h : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace)
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj M)),
        f (VectorBundleKZero.classOf X M) = K0.cls ⟨_, h⟩
declarations.comment: vector_bundle_comparison_ring_map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundleKZero.exists_tensorProduct_commRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDK.** `K₀(Vect(X))` carries a commutative ring structure whose
additive group is the one it already has, whose multiplication is the tensor product of finite
locally free modules, and whose unit is the class of the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_tensorProduct_commRing (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃ r : CommRing (VectorBundleKZero X),
      r.toAddCommGroup = (inferInstance : AddCommGroup (VectorBundleKZero X)) ∧
        (∀ M N : X.Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) M →
          IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) N →
            r.mul (classOf X M) (classOf X N) =
              classOf X (Scheme.Modules.tensorObjRingedSpace X M N)) ∧
        classOf X (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) = r.one
declarations.comment: vector_bundle_grothendieck_ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperPushforwardKZero.properPushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDL]: proper pushforward on `K'₀`.** For a proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
locally Noetherian schemes, the homomorphism `f_* : K'₀(X) ⟶ K'₀(Y)` of Grothendieck groups of
coherent sheaves determined by `f_*[ℱ] = [⨁_{i ≥ 0} R ²ⁱ f_* ℱ] − [⨁_{i ≥ 0} R ²ⁱ⁺¹ f_* ℱ]`.

Its existence is `KZero.lift` applied to `parityClass_add_of_shortExact`; the coherence of the
two sums, which is what makes the right-hand side a difference of classes in `K'₀(Y)`, is
`isCoherent_parityDirectImageSum`.
declarations.statement:
def properPushforward (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsProper f] :
    CoherentKZero X →+ CoherentKZero Y
declarations.comment: the map f_* : K'₀(X) ⟶ K'₀(Y). All three of the source's reasons for well definedness are proved: coherence of the R ⁱ f_* ℱ (Tag 02O5), local finiteness of the nonzero ones, and the long exact sequence of the R ⁱ f_* with its terms collected by the parity of the degree (`hasParityHexagons`). The remark's quasi-compact restatement f_*[ℱ] = ∑ (-1)ⁱ [R ⁱ f_* ℱ] = [Rf_* ℱ] is `AlgebraicGeometry.ProperPushforwardKZero.properPushforward_mk_eq_finsum` and `AlgebraicGeometry.ProperPushforwardKZero.properPushforward_mk_eq_derivedClass`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperPushforwardKZero.properPushforward_mk
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDL]: the value of `f_*` on the class of a coherent sheaf.** For coherent
`𝒪_Y`-modules `E` and `O` isomorphic to `⨁_{i ≥ 0} R ²ⁱ f_* ℱ` and `⨁_{i ≥ 0} R ²ⁱ⁺¹ f_* ℱ`,

  `f_*[ℱ] = [E] − [O]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_mk (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    [IsProper f]
    (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
    (E O : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf)
    (hE : E.obj ≅ parityDirectImageSum f F.obj 0)
    (hO : O.obj ≅ parityDirectImageSum f F.obj 1) :
    properPushforward f (KZero.mk _ F) = KZero.mk _ E - KZero.mk _ O
declarations.comment: the value f_*[ℱ] = [⨁ R ²ⁱ f_* ℱ] - [⨁ R ²ⁱ⁺¹ f_* ℱ] of f_* on the class of a coherent sheaf, the first assertion of the remark

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperPushforwardKZero.existsUnique_properPushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDL].** For a proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of locally Noetherian schemes there
is exactly one homomorphism `f_* : K'₀(X) ⟶ K'₀(Y)` with

  `f_*[ℱ] = [⨁_{i ≥ 0} R ²ⁱ f_* ℱ] − [⨁_{i ≥ 0} R ²ⁱ⁺¹ f_* ℱ]`

for every coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`, the two sums being read at any coherent `𝒪_Y`-modules
isomorphic to them.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_properPushforward (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsProper f] :
    ∃! φ : CoherentKZero X →+ CoherentKZero Y,
      ∀ (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
        (E O : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf),
        (E.obj ≅ parityDirectImageSum f F.obj 0) →
        (O.obj ≅ parityDirectImageSum f F.obj 1) →
          φ (KZero.mk _ F) = KZero.mk _ E - KZero.mk _ O
declarations.comment: the existence and uniqueness of the map f_* : K'₀(X) ⟶ K'₀(Y) with the value the remark prescribes on the class of a coherent sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperPushforwardKZero.properPushforward_mk_eq_finsum
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDL]: the quasi-compact restatement `f_*[ℱ] = ∑ (−1)ⁱ [R ⁱ f_* ℱ]`.** For a
proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of locally Noetherian schemes with `Y` quasi-compact, the proper
pushforward of the class of a coherent `𝒪_X`-module is the alternating sum of the classes of its
higher direct images; the sum is finite because they vanish in all large degrees.

The value of `f_*` on `[ℱ]` is `[⨁_{i ≥ 0} R ²ⁱ f_* ℱ] − [⨁_{i ≥ 0} R ²ⁱ⁺¹ f_* ℱ]`
(`properPushforward_mk`); each of the two sums has only finitely many nonzero summands by
`exists_isZero_higherDirectImage_of_compactSpace`, so `mk_eq_sum_range_of_iso_sigma` expands its
class as a finite sum, and `alternating_sum_range` recombines the two finite sums by parity.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_mk_eq_finsum (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsProper f] [CompactSpace Y]
    (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) :
    properPushforward f (KZero.mk _ F) =
      ∑ᶠ i : ℕ, ((i : ℤ).negOnePow : ℤ) • KZero.mk _ (coherentHigherDirectImage f F i)
declarations.comment: the quasi-compact restatement f_*[ℱ] = ∑ (-1)ⁱ [R ⁱ f_* ℱ] of the remark

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperPushforwardKZero.properPushforward_mk_eq_derivedClass
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDL]: the quasi-compact restatement `f_*[ℱ] = [Rf_* ℱ]`.** For a proper
morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of locally Noetherian schemes with `Y` quasi-compact and a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`, the total derived direct image `Rf_*(ℱ[0])` is an object of `D^b_Coh(𝒪_Y)`, and
under every identification `K'₀(Y) = K₀(D^b_Coh(𝒪_Y))` which sends the class of a coherent sheaf
to the class of that sheaf placed in degree `0` — the identification of [Stacks, Tag 0FDF] —
the class `f_*[ℱ]` is the class of `Rf_*(ℱ[0])`.

The identity `f_*[ℱ] = ∑ (−1)ⁱ [R ⁱ f_* ℱ]` is `properPushforward_mk_eq_finsum`, and
`∑ (−1)ⁱ [H ⁱ(K)] ↦ [K]` is the inverse of the identification: the homomorphism `φ` of
[Stacks, Tag 0FCR] for the zeroth homology functor takes `[K]` to `∑ (−1)ⁱ [H ⁱ(K)]`, and the
composite of the identification with `φ` is the identity on the classes of coherent sheaves,
hence the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_mk_eq_derivedClass (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsProper f] [CompactSpace Y]
    (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) :
    ∃ E : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory,
      Nonempty (E.obj ≅ (derivedPushforwardModules f).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F.obj)) ∧
        ∀ e : CoherentKZero Y ≃+ Pretriangulated.K0 (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory,
          (∀ (G : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf)
              (D : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
                (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory),
              (D.obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
                (SheafOfModules.{u} Y.ringCatSheaf) 0).obj G.obj) →
                e (KZero.mk _ G) = Pretriangulated.K0.cls D) →
            e (properPushforward f (KZero.mk _ F)) = Pretriangulated.K0.cls E
declarations.comment: the quasi-compact restatement f_*[ℱ] = [Rf_* ℱ] of the remark, under the identification K'₀(Y) = K₀(D^b_Coh(𝒪_Y)) of Tag 0FDF

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperPushforwardKZero.exists_addEquiv_properPushforward_eq_derivedClass
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDL]: the quasi-compact restatement `f_*[ℱ] = [Rf_* ℱ]`**, with the
identification `K'₀(Y) = K₀(D^b_Coh(𝒪_Y))` of [Stacks, Tag 0FDF] exhibited.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_addEquiv_properPushforward_eq_derivedClass (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsProper f] [CompactSpace Y] :
    ∃ e : CoherentKZero Y ≃+ Pretriangulated.K0 (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory,
      (∀ (G : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf)
          (D : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory),
          (D.obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} Y.ringCatSheaf) 0).obj G.obj) →
            e (KZero.mk _ G) = Pretriangulated.K0.cls D) ∧
        ∀ F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf,
          ∃ E : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory,
            Nonempty (E.obj ≅ (derivedPushforwardModules f).obj
                ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F.obj)) ∧
              e (properPushforward f (KZero.mk _ F)) = Pretriangulated.K0.cls E
declarations.comment: the quasi-compact restatement f_*[ℱ] = [Rf_* ℱ] of the remark, with the identification K'₀(Y) = K₀(D^b_Coh(𝒪_Y)) of Tag 0FDF exhibited

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.properPushforward_perfectCoherentSMul_perfectPullbackKZero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDM]: the projection formula on `K`-groups.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper
morphism of locally Noetherian schemes. Then

  `f_*(α · f^*β) = f_*α · β`

for `α ∈ K'₀(X)` and `β ∈ K₀(Y)`. Here `f_* : K'₀(X) ⟶ K'₀(Y)` is the proper pushforward of
[Stacks, Tag 0FDL] (`AlgebraicGeometry.ProperPushforwardKZero.properPushforward`),
`f^* : K₀(Y) ⟶ K₀(X)` is induced by the derived pullback of perfect objects
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.perfectPullbackKZero`), and `K₀(X) × K'₀(X) ⟶ K'₀(X)` is the
product of [Stacks, Tag 0FDK] given by the derived tensor product
(`AlgebraicGeometry.ParityEulerClass.perfectCoherentSMul`); on a Noetherian scheme that product is
the scalar multiplication of the module structure of
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_module_coherentKZero`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.ParityEulerClass.perfectCoherentSMul_eq_smul`).

Both sides are biadditive, so it suffices to treat `α = [ℱ]` and `β = [P]`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.ParityEulerClass.properPushforward_perfectCoherentSMul_cls_mk`: the derived
projection formula `Rf_*(ℱ ⊗^𝐋 Lf^*P) ≅ Rf_*ℱ ⊗^𝐋 P` of [Stacks, Tag 08EU], here at a perfect
object `P` where it is [Stacks, Tag 0B54], read through the identification `f_*[ℱ] = [Rf_*ℱ]` of
Remark 0FDL and the definition of the product in Remark 0FDK.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_perfectCoherentSMul_perfectPullbackKZero {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsProper f]
    (α : CoherentKZero X) (β : PerfectKZero Y) :
    ProperPushforwardKZero.properPushforward f
        (perfectCoherentSMul X (RingedSpace.perfectPullbackKZero f.toLRSHom.toShHom β) α) =
      perfectCoherentSMul Y β (ProperPushforwardKZero.properPushforward f α)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectDerivedCategory
declarations.doc:
The strictly full subcategory of perfect derived objects whose every cohomology sheaf
is set-theoretically supported on a closed subscheme.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev supportedPerfectDerivedCategory {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u} X.toRingedSpace)]
declarations.comment: supported_perfect_definition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_supportedPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Supported perfect objects form a strictly full subcategory.** Perfectness only depends on
the isomorphism class, and an isomorphism of derived objects induces an isomorphism of each
cohomology sheaf, which has no effect on its support.
declarations.statement:
instance isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_supportedPerfect {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)] :
    ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms
      (show ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)) from
        fun K => RingedSpace.IsPerfect K ∧
          ∀ n : ℤ, SheafOfModules.supp
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace) n).obj K) ⊆
              Set.range i.base)
declarations.comment: strict fullness of the supported perfect subcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isTriangulated_supportedPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Perfect complexes supported on a closed subscheme form a triangulated subcategory** of the
derived category of `O_X`-modules: the subcategory `D_{Z, perf}(O_X)` contains a zero object, is
stable under all shifts, and the middle object of a distinguished triangle whose other two
objects are perfect and supported on `Z` is again perfect and supported on `Z`.

Saturation, the remaining adjective of the source, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isSaturated_supportedPerfect`; its perfect half is Tag 08CS.
declarations.statement:
instance isTriangulated_supportedPerfect {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)] :
    ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated
      (show ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)) from
        fun K => RingedSpace.IsPerfect K ∧
          ∀ n : ℤ, SheafOfModules.supp
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace) n).obj K) ⊆
              Set.range i.base)
declarations.comment: triangulatedness of the supported perfect subcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_supportedPerfect_not_exists_unit
declarations.doc:
**In general `K₀(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X))` has no unit.** There are a scheme `X` and a closed
subscheme `Z` for which `K₀(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X))` carries a multiplication — a non-unital
commutative ring structure on its additive group whose product of two classes is the class of
the derived tensor product — and no multiplication of that kind has a unit. Here `X = Spec ℤ` and
`Z = Spec(ℤ/2)`; the general statement is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SupportedPerfectNoUnit.not_exists_unit`, for `V(f)` in the spectrum of any
Noetherian domain of dimension at most one and any nonzero nonunit `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_supportedPerfect_not_exists_unit :
    ∃ (X Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (_ : IsClosedImmersion i),
      (∃ r : NonUnitalCommRing (K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i)),
        r.toAddCommGroup = (inferInstance : AddCommGroup (K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i))) ∧
          ∀ K L : supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i,
            r.mul (K0.cls K) (K0.cls L) = K0.cls (supportedPerfectTensorObj i K L)) ∧
      ∀ r : NonUnitalCommRing (K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i)),
        r.toAddCommGroup = (inferInstance : AddCommGroup (K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i))) →
          (∀ K L : supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i,
            r.mul (K0.cls K) (K0.cls L) = K0.cls (supportedPerfectTensorObj i K L)) →
          ¬ ∃ e, ∀ a, r.mul e a = a
declarations.comment: in general `K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X))` has no unit: for `X = Spec ℤ` and `Z = Spec(ℤ/2)` the multiplication given by the derived tensor product exists, and no multiplication on `K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X))` distributive over its addition and computing the derived tensor product on classes has a unit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_supportedPerfect_nonUnitalCommRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FDN.** The `K`-group `K₀(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X))` of the perfect objects
of `D(𝒪_X)` supported on a closed subscheme `Z` carries a non-unital commutative ring
structure: its additive group is the one `K₀` already has, and the product of the classes of
two objects is the class of their derived tensor product. Associativity,
commutativity and distributivity are the fields of `NonUnitalCommRing`; no unit is asserted,
and none exists in general: `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_supportedPerfect_not_exists_unit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_supportedPerfect_nonUnitalCommRing :
    ∃ r : NonUnitalCommRing (K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i)),
      r.toAddCommGroup = (inferInstance : AddCommGroup (K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i))) ∧
        ∀ K L : supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i,
          r.mul (K0.cls K) (K0.cls L) = K0.cls (supportedPerfectTensorObj i K L)
declarations.comment: the multiplication on `K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X))` given by the derived tensor product, together with its associativity and commutativity -- the fields of `NonUnitalCommRing`. Stated at the standard derived-category model, which the source does not fix. The absence of a unit in general is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_supportedPerfect_not_exists_unit`; the definition of the subcategory and its three adjectives are in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfect/KGroups/Basic.lean` and `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfect/KGroups/Saturation.lean`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSaturated_supportedPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Perfect complexes supported on a closed subscheme form a saturated subcategory** of
`D(O_X)`: if a binary biproduct is perfect with all its cohomology sheaves supported on `Z`,
then so is each of its two summands.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_supportedPerfect` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isTriangulated_supportedPerfect` this gives all three adjectives the source
attaches to `D_{Z, perf}(O_X)`: strictly full, saturated, triangulated.
declarations.statement:
instance isSaturated_supportedPerfect {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)] :
    ObjectProperty.IsSaturated
      (show ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)) from
        fun K => RingedSpace.IsPerfect K ∧
          ∀ n : ℤ, SheafOfModules.supp
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace) n).obj K) ⊆
              Set.range i.base)
declarations.comment: saturation of the supported perfect subcategory -- the adjective `saturated` of the source, which is closure under direct summands (Tag 05RB). The two other adjectives, strict fullness and triangulatedness, and the definition of the subcategory itself, are in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfect/KGroups/Basic.lean`. The multiplication on `K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X))` is in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfect/KGroups/Ring.lean` and the absence of a unit in general in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfect/KGroups/NoUnit.lean`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_tfae_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FDP.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of finite type between locally Noetherian
schemes and let `Δ : X ⟶ X ×_Y X` be its diagonal. The following are equivalent:

1. `f` is smooth;
2. `f` is flat and `Δ` is a regular immersion;
3. `f` is flat and `Δ` is a local complete intersection morphism;
4. `f` is flat and `Δ` is perfect.

A smooth morphism is flat and its diagonal is a section of the smooth first projection, hence a
regular immersion by Stacks 067R; a regular immersion is a local complete intersection morphism
by Stacks 069L; such a morphism is perfect by Stacks 069H; and the interesting implication back
to smoothness is `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_flat_of_perfect_diagonal`, which runs Stacks 0FCX
on affine charts.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_tfae_diagonal {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    List.TFAE
      [Smooth f,
        Flat f ∧ Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.IsRegularImmersion
          (pullback.diagonal f),
        Flat f ∧ IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism (pullback.diagonal f),
        Flat f ∧ Perfect (pullback.diagonal f)]

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.finitePushforwardCoherent
declarations.doc:
Direct image along a finite morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme, as a functor on coherent
modules.
declarations.comment: the functor `π_* : Coh(X) ⥤ Coh(Y)`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.shortExact_map_finitePushforwardCoherent
declarations.doc:
Direct image along a finite morphism carries a short exact sequence of coherent modules to a
short exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_map_finitePushforwardCoherent
    ⦃S : ShortComplex (Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)⦄
    (hS : S.ShortExact) : (S.map (finitePushforwardCoherent π)).ShortExact
declarations.comment: `π_*` is an exact functor on coherent sheaves

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.finitePushforwardCoherentHom
declarations.doc:
The homomorphism `K₀(Coh(X)) → K₀(Coh(Y))` induced by direct image along a finite
morphism.
declarations.comment: the induced homomorphism `K₀(Coh(X)) → K₀(Coh(Y))`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.coherentModulesDimLE_finitePushforward
declarations.doc:
The direct image along a finite morphism of a coherent module whose support has
delta-dimension at most `k` again has support of delta-dimension at most `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentModulesDimLE_finitePushforward (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite π]
    (hπ : π ≫ sY = sX) (k : ℤ)
    (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
    (hF : coherentModulesDimLE C sX k F) :
    have : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sY
    coherentModulesDimLE C sY k ((finitePushforwardCoherent π).obj F)
declarations.comment: `π_*` sends `Coh_{≤k}(X)` into `Coh_{≤k}(Y)`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.finitePushforwardDimLE
declarations.doc:
The restriction of `π_*` to the coherent modules whose support has delta-dimension at most
`k`.
declarations.statement:
def finitePushforwardDimLE (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite π] (hπ : π ≫ sY = sX)
    (k : ℤ) : CoherentModulesDimLE C sX k ⥤ CoherentModulesDimLE C sY k
declarations.comment: the functor `π_* : Coh_{≤k}(X) ⥤ Coh_{≤k}(Y)`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.shortExact_map_finitePushforwardDimLE
declarations.doc:
Direct image along a finite morphism carries a short exact sequence of coherent modules of
support dimension at most `k` to a short exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_map_finitePushforwardDimLE (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite π]
    (hπ : π ≫ sY = sX) (k : ℤ) ⦃S : ShortComplex (CoherentModulesDimLE C sX k)⦄
    (hS : S.ShortExact) : (S.map (finitePushforwardDimLE C sX sY π hπ k)).ShortExact
declarations.comment: `π_*` is exact on `Coh_{≤k}`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.finitePushforwardDimLEHom
declarations.doc:
The homomorphism `K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(Y))` induced by direct image along a finite
morphism.
declarations.statement:
def finitePushforwardDimLEHom (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite π] (hπ : π ≫ sY = sX)
    (k : ℤ) :
    GrothendieckGroup (CoherentModulesDimLE C sX k) →+
      GrothendieckGroup (CoherentModulesDimLE C sY k)
declarations.comment: the induced homomorphism `K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(Y))`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom
declarations.doc:
The homomorphism `K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(Y)/Coh_{≤k-1}(Y))` induced by
direct image along a finite morphism.
declarations.statement:
def dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite π]
    (hπ : π ≫ sY = sX) (k : ℤ) :
    GrothendieckGroup (coherentDimensionQuotient C sX (k - 1) k) →+
      GrothendieckGroup (coherentDimensionQuotient C sY (k - 1) k)
declarations.comment: the induced homomorphism `K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X)) → K₀(Coh_{≤k}(Y)/Coh_{≤k-1}(Y))`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom_of
declarations.doc:
The homomorphism on the Grothendieck groups of the layers sends the class of the image of a
module `F` of `Coh_{≤k}(X)` to the class of the image of `π_* F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom_of (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite π]
    (hπ : π ≫ sY = sX) (k : ℤ) (F : CoherentModulesDimLE C sX k) :
    dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k
        (GrothendieckGroup.of ((lowerDimensionClass C sX (k - 1) k).isoModSerre.Q.obj F)) =
      GrothendieckGroup.of ((lowerDimensionClass C sY (k - 1) k).isoModSerre.Q.obj
        ((finitePushforwardDimLE C sX sY π hπ k).obj F))
declarations.comment: the induced homomorphism on a layer sends `[F]` to `[π_* F]`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardHom_comp_dimensionLayerCycleHom
declarations.doc:
The cycle class homomorphism `K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1}) ⟶ Z_k` commutes with direct image
along a finite morphism on the source and proper pushforward of `k`-cycles on the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforwardHom_comp_dimensionLayerCycleHom (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite π]
    (hπ : π ≫ sY = sX) (k : ℤ) :
    (properPushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k).comp (dimensionLayerCycleHom C sX k) =
      (dimensionLayerCycleHom C sY k).comp
        (dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k)
declarations.comment: commutativity of the right-hand square of the diagram

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom_comp_cycleDimensionLayerHom
declarations.doc:
For `Y` Noetherian, the homomorphism `Z_k ⟶ K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1})` commutes with proper
pushforward of `k`-cycles on the source and direct image along the finite morphism `π` on the
target.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom_comp_cycleDimensionLayerHom (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite π] [IsNoetherian Y] (hπ : π ≫ sY = sX) (k : ℤ) :
    (dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k).comp (cycleDimensionLayerHom C sX k) =
      (cycleDimensionLayerHom C sY k).comp (properPushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k)
declarations.comment: commutativity of the left-hand square of the diagram, for `Y` Noetherian

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom_cycleDimensionLayerHom
declarations.doc:
For `Y` Noetherian, the element of the Grothendieck group of the layer over `Y` attached to
the proper pushforward of a `k`-cycle `c` on `X` is the direct image along `π` of the element
attached to `c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom_cycleDimensionLayerHom (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]
    (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite π] [IsNoetherian Y] (hπ : π ≫ sY = sX) (k : ℤ)
    (c : CycleGroup C sX k) :
    dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k (cycleDimensionLayerHom C sX k c) =
      cycleDimensionLayerHom C sY k (properPushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k c)
declarations.comment: the left-hand square of the diagram on a cycle, for `Y` Noetherian

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleDimensionLayerHom_comp_properPushforwardHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FDR**, the left-hand square of the diagram. The homomorphism
`Z_k ⟶ K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1})` of Stacks 02S9 commutes with proper pushforward of `k`-cycles on
the source and direct image along the finite morphism `π` on the target.

As in the source, it follows from the right-hand square
`Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardHom_comp_dimensionLayerCycleHom` because the two maps of Tag 02S9
are mutually inverse, over `X` and over `Y`, each being merely locally of finite type over the
base.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleDimensionLayerHom_comp_properPushforwardHom :
    (cycleDimensionLayerHom C sY k).comp (properPushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k) =
      (dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k).comp
        (cycleDimensionLayerHom C sX k)
declarations.comment: commutativity of the left-hand square of the diagram

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleDimensionLayerHom_properPushforwardHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FDR**, the left-hand square read on a cycle. The element of the Grothendieck group
of the layer over `Y` attached to the proper pushforward of a `k`-cycle `c` on `X` is the direct
image along `π` of the element attached to `c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleDimensionLayerHom_properPushforwardHom (c : CycleGroup C sX k) :
    cycleDimensionLayerHom C sY k (properPushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k c) =
      dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k (cycleDimensionLayerHom C sX k c)
declarations.comment: the left-hand square of the diagram on a cycle

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.finitePushforward_dimensionLayer_diagram_commutes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FDR**, the diagram. The maps of Stacks 02S9,
`Z_k ⟶ K₀(Coh_{≤k}/Coh_{≤k-1}) ⟶ Z_k`, over `X` and over `Y`, together with proper pushforward
of `k`-cycles on the two outer columns and direct image along `π` on the middle column, form a
commutative diagram: both the left-hand and the right-hand square commute.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePushforward_dimensionLayer_diagram_commutes :
    (cycleDimensionLayerHom C sY k).comp (properPushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k) =
        (dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k).comp
          (cycleDimensionLayerHom C sX k) ∧
      (properPushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k).comp (dimensionLayerCycleHom C sX k) =
        (dimensionLayerCycleHom C sY k).comp
          (dimensionLayerFinitePushforwardHom C sX sY π hπ k)
declarations.comment: the maps of Tag 02S9 fit into a commutative diagram with `π_*`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowToWideDimensionLayerHom
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-compact scheme `X` locally of finite type over the base scheme of a Chow situation
there is a canonical homomorphism
`CH_k(X) ⟶ K₀(Coh_{≤k+1}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` sending the class of a `k`-cycle `∑ n_Z[Z]` to the
class of `[⨁_{n_Z > 0} 𝒪_Z^{⊕n_Z}] − [⨁_{n_Z < 0} 𝒪_Z^{⊕-n_Z}]` in the wide dimension layer.
declarations.comment: for a quasi-compact `X`; the cycle identity is formalized in the orientation `[𝒪_X/fI]_k − [𝒪_X/I]_k = div(f)`, correcting the sign-inverted chain of the source

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowToWideLayerHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FDS.** For a scheme `X` locally of finite type over the base of a Chow situation
there is a canonical homomorphism `CH_k(X) ⟶ K₀(Coh_{≤k+1}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` induced by the map
`Z_k(X) ⟶ K₀(Coh_{≤k}(X)/Coh_{≤k-1}(X))` of Tag 02S9: it sends the class of a `k`-cycle `c` to
the image of the class of `c` under the map widening the layer, see
`Stacks.Chow.chowToWideLayerHom_mk`.
declarations.statement:
