def chowToWideLayerHom (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (k : ℤ) : chowGroup C sX k →+ coherentDimensionKZero C sX (k - 1) (k + 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentToSupportedCoherentKZeroHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDT], the comparison homomorphism of K-groups.** Let `X` be a locally
Noetherian scheme and `Z ⊂ X` a closed subscheme. The exact inclusion functor
`Coh(𝒪_Z) ⥤ Coh_Z(X)` induces a homomorphism `K'_0(Z) = K_0(Coh(𝒪_Z)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X))` taking
the class of a coherent `𝒪_Z`-module to the class of its direct image.
declarations.comment: the exact fully faithful inclusion functor Coh(Z) → Coh_Z(X) and the homomorphism K'_0(Z) = K_0(Coh(Z)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X)) that it induces. That this homomorphism is an isomorphism is NOT covered: the source inverts it by sending a coherent module F supported on Z to the class of the graded module of its I-adic filtration. The graded pieces of that filtration are available, as the short exact sequence with the coherence and support bound of Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealAdicFiltration; what is missing is a comparison between the support and coherence predicates used there and those defining SupportedCoherentModules, and the local finiteness of the filtration over a merely locally Noetherian scheme, the available finiteness input being quasi-compact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentToSupportedCoherentKZeroHom_mk
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDT].** The comparison homomorphism `K_0(Coh(𝒪_Z)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X))` takes
the class of a coherent `𝒪_Z`-module `ℱ` to the class of its direct image `i_*ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentToSupportedCoherentKZeroHom_mk
    (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules Z.ringCatSheaf) :
    coherentToSupportedCoherentKZeroHom i (KZero.mk _ F) =
      KZero.mk _ ((coherentToSupportedCoherent i).obj F)
declarations.comment: the defining property of the comparison homomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentToSupportedCoherentKZeroHom_bijective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FDT].** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme and `Z ⊂ X` a closed
subscheme. The homomorphism `K'_0(Z) = K_0(Coh(𝒪_Z)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X))` induced by the exact
inclusion functor `Coh(𝒪_Z) ⥤ Coh_Z(X)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentToSupportedCoherentKZeroHom_bijective :
    Function.Bijective (coherentToSupportedCoherentKZeroHom i)
declarations.comment: the homomorphism K'_0(Z) = K_0(Coh(Z)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X)) induced by the exact inclusion functor is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GeneralizedBivariantClass
declarations.doc:
A generalized bivariant class of degree `p` for a diagram `X --x--> Z <--y-- Y` of schemes
locally of finite type over the base: a rule assigning to every morphism `z' : Z' ⟶ Z` locally of
finite type and every `k` an additive map `A_k(Z' ×_Z Y) ⟶ A_{k-p}(X ×_Z Z')`, natural for proper
pushforward, for flat pullback of fixed relative dimension, and for the Gysin map of the zero
scheme of a section of an invertible module on the test scheme, the Gysin maps being those of the
`Stacks.Chow.GysinSystem` `G`. The group of all of them is denoted `A^p(X ⟶ Z ⟵ Y)`.
declarations.statement:
structure GeneralizedBivariantClass (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (G : GysinSystem C)
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (sZ : Z ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sZ] (x : X ⟶ Z)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType x] (y : Y ⟶ Z) [LocallyOfFiniteType y] (hx : x ≫ sZ = sX)
    (hy : y ≫ sZ = sY) (p : ℤ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardGeneralizedBivariantClass
declarations.doc:
For a proper morphism `f : X₂ ⟶ X₁` of schemes locally of finite type over the base, proper
pushforward is a generalized bivariant class of degree `0` for the diagram
`X₁ --id--> X₁ <--f-- X₂`:

  `f_* ∈ A^0(X₁ ⟶ X₁ ⟵ X₂)`.

On a test scheme `z' : Z' ⟶ X₁` its cap operation is proper pushforward
`A_k(Z' ×_{X₁} X₂) ⟶ A_k(X₁ ×_{X₁} Z')` along the base change of `f`
(`Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardGeneralizedBivariantClass_cap`). It is formed at the Gysin system of
the first Chern class rule, `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`.
declarations.comment: the example of the remark: for a proper f : X₂ ⟶ X₁, f_* ∈ A^0(X₁ ⟶ X₁ ⟵ X₂), at the canonical Gysin system gysinSystemOfInvertible, with NOTHING ASSUMED

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardGeneralizedBivariantClass_cap
declarations.doc:
The cap operation of `f_* ∈ A^0(X₁ ⟶ X₁ ⟵ X₂)` on a test scheme `z' : Z' ⟶ X₁` is proper
pushforward along the base change `Z' ×_{X₁} X₂ ⟶ X₁ ×_{X₁} Z'` of `f`, read in degree `k - 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforwardGeneralizedBivariantClass_cap {Z' : Scheme.{u}} (z' : Z' ⟶ X₁)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType z'] (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C (pullback.snd z' f ≫ s₂) k) :
    (properPushforwardGeneralizedBivariantClass C s₁ s₂ f hf).cap z' k α =
      chowGroupDegreeEquiv C (pullback.fst (𝟙 X₁) z' ≫ s₁) (sub_zero k).symm
        (properChowPushforward C (pullback.snd z' f ≫ s₂) (pullback.fst (𝟙 X₁) z' ≫ s₁)
          (generalizedProperPushforwardMap f z')
          (generalizedProperPushforwardMap_comp_structure C s₁ s₂ f hf z') k
          (properPushforwardDescends C _ _ _ _ _) α)
declarations.comment: the class f_* ∈ A^0(X₁ ⟶ X₁ ⟵ X₂) caps by proper pushforward along the base change of f

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassBivariantCanonical
declarations.doc:
The first Chern class `c₁(ℒ) ∈ A^1(X)` of an invertible module `ℒ` on a scheme `X` locally of
finite type over the base, as a bivariant class of degree `1` for `𝟙 X` at the canonical Gysin
system.
declarations.statement:
def firstChernClassBivariantCanonical :
    BivariantClass C (canonicalGysinSystem C) sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX) 1

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassProduct_eq_zero_of_topologicalKrullDim_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FDX.** Let `X` be a scheme of finite type over the base scheme `S` of chapter 42
which has an ample invertible module `A`, and let `dim X ≤ d`. Then for invertible
`𝒪_X`-modules `ℒ_1, …, ℒ_{d+1}` on `X`

  `c₁(ℒ_1) ∘ ⋯ ∘ c₁(ℒ_{d+1}) = 0`   in `A^{d+1}(X)`,

the product being the composition of Stacks 0B75 of the bivariant first Chern classes of
Stacks 0B77, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassProduct_eq_zero_of_topologicalKrullDim_le [QuasiCompact sX]
    (A : X.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X A] (hA : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X A)
    (d : ℕ) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (L : Fin (d + 1) → X.Modules)
    [∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property (L i)] :
    firstChernClassProduct C sX d L = 0
declarations.comment: X of finite type over the base of Situation 02QL with an ample invertible module and dim X ≤ d; the product c₁(ℒ_1) ∘ ⋯ ∘ c₁(ℒ_{d+1}) of the bivariant first Chern classes (Stacks 0B77, composed by Stacks 0B75) is zero in A^{d+1}(X), by the source's induction on d

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantPieceAssemblyCap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FDZ.** The cap operation assembled from a family `(c_i)` of bivariant classes of
degree `p` for the restrictions `f_i : X_i ⟶ Y_{a(i)}`: on a test scheme `g : T ⟶ Y` it sends
`α ∈ A_k(T)` to the unique class in `A_{k-p}(X ×_Y T)` whose restriction to the `i`-th piece
`X_i ×_{Y_{a(i)}} T_{a(i)}` is `c_i ∩ α|_{T_{a(i)}}`.

It is well defined because the Chow groups of `X ×_Y T` decompose along those pieces, by
`Stacks.Chow.chowGroupPullbackPieceEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantPieceAssemblyCap
    (c : ∀ i, BivariantClass C G ((UX i).ι ≫ sX) ((UY (a i)).ι ≫ sY)
      (pieceMap f UX UY a ha i)
      (pieceMap_comp_pieceStructureMorphism C sX sY f hf UX UY a ha i) p)
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ) :
    chowGroup C (g ≫ sY) k →+ chowGroup C (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX) (k - p)
declarations.comment: the cap operation assembled from a family of bivariant classes on the pieces

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantPieceRestrictionOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FDZ.** The restriction `c_i` of a bivariant class `c` of degree `p` for `f : X ⟶ Y`
to the piece `f_i : X_i ⟶ Y_{a(i)}` of a disjoint union decomposition, at the Gysin system of the
first Chern class rule of an invertible module.

This is `Stacks.Chow.bivariantPieceRestriction` with its Gysin compatibility discharged by
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion`, so it assumes nothing.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantPieceRestrictionOfInvertible (i : I)
    (c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf p) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) ((UX i).ι ≫ sX) ((UY (a i)).ι ≫ sY)
      (pieceMap f UX UY a ha i)
      (pieceMap_comp_structureMorphism C sX sY f hf UX UY a ha i) p
declarations.comment: the restriction of a bivariant class to a piece, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with the open-immersion case of Stacks 02TA discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantPieceRestrictionHomOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FDZ.** The map `A^p(X ⟶ Y) ⟶ ∏_{i ∈ I} A^p(X_i ⟶ Y_{a(i)})` of the tag at the Gysin
system of the first Chern class rule of an invertible module, with no Gysin compatibility
assumed.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantPieceRestrictionHomOfInvertible :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf p →+
      ∀ i, BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) ((UX i).ι ≫ sX) ((UY (a i)).ι ≫ sY)
        (pieceMap f UX UY a ha i)
        (pieceMap_comp_structureMorphism C sX sY f hf UX UY a ha i) p
declarations.comment: the map from A^p(X ⟶ Y) to the product over the pieces, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with the open-immersion case of Stacks 02TA discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantPieceEquivOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FDZ.** `A^p(X ⟶ Y) = ∏_{i ∈ I} A^p(X_i ⟶ Y_{a(i)})` at the Gysin system of the
first Chern class rule of an invertible module: a bivariant class of degree `p` for `f : X ⟶ Y`
is the same thing as a family of bivariant classes of degree `p` for the restrictions
`f_i : X_i ⟶ Y_{a(i)}`.

This is `Stacks.Chow.bivariantPieceEquiv` with all three of its Gysin compatibilities discharged,
by `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion`,
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpensRestriction` and
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderPullbackComp`. Nothing remains assumed: the
Gysin system itself carries no hypothesis either.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantPieceEquivOfInvertible (hX : IsClopenDecomposition UX) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf p ≃+
      ∀ i, BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) ((UX i).ι ≫ sX) ((UY (a i)).ι ≫ sY)
        (pieceMap f UX UY a ha i)
        (pieceMap_comp_pieceStructureMorphism C sX sY f hf UX UY a ha i) p
declarations.comment: A^p(X ⟶ Y) = ∏_i A^p(X_i ⟶ Y_{a(i)}) at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with all three Gysin compatibilities discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantPieceRestrictionCap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FDZ.** The cap operation `c_i ∩ -` of the restriction of a bivariant class `c` of
degree `p` for `f : X ⟶ Y` to the piece `f_i : X_i ⟶ Y_{a(i)}`: on a test scheme
`g : T ⟶ Y_{a(i)}` it is the cap operation of `c` at `g ≫ (Y_{a(i)} ⟶ Y)`, restricted along the
open immersion `X_i ×_{Y_{a(i)}} T ⟶ X ×_Y T`.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantPieceRestrictionCap (c : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p) {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : T ⟶ (UY (a i) : Scheme.{u})) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ) :
    chowGroup C (g ≫ ((UY (a i)).ι ≫ sY)) k →+
      chowGroup C (pullback.fst (pieceMap f UX UY a ha i) g ≫ ((UX i).ι ≫ sX)) (k - p)
declarations.comment: the cap operation of the restriction of a bivariant class to a piece

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass.eq_of_clopenRestrict_cap_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FDZ, injectivity.** Two bivariant classes of degree `p` for `f : X ⟶ Y` are equal as
soon as, for every test scheme `g : T ⟶ Y` and every `k`, their cap operations agree after
restriction to each piece `X_i ×_Y T` of `X ×_Y T`.

The pieces of `X ×_Y T` are the preimages of the pieces of `X` under the projection, a
decomposition into open and closed subschemes by
`Stacks.Chow.IsClopenDecomposition.preimage`, so restriction to them is jointly injective on
`CH_{k-p}(X ×_Y T)` by `Stacks.Chow.chowGroupClopenEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
theorem BivariantClass.eq_of_clopenRestrict_cap_eq {c d : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p}
    (h : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
      (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ sY) k) (i : I),
      chowGroupRestrict C (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX)
          ((pullback.fst f g ⁻¹ᵁ UX i).ι ≫ (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX))
          (pullback.fst f g ⁻¹ᵁ UX i).ι rfl (k - p) (c.cap g k α) =
        chowGroupRestrict C (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX)
          ((pullback.fst f g ⁻¹ᵁ UX i).ι ≫ (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX))
          (pullback.fst f g ⁻¹ᵁ UX i).ι rfl (k - p) (d.cap g k α)) :
    c = d
declarations.comment: injectivity: a bivariant class is determined by its restrictions to the pieces

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isBivariantClassComposition_bivariantCompositeOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The composite class at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule is *the* composite: on
every test scheme its cap operation is cap with `b` followed by cap with `a`, pushed forward along
the associativity isomorphism of pullbacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBivariantClassComposition_bivariantCompositeOfInvertible
    (a : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf p)
    (b : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sY sZ g hg q) :
    IsBivariantClassComposition C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY sZ f g hf hg
      (properPushforwardDescends C) p q a b
      (bivariantCompositeOfInvertible C sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a b)
declarations.comment: the composite class satisfies the composition formula, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with both cases of Stacks 02TA discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE0.** The completed bivariant group `A^*(X ⟶ Y)^∧` of a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
schemes locally of finite type over the base: the product, over the connected components `X_i`
of `X`, of the graded groups `A^*(X_i ⟶ Y_{a(i)})` of bivariant classes for the restriction of
`f` to `X_i` and the connected component of `Y` it lands in. The degree support is finite on
each component but need not be bounded across components.
declarations.comment: completed_bivariant_group

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedIdentityClass
declarations.doc:
The unit `1 ∈ A^*(X)^∧` of the completed bivariant cohomology ring: on the connected
component `X_i` of `X` it is the restriction of `1 ∈ A^0(X)` to `X_i`, placed in degree `0`. By
`Stacks.Chow.completedIdentityClass_apply_heq` that restriction is `1 ∈ A^0(X_i)`.
declarations.statement: def completedIdentityClass : completedChowCohomology C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX
declarations.comment: the unit 1 of the completed bivariant cohomology ring A^*(X)^∧

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantSubgroupOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE0.** The subgroup of `∏_p A^p(X ⟶ Y)` the tag describes — the tuples
`c = (c_0, c_1, c_2, …)` such that for every connected component `X_i` of `X` the image of `c_p`
in `A^p(X_i ⟶ Y_{a(i)})` vanishes for almost all `p` — at the Gysin system of the first Chern
class rule of an invertible module.

This is `Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantSubgroup` with the Gysin compatibility it carries
discharged, by `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion`. Nothing remains
assumed: the Gysin system itself carries no hypothesis either.
declarations.statement:
abbrev completedBivariantSubgroupOfInvertible :
    AddSubgroup (∀ p : ℤ, BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf p)
declarations.comment: the almost-vanishing tuples inside the product of the bivariant groups, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with the Gysin compatibility discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.range_completedBivariantSequenceOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE0.** The image of `A^*(X ⟶ Y)^∧` in `∏_p A^p(X ⟶ Y)` is exactly the subgroup of
tuples that vanish in almost all degrees on each connected component, at the Gysin system of the
first Chern class rule of an invertible module.

This is `Stacks.Chow.range_completedBivariantSequence` with the three Gysin compatibilities of
Stacks 0FDZ discharged, by `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion`,
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpensRestriction` and
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderPullbackComp`. Nothing remains assumed: the
Gysin system itself carries no hypothesis either.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_completedBivariantSequenceOfInvertible :
    (completedBivariantSequenceOfInvertible C sX sY f hf).range =
      completedBivariantSubgroupOfInvertible C sX sY f hf
declarations.comment: the image of the completed group is the almost-vanishing tuples, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with all three Gysin compatibilities discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantGroupEquivOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE0.** The completed bivariant group is the group of almost-vanishing tuples in
`∏_p A^p(X ⟶ Y)`, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule of an invertible module.

This is `Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantGroupEquiv` with the three Gysin compatibilities of Stacks
0FDZ discharged, by `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion`,
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpensRestriction` and
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderPullbackComp`. Nothing remains assumed: the
Gysin system itself carries no hypothesis either.
declarations.statement:
def completedBivariantGroupEquivOfInvertible :
    completedBivariantGroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf ≃+
      completedBivariantSubgroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderOpenImmersion C)
declarations.comment: the completed group is the group of almost-vanishing tuples, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with all three Gysin compatibilities discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE0.** The composition
`A^*(X ⟶ Y)^∧ × A^*(Y ⟶ Z)^∧ ⟶ A^*(X ⟶ Z)^∧` extending the composition of Stacks 0B75 to the
completions, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule of an invertible module.

This is `Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantComposite` with both Gysin compatibilities of Stacks 0B75
discharged, by `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso` and
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderPullbackCompPushforward`. Nothing remains
assumed: the Gysin system itself carries no hypothesis either.
declarations.statement:
def completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible
    (c : completedBivariantGroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf)
    (d : completedBivariantGroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sY sZ g hg) :
    completedBivariantGroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sZ (f ≫ g)
      (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hf hg)
declarations.comment: the composition extended to the completed bivariant groups, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with both Gysin compatibilities discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible_of_of
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE0.** The composition on the completions extends the composition of Stacks 0B75,
with nothing assumed: at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, if `c` is concentrated in
degree `p` on the component `X_i` and `d` is concentrated in degree `q` on the component
`Y_{a(i)}`, then the composite is concentrated in degree `p + q` on `X_i` and is there the
composite bivariant class `Stacks.Chow.bivariantCompositeOfInvertible` of Stacks 0B75.
declarations.statement:
theorem completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible_of_of
    (c : completedBivariantGroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf)
    (d : completedBivariantGroup C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sY sZ g hg)
    (i : ConnectedComponents X) (p q : ℤ) (hc : c i = DirectSum.of _ p (c i p))
    (hd : d (f.continuous.connectedComponentsMap i) =
      DirectSum.of _ q (d (f.continuous.connectedComponentsMap i) q)) :
    completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible C sX sY sZ f g hf hg c d i =
      DirectSum.of _ (p + q)
        (completedBivariantCompositeTransport C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY sZ f g hf hg
          i (p + q)
          (bivariantCompositeOfInvertible C _ _ _ _ _ _ _ p q (c i p)
            (d (f.continuous.connectedComponentsMap i) q)))
declarations.comment: the composition on the completions extends the composition of homogeneous classes, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with both Gysin compatibilities discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedChowCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE0.** The *completed bivariant cohomology ring* `A^*(X)^∧ = A^*(X ⟶ X)^∧` of a
scheme `X` locally of finite type over the base: the completed bivariant group of the identity
of `X`. Its multiplication is `Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantComposite` at `f = g = 𝟙 X`, and
`Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantGroupEquiv` reads it as the group of tuples in `∏_p A^p(X)` that
vanish in almost all degrees on each connected component of `X`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev completedChowCohomology (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (G : GysinSystem C) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the completed bivariant cohomology ring A^*(X)^∧ of a scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chernClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE1, the `i`-th Chern class.** For `0 ≤ i ≤ r`, the `i`-th Chern class
`c_i(ℰ) ∈ A^i(X)` of a module `ℰ` that is finite locally free of rank `r`: it *is* the bivariant
class of degree `i` for `𝟙 X` constructed in Stacks 0B7H, namely the rule assigning to
`f : X' ⟶ X` the operation `c_i(f^*ℰ) ∩ - : CH_k(X') ⟶ CH_{k-i}(X')`.
declarations.statement:
def chernClass (i : Fin (r + 1)) :
    BivariantClass C G sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX) (i : ℤ)
declarations.comment: c_i(E) is the degree-i bivariant class of Stacks 0B7H

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.totalChernClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE1, the total Chern class.** The total Chern class
`c(ℰ) = c_0(ℰ) + c_1(ℰ) + ⋯ + c_r(ℰ)` of a module `ℰ` that is finite locally free of rank `r`:
the formal sum of the `r + 1` Chern classes of Stacks 0B7H, viewed as a nonhomogeneous bivariant
class on `X`, that is, as an element of `A^*(X ⟶ X) = ⊕_p A^p(X ⟶ X)`.
declarations.statement: def totalChernClass : nonhomogeneousBivariantGroup C G sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX)
declarations.comment: c(E) = c_0(E) + ... + c_r(E) is the formal sum of the c_i(E)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.canonicalChernClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE1, the `i`-th Chern class.** For a module `ℰ` that is finite locally free of rank
`r` on `X` and `0 ≤ i ≤ r`, the `i`-th Chern class `c_i(ℰ) ∈ A^i(X)`: the bivariant class of
degree `i` for `𝟙 X` constructed in Stacks 0B7H, which assigns to `f : X' ⟶ X` the operation
`c_i(f^*ℰ) ∩ - : A_k(X') ⟶ A_{k-i}(X')` of Stacks 02U6. It lives in the group of Stacks 0B76 at
the canonical Gysin system, and every naturality fact the construction needs is proved.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalChernClass (i : Fin (r + 1)) :
    CanonicalBivariantClass C sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX) (i : ℤ)
declarations.comment: c_i(E) ∈ A^i(X), the degree-i bivariant class of Stacks 0B7H, with the genuine cap products of Stacks 02U6 and the canonical Gysin system; nothing assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.canonicalTotalChernClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE1, the total Chern class.** For a module `ℰ` that is finite locally free of rank
`r` on `X`, the total Chern class `c(ℰ) = c_0(ℰ) + c_1(ℰ) + ⋯ + c_r(ℰ)`: the formal sum of the
`r + 1` Chern classes of Stacks 0B7H, viewed as a nonhomogeneous bivariant class on `X`, that is,
as an element of `A^*(X ⟶ X) = ⊕_p A^p(X ⟶ X)` at the canonical Gysin system. Nothing is
assumed.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalTotalChernClass :
    nonhomogeneousBivariantGroup C (canonicalGysinSystem C) sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX)
declarations.comment: c(E) = c_0(E) + ... + c_r(E), the formal sum of the c_i(E) as a nonhomogeneous bivariant class on X, with the genuine cap products and the canonical Gysin system; nothing assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.IsLocallyEquidimensional.of_isCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE3.** The relative dimension function of a Cohen--Macaulay scheme locally of
finite type over the base of a Chow situation is locally equidimensional: at each point, all
irreducible components through it have the same relative dimension at their generic points.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyEquidimensional.of_isCohenMacaulay (B : ChowSituation.{u}) (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ B.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hX : IsCohenMacaulay X) :
    IsLocallyEquidimensional (relativeDimension B.dimensionFunction f)
declarations.comment: cohen_macaulay_case

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.HasDimensionDecomposition.of_isCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE3.** A Cohen--Macaulay scheme locally of finite type over the base of a Chow
situation decomposes into open and closed subschemes of constant relative dimension.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasDimensionDecomposition.of_isCohenMacaulay (B : ChowSituation.{u}) (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ B.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hX : IsCohenMacaulay X) :
    HasDimensionDecomposition (relativeDimension B.dimensionFunction f)
declarations.comment: cohen_macaulay_case

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.IsLocallyPureDimensional.of_isCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE3.** The relative dimension function of a Cohen--Macaulay scheme locally of
finite type over the base of a Chow situation is locally pure dimensional.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyPureDimensional.of_isCohenMacaulay (B : ChowSituation.{u}) (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ B.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hX : IsCohenMacaulay X) :
    IsLocallyPureDimensional (relativeDimension B.dimensionFunction f)
declarations.comment: cohen_macaulay_case

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.locallyEquidimensional_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE3.** For an integer-valued function on a locally Noetherian scheme, having a
decomposition into pure-dimensional open and closed subschemes, being locally pure dimensional,
and being locally equidimensional are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyEquidimensional_tfae (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (δ : X → ℤ) :
    List.TFAE [
      HasDimensionDecomposition δ,
      IsLocallyPureDimensional δ,
      IsLocallyEquidimensional δ]
declarations.comment: equivalent_conditions

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.HasDimensionDecomposition.of_isNormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE3.** A locally Noetherian normal scheme decomposes into open and closed
subschemes on whose irreducible components any given integer-valued function is constant at the
generic points, the constant being the index of the piece.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasDimensionDecomposition.of_isNormal (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [IsNormal X] (δ : X → ℤ) : HasDimensionDecomposition δ
declarations.comment: normal_case

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.IsLocallyPureDimensional.of_isNormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE3.** On a locally Noetherian normal scheme every integer-valued function is
locally pure dimensional.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyPureDimensional.of_isNormal (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [IsNormal X] (δ : X → ℤ) : IsLocallyPureDimensional δ
declarations.comment: normal_case

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.IsLocallyEquidimensional.of_isNormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE3.** On a locally Noetherian normal scheme every integer-valued function is
locally equidimensional.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyEquidimensional.of_isNormal (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [IsNormal X] (δ : X → ℤ) : IsLocallyEquidimensional δ
declarations.comment: normal_case

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.fundamentalClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE4.** The fundamental class `[X] = ∑_n [X_n]_n` of a scheme whose relative
dimension function has a dimension decomposition: the family whose `n`th coordinate is the class
in `CH_n(X_n)` of the cycle associated to the piece `X_n` itself.
declarations.statement:
def fundamentalClass (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (h : HasDimensionDecomposition (relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f)) :
    degreeZeroChowGroup C f h
declarations.comment: fundamental_class

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.closedCoverPowerSum_derivedTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE5 for `P'_p`.** Let `X = X₁ ∪ X₂ = X₁' ∪ X₂'` be two closed
covers and let `E`, `E' ∈ D(𝒪_X)` be perfect objects whose Chern classes are defined and which
restrict to zero on `X₁` and `X₁'`. Write `χ_p = P'_p(E|_{X₂})` and
`χ'_p = P'_p(E'|_{X₂'})` for the classes of Stacks 0F9H. Let `Y ⊆ X` be the reduced closed
subscheme with underlying set `X₁ ∪ X₁'` (`Stacks.Chow.reducedUnionIdeal`); then
`X = Y ∪ (X₂ ∩ X₂')`, and `E ⊗^L E'` restricts to zero on `Y ∩ (X₂ ∩ X₂')`, so the class of
Stacks 0F9H of `(E ⊗^L E')|_{X₂ ∩ X₂'}` along `X = Y ∪ (X₂ ∩ X₂')` is defined; by Stacks 0FAH
it does not depend on the choice of `Y`. Then

  `P'_p((E ⊗^L E')|_{X₂ ∩ X₂'}) = ∑_{p₁ + p₂ = p} C(p, p₁) χ_{p₁} χ'_{p₂}`

in `A^p(X₂ ∩ X₂' ⟶ X)`, with the product of `Stacks.Chow.supportedIntersectionMul`, each summand
read in degree `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedCoverPowerSum_derivedTensor (perfectE : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} E)
    (perfectE' : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} E') (p : ℕ) :
    closedCoverPowerSum C sX (reducedUnionIdeal i₁ j₁).subschemeι (pullback.snd i₂ j₂ ≫ j₂) _ rfl
        ((hasDefinedChernClasses_derivedTensor hE hE').derivedPullback _) p
        (range_union_range_reducedUnionIdeal i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ hcover hcover')
        (isZero_derivedPullback_derivedTensor_reducedUnion i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ hzero hzero' perfectE
          perfectE') =
      ∑ q ∈ (antidiagonal p).attach, (p.choose q.1.1 : ℤ) •
        bivariantClassDegreeCongr C _ _ sX _ rfl
          (by have := mem_antidiagonal.1 q.2; omega)
          (supportedIntersectionMul C sX i₂ j₂ (IsPullback.of_hasPullback i₂ j₂) _ rfl
            (closedCoverPowerSumRestrict C sX i₁ i₂ hcover hE hzero q.1.1)
            (closedCoverPowerSumRestrict C sX j₁ j₂ hcover' hE' hzero' q.1.2))
declarations.comment: the formula P'_p((E tensor^L E')|_(X_2 cap X'_2)) = sum over p_1 + p_2 = p of C(p, p_1) chi_(p_1) chi'_(p_2) in A^p(X_2 cap X'_2 -> X), for every p >= 0, with E, E' perfect with defined Chern classes as in the source. The closed cover of X on which the left hand side is the class of 0F9H is X = Y cup (X_2 cap X'_2) with Y the reduced closed subscheme on |X_1| cup |X'_1| (reducedUnionIdeal); the vanishing of (E tensor^L E')|_(Y cap X_2 cap X'_2) that 0F9H needs is proved (isZero_derivedPullback_derivedTensor_reducedUnion, by derived Nakayama on the derived fibres), for E, E' perfect as in the source. The source's Y = (X_1 cap X'_1) cup (X_1 cap X'_2) cup (X_2 cap X'_1) has the same underlying set; by 0FAH the class does not depend on the choice. The product of a class on X_2 and a class on X'_2 is supportedIntersectionMul, res(c_1) o c_2 for the restriction of 0F9Z and the composition of 0B75

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.closedCoverChernClass_derivedTensor_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE5 for `c'_1`.** Let `X = X₁ ∪ X₂ = X₁' ∪ X₂'` be two closed
covers and let `E`, `E' ∈ D(𝒪_X)` be perfect objects whose Chern classes are defined and which
restrict to zero on `X₁` and `X₁'`. Write `r = P'_0(E|_{X₂})`,
`r' = P'_0(E'|_{X₂'})`, `γ_1 = c'_1(E|_{X₂})` and `γ'_1 = c'_1(E'|_{X₂'})` for the classes of
Stacks 0F9H. Let `Y ⊆ X` be the reduced closed subscheme with
underlying set `X₁ ∪ X₁'` (`Stacks.Chow.reducedUnionIdeal`); then `X = Y ∪ (X₂ ∩ X₂')`, and
`E ⊗^L E'` restricts to zero on `Y ∩ (X₂ ∩ X₂')`, so the class of Stacks 0F9H of
`(E ⊗^L E')|_{X₂ ∩ X₂'}` along `X = Y ∪ (X₂ ∩ X₂')` is defined; by Stacks 0FAH it does not
depend on the choice of `Y`. Then

  `c'_1((E ⊗^L E')|_{X₂ ∩ X₂'}) = r γ'_1 + r' γ_1`

in `A^1(X₂ ∩ X₂' ⟶ X)`, with the product of `Stacks.Chow.supportedIntersectionMul` (for `r' γ_1`
along the pullback square with the two factors exchanged), each summand read in degree `1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedCoverChernClass_derivedTensor_one (perfectE : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} E)
    (perfectE' : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} E') :
    closedCoverChernClassOfIsZero C sX (reducedUnionIdeal i₁ j₁).subschemeι
        (pullback.snd i₂ j₂ ≫ j₂) _ rfl
        ((hasDefinedChernClasses_derivedTensor hE hE').derivedPullback _)
        (range_union_range_reducedUnionIdeal i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ hcover hcover')
        (isZero_derivedPullback_derivedTensor_reducedUnion i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ hzero hzero' perfectE
          perfectE') 1 one_pos =
      bivariantClassDegreeCongr C _ _ sX _ rfl (by norm_num)
          (supportedIntersectionMul C sX i₂ j₂ (IsPullback.of_hasPullback i₂ j₂) _ rfl
            (closedCoverPowerSumRestrict C sX i₁ i₂ hcover hE hzero 0)
            (closedCoverChernClassRestrict C sX j₁ j₂ hcover' hE' hzero' 1 one_pos)) +
        bivariantClassDegreeCongr C _ _ sX _ rfl (by norm_num)
          (supportedIntersectionMul C sX j₂ i₂ (IsPullback.of_hasPullback i₂ j₂).flip _
            pullback.condition
            (closedCoverPowerSumRestrict C sX j₁ j₂ hcover' hE' hzero' 0)
            (closedCoverChernClassRestrict C sX i₁ i₂ hcover hE hzero 1 one_pos))
declarations.comment: the formula c'_1((E tensor^L E')|_(X_2 cap X'_2)) = r gamma'_1 + r' gamma_1 in A^1(X_2 cap X'_2 -> X), with E, E' perfect with defined Chern classes as in the source. The closed cover of X on which the left hand side is the class of 0F9H is X = Y cup (X_2 cap X'_2) with Y the reduced closed subscheme on |X_1| cup |X'_1| (reducedUnionIdeal); the vanishing of (E tensor^L E')|_(Y cap X_2 cap X'_2) that 0F9H needs is proved (isZero_derivedPullback_derivedTensor_reducedUnion, by derived Nakayama on the derived fibres), for E, E' perfect as in the source. The source's Y = (X_1 cap X'_1) cup (X_1 cap X'_2) cup (X_2 cap X'_1) has the same underlying set; by 0FAH the class does not depend on the choice. Products are supportedIntersectionMul, res(c_1) o c_2, landing in the class group of X_2 x_X X'_2 -> X for both orders of the factors

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.closedCoverChernClass_derivedTensor_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FE5 for `c'_2`.** Let `X = X₁ ∪ X₂ = X₁' ∪ X₂'` be two closed
covers and let `E`, `E' ∈ D(𝒪_X)` be perfect objects whose Chern classes are defined and which
restrict to zero on `X₁` and `X₁'`. Write `r = P'_0(E|_{X₂})`,
`r' = P'_0(E'|_{X₂'})`, `γ_p = c'_p(E|_{X₂})` and `γ'_p = c'_p(E'|_{X₂'})` for the classes of
Stacks 0F9H, and `C(r, 2)`, `C(r', 2)` for the classes `Stacks.Chow.closedCoverRankChoose`. Let
`Y ⊆ X` be the reduced closed subscheme with underlying set `X₁ ∪ X₁'`
(`Stacks.Chow.reducedUnionIdeal`); then `X = Y ∪ (X₂ ∩ X₂')`, and `E ⊗^L E'` restricts to zero
on `Y ∩ (X₂ ∩ X₂')`, so the class of Stacks 0F9H of `(E ⊗^L E')|_{X₂ ∩ X₂'}` along
`X = Y ∪ (X₂ ∩ X₂')` is defined; by Stacks 0FAH it does not depend on the choice of `Y`. Then

  `c'_2((E ⊗^L E')|_{X₂ ∩ X₂'}) =
    r γ'_2 + r' γ_2 + C(r, 2) (γ'_1)² + ((r r') (γ'_1 γ_1) - γ'_1 γ_1) + C(r', 2) γ_1²`

in `A^2(X₂ ∩ X₂' ⟶ X)`. The products of a class on `X₂` and a class on `X₂'` are those of
`Stacks.Chow.supportedIntersectionMul`, the squares `(γ'_1)²`, `γ_1²` and the product of `r r'`
with `γ'_1 γ_1` are the third multiplication of Stacks 0FA0 (`Stacks.Chow.supportedMul`), and each
summand is read in degree `2`.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedCoverChernClass_derivedTensor_two (perfectE : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} E)
    (perfectE' : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} E') :
    closedCoverChernClassOfIsZero C sX (reducedUnionIdeal i₁ j₁).subschemeι
        (pullback.snd i₂ j₂ ≫ j₂) _ rfl
        ((hasDefinedChernClasses_derivedTensor hE hE').derivedPullback _)
        (range_union_range_reducedUnionIdeal i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ hcover hcover')
        (isZero_derivedPullback_derivedTensor_reducedUnion i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ hzero hzero' perfectE
          perfectE') 2 two_pos =
      (bivariantClassDegreeCongr C _ _ sX _ rfl (by norm_num)
          (supportedIntersectionMul C sX i₂ j₂ (IsPullback.of_hasPullback i₂ j₂) _ rfl
            (closedCoverPowerSumRestrict C sX i₁ i₂ hcover hE hzero 0)
            (closedCoverChernClassRestrict C sX j₁ j₂ hcover' hE' hzero' 2 two_pos)) +
        bivariantClassDegreeCongr C _ _ sX _ rfl (by norm_num)
          (supportedIntersectionMul C sX j₂ i₂ (IsPullback.of_hasPullback i₂ j₂).flip _
            pullback.condition
            (closedCoverPowerSumRestrict C sX j₁ j₂ hcover' hE' hzero' 0)
            (closedCoverChernClassRestrict C sX i₁ i₂ hcover hE hzero 2 two_pos)) +
        bivariantClassDegreeCongr C _ _ sX _ rfl (by norm_num)
          (supportedIntersectionMul C sX i₂ j₂ (IsPullback.of_hasPullback i₂ j₂) _ rfl
            (closedCoverRankChoose C sX i₁ i₂ perfectE hcover hzero 2 two_pos)
            (supportedMul C (j₂ ≫ sX) sX j₂ rfl
              (closedCoverChernClassRestrict C sX j₁ j₂ hcover' hE' hzero' 1 one_pos)
              (closedCoverChernClassRestrict C sX j₁ j₂ hcover' hE' hzero' 1 one_pos))) +
        (bivariantClassDegreeCongr C _ _ sX _ rfl (by norm_num)
            (supportedMul C ((pullback.snd i₂ j₂ ≫ j₂) ≫ sX) sX (pullback.snd i₂ j₂ ≫ j₂) rfl
              (supportedIntersectionMul C sX i₂ j₂ (IsPullback.of_hasPullback i₂ j₂) _ rfl
                (closedCoverPowerSumRestrict C sX i₁ i₂ hcover hE hzero 0)
                (closedCoverPowerSumRestrict C sX j₁ j₂ hcover' hE' hzero' 0))
              (supportedIntersectionMul C sX j₂ i₂ (IsPullback.of_hasPullback i₂ j₂).flip _
                pullback.condition
                (closedCoverChernClassRestrict C sX j₁ j₂ hcover' hE' hzero' 1 one_pos)
                (closedCoverChernClassRestrict C sX i₁ i₂ hcover hE hzero 1 one_pos))) -
          bivariantClassDegreeCongr C _ _ sX _ rfl (by norm_num)
            (supportedIntersectionMul C sX j₂ i₂ (IsPullback.of_hasPullback i₂ j₂).flip _
              pullback.condition
              (closedCoverChernClassRestrict C sX j₁ j₂ hcover' hE' hzero' 1 one_pos)
              (closedCoverChernClassRestrict C sX i₁ i₂ hcover hE hzero 1 one_pos))) +
        bivariantClassDegreeCongr C _ _ sX _ rfl (by norm_num)
          (supportedIntersectionMul C sX j₂ i₂ (IsPullback.of_hasPullback i₂ j₂).flip _
            pullback.condition
            (closedCoverRankChoose C sX j₁ j₂ perfectE' hcover' hzero' 2 two_pos)
            (supportedMul C (i₂ ≫ sX) sX i₂ rfl
              (closedCoverChernClassRestrict C sX i₁ i₂ hcover hE hzero 1 one_pos)
              (closedCoverChernClassRestrict C sX i₁ i₂ hcover hE hzero 1 one_pos))))
declarations.comment: the formula for c'_2((E tensor^L E')|_(X_2 cap X'_2)) in A^2(X_2 cap X'_2 -> X), with E, E' perfect with defined Chern classes as in the source. The closed cover of X on which the left hand side is the class of 0F9H is X = Y cup (X_2 cap X'_2) with Y the reduced closed subscheme on |X_1| cup |X'_1| (reducedUnionIdeal); the vanishing of (E tensor^L E')|_(Y cap X_2 cap X'_2) that 0F9H needs is proved (isZero_derivedPullback_derivedTensor_reducedUnion, by derived Nakayama on the derived fibres), for E, E' perfect as in the source. The source's Y = (X_1 cap X'_1) cup (X_1 cap X'_2) cup (X_2 cap X'_1) has the same underlying set; by 0FAH the class does not depend on the choice. C(r, 2) is read as closedCoverRankChoose: the 0F9H extension of the restriction to X_2 of the class ofLocallyConstant of x |-> C(chi_E(x), 2), chi_E the derived-fibre Euler characteristic whose class is r(E) = P_0(E), exactly as 0FAG reads C(r(E), 2); it vanishes on X_1 because chi_E does, and C(r, 1) = r. The term (r r' - 1) gamma'_1 gamma_1 is read as (r r')(gamma'_1 gamma_1) - gamma'_1 gamma_1, since 1 is not a class supported on X_2 cap X'_2; products of classes supported on X_2 and X'_2 are supportedIntersectionMul, products of classes on one support are supportedMul (0FA0). The source's 'and so on for higher Chern classes' is not a precise assertion and is not formalized

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.supportedComposite_modificationChernClass
declarations.doc:
**Composites of the classes `c'`.** Let `b : W ⟶ 𝐏¹_X` be proper and an isomorphism over
`𝐀¹_X`, and for every index `i` let `Z_i ⊆ X` and `T_i ⊆ W_∞` be closed, `Q_i ∈ D(𝒪_W)` perfect
with defined Chern classes and `p_i ≥ 0`, such that the hypotheses of Stacks 0F9K hold for
`b, Z_i, Q_i, T_i, p_i` (`T_i` contains every point of `W_∞` over `X ∖ Z_i` and `Q_i|_{T_i}` is
finite locally free of rank `< p_i` in degree `0`), `Q_i|_{W ∖ W_i}` is finite locally free of rank
`< p_i` in degree `0` for `W_i = b^{-1}(𝐏¹_{Z_i}) = W ×_X Z_i`, and `Q_i` satisfies condition (3)
of Situation 0GUJ. Then for every sequence of indices `i_1, …, i_n` (`n ≥ 1`; the list
`L = [i_n, …, i_2]` and the first index `i_1`)

  `c'_{p_{i_n}}(Q_{i_n}) ∘ ⋯ ∘ c'_{p_{i_1}}(Q_{i_1}) =
    (W_{i_n,∞} ∩ ⋯ ∩ W_{i_1,∞} ⟶ Z_{i_n} ∩ ⋯ ∩ Z_{i_1})_* ∘
      c'_{p_{i_n}}(Q_{i_n}|_{W_{i_n,∞}}) ∘ ⋯ ∘ c'_{p_{i_1}}(Q_{i_1}|_{W_{i_1,∞}}) ∘ C`

in `A^{p_{i_n} + ⋯ + p_{i_1}}(Z_{i_n} ∩ ⋯ ∩ Z_{i_1} ⟶ X)`. Here `c'_p(Q)` is the class of
Stacks 0F9K (`Stacks.Chow.modificationChernClass`), `c'_p(Q|_{W_{i,∞}})` that of Stacks 0F9H
(`Stacks.Chow.modificationInfinityChernClass`), `C` the class of Stacks 0F9J, the composites are
the products of classes supported on closed subschemes of Stacks 0FE5
(`Stacks.Chow.supportedComposite`, `Stacks.Chow.modificationInfinityComposite`), and the right
side is `Stacks.Chow.modificationLocalization`.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedComposite_modificationChernClass
    (hrank : ∀ i, ∃ M : (T i).Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M (p i) ∧
      Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        (t i ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity f b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj (Q i) ≅
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M))
    (hperf : ∀ i, Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := W.toRingedSpace) (Q i))
    (hres : ∀ i, ∃ M : OXMod.{u, u, u} (W.toRingedSpace.restrict
          (modificationComplementOpens b (z i)).isOpenEmbedding),
        IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M (p i) ∧
          Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
            (W.toRingedSpace.ofRestrict (modificationComplementOpens b (z i)).isOpenEmbedding)).obj
              (Q i) ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M))
    (hfin : ∀ i, LocalizedChernFiniteness C (modificationProjection f b ≫ f) (Q i)) (i₁ : ι)
    (L : List ι) :
    supportedComposite z C f (fun i ↦ (p i : ℤ))
        (fun i ↦ modificationChernClass C f b hA (z i) (t i) (hQ i) (p i) (hT i) (hrank i)) i₁ L =
      modificationLocalization C f b hA (iteratedIntersection z i₁ L).2
        (modificationInfinityComposite z C f (fun i ↦ (p i : ℤ)) b
          (fun i ↦ modificationInfinityChernClass C f b (z i) (t i) (hT i) (hQ i) (p i) (hrank i))
          i₁ L)
declarations.comment: the statement for c': c'_{p_n}(Q_n) ∘ ⋯ ∘ c'_{p_1}(Q_1) = (W_{n,∞} ∩ ⋯ ∩ W_{1,∞} → Z_n ∩ ⋯ ∩ Z_1)_* ∘ c'_{p_n}(Q_n|_{W_{n,∞}}) ∘ ⋯ ∘ c'_{p_1}(Q_1|_{W_{1,∞}}) ∘ C, for every sequence of indices i_1, …, i_n

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.supportedComposite_modificationPowerSum
declarations.doc:
**Composites of the classes `P'`.** In the situation of
`Stacks.Chow.supportedComposite_modificationChernClass`, with `Q_i|_{T_i}` and `Q_i|_{W ∖ W_i}`
zero instead of finite locally free of rank `< p_i`, for every sequence of indices
`i_1, …, i_n` (`n ≥ 1`)

  `P'_{p_{i_n}}(Q_{i_n}) ∘ ⋯ ∘ P'_{p_{i_1}}(Q_{i_1}) =
    (W_{i_n,∞} ∩ ⋯ ∩ W_{i_1,∞} ⟶ Z_{i_n} ∩ ⋯ ∩ Z_{i_1})_* ∘
      P'_{p_{i_n}}(Q_{i_n}|_{W_{i_n,∞}}) ∘ ⋯ ∘ P'_{p_{i_1}}(Q_{i_1}|_{W_{i_1,∞}}) ∘ C`

in `A^{p_{i_n} + ⋯ + p_{i_1}}(Z_{i_n} ∩ ⋯ ∩ Z_{i_1} ⟶ X)`, with `P'_p(Q)` the class of
Stacks 0F9K (`Stacks.Chow.modificationPowerSum`) and `P'_p(Q|_{W_{i,∞}})` that of Stacks 0F9H
(`Stacks.Chow.modificationInfinityPowerSum`).
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedComposite_modificationPowerSum
    (hzero : ∀ i, IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      (t i ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity f b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj (Q i)))
    (hperf : ∀ i, Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := W.toRingedSpace) (Q i))
    (hres : ∀ i, IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        (W.toRingedSpace.ofRestrict (modificationComplementOpens b (z i)).isOpenEmbedding)).obj
          (Q i)))
    (hfin : ∀ i, LocalizedChernFiniteness C (modificationProjection f b ≫ f) (Q i)) (i₁ : ι)
    (L : List ι) :
    supportedComposite z C f (fun i ↦ (p i : ℤ))
        (fun i ↦ modificationPowerSum C f b hA (z i) (t i) (hQ i) (p i) (hT i) (hzero i)) i₁ L =
      modificationLocalization C f b hA (iteratedIntersection z i₁ L).2
        (modificationInfinityComposite z C f (fun i ↦ (p i : ℤ)) b
          (fun i ↦ modificationInfinityPowerSum C f b (z i) (t i) (hT i) (hQ i) (p i) (hzero i))
          i₁ L)
declarations.comment: the statement for P': P'_{p_n}(Q_n) ∘ ⋯ ∘ P'_{p_1}(Q_1) = (W_{n,∞} ∩ ⋯ ∩ W_{1,∞} → Z_n ∩ ⋯ ∩ Z_1)_* ∘ P'_{p_n}(Q_n|_{W_{n,∞}}) ∘ ⋯ ∘ P'_{p_1}(Q_1|_{W_{1,∞}}) ∘ C, for every sequence of indices i_1, …, i_n

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.LocalizedSituation.modificationChernClass_eq_localizedChern
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0GUJ, let `b : W ⟶ 𝐏¹_X` be proper and an
isomorphism over `𝐀¹_X`, let `Q ∈ D(𝒪_W)` be perfect, and let
`T ⊆ W_∞` be closed, contain every point of `W_∞` lying over `X ∖ Z`, and be such that `Q|_T` is
finite locally free of rank `< p` in degree `0`. Assume that `Q|_{b^{-1}(𝐀¹_X)}` is the pullback
of `F`, that `F|_{X ∖ Z}` is finite locally free of rank `< p` in degree `0`, and that `Q` on `W`
satisfies condition (3) of Situation 0GUJ, so that the Chern classes of `Q` are defined
(`Stacks.Chow.hasDefinedChernClasses_of_localizedChernFiniteness`, assumption (A0) of
Stacks 0F9K). Then the class `c'_p(Q)` of Stacks 0F9K is the localized Chern class
`c_p(Z ⟶ X, F)` of Stacks 0FB2.
declarations.statement:
theorem modificationChernClass_eq_localizedChern
    (hT : ∀ w, modificationProjectionAtInfinity S.a b w ∉ Set.range S.i → w ∈ Set.range t)
    (hrank : ∃ M : T.Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M S.p ∧
      Nonempty ((derivedPullback (t ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity S.a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        Q ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M))
    (h : S.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLTOnComplement) :
    modificationChernClass S.base S.a b hA S.i t
        (hasDefinedChernClasses_of_localizedChernFiniteness S.base _ Q hQp hfin) S.p hT hrank =
      S.localizedChern h

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.LocalizedSituation.modificationPowerSum_eq_localizedPowerSum
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0GUJ, let `b : W ⟶ 𝐏¹_X` be proper and an
isomorphism over `𝐀¹_X`, let `Q ∈ D(𝒪_W)` be perfect, and let
`T ⊆ W_∞` be closed, contain every point of `W_∞` lying over `X ∖ Z`, and be such that `Q|_T` is
zero. Assume that `Q|_{b^{-1}(𝐀¹_X)}` is the pullback of `F`, that `F|_{X ∖ Z}` is zero, and that
`Q` on `W` satisfies condition (3) of Situation 0GUJ, so that the Chern classes of `Q` are defined
(`Stacks.Chow.hasDefinedChernClasses_of_localizedChernFiniteness`, assumption (A0) of
Stacks 0F9K). Then the class `P'_p(Q)` of Stacks 0F9K is the localized class `P_p(Z ⟶ X, F)` of
Stacks 0FB2.

    (hT : ∀ w, modificationProjectionAtInfinity S.a b w ∉ Set.range S.i → w ∈ Set.range t)

      (t ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity S.a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Q))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.lineToBlowupAtInfinity_spec
declarations.doc:
Let `Z ⊆ X` be the closed subscheme of the closed immersion `i`, let `b : W ⟶ 𝐏¹_X` be the
blowup of `𝐏¹_X` in `∞(Z)`, with exceptional divisor `E` and fibre at infinity `W_∞`. Then
`lineToBlowupAtInfinity : 𝐏¹_Z ⟶ W` is a closed immersion, its composite with `b` is the
inclusion `𝐏¹_Z ⟶ 𝐏¹_X`, and its base change by `∞` (along `W_∞ ⟶ W`, with `(𝐏¹_Z)_∞ = Z`) is
the composite `Z ⟶ C_ZX ⟶ E ⟶ W_∞` of the vertex of the normal cone, the open immersion
`C_ZX ⟶ E` and the inclusion `E ⊆ W_∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lineToBlowupAtInfinity_spec :
    IsClosedImmersion (lineToBlowupAtInfinity i.ker) ∧
      lineToBlowupAtInfinity i.ker ≫ blowupAtInfinityToLine i.ker =
        projectiveLineBaseChange i.ker.subschemeι ∧
      IsPullback (i.toImage ≫ lineInfinitySection i.ker.subscheme)
        (normalConeZeroSection i ≫ normalConeToExceptionalDivisor i ≫
          Scheme.IdealSheafData.inclusion
            (fibreIdealAtInfinity_le_exceptionalIdealAtInfinity i.ker))
        (lineToBlowupAtInfinity i.ker) (fibreIdealAtInfinity i.ker).subschemeι
declarations.comment: a closed immersion P¹_Z → W over P¹_X whose base change by ∞ is Z → C_ZX → E → W_∞, the first arrow the vertex of the cone

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.virtualNormalGysinClass_cap_fundamentalChowClass_of_isCohenMacaulayLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEA.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Stacks 02QL, let `X` be locally of finite type over
`S`, let `𝒩` be a virtual normal sheaf for a closed subscheme `i : Z ⟶ X` (Stacks 0FBQ), and let
`g : Y ⟶ X` be locally of finite type. Given integers `r` and `n`, assume

1. `𝒩` is locally free of rank `r`,
2. every irreducible component of `Y` has `δ`-dimension `n`,
3. `dim_δ(Z ×_X Y) ≤ n - r`, and
4. `𝒪_{Y, ξ}` is Cohen–Macaulay for every `ξ ∈ Z ×_X Y` with `δ(ξ) = n - r`.

Then `c(Z ⟶ X, 𝒩) ∩ [Y]_n = [Z ×_X Y]_{n - r}` in `CH_{n - r}(Z ×_X Y)`.

The proof is the source's: at the points of `Z ×_X Y` of `δ`-dimension `n - r` the ideal of
`Z ×_X Y` is generated by a regular sequence of length `r`, so `Z ×_X Y ⟶ Y` is a regular closed
immersion of codimension `r` near them, where the excess normal sheaf vanishes and Stacks 0FBM
(`Stacks.Chow.virtualNormalGysinClass_capRegularFormula`) applies; this is
`Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass.cap_fundamentalChowClass_eq_of_capRegularFormula`.
declarations.statement:
theorem virtualNormalGysinClass_cap_fundamentalChowClass_of_isCohenMacaulayLocalRing
    [LocallyOfFiniteType i] {n : ℤ} {Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (hY : ∀ W : irreducibleComponents Y,
      deltaDimension C (g ≫ sX)
        ⟨W, W.2.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents (W : Set Y) W.2⟩ = n)
    (hZY : schemeDeltaDimension C (pullback.snd i g ≫ (g ≫ sX)) ≤ ((n - r : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hCM : ∀ ξ : (pullback i g : Scheme.{u}),
      relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (g ≫ sX) ((pullback.snd i g).base ξ) = n - r →
      letI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (g ≫ sX)
      IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk ((pullback.snd i g).base ξ))) :
    (virtualNormalBundleClass C sZ sX i hi 𝒩 r).cap g n (fundamentalChowClass C (g ≫ sX) n) =
      fundamentalChowClass C (pullback.fst i g ≫ sZ) (n - r)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isRegular_of_isCohenMacaulayLocalRing_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEA, the regular sequence of the proof.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Stacks 02QL, let
`X` be locally of finite type over `S`, let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed subscheme and let
`g : Y ⟶ X` be locally of finite type. Assume

* every irreducible component of `Y` has `δ`-dimension `n` (hypothesis (2)),
* `dim_δ(Z ×_X Y) ≤ n - r` (hypothesis (3)),
* `ξ ∈ Z ×_X Y` has `δ(ξ) = n - r` and `𝒪_{Y, ξ}` is Cohen–Macaulay (hypothesis (4)), and
* the ideal of `Z ×_X Y` in `𝒪_{Y, ξ}` is generated by a list `xs` of `r` elements, which is
  what hypothesis (1) provides.

Then `xs` is a regular sequence. Equivalently: `Z ×_X Y` is cut out of `Y` by a regular sequence
of length `r` at every point of `δ`-dimension `n - r`, which is what the source establishes
before invoking the excess intersection formula of Stacks 0FBM to conclude
`c(Z ⟶ X, 𝒩) ∩ [Y]_n = [Z ×_X Y]_{n - r}`. See the implementation notes for why that
conclusion is not stated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegular_of_isCohenMacaulayLocalRing_stalk (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (g : Y ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] {n : ℤ} {r : ℕ}
    (hY : ∀ W : irreducibleComponents Y,
      deltaDimension C (g ≫ sX)
        ⟨W, W.2.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents (W : Set Y) W.2⟩ = n)
    (hZY : schemeDeltaDimension C (pullback.snd i g ≫ (g ≫ sX)) ≤ ((n - r : ℤ) : EInt))
    (ξ : (pullback i g : Scheme.{u}))
    (hξ : relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (g ≫ sX) ((pullback.snd i g).base ξ) = n - r)
    (hCM : letI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (g ≫ sX)
      IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk ((pullback.snd i g).base ξ)))
    (xs : List (Y.presheaf.stalk ((pullback.snd i g).base ξ))) (hlen : xs.length = r)
    (hxs : Ideal.ofList xs = RingHom.ker ((pullback.snd i g).stalkMap ξ).hom) :
    RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (Y.presheaf.stalk ((pullback.snd i g).base ξ)) xs
declarations.comment: the regular sequence of the proof: hypotheses (1)-(4) force the ideal of `Z ×_X Y` in `𝒪_{Y, ξ}` to be generated by a regular sequence of length `r` at every point of `Z ×_X Y` of `δ`-dimension `n - r`. The cap product `c(Z ⟶ X, 𝒩) ∩ [Y]_n` is NOT stated, Stacks 0FBK having no carrier here. See the implementation notes

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinBivariantCap_fundamentalChowClass_normalCone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FEB.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL, let `X` be an integral
scheme locally of finite type over `S` of δ-dimension `n`, and let `Z ⊆ Y ⊆ X` be closed
subschemes which are both effective Cartier divisors in `X`. Write `o : Y ⟶ C_YX` for the zero
section of the normal line cone of `Y` in `X`. Then

    `o^*[C_ZX]_n = [C_ZY]_{n-1}` in `CH_{n-1}(Y ×_{o, C_YX} C_ZX)`.

Here `Y` and `Z` are `DY.subscheme` and `DZ.subscheme`, `Z ⊆ Y` is `hZY : DY ≤ DZ`, `o` is
`Stacks.Conormal.normalConeZeroSection`, the morphism `C_ZX ⟶ C_YX` is
`Stacks.Conormal.normalConeMapOfFactorization`, `o^*` is the cap operation
`Stacks.Chow.gysinBivariantCap` of the canonical Gysin system at the presentation of `o(Y)` by
`Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionDivisorSheaf` and `Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionDivisorSection`, and the closed
immersion `C_ZY ⟶ Y ×_{o, C_YX} C_ZX` is `Stacks.Chow.normalConeToZeroFibre`.

The proof is by the deformation to the normal cone `M = D(Z ⊆ X)`, of δ-dimension at most
`n + 1`. It carries the divisor `Z(t⁻¹) ≅ C_ZX` and the divisor `E_Z`, the inverse image of the
strict transform `E` of `Y` in `D(Y ⊆ X)`. On `C_ZX` the restriction of `𝒪(E_Z)` with its
canonical section is `g^*𝒪(o(Y))` with its canonical section (Stacks 0C4U, as `κ_Y⁻¹E = o(Y)`), so
the left-hand side is `1_{E_Z}|^* (t⁻¹)^*[M]_{n+1}` (Stacks 02TB(1) and 02TA). By
[Stacks, Tag 0B73] this is `(t⁻¹)|^* 1_{E_Z}^*[M] = (t⁻¹)|^*[E_Z]`; `[E_Z]` and `[D(Z ⊆ Y)]` differ
by a cycle supported in `Z(t⁻¹)`, on which the Gysin map of the trivial module kills it
(Stacks 02T9); and `(t⁻¹)|^*[D(Z ⊆ Y)] = [D(Z ⊆ Y) ∩ Z(t⁻¹)] = [C_ZY]` by [Stacks, Tag 02TB].
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinBivariantCap_fundamentalChowClass_normalCone [IsIntegral X]
    (hn : schemeDeltaDimension C sX = (n : EInt)) :
    gysinBivariantCap C (canonicalGysinSystem C)
        (Stacks.Conormal.normalConeToBase DY.subschemeι ≫ DY.subschemeι ≫ sX)
        (zeroSectionDivisorSheaf DY) (zeroSectionDivisorSection DY)
        (Stacks.Conormal.normalConeMapOfFactorization DZ.subschemeι DY.subschemeι (inclusion hZY)
          (inclusion_subschemeι hZY)) n
        (fundamentalChowClass C
          (Stacks.Conormal.normalConeMapOfFactorization DZ.subschemeι DY.subschemeι
              (inclusion hZY) (inclusion_subschemeι hZY) ≫
            (Stacks.Conormal.normalConeToBase DY.subschemeι ≫ DY.subschemeι ≫ sX)) n) =
      QuotientAddGroup.mk'
        (rationalEquivalences C
          (pullback.fst
              (gysinTripleInclusion (zeroSectionDivisorSheaf DY) (zeroSectionDivisorSection DY))
              (Stacks.Conormal.normalConeMapOfFactorization DZ.subschemeι DY.subschemeι
                (inclusion hZY) (inclusion_subschemeι hZY)) ≫
            (gysinTripleInclusion (zeroSectionDivisorSheaf DY) (zeroSectionDivisorSection DY) ≫
              (Stacks.Conormal.normalConeToBase DY.subschemeι ≫ DY.subschemeι ≫ sX)))
          (n - 1))
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C
          (pullback.fst
              (gysinTripleInclusion (zeroSectionDivisorSheaf DY) (zeroSectionDivisorSection DY))
              (Stacks.Conormal.normalConeMapOfFactorization DZ.subschemeι DY.subschemeι
                (inclusion hZY) (inclusion_subschemeι hZY)) ≫
            (gysinTripleInclusion (zeroSectionDivisorSheaf DY) (zeroSectionDivisorSection DY) ≫
              (Stacks.Conormal.normalConeToBase DY.subschemeι ≫ DY.subschemeι ≫ sX)))
          (normalConeToZeroFibre DY DZ.subschemeι (inclusion hZY) (inclusion_subschemeι hZY))
          (n - 1))
declarations.comment: PROVED, at the canonical Gysin system `Stacks.Chow.canonicalGysinSystem` (whose contained-component rule is the first Chern class of the restricted invertible module, Stacks 02SO), which is the o^* of the source. No hypothesis beyond the source's: X integral, locally of finite type over the base of delta-dimension n, Z and Y effective Cartier divisors with Z inside Y. The closed immersion C_ZY -> Y x_{o, C_YX} C_ZX that the source leaves implicit is constructed, as `Stacks.Chow.normalConeToZeroFibre`, the unique morphism with the two components the source names (`Stacks.Chow.normalConeZeroSectionGysinRelation_hom_ext`). The proof goes through the deformation to the normal cone D(Z in X) and Tags 0B73, 02TB, 02TA, 02T9 and 0C4U rather than through the blowups of Tag 0FBG used by the source.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinBivariantClass_cap_normalCone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEB.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL, let `X` be a scheme locally of finite
type over `S` with `dim_δ(X) ≤ n` (the source: `X` integral of `δ`-dimension `n`), and let
`Z ⊆ Y ⊆ X` be closed subschemes, `iZY : Z ⟶ Y` the inclusion, with `Y` an effective Cartier
divisor in `X` (the source also asks it of `Z`; that is not used). Let `o : Y ⟶ C_YX` be the zero
section of the normal line cone, `o(Y) = D0 = normalConeZeroSectionIdeal iY`
(`Stacks.Chow.ker_normalConeZeroSection`), an effective Cartier divisor of `C_YX`
(`Stacks.Chow.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_normalConeZeroSectionIdeal`), and let
`o^* ∈ A^1(Y ⟶ C_YX)` be its Gysin class (Stacks 0B79, `Stacks.Chow.gysinBivariantClass`, for the
canonical section of `𝒪(D0)`). Let `φ : C_ZX ⟶ C_YX` be the canonical morphism of normal cones
induced by `ℐ_Y ⊆ ℐ_Z` (`Stacks.Chow.normalConeChangeOfCentreMap`; on charts it is
`Spec Gr_{ℐ_Z} ⟶ Spec Gr_{ℐ_Y}`). Then

  `o^*[C_ZX]_n = [C_ZY]_{n-1}`  in  `CH_{n-1}(Y ×_{o, C_YX} C_ZX)`,

where the fibre product is the base change of `o(Y) ⊆ C_YX` along `φ` (Stacks 0B6Y) and
`[C_ZY]_{n-1}` is pushed forward along the closed immersion
`Stacks.Chow.normalConeToZeroSectionPullback`, whose component to `C_ZX` is the comparison
`C_ZY ⟶ C_ZX` of normal cones (`Stacks.Chow.normalConeToZeroSectionPullback_snd`).
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinBivariantClass_cap_normalCone {n : ℤ} (hZY : iZY ≫ iY = iZ)
    (hX : schemeDeltaDimension C sX ≤ (n : EInt)) :
    haveI := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    (gysinBivariantClass C (normalConeToX iY ≫ sX)
        (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf (normalConeZeroSectionIdeal iY))
        (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheafGlobalSection (normalConeZeroSectionIdeal iY))).1.cap
        (normalConeChangeOfCentreMap iZ iY (hZY ▸ Scheme.Hom.le_ker_comp iZY iY)) n
        (fundamentalChowClass C (normalConeChangeOfCentreMap iZ iY
          (hZY ▸ Scheme.Hom.le_ker_comp iZY iY) ≫ normalConeToX iY ≫ sX) n) =
      properChowPushforward C (normalConeToX iZY ≫ iY ≫ sX) _
        (normalConeToZeroSectionPullback iY iZ (hZY ▸ Scheme.Hom.le_ker_comp iZY iY) iZY
          (ker_eq_comap_ker_of_comp_eq iY iZ iZY hZY))
        (normalConeToZeroSectionPullback_toBase C sX iY iZ _ iZY _) (n - 1)
        (properPushforwardDescends C _ _ _ _ _)
        (fundamentalChowClass C (normalConeToX iZY ≫ iY ≫ sX) (n - 1))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles
declarations.doc:
For immersions `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X`, three virtual
normal bundles — `𝒩` for `Z ⊆ X`, `𝒩'` for `Z ⊆ Y` and `𝒩''` for `Y ⊆ X` — together with a
short exact sequence

  `(𝒩'')^∨|_Z ⟶ 𝒩^∨ ⟶ (𝒩')^∨`

of duals and the two commutative squares identifying it, through the structural surjections of
the three virtual normal bundles, with the conormal sequence

  `𝒞_{Y/X}|_Z ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}`

of Stacks 062S.
declarations.statement:
structure ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles {Z Y X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j]
declarations.comment: the hypothesis of the lemma: the three virtual normal bundles of Stacks 0FBQ for Z ⊆ Y ⊆ X, the short exact sequence of their duals, and its two commutative squares against the genuine conormal sequence of Stacks 062S; stated for immersions rather than closed subschemes, which is a generalization

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedChernClass_cap_eq_bivariantCompositeCap
declarations.doc:
Granted that the class attached to
`𝒩` composes the class attached to `𝒩'` with the class attached to `𝒩''`, its cap operation on
a test scheme `t : T ⟶ X` is: cap with `c(Y ⟶ X, 𝒩'')`, then cap with `c(Z ⟶ Y, 𝒩')`, then push
forward along the associativity isomorphism `(T ×_X Y) ×_Y Z ≅ T ×_X Z` of pullbacks, the
degrees `k - (p + q)` and `(k - q) - p` being identified.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedChernClass_cap_eq_bivariantCompositeCap
    (hc : IsBivariantClassComposition C G sZ sY sX i j hi hj hpp p q
      (cloc sZ sY i hi D.bundleZY p) (cloc sY sX j hj D.bundleYX q)
      (cloc sZ sX (i ≫ j) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hi hj) D.bundleZX (p + q)))
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (t : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType t] (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup C (t ≫ sX) k) :
    chowGroupDegreeEquiv C (pullback.fst (i ≫ j) t ≫ sZ)
        (by ring : k - (p + q) = (k - q) - p)
        ((cloc sZ sX (i ≫ j) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hi hj) D.bundleZX (p + q)).cap
          t k α) =
      bivariantCompositeCap C G sZ sY sX i j hi hj hpp p q (cloc sZ sY i hi D.bundleZY p)
        (cloc sY sX j hj D.bundleYX q) t k α
declarations.comment: the conclusion, reduced to the composition of bivariant classes and read on cap products; the localized Chern class c(Z ⟶ X, 𝒩) of Stacks 0FBK is not constructed in this repository and is carried as a parameter, as everywhere else here, so that the composition formula is a hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.eq_localizedChernClass_of_isBivariantClassComposition
declarations.doc:
Any bivariant class of degree `p + q` for `Z ⟶ X` that composes `c(Z ⟶ Y, 𝒩')` with
`c(Y ⟶ X, 𝒩'')` is `c(Z ⟶ X, 𝒩)`, provided the latter composes them.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_localizedChernClass_of_isBivariantClassComposition
    (hc : IsBivariantClassComposition C G sZ sY sX i j hi hj hpp p q
      (cloc sZ sY i hi D.bundleZY p) (cloc sY sX j hj D.bundleYX q)
      (cloc sZ sX (i ≫ j) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hi hj) D.bundleZX (p + q)))
    (c : BivariantClass C G sZ sX (i ≫ j) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hi hj) (p + q))
    (hc' : IsBivariantClassComposition C G sZ sY sX i j hi hj hpp p q
      (cloc sZ sY i hi D.bundleZY p) (cloc sY sX j hj D.bundleYX q) c) :
    cloc sZ sX (i ≫ j) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hi hj) D.bundleZX (p + q) = c
declarations.comment: uniqueness: the composition formula determines c(Z ⟶ X, 𝒩), so the content of the lemma reduces to exhibiting the composite; the localized Chern class of Stacks 0FBK is carried as a parameter

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedVirtualNormalGysinClass_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEC.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL, let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be
closed immersions of schemes locally of finite type over `S`, and let `𝒩`, `𝒩'`, `𝒩''` be
virtual normal sheaves for `Z ⊆ X`, `Z ⊆ Y` and `Y ⊆ X` with a short exact sequence
`(𝒩'')^∨|_Z ⟶ 𝒩^∨ ⟶ (𝒩')^∨` whose two squares against the conormal sequence
`𝒞_{Y/X}|_Z ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}` commute (`Stacks.Chow.ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles`).
Then

  `c(Z ⟶ X, 𝒩) = c(Z ⟶ Y, 𝒩') ∘ c(Y ⟶ X, 𝒩'')`   in `A^*(Z ⟶ X)^∧`,

for the classes of Stacks 0FBK (`Stacks.Chow.completedVirtualNormalGysinClass`) and the
composition of Stacks 0FE0.
declarations.statement:
theorem completedVirtualNormalGysinClass_comp :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian Z := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sZ
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sY
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    completedVirtualNormalGysinClass C sZ sX (i ≫ j) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hi hj)
        D.bundleZX =
      completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible C sZ sY sX i j hi hj
        (completedVirtualNormalGysinClass C sZ sY i hi D.bundleZY)
        (completedVirtualNormalGysinClass C sY sX j hj D.bundleYX)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.homComponent_exteriorPowerChernAltProd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEE.** For a finite locally free module `ℰ` of rank `r ≥ 1` on `Y`, the alternating
product `∏_{n = 0}^{r} c(⋀ⁿ ℰ)^{(-1)ⁿ}` of the total Chern classes of its exterior powers, in the
ring `∏_{p ≥ 0} A^p(Y)` of total Chow cohomology classes, agrees with `1 - (r - 1)! c_r(ℰ)` in
every degree `≤ r`. The `+ …` of the source is the part in degrees `> r`, on which nothing is
asserted.
declarations.statement:
theorem homComponent_exteriorPowerChernAltProd (hr : r ≠ 0) {t : ℕ} (ht : t ≤ r) :
    TotalChowClass.homComponent t (exteriorPowerChernAltProd C sY V r : TotalChowClass C sY) =
      TotalChowClass.homComponent t
        (1 - (r - 1).factorial • TotalChowClass.homComponent r (totalChern C sY V r))
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, for the library's Chern classes: c(wedge^n E) is the total Chern class totalChern of Stacks 0B7H, the product is the ordered product of units in the ring TotalChowClass = prod_{p >= 0} A^p(Y) of total Chow cohomology classes, and '= 1 - (r-1)! c_r(E) + ...' is the equality of homogeneous components in every degree <= r. The splitting principle is proved, not assumed: Stacks 02UL via exists_splittingMorphism_basechange_unconditional, the Chern roots of the exterior powers via 02UI and 02UJ (totalChern_exteriorPower_of_hasQuotients)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.homPart_altExteriorTotalChern
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEE.** Let `ℰ` be a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module of rank `r ≥ 1`. Then

  `∏_{n = 0}^{r} c(⋀ⁿ ℰ)^{(-1)ⁿ} = 1 - (r-1)! c_r(ℰ) + ⋯`,

that is, the alternating product of the total Chern classes of the exterior powers of `ℰ` has
vanishing parts in the degrees `1, …, r - 1` and the part `-(r-1)! c_r(ℰ)` in degree `r`; the part
in degree `0` is `1`, and the `⋯` of the source asserts nothing about the higher degrees. Here
`c_i(ℰ) = TotalChowClass.homComponent i (totalChern C sX ℰ r)` is the bivariant Chern class of
Stacks 0B7H in the ring `∏_p A^p(X)` of total Chow cohomology classes.

By the splitting principle (Stacks 02UL,
`Stacks.Chow.TotalChowClass.eq_of_res_eq_of_hasInvertibleFiltration`) it suffices to prove the
identities after restriction along every `h : T ⟶ X` along which `h^*ℰ` has a filtration with
invertible quotients. There `c(⋀ⁿ h^*ℰ) = ∏_{#I = n} (1 + ∑_{i ∈ I} x_i)` for the Chern roots
`x_i` (`Stacks.Chow.exists_chernRoots_exteriorPower`), and the alternating product of these is
computed by `Stacks.Chow.homPart_alternatingProd_of_roots`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homPart_altExteriorTotalChern (E : X.Modules) {r : ℕ}
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] (hr : r ≠ 0) :
    (∀ n, 0 < n → n < r →
      TotalChowClass.homComponent n (altExteriorTotalChern C sX E r : TotalChowClass C sX) = 0) ∧
      TotalChowClass.homComponent r (altExteriorTotalChern C sX E r : TotalChowClass C sX) =
        -(Nat.factorial (r - 1) • TotalChowClass.homComponent r (totalChern C sX E r))
declarations.comment: the lemma as stated, for every X locally of finite type over S and every finite locally free E of rank r >= 1, with no further hypothesis. The alternating product is altExteriorTotalChern C sX E r, the ordered product of the units totalChernUnit of the exterior powers in the ring TotalChowClass C sX of total Chow cohomology classes; c_i(E) is TotalChowClass.homComponent i (totalChern C sX E r). The + ... of the source is read as asserting nothing above degree r, as its proof does

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.altExteriorChernProduct_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEE.** For `ℰ` locally free of rank `r ≥ 1` with Chern roots `t`, the alternating
product `∏_{n = 0}^{r} c(⋀ⁿ ℰ)^{(-1)ⁿ}` has vanishing components in the degrees `1, …, r-1` and
the component `-(r-1)! c_r(ℰ)` in degree `r`; nothing is asserted in higher degrees, which is the
`+ …` of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem altExteriorChernProduct_apply (D : TotalChernClassSeries C G sX R) (E : X.Modules)
    {r : ℕ} [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r]
    (hr : r ≠ 0) (t : Fin r → chowCohomologyComponent C G sX 1)
    (hE : D.ch E = (∏ i, oneAddDegreeOne R (t i) : UnitalSeries R).1)
    (hwedge : ∀ n ≤ r, D.ch (Scheme.Modules.exteriorPower E (n : ℤ))
      = (rootTotalChern R t ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r)).powersetCard n)).1) :
    (∀ n, 0 < n → n < r → (altExteriorChernProduct D E r).1 n = 0) ∧
      (altExteriorChernProduct D E r).1 r
        = -(Nat.factorial (r - 1) • D.ch E r)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, in the carried ring A^*(X)^∧ of Stacks 0FE0 where the inverses c(E)^{-1} exist. CARRIED: the Chern roots, i.e. the display c(wedge^n E) = prod_{i_1 < ... < i_n} (1 + x_{i_1} + ... + x_{i_n}) of the source proof, i.e. the splitting principle: Stacks 02UK, 02UL and the product form of 02UJ; see the module doc. The computation is proved

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.ProjectiveCompletion.bivariantClass_zeroSecObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEF (2), as an equality of bivariant classes.** Let `π : E ⟶ X` be the projective
completion of a locally free module `𝒞` of rank `r`, `i : X ⟶ E` its zero section,
`j : C ⟶ E` and `p : C ⟶ X` the inclusion and the structure morphism of the vector bundle
`C = Spec_X(Sym^*(𝒞))`. For every `s : X ⟶ X₀` and every bivariant class `c ∈ A^q(E ⟶ X₀)`,

  `p^* ∘ π_* ∘ (c_r(i_*𝒪_X) ∘ c) = (-1)^{r-1} (r-1)! (j^* ∘ c)`  in `A^q(C ⟶ X₀)`.

Here `c_r(i_*𝒪_X) ∈ A^r(E)` is the Chern class of Stacks 0F9E, `∘` the composition of Stacks
0B75, `π_*` the pushforward of Stacks 0EPK and `p^* ∈ A^{-r}(C ⟶ X)`, `j^* ∈ A^0(C ⟶ E)` the
flat pullback classes of Stacks 0B78; the two sides are classes for the equal morphisms
`p ≫ s = j ≫ π ≫ s` and of the equal degrees `-r + (r + q) = -0 + q`, compared through the
transport `Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass.copy`. This is the form in which the source composes the
identity `p^* ∘ π_* ∘ c_r(i_*𝒪_X) = (-1)^{r-1} (r-1)! j^*` with a class on its right (Stacks 0FEG);
by the extensionality of Stacks 0B76 it is checked on the caps, which are classes on the base
changes `E ×_{X₀} T = E ×_X (X ×_{X₀} T)`, where it is the cartesian-square form
`flatPullbackChow_properChowPushforward_perfectChernClass_of_isPullback` of the second conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantClass_zeroSecObject {X₀ : Scheme.{u}} (sX₀ : X₀ ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX₀]
    (s : X ⟶ X₀) [LocallyOfFiniteType s] (hs : s ≫ sX₀ = sX) :
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_proj 𝒞 r
    haveI := flat_proj 𝒞 r
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_vectorBundleToBase 𝒞 r
    haveI := flat_vectorBundleToBase 𝒞 r
    ∀ {q : ℤ} (c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) sX₀
      (proj 𝒞 ≫ s) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq rfl hs) q),
      bivariantCompositeOfInvertible C _ sX sX₀ _ s rfl hs (-(r : ℤ)) ((r : ℤ) + q)
          (flatPullbackBivariantClassOfInvertible C
            (Scheme.Modules.vectorBundleToBase X 𝒞 ≫ sX) sX _ rfl r
            (relativeDimension_vectorBundleToBase 𝒞 r))
          (canonicalBivariantProperPushforward C (proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) sX sX₀ (proj 𝒞) s rfl hs
            ((r : ℤ) + q)
            (BivariantClass.copy C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) sX₀
              (Category.id_comp (proj 𝒞 ≫ s)) _ _ rfl
              (bivariantCompositeOfInvertible C (proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) (proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) sX₀ (𝟙 _)
                (proj 𝒞 ≫ s) (Category.id_comp _) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq rfl hs)
                (r : ℤ) q
                (perfectChernClass C (proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) (hasDefinedChernClasses_zeroSecObject 𝒞 r)
                  r) c))) =
        BivariantClass.copy C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) _ sX₀ (incl_proj_comp 𝒞 r s) _
          (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq rfl hs)
          (show -((0 : ℕ) : ℤ) + q = -(r : ℤ) + ((r : ℤ) + q) by push_cast; ring)
          ((((-1 : ℤ) ^ (r - 1) * ((r - 1).factorial : ℤ)) •
            bivariantCompositeOfInvertible C _ (proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) sX₀ (vectorBundleIncl 𝒞 r)
              (proj 𝒞 ≫ s) (vectorBundleIncl_comp_structure 𝒞 r C sX)
              (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq rfl hs) (-((0 : ℕ) : ℤ)) q
              (flatPullbackBivariantClassOfInvertible C _ _ _
                (vectorBundleIncl_comp_structure 𝒞 r C sX) 0
                (relativeDimension_of_isOpenImmersion _)) c))
declarations.comment: clause (2), as an equality of bivariant classes after composing with any c ∈ A^*(E → X₀)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.ProjectiveCompletion.chernClasses_zeroSecObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEF.** Let `𝒞` be a locally free `𝒪_X`-module of rank `r` on `X` locally of finite
type over the base of chapter 42, `π : E = Proj_X(Sym^*(𝒞)[T]) ⟶ X` its projective completion with
zero section `i : X ⟶ E`, and `j : C = Spec_X(Sym^*(𝒞)) ⟶ E`, `p : C ⟶ X` the inclusion and the
structure morphism of the vector bundle. Then

1. `c_t(i_*𝒪_X) = 0` for `t = 1, …, r - 1`, and
2. `p^* ∘ π_* ∘ c_r(i_*𝒪_X) = (-1)^{r-1} (r-1)! j^*`, as operations on every test scheme
   `g : E' ⟶ E` on which the left-hand side is defined: for every cartesian square
   `E' = E ×_X X'` over `f : X' ⟶ X` locally of finite type, with `π' : E' ⟶ X'`, every
   cartesian square `C' = C ×_E E'` with `j' : C' ⟶ E'`, and every `α ∈ A_k(E')`,
   `p'^* π'_*(c_r(i_*𝒪_X) ∩ α) = (-1)^{r-1} (r-1)! j'^* α` in `A_k(C')`, where `p' = π' ∘ j'`.

The Chern classes are those of Stacks 0F9E of the perfect object `i_*𝒪_X` of `D(𝒪_E)`, and
`c_r(i_*𝒪_X) ∩ α` is the operation of `c_r(i_*𝒪_X) ∈ A^r(E)` on the test scheme `g`.

On the reading of (2). In the conventions of bivariant classes, `c_r(i_*𝒪_X) ∈ A^r(E ⟶ E)` and the
pushforward `π_* ∘ -` of Stacks 0EPK applies to a class of `A^*(E ⟶ Z)` for a morphism `E ⟶ Z`
factoring through `π`, so `p^* ∘ π_* ∘ c_r(i_*𝒪_X)` is not a composite of bivariant classes landing
in `A⁰(C ⟶ E)`. The operation it names is defined on those test schemes `E' ⟶ E` that are base
changes of `π`, where `π'_*` exists, and these are the test schemes on which the proof of the
source compares the two sides ("after replacing `X` by a scheme locally of finite type over
`X` ... both sides have the same effect on `α ∈ CH_*(E)`"). Statement (2) is the identity of the
two operations at every such test scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernClasses_zeroSecObject :
    (letI := locallyOfFiniteType_proj_comp 𝒞 r C sX
      ∀ t : ℕ, 0 < t → t < r →
        perfectChernClass C (proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) (hasDefinedChernClasses_zeroSecObject 𝒞 r) t = 0) ∧
    ∀ {X' E' C' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X' ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (g : E' ⟶ space 𝒞)
      (π' : E' ⟶ X') (hsq : IsPullback g π' (proj 𝒞) f)
      (q : C' ⟶ Scheme.Modules.vectorBundle X 𝒞) (j' : C' ⟶ E')
      (hsqC : IsPullback q j' (vectorBundleIncl 𝒞 r) g) (k : ℤ),
      haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_proj 𝒞 r
      haveI := flat_proj 𝒞 r
      haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType g := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip inferInstance
      haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType π' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq inferInstance
      haveI : Flat π' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq inferInstance
      haveI : IsProper π' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq inferInstance
      haveI : IsOpenImmersion j' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsqC inferInstance
      ∀ α : chowGroup C (g ≫ proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) k,
      flatPullbackChow C (j' ≫ g ≫ proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (j' ≫ π')
          (incl_snd_comp_eq 𝒞 C sX hsq j') r (relativeDimension_incl_snd 𝒞 r hsq j') (k - r)
          (flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_general C _ _ _
            (incl_snd_comp_eq 𝒞 C sX hsq j') r (relativeDimension_incl_snd 𝒞 r hsq j') (k - r))
          (properChowPushforward C (g ≫ proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) π' (snd_comp_eq 𝒞 C sX hsq) (k - r)
            (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper C _ _ _
              (snd_comp_eq 𝒞 C sX hsq) (k - r))
            ((perfectChernClass C (proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) (hasDefinedChernClasses_zeroSecObject 𝒞 r)).op
              g k r α)) =
        chowGroupCast C _ (show k + ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ) = k - r + r by push_cast; ring)
          (((-1 : ℤ) ^ (r - 1) * ((r - 1).factorial : ℤ)) •
            flatPullbackChow C _ (g ≫ proj 𝒞 ≫ sX) j' rfl 0
              (relativeDimension_of_isOpenImmersion _) k
              (flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_general C _ _ _ rfl 0
                (relativeDimension_of_isOpenImmersion _) k) α)
declarations.comment: both conclusions: (1) c_t(i_*O_X) = 0 for t = 1, ..., r - 1; (2) p^* o pi_* o c_r(i_*O_X) = (-1)^(r-1) (r-1)! j^*, as an identity of operations at every test scheme E' -> E on which the left side is defined, namely every base change E' = E x_X X' of pi along f : X' -> X locally of finite type (any cartesian square), with C' = C x_E E' any cartesian square: p'^* pi'_* (c_r(i_*O_X) cap alpha) = (-1)^(r-1) (r-1)! j'^* alpha for alpha in A_k(E'). In the bivariant conventions c_r(i_*O_X) lies in A^r(E -> E) and the pushforward of 0EPK needs a class over a morphism factoring through pi, so the left side is not a composite of bivariant classes in A^0(C -> E); its operation exists exactly on these test schemes, which are those on which the source's proof compares the two sides

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chernClass_pushforward_zeroSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEF.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over the base `S` of chapter 42, `𝒞` a
finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module of rank `r ≥ 1`, `π : E = 𝐏(𝒞 ⊕ 𝒪_X) ⟶ X` the projective
completion, `i : X = 𝐏(𝒪_X) ⟶ E` the zero section, `C = Spec_X(Sym(𝒞)) = V ⊆ E` the complement
of the divisor at infinity with its inclusion `j` and projection `p : V ⟶ X`. Then

* `c_t(i_*𝒪_X) = 0` for `t = 1, …, r - 1`, and
* `p^* ∘ π_* ∘ c_r(i_*𝒪_X) = (-1)^{r-1} (r-1)! j^*` in `A^0(C → E)`: for every test scheme
  `q : X' ×_X E ⟶ E` obtained from a morphism `g : X' ⟶ X` locally of finite type, with
  `π' : X' ×_X E ⟶ X'`, `V' = q⁻¹(V)` and `p' : V' ⟶ X'`, and every `α ∈ CH_*(X' ×_X E)`,
