  `p'^*(π'_*(c_r(i_*𝒪_X) ∩ α)) = (-1)^{r-1} (r-1)! α|_{V'}`; the test scheme `𝟙_E` is stated
  separately.

The Chern classes of `i_*𝒪_X` are defined because it is resolved by the Koszul complex of
`π^*𝒞 ⊗ 𝒪_E(-1) ⟶ 𝒪_E` (`Stacks.ProjectiveCompletion.koszulResolutionZeroSection`). The rank is
taken positive, as the factor `(r-1)!` of the source presupposes.

*Why the test schemes `X' ×_X E` are the whole of the second clause.* The composite
`p^* ∘ π_* ∘ c_r(i_*𝒪_X)` is not a composite of bivariant classes for `C ⟶ E`: `π_*` is proper
pushforward along `π' : E' ⟶ X'`, which exists only for a test scheme `E'` over `E` that is the
pullback `X' ×_X E` of a scheme `X'` over `X`, and `p^*` is flat pullback along the bundle
`p' : X' ×_X C ⟶ X'`. So the composite is an operation `CH_*(X' ×_X E) ⟶ CH_*(X' ×_X C)` for
each `X' ⟶ X` locally of finite type, and the equality "in `A^0(C → E)`" with
`(-1)^{r-1}(r-1)! j^*` asserts exactly that these operations agree with `(-1)^{r-1}(r-1)!` times
restriction to `X' ×_X C`, for every such `X'`. This is the reduction the source makes in its proof
("after replacing `X` by a scheme locally of finite type over `X`, it suffices to prove that both
sides have the same effect on an element `α ∈ CH_*(E)`"), and it is the third conjunct; the second
is the case `X' = X` read on `E` itself rather than on `X ×_X E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernClass_pushforward_zeroSection (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (𝒞 : X.Modules) (r : ℕ)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} 𝒞 r]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} 𝒞] (hr : r ≠ 0) :
    haveI := flat_projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 r
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 r
    (∀ t : ℕ, 0 < t → t < r →
      perfectChernClass C (projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 ≫ sX)
        (hasDefinedChernClasses_pushforward_zeroSection 𝒞 r) t = 0) ∧
    (∀ (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C (𝟙 _ ≫ projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 ≫ sX) (k + r)),
      chowGroupCast C ((complementOpen 𝒞).ι ≫ 𝟙 _ ≫ projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 ≫ sX) (by ring)
        (bundlePullback C sX ((complementOpen 𝒞).ι ≫ 𝟙 _ ≫ projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 ≫ sX)
        ((complementOpen 𝒞).ι ≫ projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞) (by simp) r
        (relativeDimension_complementOpen_ι_comp 𝒞 r) (k + r - r)
        (properChowPushforward C (𝟙 _ ≫ projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 ≫ sX) sX
          (projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞) (by simp) (k + r - r)
          (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper C _ sX _ (by simp) _)
          ((perfectChernClass C (projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 ≫ sX)
            (hasDefinedChernClasses_pushforward_zeroSection 𝒞 r)).op (𝟙 _) (k + r) r α))) =
        ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (r - 1) * (Nat.factorial (r - 1) : ℤ)) •
          chowGroupOpensRestrictOfIsOpenImmersion C (𝟙 _ ≫ projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 ≫ sX)
            (complementOpen 𝒞) (k + r) α) ∧
    (∀ {X' : Scheme.{u}} (sX' : X' ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX'] (g : X' ⟶ X)
      [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (hg : g ≫ sX = sX') (k : ℤ)
      (α : chowGroup C (pullback.snd g (projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞) ≫
        projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 ≫ sX) (k + r)),
      chowGroupCast C _ (by ring) (bundlePullback C sX'
        ((complementOpenBaseChange g 𝒞).ι ≫ pullback.snd g (projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞) ≫
          projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 ≫ sX)
        ((complementOpenBaseChange g 𝒞).ι ≫ pullback.fst g (projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞))
        (by rw [Category.assoc, pullback_fst_comp_eq_pullback_snd_comp C sX sX' g hg 𝒞]) r
        (relativeDimension_complementOpenBaseChange g 𝒞 r) (k + r - r)
        (properChowPushforward C
          (pullback.snd g (projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞) ≫ projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 ≫ sX) sX'
          (pullback.fst g (projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞))
          (pullback_fst_comp_eq_pullback_snd_comp C sX sX' g hg 𝒞) (k + r - r)
          (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper C _ sX' _
            (pullback_fst_comp_eq_pullback_snd_comp C sX sX' g hg 𝒞) _)
          ((perfectChernClass C (projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 ≫ sX)
            (hasDefinedChernClasses_pushforward_zeroSection 𝒞 r)).op
            (pullback.snd g (projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞)) (k + r) r α))) =
        ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (r - 1) * (Nat.factorial (r - 1) : ℤ)) •
          chowGroupOpensRestrictOfIsOpenImmersion C
            (pullback.snd g (projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞) ≫ projectiveCompletionProj 𝒞 ≫ sX)
            (complementOpenBaseChange g 𝒞) (k + r) α)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, for r ≥ 1 (the source's (r-1)! presupposes it): c_t(i_*O_X) = 0 for 0 < t < r, and p^* ∘ π_* ∘ c_r(i_*O_X) = (-1)^{r-1}(r-1)! j^* on every test scheme X' ×_X E ⟶ E, which are the test schemes on which the composite p^* ∘ π_* ∘ c_r is defined

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isRegularImmersionChernFormula_regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation
declarations.doc:
Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a regular closed immersion of codimension `r ≥ 1` of schemes locally of
finite type over the base of chapter 42, with `X` quasi-compact or with quasi-compact irreducible
components, and `𝒩 = 𝒞_{Z/X}^∨` its normal sheaf. Then `c_t(Z ⟶ X, i_*𝒪_Z) = 0` for
`t = 1, …, r - 1` and `c_r(Z ⟶ X, i_*𝒪_Z) = (-1)^{r-1}(r-1)! c(Z ⟶ X, 𝒩)` in `A^r(Z ⟶ X)`, the
localized Chern classes being those of Definition 0FB5
(`Stacks.Chow.LocalizedSituation.IsRegularImmersionChernFormula` for the situation
`Stacks.Chow.regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation` of `i_*𝒪_Z`). The codimension is positive, as
the factor `(r-1)!` of the source presupposes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularImmersionChernFormula_regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation (hr : 0 < r) :
    (regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation C sX i hreg hX 0).IsRegularImmersionChernFormula
      (isZeroOnComplement_regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation C sX i hreg hX 0) hreg hr
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: c_t(Z → X, i_*O_Z) = 0 for 0 < t < r and c_r(Z → X, i_*O_Z) = (-1)^{r-1}(r-1)! c(Z → X, N), for X quasi-compact or with quasi-compact irreducible components and r ≥ 1 (presupposed by (r-1)!)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation_capFundamentalClass
declarations.doc:
Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a regular closed immersion of codimension `r ≥ 1` of schemes locally of
finite type over the base, `X` quasi-compact or with quasi-compact irreducible components, and
`dim_δ(X) ≤ n` (the source's `dim_δ(X) = n`). Then

1. `c_t(Z ⟶ X, i_*𝒪_Z) ∩ [X]_n = 0` for `1 ≤ t < r`,
2. `c_r(Z ⟶ X, i_*𝒪_Z) ∩ [X]_n = (-1)^{r-1}(r-1)! [Z]_{n-r}`,
3. `ch_t(Z ⟶ X, i_*𝒪_Z) ∩ [X]_n = 0` for `0 ≤ t < r`, and
4. `ch_r(Z ⟶ X, i_*𝒪_Z) ∩ [X]_n = [Z]_{n-r}`,

with `c_t(Z ⟶ X, i_*𝒪_Z)` the class of Stacks 0FB2 for the situation in degree `t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation_capFundamentalClass (hr : 0 < r) (n : ℤ)
    (hXn : schemeDeltaDimension C sX ≤ (n : EInt)) :
    (∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t), t < r →
      capFundamentalClassAt C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (i ≫ sX) sX i rfl t n
        ((regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation C sX i hreg hX t).localizedChern
          (isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLTOnComplement_regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation C sX
            i hreg hX ht)) = 0) ∧
    capFundamentalClassAt C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (i ≫ sX) sX i rfl r n
        ((regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation C sX i hreg hX r).localizedChern
          (isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLTOnComplement_regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation C sX
            i hreg hX hr)) =
      ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (r - 1) * ((r - 1).factorial : ℤ)) • fundamentalChowClass C (i ≫ sX) (n - r) ∧
    (∀ t : ℕ, t < r →
      (capFundamentalClassAt C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (i ≫ sX) sX i rfl t
          n).toIntLinearMap.lTensor ℚ
        ((regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation C sX i hreg hX 0).localizedChernChar
          (isZeroOnComplement_regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation C sX i hreg hX 0) t) = 0) ∧
    (capFundamentalClassAt C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (i ≫ sX) sX i rfl r
        n).toIntLinearMap.lTensor ℚ
        ((regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation C sX i hreg hX 0).localizedChernChar
          (isZeroOnComplement_regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation C sX i hreg hX 0) r) =
      (1 : ℚ) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] fundamentalChowClass C (i ≫ sX) (n - r)
declarations.comment: all four parts, for X quasi-compact or with quasi-compact irreducible components, r ≥ 1 and dim_δ(X) ≤ n (the source's dim_δ(X) = n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundleKZero.exists_secondAdamsOperator_pullbackRingHom
declarations.doc:
For every scheme `X` there is a ring map `ψ²_X : K₀(Vect(X)) → K₀(Vect(X))` with
`ψ²_X([ℰ]) = [Sym² ℰ] - [⋀² ℰ]` on finite locally free modules, `ψ²_X([ℒ]) = [ℒ ⊗ ℒ]` on
invertible modules, and compatible with pullbacks: for every morphism `f : Y ⟶ X`,
`ψ²_Y ∘ f^* = f^* ∘ ψ²_X`, where `f^*` is the pullback ring map `pullbackRingHom f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_secondAdamsOperator_pullbackRingHom :
    ∃ ψ : ∀ X : Scheme.{u}, VectorBundleKZero X →+* VectorBundleKZero X,
      (∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (E : X.Modules),
          IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) E →
            ψ X (classOf X E) =
              classOf X (secondSymmetricPower X E) - classOf X (secondExteriorPower X E)) ∧
        (∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules),
          Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L →
            ψ X (classOf X L) = classOf X (Scheme.Modules.tensorObjRingedSpace X L L)) ∧
        (∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X),
          (ψ Y).comp (pullbackRingHom f) = (pullbackRingHom f).comp (ψ X))
declarations.comment: for every scheme `X` a ring map `ψ²_X : K₀(Vect(X)) → K₀(Vect(X))` with `ψ²_X([ℒ]) = [ℒ ⊗ ℒ]` for invertible `ℒ` and `ψ²_X([ℰ]) = [Sym² ℰ] - [⋀² ℰ]` for finite locally free `ℰ`, compatible with pullbacks: `ψ²_Y ∘ f^* = f^* ∘ ψ²_X` for every morphism `f : Y ⟶ X`, with `f^*` the ring map `pullbackRingHom f`

declarations.name: Stacks.SecondAdamsPerfect.swapSquare_comp_swapSquare
declarations.doc:
**The switch is an involution.** This is the symmetry of the commutativity constraint, read
at `(L, L)`, and it is what makes the group `{±1}` act on `L ⊗ L`.
declarations.statement: theorem swapSquare_comp_swapSquare (L : C) : swapSquare L ≫ swapSquare L = 𝟙 (L ⊗ L)
declarations.comment: the switch of the two factors of a tensor square is an involution

declarations.name: Stacks.SecondAdamsPerfect.swapSquareAction
declarations.doc:
**The action of the group `{±1}` on `L ⊗ L` by switching the factors**: the unit `1` acts by
the identity and the unit `-1` by the switch, which is an involution.
declarations.statement: def swapSquareAction (L : C) : ℤˣ →* End (L ⊗ L)
declarations.comment: the action of the group of units {±1} on the tensor square by switching the two factors

declarations.name: Stacks.SecondAdamsPerfect.invariantProjector_add_antiInvariantProjector
declarations.doc: The two projectors are complementary: their sum is the identity of `L ⊗ L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem invariantProjector_add_antiInvariantProjector :
    invariantProjector R L + antiInvariantProjector R L = 𝟙 (L ⊗ L)
declarations.comment: the invariant and anti-invariant projectors of the switch are complementary

declarations.name: Stacks.SecondAdamsPerfect.cls_tensorObj_eq_add
declarations.doc:
**`[L ⊗ L] = [(L ⊗ L)^+] + [(L ⊗ L)^-]` in the `K`-group**: the invariants and the
anti-invariants of the switch exhibit the tensor square as their biproduct, and the split
triangle on a biproduct is distinguished.
declarations.statement:
theorem cls_tensorObj_eq_add (P : IdempotentSplitting (invariantProjector R L))
    (N : IdempotentSplitting (antiInvariantProjector R L)) :
    K0.cls (L ⊗ L) = K0.cls P.obj + K0.cls N.obj
declarations.comment: the class of the tensor square is the sum of the classes of the invariants and of the anti-invariants of the switch

declarations.name: Stacks.SecondAdamsPerfect.cls_sub_cls_eq
declarations.doc:
**The difference `[(L ⊗ L)^+] - [(L ⊗ L)^-]` is independent of the chosen invariants and
anti-invariants**, hence a well-defined element of the `K`-group attached to `L`. This is the
value the second Adams operator of the source is to take on `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cls_sub_cls_eq (P P' : IdempotentSplitting (invariantProjector R L))
    (N N' : IdempotentSplitting (antiInvariantProjector R L)) :
    K0.cls P.obj - K0.cls N.obj = K0.cls P'.obj - K0.cls N'.obj
declarations.comment: the difference of the classes of the invariants and of the anti-invariants of the switch on the tensor square is a well-defined element of the K-group attached to the object; its additivity along distinguished triangles is not proved

declarations.name: Stacks.SecondAdamsPerfect.derivedSwapSquare_comp_self
declarations.doc: **The switch of the two factors of `L ⊗^L_{O_X} L` is an involution.**
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSwapSquare_comp_self (L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
    derivedSwapSquare Rc L ≫ derivedSwapSquare Rc L = 𝟙 (((derivedTensor Rc).obj L).obj L)
declarations.comment: the switch of the two factors of the derived tensor square on a ringed space is an involution

declarations.name: Stacks.SecondAdamsPerfect.derivedSwapSquareAction
declarations.doc:
**The action of the group `{±1}` on `L ⊗^L_{O_X} L` by switching the factors**, in the
derived category of a ringed space.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSwapSquareAction (L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
    ℤˣ →* End (((derivedTensor Rc).obj L).obj L)
declarations.comment: the action of the group {±1} on the derived tensor square of an object of D(O_X) by switching the two factors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.secondAdamsPerfect
declarations.doc:
The second Adams operator `ψ²` on `K₀(D_perf(𝒪_X))`, for a scheme `X` on which `2` is
invertible: the additive endomorphism sending the class of a perfect object `L` to
`[(L ⊗^L L)^+] - [(L ⊗^L L)^-]` (`secondAdamsPerfect_cls`).
declarations.statement:
def secondAdamsPerfect (h2 : IsUnit (2 : Γ(X, ⊤))) :
    K0 𝒟ₚ →+ K0 𝒟ₚ
declarations.comment: the second Adams operator ψ² on K₀(D_perf(𝒪_X)), for any model of D(𝒪_X), as an additive endomorphism; its value on classes is `secondAdamsPerfect_cls`, and its well-definedness (additivity along distinguished triangles) is `secondAdamsPerfect_distinguished`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_switchSplittings_perfect
declarations.doc:
For a perfect object `L` of `D(𝒪_X)`, with `2` invertible on `X`, the idempotents `(𝟙 + σ)/2`
and `(𝟙 - σ)/2` of the switch `σ` of `L ⊗^L L` split, and the objects splitting them — the
invariants `(L ⊗^L L)^+` and the anti-invariants `(L ⊗^L L)^-` — are perfect, whichever splittings
are taken.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_switchSplittings_perfect (h2 : IsUnit (2 : Γ(X, ⊤))) (L : 𝒟ₚ) :
    letI := derivedMonoidal X.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    letI := derivedSymmetric X.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    haveI := isIso_two_smul_id X.toRingedSpace.sheaf (isUnit_two_presheaf_obj X h2)
    Nonempty (IdempotentSplitting
        (invariantIdempotent ((β_ L.obj L.obj).hom : L.obj ⊗ L.obj ⟶ _))) ∧
      Nonempty (IdempotentSplitting
        (antiInvariantIdempotent ((β_ L.obj L.obj).hom : L.obj ⊗ L.obj ⟶ _))) ∧
      (∀ s : IdempotentSplitting
        (invariantIdempotent ((β_ L.obj L.obj).hom : L.obj ⊗ L.obj ⟶ _)),
          IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) s.obj) ∧
      (∀ s : IdempotentSplitting
        (antiInvariantIdempotent ((β_ L.obj L.obj).hom : L.obj ⊗ L.obj ⟶ _)),
          IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) s.obj)
declarations.comment: the invariants (L ⊗^L L)^+ and the anti-invariants (L ⊗^L L)^- of the switch on the derived tensor square of a perfect object exist, and are perfect for every choice

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.secondAdamsPerfect_cls
declarations.doc:
For a scheme `X` on which `2` is invertible and a perfect object `L` of `D(𝒪_X)`, the second
Adams operator sends the class of `L` to the class of the invariants minus the class of the
anti-invariants of the switch on `L ⊗^L L`, for any choice of the two (which exist and are perfect
by `exists_switchSplittings_perfect`).
declarations.statement:
theorem secondAdamsPerfect_cls (h2 : IsUnit (2 : Γ(X, ⊤))) (L : 𝒟ₚ) :
    letI := derivedMonoidal X.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    letI := derivedSymmetric X.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    haveI := isIso_two_smul_id X.toRingedSpace.sheaf (isUnit_two_presheaf_obj X h2)
    ∀ (sp : IdempotentSplitting
        (invariantIdempotent ((β_ L.obj L.obj).hom : L.obj ⊗ L.obj ⟶ _)))
      (sm : IdempotentSplitting
        (antiInvariantIdempotent ((β_ L.obj L.obj).hom : L.obj ⊗ L.obj ⟶ _)))
      (hp : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) sp.obj) (hm : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) sm.obj),
      secondAdamsPerfect X h2 (K0.cls L) = K0.cls (⟨sp.obj, hp⟩ : 𝒟ₚ) -
        K0.cls (⟨sm.obj, hm⟩ : 𝒟ₚ)
declarations.comment: ψ²([L]) = [(L ⊗^L L)^+] - [(L ⊗^L L)^-] for every perfect L and every choice of the invariants and the anti-invariants of the switch

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.secondAdamsPerfect_distinguished
declarations.doc:
For a distinguished triangle `L₁ ⟶ L₂ ⟶ L₃ ⟶ L₁[1]` of `D_perf(𝒪_X)`, `2` being invertible on
`X`, and for any choices `sᵢ^±` of the invariants and the anti-invariants of the switch on
`Lᵢ ⊗^L Lᵢ`,

`[s₂^+] - [s₂^-] = ([s₁^+] - [s₁^-]) + ([s₃^+] - [s₃^-])`

in `K₀(D_perf(𝒪_X))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem secondAdamsPerfect_distinguished (h2 : IsUnit (2 : Γ(X, ⊤)))
    (T : Triangle 𝒟ₚ) (hT : T ∈ distTriang _) :
    letI := derivedMonoidal X.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    letI := derivedSymmetric X.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    haveI := isIso_two_smul_id X.toRingedSpace.sheaf (isUnit_two_presheaf_obj X h2)
    ∀ (sp₁ : IdempotentSplitting
        (invariantIdempotent ((β_ T.obj₁.obj T.obj₁.obj).hom : T.obj₁.obj ⊗ T.obj₁.obj ⟶ _)))
      (sm₁ : IdempotentSplitting
        (antiInvariantIdempotent ((β_ T.obj₁.obj T.obj₁.obj).hom : T.obj₁.obj ⊗ T.obj₁.obj ⟶ _)))
      (sp₂ : IdempotentSplitting
        (invariantIdempotent ((β_ T.obj₂.obj T.obj₂.obj).hom : T.obj₂.obj ⊗ T.obj₂.obj ⟶ _)))
      (sm₂ : IdempotentSplitting
        (antiInvariantIdempotent ((β_ T.obj₂.obj T.obj₂.obj).hom : T.obj₂.obj ⊗ T.obj₂.obj ⟶ _)))
      (sp₃ : IdempotentSplitting
        (invariantIdempotent ((β_ T.obj₃.obj T.obj₃.obj).hom : T.obj₃.obj ⊗ T.obj₃.obj ⟶ _)))
      (sm₃ : IdempotentSplitting
        (antiInvariantIdempotent ((β_ T.obj₃.obj T.obj₃.obj).hom : T.obj₃.obj ⊗ T.obj₃.obj ⟶ _)))
      (hp₁ : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) sp₁.obj)
      (hm₁ : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) sm₁.obj)
      (hp₂ : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) sp₂.obj)
      (hm₂ : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) sm₂.obj)
      (hp₃ : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) sp₃.obj)
      (hm₃ : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) sm₃.obj),
      K0.cls (⟨sp₂.obj, hp₂⟩ : 𝒟ₚ) -
          K0.cls (⟨sm₂.obj, hm₂⟩ : 𝒟ₚ) =
        (K0.cls (⟨sp₁.obj, hp₁⟩ : 𝒟ₚ) -
          K0.cls (⟨sm₁.obj, hm₁⟩ : 𝒟ₚ)) +
        (K0.cls (⟨sp₃.obj, hp₃⟩ : 𝒟ₚ) -
          K0.cls (⟨sm₃.obj, hm₃⟩ : 𝒟ₚ))
declarations.comment: well-definedness on K₀: [(L ⊗^L L)^+] - [(L ⊗^L L)^-] is additive along distinguished triangles of D_perf(𝒪_X), for every choice of invariants and anti-invariants

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.perfectKZeroSecondAdams
declarations.doc:
The second Adams operator on the group `AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectKZero X = K₀(D_perf(𝒪_X))`
of [Stacks, Tag 0FDG]: `secondAdamsPerfect` at the standard model of the derived category.
declarations.statement: def perfectKZeroSecondAdams (h2 : IsUnit (2 : Γ(X, ⊤))) : PerfectKZero X →+ PerfectKZero X
declarations.comment: ψ² on K₀(X) = PerfectKZero X of Tag 0FDG: `secondAdamsPerfect` at the standard model of D(𝒪_X) that PerfectKZero is defined with

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.totalChernKGroupMap
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0FEL.** The Chern class map `c : K_0(Vect(X)) ⟶ ∏_{i ≥ 0} A^i(X)`.
declarations.statement: def totalChernKGroupMap (α : VectorBundleKZero X) : TotalChowClass C sX
declarations.comment: the canonical map c : K_0(Vect(X)) -> prod_{i >= 0} A^i(X), into the ring Stacks.Chow.TotalChowClass of total Chow cohomology classes under the composition product of Tag 0FE0, sending [E] to the total Chern class of Tag 0ESW of E (any rank); its properties are Stacks.Chow.totalChernKGroupMap_spec

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.totalChernKGroupMap_spec
declarations.statement:
theorem totalChernKGroupMap_spec :
    (∀ (E : X.Modules) [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E],
      totalChernKGroupMap C sX (VectorBundleKZero.classOf X E) = totalChernClassOfModule C sX E ∧
        totalChernClassOfModule C sX E 0 = (1 : TotalChowClass C sX) 0 ∧
        ∀ p : ℕ, totalChernClassOfModule C sX E p = chernClassOfModule C sX E p) ∧
    (∀ α β : VectorBundleKZero X,
      totalChernKGroupMap C sX (α + β) = totalChernKGroupMap C sX α * totalChernKGroupMap C sX β) ∧
    (∀ (E : X.Modules) [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E],
      totalChernKGroupMap C sX (-VectorBundleKZero.classOf X E) *
          totalChernClassOfModule C sX E = 1 ∧
        totalChernClassOfModule C sX E *
          totalChernKGroupMap C sX (-VectorBundleKZero.classOf X E) = 1) ∧
    (∀ c : VectorBundleKZero X → TotalChowClass C sX,
      (∀ (E : X.Modules) [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E],
        c (VectorBundleKZero.classOf X E) = totalChernClassOfModule C sX E) →
      (∀ α β, c (α + β) = c α * c β) → c = totalChernKGroupMap C sX)
declarations.comment: the canonical map c : K_0(Vect(X)) -> prod_{i >= 0} A^i(X) in full, for X locally of finite type over the base of Situation 02QL: the target is Stacks.Chow.TotalChowClass, the product of the Chow cohomology groups A^i(X) of Tag 0B7E with the Cauchy product of the composition of bivariant classes (Tag 0FE0); the value on [E], for E finite locally free of any, possibly non-constant, rank, is the total Chern class 1 + c_1(E) + c_2(E) + ... of Tag 0ESW, assembled over the open and closed loci where the rank is constant; the map is multiplicative, sends -[E] to the two-sided inverse c(E)^{-1}, and is the unique such map; well-definedness is the Whitney sum formula of Tag 02UI, proved as Stacks.Chow.totalChernClassOfModule_eq_mul_of_shortExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundleKZero.existsUnique_ringHom_of_tensorMultiplicative
declarations.doc:
An assignment `ℰ ↦ ch(ℰ)` of an element of a ring `R` to each `𝒪_X`-module which vanishes off
the finite locally free modules, is additive along their short exact sequences and
multiplicative on tensor products, and takes the value `1` on `𝒪_X`, extends to a ring
homomorphism on `K₀(Vect(X))`, and to exactly one. For the Chern character with values in
`∏_{i ≥ 0} A^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐` this is the ring map `ch : K₀(Vect(X)) ⟶ ∏_{i ≥ 0} A^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_ringHom_of_tensorMultiplicative
    (hzero : ∀ M : X.Modules,
      ¬ IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) M → ch M = 0)
    (hadd : ∀ {E F G : X.Modules} (f : E ⟶ F) (g : F ⟶ G) (w : f ≫ g = 0),
      IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) E →
        IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) F →
          IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) G →
            Mono f → Epi g → (ShortComplex.mk f g w).Exact → ch F = ch E + ch G)
    (hmul : ∀ M N : X.Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) M →
      IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) N →
        ch (Scheme.Modules.tensorObjRingedSpace X M N) = ch M * ch N)
    (hone : ch (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) = 1) :
    ∃! φ : VectorBundleKZero X →+* R,
      ∀ M : X.Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) M →
        φ (classOf X M) = ch M
declarations.comment: the canonical ring map on `K₀(Vect(X))` that the Chern character defines, and its uniqueness; additivity along short exact sequences (Tag 0F9C), multiplicativity on tensor products (Tag 0F9D) and the value on `𝒪_X` are properties of the Chern character of a module and are hypotheses, and `∏_{i ≥ 0} A^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐` is read as an arbitrary ring, which it has no construction as in this repository

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterRingHom_spec
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be locally of finite type over the base of chapter 42. The Chern character defines a
canonical ring map

  `ch : K_0(Vect(X)) ⟶ ∏_{i ≥ 0} A^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐`

(`Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterRingHom`, a ring homomorphism into the ring
`Stacks.Chow.instRingFullRationalChowCohomology`) which

1. sends a generator `[ℰ]`, `ℰ` finite locally free of any rank, to `ch(ℰ)`, whose degree-`p`
   component is `ch_p(ℰ) = P_p(ℰ)/p!` (`Stacks.Chow.moduleChernCharacterComponent`);
2. is the only ring map with property 1 (it is obtained "by extending additively").

It is well defined by Stacks 0F9C (`Stacks.Chow.moduleChernCharacter_eq_add_of_shortExact`) and a
ring map by Stacks 0F9D (`Stacks.Chow.moduleChernCharacter_tensorObj`).
declarations.statement:
theorem chernCharacterRingHom_spec :
    (∀ (E : X.Modules) [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E],
      chernCharacterRingHom C sX (VectorBundleKZero.classOf X E) = moduleChernCharacter C sX E ∧
        ∀ p : ℕ, chernCharacterRingHom C sX (VectorBundleKZero.classOf X E) p =
          ((Nat.factorial p : ℚ)⁻¹) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] modulePowerSumComponentArbitraryRank C sX E p) ∧
    (∀ φ : VectorBundleKZero X →+* fullRationalChowCohomology C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX,
      (∀ (E : X.Modules) [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E],
        φ (VectorBundleKZero.classOf X E) = moduleChernCharacter C sX E) →
      φ = chernCharacterRingHom C sX)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.existsUnique_ringHom_chernCharacter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEM.** The Chern character defines a canonical ring map

  `ch : K_0(Vect(X)) ⟶ ∏_{i ≥ 0} A^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐`:

there is a unique ring homomorphism sending the class of every finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module
`ℰ`, of arbitrary rank, to its Chern character `ch(ℰ) = (P_p(ℰ)/p!)_{p ≥ 0}`. It is
`Stacks.Chow.rationalTotalChernCharacterRingHom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_ringHom_chernCharacter :
    ∃! φ : VectorBundleKZero X →+* RationalTotalChowClass C sX,
      ∀ (E : X.Modules) [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E],
        φ (VectorBundleKZero.classOf X E) = rationalTotalChernCharacter C sX E
declarations.comment: the remark as stated: the unique ring map K_0(Vect(X)) -> prod over i >= 0 of A^i(X) tensor Q sending [E] to ch(E), for every X locally of finite type over S, with no further hypothesis; the target is the ring Stacks.Chow.RationalTotalChowClass C sX (Cauchy product of the products A^i(X) x A^j(X) -> A^{i+j}(X) of Stacks 0B75, tensored with Q), ch(E) is Stacks.Chow.rationalTotalChernCharacter (components P_p(E)/p!, E of arbitrary rank), and the map is Stacks.Chow.rationalTotalChernCharacterRingHom; additivity is Stacks 0F9C and multiplicativity Stacks 0F9D, both proved

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chernClass_chernCharacter_secondAdams
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FEN.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL and let `X` be locally of
finite type over `S`. Let `ψ²`
be the second Adams operator of Stacks 0FEJ
(`AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundleKZero.secondAdamsRingHom` at
`AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundleKZero.squarePowersData X`), and let `c` and `ch` be the maps of
Stacks 0FEL and Stacks 0FEM (`Stacks.Chow.totalChernKGroupMap`, into `∏_{i ≥ 0} A^i(X)`, and
`Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterRingHom`, into `∏_{i ≥ 0} A^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐`). Then for every
`α ∈ K_0(Vect(X))` and every `i`

  `c_i(ψ²(α)) = 2^i c_i(α)`  and  `ch_i(ψ²(α)) = 2^i ch_i(α)`,

the subscript `i` being the component in `A^i(X)`, resp. `A^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐`.

Both maps are the genuine ones, and there is no hypothesis beyond the source's. In particular the
Chern character is that of Stacks 0FEM: `ch_p(α) = P_p(α)/p!`
(`Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterRingHom_apply`) with `P_0` the rank, so that `ch_0([ℰ])` is the rank
of `ℰ` (`Stacks.Chow.moduleChernCharacter_zero`, `Stacks.Chow.modulePowerSum_zero`); the case
`i = 0` of the second equation is the statement `rank(ψ²(α)) = rank(α)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernClass_chernCharacter_secondAdams (α : VectorBundleKZero X) (i : ℕ) :
    totalChernKGroupMap C sX
        (VectorBundleKZero.secondAdamsRingHom (VectorBundleKZero.squarePowersData X) α) i =
      (2 ^ i : ℤ) • totalChernKGroupMap C sX α i ∧
    chernCharacterRingHom C sX
        (VectorBundleKZero.secondAdamsRingHom (VectorBundleKZero.squarePowersData X) α) i =
      (2 ^ i : ℤ) • chernCharacterRingHom C sX α i
declarations.comment: both equations, c_i(ψ²(α)) = 2^i c_i(α) and ch_i(ψ²(α)) = 2^i ch_i(α) for every α ∈ K_0(Vect(X)), every i ≥ 0 and every X locally of finite type over S, with no further hypothesis: ψ² is AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundleKZero.secondAdamsRingHom (Stacks 0FEJ), c is Stacks.Chow.totalChernKGroupMap (Remark 0FEL) and ch is the ring map Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterRingHom (Remark 0FEM), whose degree-0 component is the rank

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterVectorBundle_secondAdams
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FEN, the second equation.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 42.7.1 and
let `X` be locally of finite type over `S`. For every `α ∈ K_0(Vect(X))` and every `p ≥ 0`,

  `ch_p(ψ²(α)) = 2^p ch_p(α)`   in `A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐`,

where `ψ²` is the second Adams operation of Stacks 0FEJ and `ch` the Chern character of
Stacks 0FEM.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernCharacterVectorBundle_secondAdams (a : VectorBundleKZero X) (p : ℕ) :
    chernCharacterVectorBundle C sX (secondAdamsRingHom (squarePowersData X) a) p =
      (2 ^ p : ℚ) • chernCharacterVectorBundle C sX a p
declarations.comment: the ch_i equation: ch_p(ψ²(α)) = 2^p ch_p(α), for every α ∈ K_0(Vect(X)) and every X locally of finite type over S, with no further hypothesis: ψ² is AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundleKZero.secondAdamsRingHom (Stacks 0FEJ) and ch is Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterVectorBundle (Stacks 0FEM), with values in A^p(X) ⊗ Q

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.totalChernKClass_secondAdams
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FEN, the first equation.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 42.7.1 and
let `X` be locally of finite type over `S`. For every `α ∈ K_0(Vect(X))` and every `i ≥ 0`,

  `c_i(ψ²(α)) = 2^i c_i(α)`   in `A^i(X)`,

where `ψ²` is the second Adams operation of Stacks 0FEJ and `c` the total Chern class of
Remark 0FEL (`Stacks.Chow.totalChernKClass`).
declarations.statement:
theorem totalChernKClass_secondAdams (a : VectorBundleKZero X) (i : ℕ) :
    totalChernKClass C sX (secondAdamsRingHom (squarePowersData X) a) i =
      (2 ^ i : ℤ) • totalChernKClass C sX a i
declarations.comment: the c_i equation: c_i(ψ²(α)) = 2^i c_i(α) in A^i(X), for every α ∈ K_0(Vect(X)) and every X locally of finite type over S, with no further hypothesis: ψ² is AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundleKZero.secondAdamsRingHom (Stacks 0FEJ) and c is the total Chern class map of Remark 0FEL, Stacks.Chow.totalChernKClass, constructed here for modules of arbitrary rank

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectEulerHom
declarations.doc:
The homomorphism `K_0(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X))`. Let `X` be a Noetherian regular
scheme and `Z ⊂ X` a closed subscheme. Taking the alternating sum of the cohomology sheaves of a
perfect complex supported on `Z` defines a homomorphism from the `K`-group of `D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X)`
to the Grothendieck group of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules supported on `Z`.
declarations.statement:
def supportedPerfectEulerHom :
    Pretriangulated.K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i) →+ KZero (SupportedCoherentModules i)
declarations.comment: the homomorphism K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X)). Two departures from the source, both recorded in the module docstring: the value on a class is the alternating sum ∑_n (-1)^n [H^n(E)] rather than [⊕_n H^{2n}(E)] - [⊕_n H^{2n+1}(E)] (the same element of K_0, but the identification of the two expressions is NOT proved here), and X is assumed Noetherian regular, the hypotheses of Stacks 0FER, rather than merely locally Noetherian, because the global coherence and boundedness of the cohomology sheaves used here come from the converse half of Stacks 0FDC. The identification K_0(Coh_Z(X)) = K'_0(Z) is Stacks 0FDT and is NOT covered

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectEulerHom_cls
declarations.doc:
The homomorphism `K_0(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X))` sends the
class of a perfect complex `E` supported on `Z` to the alternating sum `∑_n (-1)^n [H^n(E)]` of
the classes of its cohomology sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedPerfectEulerHom_cls (E : supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i) :
    supportedPerfectEulerHom i hX (Pretriangulated.K0.cls E) =
      eulerClass (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i) (SupportedCoherentModules i)
        (supportedPerfectHomology i hX) E
declarations.comment: the defining property of the homomorphism, in the alternating-sum form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SupportedCoherentModules
declarations.doc: The full subcategory of coherent sheaves supported on `Z`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev SupportedCoherentModules {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
declarations.comment: supported_coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedCoherentIsSerreClass
declarations.doc: Coherent sheaves supported on a closed subscheme form a Serre subcategory.
declarations.comment: supported_coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectEulerHom'
declarations.doc:
**The homomorphism `K_0(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X))` of [Stacks, Tag 0FEP]**, in the
unnested spelling of `Coh_Z(X)`: the alternating sum of the classes of the cohomology sheaves of a
perfect complex supported on `Z`.
declarations.comment: the homomorphism K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X)), with Coh_Z(X) spelled as a weak Serre subcategory of all O_X-modules. As for the nested spelling: the value on a class is the alternating sum ∑_n (-1)^n [H^n(E)] rather than the source's [⊕_n H^{2n}(E)] - [⊕_n H^{2n+1}(E)], the same element of K_0 but the identification of the two expressions is NOT proved; and X is Noetherian regular, the hypotheses of Stacks 0FER, rather than locally Noetherian. The identification K_0(Coh_Z(X)) = K'_0(Z) is Stacks 0FDT and is NOT covered

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectEulerHom'_cls
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FEP].** The homomorphism `K_0(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X))` sends the
class of a perfect complex supported on `Z` to the alternating sum of the classes of its cohomology
sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedPerfectEulerHom'_cls (E : supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i) :
    supportedPerfectEulerHom' i hX (Pretriangulated.K0.cls E) =
      eulerClass (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i)
        (coherentSupportedProperty i).FullSubcategory (supportedPerfectHomology' i hX) E
declarations.comment: the defining property of the homomorphism, in the alternating-sum form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectCohomologyHom
declarations.doc:
**The homomorphism `K_0(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X))` of [Stacks, Tag 0FEP].**
Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme and `Z ⊂ X` a closed subscheme. The rule
`E ↦ [⊕_{i ∈ ℤ} H^{2i}(E)] - [⊕_{i ∈ ℤ} H^{2i + 1}(E)]` is additive on distinguished triangles of
`D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X)`, hence defines a homomorphism of groups; its value on the class of `E` is
`supportedPerfectCohomologyHom_cls`.
declarations.comment: the homomorphism K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X)) for X locally Noetherian and Z ⊂ X a closed subscheme; its defining property is `supportedPerfectCohomologyHom_cls`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectCohomologyHom_cls
declarations.doc:
**The defining property of the homomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 0FEP].** The class of a perfect
complex `E` with cohomology sheaves supported on `Z` is sent to
`[⊕_{i ∈ ℤ} H^{2i}(E)] - [⊕_{i ∈ ℤ} H^{2i + 1}(E)]`, the direct sums being taken in the category
of `𝒪_X`-modules (`evenHomologySupported_obj_obj`, `oddHomologySupported_obj_obj`).
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedPerfectCohomologyHom_cls (E : supportedPerfectDerivedCategory.{u, d} i) :
    supportedPerfectCohomologyHom i (Pretriangulated.K0.cls E) =
      KZero.mk _ (evenHomologySupported i E) - KZero.mk _ (oddHomologySupported i E)
declarations.comment: the defining property: [E] ↦ [⊕_{i ∈ ℤ} H^{2i}(E)] - [⊕_{i ∈ ℤ} H^{2i+1}(E)], the direct sums taken in Mod(O_X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectCohomologyHomToCoherent
declarations.doc:
**The homomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 0FEP] with target `K'_0(Z) = K_0(Coh(𝒪_Z))`**, through
the identification `K_0(Coh(𝒪_Z)) ≅ K_0(Coh_Z(X))` of [Stacks, Tag 0FDT].
declarations.comment: the same homomorphism with target K'_0(Z) = K_0(Coh(Z)), through the identification K_0(Coh_Z(X)) = K'_0(Z) of Stacks 0FDT

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfect_isStrictlyFull_isTriangulated_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
**`D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X)` is a strictly full, saturated, triangulated subcategory of
`D(𝒪_X)`.** The perfect complexes of `𝒪_X`-modules whose cohomology sheaves are set-theoretically
supported on `Z` form a property of objects which is closed under isomorphisms, triangulated, and
stable under retracts, hence saturated (closed under direct summands).
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedPerfect_isStrictlyFull_isTriangulated_isSaturated :
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)) :=
      fun K => RingedSpace.IsPerfect K ∧
        ∀ n : ℤ, SheafOfModules.supp
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)
            n).obj K) ⊆ Set.range i.base
    P.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧ P.IsTriangulated ∧ P.IsStableUnderRetracts ∧
      P.IsSaturated
declarations.comment: D_{Z, perf}(O_X) is a strictly full, saturated, triangulated subcategory of D(O_X): closed under isomorphisms, triangulated, stable under retracts, hence saturated

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectCohomology.isCoherent_homology
declarations.doc: Every cohomology module of a perfect object on a locally Noetherian scheme is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_homology (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K) (n : ℤ) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace) n).obj K)
declarations.comment: locally_finite_cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectCohomology.locally_finite_homology
declarations.doc:
Near every point only finitely many cohomology modules of a perfect object have nonempty
support.
declarations.statement:
theorem locally_finite_homology (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K) (x : X) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧
      {n : ℤ | ∃ y : X, y ∈ U ∧ y ∈ SheafOfModules.supp
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace) n).obj K)}.Finite
declarations.comment: locally_finite_cohomology

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectDerivedCategory
registrations.comment: supported_perfect_complexes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentToSupportedPerfectHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FEQ.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of schemes with `X`
regular. There is a canonical homomorphism `K₀(Coh(𝒪_Z)) → K₀(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X))` taking the class
of a coherent `𝒪_Z`-module `ℱ` to the class of its direct image placed in degree zero.

The source is the Grothendieck group of the abelian category of coherent `𝒪_Z`-modules and the
target is the `K`-group of the triangulated category of perfect complexes on `X` supported on the
closed subset underlying `Z`. The map is well defined because the direct image of a short exact
sequence of coherent modules is short exact, hence gives a distinguished triangle of the three
degree-zero complexes.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentToSupportedPerfectHom_mk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FEQ.** The canonical homomorphism
`K₀(Coh(𝒪_Z)) → K₀(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X))` takes the class of a coherent `𝒪_Z`-module `ℱ` to the class
of the perfect complex `(i_*ℱ)[0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentToSupportedPerfectHom_mk
    (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules Z.ringCatSheaf) :
    coherentToSupportedPerfectHom i hX (KZero.mk _ F) =
      Pretriangulated.K0.cls (singlePushforwardSupportedPerfect i hX F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentToSupportedPerfectHomGeneral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FEQ.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of schemes with `X`
regular. There is a canonical homomorphism `K₀(Coh(𝒪_Z)) → K₀(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X))` taking the class
of a coherent `𝒪_Z`-module `ℱ` to the class of its direct image placed in degree zero.

The source is the Grothendieck group of the abelian category of coherent `𝒪_Z`-modules and the
target is the `K`-group of the triangulated category of perfect complexes on `X` supported on the
closed subset underlying `Z`. The map is well defined because the direct image of a short exact
sequence of coherent modules is short exact, hence gives a distinguished triangle of the three
degree-zero complexes.
declarations.statement:
def coherentToSupportedPerfectHomGeneral
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)] :
    KZero (Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules Z.ringCatSheaf) →+
      Pretriangulated.K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentToSupportedPerfectHomGeneral_mk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FEQ.** The canonical homomorphism
`K₀(Coh(𝒪_Z)) → K₀(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X))` takes the class of a coherent `𝒪_Z`-module `ℱ` to the class
of the perfect complex `(i_*ℱ)[0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentToSupportedPerfectHomGeneral_mk
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)]
    (F : Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules Z.ringCatSheaf) :
    coherentToSupportedPerfectHomGeneral i hX (KZero.mk _ F) =
      Pretriangulated.K0.cls (singlePushforwardSupportedPerfectGeneral i hX F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentToSupportedPerfectHom_mutuallyInverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FER.** Let `X` be a Noetherian regular scheme and `i : Z ⟶ X` a closed
immersion. The homomorphism `K'_0(Z) = K_0(Coh(𝒪_Z)) → K_0(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X))`,
`[ℱ] ↦ [(i_*ℱ)[0]]`, of [Stacks, Tag 0FEQ] and the homomorphism
`K_0(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X)) → K'_0(Z)`, `[E] ↦ [⊕_n H^{2n}(E)] - [⊕_n H^{2n+1}(E)]`, of
[Stacks, Tag 0FEP] are mutually inverse.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentToSupportedPerfectHom_mutuallyInverse :
    (supportedPerfectCohomologyHomToCoherent i).comp (coherentToSupportedPerfectHom i hX) =
        AddMonoidHom.id _ ∧
      (coherentToSupportedPerfectHom i hX).comp (supportedPerfectCohomologyHomToCoherent i) =
        AddMonoidHom.id _

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentKZeroEquivSupportedPerfectKZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FER**, as an isomorphism: `K'_0(Z) ≃+ K_0(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X))` for a
closed subscheme `Z` of a Noetherian regular scheme `X`, given by the mutually inverse
homomorphisms of [Stacks, Tag 0FEQ] and [Stacks, Tag 0FEP].
declarations.comment: the resulting identification K'_0(Z) = K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectEulerHom_comp_coherentToSupportedPerfectHom
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian regular scheme and `Z ⊂ X` a closed subscheme. The composite of
`coherentToSupportedPerfectHom : K_0(Coh(𝒪_Z)) → K_0(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X))` with
`supportedPerfectEulerHom : K_0(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X))` is the comparison
homomorphism `coherentToSupportedCoherentKZeroHom : K_0(Coh(𝒪_Z)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X))` of direct
image.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedPerfectEulerHom_comp_coherentToSupportedPerfectHom :
    (supportedPerfectEulerHom i hX).comp (coherentToSupportedPerfectHom i hX) =
      coherentToSupportedCoherentKZeroHom i
declarations.comment: the round trip K_0(Coh(Z)) → K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X)) is the comparison homomorphism of Stacks 0FDT, which is step (1) of the source's proof ('the composite is the identity'), stated without the 0FDT identification because that identification is not available. What is NOT covered: step (2), surjectivity of K_0(Coh(Z)) → K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X)), which the source gets from the truncation triangles together with the finite filtration of a coherent module supported on Z by O_Z-modules; and therefore NOT the conclusion that the two maps are mutually inverse

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectEulerHom'_comp_supportedCoherentToPerfectHom
declarations.doc:
**The first of the two inverse identities of [Stacks, Tag 0FER].** Taking the alternating sum
of the cohomology sheaves of a coherent module supported on `Z`, placed in degree zero, returns the
class of that module: the only nonvanishing cohomology sheaf is the module itself, in degree zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedPerfectEulerHom'_comp_supportedCoherentToPerfectHom :
    (supportedPerfectEulerHom' i hX).comp (supportedCoherentToPerfectHom i hX) =
      AddMonoidHom.id (KZero (coherentSupportedProperty i).FullSubcategory)
declarations.comment: the identity K_0(Coh_Z(X)) → K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X)); the identification K_0(Coh_Z(X)) = K'_0(Z) of Stacks 0FDT, under which this is the source's statement about K_0(Coh(Z)), is NOT covered

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedCoherentToPerfectHom_comp_supportedPerfectEulerHom'
declarations.doc:
**The two homomorphisms of [Stacks, Tag 0FEP] and [Stacks, Tag 0FEQ] are mutually inverse**, so
`K_0(Coh_Z(X)) = K_0(D_{Z, perf}(𝒪_X))`: the alternating sum of cohomology sheaves and the
placement of a coherent module supported on `Z` in degree zero compose to the identity in this
direction, and `supportedPerfectEulerHom'_comp_supportedCoherentToPerfectHom` is the other
direction.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedCoherentToPerfectHom_comp_supportedPerfectEulerHom' :
    (supportedCoherentToPerfectHom i hX).comp (supportedPerfectEulerHom' i hX) =
      AddMonoidHom.id (Pretriangulated.K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i))
declarations.comment: the identity K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X)) → K_0(Coh_Z(X)) → K_0(D_{Z, perf}(O_X)); with supportedPerfectEulerHom'_comp_supportedCoherentToPerfectHom this is the source's 'mutually inverse', EXCEPT that the source's left hand side is K'_0(Z) = K_0(Coh(Z)) and here it is K_0(Coh_Z(X)); the identification of the two is Stacks 0FDT and is NOT covered

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedChernClassKMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FES: the localized Chern class map**
`c(Z ⟶ X, -) : K₀(D_{Z,perf}(𝒪_X)) ⟶ A⁰(X) × ∏_{i ≥ 1} Aⁱ(Z ⟶ X)`, for `X` locally of finite type
over `S` with quasi-compact irreducible components (for instance `X` quasi-compact) and a closed
immersion `i : Z ⟶ X`: the homomorphism from `K₀(D_{Z,perf}(𝒪_X))`, written multiplicatively, to
the ring `A⁽¹⁾(Z ⟶ X)` with the product of Remark 0FA0, sending `[E]` to
`c(Z ⟶ X, E) = 1 + c₁(Z ⟶ X, E) + c₂(Z ⟶ X, E) + ⋯`
(`Stacks.Chow.localizedChernClassKMap_cls`), extended multiplicatively
(`Stacks.Chow.localizedChernClassKMap_add`). It is well defined by Lemma 0FBD
(`Stacks.Chow.supportedTotalLocalizedChern_triangle`).

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedChernClassKMap_cls
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0FES, the value on a generator**: `c(Z ⟶ X, [E]) = c(Z ⟶ X, E)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedChernClassKMap_cls (E : supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i) :
    localizedChernClassKMap C a hX (Multiplicative.ofAdd (K0.cls E)) =
      supportedTotalLocalizedChern C a hX E
declarations.comment: the value `c(Z → X, E) = 1 + c_1(Z → X, E) + ⋯` on a generator `[E]`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedChernClassKMap_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FES, multiplicativity**: `c(Z ⟶ X, α + β) = c(Z ⟶ X, α) c(Z ⟶ X, β)` in
`A⁽¹⁾(Z ⟶ X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedChernClassKMap_add (α β : K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i)) :
    localizedChernClassKMap C a hX (Multiplicative.ofAdd (α + β)) =
      localizedChernClassKMap C a hX (Multiplicative.ofAdd α) *
        localizedChernClassKMap C a hX (Multiplicative.ofAdd β)
declarations.comment: the map is extended multiplicatively: `c(Z → X, α + β) = c(Z → X, α) c(Z → X, β)`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedChernCharKMap
declarations.doc:
**The localized Chern character map of Stacks 0FET**
`ch(Z ⟶ X, -) : K₀(D_{Z,perf}(𝒪_X)) ⟶ ∏_{p ≥ 0} A^p(Z ⟶ X) ⊗ 𝐐`, for `X` with quasi-compact
irreducible components: `[E] ↦ ch(Z ⟶ X, E)`, extended additively. It is well defined because the
localized Chern character is additive along distinguished triangles (Lemma 0FBE,
`Stacks.Chow.supportedLocalizedChernChar_triangle`).
declarations.statement:
def localizedChernCharKMap :
    K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i) →+
      ∀ p : ℕ, TensorProduct ℤ ℚ (BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (i ≫ a) a i rfl
        (p : ℤ))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedChernCharKMap_cls
declarations.doc: The localized Chern character map on a class: `[E] ↦ ch(Z ⟶ X, E)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedChernCharKMap_cls (E : supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i) :
    localizedChernCharKMap C a hX (K0.cls E) = supportedLocalizedChernChar C a hX E
declarations.comment: localized_chern_character_k_map: the generator [E] is sent to ch(Z → X, E), and the map is the additive extension

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_localizedChernCharKMap_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
If `X` is quasi-compact, the localized Chern character map takes values in `A^*(Z ⟶ X) ⊗ 𝐐`:
every value has only finitely many nonzero components.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_localizedChernCharKMap_eq_zero (x : K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i)) :
    ∃ N, ∀ p ≥ N, localizedChernCharKMap C a hX x p = 0
declarations.comment: localized_chern_character_k_finite_support: for X quasi-compact the image lies in A^*(Z → X) ⊗ Q, every value having finitely many nonzero components

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedChernCharKMap_mul
declarations.doc:
**The localized Chern character map is multiplicative.** For `X` with quasi-compact
irreducible components and `α, β ∈ K₀(D_{Z,perf}(𝒪_X))`, multiplied by the derived tensor product
(Remark 0FDN),

  `ch(Z ⟶ X, α β) = ch(Z ⟶ X, α) ch(Z ⟶ X, β)`

in `∏_{p ≥ 0} A^p(Z ⟶ X) ⊗ 𝐐` (`Stacks.Chow.rationalSupportedProductMul`).
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedChernCharKMap_mul (x y : K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory i)) :
    localizedChernCharKMap C a hX (x * y) =
      rationalSupportedProductMul C a i (localizedChernCharKMap C a hX x)
        (localizedChernCharKMap C a hX y)
declarations.comment: localized_chern_character_k_multiplicative: ch(Z → X, αβ) = ch(Z → X, α) ch(Z → X, β), the product on K_0(D_{Z,perf}(O_X)) being derived tensor product (0FDN) and that on ∏ A^p(Z → X) ⊗ Q the Cauchy product of the products res(c) ∘ c' of 0FA0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectDerivedCategory_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEU.** Perfect objects of the derived category supported on the whole scheme are
exactly the perfect objects: `D_{X, perf}(O_X) = D_perf(O_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedPerfectDerivedCategory_id (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    supportedPerfectDerivedCategory (𝟙 X) = PerfectDerivedCategory X
declarations.comment: supported_perfect

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectKZeroEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEU.** The `K`-group of perfect complexes supported on the whole scheme is the
Grothendieck group `K_0(X) = K_0(D_perf(O_X))` of the scheme.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def supportedPerfectKZeroEquiv (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    Pretriangulated.K0 (supportedPerfectDerivedCategory (𝟙 X)) ≃+
      Pretriangulated.K0 (PerfectDerivedCategory X)
declarations.comment: k_group

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectKZeroEquiv_cls
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEU.** The identification of `K`-groups takes the class of a perfect complex
supported on the whole scheme to the class of the same complex in `K_0(D_perf(O_X))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedPerfectKZeroEquiv_cls (X : Scheme.{u})
    (K : supportedPerfectDerivedCategory (𝟙 X)) :
    supportedPerfectKZeroEquiv X (Pretriangulated.K0.cls K) =
      Pretriangulated.K0.cls (⟨K.obj, K.property.1⟩ : PerfectDerivedCategory X)
declarations.comment: k_group

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.perfectKZeroChernClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEU, the Chern class map `c : K_0(X) ⟶ ∏_{i ≥ 0} A^i(X)`**, sending `[E]` to the
total Chern class `c(E)` of Stacks 0F9E and sums to products.
declarations.statement: def perfectKZeroChernClass (α : K0 (PerfectDerivedCategory X)) : TotalChowClass C sX
declarations.comment: the map c : K_0(X) -> prod A^i(X), [E] |-> c(E) extended multiplicatively, built directly from Definition 0F9E and Lemma 0F9F as the remark allows; X has quasi-compact irreducible components

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.perfectKZeroChernCharacter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEU, the Chern character `ch : K_0(X) ⟶ ∏_{i ≥ 0} A^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐`**, additive and
sending `[E]` to `ch(E)`; well defined by Stacks 0F9F.
declarations.statement:
def perfectKZeroChernCharacter :
    K0 (PerfectDerivedCategory X) →+ fullRationalChowCohomology C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX
declarations.comment: the map ch : K_0(X) -> prod A^i(X) tensor Q, [E] |-> ch(E) extended additively, built directly from Definition 0F9E and Lemma 0F9F as the remark allows

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.perfectKZero_chernMaps_spec
declarations.statement:
theorem perfectKZero_chernMaps_spec :
    AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectDerivedCategory (𝟙 X) = PerfectDerivedCategory X ∧
    (∀ K : AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectDerivedCategory (𝟙 X),
      AlgebraicGeometry.supportedPerfectKZeroEquiv X (K0.cls K) =
        K0.cls (⟨K.obj, K.property.1⟩ : PerfectDerivedCategory X)) ∧
    (∀ (E : PerfectDerivedCategory X) (hE : HasDefinedChernClasses E.obj),
      perfectKZeroChernClass C sX hqc (K0.cls E) = perfectChernClass C sX hE) ∧
    (∀ α β : K0 (PerfectDerivedCategory X), perfectKZeroChernClass C sX hqc (α + β) =
      perfectKZeroChernClass C sX hqc α * perfectKZeroChernClass C sX hqc β) ∧
    (∀ (E : PerfectDerivedCategory X) (hE : HasDefinedChernClasses E.obj),
      perfectKZeroChernCharacter C sX hqc (K0.cls E) = perfectChernCharacter C sX hE) ∧
    (∀ α : VectorBundleKZero X, perfectKZeroChernClass C sX hqc (vectorBundleKZeroToPerfect X α) =
      totalChernKGroupMap C sX α) ∧
    (perfectKZeroChernCharacter C sX hqc).comp (vectorBundleKZeroToPerfect X) =
      (chernCharacterRingHom C sX).toAddMonoidHom
declarations.comment: the whole remark: D_{X,perf} = D_perf, K_0(D_{X,perf}) = K_0(X), the maps c and ch on K_0(X), and the commutativity of both triangles with K_0(Vect(X)) -> K_0(X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowToGradedCoherentKZero_injective
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `CH_k(X) ⊗ 𝐐 ⟶ gr_k K'₀(X) ⊗ 𝐐` is injective, for a homomorphism
`ch : K'₀(X) → CH_*(X) ⊗ 𝐐` such that the class of a coherent module whose support has
delta-dimension at most `j` has vanishing components in degrees above `j` (`hch_triangular`), and
the degree `k` component of a lift to `F_k K'₀(X)` of `cls k α` is `1 ⊗ α` (`hch_diagonal`).
declarations.statement:
theorem chowToGradedCoherentKZero_injective
    (ch : CoherentKZero X →+ DirectSum ℤ fun j => TensorProduct ℤ ℚ (chowGroup C f j))
    (hch_triangular : ∀ (j j' : ℤ) (F : CoherentModulesDimLE C f j), j < j' →
      ch (KZero.mk _ F.obj) j' = 0)
    (cls : ∀ j : ℤ, chowGroup C f j →+ gradedCoherentKZero C f j) (k : ℤ)
    (hch_diagonal : ∀ (α : chowGroup C f k) (x : coherentKZeroFiltration C f k),
      toGradedCoherentKZero C f k x = cls k α →
        ch (x : CoherentKZero X) k = (1 : ℚ) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] α) :
    Function.Injective
      (TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : ℚ →ₗ[ℤ] ℚ) (cls k).toIntLinearMap)
declarations.comment: injectivity of the canonical map `CH_k(X) ⊗ 𝐐 ⟶ gr_k K'₀(X) ⊗ 𝐐`; the composition `K'₀(X) → K₀(D_{X, perf}(𝒪_Y)) → A^*(X ⟶ Y) ⊗ 𝐐 → CH_*(X) ⊗ 𝐐`, the canonical maps of Lemma 42.23.4, and the two conditions (1) and (2) that the proof establishes for the composition and reduces the proposition to, are hypotheses: none of the three legs of the composition is constructed in this repository, `A^*` carrying no multiplication

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalCoherentKZeroToChowHomology_surjective
declarations.doc:
A homomorphism `ch : K'₀(X) → CH_*(X) ⊗ 𝐐` satisfying the conditions `hch_triangular` and
`hch_diagonal` of `Stacks.Chow.chowToGradedCoherentKZero_injective` (the latter in every degree)
becomes surjective after tensoring the source with `𝐐`, provided `δ_{X/S}` is bounded below.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalCoherentKZeroToChowHomology_surjective
    (ch : CoherentKZero X →+ DirectSum ℤ fun j => TensorProduct ℤ ℚ (chowGroup C f j))
    (hch_triangular : ∀ (j j' : ℤ) (F : CoherentModulesDimLE C f j), j < j' →
      ch (KZero.mk _ F.obj) j' = 0)
    (cls : ∀ j : ℤ, chowGroup C f j →+ gradedCoherentKZero C f j)
    (hch_diagonal : ∀ (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C f k) (x : coherentKZeroFiltration C f k),
      toGradedCoherentKZero C f k x = cls k α →
        ch (x : CoherentKZero X) k = (1 : ℚ) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] α)
    (lo : ℤ) (hlo : ∀ x : X, lo ≤ relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f x) :
    Function.Surjective (ch.toIntLinearMap.liftBaseChange ℚ)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of the composition `K'₀(X) ⊗ 𝐐 → CH_*(X) ⊗ 𝐐`; as for the injectivity statement in this file the composition, the canonical maps of Lemma 42.23.4 and the two conditions (1) and (2) that the proof establishes for the composition are hypotheses, none of the three legs of the composition being constructed in this repository; the injectivity of the composition is not proved, needing the surjectivity of the canonical maps and hence the unformalized half of Tag 02S9

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bijective_liftBaseChange_coherentChowCharacter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FEW.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL and let `i : X ⟶ Y` be a closed
immersion of schemes locally of finite type over `S`, with `Y` regular and quasi-compact. Then
the composition `K'₀(X) ⟶ K₀(D_{X, perf}(𝒪_Y)) ⟶ A^*(X ⟶ Y) ⊗ 𝐐 ⟶ CH_*(X) ⊗ 𝐐`,
`[ℱ] ↦ ch(X ⟶ Y, ℱ[0]) ∩ [Y]`, induces an isomorphism `K'₀(X) ⊗ 𝐐 ≅ CH_*(X) ⊗ 𝐐`; moreover the
canonical map `CH_k(X) ⊗ 𝐐 ⟶ gr_k K'₀(X) ⊗ 𝐐` is an isomorphism for every `k`.

Surjectivity and the "moreover" are conditions (1) and (2) of the source's proof
(`Stacks.Chow.surjective_liftBaseChange_coherentChowCharacter`,
`Stacks.Chow.bijective_rTensor_chowToGradedCoherentKZero_of_isClosedImmersion`); injectivity is
`Stacks.Chow.injective_liftBaseChange_coherentChowCharacter`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_liftBaseChange_coherentChowCharacter :
    haveI := isNoetherian_of_isClosedImmersion_of_compactSpace C a i
    Function.Bijective ((coherentChowCharacter C a i hY).toIntLinearMap.liftBaseChange ℚ) ∧
      ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : ℚ →ₗ[ℤ] ℚ)
        (chowToGradedCoherentKZero C (i ≫ a) k).toIntLinearMap)
declarations.comment: the whole proposition: the map K'_0(X) ⊗ Q → CH_*(X) ⊗ Q, [F] ↦ ch(X → Y, F[0]) ∩ [Y], is bijective, and CH_k(X) ⊗ Q → gr_k K'_0(X) ⊗ Q is bijective for every k, for a closed immersion X → Y of schemes locally of finite type over S with Y regular and quasi-compact, (S, δ) as in Situation 02QL

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalIntersectionProduct
declarations.doc:
**The intersection product of Stacks Section 0FEX** on `CH_*(X) ⊗ 𝐐`, for `X` Noetherian
(equivalently quasi-compact), regular, of finite type over `S`, with affine diagonal and `δ_{X/S}`
bounded: `α · β = ch(α') ∩ β`, where `α' ∈ K_0(Vect(X)) ⊗ 𝐐` is the unique class with
`ch(α') ∩ [X] = α` (Stacks 0FEY, `Stacks.Chow.bijective_flip_rationalChernCharacterCap`).
declarations.statement: def rationalIntersectionProduct : CHQ →ₗ[ℚ] CHQ →ₗ[ℚ] CHQ
declarations.comment: the construction of the section: for X as in 0FEY (Noetherian, equivalently quasi-compact, given locally of finite type over S), α · β = ch(α') ∩ β with α' the unique class with ch(α') ∩ [X] = α; CH^*(X) ⊗ Q is CH_*(X) ⊗ Q, the internal direct sum of the codimension pieces codimensionChowSubmodule

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalIntersectionProduct_comm
declarations.doc:
**The product is commutative** (Section 0FEX: "this is a symmetric pairing"), the operators
`ch(α') ∩ -` pairwise commuting.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalIntersectionProduct_comm (α β : CHQ) :
    rationalIntersectionProduct hX hb α β = rationalIntersectionProduct hX hb β α
declarations.comment: the product of the section is symmetric: α · β = β · α, for X as in 0FEY

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalIntersectionProduct_assoc
declarations.doc:
**The product is associative** (Section 0FEX): both bracketings of `α · β · γ` are
`ch(α') ∩ ch(β') ∩ ch(γ') ∩ [X]`, up to reordering the commuting operators.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalIntersectionProduct_assoc (α β γ : CHQ) :
    rationalIntersectionProduct hX hb (rationalIntersectionProduct hX hb α β) γ =
      rationalIntersectionProduct hX hb α (rationalIntersectionProduct hX hb β γ)
declarations.comment: the product of the section is associative: (α · β) · γ = α · (β · γ), for X as in 0FEY

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalIntersectionProduct_eq_rationalChernCharacterComponentCap
declarations.doc:
**The product of a class of codimension `i` is computed by `ch_i`** (Section 0FEX). If
`α = ch(α') ∩ [X]` lies in `CH^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐` then `α · β = ch_i(α') ∩ β`, the definition of the
source.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalIntersectionProduct_eq_rationalChernCharacterComponentCap
    {i : ℕ} {α : CHQ} (hα : α ∈ codimensionChowSubmodule C sX i)
    {a : ℚ ⊗[ℤ] VectorBundleKZero X}
    (ha : rationalChernCharacterCap C sX a (rationalFundamentalClass C sX) = α) (β : CHQ) :
    rationalIntersectionProduct hX hb α β = rationalChernCharacterComponentCap C sX i a β
declarations.comment: the defining formula of the section: for α ∈ CH^i(X) ⊗ Q with ch(α') ∩ [X] = α, α · β = ch(α') ∩ β = ch_i(α') ∩ β, for X as in 0FEY

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalIntersectionProduct_mem_codimensionChowSubmodule
declarations.doc:
**The product is graded by codimension** (Section 0FEX: `α · β ∈ CH^{i+j}(X) ⊗ 𝐐`):
`CH^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐 · CH^j(X) ⊗ 𝐐 ⊆ CH^{i+j}(X) ⊗ 𝐐`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalIntersectionProduct_mem_codimensionChowSubmodule
    {i j : ℕ} {α β : CHQ} (hα : α ∈ codimensionChowSubmodule C sX i)
    (hβ : β ∈ codimensionChowSubmodule C sX j) :
    rationalIntersectionProduct hX hb α β ∈ codimensionChowSubmodule C sX (i + j)
declarations.comment: the product of the section is graded: CH^i(X) ⊗ Q · CH^j(X) ⊗ Q ⊆ CH^{i+j}(X) ⊗ Q, for X as in 0FEY

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.existsUnique_rationalIntersectionProduct
declarations.doc:
For `X` as in Stacks 0FEY (Noetherian, equivalently quasi-compact, regular, of finite type over
`S`, with affine diagonal and `δ_{X/S}` bounded), `rationalIntersectionProduct` is the unique
bilinear product on `CH^*(X) ⊗ 𝐐 = CH_*(X) ⊗ 𝐐` which is commutative, associative, graded by the
codimension pieces `codimensionChowSubmodule`, and for which `α' ↦ ch(α') ∩ [X]` is multiplicative,
that is, an isomorphism of rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_rationalIntersectionProduct :
    ∃! μ : CHQ →ₗ[ℚ] CHQ →ₗ[ℚ] CHQ,
      (∀ a b, μ (rationalChernCharacterCap C sX a (rationalFundamentalClass C sX))
          (rationalChernCharacterCap C sX b (rationalFundamentalClass C sX)) =
        rationalChernCharacterCap C sX (a * b) (rationalFundamentalClass C sX)) ∧
      (∀ α β, μ α β = μ β α) ∧ (∀ α β γ, μ (μ α β) γ = μ α (μ β γ)) ∧
      ∀ {i j : ℕ} {α β : CHQ}, α ∈ codimensionChowSubmodule C sX i →
        β ∈ codimensionChowSubmodule C sX j → μ α β ∈ codimensionChowSubmodule C sX (i + j)
declarations.comment: the closing reformulation of the section: for X as in 0FEY, there is a unique commutative, associative intersection product on CH^*(X) ⊗ Q compatible with the grading such that K_0(Vect(X)) ⊗ Q → CH^*(X) ⊗ Q is a ring isomorphism, and it is the product of the section

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalChernCharacterAlgEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The map of Stacks 0FEY is an isomorphism of rings**: for `X` as in Stacks 0FEY,
`α' ↦ ch(α') ∩ [X]` is an isomorphism of `𝐐`-algebras from `K_0(Vect(X)) ⊗ 𝐐` onto the rational
Chow ring `CH^*(X) ⊗ 𝐐 = CH_*(X) ⊗ 𝐐` with the product `rationalIntersectionProduct`.
declarations.statement:
def rationalChernCharacterAlgEquiv :
    ℚ ⊗[ℤ] VectorBundleKZero X ≃ₐ[ℚ] RationalIntersectionRing hX hb
declarations.comment: the closing sentence of the section: for X as in 0FEY, K_0(Vect(X)) ⊗ Q → CH^*(X) ⊗ Q, α' ↦ ch(α') ∩ [X], is an isomorphism of rings for the product of the section

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalSecondAdams_eq_smul_of_rationalChernCharacterCap_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0FEX: the class answering to a cycle class of codimension `i` is a
`2^i`-eigenvector of `ψ²`.** Let `X` be as in Stacks 0FEY (Noetherian, equivalently quasi-compact,
regular, of finite type over `S`, with affine diagonal and `δ_{X/S}` bounded). If
`α ∈ CH^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐` and `α' ∈ K_0(Vect(X)) ⊗ 𝐐` is the (unique, by Stacks 0FEY) class with
`ch(α') ∩ [X] = α`, then `ψ²(α') = 2^i α'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalSecondAdams_eq_smul_of_rationalChernCharacterCap_mem (hX : IsRegular X)
    (hb : ∃ lo hi : ℤ, ∀ x : X, lo ≤ relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction sX x ∧
      relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction sX x ≤ hi)
    {i : ℕ} {a : ℚ ⊗[ℤ] VectorBundleKZero X}
    (ha : rationalChernCharacterCap C sX a (rationalFundamentalClass C sX) ∈
      codimensionChowSubmodule C sX i) :
    rationalSecondAdams X a = (2 ^ i : ℚ) • a
declarations.comment: the eigenvalue statement of the section: for X as in 0FEY, α ∈ CH^i(X) ⊗ Q and α' ∈ K_0(Vect(X)) ⊗ Q with ch(α') ∩ [X] = α, ψ²(α') = 2^i α', where ψ² is the second Adams operation of 0FEJ extended Q-linearly (Stacks.Chow.rationalSecondAdams); proved from 0FEN (Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterVectorBundle_secondAdams) and the uniqueness in 0FEY, as in the source

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalChernCharacterVectorBundle_eq_zero_of_rationalChernCharacterCap_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0FEX: the components of `ch(α')` off the codimension vanish.** For
`X` as in Stacks 0FEY, `α ∈ CH^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐` and `α' ∈ K_0(Vect(X)) ⊗ 𝐐` with `ch(α') ∩ [X] = α`, one
has `ch_j(α') = 0` in `A^j(X) ⊗ 𝐐` for every `j ≠ i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalChernCharacterVectorBundle_eq_zero_of_rationalChernCharacterCap_mem
    (hX : IsRegular X)
    (hb : ∃ lo hi : ℤ, ∀ x : X, lo ≤ relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction sX x ∧
      relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction sX x ≤ hi)
    {i : ℕ} {a : ℚ ⊗[ℤ] VectorBundleKZero X}
    (ha : rationalChernCharacterCap C sX a (rationalFundamentalClass C sX) ∈
      codimensionChowSubmodule C sX i) {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≠ i) :
    rationalChernCharacterVectorBundle C sX a j = 0
declarations.comment: the vanishing statement of the section: for X as in 0FEY, α ∈ CH^i(X) ⊗ Q and α' ∈ K_0(Vect(X)) ⊗ Q with ch(α') ∩ [X] = α, ch_j(α') = 0 in A^j(X) ⊗ Q for every j ≠ i, from ψ²(α') = 2^i α' and 0FEN, as in the source

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalChernCharacterComponentCap_rationalFundamentalClass_of_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0FEX: `ch_{i'}(α') ∩ [X] = 0` for `i' ≠ i` and
`ch_i(α') ∩ [X] = α`.** For `X` as in Stacks 0FEY, `α ∈ CH^i(X) ⊗ 𝐐` and
`α' ∈ K_0(Vect(X)) ⊗ 𝐐` with `ch(α') ∩ [X] = α`, the components of `ch(α')` other than the
`i`-th cap `[X]` to zero, and the `i`-th one caps `[X]` to `α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalChernCharacterComponentCap_rationalFundamentalClass_of_mem (hX : IsRegular X)
    (hb : ∃ lo hi : ℤ, ∀ x : X, lo ≤ relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction sX x ∧
      relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction sX x ≤ hi)
    {i : ℕ} {a : ℚ ⊗[ℤ] VectorBundleKZero X}
    (ha : rationalChernCharacterCap C sX a (rationalFundamentalClass C sX) ∈
      codimensionChowSubmodule C sX i) :
    (∀ j : ℕ, j ≠ i →
        rationalChernCharacterComponentCap C sX j a (rationalFundamentalClass C sX) = 0) ∧
      rationalChernCharacterComponentCap C sX i a (rationalFundamentalClass C sX) =
        rationalChernCharacterCap C sX a (rationalFundamentalClass C sX)
declarations.comment: the consequence the section draws from the vanishing statement: for X as in 0FEY, α ∈ CH^i(X) ⊗ Q and α' ∈ K_0(Vect(X)) ⊗ Q with ch(α') ∩ [X] = α, ch_{i'}(α') ∩ [X] = 0 for i' ≠ i and ch_i(α') ∩ [X] = α

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bijective_rationalChernCharacterCapFundamentalClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FEY.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 42.7.1 and let `X` be a
quasi-compact regular scheme of finite type over `S` with affine diagonal and `δ_{X/S}` bounded.
Then the composition

  `K_0(Vect(X)) ⊗ 𝐐 ⟶ ∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐 ⟶ CH_*(X) ⊗ 𝐐`,   `α ↦ ch(α) ∩ [X]`,

of the Chern character of Remark 0FEM and the map `c ↦ c ∩ [X]` is bijective.

The map is `Stacks.Chow.rationalChernCharacterCapFundamentalClass`, the sum over `p` of
`ch_p(α) ∩ [X]` (`Stacks.Chow.rationalChernCharacterCapFundamentalClass_eq_sum`). The proof is
`Stacks.Chow.bijective_rationalChernCharacterCapFundamentalClass_of_chernFormula` (Proposition 0FEW
for `X = Y`, Remark 0FEU) applied to Lemma 0FEG
(`Stacks.Chow.isRegularImmersionChernFormula_of_compactSpace`).
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_rationalChernCharacterCapFundamentalClass [CompactSpace X] (hX : IsRegular X)
    (hb : ∃ lo hi : ℤ, ∀ x : X, lo ≤ relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction sX x ∧
      relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction sX x ≤ hi) :
    haveI := isNoetherian_of_compactSpace sX
    Function.Bijective (rationalChernCharacterCapFundamentalClass C sX)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: for X quasi-compact, regular, of finite type over S, with affine diagonal and δ_{X/S} bounded, α ↦ ch(α) ∩ [X], K_0(Vect(X)) ⊗ Q → A^*(X) ⊗ Q → CH_*(X) ⊗ Q, is bijective; ch is the ring map of 0FEM into ∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ Q, whose cap with [X] is a finite sum since δ_{X/S} is bounded

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FF0, the geometric input of the second assertion.** The three normal bundles of a
pair of regular immersions `Z ⟶ Y ⟶ X` of locally Noetherian schemes form a conormal-compatible
triple in the sense of Stacks 0FEC: the sequence of their duals is the conormal sequence of
Stacks 062S conjugated by the three reflexivity isomorphisms, it is short exact by Stacks 063N,
and its two squares against the conormal sequence commute because the three structural
surjections are the inverses of those isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
def ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion :
    ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles i j
declarations.comment: second assertion: the three normal bundles of a pair of regular immersions satisfy the hypothesis of Stacks 0FEC, by the short exact conormal sequence of Stacks 063N

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedChernClass_cap_eq_bivariantCompositeCap_of_isRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FF0, second assertion, read on cap products.** For regular immersions
`i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` of schemes locally of finite type over the base, equipped with their
canonical normal bundles, the Gysin map of `j ∘ i` on a test scheme `t : T ⟶ X` is: cap with
`j^!`, then cap with `i^!`, then push forward along the associativity isomorphism
`(T ×_X Y) ×_Y Z ≅ T ×_X Z` of pullbacks.

This is Stacks 0FEC at the conormal-compatible triple of the two regular immersions, so the
composition formula for the three parameterized classes of Stacks 0FBK is an input, as it is in
the two theorems of Stacks 0FEC themselves.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedChernClass_cap_eq_bivariantCompositeCap_of_isRegularImmersion
    (hc : IsBivariantClassComposition C G sZ sY sX i j hsi hsj hpp p q
      (cloc sZ sY i hsi
        (ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion i j hi hj).bundleZY p)
      (cloc sY sX j hsj
        (ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion i j hi hj).bundleYX q)
      (cloc sZ sX (i ≫ j) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hsi hsj)
        (ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion i j hi hj).bundleZX (p + q)))
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (t : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType t] (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup C (t ≫ sX) k) :
    chowGroupDegreeEquiv C (pullback.fst (i ≫ j) t ≫ sZ)
        (by ring : k - (p + q) = (k - q) - p)
        ((cloc sZ sX (i ≫ j) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hsi hsj)
          (ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion i j hi hj).bundleZX
          (p + q)).cap t k α) =
      bivariantCompositeCap C G sZ sY sX i j hsi hsj hpp p q
        (cloc sZ sY i hsi
          (ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion i j hi hj).bundleZY p)
        (cloc sY sX j hsj
          (ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion i j hi hj).bundleYX q)
        t k α
declarations.comment: second assertion, (j ∘ i)^! = i^! ∘ j^! read on cap products, at the canonical normal bundles of the two regular immersions; the localized Chern class of Stacks 0FBK is a parameter and the composition formula of Stacks 0FEC is an input, exactly as in Stacks 0FEC

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedChernClass_eq_bivariantComposite_of_isRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FF0, second assertion, as an equality of bivariant classes.** For regular
immersions `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` of schemes locally of finite type over the base, equipped
with their canonical normal bundles, the Gysin class of `j ∘ i` is the composite of Stacks 0B75
of the Gysin class of `i` with the Gysin class of `j`:

  `(j ∘ i)^! = i^! ∘ j^!`   in `A^{p+q}(Z ⟶ X)`.

Both classes satisfy the composition formula of Stacks 0FEC — the composite by Stacks 0FE0 — and
that formula determines the class, so they agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedChernClass_eq_bivariantComposite_of_isRegularImmersion
    (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso)
    (hgysc : G.IsNaturalUnderPullbackCompPushforward)
    (hc : IsBivariantClassComposition C G sZ sY sX i j hsi hsj hpp p q
      (cloc sZ sY i hsi
        (ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion i j hi hj).bundleZY p)
      (cloc sY sX j hsj
        (ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion i j hi hj).bundleYX q)
      (cloc sZ sX (i ≫ j) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hsi hsj)
        (ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion i j hi hj).bundleZX
        (p + q))) :
    cloc sZ sX (i ≫ j) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hsi hsj)
        (ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion i j hi hj).bundleZX
        (p + q) =
      bivariantComposite C G sZ sY sX i j hsi hsj p q
        (cloc sZ sY i hsi
          (ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion i j hi hj).bundleZY p)
        (cloc sY sX j hsj
          (ConormalCompatibleVirtualNormalBundles.ofIsRegularImmersion i j hi hj).bundleYX q)
        hgys hgysc
declarations.comment: second assertion, (j ∘ i)^! = i^! ∘ j^! as an equality of bivariant classes, at the canonical normal bundles of the two regular immersions; the localized Chern class of Stacks 0FBK is a parameter and the composition formula of Stacks 0FEC is an input, exactly as in Stacks 0FEC

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedVirtualNormalGysinClassOfImmersion_comp_ofIsRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FF0.** Let `s : X ⟶ W` and `j : W ⟶ P` be regular immersions of schemes locally of
finite type over the base. Then `s ≫ j` is a regular immersion and

  `(j ∘ s)^! = s^! ∘ j^!`   in `A^*(X ⟶ P)^∧`,

where `(−)^!` is the class `c(− , 𝒩)` of Stacks 0FBQ (3) of the normal bundle `𝒩 = 𝒞^∨` of the
regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem completedVirtualNormalGysinClassOfImmersion_comp_ofIsRegularImmersion
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X W P : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (sW : W ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sW] (sP : P ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sP]
    (s : X ⟶ W) (j : W ⟶ P) [IsImmersion s] [IsImmersion j] (hs : s ≫ sW = sX)
    (hj : j ≫ sP = sW) (hsr : IsRegularImmersion s) (hjr : IsRegularImmersion j) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian W := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sW
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian P := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sP
    ∃ hr : IsRegularImmersion (s ≫ j),
      completedVirtualNormalGysinClassOfImmersion C sX sP (s ≫ j)
          (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hs hj)
          (VirtualNormalBundle.ofIsRegularImmersion (s ≫ j) hr) =
        completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible C sX sW sP s j hs hj
          (completedVirtualNormalGysinClassOfImmersion C sX sW s hs
            (VirtualNormalBundle.ofIsRegularImmersion s hsr))
          (completedVirtualNormalGysinClassOfImmersion C sW sP j hj
            (VirtualNormalBundle.ofIsRegularImmersion j hjr))

registrations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_comp
registrations.comment: first assertion: the composite of two regular immersions of schemes locally of finite type over the base is a regular immersion; local finite type over the base is not used, and the assertion is Stacks 067Q

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible_completedFlatPullbackOfSmooth_of_section
declarations.doc:
Let `p : P ⟶ X` be a smooth morphism of schemes locally of finite type over the base and
`s : X ⟶ P` a section of `p`, a regular immersion by
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_of_smooth_section`. Then

  `1 = s^! ∘ p^*` in `A^*(X)^∧`,

for `s^! = c(X ⟶ P, 𝒩_{X/P})` the class of Stacks 0FBQ (3) of the normal sheaf of `s` and `p^*`
the flat pullback of Stacks 0B78; the composite, a class for `s ≫ p`, is read as a class for
`𝟙 X = s ≫ p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible_completedFlatPullbackOfSmooth_of_section :
    letI : IsImmersion s := Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isImmersion_of_comp_eq_id s p hs
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian P := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sP
    completedBivariantGroup.copy C hs
        (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq (comp_structureMorphism_of_comp_eq_id hp hs) hp)
        (Category.id_comp sX)
        (completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible C sX sP sX s p
          (comp_structureMorphism_of_comp_eq_id hp hs) hp
          (completedVirtualNormalGysinClassOfImmersion C sX sP s
            (comp_structureMorphism_of_comp_eq_id hp hs)
            (VirtualNormalBundle.ofIsRegularImmersion s
              (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_of_smooth_section p s hs)))
          (completedFlatPullbackOfSmooth C sP sX p hp)) =
      completedIdentityClass C sX
