Correspondences form a graded category over `ℚ` in the sense of Definition 09L2: the morphism
module `⨁ᵣ Corrʳ(X, Y)` is the direct sum of its homogeneous pieces `Corrʳ(X, Y)`, the
identity — the diagonal class — is homogeneous of degree zero, and composing correspondences of
degrees `r` and `s` gives one of degree `r + s`.
declarations.statement: instance gradedCategory : GradedCategory ℚ D.Obj
declarations.comment: correspondences form a graded category over Q

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.canonicalGraphFunctor
declarations.doc:
The contravariant functor from smooth projective schemes over `k` to the category of
correspondences which is the identity on objects and sends `f : X ⟶ Y` to the class
`[Γ_f] ∈ Corr⁰(Y, X)` of its graph.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalGraphFunctor :
    ((SmoothProjectiveScheme k).FullSubcategory)ᵒᵖ ⥤
      (canonicalCorrespondenceCompositionData k).Obj

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.GradedCompositionData.PushforwardData.graphFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG3.** The contravariant functor from the ambient category — in the
source the smooth projective schemes over `k` — to the category of correspondences which is the
identity on objects and sends `f : Y ⟶ X` to the class `[Γ_f] ∈ Corr⁰(X, Y)` of its graph.

Keyed: the functor, its two laws and the identity on objects are all proved. The carried input
is the composition of correspondences of `Stacks.WeilCohomology.GradedCompositionData`, as for
Stacks 0FG2, together with proper pushforward of correspondences along `u ×ₛ 𝟙` and its
compatibilities in `Stacks.WeilCohomology.GradedCompositionData.PushforwardData` — Stacks 02RW,
02S2, the three-projection formula of Stacks 0FG0 and the projection formula of Stacks 0FFC.
No carried field refers to graphs. See the implementation notes of the file.
declarations.statement: def graphFunctor : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D.Obj
declarations.comment: the contravariant functor f ↦ [graph f] to correspondences, identity on objects

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.cycleTranspose
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG4.** Transposition of cycles on a fibre product: proper pushforward
along the factor switch `X ×_S Y ≅ Y ×_S X`.
declarations.statement:
def cycleTranspose (n : ℤ) :
    CycleGroup C (pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX) n →+ CycleGroup C (pullback.fst sY sX ≫ sY) n
declarations.comment: transpose

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.chowTranspose
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG4.** Transposition of Chow classes on a fibre product, induced by
transposition of cycles. The factor switch is an isomorphism, so this needs no instance of
Stacks 02S2.
declarations.statement:
def chowTranspose (n : ℤ) :
    chowGroup C (pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX) n →+ chowGroup C (pullback.fst sY sX ≫ sY) n
declarations.comment: transpose

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.cycleTransposeEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG4.** Transposition of cycles on a fibre product is an isomorphism
of groups of `n`-cycles, with inverse the transposition in the other direction.
declarations.statement:
def cycleTransposeEquiv (n : ℤ) :
    CycleGroup C (pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX) n ≃+ CycleGroup C (pullback.fst sY sX ≫ sY) n
declarations.comment: the transpose is an isomorphism, on cycles

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.chowTransposeEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG4.** Transposition of Chow classes on a fibre product is an
isomorphism of Chow groups, with inverse the transposition in the other direction.
declarations.statement:
def chowTransposeEquiv (n : ℤ) :
    chowGroup C (pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX) n ≃+ chowGroup C (pullback.fst sY sX ≫ sY) n
declarations.comment: the transpose is an isomorphism, on cycle classes

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.transpose
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG4.** The transpose `c ↦ cᵗ` of a rational correspondence. For `X`
equidimensional of dimension `d` and `Y` equidimensional of dimension `e` it maps
`Corrʳ(X, Y)` to `Corr^{d - e + r}(Y, X)`.
declarations.statement:
def transpose (d e r : ℤ) :
    Correspondence C sX sY e r →ₗ[ℤ] Correspondence C sY sX d (d - e + r)
declarations.comment: transpose

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.transposeEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG4.** For `X` equidimensional of dimension `d` and `Y`
equidimensional of dimension `e`, the factor switch `X ×_S Y ≅ Y ×_S X` determines an
*isomorphism*

  `Corrʳ(X, Y) ≃ Corr^{d - e + r}(Y, X)`, `c ↦ cᵗ`,

the transpose, with inverse the transpose in the other direction.
declarations.statement:
def transposeEquiv (d e r : ℤ) :
    Correspondence C sX sY e r ≃ₗ[ℚ] Correspondence C sY sX d (d - e + r)
declarations.comment: the transpose is an isomorphism Corr^r(X, Y) = Corr^{d - e + r}(Y, X)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.cycleTranspose_graph
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG4.** Transposing the cycle of the graph of `f : Y ⟶ X` gives the
cycle of the transposed graph.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleTranspose_graph (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : f ≫ sX = sY) (k : ℤ) :
    cycleTranspose C sX sY k
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C (pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX)
          (graphMorphism sX sY f hf).imageι k) =
      cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C (pullback.fst sY sX ≫ sY)
        (graphMorphism sX sY f hf ≫ (pullbackSymmetry sX sY).hom).imageι k
declarations.comment: transpose_graph

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.transpose_graph
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG4.** The transpose of the rational correspondence of the graph of
`f : Y ⟶ X` is the rational correspondence of the transposed graph: `[Γ_f]ᵗ = [Γ_fᵗ]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem transpose_graph (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : f ≫ sX = sY) (d e r : ℤ) (q : ℚ) :
    transpose C sX sY d e r (q ⊗ₜ[ℤ] QuotientAddGroup.mk
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C (pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX)
          (graphMorphism sX sY f hf).imageι (e - r))) =
      q ⊗ₜ[ℤ] chowGroupDegreeEquiv C (pullback.fst sY sX ≫ sY)
        (show e - r = d - (d - e + r) by omega)
        (QuotientAddGroup.mk (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C (pullback.fst sY sX ≫ sY)
          (graphMorphism sX sY f hf ≫ (pullbackSymmetry sX sY).hom).imageι (e - r)))
declarations.comment: transpose_graph

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.pullback_graphCorrespondenceSP
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG5 (2).** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of smooth projective
schemes over `k` and `[Γ_f] ∈ Corr⁰(X, Y)` its graph (Example 0FG1). Pullback of cycles by the
correspondence `[Γ_f]`, `β ↦ pr₁,*([Γ_f] · pr₂^*β)`, agrees with proper pushforward
`f_* : CH_m(Y) ⊗ ℚ ⟶ CH_m(X) ⊗ ℚ`, in every dimension `m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullback_graphCorrespondenceSP (m : ℤ) :
    haveI := isProper_of_comp_eq X.obj.hom Y.obj.hom (Over.w f.hom)
    pullback k X.obj.hom Y.obj.hom (canonicalDiagonalClassFamily k) 0 m
        (SmoothProjectiveCorr.toCorr X Y 0 (graphCorrespondenceSP f)) =
      ((chowGroupDegreeEquiv (fieldChowSituation k) X.obj.hom (sub_zero m).symm).toAddMonoidHom.comp
        (properChowPushforward (fieldChowSituation k) Y.obj.hom X.obj.hom f.hom.left
          (Over.w f.hom) m
          (properPushforwardDescends _ _ _ _ _ _))).toIntLinearMap.baseChange ℚ
declarations.comment: (2): pullback of cycles by the correspondence [Γ_f] agrees with the pushforward f_* : CH_*(Y) → CH_*(X), in every dimension, with rational coefficients

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.pullback_transposeGraphCorrespondenceSP
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG5 (3)(b).** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of smooth projective
schemes over `k`, with `X` and `Y` equidimensional of dimensions `d` and `e`. Pullback of cycles
by the transposed graph `[Γ_f]ᵗ ∈ Corr^{d-e}(Y, X)` of Remark 0FG4,
`β ↦ pr₁,*([Γ_f]ᵗ · pr₂^*β)`, agrees with the Gysin map
`f^! : CH_m(X) ⊗ ℚ ⟶ CH_{m-(d-e)}(Y) ⊗ ℚ` of Stacks 0FF3, in every dimension `m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullback_transposeGraphCorrespondenceSP {d e : ℕ} (hX : RelativeDimension X.obj.hom d)
    (hY : RelativeDimension Y.obj.hom e) (m : ℤ) :
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_comp_eq (Over.w f.hom)
    pullback k Y.obj.hom X.obj.hom (canonicalDiagonalClassFamily k) ((d : ℤ) - e) m
        (SmoothProjectiveCorr.toCorr Y X _ (transposeGraphCorrespondenceSP f d e)) =
      (smoothGysinChow (fieldChowSituation k) Y.obj.hom X.obj.hom (Over.w f.hom) ((d : ℤ) - e)
        m).toIntLinearMap.baseChange ℚ
declarations.comment: (3)(b): for X and Y equidimensional of dimensions d and e, pullback of cycles by the transposed graph [Γ_f]ᵗ ∈ Corr^{d-e}(Y, X) of Remark 0FG4 agrees with the Gysin map f^!, in every dimension, with rational coefficients

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.pushforward_transposeGraphCorrespondenceSP
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG5 (3)(a).** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of smooth projective
schemes over `k`, with `X` and `Y` equidimensional of dimensions `d` and `e`. Pushforward of
cycles by the transposed graph `[Γ_f]ᵗ ∈ Corr^{d-e}(Y, X)` of Remark 0FG4,
`α ↦ pr₂,*([Γ_f]ᵗ · pr₁^*α)`, corresponds to pushforward of cycles by `f`,
`f_* : CH^i(Y) = CH_{e-i}(Y) ⟶ CH_{e-i}(X) = CH^{i+d-e}(X)`, on `CH^i(Y) ⊗ ℚ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforward_transposeGraphCorrespondenceSP {d e : ℕ}
    (hX : RelativeDimension X.obj.hom d) (hY : RelativeDimension Y.obj.hom e) (i : ℤ) :
    haveI : CompactSpace X.obj.left := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace X.obj.hom
    haveI : CompactSpace Y.obj.left := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace Y.obj.hom
    pushforward k Y.obj.hom X.obj.hom (canonicalDiagonalClassFamily k) ((d : ℤ) - e) i
        (SmoothProjectiveCorr.toCorr Y X _ (transposeGraphCorrespondenceSP f d e)) ∘ₗ
        rationalCodimensionToCodimChow k Y.obj.hom i =
      rationalCodimensionToCodimChow k X.obj.hom (i + ((d : ℤ) - e)) ∘ₗ
        (equidimensionalPushforward f e d i (i + ((d : ℤ) - e)) (by ring)).toIntLinearMap.baseChange
          ℚ
declarations.comment: (3)(a): for X and Y equidimensional of dimensions d and e, pushforward of cycles by the transposed graph [Γ_f]ᵗ ∈ Corr^{d-e}(Y, X) of Remark 0FG4 corresponds to pushforward of cycles by f, on CH^i(Y) ⊗ Q for every i

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.pushforward_graphCorrespondenceSP
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG5 (1).** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of smooth projective
schemes over `k` and `[Γ_f] ∈ Corr⁰(X, Y)` its graph (Example 0FG1). Pushforward of cycles by
the correspondence `[Γ_f]`, `α ↦ pr₂,*([Γ_f] · pr₁^*α)`, agrees with the Gysin map
`f^! : CH^i(X) ⟶ CH^i(Y)` of Stacks 0FF3, on `CH^i(X) ⊗ ℚ` for every `i`. The schemes need not be
equidimensional: `CH^i(X) = ∏_d CH_{d-i}(X_d)` is graded by codimension on the parts `X_d` of
constant dimension.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforward_graphCorrespondenceSP (i : ℤ) :
    haveI : CompactSpace X.obj.left := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace X.obj.hom
    haveI : CompactSpace Y.obj.left := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace Y.obj.hom
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_comp_eq (Over.w f.hom)
    pushforward k X.obj.hom Y.obj.hom (canonicalDiagonalClassFamily k) 0 i
        (SmoothProjectiveCorr.toCorr X Y 0 (graphCorrespondenceSP f)) ∘ₗ
        rationalCodimensionToCodimChow k X.obj.hom i =
      (codimChowCongr k Y.obj.hom (add_zero i).symm).toLinearMap ∘ₗ
        rationalCodimensionToCodimChow k Y.obj.hom i ∘ₗ
          (codimensionGysin Y.obj.hom X.obj.hom (Over.w f.hom) i).toIntLinearMap.baseChange ℚ
declarations.comment: (1): pushforward of cycles by the correspondence [Γ_f] agrees with the Gysin map f^! : CH^*(X) → CH^*(Y), on CH^i(X) ⊗ Q for every i, X and Y not necessarily equidimensional

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.projectiveLineCorrEquiv
declarations.doc:
`Corr⁰(P¹_k, P¹_k) = CH¹(P¹ × P¹) ⊗ ℚ = CH₁(P¹ × P¹) ⊗ ℚ`: a correspondence of degree zero
on the projective line is a rational cycle class of dimension one on `P¹_k ×_k P¹_k`.
declarations.comment: Corr⁰(X, X) = CH¹(X × X) ⊗ ℚ = CH₁(X × X) ⊗ ℚ

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.projectiveLineCorrBasis
declarations.doc: A basis of `Corr⁰(P¹_k, P¹_k)` over `ℚ`, formed by `c₀ = [x × P¹]` and `c₂ = [P¹ × x]`.
declarations.statement:
def projectiveLineCorrBasis :
    Module.Basis (Fin 2) ℚ (SmoothProjectiveCorr (projectiveLineObj k) (projectiveLineObj k) 0)
declarations.comment: c₀ and c₂ are a basis of Corr⁰(X, X)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.projectiveLinePointFibreCorr
declarations.doc: The correspondence `c₀ = [x × P¹] ∈ Corr⁰(P¹_k, P¹_k)` of a rational point `x`.
declarations.statement:
def projectiveLinePointFibreCorr :
    SmoothProjectiveCorr (projectiveLineObj k) (projectiveLineObj k) 0
declarations.comment: c₀ = [x × X]

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.projectiveLineFibrePointCorr
declarations.doc: The correspondence `c₂ = [P¹ × x] ∈ Corr⁰(P¹_k, P¹_k)` of a rational point `x`.
declarations.statement:
def projectiveLineFibrePointCorr :
    SmoothProjectiveCorr (projectiveLineObj k) (projectiveLineObj k) 0
declarations.comment: c₂ = [X × x]

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.projectiveLine_diagonal_eq_add
declarations.doc: `1 = [Δ] = c₀ + c₂` in `Corr⁰(P¹_k, P¹_k)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveLine_diagonal_eq_add :
    (canonicalCorrespondenceCompositionData k).diagonal (projectiveLineObj k) =
      projectiveLinePointFibreCorr x hx + projectiveLineFibrePointCorr x hx
declarations.comment: 1 = [Δ] = c₀ + c₂

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.projectiveLine_pointFibre_comp_pointFibre
declarations.doc: `c₀ ∘ c₀ = c₀` in the category of correspondences.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveLine_pointFibre_comp_pointFibre :
    projectiveLinePointFibreHom x hx ≫ projectiveLinePointFibreHom x hx =
      projectiveLinePointFibreHom x hx
declarations.comment: c₀ ∘ c₀ = c₀

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.projectiveLine_fibrePoint_comp_pointFibre
declarations.doc: `c₀ ∘ c₂ = 0` in the category of correspondences.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveLine_fibrePoint_comp_pointFibre :
    projectiveLineFibrePointHom x hx ≫ projectiveLinePointFibreHom x hx = 0
declarations.comment: c₀ ∘ c₂ = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.projectiveLine_pointFibre_comp_fibrePoint
declarations.doc: `c₂ ∘ c₀ = 0` in the category of correspondences.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveLine_pointFibre_comp_fibrePoint :
    projectiveLinePointFibreHom x hx ≫ projectiveLineFibrePointHom x hx = 0
declarations.comment: c₂ ∘ c₀ = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.projectiveLine_fibrePoint_comp_fibrePoint
declarations.doc: `c₂ ∘ c₂ = c₂` in the category of correspondences.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveLine_fibrePoint_comp_fibrePoint :
    projectiveLineFibrePointHom x hx ≫ projectiveLineFibrePointHom x hx =
      projectiveLineFibrePointHom x hx
declarations.comment: c₂ ∘ c₂ = c₂

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.projectiveLineCorrAlgEquiv
declarations.doc:
`Corr⁰(P¹_k, P¹_k) = ℚ × ℚ` as a `ℚ`-algebra: the degree-zero endomorphisms of `P¹_k` in the
category of correspondences, with composition as multiplication, are the product algebra, via
`(a, b) ↦ a c₀ + b c₂`.
declarations.statement: def projectiveLineCorrAlgEquiv : (ℚ × ℚ) ≃ₐ[ℚ] degreeZeroSubalgebra (R := ℚ) 𝐗
declarations.comment: Corr⁰(X, X) = ℚ × ℚ as a ℚ-algebra

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.mul_self_of_add_eq_one
declarations.doc:
The complement of an idempotent is idempotent: from `[Δ] = c₀ + c₂` and `c₀ ∘ c₀ = c₀`
follows `c₂ ∘ c₂ = c₂`.
declarations.statement: theorem mul_self_of_add_eq_one (hsum : c₀ + c₂ = 1) (h₀ : c₀ * c₀ = c₀) : c₂ * c₂ = c₂
declarations.comment: c₂ ∘ c₂ = c₂

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.mul_eq_zero_of_add_eq_one
declarations.doc:
An idempotent and its complement are orthogonal: from `[Δ] = c₀ + c₂` and `c₀ ∘ c₀ = c₀`
follows `c₀ ∘ c₂ = 0`.
declarations.statement: theorem mul_eq_zero_of_add_eq_one (hsum : c₀ + c₂ = 1) (h₀ : c₀ * c₀ = c₀) : c₀ * c₂ = 0
declarations.comment: c₀ ∘ c₂ = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.mul_eq_zero_of_add_eq_one'
declarations.doc:
An idempotent and its complement are orthogonal in the other order too: from
`[Δ] = c₀ + c₂` and `c₀ ∘ c₀ = c₀` follows `c₂ ∘ c₀ = 0`.
declarations.statement: theorem mul_eq_zero_of_add_eq_one' (hsum : c₀ + c₂ = 1) (h₀ : c₀ * c₀ = c₀) : c₂ * c₀ = 0
declarations.comment: c₂ ∘ c₀ = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.algEquivProdOfBasisOfAddEqOne
declarations.doc:
An algebra with a two-element basis `c₀`, `c₂` whose sum is the identity and whose first
member is idempotent is the product algebra `R × R`: the two basis elements are orthogonal
idempotents, so multiplication is coordinatewise. For the projective line this is
`Corr⁰(P¹, P¹) = ℚ × ℚ`, with `c₀ = [x × P¹]` and `c₂ = [P¹ × x]`.
declarations.statement:
def algEquivProdOfBasisOfAddEqOne (b : Module.Basis (Fin 2) R A) (hsum : b 0 + b 1 = 1)
    (h₀ : b 0 * b 0 = b 0) : (R × R) ≃ₐ[R] A
declarations.comment: Corr⁰(X, X) = ℚ × ℚ as a ℚ-algebra

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.pointFibreCorrespondence
declarations.doc:
The degree-zero correspondence `c₀ = [x × X]` attached to a section `x` of `sX`, for a source
equidimensional of dimension `d`: the rational class of the fibre `x × X ⊆ X ×_S X`, which is the
graph of the constant morphism of `X` through `x`.
declarations.statement: def pointFibreCorrespondence (d : ℤ) : Correspondence C sX sX d 0
declarations.comment: c₀ = [x × X]

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.fibrePointCorrespondence
declarations.doc:
The degree-zero correspondence `c₂ = [X × x]` attached to a section `x` of `sX`: the rational
class of the fibre `X × x ⊆ X ×_S X`, the factor switch of `x × X`.
declarations.statement: def fibrePointCorrespondence (d : ℤ) : Correspondence C sX sX d 0
declarations.comment: c₂ = [X × x]

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.cycleTranspose_pointFibre
declarations.doc:
The fibre `X × x` is the transpose of the fibre `x × X`: transposing the cycle of the one gives
the cycle of the other.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleTranspose_pointFibre (k : ℤ) :
    cycleTranspose C sX sX k
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C (pullback.fst sX sX ≫ sX)
          (graphMorphism sX sX (sX ≫ x) (constantMorphism_comp_base sX x hx)).imageι k) =
      cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C (pullback.fst sX sX ≫ sX)
        (graphMorphism sX sX (sX ≫ x) (constantMorphism_comp_base sX x hx) ≫
          (pullbackSymmetry sX sX).hom).imageι k
declarations.comment: [X × x] is the transpose of [x × X]

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.correspondence_zero_eq
declarations.doc:
For a source equidimensional of dimension one, such as the projective line, the degree-zero
correspondences are the rational dimension-one Chow classes of the square,
`Corr⁰(X, X) = CH₁(X × X) ⊗ ℚ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem correspondence_zero_eq :
    Correspondence C sX sX 1 0 =
      TensorProduct ℤ ℚ (chowGroup C (pullback.fst sX sX ≫ sX) 1)
declarations.comment: Corr⁰(X, X) = CH₁(X × X) ⊗ ℚ

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceCategory.monoidalCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG7** (monoidal structure). The tensor product of correspondences
`c ⊗ c' = pr₁₃^* c · pr₂₄^* c'` turns the category of correspondences between smooth projective
schemes over `k` (Stacks 0FG2) into a monoidal category, with `X ⊗ Y = X × Y`, unit `Spec k`, and
as associativity constraint the usual associativity constraint of products of schemes (taken
through the graph functor of Stacks 0FG3).
declarations.statement: instance monoidalCategory : MonoidalCategory (CorrespondenceCategory k)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceCategory.symmetricCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG7.** The tensor product of correspondences
`c ⊗ c' = pr₁₃^* c · pr₂₄^* c'` turns the category of correspondences between smooth projective
schemes over `k` (Stacks 0FG2) into a symmetric monoidal category with unit `Spec k`: the
associativity constraint is the usual associativity constraint on products of schemes and the
commutativity constraint is the isomorphism `X × Y ⟶ Y × X` switching the factors, both taken
through the graph functor of Stacks 0FG3.
declarations.statement: instance symmetricCategory : SymmetricCategory (CorrespondenceCategory k)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.monoidalCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG7.** The exterior product of correspondences makes the category of
correspondences monoidal. The pentagon and the triangle hold because every morphism they
involve is a graph, so both sides are the graph of the corresponding composite in `C`.
declarations.statement: instance monoidalCategory : MonoidalCategory S.Obj
declarations.comment: the category of correspondences is monoidal for the exterior product

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.symmetricCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG7.** The exterior product of correspondences makes the category of
correspondences symmetric monoidal with unit `Spec(k)`: the commutativity constraint is the
graph of the factor switch, which is an involution.
declarations.statement: instance symmetricCategory : SymmetricCategory S.Obj
declarations.comment: the category of correspondences is symmetric monoidal with unit Spec(k)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.graph_tensor_diagonal_fundamental_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FG8.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of smooth projective schemes over
`k`, with `X` and `Y` equidimensional of dimensions `d` and `e`. Let `a = [Γ_f] ∈ Corr⁰(X, Y)`,
`aᵗ = [Γ_fᵗ] ∈ Corr^{d-e}(Y, X)`, `η_X = [Γ_{X → X × X}] ∈ Corr⁰(X × X, X)`,
`η_Y = [Γ_{Y → Y × Y}] ∈ Corr⁰(Y × Y, Y)`, and let `[X] ∈ Corr^{-d}(X, Spec k)` and
`[Y] ∈ Corr^{-e}(Y, Spec k)` be the fundamental classes. Then the diagram

  `X ⊗ Y --(a ⊗ 1)--> Y ⊗ Y --η_Y--> Y --[Y]--> Spec k`,
  `X ⊗ Y --(1 ⊗ aᵗ)--> X ⊗ X --η_X--> X --[X]--> Spec k`

commutes in the category of correspondences. Here `⊗` on morphisms is the tensor product of
correspondences `c ⊗ c' = pr₁₃^* c · pr₂₄^* c'`,
`Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceCategory.tensorHom`, which is the tensor product of morphisms
of the symmetric monoidal structure of Stacks 0FG7 (`CorrespondenceCategory.tensorHom_eq` in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.WeilCohomology.Concrete.CorrespondenceMonoidal`).
declarations.statement:
theorem graph_tensor_diagonal_fundamental_comm (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    CorrespondenceCategory.tensorHom (graphHom f : (GradedCompositionData.Obj.mk X :
        CorrespondenceCategory k) ⟶ GradedCompositionData.Obj.mk Y)
        (𝟙 (GradedCompositionData.Obj.mk Y : CorrespondenceCategory k)) ≫
        diagonalGraphHom Y ≫ fundamentalClassHom hY =
      CorrespondenceCategory.tensorHom (𝟙 (GradedCompositionData.Obj.mk X :
          CorrespondenceCategory k)) (transposeGraphHom f d e) ≫
        diagonalGraphHom X ≫ fundamentalClassHom hX

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat
declarations.doc:
The category `M_k` of Chow motives over `k`. An object is a triple `(X, p, m)` of a smooth
projective scheme `X` over `k`, a projector `p ∈ Corr⁰(X, X)` (`p ∘ p = p`) and a twist `m ∈ ℤ`;
a morphism `(X, p, m) ⟶ (Y, q, n)` is a correspondence in `q ∘ Corr^{n-m}(X, Y) ∘ p`, and
composition is composition of correspondences.
declarations.statement: abbrev ChowMotiveCat : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the category M_k of Chow motives (X, p, m) over k

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.homEquiv
declarations.doc:
The morphisms of `M_k` from `(X, p, m)` to `(Y, q, n)` are the correspondences in
`q ∘ Corr^{n-m}(X, Y) ∘ p ⊂ Corr^{n-m}(X, Y)`: an isomorphism of `ℚ`-vector spaces sending a
morphism to the underlying correspondence.
declarations.statement: def homEquiv (M N : ChowMotiveCat k) : (M ⟶ N) ≃ₗ[ℚ] corrHom M N
declarations.comment: Hom((X, p, m), (Y, q, n)) = q o Corr^{n-m}(X, Y) o p, as Q-vector spaces

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.homEquiv_id
declarations.doc:
The identity morphism of the motive `(X, p, m)` is the projector `p` (compared after
`DirectSum.of`, the degree `m - m` being `0`).
declarations.statement:
theorem homEquiv_id (M : ChowMotiveCat k) :
    DirectSum.of (fun i ↦ SmoothProjectiveCorr M.scheme M.scheme i) (M.twist - M.twist)
        (homEquiv M M (𝟙 M)).1 =
      DirectSum.of (fun i ↦ SmoothProjectiveCorr M.scheme M.scheme i) 0 M.projector
declarations.comment: the identity of (X, p, m) is p

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.homEquiv_comp
declarations.doc:
Composition of morphisms of motives is composition of correspondences: for
`f : (X, p, m) ⟶ (Y, q, n)` and `g : (Y, q, n) ⟶ (Z, r, l)` the correspondence of `f ≫ g` is
`g ∘ f` (compared after `DirectSum.of`, the degrees `l - m` and `(n - m) + (l - n)` being
equal).
declarations.statement:
theorem homEquiv_comp {M N P : ChowMotiveCat k} (f : M ⟶ N) (g : N ⟶ P) :
    DirectSum.of (fun i ↦ SmoothProjectiveCorr M.scheme P.scheme i) (P.twist - M.twist)
        (homEquiv M P (f ≫ g)).1 =
      DirectSum.of (fun i ↦ SmoothProjectiveCorr M.scheme P.scheme i)
        ((N.twist - M.twist) + (P.twist - N.twist))
        ((canonicalCorrespondenceCompositionData k).comp (homEquiv M N f).1
          (homEquiv N P g).1)
declarations.comment: composition of morphisms of motives is composition of correspondences

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.linear
declarations.doc:
The category `M_k` of Chow motives is `ℚ`-linear: the morphism spaces are the `ℚ`-vector
spaces `q ∘ Corr^{n-m}(X, Y) ∘ p` and composition is `ℚ`-bilinear, composition of
correspondences being so (Stacks 0FG0 (1)).
declarations.statement: abbrev linear : Linear ℚ (ChowMotiveCat k)
declarations.comment: M_k is a Q-linear category

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.h
declarations.doc:
The contravariant functor `h : {smooth projective schemes over k} ⟶ M_k`,
`h(X) = (X, 1, 0)` with `1 = [Δ_X]` the identity correspondence, and
`h(f) = [Γ_f] ∈ Corr⁰(X, Y)` for `f : Y ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement: def h : ((SmoothProjectiveScheme k).FullSubcategory)ᵒᵖ ⥤ ChowMotiveCat k
declarations.comment: the contravariant functor h, h(X) = (X, 1, 0), h(f) = [Gamma_f]

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.h_obj_projector
declarations.doc: The projector of `h(X)` is `1 = [Δ_X] ∈ Corr⁰(X, X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem h_obj_projector (X : (SmoothProjectiveScheme k).FullSubcategory) :
    ((h k).obj (Opposite.op X)).projector = correspondenceDiagonal k X
declarations.comment: h(X) = (X, 1, 0): the projector

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.h_obj_twist
declarations.doc: The twist of `h(X)` is `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem h_obj_twist (X : (SmoothProjectiveScheme k).FullSubcategory) :
    ((h k).obj (Opposite.op X)).twist = 0
declarations.comment: h(X) = (X, 1, 0): the twist

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.homEquiv_h_map
declarations.doc:
For `f : Y ⟶ X`, the correspondence of `h(f) : h(X) ⟶ h(Y)` is the graph class
`[Γ_f] ∈ Corr⁰(X, Y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homEquiv_h_map {X Y : (SmoothProjectiveScheme k).FullSubcategory} (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    (homEquiv _ _ ((h k).map f.op)).1 = graphCorrespondenceSP f
declarations.comment: h(f) = [Gamma_f]

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.Motive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGA.** The category `M_k` of Chow motives over `k`: the Karoubi
envelope of the category of correspondences. An object is a pair of an object of the ambient
category — a smooth projective scheme together with its Tate twist — and a projector in
`Corr⁰(X, X)`, that is a triple `(X, p, m)`; a morphism `(X, p, m) ⟶ (Y, q, n)` is a
correspondence in `Corr^{n-m}(X, Y)` fixed by the two projectors.
declarations.statement: abbrev Motive (S : CorrespondenceStructure.{v, u, w} D)
declarations.comment: the category M_k of Chow motives over k, whose objects are the triples (X,p,m)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.hom_motive_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGA.** The morphisms of `M_k` are the correspondences cut out by the
two projectors: `Hom((X, p, m), (Y, q, n)) = q ∘ Corr^{n-m}(X, Y) ∘ p`.
declarations.comment: Hom((X,p,m),(Y,q,n)) = q o Corr^{n-m}(X,Y) o p

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.motiveFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGA.** The functor `h` of Stacks 0FGA, from the ambient category of
smooth projective schemes over `k` to the category of Chow motives: `h(X) = (X, 1, 0)` is the
motive of `X` with the identity as projector and no twist, and `h(f) = [Γ_f]` is the graph of a
morphism.

The source's `h` is contravariant on schemes, `h(f) = [Γ_f] ∈ Corr⁰(X, Y)` for `f : Y → X`,
while `Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.graph` is covariant on the ambient
category; so the ambient category here is the opposite of the category of smooth projective
schemes over `k` enlarged by the Tate twists, and `h` is then the source's functor.
declarations.statement: def motiveFunctor (S : CorrespondenceStructure.{v, u, w} D) : D ⥤ S.Motive
declarations.comment: the functor h into M_k, with h(X) = (X,1,0) and h(f) = [Gamma_f]

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.linear
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGA.** The category `M_k` of Chow motives is `ℚ`-linear, the
category of correspondences being so. The `ℚ`-linear structure of the correspondence spaces is
the content of Stacks 0FG2 and enters as a hypothesis; what is proved is that it passes to the
Karoubi envelope.
declarations.statement:
def linear (S : CorrespondenceStructure.{v, u, w} D) [Preadditive S.Obj] [Linear ℚ S.Obj] :
    Linear ℚ S.Motive
declarations.comment: M_k is a Q-linear category, given the Q-linear structure on correspondences

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.MotiveCalculus.mem_homSubmodule_iff
declarations.doc:
A total correspondence is a morphism of motives `(X, p, m) → (Y, q, n)` exactly when it is a
sandwich `p ∘ a ∘ q` of a correspondence `a` homogeneous of degree `n - m`: the fixed set of the
idempotent sandwich operator is its image.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_homSubmodule_iff {M N : ChowMotive C D.toCorrespondenceCalculus}
    {f : TotalCorr C (motiveObj M) (motiveObj N)} :
    f ∈ D.homSubmodule M N ↔
      ∃ a ∈ corrGrade C (motiveObj M) (motiveObj N) (N.twist - M.twist),
        D.compTotal (motiveObj M) (motiveObj N) (motiveObj N)
          (D.compTotal (motiveObj M) (motiveObj M) (motiveObj N) (D.projectorTotal M) a)
          (D.projectorTotal N) = f
declarations.comment: the morphisms of the category of motives are the sandwiched correspondences

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.MotiveCalculus.category
declarations.doc:
The category of Chow motives: Chow motives as objects, the sandwiched correspondences of
degree `n - m` as morphisms, the projector as the identity and composition of correspondences as
composition.
declarations.statement: instance category : Category.{u} D.Obj
declarations.comment: the category of Chow motives

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.hasKernel_of_idem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGB.** The category `M_k` of Chow motives is Karoubian in the sense of
Homology, Definition 09SG: every idempotent endomorphism `a` of a motive `M` has a kernel.
declarations.statement: theorem hasKernel_of_idem (M : ChowMotiveCat k) (a : M ⟶ M) (ha : a ≫ a = a) : HasKernel a

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.monoidalCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGC.** The category `M_k` of Chow motives is monoidal for
`(X, p, m) ⊗ (Y, q, n) = (X × Y, p ⊗ q, m + n)`, with the tensor product of correspondences on
morphisms, unit `𝟏 = (Spec(k), 1, 0)`, and the associativity constraint of correspondences (the
graph of the associativity isomorphism of products of schemes) cut down by the projectors.
declarations.statement: instance monoidalCategory : MonoidalCategory (ChowMotiveCat k)
declarations.comment: M_k is monoidal for (X,p,m) ⊗ (Y,q,n) = (X × Y, p ⊗ q, m + n), unit (Spec k, 1, 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.braidedCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGC.** The category `M_k` of Chow motives is braided by the
commutativity constraint of correspondences, the graph of the factor switch
`X × Y ≅ Y × X`, cut down by the projectors.
declarations.statement: instance braidedCategory : BraidedCategory (ChowMotiveCat k)
declarations.comment: the commutativity constraint of M_k

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.symmetricCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGC.** The category `M_k` of Chow motives is symmetric monoidal with
the obvious associativity and commutativity constraints and with unit `𝟏 = (Spec(k), 1, 0)`.
declarations.statement: instance symmetricCategory : SymmetricCategory (ChowMotiveCat k)
declarations.comment: M_k is symmetric monoidal

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.tensorObj_mk'_p
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGC.** The tensor product of motives on objects:
`(X, p, m) ⊗ (Y, q, n) = (X × Y, p ⊗ q, m + n)`; this is the projector, `p ⊗ q`, the tensor product
of correspondences (`tensorObj_mk'_scheme` and `tensorObj_mk'_twist` give `X × Y` and `m + n`).
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorObj_mk'_p (X Y : (SmoothProjectiveScheme k).FullSubcategory)
    (p : SmoothProjectiveCorr X X 0)
    (q : SmoothProjectiveCorr Y Y 0)
    (hp : (canonicalCorrespondenceCompositionData k).comp p p = p)
    (hq : (canonicalCorrespondenceCompositionData k).comp q q = q) (m n : ℤ) :
    (mk' X p hp m ⊗ mk' Y q hq n).p = homOf (0 + 0) (CorrespondenceCategory.tensorCorr 0 0 p q)
declarations.comment: (X, p, m) ⊗ (Y, q, n) = (X × Y, p ⊗ q, m + n)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.tensorHom_val_eq_homOf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGC.** The tensor product of morphisms of motives is the tensor
product of correspondences: if `f : (X, p, m) ⟶ (Y, q, n)` is the correspondence
`a ∈ Corr^{n-m}(X, Y)` and `f' : (X', p', m') ⟶ (Y', q', n')` is `a' ∈ Corr^{n'-m'}(X', Y')`, then
`f ⊗ f'` is `a ⊗ a' ∈ Corr^{(n-m)+(n'-m')}(X × X', Y × Y')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorHom_val_eq_homOf {M N M' N' : ChowMotiveCat k} (f : M ⟶ N) (f' : M' ⟶ N')
    {r r' : ℤ} (a : SmoothProjectiveCorr M.scheme N.scheme r)
    (a' : SmoothProjectiveCorr M'.scheme N'.scheme r') (ha : f.val = homOf r a)
    (ha' : f'.val = homOf r' a') :
    (f ⊗ₘ f').val = homOf (r + r') (CorrespondenceCategory.tensorCorr r r' a a')
declarations.comment: on morphisms, (a, a') ↦ a ⊗ a' with ⊗ the tensor product of correspondences

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.tensorUnit_eq_tate
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0FGC.** The unit of `M_k` is `𝟏 = 𝟏(0) = (Spec(k), 1, 0)`.
declarations.statement: theorem tensorUnit_eq_tate : 𝟙_ (ChowMotiveCat k) = tate k 0
declarations.comment: the unit of M_k is 1 = (Spec k, 1, 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.associator_hom_val
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGC.** The associativity constraint of `M_k` is the obvious one: the
graph of the associativity isomorphism `(X × Y) × Z ≅ X × (Y × Z)`, cut down by the
projectors.
declarations.statement:
theorem associator_hom_val (M N P : ChowMotiveCat k) :
    (α_ M N P).hom.val =
      ((M ⊗ N) ⊗ P).p ≫ graphHom (α_ M.scheme N.scheme P.scheme).inv
declarations.comment: the associativity constraint of M_k is the obvious one

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.braiding_hom_val
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGC.** The commutativity constraint of `M_k` is the obvious one: the
graph of the factor switch `X × Y ≅ Y × X`, cut down by the projectors.
declarations.statement:
theorem braiding_hom_val (M N : ChowMotiveCat k) :
    (β_ M N).hom.val = (M ⊗ N).p ≫ graphHom (β_ M.scheme N.scheme).inv
declarations.comment: the commutativity constraint of M_k is the obvious one

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.motiveMonoidalCategory
declarations.doc:
The category `M_k` of Chow motives is monoidal for the tensor product
`(X, p, m) ⊗ (Y, q, n) = (X × Y, p ⊗ q, m + n)`, given the monoidal structure on the category of
correspondences, which is taken as a hypothesis and passes to the Karoubi envelope.
declarations.statement: def motiveMonoidalCategory : MonoidalCategory S.Motive
declarations.comment: M_k is monoidal for (X,p,m) ⊗ (Y,q,n) = (X × Y, p ⊗ q, m+n)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.motiveSymmetricCategory
declarations.doc:
The category `M_k` of Chow motives is symmetric monoidal, with the associativity and
commutativity constraints of the category of correspondences cut down by the projectors, and with
unit `𝟏 = (Spec(k), 1, 0)`.
declarations.statement: def motiveSymmetricCategory : SymmetricCategory S.Motive
declarations.comment: M_k is symmetric monoidal with unit 1 = (Spec(k), 1, 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.motive_associator_hom_f
declarations.doc:
The associativity constraint of `M_k` is the graph of the associativity constraint of the
ambient category, cut down by the projectors.
declarations.statement:
theorem motive_associator_hom_f (M N P : S.Motive) :
    (α_ M N P).hom.f = ((M ⊗ N) ⊗ P).p ≫ S.graph (α_ M.X.as N.X.as P.X.as).hom
declarations.comment: the associativity constraint of M_k is the obvious one

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.motive_braiding_hom_f
declarations.doc:
The commutativity constraint of `M_k` is the graph of the factor switch of the ambient
category, cut down by the projectors.
declarations.statement:
theorem motive_braiding_hom_f (M N : S.Motive) :
    (β_ M N).hom.f = (M ⊗ N).p ≫ S.graph (β_ M.X.as N.X.as).hom
declarations.comment: the commutativity constraint of M_k is the obvious one

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.motive_tensorUnit_as
declarations.doc:
The scheme underlying the unit motive `𝟏 = (Spec(k), 1, 0)` is `Spec(k)`, the unit of the
ambient category.
declarations.statement: theorem motive_tensorUnit_as : (𝟙_ S.Motive).X.as = 𝟙_ D
declarations.comment: the unit of M_k is 1 = (Spec(k), 1, 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.motive_tensorUnit_p
declarations.doc: The projector of the unit motive `𝟏 = (Spec(k), 1, 0)` is the diagonal correspondence.
declarations.statement: theorem motive_tensorUnit_p : (𝟙_ S.Motive).p = S.id (𝟙_ D)
declarations.comment: the projector of the unit of M_k is the diagonal 1

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.projectiveLinePointFibreMotiveIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGD (1).** For a rational point `x` of `X = P¹_k`, the motive
`(X, c₀, 0)`, with `c₀ = [x × X]`, is isomorphic to `1 = (Spec k, 1, 0)`. The mutually inverse
morphisms are the graph classes of the structure morphism `X → Spec k` and of the point
`x : Spec k → X`.
declarations.comment:
part (1): the motive (P¹_k, c₀, 0) is isomorphic to 1 = (Spec k, 1, 0), in the
category of Chow motives built on the actual composition of correspondences

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.projectiveLineFibrePointMotiveIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGD (2).** For a rational point `x` of `X = P¹_k`, the motive
`(X, c₂, 0)`, with `c₂ = [X × x]`, is isomorphic to `1(-1) = (Spec k, 1, -1)`. The mutually
inverse morphisms are the class `a' ∈ Corr¹(Spec k, X)` of the point `x` and the fundamental class
`b' ∈ Corr^{-1}(X, Spec k)`, whose compositions `b' ∘ a' = 1` and `a' ∘ b' = c₂` are computed by
intersecting cycles.
declarations.statement: def projectiveLineFibrePointMotiveIso : lefschetzMotive x hx ≅ tate k (-1)
declarations.comment:
part (2): the motive (P¹_k, c₂, 0) is isomorphic to 1(-1) = (Spec k, 1, -1), with
b' ∘ a' = 1 and a' ∘ b' = c₂ proved by intersecting the actual cycles

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.constantGraphMotiveIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGD (1).** The motive `(X, c₀, 0)` is isomorphic to the motive
`h(Spec k) = 1 = (Spec k, 1, 0)`.

The graph classes of the structure morphism and of the rational point are the source's
`a ∈ Corr⁰(Spec k, X)` and `b ∈ Corr⁰(X, Spec k)`. Functoriality of the graph turns the identity
`x ≫ (X → Spec k) = 1` of the source into `b ∘ a = 1` and gives `a ∘ b = [Γ_{X → x → X}] = c₀`,
so `c₀` splits through `Spec k` and `a`, `b` are mutually inverse morphisms of motives.
declarations.statement:
def constantGraphMotiveIso {P Q : D} (α : P ⟶ Q) (β : Q ⟶ P) (hαβ : α ≫ β = 𝟙 P) :
    S.constantGraphMotive α β hαβ ≅ S.motiveFunctor.obj P
declarations.comment: part (1): the motive (X, c_0, 0) is isomorphic to 1 = (Spec k, 1, 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.lefschetzMotive
declarations.doc:
The *Lefschetz motive* `(P¹_k, c₂, 0)`: the projective line, cut down by the projector
`c₂ = [P¹_k × x]` of Example 0FG6 attached to a `k`-rational point `x`, with no twist, as an
object of the category `M_k` of Chow motives. In the literature it is denoted `L`, `𝐋`, `𝐐(-1)`
or `h²(P¹_k)`. Its invertibility, the content of Remark 0FGE, is
`Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.isInvertible_lefschetzMotive`.
declarations.statement: def lefschetzMotive : ChowMotiveCat k
declarations.comment:
the Lefschetz motive (X, c_2, 0) in M_k for X = P^1_k and c_2 as in 0FG6, written
L, bold L, Q(-1) or h^2(P^1_k)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.lefschetzMotiveHasInverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGE.** The Lefschetz motive `L = (P¹_k, c₂, 0)` is invertible in the
symmetric monoidal category `M_k`, with inverse the Tate motive `1(1) = (Spec k, 1, 1)`: a
two-sided tensor inverse `L ⊗ 1(1) ≅ 1`, `1(1) ⊗ L ≅ 1`, obtained by carrying the inverse
`1(1)` of `1(-1)` along the isomorphism `L ≅ 1(-1)` of Lemma 0FGD.
declarations.statement: def lefschetzMotiveHasInverse : HasInverse (lefschetzMotive x hx)
declarations.comment:
the Lefschetz motive (P^1_k, c_2, 0) is invertible in M_k, with inverse the Tate
motive 1(1), via the isomorphism with 1(-1) of 0FGD; unconditional

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.lefschetzMotiveHasInverse_inv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGE.** The inverse of the Lefschetz motive is the Tate motive
`1(1) = (Spec k, 1, 1)`, also written `L⁻¹`, `𝐋⁻¹`, `𝐓` or `𝐐(1)`.
declarations.statement: theorem lefschetzMotiveHasInverse_inv : (lefschetzMotiveHasInverse x hx).inv = tate k 1
declarations.comment: the inverse of the Lefschetz motive is the Tate motive 1(1) = (Spec k, 1, 1)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.isInvertible_lefschetzMotive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGE.** The Lefschetz motive is invertible in `M_k` in the sense of
Categories, Definition 0FFN, for every field `k` and `k`-rational point `x` of `P¹_k`.
declarations.statement: theorem isInvertible_lefschetzMotive : IsInvertible (lefschetzMotive x hx)
declarations.comment: the Lefschetz motive is invertible in M_k (Categories, Definition 0FFN)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.hasFiniteBiproducts
declarations.doc:
The category `M_k` of Chow motives is additive: it is preadditive (`ℚ`-linear, Stacks 0FGA)
and has finite direct sums. A zero object is a motive with zero projector; two motives
`(Y, p, m)`, `(Z, q, m)` with the same twist have the direct sum `(Y ⨿ Z, p + q, m)`; and a
motive `(Z, q, n)` is isomorphic to `(Z, q, m) ⊗ (P¹_k, c₂, 0)^{⊗ (m - n)}`, of twist `m`, since
`(P¹_k, c₂, 0) ≅ 𝟏(-1)`.
declarations.statement: instance hasFiniteBiproducts : HasFiniteBiproducts (ChowMotiveCat k)
declarations.comment:
M_k is additive: finite direct sums, via (Y ⨿ Z, p + q, m) for equal twists and
(Z, q, n) ≅ (Z, q, m) ⊗ (P¹, c₂, 0)^{⊗(m-n)}

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.projectiveLineMotiveBiproductData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGG.** In `M_k` the motive `h(P¹_k)` is the direct sum of
`1 = (Spec k, 1, 0)` and `1(-1) = (Spec k, 1, -1)`: a bilimit binary bicone over `1` and `1(-1)`
whose point is `h(P¹_k)`, see
`Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.projectiveLineMotiveBiproductData_bicone_pt`.

It is obtained from the splitting `h(P¹_k) = (P¹_k, c₀, 0) ⊕ (P¹_k, c₂, 0)` by the projectors of
Example 0FG6 attached to the `k`-rational point `x`, followed by the two isomorphisms
`(P¹_k, c₀, 0) ≅ 1` and `(P¹_k, c₂, 0) ≅ 1(-1)` of Lemma 0FGD.
declarations.statement: def projectiveLineMotiveBiproductData : BinaryBiproductData (tate k 0) (tate k (-1))
declarations.comment:
h(P^1_k) is the direct sum of 1 and 1(-1) in M_k: a bilimit bicone over 1 and
1(-1) with point h(P^1_k), built from any k-rational point of the actual P^1_k, in the actual
category of Chow motives, with Example 0FG6 and Lemma 0FGD proved for it

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.projectiveLineMotiveIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGG.** In `M_k` we have `h(P¹_k) ≅ 1 ⊕ 1(-1)`.

This is `Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.projectiveLineMotiveBiproductData`, at the rational
point `∞` of `P¹_k`, compared with the chosen direct sum `1 ⊞ 1(-1)`, whose existence is
`Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.hasBinaryBiproduct_tate_zero_tate_neg_one`. Nothing beyond
the field `k` is assumed: the relations of Example 0FG6 and the isomorphisms of Lemma 0FGD are
proved for `P¹_k`. The abstract form of the deduction, for an arbitrary category of
correspondences, is `Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceStructure.projectiveLineMotiveIso`.
declarations.statement:
def projectiveLineMotiveIso :
    (h k).obj (Opposite.op (projectiveLineObj k)) ≅ tate k 0 ⊞ tate k (-1)
declarations.comment:
in M_k we have h(P^1_k) iso 1 + 1(-1), for the actual P^1_k and the actual category
of Chow motives, with Example 0FG6 and Lemma 0FGD proved for P^1_k

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.universalProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGH.** Let `X = P¹_k`, `x` a rational point and `c₂ = [X × x]`
(Example 0FG6). Let `𝒞` be a `ℚ`-linear Karoubian symmetric monoidal category. A `ℚ`-linear functor
of symmetric monoidal categories `F` from the category of smooth projective schemes over `k` with
correspondences of degree `0` to `𝒞`, such that the image of `F(c₂)` on `F(X)` is an invertible
object, factors through a functor `G : M_k ⥤ 𝒞` of symmetric monoidal categories along
`X ↦ (X, 1, 0)` — by a monoidal isomorphism, `G` being moreover additive and `ℚ`-linear — and the
factorization is unique: any two are related by a unique monoidal isomorphism compatible with the
identifications.

This is the declaration registered for Stacks 0FGH; the Karoubi-envelope lemmas of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.WeilCohomology.Motives.UniversalProperty` are auxiliary.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalProperty {𝒞 : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} 𝒞] [MonoidalCategory 𝒞]
    [SymmetricCategory 𝒞] [Preadditive 𝒞] [Linear ℚ 𝒞] [MonoidalPreadditive 𝒞]
    [IsIdempotentComplete 𝒞]
    (F : DegreeZero ℚ (CorrespondenceCategory k) ⥤ 𝒞) [F.Braided] [F.Additive]
    [Functor.Linear ℚ F]
    (hF : ∃ (U : 𝒞) (i : U ⟶ F.obj (projectiveLineDegreeZero k))
      (e : F.obj (projectiveLineDegreeZero k) ⟶ U),
      i ≫ e = 𝟙 U ∧ e ≫ i = F.map (projectiveLineFibrePointDegreeZero x hx) ∧ IsInvertible U) :
    (∃ (G : ChowMotiveCat k ⥤ 𝒞) (_ : G.Braided) (_ : G.Additive) (_ : Functor.Linear ℚ G)
        (φ : TwistedKaroubi.untwistedOfObj (CorrespondenceCategory k) ⋙ G ≅ F),
        NatTrans.IsMonoidal φ.hom) ∧
      ∀ (G₁ G₂ : ChowMotiveCat k ⥤ 𝒞) [G₁.Braided] [G₂.Braided]
        (φ₁ : TwistedKaroubi.untwistedOfObj (CorrespondenceCategory k) ⋙ G₁ ≅ F)
        (φ₂ : TwistedKaroubi.untwistedOfObj (CorrespondenceCategory k) ⋙ G₂ ≅ F)
        [NatTrans.IsMonoidal φ₁.hom] [NatTrans.IsMonoidal φ₂.hom],
        ∃! θ : G₁ ≅ G₂, NatTrans.IsMonoidal θ.hom ∧
          Functor.whiskerLeft (TwistedKaroubi.untwistedOfObj (CorrespondenceCategory k)) θ.hom ≫
            φ₂.hom = φ₁.hom
declarations.comment:
a Q-linear symmetric monoidal functor F on degree-0 correspondences with the image
of F(c₂) on F(P¹) invertible factors through M_k, uniquely up to unique monoidal isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.motiveExactPairing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGI.** Let `X` be a smooth projective scheme over `k` which is
equidimensional of dimension `d`. Then `h(X)(d) = h(X) ⊗ 𝟏(d)` is a left dual of `h(X)` in the
category `M_k` of Chow motives: there are `η : 𝟏 ⟶ h(X) ⊗ h(X)(d)` and
`ε : h(X)(d) ⊗ h(X) ⟶ 𝟏`, both the class `[Δ]` of the diagonal, satisfying the two triangle
identities (Categories, Definition 0FFP; Mathlib's `ExactPairing`). Equidimensionality of
dimension `d` is `RelativeDimension X.obj.hom d`; `X` may be empty.

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.nonempty_exactPairing_motive
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0FGI**, as a statement: `h(X)` has `h(X)(d)` as a left dual in `M_k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_exactPairing_motive (hX : RelativeDimension X.obj.hom d) :
    Nonempty (ExactPairing ((ChowMotiveCat.h k).obj (op X))
      ((ChowMotiveCat.h k).obj (op X) ⊗ ChowMotiveCat.tate k d))

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.selfCorrespondenceEquivCoevaluation
declarations.doc:
For `X` equidimensional of dimension `d`, so that `X × X` is
equidimensional of dimension `2 * d`, the canonical `ℚ`-linear isomorphism

  `Corr⁰(X, X) = CH^d(X × X) ⊗ ℚ = Corr^d(Spec k, X × X)`.

The left-hand group is `Hom(h(X), h(X))`, which contains the identity `[Δ]`; the right-hand one
is `Hom(1, h(X) ⊗ h(X)(d))`, which contains the unit `η` of the duality. The identification is
that of Tag 0FG0 (3), proper pushforward along the collapsing projection
`Spec k × (X × X) ≅ X × X`.
declarations.comment:
the identification Corr^0(X,X) = Corr^d(Spec k, X x X) = CH^d(X x X) tensor Q, which puts
the identity [D] of h(X) and the unit of the duality in one group

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.selfCorrespondenceEquivEvaluation
declarations.doc:
For `X` equidimensional of dimension `d` the canonical
`ℚ`-linear isomorphism

  `Corr⁰(X, X) = CH_d(X × X) ⊗ ℚ = Corr^{-d}(X × X, Spec k)`.

The right-hand group is `Hom(h(X)(d) ⊗ h(X), 1)`, which contains the counit `ε` of the duality.
The identification is that of Tag 0FG0 (2), proper pushforward along the collapsing projection
`(X × X) × Spec k ≅ X × X`.
declarations.comment:
the identification Corr^0(X,X) = Corr^{-d}(X x X, Spec k) = CH_d(X x X) tensor Q, which puts
the identity [D] of h(X) and the counit of the duality in one group

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.dualityCorrespondenceEquiv
declarations.doc:
The group of candidate units of the duality and the group of
candidate counits are canonically the same, both being `CH^d(X × X) ⊗ ℚ = CH_d(X × X) ⊗ ℚ`:

  `Corr^d(Spec k, X × X) = Corr^{-d}(X × X, Spec k)`.
declarations.comment:
the identification Corr^d(Spec k, X x X) = Corr^{-d}(X x X, Spec k) that makes one class [D]
serve as identity, as unit and as counit

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.rightRigidCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FGJ.** Every object of the category `M_k` of Chow motives has a left dual:
`M_k` is (right) rigid, in Mathlib's naming.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance rightRigidCategory : RightRigidCategory (ChowMotiveCat k)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.nonempty_hasRightDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FGJ**, objectwise: every Chow motive `M` has a left dual (Stacks' "`Mᘁ` is a left
dual of `M`" is Mathlib's `ExactPairing M Mᘁ`).
declarations.statement: theorem nonempty_hasRightDual (M : ChowMotiveCat k) : Nonempty (HasRightDual M)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.rightRigidCategoryOfRetractTwist
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGJ.** Every object of the category `M_k` of motives has a left dual,
i.e. `M_k` is a rigid category.

Here `Mot` is the category `M_k` of motives of Stacks 0FGA, monoidal by Stacks 0FGC, `h X` is the
motive of a smooth projective scheme `X` over `k`, and `T m` is the Tate object `1(m)`. The
hypothesis `hh` is Stacks 0FGI, that `h(X)` has a left dual — supplied from this repository's
own 0FGI by `Stacks.WeilCohomology.rightRigidCategoryOfDiagonalPairingData` below; `hT` is the
invertibility of the Tate motive, that `1(m)` is a left dual of `1(-m)`; and `hgen` says that
every motive is a direct summand of a twist `h(X)(m)`. See the implementation notes of this file
for why each is carried rather than used.
declarations.statement:
def rightRigidCategoryOfRetractTwist (h : D → Mot) (hh : ∀ X : D, HasRightDual (h X))
    (T : ℤ → Mot) (hT : ∀ m : ℤ, ExactPairing (T (-m)) (T m))
    (hgen : ∀ L : Mot, ∃ (X : D) (m : ℤ), Nonempty (Retract L (h X ⊗ T m))) :
    RightRigidCategory Mot
declarations.comment:
every object of M_k has a left dual, i.e. M_k is right rigid in Mathlib's naming.
STATED IN AN ABSTRACT MONOIDAL CATEGORY, not on this library's category of motives, because the
monoidal structure on Karoubi S.Obj is Stacks 0FGC, which is not yet formalized in this repository,
so the twist h(X)(m) = h(X) tensor 1(m) cannot be written on `S.Motive` at all. The
statement specialises to the source's setting as soon as 0FGC is formalized, and h : D → Mot is kept
untwisted on purpose, the Tate objects being supplied separately as T : Z → Mot, exactly as in
the 0FGN statement of ManinIdentityPrinciple whose `hdual` hypothesis this discharges. Three
pieces of data are carried rather than used, each named in the signature: Stacks 0FGI that h(X)
has a left dual (hh), which this repository does prove from DiagonalPairingData and which
rightRigidCategoryOfDiagonalPairingData feeds in; invertibility of the Tate motive, that 1(m) is
a left dual of 1(-m) in the Stacks 0FFP sense (hT); and generation, that every motive is a
retract of a twist h(X)(m) (hgen), taken in the weak Retract sense so the theorem is stronger.
Karoubianness of M_k is the typeclass IsIdempotentComplete. Reused rather than reproved: Stacks
0FFS as Mathlib's hasRightDualTensor and Stacks 0FFU as this library's
nonempty_hasRightDual_of_retract

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.SmoothProjectiveScheme.ChowMotive.chowGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGL.** The `i`-th Chow group of a Chow motive `M = (X, p, m)` over a
field `k`,

  `CH^i(M) = p(CH^{i + m}(X) ⊗ ℚ)`,

the image of the pushforward action `p_*` of the projector `p ∈ Corr⁰(X, X)` (Section 0FFZ) on
the rational Chow group of codimension `i + m` classes of the smooth projective scheme `X`, as a
`ℚ`-subspace of `CH^{i + m}(X) ⊗ ℚ`.

This is the complete, unconditional registration of Stacks 0FGL: the composition and the
pushforward of correspondences are the ones constructed in this file. It supersedes
`Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotive.chowGroup`, which takes them as a carried
`Stacks.WeilCohomology.CorrespondenceCalculus` and no longer carries the tag.
declarations.statement: def chowGroup (i : ℤ) : Submodule ℚ (RationalCodimChowGroup M.X (i + M.twist))
declarations.comment: the i-th Chow group CH^i(M) = p(CH^{i+m}(X) ⊗ Q) of a Chow motive M = (X, p, m) over a field, X smooth projective and p_* the pushforward action of the projector

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.SmoothProjectiveScheme.ChowMotive.mem_chowGroup_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGL.** The classes of `CH^i(M)` are the classes `p_*(β)` for
`β ∈ CH^{i + m}(X) ⊗ ℚ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_chowGroup_iff (i : ℤ) (α : RationalCodimChowGroup M.X (i + M.twist)) :
    α ∈ M.chowGroup i ↔ ∃ β, M.projectorAction i β = α
declarations.comment: membership in CH^i(M) = p(CH^{i+m}(X) ⊗ Q)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.chowGroupEquivHom
declarations.doc:
The functor `CH^i(-)` on the category `M_k` of Chow motives is representable by `𝟏(-i)`: for
every motive `M` there is a `ℚ`-linear isomorphism

  `CH^i(M) = Hom_{M_k}(𝟏(-i), M)`,

sending `α ∈ CH^i(X, p, m) = p(CH^{i+m}(X) ⊗ ℚ)` to the correspondence
`α ∈ Corr^{i+m}(Spec k, X)` of Stacks 0FG0 (3). It is natural in `M`:
`Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.chowGroupEquivHom_naturality`.
declarations.statement: def chowGroupEquivHom (M : ChowMotiveCat k) (i : ℤ) : chowGroup M i ≃ₗ[ℚ] (tate k (-i) ⟶ M)
declarations.comment: CH^i(M) = Hom_{M_k}(1(-i), M)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.chowGroupEquivHom_naturality
declarations.doc:
The identification `CH^i(M) = Hom_{M_k}(𝟏(-i), M)` is natural in `M`: for a morphism of
motives `c : M ⟶ N` it carries `c_* : CH^i(M) ⟶ CH^i(N)` to postcomposition with `c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowGroupEquivHom_naturality {M N : ChowMotiveCat k} (f : M ⟶ N) (i : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup M i) :
    chowGroupEquivHom N i (chowMap f i α) = chowGroupEquivHom M i α ≫ f
declarations.comment: CH^i(M) = Hom_{M_k}(1(-i), M) functorially in M

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.chowFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
The functor `CH^i(-) : M_k ⥤ ℚ-vector spaces` is representable by `𝟏(-i)`: it is isomorphic
to the functor `Hom_{M_k}(𝟏(-i), -)`, functorially in the motive.
declarations.statement:
def chowFunctorIso (i : ℤ) :
    chowFunctor k i ≅ (linearCoyoneda ℚ (ChowMotiveCat k)).obj (Opposite.op (tate k (-i)))
declarations.comment: the functor CH^i(-) on M_k is representable by 1(-i)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.MotiveCalculus.chowGroupEquivHom
declarations.doc:
The functor `CH^i(-)` on the category of Chow motives is represented by the `(-i)`-twist of
the unit motive: the identification
`CH^{i+m}(X) ⊗ ℚ = Corr^{i+m}(Spec k, X)` of Stacks 0FG0 (3) restricts to an isomorphism of
`ℚ`-vector spaces

  `CH^i(M) ≃ Hom_{M_k}(𝟙(-i), M)`.

Naturality in `M` is `Stacks.WeilCohomology.MotiveCalculus.chowGroupEquivHom_naturality`, and
the two together are packaged as
`Stacks.WeilCohomology.MotiveCalculus.chowFunctorIso`.
declarations.statement: def chowGroupEquivHom (M : D.Obj) (i : ℤ) : ↥(M.as.chowGroup i) ≃ₗ[ℚ] (D.unitTwist i ⟶ M)
declarations.comment: CH^i(M) = Hom(1(-i), M)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.MotiveCalculus.chowGroupEquivHom_naturality
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism `CH^i(M) ≃ Hom(𝟙(-i), M)` is natural in `M`: it carries the map on Chow
groups induced by a morphism of motives `f : M → N` — the restriction of the action of the
correspondence underlying `f` — to postcomposition with `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowGroupEquivHom_naturality {M N : D.Obj} (i : ℤ) (f : M ⟶ N)
    (α : ↥(M.as.chowGroup i)) :
    D.chowGroupEquivHom N i (D.chowGroupMap i f α) = D.chowGroupEquivHom M i α ≫ f
declarations.comment: the identification is functorial in the motive

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.MotiveCalculus.chowFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
The functor `CH^i(-)` on the category of Chow motives is representable by `𝟙(-i)`: an
isomorphism of functors `CH^i(-) ≅ Hom_{M_k}(𝟙(-i), -)` with values in `ℚ`-vector spaces.
declarations.statement: def chowFunctorIso (i : ℤ) : D.chowFunctor i ≅ D.homFunctor i
declarations.comment: CH^i(-) is representable by 1(-i), as functors

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.ChowMotiveCat.isIso_of_bijective_chowMap_tensorHom_h
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGN** (Manin's identity principle). Let `k` be a field and let
`c : M ⟶ N` be a morphism of Chow motives over `k`. If for every smooth projective scheme `X` over
`k` the morphism `c ⊗ 1 : M ⊗ h(X) ⟶ N ⊗ h(X)` induces an isomorphism
`CH^i(M ⊗ h(X)) → CH^i(N ⊗ h(X))` on Chow groups in every degree `i`, then `c` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_bijective_chowMap_tensorHom_h {M N : ChowMotiveCat k} (c : M ⟶ N)
    (hc : ∀ (X : (SmoothProjectiveScheme k).FullSubcategory) (i : ℤ),
      Function.Bijective (chowMap (c ⊗ₘ 𝟙 ((h k).obj (op X))) i)) :
    IsIso c
declarations.comment: Manin's identity principle, on the category M_k of Chow motives

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.isIso_of_bijective_chowMap_tensorUnitHom
declarations.doc:
**Manin's identity principle.** Let `c : M ⟶ N` be a morphism of motives. If for every
smooth projective scheme `X` over `k` the morphism `c ⊗ 1 : M ⊗ h(X) ⟶ N ⊗ h(X)` induces an
isomorphism on the Chow group `CH^i` in every degree `i ∈ ℤ`, then `c` is an isomorphism.

Here `Mot` stands for the monoidal category `M_k` of motives, `h X` is the motive of a smooth
projective scheme `X` over `k`, and `R` carries the Chow groups together with the
representability `CH^i(-) = Hom(1(-i), -)`. The theorem takes as hypotheses `hdual`, that every
object of `M_k` has a left dual, and `hgen`, that every object of `M_k` is a direct summand of a
twist `h(X)(m)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_bijective_chowMap_tensorUnitHom (R : ChowRepresentability Mot)
    (hdual : ∀ L : Mot, HasRightDual L) {D : Type w} (h : D → Mot)
    (hgen : ∀ L : Mot, ∃ (X : D) (m : ℤ), Nonempty (Retract L (h X ⊗ R.unitTwist m)))
    {M N : Mot} (c : M ⟶ N)
    (hc : ∀ (X : D) (i : ℤ), Function.Bijective (R.chowMap i (c ⊗ₘ 𝟙 (h X)))) :
    IsIso c
declarations.comment:
Manin's identity principle: c is an isomorphism if c tensor 1 is an isomorphism
on the Chow groups of M tensor h(X) for every smooth projective X, over every degree i.
STATED IN AN ABSTRACT MONOIDAL CATEGORY, not on this library's category of motives, because the
monoidal structure on Karoubi S.Obj is Stacks 0FGC, which is only stated, not constructed, in this
library -- so `M ⊗ h(X)` cannot be written on `S.Motive` at all. The statement specialises to the
source's setting as soon as 0FGC is available, and `h : D → Mot` is kept untwisted on purpose so
that quantifying the hypothesis over D does not silently assume it for the twists h(X)(m), which is
what the source's proof has to earn. Four pieces of data are carried rather than used, each
named in the signature: the representability CH^i(-) = Hom(1(-i), -) of Stacks 0FGM (the field
chowEquiv of ChowRepresentability, together with its naturality), invertibility of the Tate
motive in the Stacks 0FFP sense (tateExactPairing), Stacks 0FGJ that every object has a left
dual (hdual), and generation, that every motive is a retract of a twist h(X)(m) (hgen), taken in
the weak Retract sense so the theorem is stronger. Proved here rather than carried: Stacks 0FFQ,
the summand step, the degree shift and the Yoneda step

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.isIso_projectiveBundleFormula
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FGQ (the projective space bundle formula).** Let `k` be a field, `X` a
smooth projective scheme over `k`, `ℰ` a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module of rank `r` and
`p : P = 𝐏(ℰ) ⟶ X` its projective bundle, with `𝒪_P(1)` normalized so that `p_*𝒪_P(1) = ℰ`. For
`i = 0, …, r - 1` let `c_i = c₁(pr₂^*𝒪_P(1))^i ∩ [Γ_p] ∈ Corr^i(X, P)`, read as a morphism
`h(X)(-i) ⟶ h(P)`, where `h(Y)(m) = (Y, 1, m)` is `Stacks.WeilCohomology.twistedMotive Y m` and
`h(P) = (P, 1, 0) = twistedMotive P 0` (`Stacks.WeilCohomology.twistedMotive_zero`). Then

  `∑_{i < r} c_i : ⨁_{i < r} h(X)(-i) ⟶ h(P)`

is an isomorphism in the category `M_k` of Chow motives.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_projectiveBundleFormula :
    IsIso (biproduct.desc (projectiveBundleOfRankHom X E r) :
      (⨁ fun i : Fin r ↦ twistedMotive X (-((i : ℕ) : ℤ))) ⟶
        twistedMotive (projectiveBundleOfRank X E r) 0)
declarations.comment:
the projective space bundle formula: the sum of the c_i = c_1(pr_2^*O_P(1))^i ∩
[Gamma_p], from the direct sum of the h(X)(-i), i < r, to h(P), is an isomorphism in M_k

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.diagonal_projectiveBundle_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FGR.** Let `X` be smooth and separated over a field `k` (for instance smooth
projective, as in Lemma 0FGQ), `ℰ` a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module of rank `r = n + 1`,
`p : P = 𝐏(ℰ) ⟶ X` its projective bundle with `𝒪_P(1)` normalized so that `p_*𝒪_P(1) = ℰ`
(`Stacks.Chow.bundle`, `Stacks.Chow.bundleTwist`), and `𝒮` the kernel of the canonical surjection
`p^*ℰ ⟶ 𝒪_P(1)`. Then the class of the diagonal of `P` in the Chow groups of `P × P` is

  `[Δ_P] = (∑_{i = 0}^{r - 1} c_{r-1-i}(pr₁^*𝒮^∨) ∩ c₁(pr₂^*𝒪_P(1))^i) ∩ (p × p)^*[Δ_X]`,

with integer coefficients. The identity is stated dimension by dimension, which is the whole of
it since `[Δ_P] = ∑_m [Δ_P]_m`: for every `m`, the part of dimension `m + n` of the cycle of the
diagonal `Δ_P ⊂ P ×_k P` is the sum over `i ≤ n` of `c_{n-i}(pr₁^*𝒮^∨) ∩ c₁(pr₂^*𝒪_P(1))^i ∩
(p × p)^*[Δ_X]_m`, where `[Δ_X]_m` is the part of dimension `m` of the cycle of `Δ_X ⊂ X ×_k X`,
`(p × p)^*` is flat pullback (of relative dimension `2n`), `c₁(-)^i ∩` is the `i`-th power of the
first Chern class cap (Stacks 02SO) and `c_j(-) ∩` the Chern class cap of Stacks 02U6.

The tag as printed weights the `i`-th summand by a binomial coefficient `C(r - 1, i)`. Read
literally that is false: for `X = Spec k` and `r = 3` (so `P = 𝐏²`) it gives
`h₁² + 2h₁h₂ + h₂²` for the diagonal class instead of `h₁² + h₁h₂ + h₂²`. The coefficients are
dropped here, which is the identity the source's proof establishes: the diagonal is the zero
scheme of the section of `pr₁^*𝒮^∨ ⊗ pr₂^*𝒪_P(1)`, whose top Chern class expands without them.
declarations.statement:
theorem diagonal_projectiveBundle_eq_sum (m : ℤ) :
    letI := flat_bundleProdMap sX E n
    letI := locallyOfFiniteType_bundleProdMap sX E n
    QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences (fieldChowSituation k)
        (prodBase (bundleProj E ≫ sX) (bundleProj E ≫ sX)) (m + n))
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (fieldChowSituation k)
          (prodBase (bundleProj E ≫ sX) (bundleProj E ≫ sX))
          (pullback.diagonal (bundleProj E ≫ sX)) (m + n)) =
      ∑ i : Fin (n + 1), chowGroupCast (fieldChowSituation k)
        (prodBase (bundleProj E ≫ sX) (bundleProj E ≫ sX)) (by have := i.isLt; omega)
        (GenuineChern.chernFamily (fieldChowSituation k)
          (prodBase (bundleProj E ≫ sX) (bundleProj E ≫ sX))
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst (bundleProj E ≫ sX) (bundleProj E ≫ sX))).obj
            (dualSheaf (kernel (bundleTautological E)))) n
          (m + ((n + n : ℕ) : ℤ) - (i : ℕ)) (n - i)
          (capPow (fieldChowSituation k) (prodBase (bundleProj E ≫ sX) (bundleProj E ≫ sX))
            (invCap (fieldChowSituation k) (prodBase (bundleProj E ≫ sX) (bundleProj E ≫ sX))
              ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd (bundleProj E ≫ sX) (bundleProj E ≫ sX))).obj
                (bundleTwist E))) i (m + ((n + n : ℕ) : ℤ)) (m + ((n + n : ℕ) : ℤ) - (i : ℕ))
            (by ring)
            (flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension (fieldChowSituation k)
              (prodBase (bundleProj E ≫ sX) (bundleProj E ≫ sX)) (prodBase sX sX)
              (pullback.map (bundleProj E ≫ sX) (bundleProj E ≫ sX) sX sX (bundleProj E)
                (bundleProj E) (𝟙 _) (Category.comp_id _) (Category.comp_id _))
              (bundleProdMap_comp_prodBase sX E) (n + n) (relativeDimension_bundleProdMap sX E n) m
              (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences (fieldChowSituation k) (prodBase sX sX) m)
                (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (fieldChowSituation k) (prodBase sX sX)
                  (pullback.diagonal sX) m)))))

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.PoincareDualityPushforwardSetup.mul_pushforward_one
declarations.doc:
Cup product with the pushforward `f_*1` of the unit is `f_* ∘ f^*`, for a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Z` of smooth projective schemes over `k` of equal dimension:
`a ∪ f_*1 = f_*(f^*a ∪ 1) = f_*(f^*a)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mul_pushforward_one (f : X ⟶ Z) (hd : S.dimension X = S.dimension Z) (n : ℤ)
    (a : (S.H Z).piece n) :
    ExternallyGraded.degreeCast (R := F) (X := (S.H Z).piece) (add_zero n)
        ((S.H Z).mul n 0 a
          (ExternallyGraded.degreeCast (R := F) (X := (S.H Z).piece)
            (show 2 * (S.dimension Z : ℤ) - 2 * (S.dimension Z : ℤ) = 0 by omega)
            (S.pushforward f (2 * (S.dimension Z : ℤ))
              (ExternallyGraded.degreeCast (R := F) (X := (S.H X).piece)
                (show (0 : ℤ) = 2 * (S.dimension X : ℤ) - 2 * (S.dimension Z : ℤ) by omega)
                (S.H X).one)))) =
      ExternallyGraded.degreeCast (R := F) (X := (S.H Z).piece)
        (show 2 * (S.dimension Z : ℤ) - (2 * (S.dimension Z : ℤ) - n) = n by omega)
        (S.pushforward f (2 * (S.dimension Z : ℤ) - n)
          (ExternallyGraded.degreeCast (R := F) (X := (S.H X).piece)
            (show n = 2 * (S.dimension X : ℤ) - (2 * (S.dimension Z : ℤ) - n) by omega)
            (S.pullback f n a)))
declarations.comment: cup product with the pushforward of the unit

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.PoincareDualityPushforwardSetup.pushforward_mul_pullback
declarations.doc:
The projection formula `f_*(f^*b ∪ a) = b ∪ f_*a` for the pushforward determined by Poincaré
duality.
declarations.statement:
theorem PoincareDualityPushforwardSetup.pushforward_mul_pullback
    {X Y : (SmoothProjective k).FullSubcategory} (f : X ⟶ Y) (i j : ℤ)
    (b : (S.H Y).piece j) (a : (S.H X).piece (2 * (S.dimension X : ℤ) - (i + j))) :
    S.pushforward f i
        (ExternallyGraded.degreeCast (R := F) (by omega)
          ((S.H X).mul j (2 * (S.dimension X : ℤ) - (i + j)) (S.pullback f j b) a)) =
      ExternallyGraded.degreeCast (R := F) (by omega)
        ((S.H Y).mul j (2 * (S.dimension Y : ℤ) - (i + j)) b (S.pushforward f (i + j) a))
declarations.comment: projection_formula

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.PoincareDualityPushforwardSetup.pushforward_comp
declarations.doc:
The pushforward determined by Poincaré duality is covariantly functorial:
`g_* ∘ f_* = (g ∘ f)_*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PoincareDualityPushforwardSetup.pushforward_comp
    {X Y Z : (SmoothProjective k).FullSubcategory} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (i : ℤ) :
    (S.pushforward g i).comp (S.pushforward f i) = S.pushforward (f ≫ g) i
declarations.comment: pushforward_functoriality

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.cycleClass_mul_iff_cycleClass_codimensionExteriorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0FGU.** Let `H^*` with its trace maps be a Poincaré duality setup on the smooth
projective varieties over an algebraically closed field `k`, and let `γ : CH^r(X) ⟶ H^{2r}(X)`
be group homomorphisms on the Chow groups of Chapter 42, graded by codimension, satisfying axiom
(C)(a), `γ(f^!β) = f^*γ(β)` for the Gysin maps of Stacks 0FF3. Then axiom (C)(c),
`γ(α · β) = γ(α) ∪ γ(β)` for the intersection product of Stacks 0FC0, holds if and only if `γ` is
compatible with exterior products: `γ(α × β) = pr₁^*γ(α) ∪ pr₂^*γ(β)` in `H^*(X ×_k X)` for the
exterior product of Stacks 0FBV, for every smooth projective variety `X` and `α ∈ CH^r(X)`,
`β ∈ CH^s(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleClass_mul_iff_cycleClass_codimensionExteriorProduct
    (S : PoincareDualityPushforwardSetup.{u, v, w} k F)
    (cycleClass : ∀ (X : (SmoothProjective k).FullSubcategory) (r : ℤ),
      (chowCycleData k).group X r →+ (S.H X).piece (2 * r))
    (cycleClass_gysin : ∀ {X Y : (SmoothProjective k).FullSubcategory} (f : X ⟶ Y) (r : ℤ)
      (β : (chowCycleData k).group Y r),
      cycleClass X r ((chowCycleData k).gysin f r β) = S.pullback f (2 * r) (cycleClass Y r β)) :
    (∀ (X : (SmoothProjective k).FullSubcategory) (r s : ℤ) (α : (chowCycleData k).group X r)
        (β : (chowCycleData k).group X s),
        cycleClass X (r + s) (codimensionIntersectionProduct k _ r s α β) =
          (S.H X).evenCup r s (cycleClass X r α) (cycleClass X s β)) ↔
      ∀ (X : (SmoothProjective k).FullSubcategory) (r s : ℤ) (α : (chowCycleData k).group X r)
        (β : (chowCycleData k).group X s),
        cycleClass (prod X X) (r + s) (codimensionExteriorProduct k _ _ r s α β) =
          (S.H (prod X X)).evenCup r s (S.pullback (fst X X) (2 * r) (cycleClass X r α))
            (S.pullback (snd X X) (2 * s) (cycleClass X s β))
declarations.comment: given (C)(a), axiom (C)(c) is equivalent to compatibility of γ with exterior products, γ(α × β) = pr₁^*γ(α) ∪ pr₂^*γ(β) in H^*(X ×_k X), for the data of a classical Weil cohomology theory with cycle classes on the Chow groups of Chapter 42

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.diagonalPullback_kunneth
declarations.doc:
Pulling the Künneth exterior product `pr₁^*a ∪ pr₂^*b` back along the diagonal
`Δ : X ⟶ X × X` gives the cup product `a ∪ b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem diagonalPullback_kunneth (k : Type u) [Field k] (F : Type v) [Field F]
    (H : (SmoothProjective k).FullSubcategory → ExternallyGradedAlgebra.{v, w} F)
    (pullback : ∀ {X Y : (SmoothProjective k).FullSubcategory},
      (X ⟶ Y) → ∀ i : ℤ, (H Y).piece i →ₗ[F] (H X).piece i)
    (pullback_id : ∀ (X) (i : ℤ), pullback (𝟙 X) i = LinearMap.id)
    (pullback_comp : ∀ {X Y Z} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (i : ℤ),
      pullback (f ≫ g) i = (pullback f i).comp (pullback g i))
    (pullback_mul : ∀ {X Y} (f : X ⟶ Y) (i j : ℤ) (a : (H Y).piece i) (b : (H Y).piece j),
      pullback f (i + j) ((H Y).mul i j a b) =
        (H X).mul i j (pullback f i a) (pullback f j b))
    (X : (SmoothProjective k).FullSubcategory) [HasBinaryProduct X X]
    (i j : ℤ) (a : (H X).piece i) (b : (H X).piece j) :
    pullback (prod.lift (𝟙 X) (𝟙 X) : X ⟶ X ⨯ X) (i + j)
        ((H (X ⨯ X)).mul i j
          (pullback (prod.fst : X ⨯ X ⟶ X) i a) (pullback (prod.snd : X ⨯ X ⟶ X) j b)) =
      (H X).mul i j a b
declarations.comment: diagonal_pullback_cup
