declarations.name: SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras.determinant_isInvertible_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FJN].** The determinant of a flat sheaf of modules of finite presentation on
a ringed space is an invertible module.

Its hypotheses on `F` are exactly the source's: `F` is flat, in the sense
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat` that the source assumes, and of finite presentation.
Nothing is assumed about `det(F)`. Three statements stand behind it, each proved in this
repository: every stalk of `det(F)` is an invertible module
(`SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras.determinant_stalk_invertible`, with Tag 05NE
turning flatness of the sheaf into flatness of the stalks); `det(F)` is of finite presentation
(`isFinitePresentation_determinant_of_isFlat` above); and invertibility descends from the stalks
for a sheaf of modules of finite presentation
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.stalkwiseInvertibleDescent`).

**This is the whole covering set of Tag 0FJN.** The two other statements of the tag's
conclusion — `determinant_isInvertible` in
`StacksFrontier/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf/ExteriorAlgebraDeterminant.lean` and
`determinant_isInvertible_of_finitePresentationDescent` in
`StacksFrontier/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf/ExteriorAnnihilatorStalk.lean` — assume more than
this one and do not carry the attribute.

The statement lives here rather than beside
`determinant_stalk_invertible_of_isFlat`, which is where it was while the finite presentation of
`det(F)` was a hypothesis, because
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorDeterminantInvertible` cannot import the
file that proves that finite presentation: the closure of
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorPowerShortExact`, which this file needs
through the two retract conditions, makes `HasCoproduct` unsynthesizable in the coproduct
section of that file, where a family of sheaves of modules on a space is summed. That is a
pre-existing incompatibility between those two files and has nothing to do with the determinant;
it is recorded here because it is the reason for the split.
declarations.statement:
theorem determinant_isInvertible_of_isFlat {Y : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)) [G.IsFinitePresentation]
    (A : TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y.carrier) G)
    (hflat : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := Y.sheaf) G) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
      (Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf _ Y.presheaf
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u}) Y.IsSheaf) A.determinant
declarations.comment: flatness and finite presentation of F are its only hypotheses on F, which is what the source assumes, and it carries no hypothesis about det(F)

declarations.name: Ideal.exists_isRegular_generator_of_isCompl_cotangent
declarations.doc:
A direct summand of `I/I²` isomorphic to `R/I`, for an ideal `I` of finite projective
dimension in a Noetherian local ring, is generated by the class of a nonzerodivisor of `R`
belonging to `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRegular_generator_of_isCompl_cotangent
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : Module.projectiveDimension R I ≠ ⊤)
    (F : Submodule (R ⧸ I) I.Cotangent)
    (hF : ∃ F' : Submodule (R ⧸ I) I.Cotangent, IsCompl F F')
    (hFfree : Nonempty (F ≃ₗ[R ⧸ I] R ⧸ I)) :
    ∃ (x : R) (hx : x ∈ I), IsRegular x ∧
      Submodule.span (R ⧸ I) {I.toCotangent ⟨x, hx⟩} = F

declarations.name: Ideal.exists_isRegular_of_isCompl_cotangent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FJR, with the positive-rank properness correction.** A finite-rank
free direct summand of `I/I²`, for an ideal `I` of finite projective dimension in a Noetherian
local ring, lifts to a regular sequence in `I` whose residue classes generate that summand,
provided `I` is proper when the rank is positive.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRegular_of_isCompl_cotangent
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (r : ℕ) (F : Submodule (R ⧸ I) I.Cotangent)
    (hproper : r = 0 ∨ I ≠ ⊤)
    (hpd : Module.projectiveDimension R I ≠ ⊤)
    (hcompl : ∃ F' : Submodule (R ⧸ I) I.Cotangent, IsCompl F F')
    (hfree : Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin r) (R ⧸ I) F)) :
    ∃ x : Fin r → I,
      RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R (List.ofFn fun i ↦ (x i : R)) ∧
        Submodule.span (R ⧸ I) (Set.range fun i ↦ I.toCotangent (x i)) = F

declarations.name: Ideal.isRegular_of_projectiveDimension_ne_top_of_isFiniteLocallyFree_cotangent
declarations.doc:
An ideal of a Noetherian ring which has finite projective dimension and whose conormal
module is finite locally free over the quotient is a regular ideal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegular_of_projectiveDimension_ne_top_of_isFiniteLocallyFree_cotangent
    (I : Ideal R) (hpd : Module.projectiveDimension R I ≠ ⊤)
    (hconormal : Module.IsFiniteLocallyFree (R ⧸ I) I.Cotangent) : I.IsRegular

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.hasTorAmplitude_tfae_isLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a perfect ring homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Then the
naive cotangent complex `NL_{B/A}` has Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]` if and only if it is a perfect
object of `D(B)` with Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`, if and only if `A → B` is a local complete
intersection.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasTorAmplitude_tfae_isLocalCompleteIntersection
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra.Perfect A B] :
    List.TFAE
      [HasTorAmplitude
          (CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct B).tensor
          (canonicalTensorComparison B) (canonicalTensorIsLeftDerived B)
          (naiveCotangentObject A B) (-1) 0,
        StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect (naiveCotangentObject A B) ∧
          HasTorAmplitude
            (CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct B).tensor
            (canonicalTensorComparison B) (canonicalTensorIsLeftDerived B)
            (naiveCotangentObject A B) (-1) 0,
        RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (algebraMap A B)]

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.naiveCotangentComplex_quasiIso_baseChange_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FJU.** Let `A → B` be flat, let `A → A'` be arbitrary and let `B' = A' ⊗[A] B` be
the pushout, so that the square with corners `A, A', B, B'` is cocartesian. Then the canonical
map `NL_{B/A} ⊗_B B' → NL_{B'/A'}` is a quasi-isomorphism, and if in addition `NL_{B/A}` has Tor
amplitude in `[-1, 0]` then the derived base-change map `NL_{B/A} ⊗_B^L B' → NL_{B'/A'}` is a
quasi-isomorphism too.

The naive cotangent complexes are the two-term complexes `HomologicalComplex.double` of the
canonical presentations, in cohomological degrees `-1` and `0`, with their modules and rings
lifted to one universe. The map of the first assertion is the displayed chain map `g`; the map of
the second is that chain map composed with the comparison from derived to ordinary extension of
scalars, which is what makes the composite the derived base-change map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem naiveCotangentComplex_quasiIso_baseChange_of_flat
    {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB} {A' : Type uC}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing A'] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A A'] [Module.Flat A B] :
    let B' := A' ⊗[A] B
    letI : Algebra B B' := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    let P := Algebra.Generators.self A B
    let P' := Algebra.Generators.self A' B'
    let h := (P.defaultHom P').toExtensionHom
    let X₁ : ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B) :=
      ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B)
        (ULift.{max uA uB uC} P.toExtension.Cotangent)
    let X₀ : ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B) :=
      ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B)
        (ULift.{max uA uB uC} P.toExtension.CotangentSpace)
    let X₁' : ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B') :=
      ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B')
        (ULift.{max uA uB uC} P'.toExtension.Cotangent)
    let X₀' : ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B') :=
      ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B')
        (ULift.{max uA uB uC} P'.toExtension.CotangentSpace)
    let d : X₁ ⟶ X₀ := ModuleCat.ofHom {
      toFun := fun x => ULift.up (P.toExtension.cotangentComplex x.down)
      map_add' := by
        intro x y
        exact congrArg ULift.up (P.toExtension.cotangentComplex.map_add x.down y.down)
      map_smul' := by
        intro r x
        exact congrArg ULift.up (P.toExtension.cotangentComplex.map_smul r.down x.down) }
    let d' : X₁' ⟶ X₀' := ModuleCat.ofHom {
      toFun := fun x => ULift.up (P'.toExtension.cotangentComplex x.down)
      map_add' := by
        intro x y
        exact congrArg ULift.up (P'.toExtension.cotangentComplex.map_add x.down y.down)
      map_smul' := by
        intro r x
        exact congrArg ULift.up (P'.toExtension.cotangentComplex.map_smul r.down x.down) }
    let hd : (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel (-1) 0 := by decide
    let hne : (-1 : ℤ) ≠ 0 := by decide
    let K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B)) ℤ :=
      HomologicalComplex.double d hd
    let K' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B')) ℤ :=
      HomologicalComplex.double d' hd
    let E : ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B) ⥤
        ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B') :=
      ModuleCat.extendScalars.{max uA uB uC, max uA uB uC, max uA uB uC}
        ((algebraMap B B').ulift)
    let f₁ : E.obj X₁ ⟶ X₁' :=
      ModuleCat.ExtendRestrictScalarsAdj.HomEquiv.fromExtendScalars ((algebraMap B B').ulift)
        (ModuleCat.ofHom (Y := (ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((algebraMap B B').ulift)).obj X₁')
          { toFun := fun x => ULift.up (Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map h x.down)
            map_add' := by
              intro x y
              exact congrArg ULift.up ((Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map h).map_add x.down y.down)
            map_smul' := by
              intro r x
              change ULift.up _ = ULift.up _
              congr 1
              change (Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map h) (r.down • x.down) =
                (algebraMap B B' r.down) • (Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map h x.down)
              exact (Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map h).map_smul r.down x.down })
    let f₀ : E.obj X₀ ⟶ X₀' :=
      ModuleCat.ExtendRestrictScalarsAdj.HomEquiv.fromExtendScalars ((algebraMap B B').ulift)
        (ModuleCat.ofHom (Y := (ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((algebraMap B B').ulift)).obj X₀')
          { toFun := fun x => ULift.up (Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map h x.down)
            map_add' := by
              intro x y
              exact congrArg ULift.up
                ((Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map h).map_add x.down y.down)
            map_smul' := by
              intro r x
              change ULift.up _ = ULift.up _
              congr 1
              change (Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map h) (r.down • x.down) =
                (algebraMap B B' r.down) • (Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map h x.down)
              rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_smul]
              exact (Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map h).map_smul r.down x.down })
    ∀ (derivedTensor :
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B)) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B)) ⥤
            DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B)))
      (tensorComparison : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B),
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
              (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B)) 0).obj M) ⟶
          (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.tensorModuleRight M).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
      (tensorIsLeftDerived : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B),
        (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B))
            0).obj M)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
          (tensorComparison M)
          (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso
            (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
      (tensorCommShift : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B),
        (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B)) 0).obj M)).CommShift ℤ)
      (tensorTriangulated : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B),
        letI := tensorCommShift M
        (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B)) 0).obj M)).IsTriangulated)
      (derivedExtension :
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B)) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B')))
      (extensionComparison :
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ derivedExtension ⟶
          E.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
      (_extensionIsLeftDerived : derivedExtension.IsLeftDerivedFunctor extensionComparison
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso
          (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uC} (ULift.{max uA uB uC} B)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))),
    ∃ g : (E.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K ⟶ K',
      g.f (-1) =
          E.map (HomologicalComplex.doubleXIso₀ d hd).hom ≫ f₁ ≫
            (HomologicalComplex.doubleXIso₀ d' hd).inv ∧
        g.f 0 =
          E.map (HomologicalComplex.doubleXIso₁ d hd hne).hom ≫ f₀ ≫
            (HomologicalComplex.doubleXIso₁ d' hd hne).inv ∧
        QuasiIso g ∧
        (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor tensorComparison
            tensorIsLeftDerived (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) (-1) 0 →
          IsIso (extensionComparison.app K ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map g))

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.hasTorAmplitude_tfae_syntomic
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a flat ring homomorphism of finite presentation. Then the
naive cotangent complex `NL_{B/A}` has Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]` if and only if it is a perfect
object of `D(B)` with Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`, if and only if `A → B` is syntomic, if and only
if `A → B` is a local complete intersection.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasTorAmplitude_tfae_syntomic
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.FinitePresentation A B] :
    List.TFAE
      [HasTorAmplitude
          (CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct B).tensor
          (canonicalTensorComparison B) (canonicalTensorIsLeftDerived B)
          (naiveCotangentObject A B) (-1) 0,
        StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect (naiveCotangentObject A B) ∧
          HasTorAmplitude
            (CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct B).tensor
            (canonicalTensorComparison B) (canonicalTensorIsLeftDerived B)
            (naiveCotangentObject A B) (-1) 0,
        Algebra.Syntomic A B,
        RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (algebraMap A B)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.specDet
declarations.doc:
The determinant functor on `Spec R`, from the groupoid of perfect objects of `D(𝒪_{Spec R})` of
Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]` and their isomorphisms to the groupoid of invertible
`𝒪_{Spec R}`-modules and their isomorphisms.

It is the determinant of More on Algebra, Section 0FJI, transported along the identification of
the source groupoid with the ring-level one and along the associated-sheaf functor.
declarations.statement:
def specDet (R : CommRingCat.{u}) :
    Core (PerfectTwoTermAmplitude (Spec R)) ⥤ Core (InvertibleModuleCat (Spec R))
declarations.comment: the determinant functor, for an affine scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.specDelta
declarations.doc:
The canonical global section `δ(L)` of the determinant of a rank-zero object of the source
groupoid on `Spec R`: the canonical element of More on Algebra, Section 0FJI, read as a global
section.
declarations.statement:
def specDelta (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (L : PerfectTwoTermAmplitude (Spec R))
    (hL : IsRankZeroSpec R L) : Γ(((specDet R).obj ⟨L⟩).of.obj, ⊤)
declarations.comment:
the canonical global section δ(L) of the determinant of a rank-zero object, for an
affine scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.specDet_map_specDelta
declarations.doc:
For every isomorphism `a : L ⟶ K` of rank-zero objects of the source groupoid on `Spec R`,
`det(a)(δ(L)) = δ(K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem specDet_map_specDelta (R : CommRingCat.{u}) {L K : PerfectTwoTermAmplitude (Spec R)}
    (a : (⟨L⟩ : Core (PerfectTwoTermAmplitude (Spec R))) ⟶ ⟨K⟩)
    (hL : IsRankZeroSpec R L) (hK : IsRankZeroSpec R K) :
    Scheme.Modules.Hom.app
        ((IsInvertibleProperty (Spec R)).ι.map ((specDet R).map a).iso.hom) ⊤
        (specDelta R L hL) = specDelta R K hK
declarations.comment:
the compatibility det(a)(δ(L)) = δ(K) of the canonical global section with
isomorphisms, for an affine scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.specDetPresentationIso
declarations.doc:
The determinant on `Spec R` of an object of the source groupoid is the sheaf associated with
the determinant line of More on Algebra, Section 0FJI of any two-term finite-projective
presentation of the corresponding complex of `R`-modules. Such a presentation always exists,
`TwoTermDeterminant.presentation` being one.
declarations.statement:
def specDetPresentationIso (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (L : PerfectTwoTermAmplitude (Spec R))
    (P : TwoTermPresentation (sourceComplex R L).obj) :
    letI := P.finite (-1)
    letI := P.projective (-1)
    letI := P.finite 0
    letI := P.projective 0
    ((specDet R).obj ⟨L⟩).of.obj ≅
      tilde (ModuleCat.of R
        (TwoTermComplex.determinantLine (P.complex.d (-1) 0).hom))
declarations.comment:
the construction is locally the one of More on Algebra, Section 0FJI: on an affine
scheme the determinant is the determinant line of a two-term finite-projective presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.specDetPresentationIso_specDelta
declarations.doc:
Under the identification of the determinant with the determinant line of a rank-zero two-term
finite-projective presentation, the canonical global section is the canonical element of More on
Algebra, Section 0FJI of that presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem specDetPresentationIso_specDelta (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (L : PerfectTwoTermAmplitude (Spec R)) (P : TwoTermPresentation (sourceComplex R L).obj)
    (hP : P.IsRankZero) (hL : IsRankZeroSpec R L) :
    letI := P.finite (-1)
    letI := P.projective (-1)
    letI := P.finite 0
    letI := P.projective 0
    Scheme.Modules.Hom.app (specDetPresentationIso R L P).hom ⊤ (specDelta R L hL) =
      (tilde.toOpen (ModuleCat.of R
        (TwoTermComplex.determinantLine (P.complex.d (-1) 0).hom)) ⊤).hom
          (TwoTermComplex.delta (P.complex.d (-1) 0).hom hP)
declarations.comment:
the canonical global section is locally the canonical element of More on Algebra,
Section 0FJI: on an affine scheme it is the determinant of the differential of a two-term
finite-projective presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.determinantFunctor
declarations.doc:
The determinant functor on an arbitrary scheme, from the groupoid of perfect objects of
`D(𝒪_X)` of Tor-amplitude in `[-1, 0]` and their isomorphisms to the groupoid of invertible
`𝒪_X`-modules and their isomorphisms.

The value at `L` is the invertible module glued from the determinants of `L` on the affine opens
of `X`, and the value at an isomorphism is glued from the determinants of its restrictions to the
affine charts.
declarations.statement:
def determinantFunctor (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    Core (PerfectTwoTermAmplitude X) ⥤ Core (InvertibleModuleCat X)
declarations.comment:
part (1): the determinant functor, from the groupoid of perfect objects of Tor
amplitude in [-1, 0] and their isomorphisms to the groupoid of invertible modules and their
isomorphisms, on an arbitrary scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.determinantSection
declarations.doc:
The canonical global section `δ(L)` of the determinant of a rank-zero perfect object of
`D(𝒪_X)` of Tor-amplitude in `[-1, 0]` on an arbitrary scheme: the global section glued from the
canonical elements of More on Algebra, Section 0FJI on the affine charts, which are matched by the
chart comparisons.
declarations.statement:
def determinantSection {L : PerfectTwoTermAmplitude X} (hL : IsRankZeroOn L) :
    Γ(((determinantFunctor X).obj ⟨L⟩).of.obj, ⊤)
declarations.comment:
part (2): the canonical global section δ(L) of the determinant of a rank-zero
object, on an arbitrary scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.determinantChartPresentationIso
declarations.doc:
On an affine open `V` of an arbitrary scheme `X` the determinant of `L` is the sheaf
associated with the determinant line of More on Algebra, Section 0FJI of *any* two-term
finite-projective presentation `P` of the complex of `Γ(X, V)`-modules that `L` restricts to on the
chart of `V`: the restriction of the determinant to `V` is the pullback along
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.isoSpec` of that associated sheaf.

The isomorphism is the glueing comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineOpensGlue.ChartComparison.chartIso` of the datum, followed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.chartDetPresentationIso`.
declarations.statement:
def determinantChartPresentationIso (L : PerfectTwoTermAmplitude X) (V : X.affineOpens)
    (P : TwoTermPresentation (chartComplex L V).obj) :
    letI := P.finite (-1)
    letI := P.projective (-1)
    letI := P.finite 0
    letI := P.projective 0
    Scheme.Modules.restrict ((determinantFunctor X).obj ⟨L⟩).of.obj
        (AffineOpensGlue.chart X V) ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback V.2.isoSpec.hom).obj
        (tilde (ModuleCat.of Γ(X, (V.1 : X.Opens))
          (TwoTermComplex.determinantLine (P.complex.d (-1) 0).hom)))
declarations.comment:
part (3): the construction is affine locally the one of More on Algebra, Section
0FJI — on an affine open of an arbitrary scheme the determinant is the determinant line of a
two-term finite-projective presentation of the complex the object restricts to there

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.determinantFunctor_map_determinantSection
declarations.doc:
For every isomorphism `a : L ⟶ K` of rank-zero perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)` of Tor-amplitude in
`[-1, 0]` on an arbitrary scheme `X`, the determinant of `a` carries the canonical global section
of the determinant of `L` to that of `K`: `det(a)(δ(L)) = δ(K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem determinantFunctor_map_determinantSection {L K : PerfectTwoTermAmplitude X}
    (a : (⟨L⟩ : Core (PerfectTwoTermAmplitude X)) ⟶ ⟨K⟩)
    (hL : IsRankZeroOn L) (hK : IsRankZeroOn K) :
    Scheme.Modules.Hom.app
        ((IsInvertibleProperty X).ι.map ((determinantFunctor X).map a).iso.hom) ⊤
        (determinantSection hL) = determinantSection hK
declarations.comment:
part (2): the compatibility det(a)(δ(L)) = δ(K) of the canonical global section with
isomorphisms, on an arbitrary scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.determinantChartPresentationIso_determinantSection
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a scheme, `L` a rank-zero perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` of Tor-amplitude in `[-1, 0]`,
`V` an affine open of `X` and `P` a rank-zero two-term finite-projective presentation of the
complex of `Γ(X, V)`-modules that `L` restricts to on the chart of `V`. Then the canonical global
section `δ(L)` of the determinant of `L`, restricted to `V` and read on the chart of `V` through
`AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.chartDetRestrictPresentationIso`, is the canonical element of
More on Algebra, Section 0FJI of `P` — the determinant of the differential of `P` — read as a
global section of the associated sheaf of the determinant line and restricted to the image open.

So the construction is affine locally the one of More on Algebra, Section 0FJI, canonical element
included: `δ(L)` reads on an affine open as `TwoTermComplex.delta` of the differential of any
two-term finite-projective presentation there.
declarations.statement:
theorem determinantChartPresentationIso_determinantSection {L : PerfectTwoTermAmplitude X}
    (hL : IsRankZeroOn L) (V : X.affineOpens)
    (P : TwoTermPresentation (chartComplex L V).obj) (hP : P.IsRankZero) :
    letI := P.finite (-1)
    letI := P.projective (-1)
    letI := P.finite 0
    letI := P.projective 0
    Scheme.Modules.Hom.app (chartDetRestrictPresentationIso L V P).hom
        ((V.1 : X.Opens).ι ⁻¹ᵁ (V.1 : X.Opens))
        ((chartComparison L).chartSec V (V.1 : X.Opens)
          ((chartComparison L).glued.val.map (homOfLE le_top).op (determinantSection hL))) =
      (tilde (ModuleCat.of Γ(X, (V.1 : X.Opens))
          (TwoTermComplex.determinantLine (P.complex.d (-1) 0).hom))).val.map
        (homOfLE (le_top :
          V.2.isoSpec.hom ''ᵁ ((V.1 : X.Opens).ι ⁻¹ᵁ (V.1 : X.Opens)) ≤ ⊤)).op
        ((tilde.toOpen (ModuleCat.of Γ(X, (V.1 : X.Opens))
          (TwoTermComplex.determinantLine (P.complex.d (-1) 0).hom)) ⊤).hom
          (TwoTermComplex.delta (P.complex.d (-1) 0).hom hP))
declarations.comment:
part (3): the canonical global section is affine locally the canonical element of
More on Algebra, Section 0FJI — on an affine open of an arbitrary scheme it is the determinant of
the differential of a two-term finite-projective presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.pullbackDeterminantIso
declarations.doc:
**The determinant functor commutes with pullback.** For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` and
a perfect object `K` of `D(𝒪_Y)` of Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`, the canonical identification
`f^* det(K) ≅ det(Lf^*K)` of the values of the determinant functor of Stacks 0FJX.
declarations.comment:
(b) the canonical identification f^*det(K) → det(Lf^*K), for the determinant
functor of Lemma 0FJX (determinantFunctor)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.pullbackDeterminantIso_hom_pullbackSection
declarations.doc:
**The identification `f^* det(K) ≅ det(Lf^*K)` is canonical: on affine opens it is the base
change of local determinants.** For affine opens `V ⊆ Y` and `W ⊆ f⁻¹V`, it sends the pullback of
a section `a` of `det(K)` over `V` to the section of `det(Lf^*K)` over `W` which is the image of
`a ∈ det(M_V)` under the base change `det(M_V) → Γ(X, W) ⊗_{Γ(Y, V)} det(M_V) = det(M'_W)` of the
determinants of More on Algebra, Section 0FJI; the sections over affine opens are read as
determinant modules through `globalDetSectionsEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackDeterminantIso_hom_pullbackSection (V : Y.affineOpens) (W : X.affineOpens)
    (h : (W : X.Opens) ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (a : Γ(((determinantFunctor Y).obj ⟨K⟩).of.obj, V)) :
    (globalDetSectionsEquiv (pullbackObj f K) W).symm
        ((pullbackDeterminantIso f K).hom.val.app (op (W : X.Opens))
          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackSection f _ V W h a)) =
      pullbackDetMap f K V W h ((globalDetSectionsEquiv K V).symm a)
declarations.comment:
(b) the identification f^*det(K) → det(Lf^*K) is canonical: over affine opens
W ⊆ f⁻¹V it is the base change of the determinant of More on Algebra 0FJI of the complex
representing K over V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.pullbackDeterminantIso_hom_determinantSection
declarations.doc:
**The canonical global section pulls back to the canonical global section.** If `K` has rank
zero, the identification `f^* det(K) ≅ det(Lf^*K)` carries the pullback of the canonical global
section `δ(K)` of Stacks 0FJX to `δ(Lf^*K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackDeterminantIso_hom_determinantSection {K : PerfectTwoTermAmplitude Y}
    (hK : IsRankZeroOn K) :
    (pullbackDeterminantIso f K).hom.val.app (op ⊤)
        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackSection f _ ⊤ ⊤ le_top (determinantSection hK)) =
      determinantSection (isRankZeroOn_pullbackObj f hK)
declarations.comment:
(c) if K has rank 0, δ(K) pulls back to δ(Lf^*K) via f^*det(K) → det(Lf^*K), for
the determinant functor of Lemma 0FJX and its canonical section (determinantSection)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeterminantTwoTerm.isPerfectTwoTermAmplitude_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**The source category is preserved by derived pullback.** For a morphism of schemes
`f : X ⟶ Y`, the derived pullback `Lf^*K` of a perfect object `K` of `D(𝒪_Y)` of Tor amplitude in
`[-1, 0]` is again perfect of Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectTwoTermAmplitude_derivedPullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (K : DerivedCategory Y.Modules) (hK : IsPerfectTwoTermAmplitude Y K) :
    IsPerfectTwoTermAmplitude X
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K)
declarations.comment: the derived pullback lands in the source category

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.quasiIso_baseChangeMapOfComparison_of_flat_base
declarations.doc:
**Flat base change.**  For a cartesian square of schemes whose lower horizontal morphism
`g : Y' ⟶ Y` is flat, the canonical comparison `(g')^*NL_{X/Y} ⟶ NL_{X'/Y'}`, taken against the
canonical base-ring comparison `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison` of the
square, is a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_baseChangeMapOfComparison_of_flat_base (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g) [AlgebraicGeometry.Flat g] :
    QuasiIso (baseChangeMapOfComparison f f' g'
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison f f' g' g hsq.w)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison_comp f f' g' g hsq.w))
declarations.comment: the flat-base-change quasi-isomorphism, with no hypotheses beyond a CARTESIAN square (`hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g`) and `[Flat g]`. The canonical map is CONSTRUCTED, not assumed: `Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.baseChangeMapOfComparison` is the source's own composite of the [Stacks, Tag 08TM] identification of `(g')^*NL_{X/Y}` with a base change (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.pulledNaiveCotangentComparison`), the base-change map `NL_{B/A} (x)_B C -> NL_{C/A}` of [Stacks, Tag 0E1Y] (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.spaceBaseChangeNaiveCotangentMap`) for the tower `(g')^-1 f^-1 O_Y -> (g')^-1 O_X -> O_{X'}`, and the relative map `NL_{C/A} -> NL_{C/B}` (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.spaceRelativeNaiveCotangentComplexMap`) for the tower through `(f')^-1 O_{Y'}`. The base-ring comparison it is taken against is the CANONICAL one of the square, `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison`, together with its compatibility `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison_comp`; it is built from the square and is not a `Classical.choose` of a non-unique existence statement. PROVED: the construction of the map; the degreewise vanishing outside degrees -1 and 0 (`isZero_pulledComplex_X`); the reduction of quasi-isomorphy to the stalks (`quasiIso_baseChangeMapOfComparison_of_forall_stalk`, resting on [Stacks, Tag 08TL] `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.quasiIso_of_forall_stalk_quasiIso`); and the stalkwise statement itself, `Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChangeStalk.quasiIso_stalkFunctor_map_baseChangeMapOfComparison`. That stalkwise statement is `Stacks.NaiveCotangentTowerStalk.quasiIso_stalkFunctor_map_towerComposite` fed with the ring-level flat base change `NaiveCotangent.isQuasiIso_nlExtensionBaseChangeMap_of_flat_base` ([Stacks, Tag 00S4]), read through the stalk identification of the naive cotangent complex ([Stacks, Tag 0D09], `Stacks.SheafOfModules.stalkLegNegOne` / `stalkLegZero` / `stalkLeg_d`). Its two ring-level inputs are both discharged here: the flatness of the stalk of the canonical base-ring comparison, which `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.stalkFunctor_map_baseRingComparison` identifies with the stalk map of `g` conjugated by three isomorphisms and which Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.stalkMap` then makes flat, so `[Flat g]` does work here and is not decorative; and the identification of `O_{X',x'}` as a localization of `O_{Y',y'} (x)_{O_{Y,y}} O_{X,x}`, which is `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.stalk_isLocalization_of_isPullback_inverseImage_comm` ([Stacks, Tag 01JR]) and is the one place cartesianness of the square is used. SCOPE: the statement is about the undecorated comparison `(g')^*NL_{X/Y} -> NL_{X'/Y'}`; nothing is claimed here about the derived pullback `L(g')^*NL_{X/Y}`

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentDerivedFlatBaseChange.isIso_derivedBaseChangeMapOfComparison_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FK0, the derived clause.**  For a cartesian square of schemes whose right vertical
morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` is flat and whose naive cotangent complex `NL_{X/Y}` has Tor amplitude in
`[-1, 0]`, the canonical derived comparison `L(g')^*NL_{X/Y} ⟶ NL_{X'/Y'}` is an isomorphism in
`D(𝒪_{X'})`.

The Tor amplitude makes `NL_{X/Y}` K-flat, so the comparison `L(g')^*NL_{X/Y} ⟶ (g')^*NL_{X/Y}`
is invertible by Stacks 06YJ; the remaining factor is the base change map of complexes, which is
a quasi-isomorphism by the first clause.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedBaseChangeMapOfComparison_of_flat (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g) [AlgebraicGeometry.Flat f]
    (htor : Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0) :
    IsIso (derivedBaseChangeMapOfComparison f f' g'
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison f f' g' g hsq.w)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison_comp f f' g' g hsq.w))
declarations.comment: the SECOND clause -- the DERIVED comparison `L(g')^* NL_{X/Y} -> NL_{X'/Y'}` is a quasi-isomorphism when `NL_{X/Y}` has tor-amplitude in [-1,0] -- with no hypotheses beyond a CARTESIAN square (`hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g`), `[Flat f]` and that tor-amplitude. The first clause is `Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.quasiIso_baseChangeMapOfComparison_of_flat_algebra`. The DERIVED PULLBACK is not assumed: it is `Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback`, the total left derived functor of termwise pullback of [Stacks, Tag 06YJ], which exists for every morphism of ringed spaces, and the comparison `L(g')^* K -> (g')^* K` at a complex is `Stacks.DerivedPullback.Composition.derivedPullbackComparisonOnComplex`. TOR AMPLITUDE is the ringed-space notion of [Stacks, Tag 08CG], `Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude`, tested against EVERY `O_X`-module. The map is CONSTRUCTED, not assumed: `derivedBaseChangeMapOfComparison` is the Tag 06YJ comparison, then the identification `pulledComplexIso` of Mathlib's termwise pullback with the inverse-image-then-extend-scalars model, then the first clause's map of complexes `Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.baseChangeMapOfComparison`, taken against the CANONICAL base-ring comparison `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison` of the square. PROVED HERE: that `NL_{X/Y}` is K-flat under the tor-amplitude hypothesis (`kFlat_naiveCotangentComplex_of_hasTorAmplitude`), which is the whole content of the clause beyond the first -- its degree 0 term is flat because each stalk is the free cotangent space of the canonical presentation of the stalk map (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFlat_naiveCotangentComplex_X_zero`, [Stacks, Tag 05NE] plus `Algebra.Generators.cotangentSpaceBasis`), so its degree -1 term is flat by the ringed-space form of [Stacks, Tag 0653] (`Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.DoubleFlat.isFlat_X_negOne_of_hasTorAmplitude`, the stupid filtration of a two-term complex fed to [Stacks, Tag 08CJ] (1)), and a bounded-above complex of flat modules is K-flat by [Stacks, Tag 06YQ]; and that a K-flat complex inverts the Tag 06YJ comparison (`isIso_derivedPullbackComparisonOnComplex_of_kFlat`). The two models of `(g')^*` are identified by `RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullbackIsoTwoStep`, proved here from uniqueness of left adjoints, which closes the input that `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/EtaleAlgebra/FlatBaseChange/StructureSheaf.lean` had recorded as open. SCOPE: the undecorated first clause is on `Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.quasiIso_baseChangeMapOfComparison_of_flat_algebra`; the two declarations together are the whole tag

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.quasiIso_baseChangeMapOfComparison_of_flat_algebra
declarations.doc:
**Base change along a flat morphism.**  For a cartesian square of schemes whose right
vertical morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` is flat, the canonical comparison `(g')^*NL_{X/Y} ⟶ NL_{X'/Y'}`,
taken against the canonical base-ring comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison` of the square, is a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_baseChangeMapOfComparison_of_flat_algebra (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g' : X' ⟶ X) (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g) [AlgebraicGeometry.Flat f] :
    QuasiIso (baseChangeMapOfComparison f f' g'
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison f f' g' g hsq.w)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison_comp f f' g' g hsq.w))
declarations.comment: the FIRST clause -- the quasi-isomorphism when `X -> Y` is flat -- with no hypotheses beyond a CARTESIAN square (`hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g`) and `[Flat f]`. The canonical map is CONSTRUCTED, not assumed, exactly as on `Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.quasiIso_baseChangeMapOfComparison_of_flat_base`: `Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.baseChangeMapOfComparison` is the source's own composite of the [Stacks, Tag 08TM] identification of `(g')^*NL_{X/Y}` with a base change (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.pulledNaiveCotangentComparison`), the base-change map `NL_{B/A} (x)_B C -> NL_{C/A}` of [Stacks, Tag 0E1Y] (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.spaceBaseChangeNaiveCotangentMap`) for the tower `(g')^-1 f^-1 O_Y -> (g')^-1 O_X -> O_{X'}`, and the relative map `NL_{C/A} -> NL_{C/B}` (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.spaceRelativeNaiveCotangentComplexMap`) for the tower through `(f')^-1 O_{Y'}`. The base-ring comparison it is taken against is the CANONICAL one of the square, `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison`, together with its compatibility `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison_comp`; it is built from the square and is not a `Classical.choose` of a non-unique existence statement. PROVED: the construction of the map; the degreewise vanishing outside degrees -1 and 0 (`isZero_pulledComplex_X`); the reduction of quasi-isomorphy to the stalks (`quasiIso_baseChangeMapOfComparison_of_forall_stalk`, resting on [Stacks, Tag 08TL] `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.quasiIso_of_forall_stalk_quasiIso`); and the stalkwise statement itself, `Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatAlgebraBaseChangeStalk` `.quasiIso_stalkFunctor_map_baseChangeMapOfComparison`. That stalkwise statement is `Stacks.NaiveCotangentTowerStalk.quasiIso_stalkFunctor_map_towerComposite` fed with the ring-level base change for a flat algebra `NaiveCotangent.isQuasiIso_nlExtensionBaseChangeMap_of_flat_algebra`, read through the stalk identification of the naive cotangent complex ([Stacks, Tag 0D09] / [Stacks, Tag 0098]). That ring-level statement is proved here from the two elementwise inputs of [Stacks, Tag 0FJU]: surjectivity on the degree -1 cycles and bijectivity on the cokernels, which hold for an arbitrary base change by [Stacks, Tag 0FUZ] (`NaiveCotangent.naiveCotangentComplex_baseChange_homology`), and injectivity on those cycles, which is what flatness of the algebra buys (`NaiveCotangent.cotangent_intrinsic_baseChange_cycle_injective_of_flat`); then flat base change to the pushout is composed with localization of the target over a fixed base ([Stacks, Tag 00S7]). Its two geometric inputs are both discharged here: the flatness of the stalk of the first map of the tower, which `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.stalkInverseImageBaseRingIso_hom_comp_stalkMap` identifies with the stalk map of `f` conjugated by two isomorphisms and which Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.stalkMap` then makes flat, so `[Flat f]` does work here and is not decorative; and the identification of `O_{X',x'}` as a localization of `O_{Y',y'} (x)_{O_{Y,y}} O_{X,x}`, which is `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.stalk_isLocalization_of_isPullback_inverseImage_comm` ([Stacks, Tag 01JR]) and is the one place cartesianness of the square is used. SCOPE: the statement is about the undecorated comparison `(g')^*NL_{X/Y} -> NL_{X'/Y'}`, which is the tag's first clause; nothing is claimed here about the tag's second clause, the DERIVED comparison `L(g')^*NL_{X/Y} -> NL_{X'/Y'}` under Tor amplitude in [-1,0]

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isRegularImmersion_of_perfect_of_conormalSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0FK1.**  An immersion `i : X ⟶ Y` which is perfect, whose target is locally
Noetherian and whose conormal sheaf is finite locally free, is a regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularImmersion_of_perfect_of_conormalSheaf (i : X ⟶ Y) [IsImmersion i]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.Perfect i] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
      (Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf i)] :
    IsRegularImmersion i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FK2, the implication (1) ⇒ (2).** If a perfect morphism of locally Noetherian
schemes is a local complete intersection morphism, then `NL_{X/Y}` has Tor amplitude in
`[-1, 0]`.

The three standing hypotheses are not used: Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]` holds for the naive
cotangent complex of any local complete intersection morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex_of_perfect {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [Perfect f]
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0
declarations.comment: (1) ⇒ (2): for a perfect morphism of locally Noetherian schemes which is a local complete intersection morphism, NL_{X/Y} has tor-amplitude in [-1,0]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FK2, the implication (1) ⇒ (3).** If a perfect morphism of locally Noetherian
schemes is a local complete intersection morphism, then `NL_{X/Y}` is perfect with Tor amplitude
in `[-1, 0]`.

The three standing hypotheses are not used: both conditions hold for the naive cotangent complex
of any local complete intersection morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex_of_perfect {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [Perfect f]
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace)
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
      Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0
declarations.comment: (1) ⇒ (3): for a perfect morphism of locally Noetherian schemes which is a local complete intersection morphism, NL_{X/Y} is perfect with tor-amplitude in [-1,0]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.naiveCotangentComplex_tfae_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FK2.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a perfect morphism of locally Noetherian schemes. The
following are equivalent:

1. `f` is a local complete intersection morphism;
2. `NL_{X/Y}` has Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`;
3. `NL_{X/Y}` is perfect with Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.

Here `NL_{X/Y}` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex`, Stacks 0D0H, read at its
class in `D(𝒪_X)`; Tor amplitude is `Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude`, Stacks
08CG, taken against the canonical derived tensor product of a ringed space, and perfectness is
`Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect`, Stacks 08CM. Both are stated at the underlying
ringed space of `X`, with the standard derived category, as they are for Stacks 08E9 and Stacks
08EB.

Rendered on sections over a compatible pair of affine opens the statement is Stacks 0FJT; the
translation is Stacks 07DB and Stacks 0D0I together with Stacks 08E9 and Stacks 08EB.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentComplex_tfae_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [Perfect f] :
    List.TFAE
      [IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f,
        Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0,
        Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace)
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
          Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_iff_syntomic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FK3, the equivalence of (1) and (2).** A flat morphism of finite presentation is a
local complete intersection morphism exactly when it is syntomic.

Finite presentation is a standing hypothesis of the source and is not used: the equivalence holds
for any flat morphism, by Stacks 069K.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_iff_syntomic {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Flat f] (_hfp : FinitePresentation f) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f ↔ Syntomic f
declarations.comment: (1) ⇔ (2): a flat morphism of finite presentation is a local complete intersection morphism iff it is syntomic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex_of_isPerfect_of_hasTorAmplitude
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FK3, the implication (4) ⇒ (3).** If `NL_{X/Y}` is perfect with Tor amplitude in
`[-1, 0]`, then it has Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.

The implication is a projection, as it is in the source. The declaration's purpose is to pin
conditions (3) and (4) of the tag to `Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude` of Stacks
08CG, taken against the canonical derived tensor product of Stacks 06YU, and to
`Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect` of Stacks 08CM; the tree carries several further
spellings of each. The tag's standing hypotheses are not needed, so the statement is made for an
arbitrary morphism of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex_of_isPerfect_of_hasTorAmplitude
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace)
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
      Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0
declarations.comment: (4) ⇒ (3), which is a projection: NL_{X/Y} perfect with tor-amplitude in [-1,0] has tor-amplitude in [-1,0]. Fixes which library predicates conditions (3) and (4) are read at

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FK3, the implication (1) ⇒ (3).** If a flat morphism of finite presentation is a
local complete intersection morphism, then `NL_{X/Y}` has Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.

The two standing hypotheses are not used: Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]` holds for the naive
cotangent complex of any local complete intersection morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex_of_flat {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Flat f] (_hfp : FinitePresentation f) (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0
declarations.comment: (1) ⇒ (3): for a flat morphism of finite presentation which is a local complete intersection morphism, NL_{X/Y} has tor-amplitude in [-1,0]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FK3, the implication (1) ⇒ (4).** If a flat morphism of finite presentation is a
local complete intersection morphism, then `NL_{X/Y}` is perfect with Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.

The two standing hypotheses are not used: both conditions hold for the naive cotangent complex
of any local complete intersection morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex_of_flat {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [Flat f] (_hfp : FinitePresentation f)
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace)
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
      Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0
declarations.comment: (1) ⇒ (4): for a flat morphism of finite presentation which is a local complete intersection morphism, NL_{X/Y} is perfect with tor-amplitude in [-1,0]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.syntomic_of_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FK3, the implication (3) ⇒ (2).** A flat morphism of finite presentation whose
naive cotangent complex has Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]` is syntomic.

Syntomicity is a condition at each point of the source, asking for affine opens `V ∋ x` of `X`
and `U` of `Y` with `V ⊆ f⁻¹(U)` over which the morphism is syntomic on sections. On such a pair
the hypothesis descends to Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]` of `NL_{Γ(X, V)/Γ(Y, U)}` in
`D(Γ(X, V))`, and `Γ(Y, U) → Γ(X, V)` is flat of finite presentation, so Stacks 0FJV makes it
syntomic. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem syntomic_of_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Flat f] (hfp : FinitePresentation f)
    (hamp : Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0) :
    Syntomic f
declarations.comment: (3) ⇒ (2): a flat morphism of finite presentation whose naive cotangent complex has tor-amplitude in [-1,0] is syntomic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FK3, the implication (3) ⇒ (1).** A flat morphism of finite presentation whose
naive cotangent complex has Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]` is a local complete intersection
morphism: it is syntomic, and a syntomic morphism is Koszul by Stacks 069K.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Flat f] (hfp : FinitePresentation f)
    (hamp : Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f
declarations.comment: (3) ⇒ (1): a flat morphism of finite presentation whose naive cotangent complex has tor-amplitude in [-1,0] is a local complete intersection morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.naiveCotangentComplex_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FK3.** For a flat morphism of finite presentation `f : X ⟶ Y` the following are
equivalent: `f` is a local complete intersection morphism; `f` is syntomic; `NL_{X/Y}` has Tor
amplitude in `[-1, 0]`; `NL_{X/Y}` is perfect with Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentComplex_tfae {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Flat f] (hfp : FinitePresentation f) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f,
        Syntomic f,
        Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0,
        Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace)
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
          Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NoTraceOnOneForms.two_mul_x_dy_not_mem_span
declarations.doc: The form `2 x dy` does not lie in the `B`-span of the differentials of `x²`, `xy` and `y²`.
declarations.statement:
theorem two_mul_x_dy_not_mem_span :
    (2 : B) • (x • KaehlerDifferential.D ℂ B y) ∉
      Submodule.span B
        ({KaehlerDifferential.D ℂ B (x * x),
          KaehlerDifferential.D ℂ B (x * y),
          KaehlerDifferential.D ℂ B (y * y)} : Set Ω[B⁄ℂ])
declarations.comment: failure of descent for one-forms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NoTraceOnOneForms.two_mul_x_dy_not_mem_range
declarations.doc: Twice the invariant one-form does not come from the invariant ring.

      LinearMap.range (KaehlerDifferential.map ℂ ℂ A B)
declarations.comment: failure of the differential map to capture the invariant form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_dense_opens_etale_universalQuasiFiniteMorphism

        Etale (V.ι ≫ universalQuasiFiniteMorphism n d)
