declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPullback_universalQuasiFiniteMorphismLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FKA.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of schemes satisfying the
equivalent conditions of Stacks 0BWE (locally quasi-finite and syntomic). Then for every point
`y` of `Y` there are integers `n, d ≥ 1`, opens `U ⊆ X` and `V ⊆ Y` with `y ∈ V` and
`f(V) ⊆ U`, and a commutative diagram
```
Y ← V → Y_{n, d}
↓   ↓      ↓
X ← U → X_{n, d}
```
whose left-hand square is formed by the open immersions and the restriction `f.resLE U V hVU`,
and whose right-hand square, over the family `Y_{n, d} ⟶ X_{n, d}` of Example 0FK8, is
cartesian. The schemes may live in any universe `u`; the family `Y_{n, d} ⟶ X_{n, d}` is then
`universalQuasiFiniteMorphismLift`, the family of Example 0FK8 built over the universe lift of
the coefficient ring `ℤ[a_{i, E}]` (see `universalQuotientRingLiftEquiv`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPullback_universalQuasiFiniteMorphismLift {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X}
    (hqf : LocallyQuasiFinite f) (hsyn : Syntomic f) (y : Y) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (V : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ V) (hVU : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (n d : ℕ)
      (_ : NeZero n) (_ : NeZero d) (p : U.toScheme ⟶ universalBaseSchemeLift.{u} n d)
      (q : V.toScheme ⟶ universalQuasiFiniteSchemeLift.{u} n d),
      IsPullback (f.resLE U V hVU) q p (universalQuasiFiniteMorphismLift.{u} n d)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_square_presentation_hasJacobianDelta
declarations.doc:
Around every point of the source of a locally quasi-finite syntomic morphism of schemes there
is a square relative global complete intersection presentation `B = A[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_n)`
with the local Jacobian picture of the determinant of its naive cotangent complex: the conormal
module is free on the classes of the relations, the differential is the Jacobian matrix in that
basis and the basis `dxᵢ`, the determinant line is free of rank one on the generator matching
those two bases, and the canonical section is the Jacobian determinant times that generator.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_square_presentation_hasJacobianDelta {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X}
    (hqf : LocallyQuasiFinite f) (hf : Syntomic f) (y : Y) :
    ∃ (V : Y.affineOpens) (U : X.affineOpens) (_ : y ∈ V.1) (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1),
      letI : Algebra Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) := (f.appLE U.1 V.1 hVU).hom.toAlgebra
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (P : Algebra.Presentation Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) (Fin n) (Fin n))
          (hP : P.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection),
        letI := hP
        P.HasJacobianDelta
declarations.comment:
the local picture around a point of the source of a locally quasi-finite
syntomic morphism; the presentation is chosen by Tag 0BWE part (5)

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.toMatrix_cotangentComplex_eq_relationJacobiMatrix
declarations.doc:
In a basis of the conormal module given by the classes of the relations and the basis `dxᵢ`
of the cotangent space, the differential of the naive cotangent complex is the Jacobian matrix.
declarations.statement:
theorem Presentation.toMatrix_cotangentComplex_eq_relationJacobiMatrix
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) B P.toExtension.Cotangent)
    (hb : ∀ i, b i = Extension.Cotangent.mk ⟨P.relation i, P.relation_mem_ker i⟩) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix b P.cotangentSpaceBasis P.toExtension.cotangentComplex =
      P.relationJacobiMatrix
declarations.comment:
NL_{B/A} is the two-term complex (f)/(f)^2 -> sum_i B dx_i: its differential,
in the basis of the relation classes and the basis dx_i, is the matrix df_j/dx_i

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.isRankZero_cotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
The naive cotangent complex of a relative global complete intersection with as many relations
as variables has rank zero: both of its terms are free of rank the number of variables.
declarations.statement:
theorem Presentation.isRankZero_cotangentComplex :
    TwoTermComplex.IsRankZero P.toExtension.cotangentComplex
declarations.comment: the two terms of NL_{B/A} have equal rank, so delta(NL_{B/A}) is defined

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.cotangentDeterminantBasis
declarations.doc:
The determinant line of the naive cotangent complex of a relative global complete
intersection with as many relations as variables, as a free module of rank one on the
isomorphism matching a basis of the conormal module with the basis `dxᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Presentation.cotangentDeterminantBasis
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) B P.toExtension.Cotangent) :
    Module.Basis (Fin 1) B (TwoTermComplex.determinantLine P.toExtension.cotangentComplex)
declarations.comment: det(L_{B/A}) is free of rank one

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.coe_cotangentDeterminantBasis_apply
declarations.doc:
The generator of the determinant line of the naive cotangent complex carries the wedge of the
classes of the relations to the wedge of the `dxᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Presentation.coe_cotangentDeterminantBasis_apply
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) B P.toExtension.Cotangent)
    (hb : ∀ i, b i = Extension.Cotangent.mk ⟨P.relation i, P.relation_mem_ker i⟩) (k : Fin 1)
    (x : ProjectiveDeterminant.module (R := B) (M := P.toExtension.Cotangent))
    (hx : (x : ExteriorAlgebra B P.toExtension.Cotangent) =
      ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti B n
        fun j ↦ Extension.Cotangent.mk ⟨P.relation j, P.relation_mem_ker j⟩) :
    ((P.cotangentDeterminantBasis b k x :
        ProjectiveDeterminant.module (R := B) (M := P.toExtension.CotangentSpace)) :
          ExteriorAlgebra B P.toExtension.CotangentSpace) =
      ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti B n P.cotangentSpaceBasis
declarations.comment:
the generator of det(L_{B/A}) is dx_1 ^ ... ^ dx_n tensor
(f-bar_1 ^ ... ^ f-bar_n)^{tensor -1}: it carries the wedge of the relation classes to the
wedge of the dx_i

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.delta_cotangentComplex_eq
declarations.doc:
The canonical section of the determinant line of the naive cotangent complex is the Jacobian
determinant times the generator given by the classes of the relations and the `dxᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Presentation.delta_cotangentComplex_eq
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) B P.toExtension.Cotangent)
    (hb : ∀ i, b i = Extension.Cotangent.mk ⟨P.relation i, P.relation_mem_ker i⟩) (k : Fin 1) :
    TwoTermComplex.delta P.toExtension.cotangentComplex P.isRankZero_cotangentComplex =
      P.relationJacobiMatrix.det • P.cotangentDeterminantBasis b k
declarations.comment:
delta(NL_{B/A}) = det(df_j/dx_i) . dx_1 ^ ... ^ dx_n tensor
(f-bar_1 ^ ... ^ f-bar_n)^{tensor -1}. Not a tautology: `TwoTermComplex.delta` is the
pre-existing general construction `ProjectiveDeterminant.map`, defined with no reference to
any Jacobian or basis, and this computes it in the two ordered bases

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.hasJacobianDelta
declarations.doc:
A relative global complete intersection presentation with as many relations as variables has
the local Jacobian picture of the determinant of its naive cotangent complex.
declarations.statement: theorem Presentation.hasJacobianDelta : P.HasJacobianDelta
declarations.comment:
the four assertions bundled for one square relative global complete
intersection presentation

registrations.name: Algebra.Presentation.exists_basis_cotangent_relation
registrations.comment: the conormal module (f_1, ..., f_n)/(f_1, ..., f_n)^2 is free on the classes f-bar_i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TateMap.existsUnique_tateRule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FKD.** There exists a unique rule that to every locally quasi-finite
syntomic morphism of locally Noetherian schemes `Y → X` assigns an isomorphism
`c_{Y/X} : det(NL_{Y/X}) ≅ ω_{Y/X}` such that

1. the section `δ(NL_{Y/X})` is mapped to `τ_{Y/X}`, and
2. the rule is compatible with restriction to opens and with base change.

The source of a locally quasi-finite morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme is locally
Noetherian, so the hypothesis is placed on the target only.
declarations.statement: theorem existsUnique_tateRule : ∃! c : TateRule.{u}, IsTateRule c
declarations.comment:
the unique rule c_{Y/X} : det(NL_{Y/X}) ≅ ω_{Y/X} carrying δ(NL_{Y/X}) to τ_{Y/X}
and compatible with restriction to opens and with base change

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.deRhamDifferential_comp_self
declarations.doc:
**The de Rham differential of `B` over `A` squares to zero.**  The elements
`b₀ · (d b₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d b_p)` span `Ω^p_{B/A}` over `A`, and on such an element the defining rule
computes the composite as a wedge whose first factor is `d 1 = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem deRhamDifferential_comp_self (p : ℕ) (ξ : ⋀[B]^p (Ω[B⁄A])) :
    deRhamDifferential (A := A) (p + 1) (deRhamDifferential p ξ) = 0
declarations.comment: the complex property d ∘ d = 0 of the de Rham complex of a ring map, on the exterior powers of the Kaehler differentials

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.deRhamDifferential_comp_deRhamDifferential
declarations.doc:
**Consecutive de Rham differentials compose to zero**, as an equality of `A`-linear maps.
This is the complex property of the de Rham complex of `B` over `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem deRhamDifferential_comp_deRhamDifferential (p : ℕ) :
    (deRhamDifferential (A := A) (B := B) (p + 1)).comp (deRhamDifferential p) = 0
declarations.comment: the complex property d ∘ d = 0 of the de Rham complex of a ring map, as an equality of A-linear maps

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.DifferentialDescent.sourceDeRham
declarations.doc:
**The de Rham complex of `B` over `A`**, as a term of `SourceDeRham A B`: the de Rham
differentials `KaehlerDifferential.deRhamDifferential` on the exterior powers of `Ω[B⁄A]`, which
obey the defining rule on generators by
`KaehlerDifferential.deRhamDifferential_smul_ιMulti_D`.  Nothing is supposed: the descent datum
of Tag 07HY is produced here, and its complex property is the theorem
`KaehlerDifferential.deRhamDifferential_comp_deRhamDifferential`, reached through the default
value of the field `complex`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sourceDeRham (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] :
    SourceDeRham A B
declarations.comment: the de Rham complex of a ring map A → B, as the family of A-linear differentials on the exterior powers of the Kaehler differentials together with the defining rule on generators and the complex property d ∘ d = 0; this construction has no hypothesis

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.deRhamComplex
declarations.doc:
The de Rham complex `Ω^0_{B/A} → Ω^1_{B/A} → Ω^2_{B/A} → ⋯` of `B` over `A`: the exterior
powers of `Ω[B⁄A]`, as `A`-modules, with the de Rham differentials as its arrows.  The
construction has no hypothesis — the arrows are `deRhamDifferential` and the square-zero
condition is `deRhamDifferential_comp_deRhamDifferential`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def deRhamComplex (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A B] : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℕ
declarations.comment: the de Rham complex Ω^0_{B/A} → Ω^1_{B/A} → ⋯ of a ring map A → B, as a CochainComplex of A-modules indexed by ℕ; the construction has no hypothesis

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.deRhamDifferential
declarations.doc:
The de Rham differential `d : Ω^p_{B/A} → Ω^{p+1}_{B/A}` in degree `p`: the `A`-linear map
with `d (b₀ · d b₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d b_p) = d b₀ ∧ d b₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d b_p` for all `b₀, …, b_p ∈ B`, where
`d : B → Ω[B⁄A]` is the universal `A`-derivation.  That rule is
`deRhamDifferential_smul_ιMulti_D` and `deRhamDifferential_unique` says it pins the map down.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def deRhamDifferential (p : ℕ) :
    ⋀[B]^p (Ω[B⁄A]) →ₗ[A] ⋀[B]^(p + 1) (Ω[B⁄A])
declarations.comment: the differential itself

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.deRhamDifferential_smul_ιMulti_D
declarations.doc:
The defining rule of the de Rham differential:
`d (b₀ · d b₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d b_p) = d b₀ ∧ d b₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d b_p`.  The leading scalar `b₀` contributes the
factor `d b₀` through `dp_apply_smul`, and `G_exact` kills the wedge of exact forms.
declarations.comment: the defining rule of `deRhamDifferential`

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.deRhamDifferential_unique
declarations.doc:
`deRhamDifferential p` is the only `A`-linear map `Ω^p_{B/A} → Ω^{p+1}_{B/A}` with
`d (b₀ · d b₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d b_p) = d b₀ ∧ d b₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d b_p`, because those elements span
`Ω^p_{B/A}` over `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem deRhamDifferential_unique (p : ℕ)
    (d : ⋀[B]^p (Ω[B⁄A]) →ₗ[A] ⋀[B]^(p + 1) (Ω[B⁄A]))
    (hd : ∀ b : Fin (p + 1) → B,
      d (b 0 • exteriorPower.ιMulti B p fun i ↦ D A B (b i.succ)) =
        exteriorPower.ιMulti B (p + 1) fun i ↦ D A B (b i)) :
    d = deRhamDifferential p
declarations.comment: uniqueness of `deRhamDifferential`

declarations.name: isHomotopyEquiv_total_of_isHomotopyEquiv
declarations.doc:
Let `M^•` be a complex of an abelian category and `A^{•,•}` a complex of
complexes. If `a : M^•[0] ⟶ A^{•,•}` is part of a homotopy equivalence in the
category of complexes of complexes, then the canonical induced map
`α : M^• ⟶ Tot(A^{•,•})` is a homotopy equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHomotopyEquiv_total_of_isHomotopyEquiv
    {V : Type*} [Category V] [Abelian V]
    (M : HomologicalComplex V (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    (A : HomologicalComplex₂ V (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    [A.HasTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ)]
    (a : HomotopyEquiv (singleObjComplex M) A) :
    Nonempty {e : HomotopyEquiv M (A.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) //
        e.hom = totalAlpha M A a.hom}

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.exists_degenerateComplex_eq_sup_imageSubobject_σ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FKI**.
Let `A` be an abelian category. The functorial splitting `s(U) = N(U) ⊕ D(U)` of the Moore complex
of a simplicial object `U` of `A` along its normalized subcomplex ([Stacks, Tag 019A]) can be
chosen so that the degenerate part is described degreewise as the subobject of `U_n` generated by
the degenerate simplices: `D(U)_0 = 0` and `D(U)_{n + 1}` is the supremum of the images of the
degeneracy operators `σ_i : U_n ⟶ U_{n + 1}`, `i = 0, …, n`. For a simplicial abelian group this
says that the elements of `D(U)_n` are exactly the sums of degenerate `n`-simplices.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_degenerateComplex_eq_sup_imageSubobject_σ :
    ∃ (D : SimplicialObject A ⥤ ChainComplex A ℕ)
      (e : normalizedMooreComplex A ⊞ D ≅ alternatingFaceMapComplex A),
      biprod.inl ≫ e.hom = inclusionOfMooreComplex A ∧
        ∀ U : SimplicialObject A,
          IsZero ((D.obj U).X 0) ∧
            ∀ n : ℕ, imageSubobject (((biprod.inr ≫ e.hom).app U).f (n + 1)) =
              Finset.univ.sup fun i : Fin (n + 1) => imageSubobject (U.σ i)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CosimplicialObject.exists_homotopy_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FKJ**.
A *homotopy from `a` to `b`*, for `a b : U ⟶ V` morphisms of cosimplicial objects of a category `C`
with no assumptions whatsoever, is a family of morphisms `h_{n, α} : U_n ⟶ V_n` indexed by the
objects `⦋n⦌` of `Δ` and the simplices `α ∈ Δ[1]_n`, satisfying
`h_{m, α} ∘ U(f) = V(f) ∘ h_{n, α ∘ f}` for every morphism `f : ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋m⦌` of `Δ`
([Stacks, Tag 07KB]) and having `a_n` and `b_n` as its components at the two constant maps
`⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋1⦌`, with value `0` resp. `1`. This notion agrees with the one of [Stacks, Tag 019W], which
needs the products `∏_{α ∈ Δ[1]_n} V_n` naming `Hom(Δ[1], V)`: whenever those exist, a family is a
homotopy in the above sense if and only if it is the family of components of a homotopy
`h : U ⟶ Hom(Δ[1], V)` from `a` to `b`, with `h_n = ∏_{α ∈ Δ[1]_n} h_{n, α}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_homotopy_iff (a b : U ⟶ V)
    (h : ∀ n : SimplexCategory, (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op n) → (U.obj n ⟶ V.obj n)) :
    (∃ H : Homotopy a b, ∀ n, H.h.app n = Pi.lift (h n)) ↔
      (∀ ⦃n m : SimplexCategory⦄ (f : n ⟶ m) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op m)),
          U.map f ≫ h m α = h n ((Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).map f.op α) ≫ V.map f) ∧
        (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 0 (op n)) = a.app n) ∧
        (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 1 (op n)) = b.app n)
declarations.comment: the remark's comparison of its notion with the one of 019W, `this new notion is the same as the old one in case finite products exist`, stated for a given family and with the correspondence pinned degreewise to `h_n = ∏_α h_{n, α}`; the finite products of 019W are weakened to the products naming `Hom(Δ[1], V)`, and the right hand side, which needs no products, is the remark's definition, in the form its dependents use. Part (2), homotopic, is `Relation.EqvGen` of the existence of such a family, as in 019W and 019S; the remark's functoriality assertions are 019Y (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.homotopyEquivalences_moore_and_normalizedCochainComplex_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FKK**.
Homotopy equivalences of cosimplicial objects induce homotopy equivalences of cochain complexes.
Let `a : U ⟶ V` be a homotopy equivalence of cosimplicial objects of `A`: there is `b : V ⟶ U`
such that `a ≫ b` is homotopic to `𝟙 U` and `b ≫ a` is homotopic to `𝟙 V`, where two morphisms
`f`, `g` of cosimplicial objects are *homotopic* when they are related by the equivalence relation
generated by the existence of a homotopy from one to the other, a homotopy being a family of
morphisms `h_{n, α}` indexed by the simplices `α ∈ Δ[1]ₙ` with
`h_{m, α} ∘ U(u) = V(u) ∘ h_{n, α ∘ u}` for every morphism `u : ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋m⦌` of `Δ`, whose
components at the constant maps `⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋1⦌` with values `0` and `1` are `f_n` and `g_n`
([Stacks, Tag 0FKJ]).
1. If `A` is preadditive, then `s(a) : s(U) ⟶ s(V)` is a homotopy equivalence of Moore cochain
  complexes.
2. If `A` is abelian, then `Q(a) : Q(U) ⟶ Q(V)` is a homotopy equivalence of normalized cochain
  complexes, for any normalized cochain complex functor `Q` with projection `π : s ⟶ Q`, which is
  an isomorphism in degree `0` and a cokernel of the cofaces `δ i : Uₙ ⟶ Uₙ₊₁`, `i ≤ n`, in degree
  `n + 1` ([Stacks, Tag 019I]).
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopyEquivalences_moore_and_normalizedCochainComplex_map :
    (∀ (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Preadditive A] (U V : CosimplicialObject A) (a : U ⟶ V),
      (∃ b : V ⟶ U,
        Relation.EqvGen (fun f₁ f₂ : U ⟶ U => ∃ h : ∀ n : SimplexCategory,
            (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op n) → (U.obj n ⟶ U.obj n),
          (∀ ⦃n m : SimplexCategory⦄ (u : n ⟶ m) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op m)),
              U.map u ≫ h m α = h n ((Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).map u.op α) ≫ U.map u) ∧
            (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 0 (op n)) = f₁.app n) ∧
            (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 1 (op n)) = f₂.app n))
          (a ≫ b) (𝟙 U) ∧
        Relation.EqvGen (fun f₁ f₂ : V ⟶ V => ∃ h : ∀ n : SimplexCategory,
            (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op n) → (V.obj n ⟶ V.obj n),
          (∀ ⦃n m : SimplexCategory⦄ (u : n ⟶ m) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op m)),
              V.map u ≫ h m α = h n ((Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).map u.op α) ≫ V.map u) ∧
            (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 0 (op n)) = f₁.app n) ∧
            (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 1 (op n)) = f₂.app n))
          (b ≫ a) (𝟙 V)) →
      HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences A (ComplexShape.up ℕ)
        ((alternatingCofaceMapComplex A).map a)) ∧
    (∀ (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
      (Q : CosimplicialObject A ⥤ CochainComplex A ℕ) (π : alternatingCofaceMapComplex A ⟶ Q),
      (∀ U : CosimplicialObject A, IsIso ((π.app U).f 0)) →
      (∀ (U : CosimplicialObject A) (n : ℕ),
        ∃ e : cokernel (Sigma.desc (f := fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => U.obj ⦋n⦌)
            fun i => U.δ i.castSucc) ≅ (Q.obj U).X (n + 1),
          cokernel.π _ ≫ e.hom = (π.app U).f (n + 1)) →
      ∀ (U V : CosimplicialObject A) (a : U ⟶ V),
      (∃ b : V ⟶ U,
        Relation.EqvGen (fun f₁ f₂ : U ⟶ U => ∃ h : ∀ n : SimplexCategory,
            (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op n) → (U.obj n ⟶ U.obj n),
          (∀ ⦃n m : SimplexCategory⦄ (u : n ⟶ m) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op m)),
              U.map u ≫ h m α = h n ((Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).map u.op α) ≫ U.map u) ∧
            (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 0 (op n)) = f₁.app n) ∧
            (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 1 (op n)) = f₂.app n))
          (a ≫ b) (𝟙 U) ∧
        Relation.EqvGen (fun f₁ f₂ : V ⟶ V => ∃ h : ∀ n : SimplexCategory,
            (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op n) → (V.obj n ⟶ V.obj n),
          (∀ ⦃n m : SimplexCategory⦄ (u : n ⟶ m) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op m)),
              V.map u ≫ h m α = h n ((Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).map u.op α) ≫ V.map u) ∧
            (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 0 (op n)) = f₁.app n) ∧
            (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 1 (op n)) = f₂.app n))
          (b ≫ a) (𝟙 V)) →
      HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences A (ComplexShape.up ℕ) (Q.map a))
declarations.comment: the source's additive `A` is generalized to preadditive in the assertion for `s`, which is all `s` uses. Being a homotopy equivalence of cochain complexes is `HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences`, which pins the map. A homotopy equivalence of cosimplicial objects is spelled out (the source defines it by duality with 019N): a homotopy is its family of components as in 0FKJ and 07KB, which needs no products in `A`, and being homotopic is `Relation.EqvGen` of the existence of such a family, the spelling of 01A0. The normalized cochain complex `Q` is any functor with a projection `π : s ⟶ Q` that is an isomorphism in degree 0 and the cokernel of the cofaces `δ_i`, `i < n`, in degree `n`, the description of 019I, which provides one; the differential of `Q` is then the one induced by `(-1)^{n+1} δ_{n+1}`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential
declarations.doc:
**The relative de Rham differential of `φ` exists.** The differential in each degree is the
sheafification of the ring-level de Rham differential, read on `⋀ᵖ Ω` through the exact-wedge
comparison; it squares to zero and obeys the de Rham rule because the sectionwise differential
does.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def deRhamDifferential : DeRhamDifferential B
declarations.comment: existence: the de Rham differential exists. The tag defines the complex by a uniqueness property, so the covering set is this construction, `relativeDeRhamComplex` and `deRhamDifferential_unique`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.relativeDeRhamComplex
declarations.doc: **The relative de Rham complex** `⋀⁰ Ω → ⋀¹ Ω → ⋀² Ω → ⋯` of sheaves of `A`-modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev relativeDeRhamComplex :
    CochainComplex
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} A)) ℕ
declarations.comment: the canonical complex: the de Rham complex of `B` over `A`, assembled from the differential of `deRhamDifferential`. Its terms and arrows are `deRhamComplex_X` and `deRhamComplex_d`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential_unique
declarations.doc:
**The relative de Rham differential is unique.** This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.DeRhamDifferential.eq` read at the constructed differential.
declarations.statement: theorem deRhamDifferential_unique (D : DeRhamDifferential B) : D = deRhamDifferential B
declarations.comment: uniqueness: a de Rham differential is the one constructed here, so the complex of Tag 0FKM is well defined. The general two-differential form is `DeRhamDifferential.eq` of `StacksFrontier.Topology.Sheaves.Modules.DeRhamUniqueness`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.inverseImageExteriorAlgebraIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FKP, canonicality.** The canonical comparison between the inverse image
of the exterior algebra of `Ω_{ℬ/𝒜}` and the exterior algebra of `Ω_{f⁻¹ℬ/f⁻¹𝒜}`, in every degree
and on the underlying direct-sum sheaf, together with its compatibility with the exterior products,
the degree-zero units and the degree-one generators. Those compatibilities determine the
comparison, by `Stacks.PullbackExteriorAlgebra.exteriorAlgebraPullbackIso_unique`.
declarations.statement:
def inverseImageExteriorAlgebraIso :
    ExteriorAlgebraPullbackIso (RingedSpace.inverseImageProjection X f)
      (differentialAlgebras.{u} φ).exterior (differentialAlgebras.{u} φ).exteriorGenerator
      (differentialAlgebras.{u} (inverseImageRingMap φ f)).exterior
      (inverseImageExteriorGenerator φ f)
declarations.comment: canonicality of the identification of the terms, as sheaves of `f⁻¹ℬ`-modules: the comparison is the one compatible with the exterior products, the units and the exact differentials, and that determines it. The complex-level statement of the tag is `inverseImageDeRhamComplexIso` below.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.inverseImageDifferentialForms
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FKP, on the terms.** The canonical identification
`f⁻¹ Ωᵖ_{ℬ/𝒜} = Ωᵖ_{f⁻¹ℬ/f⁻¹𝒜}` of the inverse image of the sheaf of relative differential
`p`-forms with the sheaf of relative differential `p`-forms of the inverse-image rings.
declarations.comment: the identification of the terms: in each degree `p` the inverse image of `Ωᵖ_{ℬ/𝒜}` is `Ωᵖ_{f⁻¹ℬ/f⁻¹𝒜}`, as sheaves of `f⁻¹ℬ`-modules. The identification of the complexes of `f⁻¹𝒜`-modules is `inverseImageDeRhamComplexIso` below, which is built from this one by `inverseImageRestrictScalarsIso`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.inverseImageDeRhamComplexIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FKP.** The canonical identification
`f⁻¹Ω•_{ℬ/𝒜} = Ω•_{f⁻¹ℬ/f⁻¹𝒜}` of de Rham complexes: the degreewise identification of the
differential forms, moved into sheaves of `f⁻¹𝒜`-modules and assembled into an isomorphism of
complexes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseImageDeRhamComplexIso :
    inverseImageDeRhamComplex φ f ≅
      relativeDeRhamComplex (differentialAlgebras.{u} (inverseImageRingMap φ f))
declarations.comment: the identification of the de Rham COMPLEXES: `f⁻¹Ω•_{ℬ/𝒜} = Ω•_{f⁻¹ℬ/f⁻¹𝒜}` as complexes of sheaves of `f⁻¹𝒜`-modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.inverseImageDeRhamComplexIso_canonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FKP, canonicality.** The identification of the complexes is the one
that carries each local multiple of an ordered product of exact differentials to the same
expression in the inverse-image rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem inverseImageDeRhamComplexIso_canonical :
    IsCanonicalInverseImageDeRhamIso φ f (inverseImageDeRhamComplexIso φ f)
declarations.comment: canonicality of the identification of the complexes: it is the map determined by `b · d b₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d bₚ ↦ f⁻¹b · d(f⁻¹b₁) ∧ ⋯ ∧ d(f⁻¹bₚ)` on the inverse-image sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.inverseImageDeRhamComplexIso_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FKP, uniqueness.** Canonicality determines the identification of the
complexes: the local multiples of the ordered products of exact differentials generate the terms
locally, so an isomorphism of complexes prescribed on them is prescribed.
declarations.statement:
theorem inverseImageDeRhamComplexIso_unique
    (e : inverseImageDeRhamComplex φ f ≅
      relativeDeRhamComplex (differentialAlgebras.{u} (inverseImageRingMap φ f)))
    (he : IsCanonicalInverseImageDeRhamIso φ f e) :
    e = inverseImageDeRhamComplexIso φ f
declarations.comment: uniqueness: a canonical identification of the de Rham complexes is the one constructed here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.deRhamComplex
declarations.doc:
**The relative de Rham complex** `Ω^•_{X/S}` of a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S`: the de
Rham complex of `𝒪_X` over `f^{-1}𝒪_S`, a cochain complex of sheaves of `f^{-1}𝒪_S`-modules
on `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def deRhamComplex :
    CochainComplex (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.underlyingRingSheaf
        ((TopCat.Sheaf.pullback CommRingCat.{u} f.base).obj S.sheaf))) ℕ
declarations.comment: the morphism-of-schemes case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.relativeDeRhamComplex
declarations.doc: **The relative de Rham complex** `⋀⁰ Ω → ⋀¹ Ω → ⋀² Ω → ⋯` of sheaves of `A`-modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev relativeDeRhamComplex :
    CochainComplex
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} A)) ℕ
declarations.comment: the morphism-of-ringed-spaces case, at `A := f⁻¹𝒪_Y`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GodementResolution.isFlasque_iterate_modulePullbackPushforward
declarations.doc:
Every positive iterate `(f_* f^*)^(n+1) F` of a morphism out of a discrete space is a flasque
sheaf of modules: a sheaf on a discrete space is flasque, and pushforward preserves flasqueness.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlasque_iterate_modulePullbackPushforward
    {Xdisc X : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (f : Xdisc ⟶ X) [DiscreteTopology Xdisc]
    (n : ℕ) (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) :
    TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheafRing X)).obj
      (((RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback f ⋙
        RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePushforward f).iterate (n + 1)).obj F))
declarations.comment: each term f_* f^* ⋯ f_* f^* F is a flasque module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GodementResolution.exists_functorial_flasque_godementComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FKS**, the complex and its flasque terms. For a ringed space `(X, O_X)` there is a
functor `G` from sheaves of `O_X`-modules to cochain complexes, with an augmentation `η` from the
complex concentrated in degree `0`, whose term in degree `n` is the iterate
`(f_* f^*)^(n+1) F` along the morphism `f : X_disc ⟶ X` from the points of `X` with the discrete
topology, and each of whose terms is a flasque `O_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_functorial_flasque_godementComplex (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) :
    ∃ (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X) ⥤
        CochainComplex
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ℕ)
      (_η : CochainComplex.single₀
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⟶ G)
      (_termIso : ∀ n,
        G ⋙ HomologicalComplex.eval
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
            (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n ≅
          (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback (fromDiscrete X) ⋙
            RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePushforward (fromDiscrete X)).iterate (n + 1)),
      ∀ F n, TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheafRing X)).obj
          ((G.obj F).X n))
declarations.comment: the functorial complex of flasque terms f_* f^* ⋯ f_* f^* F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GodementResolution.homotopyEquivalences_stalk_godementAugmentation
declarations.doc:
**Clause (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0FKS]**, at one sheaf and one point. The augmentation
`F[0] ⟶ (f_* f^* F → f_* f^* f_* f^* F → ⋯)` of the Godement complex, read on the stalk at `x`,
is a homotopy equivalence of complexes of `𝒪_{X,x}`-modules.

This is `hasNaturalStalkHomotopy_godementAugmentation` evaluated at `F`: evaluation at `F` is an
additive functor, so it carries the homotopy equivalence of complexes of functors to one of
complexes of modules, and the compatibility clause identifies the result with the stalk of the
augmentation up to the two isomorphisms `i` and `j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homotopyEquivalences_stalk_godementAugmentation (x : X)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) :
    HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences (StalkModuleCat X x) (ComplexShape.up ℕ)
      (((SheafOfModules.stalkFunctor (structureSheafRing X) x).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).map ((godementAugmentation X).app F))
declarations.comment: the stalkwise homotopy equivalence F_x[0] ≃ ((f_* f^* F)_x → ⋯)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GodementResolution.quasiIso_godementAugmentation
declarations.doc:
**Clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0FKS]: the augmented Godement complex is exact.** The
augmentation `F[0] ⟶ G(F)` is a quasi-isomorphism, so
`0 → F → f_* f^* F → f_* f^* f_* f^* F → ⋯` is exact and the Godement complex is a flasque
resolution of `F`.

Quasi-isomorphy is detected on stalks (`quasiIso_of_forall_stalk_quasiIso_nat`), and on each
stalk the augmentation is a homotopy equivalence by
`homotopyEquivalences_stalk_godementAugmentation`, hence a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_godementAugmentation (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) :
    QuasiIso ((godementAugmentation X).app F)
declarations.comment: exactness of the augmented complex 0 → F → f_* f^* F → ⋯

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GodementResolution.exists_quasiIso_boundedBelow_isFlasque_isHomotopyEquiv_stalk_godement
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FKT], all four clauses, for the Godement resolution.** For a bounded below
complex `F` of `𝒪_X`-modules there is a quasi-isomorphism `F ⟶ G` with `G` bounded below in the
same degree, every term of `G` flasque, and, for every `x ∈ X`, the stalk map `F_x ⟶ G_x` a
homotopy equivalence of complexes of `𝒪_{X,x}`-modules. The map is `godementComparisonMap` onto
the totalisation of the Godement double complex of `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quasiIso_boundedBelow_isFlasque_isHomotopyEquiv_stalk_godement
    (hF : ∃ n : ℤ, F.IsStrictlyGE n) :
    ∃ (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ℤ) (f : F ⟶ G),
      QuasiIso f ∧ (∃ n : ℤ, G.IsStrictlyGE n) ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ, TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque
          ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheafRing X)).obj (G.X i))) ∧
        (∀ x : X, ∃ e : HomotopyEquiv ((stalkComplexFunctor X x).obj F)
            ((stalkComplexFunctor X x).obj G), e.hom = (stalkComplexFunctor X x).map f)
declarations.comment: Godement resolution; all four clauses, including the stalkwise homotopy equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedGlobalCupProduct.section_cupProduct_canonical
declarations.doc:
**Cohomology, Section 0FKU in full, with no parameter: both displays of the section, for the
global cup product of an arbitrary ringed space.**

Let `(S, 𝒪_S)` be a ringed space, `A = Γ(S, 𝒪_S)` and `π : (S, 𝒪_S) ⟶ ({*}, A)` the morphism of
ringed spaces of Tag 01BH. The global cup product `μ` is
`globalCupProduct (canonicalOnePointComparison S)` (also spelled `cupProductOnSpace S`), a
morphism `RΓ(S, K) ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(S, M) ⟶ RΓ(S, K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} M)` in `D(A)` for all `K, M ∈ D(𝒪_S)`. The
conjuncts are:

* the canonical one-point comparison is the one presented by `Lπ^*` through the one-point
  identification `D(A) ≌ D(𝒪_{({*}, A)})`, the adjunction `Lπ^* ⊣ Rπ_*` of Tag 079W, the Leray
  identification `RΓ({*}, Rπ_*(-)) ≅ RΓ(S, -)` of Tag 0D5W, and the comparison of Tag 079U
  (`canonicalPointPresentation S` and `canonicalSectionsIso S`);
* `μ` is the relative cup product construction (Tag 0B68) for that adjunction and comparison;
* **the source's definition of `μ`**: read through the Leray identification in each factor and at
  the target, `μ` is the doubled-counit morphism of the canonical presentation, and that morphism
  is, across the equality of rings `Γ({*}, 𝒪) = A`, the relative cup product of Tag 0B68 for `π`
  at `(K, M)` composed with the identification of `⊗^𝐋_A` with `⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_{({*}, A)}}` — that is,
  "the relative cup product for `f : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (pt, A)` via `D(pt, A) = D(A)`";
* the tensor comparison is invertible (so in particular it is not the zero morphism);
* `μ` is natural in the two complexes jointly;
* the second display: the pairings `∪ : Hⁱ(S, K) ⊗_A Hʲ(S, M) ⟶ Hⁱ⁺ʲ(S, K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} M)` are the
  tensoring of classes of More on Algebra, Section 15.64 followed by `Hⁱ⁺ʲ(μ)`, i.e.
  `ξ ∪ η = μ(ξ ⊗ η)`.

The numbered items of Section 20.31 are excluded, each carrying its own tag: Lemma 20.31.1 is
Tag 0FP2, Remark 20.31.2 is Tag 0G6W, Lemma 20.31.3 is Tag 0FP3, Lemma 20.31.4 is Tag 0FKV, and
Lemmas 20.31.5 to 20.31.8 are Tags 0FP4, 0FP5, 0FP6 and 0H99.
declarations.statement:
theorem section_cupProduct_canonical (S : RingedSpace.{u, u}) :
    canonicalOnePointComparison S =
        (canonicalPointPresentation S).toComparison S (baseRing_coeffPoint S)
          (canonicalSectionsIso S) ∧
    (∀ K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S)),
      (globalCupProduct (canonicalOnePointComparison S)).app (K, M) =
        adjunctionBitensorMap (canonicalOnePointComparison S).adjunction
          (Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S))
          (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor S.sheaf))
          (canonicalOnePointComparison S).tensorComparison K M) ∧
    (∀ K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S)),
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S)).map
            ((canonicalSectionsIso S).hom.app K ×ₘ (canonicalSectionsIso S).hom.app M) ≫
          (globalCupProduct (canonicalOnePointComparison S)).app (K, M) =
        (canonicalPointPresentation S).bitensorMap S (baseRing_coeffPoint S) K M ≫
          (canonicalSectionsIso S).hom.app ((spaceTensor S).obj (K, M))) ∧
    (∀ K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S)),
      HEq ((canonicalPointPresentation S).bitensorMap S (baseRing_coeffPoint S) K M)
        (adjunctionBitensorMap (onePointDerivedAdjunction ↥(baseRing S))
            (coeffTensor S) (pointTensor S)
            (onePointDerivedTensorIso ↥(baseRing S)).hom
            ((derivedPushforward (toCoeffPoint S)).obj K)
            ((derivedPushforward (toCoeffPoint S)).obj M) ≫
          (baseSections (coeffPt S)).map (relativeCupProduct (toCoeffPoint S) K M))) ∧
    IsIso (canonicalOnePointComparison S).tensorComparison ∧
    (∀ K K' M M' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S)),
      ∀ (k : K ⟶ K') (m : M ⟶ M'),
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S)).map
            ((baseSections S).map k ×ₘ (baseSections S).map m) ≫
          (globalCupProduct (canonicalOnePointComparison S)).app (K', M') =
        (globalCupProduct (canonicalOnePointComparison S)).app (K, M) ≫
          (baseSections S).map
            ((Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor S.sheaf)).map (k ×ₘ m))) ∧
    (∀ (K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S))) (i j : ℤ),
      ∃ p : RingTheory.TorProducts.CohomologyTensorProduct ((baseSections S).obj K)
          ((baseSections S).obj M) i j,
        cupPairing (globalCupProduct (canonicalOnePointComparison S)) K M i j =
          p.map ≫ (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing S)) (i + j)).map
            ((globalCupProduct (canonicalOnePointComparison S)).app (K, M)))
declarations.comment:
Section 20.31 IN FULL, both displays, on an arbitrary ringed space and with no
  parameter: the global cup product μ : RΓ(X, K) ⊗^L_A RΓ(X, M) ⟶ RΓ(X, K ⊗^L M) in D(A) is
  globalCupProduct (canonicalOnePointComparison X), built from Lπ^* ⊣ Rπ_* for the morphism
  π : (X, O_X) ⟶ (pt, A) and the comparison of Tag 079U (first conjunct); it is the relative cup
  product recipe for that datum (second); read through the Leray identification it is the
  relative cup product of Tag 0B68 for π via D(pt, A) = D(A) (third and fourth); its tensor
  comparison is invertible (fifth); it is natural in both complexes (sixth); and the induced
  pairings H^i(X, K) × H^j(X, M) ⟶ H^{i+j}(X, K ⊗^L M) are ξ ∪ η = μ(ξ ⊗ η) with the tensoring
  of classes of More on Algebra, Section 15.64 (seventh). The numbered items of the section are
  excluded, each having its own tag: 0FP2, 0G6W, 0FP3, 0FKV, 0FP4, 0FP5, 0FP6, 0H99

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.CupProductSquare.cupProductSquareCommutes
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FKV].**  Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space, `A = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`, `𝒦^•` and `ℳ^•`
bounded below complexes of `𝒪_X`-modules and `𝒰 : X = ⋃ Uᵢ` an open covering.  The diagram

```
Tot(Č(𝒰,𝒦)) ⊗^𝐋_A Tot(Č(𝒰,ℳ)) ─────────→ RΓ(X,𝒦) ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(X,ℳ)
            │                                        │ μ
            ↓                                        ↓
Tot(Tot(Č(𝒰,𝒦)) ⊗_A Tot(Č(𝒰,ℳ)))          RΓ(X, 𝒦 ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} ℳ)
            │                                        │
            ↓                                        ↓
Tot(Č(𝒰, Tot(𝒦 ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℳ))) ─────────────→ RΓ(X, Tot(𝒦 ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℳ))
```

commutes in `D(A)`: the left-hand leg `cechLeftLeg` (the canonical map to the total tensor
complex, then the Čech cup product of [Stacks, Tag 07MB], then the comparison of
[Stacks, Tag 08BN]) equals the right-hand leg `cechRightLeg` (the comparison of Tag 08BN in both
factors, then the global cup product `μ`, then `RΓ(X, -)` of the canonical map
`𝒦^• ⊗^𝐋 ℳ^• ⟶ Tot(𝒦^• ⊗ ℳ^•)`).
declarations.statement:
theorem cupProductSquareCommutes :
    cechLeftLeg S Ui hU K M = cechRightLeg S Ui hU K M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_syntomic_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_syntomic_tfae {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsFinite f ∧ Syntomic f,
      (IsFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f,
      ((IsFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
        ∀ x : X, IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOverField (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x)]
declarations.comment:
the equivalence of (1), (2) and (3). Parts (5) and (6), the conditions on the
naive cotangent complex, are not among the three conditions of this equivalence; for those see
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Syntomic/FiniteNaiveCotangent.lean`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_and_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_finite_syntomic
declarations.doc: A finite syntomic morphism of schemes is flat and a local complete intersection morphism.
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_lci_fibers_of_finite_flat_lci
declarations.doc:
A finite flat local complete intersection morphism of schemes is locally of finite presentation
and all of its fibres are local complete intersections over the residue fields of their base
points.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_lci_fibers_of_finite_flat_lci {Y X : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : Y ⟶ X} (h : (IsFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    ((IsFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
      ∀ x : X, IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOverField (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x)
declarations.comment: the implication (2) ⟹ (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_syntomic_of_finite_flat_lci_fibers
declarations.doc:
A finite flat morphism of schemes which is locally of finite presentation and all of whose
fibres are local complete intersections over the residue fields of their base points is
syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_syntomic_of_finite_flat_lci_fibers {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X}
    (h : ((IsFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
      ∀ x : X, IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOverField (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x)) :
    IsFinite f ∧ Syntomic f
declarations.comment: the implication (3) ⟹ (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_syntomic_of_hasAffineSquarePresentation

A finite morphism of schemes whose preimages of suitable affine opens of the target are cut out
by as many equations as variables is syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_syntomic_of_hasAffineSquarePresentation {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasAffineSquarePresentation_of_finite_syntomic
declarations.doc:
A finite syntomic morphism of schemes is, over a suitable affine open neighbourhood of every
point of the target, cut out of a polynomial ring by as many equations as variables.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasAffineSquarePresentation_of_finite_syntomic {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X}

declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_flat_lfp_and_hasTorAmplitude_of_finite_syntomic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FKY, the implication (1) ⟹ (5).** A finite syntomic morphism of
schemes is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, and `NL_{Y/X}` has Tor amplitude in
`[-1, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_flat_lfp_and_hasTorAmplitude_of_finite_syntomic {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X}
    (h : IsFinite f ∧ Syntomic f) :
    ((IsFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
      Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude Y.toRingedSpace
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_flat_lfp_and_isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude_of_finite_syntomic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FKY, the implication (1) ⟹ (6).** A finite syntomic morphism of schemes
is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, and `NL_{Y/X}` is a perfect object of
`D(𝒪_Y)` of rank zero with Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_flat_lfp_and_isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude_of_finite_syntomic {Y X : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : Y ⟶ X} (h : IsFinite f ∧ Syntomic f) :
    ((IsFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
      (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := Y.toRingedSpace)
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
        DeterminantTwoTerm.IsRankZeroScheme
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
        Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude Y.toRingedSpace
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0)
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (6)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_syntomic_of_finite_flat_lfp_of_hasTorAmplitude
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FKY, the implication (5) ⟹ (1).** A finite flat morphism of schemes
which is locally of finite presentation and whose naive cotangent complex has Tor amplitude in
`[-1, 0]` is syntomic.

A finite morphism is affine, so the preimage of an affine open `U` of the target is an affine
open `V`; there the hypotheses say that `Γ(Y, U) → Γ(X, V)` is flat of finite presentation with
`NL_{Γ(X, V)/Γ(Y, U)}` of Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`, and that map is syntomic by Stacks
0FJV.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_syntomic_of_finite_flat_lfp_of_hasTorAmplitude {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X}
    (h : ((IsFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
      Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude Y.toRingedSpace
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0) :
    IsFinite f ∧ Syntomic f
declarations.comment: the implication (5) ⟹ (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_syntomic_iff_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FKY, the equivalence of (1) and (5).** A morphism of schemes is finite
and syntomic if and only if it is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation with `NL_{Y/X}`
of Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_syntomic_iff_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex {Y X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    (IsFinite f ∧ Syntomic f) ↔
      (((IsFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
        Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude Y.toRingedSpace
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0)
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_syntomic_iff_isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FKY, the equivalence of (1) and (6).** A morphism of schemes is finite
and syntomic if and only if it is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation with `NL_{Y/X}`
a perfect object of `D(𝒪_Y)` of rank zero with Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_syntomic_iff_isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    (IsFinite f ∧ Syntomic f) ↔
      (((IsFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
        (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := Y.toRingedSpace)
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
          DeterminantTwoTerm.IsRankZeroScheme
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
          Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude Y.toRingedSpace
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0))
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) and (6)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universalSyntomicOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FL0.** The open subscheme of the base `X_d` of the universal finite
free family of rank `d` over which the family is syntomic.

It is the interior of `AlgebraicGeometry.universalSyntomicLocus`; that set is already open, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.universalSyntomicLocus_isOpen`.
declarations.statement: def universalSyntomicOpen : (scheme.{u} d).Opens
declarations.comment: the open subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.factorsThrough_universalSyntomicOpen_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FL0.** A morphism `g : T ⟶ X_d` to the base of the universal finite
free family of rank `d` factors through the open subscheme
`AlgebraicGeometry.universalSyntomicOpen` exactly when the base change of the family along `g` is
syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThrough_universalSyntomicOpen_iff (T : Scheme.{u})
    (g : T ⟶ scheme.{u} d) :
    (∃ ĝ : T ⟶ (universalSyntomicOpen.{u} d).toScheme,
        ĝ ≫ (universalSyntomicOpen.{u} d).ι = g) ↔
      Syntomic (pullback.snd (universalFamily.{u} d (universalAlgebraStructure d)) g)
declarations.comment: universal property

public instance universalSyntomicOpen_smooth_uLift (d : ℕ) [NeZero d] :
