    IsIso (derivedBaseChangeMap g'.toLRSHom.toShHom f'.toLRSHom.toShHom f.toLRSHom.toShHom
        g.toLRSHom.toShHom (toShHom_comm hsq.w) (formsObj f p) ≫
      (derivedPushforward f'.toLRSHom.toShHom).map
        (formsBaseChangeComparison g' f' f g hsq.w p))
declarations.comment: formation of Rf_*Omega^p_X/S commutes with arbitrary change of base: for a proper smooth f and any cartesian square the derived base change map of Tag 08HY at Omega^p_X/S followed by Rf'_* of the canonical map L(g')^*Omega^p_X/S -> Omega^p_X'/S' is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSmoothDeRham.isPerfect_derivedPushforward_forms
declarations.doc:
**Perfectness of `Rf_*Ω^p_{X/S}`.** For a proper smooth morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S`
the derived direct image `Rf_*Ω^p_{X/S}` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_S)`. Perfectness is local
on `S`, its restriction to an affine open `V` is the derived direct image of `Ω^p` along the
base change of `f` to `V` by base change, and over an affine base this is
`isPerfect_derivedPushforward_forms_of_isAffine`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedPushforward_forms (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [Smooth f] (p : ℕ) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := S.toRingedSpace)
      ((derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj (formsObj f p))
declarations.comment: Rf_*Omega^p_X/S is a perfect object of D(O_S) for a proper smooth f, for every p >= 0, over an arbitrary base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.wedgeProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FM2.** The wedge product
`∧ : Tot(Ω^• ⊗_A Ω^•) ⟶ Ω^•` of relative differential forms, as a morphism of complexes of
sheaves of `A`-modules: on the `(p, q)` summand of the total complex it is wedge multiplication of
a `p`-form by a `q`-form, and the graded Leibniz rule is exactly the statement that this family
commutes with the differentials.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def wedgeProduct : tensorSquare B D ⟶ deRhamComplex B D

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.wedgeProduct_summand_unit_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FM2.** On the `(p, q)` summand of the total complex the wedge product
sends a local pure tensor `ω ⊗ η` to the wedge product `ω ∧ η`.

The two sides live in the exterior powers of degrees `((p + q : ℕ) : ℤ)` and `(p : ℤ) + q`, which
is why this is a heterogeneous equality.
declarations.statement:
theorem wedgeProduct_summand_unit_apply (p q : ℕ) (U : (Opens X.carrier)ᵒᵖ)
    (ω : (deRhamTerm B p).val.obj U) (η : (deRhamTerm B q).val.obj U) :
    HEq ((HomologicalComplex.ιMapBifunctor
      (D := _root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} A))
            (deRhamComplex B D) (deRhamComplex B D)
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℕ) p q
              (p + q) rfl ≫
          (wedgeProduct B D).f (p + q)).val.app U
        (((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
          (R := Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf A)
          (𝟙 (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf A).obj)).unit.app
          (PresheafOfModules.tensorObj ((deRhamTerm B p)).val ((deRhamTerm B q)).val)).app U
            (ω ⊗ₜ[A.obj.obj U] η)))
      ((B.exterior.mul (p : ℤ) (q : ℤ)).app U ω η)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomologyCup_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FM3.** The cup product on `H^*_{dR}(X/S)` is **associative**:
`(ξ ∪ η) ∪ ζ = ξ ∪ (η ∪ ζ)`, the left-hand side transported from degree `(i + j) + k` to degree
`i + (j + k)`. This is Cohomology, Lemma 0FP4 together with the associativity of the wedge
product.
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamCohomologyCup_assoc (i j k : ℤ) (ξ : deRhamCohomology B D i)
    (η : deRhamCohomology B D j) (ζ : deRhamCohomology B D k) :
    reindexDeRhamCohomology B D (add_assoc i j k)
        (deRhamCohomologyCup B D (i + j) k (deRhamCohomologyCup B D i j ξ η) ζ) =
      deRhamCohomologyCup B D i (j + k) ξ (deRhamCohomologyCup B D j k η ζ)
declarations.comment: the cup product on H^*_dR(X/S), the cup product of Cohomology Section 0FKU composed with the wedge product of 0FM2, is associative; no parameter, no hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomologyCup_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FM3.** The cup product on `H^*_{dR}(X/S)` is **graded commutative**:
`ξ ∪ η = (-1)^{ij} η ∪ ξ` for `ξ` of degree `i` and `η` of degree `j`, the right-hand side
transported from degree `j + i` to degree `i + j`. This is Cohomology, Lemma 0FP5 together with
the graded commutativity of the wedge product.
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamCohomologyCup_comm (i j : ℤ) (ξ : deRhamCohomology B D i)
    (η : deRhamCohomology B D j) :
    deRhamCohomologyCup B D i j ξ η =
      ((i * j).negOnePow : ℤ) • reindexDeRhamCohomology B D (add_comm j i)
        (deRhamCohomologyCup B D j i η ξ)
declarations.comment: the cup product on H^*_dR(X/S), the cup product of Cohomology Section 0FKU composed with the wedge product of 0FM2, is graded commutative with sign (-1)^(ij); no parameter, no hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.wedgeProduct_summand_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FM3.** The wedge product of Tag 0FM2 is **associative** on the summands
of the total complex: the two bracketings of a triple wedge of local forms agree.

This is the associativity clause of the proof of Tag 0FM3, "the fact that `∧` is associative"; the
associativity of the cup product on `H^*_{dR}` is this together with Cohomology, Tag 0FP4.
declarations.statement:
theorem wedgeProduct_summand_assoc (p q r : ℕ) (U : (Opens X.carrier)ᵒᵖ)
    (ω : (deRhamTerm B p).val.obj U) (η : (deRhamTerm B q).val.obj U)
    (ζ : (deRhamTerm B r).val.obj U) :
    HEq (summandValue B D (wedgeProduct B D) (p + q) r U
        (summandValue B D (wedgeProduct B D) p q U ω η) ζ)
      (summandValue B D (wedgeProduct B D) p (q + r) U ω
        (summandValue B D (wedgeProduct B D) q r U η ζ))
declarations.comment: the wedge product of 0FM2 is associative

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.wedgeProduct_summand_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FM3.** The wedge product of Tag 0FM2 is **graded commutative** on the
summands of the total complex: on the local pure tensor `ω ⊗ η` of a `p`-form and a `q`-form its
value is `(-1)^{pq}` times its value on `η ⊗ ω`.

This is the graded commutativity clause of the proof of Tag 0FM3, "the fact that `∧` is graded
commutative"; the graded commutativity of the cup product on `H^*_{dR}` is this together with
Cohomology, Tag 0FP5.
declarations.statement:
theorem wedgeProduct_summand_comm (p q : ℕ) (U : (Opens X.carrier)ᵒᵖ)
    (ω : (deRhamTerm B p).val.obj U) (η : (deRhamTerm B q).val.obj U) :
    HEq (summandValue B D (wedgeProduct B D) p q U ω η)
      ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (p * q) • summandValue B D (wedgeProduct B D) q p U η ω)
declarations.comment: the wedge product of 0FM2 is graded commutative, with the sign (-1)^(pq)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeTotalCupProduct_assoc
declarations.doc:
The cup product on `H^*_{Hodge}(X/S)` is associative: `(x ∪ y) ∪ z = x ∪ (y ∪ z)` for `x`,
`y`, `z` of total degrees `n`, `m`, `l`, the two sides read in the same group
`H^{n + m + l}_{Hodge}(X/S)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hodgeTotalCupProduct_assoc (n m l : ℕ) (x : hodgeCohomology B n)
    (y : hodgeCohomology B m) (z : hodgeCohomology B l) :
    reindexHodgeTotal B (add_assoc n m l)
        (hodgeTotalCupProduct B (n + m) l (hodgeTotalCupProduct B n m x y) z) =
      hodgeTotalCupProduct B n (m + l) x (hodgeTotalCupProduct B m l y z)
declarations.comment: the cup product on H^*_Hodge(X/S) = ⨁_{p+q=n} H^q(X, Ω^p) is associative; the cup product is constructed (hodgeCohomologyCupProduct: the 0FKU pairing of the ringed space (X, A) along the wedge product), nothing assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeTotalCupProduct_comm
declarations.doc:
The cup product on `H^*_{Hodge}(X/S)` is graded commutative: `x ∪ y = (-1)^{nm} y ∪ x` for
`x` of degree `n` and `y` of degree `m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hodgeTotalCupProduct_comm (n m : ℕ) (x : hodgeCohomology B n)
    (y : hodgeCohomology B m) :
    hodgeTotalCupProduct B n m x y =
      ((((n : ℤ) * m).negOnePow : ℤ)) •
        reindexHodgeTotal B (add_comm m n) (hodgeTotalCupProduct B m n y x)
declarations.comment: the cup product on H^*_Hodge(X/S) is graded commutative, x ∪ y = (-1)^(nm) y ∪ x for x, y of total degrees n, m; the cup product is constructed (hodgeCohomologyCupProduct), nothing assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeToDeRhamFirstPage
declarations.doc:
**The `q`-th row `E_1^{•, q}` of the first page of the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence of
Stacks Section 0FM6.** The term in position `p` is the Hodge cohomology group
`H^q(X, Ω^p_{𝒪_X/A})` and the differential `d_1^{p, q} : H^q(X, Ω^p) ⟶ H^q(X, Ω^{p + 1})` is the
map induced by the de Rham differential `d : Ω^p ⟶ Ω^{p + 1}`; it squares to zero because the de
Rham differential does.
declarations.statement: abbrev hodgeToDeRhamFirstPage (q : ℕ) : CochainComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u} ℕ
declarations.comment:
the rows E_1^{•,q} of the first page of the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence as
cochain complexes: E_1^{p,q} = H^q(X, Ω^p) with d_1 induced by the de Rham differential; the
spectral sequences are exists_hodgeToDeRham_and_conjugate_spectralSequences

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.exists_hodgeToDeRham_and_conjugate_spectralSequences
declarations.doc:
**The Hodge-to-de Rham and the conjugate spectral sequences** of Stacks Section 0FM6.

There are two cohomological spectral sequences `E₁` (starting at the page `0`) and `E₂` such that

* `E₁` is the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence: its first page is
  `E_1^{p,q} = H^q(X, Ω^p_{X/S})`, and under this identification `d_1^{p,q}` is the map
  `H^q(X, Ω^p_{X/S}) → H^q(X, Ω^{p+1}_{X/S})` induced by the de Rham differential;
* `E₂` is the conjugate spectral sequence: its second page is `E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X, 𝓗^q)`, with
  `𝓗^q = H^q(Ω^•_{X/S})` the `q`-th cohomology sheaf of the de Rham complex;
* both are bounded, and both converge to `H^*_{dR}(X/S)`: every `H^n_{dR}(X/S)` carries a finite
  decreasing filtration whose graded pieces are the terms `E_∞^{p, n - p}`.

Both come from [Stacks, Tag 015J] applied to `Γ(X, -)` and a Cartan-Eilenberg resolution of the
de Rham complex ([Stacks, Tag 015I]).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hodgeToDeRham_and_conjugate_spectralSequences :
    ∃ E₁ E₂ : CohomologicalSpectralSequence AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0,
      (∃ α : ∀ p q : ℤ, (E₁.page 1 zero_le_one).X (p, q) ≅
          ((sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus q).obj
            ((deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D).X p),
        ∀ p q : ℤ, (E₁.page 1 zero_le_one).d (p, q) (p + 1, q) ≫ (α (p + 1) q).hom =
          (α p q).hom ≫ ((sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus q).map
            ((deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D).d p (p + 1))) ∧
      Nonempty (∀ p q : ℤ, (E₂.page 2 zero_le_two).X (p, q) ≅
        ((sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus p).obj
          ((deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D).homology q)) ∧
      IsBounded E₁ ∧ IsBounded E₂ ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo E₁ (deRhamCohomologyAbelian B D) ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo E₂ (deRhamCohomologyAbelian B D)
declarations.comment:
the two spectral sequences of a Cartan-Eilenberg resolution of the de Rham
complex (Tag 015J for Γ(X, -)), both bounded and converging to H^*_dR(X/S): the Hodge-to-de Rham
spectral sequence with E_1^{p,q} = H^q(X, Ω^p) and d_1 induced by d, and the conjugate spectral
sequence with E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X, H^q(Ω^•)); the resolution is taken in abelian sheaves, the
category in which H^*_dR(X/S) is computed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.nonempty_deRhamCohomologyAbelian_zero_iso_kernel
declarations.doc:
**`H^0_{dR}(X/S) = Ker(d : H^0(X, 𝒪_X) → H^0(X, Ω^1_{X/S}))`**, read off the Hodge-to-de Rham
spectral sequence of Stacks Section 0FM6: in total degree `0` only `E_2^{0,0}` survives, and
`E_2^{0,0}` is the kernel of `d_1^{0,0} : H^0(X, Ω^0_{X/S}) → H^0(X, Ω^1_{X/S})`, the map induced on
`H^0(X, -)` by the de Rham differential `d : Ω^0_{X/S} = 𝒪_X → Ω^1_{X/S}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_deRhamCohomologyAbelian_zero_iso_kernel :
    Nonempty (deRhamCohomologyAbelian B D 0 ≅
      kernel (((sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus 0).map
        ((deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D).d 0 1)))
declarations.comment:
the conclusion read off the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence in degree 0:
H^0_dR(X/S) = Ker(d : H^0(X, O_X) → H^0(X, Ω^1_{X/S})), with O_X = Ω^0_{X/S} the degree 0 term
of the de Rham complex

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.nonempty_deRhamCohomologyAbelian_zero_iso_cohomologySheaf
declarations.doc:
**`H^0_{dR}(X/S) = H^0(X, 𝓗^0)`**, read off the conjugate spectral sequence of Stacks Section
0FM6: in total degree `0` only `E_2^{0,0} = H^0(X, 𝓗^0)` survives, where `𝓗^0 = H^0(Ω^•_{X/S})`
is the zeroth cohomology sheaf of the de Rham complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_deRhamCohomologyAbelian_zero_iso_cohomologySheaf :
    Nonempty (deRhamCohomologyAbelian B D 0 ≅
      ((sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus 0).obj
        ((deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D).homology 0))
declarations.comment:
the conclusion read off the conjugate spectral sequence in degree 0:
H^0_dR(X/S) = H^0(X, H^0), with H^0 = H^0(Ω^•_{X/S}) the zeroth cohomology sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.exists_exact_deRhamCohomologyAbelian_one_two
declarations.doc:
**The exact sequence of Stacks Section 0FM6 in degrees `1` and `2`**, read off the conjugate
spectral sequence: with `𝓗^q = H^q(Ω^•_{X/S})` the cohomology sheaves of the de Rham complex,
there is an exact sequence
`0 → H^1(X, 𝓗^0) → H^1_{dR}(X/S) → H^0(X, 𝓗^1) → H^2(X, 𝓗^0) → H^2_{dR}(X/S)`.
It is the five term exact sequence of the first-quadrant spectral sequence
`E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X, 𝓗^q) ⇒ H^{p+q}_{dR}(X/S)`, the third map being `d_2^{0,1}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_exact_deRhamCohomologyAbelian_one_two :
    ∃ (a : ((sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus 1).obj
          ((deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D).homology 0) ⟶ deRhamCohomologyAbelian B D 1)
      (b : deRhamCohomologyAbelian B D 1 ⟶ ((sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus 0).obj
          ((deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D).homology 1))
      (c : ((sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus 0).obj
          ((deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D).homology 1) ⟶
        ((sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus 2).obj
          ((deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D).homology 0))
      (t : ((sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus 2).obj
          ((deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D).homology 0) ⟶ deRhamCohomologyAbelian B D 2)
      (hab : a ≫ b = 0) (hbc : b ≫ c = 0) (hct : c ≫ t = 0),
      Mono a ∧ (ShortComplex.mk a b hab).Exact ∧ (ShortComplex.mk b c hbc).Exact ∧
        (ShortComplex.mk c t hct).Exact
declarations.comment:
the exact sequence read off the conjugate spectral sequence in degree 1:
0 → H^1(X, H^0) → H^1_dR(X/S) → H^0(X, H^1) → H^2(X, H^0) → H^2_dR(X/S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_hodgeToDeRham_and_conjugate_spectralSequences
declarations.doc:
**The Hodge-to-de Rham and the conjugate spectral sequences of a morphism of schemes**
`f : X → S` (Stacks Section 0FM6): two bounded spectral sequences converging to
`H^*_{dR}(X/S)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.deRhamCohomology`), the first with
`E_1^{p,q} = H^q(X, Ω^p_{X/S})` and `d_1` induced by the de Rham differential, the second with
`E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X, 𝓗^q)`. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.exists_hodgeToDeRham_and_conjugate_spectralSequences` for
`f^{-1}𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hodgeToDeRham_and_conjugate_spectralSequences :
    ∃ E₁ E₂ : CohomologicalSpectralSequence AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0,
      (∃ α : ∀ p q : ℤ, (E₁.page 1 zero_le_one).X (p, q) ≅
          ((Stacks.Cohomology.Leray.sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus q).obj
            ((SheafOfModules.deRhamAbelianComplexInt (deRhamAlgebras f)
              (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (deRhamAlgebras f))).X p),
        ∀ p q : ℤ, (E₁.page 1 zero_le_one).d (p, q) (p + 1, q) ≫ (α (p + 1) q).hom =
          (α p q).hom ≫ ((Stacks.Cohomology.Leray.sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus
            q).map ((SheafOfModules.deRhamAbelianComplexInt (deRhamAlgebras f)
              (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (deRhamAlgebras f))).d p (p + 1))) ∧
      Nonempty (∀ p q : ℤ, (E₂.page 2 zero_le_two).X (p, q) ≅
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.Leray.sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerivedPlus p).obj
          ((SheafOfModules.deRhamAbelianComplexInt (deRhamAlgebras f)
            (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (deRhamAlgebras f))).homology q)) ∧
      IsBounded E₁ ∧ IsBounded E₂ ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo E₁ (f.deRhamCohomology) ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo E₂ (f.deRhamCohomology)
declarations.comment:
for a morphism of schemes X → S: the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence
E_1^{p,q} = H^q(X, Ω^p_{X/S}) with d_1 induced by d, and the conjugate spectral sequence
E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X, H^q(Ω^•_{X/S})), both bounded and converging to H^*_dR(X/S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeFiltrationCup
declarations.doc:
**The cup product of Section 50.7 on the hypercohomology of the brutal truncations**,

`H^n(X, σ^{≥i}Ω^•_{X/S}) × H^m(X, σ^{≥j}Ω^•_{X/S}) ⟶ H^{n + m}(X, σ^{≥(i + j)}Ω^•_{X/S})`:

the cup product of Cohomology, Section 0FKU along the multiplication
`Tot(σ^{≥i}Ω^• ⊗_A σ^{≥j}Ω^•) ⟶ σ^{≥(i + j)}Ω^•` that the wedge product of Tag 0FM2 restricts to,
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeFiltrationWedge`.
declarations.comment: Section 50.7, the top row of the displayed diagram: the cup products H^n(X, σ^{≥i}Ω^•) × H^m(X, σ^{≥j}Ω^•) ⟶ H^{n+m}(X, σ^{≥(i+j)}Ω^•), the cup product of Cohomology Section 0FKU (the global cup product of the ringed space (X, A) built from the canonical one-point comparison) along the multiplication Tot(σ^{≥i}Ω^• ⊗ σ^{≥j}Ω^•) ⟶ σ^{≥(i+j)}Ω^• that the wedge product of 0FM2 restricts to

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap_hodgeFiltrationCup
declarations.doc:
**The commutative diagram of Section 50.7**: the maps
`H^n(X, σ^{≥p}Ω^•_{X/S}) ⟶ H^n_{dR}(X/S)` induced by the inclusions of the brutal truncations
carry the cup product on the brutal truncations to the cup product on de Rham cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap_hodgeFiltrationCup (p q i j : ℤ)
    (x : truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelian B D p i)
    (y : truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelian B D q j) :
    (truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap B D (p + q) (i + j)).hom
        (hodgeFiltrationCup B D p q i j x y) =
      deRhamCup B D i j ((truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap B D p i).hom x)
        ((truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap B D q j).hom y)
declarations.comment: Section 50.7, the commutative diagram it displays, with no parameter: the maps H^n(X, σ^{≥p}Ω^•) ⟶ H^n_dR(X/S) induced by the inclusions σ^{≥p}Ω^• ⟶ Ω^• carry the cup product H^n(X, σ^{≥i}Ω^•) × H^m(X, σ^{≥j}Ω^•) ⟶ H^{n+m}(X, σ^{≥(i+j)}Ω^•) to the cup product on H^*_dR(X/S), both cup products being those of Cohomology Section 0FKU

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamCup_mem_hodgeFiltrationAbelian
declarations.doc:
**The Hodge filtration is multiplicative**, the last assertion of Section 50.7:

`F^iH^n_{dR}(X/S) ∪ F^jH^m_{dR}(X/S) ⊂ F^{i + j}H^{n + m}_{dR}(X/S)`

for the cup product of Cohomology, Section 0FKU on de Rham cohomology. Membership in a step of
the filtration `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeFiltrationAbelian` of Tag 0FM8, a subobject
of `H^n_{dR}`, means being the image of an element of that subobject.
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamCup_mem_hodgeFiltrationAbelian (p q i j : ℤ)
    (x : deRhamCohomologyAbelian B D i) (y : deRhamCohomologyAbelian B D j)
    (hx : ∃ u : (hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D p i : AddCommGrpCat.{u}),
      ((hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D p i).arrow).hom u = x)
    (hy : ∃ v : (hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D q j : AddCommGrpCat.{u}),
      ((hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D q j).arrow).hom v = y) :
    ∃ w : (hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D (p + q) (i + j) : AddCommGrpCat.{u}),
      ((hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D (p + q) (i + j)).arrow).hom w = deRhamCup B D i j x y
declarations.comment: Section 50.7, its last assertion, with no parameter: the Hodge filtration is multiplicative for the cup product of Cohomology Section 0FKU on de Rham cohomology, F^i H^n_dR(X/S) ∪ F^j H^m_dR(X/S) ⊂ F^{i+j} H^{n+m}_dR(X/S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.exists_hodgeFiltrationSpectralSequence_iso_cartanEilenbergFirst
declarations.doc:
**The spectral sequence of the Hodge filtration is the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence of
Section 0FM6.** The spectral sequence of Cohomology, Lemma 0BKK for `Ω^•_{X/S}` filtered by its
brutal truncations is bounded, converges to the hypercohomology of `Ω^•_{X/S}`, and is isomorphic
to the first spectral sequence of every Cartan-Eilenberg resolution of `Ω^•_{X/S}`
(Derived Categories, Lemma 015J), which is how Section 0FM6 constructs the Hodge-to-de Rham
spectral sequence; this is Cohomology, Example 0FLK, clause (3), for the de Rham complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hodgeFiltrationSpectralSequence_iso_cartanEilenbergFirst :
    ∃ S : Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.StupidTruncationSpectralSequence
        (baseRingedSpace A) (deRhamComplexInt (X := X) B D),
      IsBounded S.spectralSequence ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo S.spectralSequence (fun n =>
        Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.hypercohomology (baseRingedSpace A) S.RΓ
          (deRhamComplexInt (X := X) B D) n) ∧
      ∀ I : (deRhamComplexInt (X := X) B D).CartanEilenbergResolution,
        Nonempty (S.spectralSequence ≅
          Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.cartanEilenbergFirstSpectralSequence
            (baseRingedSpace A) I)
declarations.comment: Section 50.7: the spectral sequence of Cohomology Lemma 0BKK for Ω^•_{X/S} viewed as a filtered complex (by its brutal truncations) is the same as the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence of Section 0FM6, i.e. the first spectral sequence of Derived Categories Lemma 015J built from a Cartan-Eilenberg resolution of Ω^•_{X/S}: one package, bounded, converging to the hypercohomology of Ω^•_{X/S}, and isomorphic to the first spectral sequence of every Cartan-Eilenberg resolution (Cohomology Example 0FLK)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamStupidSubcomplex_antitone
declarations.doc:
The brutal truncations form a **decreasing** chain of subcomplexes of the de Rham complex:
`σ^{≥1}Ω^• ⊃ σ^{≥2}Ω^• ⊃ ⋯`, because for `p ≤ q` the inclusion of `σ^{≥q}Ω^•` factors through
`σ^{≥p}Ω^•`.
declarations.statement: theorem deRhamStupidSubcomplex_antitone : Antitone (deRhamStupidSubcomplex B D)
declarations.comment:
the brutal truncations are subcomplexes of the relative de Rham complex and form
a decreasing filtration of it, the chain Ω^• = σ^{≥0}Ω^• ⊃ σ^{≥1}Ω^• ⊃ σ^{≥2}Ω^• ⊃ ⋯; this is
the decreasing half, that σ^{≥q}Ω^• ⊆ σ^{≥p}Ω^• for p ≤ q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamStupidSubcomplex_zero
declarations.doc:
The chain of brutal truncations starts at the de Rham complex itself:
`Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A} = σ^{≥0}Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A}`, because the de Rham complex is concentrated in nonnegative
degrees.
declarations.statement: theorem deRhamStupidSubcomplex_zero : deRhamStupidSubcomplex B D 0 = ⊤
declarations.comment:
the chain Ω^• = σ^{≥0}Ω^• ⊃ σ^{≥1}Ω^• ⊃ ⋯ starts at the de Rham complex itself:
the equality Ω^•_{X/S} = σ^{≥0}Ω^•_{X/S} at the left end of the display

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamStupidGradedPieceDerivedIso
declarations.doc:
**`gr^p(Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A}) = Ω^p_{𝒪_X/A}[-p]`.** In the derived category of sheaves of
`A`-modules the `p`-th graded piece of the brutal filtration of the de Rham complex is the sheaf
`Ω^p_{𝒪_X/A}` of relative `p`-forms, shifted down by `p`.
declarations.statement:
def deRhamStupidGradedPieceDerivedIso (p : ℕ) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((FilteredObject.gr (p : ℤ)).obj
        (CochainComplex.stupidTruncationFiltration (deRhamComplexInt (X := X) B D))) ≅
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj ((deRhamComplex B D).X p))⟦(-(p : ℤ))⟧
declarations.comment:
gr^p(Ω^•_{X/S}) = Ω^p_{X/S}[-p], the identification of the graded pieces of the
brutal filtration of the relative de Rham complex

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.exists_hodgeToDeRhamSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**The Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence of the brutal filtration of the de Rham complex.**

Read `Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A}` as a filtered complex of sheaves through its brutal truncations
`σ^{≥p}Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A}`. Its spectral sequence in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 0BKK] exists — through
the bounded-below form [Stacks, Tag 0BKL], the de Rham complex being concentrated in nonnegative
degrees — and comes packaged as a
`Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.StupidTruncationSpectralSequence`, the brutal-truncation
spectral sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0FLK], whose `e₁Iso` field is the first-page formula
`E_1^{p, q} = H^q(X, Ω^p_{𝒪_X/A})` of the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence of Section 50.6. So
the two spectral sequences of Section 50.7's third assertion are one object, constructed once.

It is **bounded**, it **abuts to relative de Rham cohomology** `H^n_{dR}(X/A)`, and the
filtration of the abutment along which it converges is the **Hodge filtration**
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeFiltration` of [Stacks, Tag 0FM8]: the last conjunct
identifies `E_∞^{p, q}` with `F^pH^{p + q}_{dR} / F^{p + 1}H^{p + q}_{dR}`.

The fourth conjunct reads the first page in the abelian-sheaf realization: with the `A(X)`-module
structure forgotten, `E_1^{p, q}` is the term in position `p` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeToDeRhamFirstPage B D q`, the `q`-th row of the first page
of Section 50.6.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hodgeToDeRhamSpectralSequence :
    ∃ S : Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.StupidTruncationSpectralSequence
        (baseRingedSpace A) (deRhamComplexInt (X := X) B D),
      IsBounded S.spectralSequence ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo S.spectralSequence (deRhamCohomology (X := X) B D) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ hodgeFiltration B D a n = ⊤ ∧
        hodgeFiltration B D b n = ⊥) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℕ, Nonempty
        ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} ((underlyingRingSheaf A).obj.obj (op ⊤))) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
            (((Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.globalSectionsSpectralSequence
                (baseRingedSpace A) S.replacement).page 1 (by omega)).X ((p : ℤ), (q : ℤ))) ≅
          (hodgeToDeRhamFirstPage B D q).X p)) ∧
      ∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty (S.spectralSequence.pageInfinity (p, q) ≅
        cokernel (Subobject.ofLE (hodgeFiltration B D (p + 1) (p + q))
          (hodgeFiltration B D p (p + q))
          (hodgeFiltration_antitone B D (p + q) (by omega))))
declarations.comment:
the spectral sequence of Cohomology Lemma 0BKK for Ω^•_{X/S} viewed as a filtered
complex of sheaves is the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence built by Cohomology Example 0FLK:
one object, carrying the Tag 0FLK first page E_1^{p,q} = H^q(X, Ω^p), bounded, abutting to
H^n_dR(X/S), and converging along the Hodge filtration of Tag 0FM8. Its first page is identified
term by term with the abelian-sheaf first page `hodgeToDeRhamFirstPage` of Section 0FM6; the
differentials d_1 of the two first pages are not compared

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeFiltrationWedge
declarations.doc:
**The multiplication of the Hodge filtration**

`Tot(σ^{≥i}Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A} ⊗_A σ^{≥j}Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A}) ⟶ σ^{≥(i + j)}Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A}`

induced by the wedge product of Tag 0FM2: the restriction of `∧` to the brutal truncations lands
in the `(i + j)`-th step of the filtration, because its source vanishes in every lower degree
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isZero_truncatedTensorSquare_X`).
declarations.statement:
def hodgeFiltrationWedge (i j : ℕ) :
    truncatedTensorSquare B D i j ⟶ deRhamBrutal B D (i + j)
declarations.comment: the wedge product of equation 0FM2 sends Tot(σ^{≥i}Ω^•_{X/S} ⊗_{p⁻¹𝒪_S} σ^{≥j}Ω^•_{X/S}) into σ^{≥(i+j)}Ω^•_{X/S}: the multiplication of the Hodge filtration on complexes. One assertion of the section; the hypercohomology diagrams it leads to are registered on `truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap_hodgeFiltrationCup` and `deRhamCup_mem_hodgeFiltrationAbelian`, and the filtration, its graded pieces and its spectral sequence on the declarations named in this file's module docstring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeFiltrationWedge_ιBrutal
declarations.doc:
**The multiplication of the Hodge filtration is the wedge product**: composing it with the
inclusion `σ^{≥(i + j)}Ω^• ⟶ Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A}` returns `∧` restricted to the truncations.
declarations.statement:
theorem hodgeFiltrationWedge_ιBrutal (i j : ℕ) :
    hodgeFiltrationWedge B D i j ≫ CochainComplex.ιBrutal (deRhamComplex B D) (i + j) =
      truncatedWedge B D i j
declarations.comment: that the morphism Tot(σ^{≥i}Ω^• ⊗ σ^{≥j}Ω^•) ⟶ σ^{≥(i+j)}Ω^• of the previous declaration really is the wedge product of equation 0FM2, i.e. that it lies over ∧ under the inclusion σ^{≥(i+j)}Ω^• ⟶ Ω^•. Without this the previous declaration would be some morphism into the (i+j)-th step rather than the section's assertion about ∧

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeFiltration
declarations.doc:
**The Hodge filtration** on relative de Rham cohomology: the `p`-th step
`F^p H^n_{dR} = Im (H^n(X, σ^{≥p}Ω^•) ⟶ H^n_{dR})` is the image of the hypercohomology of the
brutal truncation `σ^{≥p}Ω^•` of the de Rham complex, under the map induced by the inclusion of
that truncation.
declarations.statement: def hodgeFiltration (p n : ℤ) : Subobject (deRhamCohomology B D n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeFiltrationAbelian
declarations.doc:
**The Hodge filtration** on relative de Rham cohomology in the abelian-sheaf realization, in
every degree: the image of the hypercohomology of the brutal truncation `σ^{≥p}Ω^•` under the map
induced by its inclusion into the de Rham complex.
declarations.statement: def hodgeFiltrationAbelian (p n : ℤ) : Subobject (deRhamCohomologyAbelian B D n)
declarations.comment: abelian-sheaf realization in every degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.deRhamBoxTotalIso
declarations.doc:
For two morphisms of schemes `a : X ⟶ S` and `b : Y ⟶ S` there is a canonical isomorphism of
complexes

`Tot(Ω^•_{X/S} ⊠ Ω^•_{Y/S}) ≅ Ω^•_{X ×_S Y / S}`

between the total complex of the box product of the two relative de Rham complexes and the
relative de Rham complex of the fibre product. In degree `n` it is the isomorphism assembled from
the splitting of `Ω_{X ×_S Y/S}` of [Stacks, Tag 01V1], the Künneth decomposition of an exterior
power of a direct sum and the comparison of [Stacks, Tag 01CI], which on the `(p, q)` summand is
`ω ⊗ η ↦ pr₁^*ω ∧ pr₂^*η`; the compatibility with the differentials is the graded Leibniz
rule.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def deRhamBoxTotalIso :
    deRhamBoxTotal a b ≅ deRhamDiffOpComplex (pullback.fst a b ≫ a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.deRhamBoxTotalDegreeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FMA, the degreewise isomorphism.** In each degree `n` the total
complex `Tot(Ω^•_{X/S} ⊠ Ω^•_{Y/S})` of the box product of the two relative de Rham complexes is
canonically isomorphic to `Ω^n_{X ×_S Y / S}`, as objects of the category of finite-order
differential operators on `X ×_S Y / S`.

**Compatibility with the differentials is not included**: this is an isomorphism of the terms in
each fixed degree, not a morphism of complexes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def deRhamBoxTotalDegreeIso (n : ℕ) :
    (deRhamBoxTotal a b).X n ≅ (deRhamDiffOpComplex (pullback.fst a b ≫ a)).X n
declarations.comment: the degreewise isomorphism: in each degree `n` an isomorphism `Tot(Ω^•_{X/S} ⊠ Ω^•_{Y/S})^n ≅ Ω^n_{X ×_S Y/S}`. NOT compatibility with the differentials, and so NOT the isomorphism of complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.deRhamGlobalKunnethMap
declarations.doc:
**The de Rham Künneth map of [Stacks, Tag 0FMB]**

`RΓ(X, Ω^•_{X/S}) ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(Y, Ω^•_{Y/S}) ⟶ RΓ(X ×_S Y, Ω^•_{X ×_S Y/S})`

in `D(A)` for `A = Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`: the global Künneth map of [Stacks, Tag 0FLR] at the two relative
de Rham complexes, read as `ℤ`-indexed complexes by extension by zero, followed by derived global
sections of the isomorphism `Tot(Ω^•_{X/S} ⊠ Ω^•_{Y/S}) ≅ Ω^•_{X ×_S Y/S}` of
[Stacks, Tag 0FMA]. The complexes whose derived global sections are taken are the complexes of
inverse-image modules underlying the de Rham complexes; the global cup product `κ` is the one
parameter that the map of [Stacks, Tag 0FLR] carries, its step-(5) comparison being constructed
as `Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxTotalComparison`. The map of the source is this one at the
canonical global cup product `Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalKunneth.globalCupProductCanonical` of
[Stacks, Section 0FKU].
declarations.statement:
def deRhamGlobalKunnethMap (κ : GlobalCupProduct S.toRingedSpace) :
    ((tensorBase S.toRingedSpace).obj
          ((sectionsOverBase (inverseImageBaseProjection a)).obj
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (leftComplex a (deRhamDiffOpCochainComplex a))))).obj
        ((sectionsOverBase (inverseImageBaseProjection b)).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (rightComplex b (deRhamDiffOpCochainComplex b)))) ⟶
      (sectionsOverBase (inverseImageBaseProjection (pullback.fst a b ≫ a))).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((toInverseImageModules (pullback.fst a b ≫ a)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj ((deRhamDiffOpComplex (pullback.fst a b ≫ a)).extend
              ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)))
declarations.comment: the map: the global Künneth map of Tag 0FLR at the two de Rham complexes, read as ℤ-indexed complexes by extension by zero, followed by derived global sections of the Tag 0FMA isomorphism; it carries the one parameter of the Tag 0FLR map, the global cup product on the base, and the map of the source is this at the canonical global cup product globalCupProductCanonical of Section 0FKU. The step-(5) comparison is not carried, being constructed

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.isIso_deRhamGlobalKunnethMap_canonical
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FMB].** Let `S = Spec(A)` be affine and let `a : X ⟶ S` and `b : Y ⟶ S` be
smooth and quasi-compact with affine diagonal over `S`. Then the de Rham Künneth map

`RΓ(X, Ω^•_{X/S}) ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(Y, Ω^•_{Y/S}) ⟶ RΓ(X ×_S Y, Ω^•_{X ×_S Y/S})`

is an isomorphism in `D(A)`. The map is `deRhamGlobalKunnethMap` at the canonical global cup
product of [Stacks, Section 0FKU]. Nothing is assumed: the relative isomorphism of
[Stacks, Tag 0FMC] holds at these hypotheses, and over the affine base it gives the global one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_deRhamGlobalKunnethMap_canonical [IsAffine S]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth a] [AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth b] [QuasiCompact a] [QuasiCompact b]
    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal a)] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal b)] :
    IsIso (deRhamGlobalKunnethMap a b (globalCupProductCanonical S.toRingedSpace))
declarations.comment:
the isomorphism at the source's hypotheses (S affine; X, Y smooth and quasi-compact
  with affine diagonal over S), for the map built from the canonical global cup product of
  Section 0FKU; nothing is assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.deRhamRelativeKunnethMap
declarations.doc:
**The relative cup product of [Stacks, Tag 0FMC]**

`Ra_*Ω^•_{X/S} ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} Rb_*Ω^•_{Y/S} ⟶ Rf_*Ω^•_{X ×_S Y/S}`

in `D(𝒪_S)`: the relative Künneth map of [Stacks, Tag 0G4B] at the two relative de Rham
complexes, read as `ℤ`-indexed complexes by extension by zero, followed by `Rf_*` of the
isomorphism `Tot(Ω^•_{X/S} ⊠ Ω^•_{Y/S}) ≅ Ω^•_{X ×_S Y/S}` of [Stacks, Tag 0FMA]. The complexes
pushed forward are the complexes of inverse-image modules underlying the de Rham complexes. The
map of [Stacks, Tag 0G4B] carries no parameter: its step-(5) comparison is constructed, as
`Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxTotalComparison`, and is unique by
`Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.BoxTotalComparison.hom_unique`.
declarations.statement:
def deRhamRelativeKunnethMap :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor.{u, u + 1} (SheafedSpace.sheaf S.toRingedSpace)).obj
          ((derivedPushforward.{u, u + 1, u + 1} (inverseImageBaseProjection a)).obj
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (leftComplex a (deRhamDiffOpCochainComplex a))))).obj
        ((derivedPushforward.{u, u + 1, u + 1} (inverseImageBaseProjection b)).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (rightComplex b (deRhamDiffOpCochainComplex b)))) ⟶
      (derivedPushforward.{u, u + 1, u + 1}
          (inverseImageBaseProjection (pullback.fst a b ≫ a))).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((toInverseImageModules (pullback.fst a b ≫ a)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj ((deRhamDiffOpComplex (pullback.fst a b ≫ a)).extend
              ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)))
declarations.comment: the relative cup product whose invertibility the tag asserts

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.isIso_deRhamRelativeKunnethMap_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FMC]: the relative Künneth formula for de Rham complexes.** Let `a : X ⟶ S`
and `b : Y ⟶ S` be smooth and quasi-compact morphisms of schemes with affine diagonals. Then the
relative cup product
`Ra_*Ω^•_{X/S} ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} Rb_*Ω^•_{Y/S} ⟶ Rf_*Ω^•_{X ×_S Y/S}`
is an isomorphism in `D(𝒪_S)`. The relative Künneth map of [Stacks, Tag 0G4B] is invertible at
two flat modules in single degrees, by [Stacks, Tag 0FLQ] through the change of rings
(`isIso_relativeBoxKunnethMap_single`); hence at bounded complexes with flat terms, by the
dévissage of [Stacks, Tag 0FLT] (`isIso_relativeBoxKunnethMap_of_isIso_single`); hence at the
locally bounded de Rham complexes, by truncation
(`isIso_relativeBoxKunnethMap_of_isIso_stupidTrunc`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_deRhamRelativeKunnethMap_of_smooth {Y : Scheme.{u}} (b : Y ⟶ S) [Smooth a]
    [Smooth b] [QuasiCompact a] [QuasiCompact b] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal a)]
    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal b)] :
    IsIso (deRhamRelativeKunnethMap a b)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian_schemePullbackClassHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FMD.** **The de Rham first Chern class commutes with pullback**: for
a commutative square of schemes with horizontal arrows `f : X' ⟶ X` and `g : S' ⟶ S`, the square
formed by `c₁^{dR}`, by pullback of Picard classes and by the de Rham pullback
`H²_{dR}(X/S) ⟶ H²_{dR}(X'/S')` of [Stacks, Tag 0FL6] commutes.
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian_schemePullbackClassHom (c : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X) :
    SheafOfModules.deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian (deRhamAlgebras p')
        (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (deRhamAlgebras p'))
        (Stacks.GluePicard.picardModelAddEquiv X'.toRingedSpace
          (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom f c)) =
      (deRhamCohomologyPullback f p p' g hcomm 2).hom
        (SheafOfModules.deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian (deRhamAlgebras p)
          (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (deRhamAlgebras p))
          (Stacks.GluePicard.picardModelAddEquiv X.toRingedSpace c))
declarations.comment: the de Rham square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.hodgeFirstChernClass_schemePullbackClassHom
declarations.doc:
**The Hodge first Chern class commutes with pullback**: for a commutative square of schemes
with horizontal arrows `f : X' ⟶ X` and `g : S' ⟶ S`, the square formed by `c₁^{Hodge}`, by
pullback of Picard classes and by pullback on `H¹(-, Ω)` commutes.
declarations.statement:
theorem hodgeFirstChernClass_schemePullbackClassHom (c : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X) :
    hodgeFirstChernClass p' (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom f c) =
      (hodgeCohomologyOnePullback f p p' g hcomm).hom (hodgeFirstChernClass p c)
declarations.comment: the Hodge square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.filteredChernProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FME.** **The `a`-fold cup product
`ξ = γ₁(L₁) ∪ … ∪ γ₁(L_a) ∈ H^{2a}(X, σ^{≥a}Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A})`** of Hodge-filtered first Chern
classes, for `a = k + 1` invertible modules with Picard classes `L 0, …, L k`, the cup product
being the one of Section 50.7, `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeFiltrationCup`.

The filtration index and the cohomological degree are `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.cupLength`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.cupDegree`, which `cupLength_eq` and `cupDegree_eq` identify
with `a` and `2a`.
declarations.statement:
def filteredChernProduct : (k : ℕ) →
    (ℕ → Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property) →
      truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelian B D (cupLength k) (cupDegree k)
declarations.comment: Remark 50.9.2, clause F of A-I: the a-fold cup product ξ = γ₁(L₁) ∪ … ∪ γ₁(L_a) ∈ H^{2a}(X, σ^{≥a}Ω^•), for every a, formed with the cup product of Section 50.7 on the hypercohomology of the brutal truncations (`hodgeFiltrationCup`, the cup product of Cohomology Section 0FKU along the multiplication of the Hodge filtration) from the class γ₁ of clause B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap_filteredChernProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FME.** **The image of `ξ = γ₁(L₁) ∪ … ∪ γ₁(L_a)` under
`σ^{≥a}Ω^• ⟶ Ω^•` is `c₁^{dR}(L₁) ∪ … ∪ c₁^{dR}(L_a)` in `H^{2a}_{dR}(X/S)`.**

The induction is on the number of factors: for one factor this is clause `C`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian_eq`, and the inductive step is the
commutative diagram of Section 50.7,
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap_hodgeFiltrationCup`.
declarations.statement:
theorem truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap_filteredChernProduct (k : ℕ)
    (L : ℕ → Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property) :
    (truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap B D (cupLength k) (cupDegree k)).hom
        (filteredChernProduct B D k L) = deRhamChernProduct B D k L
declarations.comment: Remark 50.9.2, clause G of A-I: the map σ^{≥a}Ω^• ⟶ Ω^• sends ξ to the a-fold product c₁^dR(L₁) ∪ … ∪ c₁^dR(L_a) in H^{2a}_dR(X/S), for every a, both cup products being those of Cohomology Section 0FKU (`hodgeFiltrationCup` and `deRhamCup`)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamChernProduct_mem_hodgeFiltrationAbelian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FME.** **`c₁^{dR}(L₁) ∪ … ∪ c₁^{dR}(L_a)` lies in
`F^a H^{2a}_{dR}(X/S)`**, the `a`-th step of the Hodge filtration of Tag 0FM8.

The step `F^a H^{2a}_{dR}` is the image of `H^{2a}(X, σ^{≥a}Ω^•) ⟶ H^{2a}_{dR}`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap_filteredChernProduct`
exhibits the `a`-fold product as the image of `ξ` under exactly that map. Membership in the step is
written as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian_mem_hodgeFiltrationAbelian`: the
class is the image of an element of the subobject.
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamChernProduct_mem_hodgeFiltrationAbelian (k : ℕ)
    (L : ℕ → Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property) :
    ∃ y : (hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D (cupLength k) (cupDegree k) : AddCommGrpCat.{u}),
      ((hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D (cupLength k) (cupDegree k)).arrow).hom y =
        deRhamChernProduct B D k L
declarations.comment: Remark 50.9.2, clause H of A-I: the a-fold product c₁^dR(L₁) ∪ … ∪ c₁^dR(L_a), for the cup product of Cohomology Section 0FKU on de Rham cohomology (`deRhamCup`), is contained in the a-th step F^a H^{2a}_dR(X/S) of the Hodge filtration, for every a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeGradedIso_inv_gradedPieceProjection_filteredChernProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FME.** **The image of `ξ = γ₁(L₁) ∪ … ∪ γ₁(L_a)` under
`σ^{≥a}Ω^• ⟶ Ω^a_{𝒪_X/A}[-a]`, read in `H^a(X, Ω^a_{𝒪_X/A})`, is
`(-1)^{a(a - 1)/2} · c₁^{Hodge}(L₁) ∪ … ∪ c₁^{Hodge}(L_a)`**, the cup product being the one on
Hodge cohomology of Tag 0FM4, `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeCup`: the cup product of
Cohomology, Section 0FKU along the wedge product `Ω^p ⊗_A Ω^q ⟶ Ω^{p + q}` on the sheaves of forms
placed in degree `0`. The identification `H^{2a}(X, Ω^a[-a]) = H^a(X, Ω^a)` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeGradedIso`, the comparison of the two indexings of the
right derived functors followed by the degree shift of
`DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorShiftIso`, which for `a = 1` is the
identification of clause `E`.

**The sign.** The source states clause `I` without a sign. Through these identifications the cup
product on the graded pieces is the Hodge cup product up to `(-1)^{ib}` on
`H^{i + a}(Ω^a[-a]) × H^{j + b}(Ω^b[-b])`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeCohomologyIsoGradedPiece_gradedPieceCup`): moving the
shift `[-b]` of the second factor past a class of degree `i` costs `(-1)^{ib}`
(`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedGlobalCupProduct.totalCupPairing_shift₂`), and moving the shift `[-a]`
of the first factor costs nothing (`totalCupPairing_shift₁`). Each new factor `c₁(L)` has `i = 1`,
so the `(k + 1)`-st factor contributes `(-1)^k`, and the product of `a` factors carries
`(-1)^{0 + 1 + ⋯ + (a - 1)} = (-1)^{a(a - 1)/2}`, which is `-1` for `a ≡ 2, 3 mod 4`. This is the
corrected form of clause `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hodgeGradedIso_inv_gradedPieceProjection_filteredChernProduct (k : ℕ)
    (L : ℕ → Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property) :
    (hodgeGradedIso B D (k + 1) (k + 1) (cupLength k) (cupDegree k) (cast_eq_cupLength k)
        (cast_add_cupLength k)).inv.hom
      ((gradedPieceProjectionCohomologyMap B D (cupLength k) (cupDegree k)).hom
        (filteredChernProduct B D k L)) =
      hodgeChernSign k • hodgeCupChernProduct B D k L
declarations.comment: Remark 50.9.2, clause I of A-I, with the sign the identifications force: the map σ^{≥a}Ω^• ⟶ Ω^a[-a] sends ξ to (-1)^{a(a-1)/2} · c₁^Hodge(L₁) ∪ … ∪ c₁^Hodge(L_a) in H^{2a}(X, Ω^a[-a]) = H^a(X, Ω^a), for every a, the cup product being the Hodge cup product of Tag 0FM4 (`hodgeCup`: the cup product of Cohomology Section 0FKU along the wedge product Ω^p ⊗ Ω^q ⟶ Ω^{p+q} on the sheaves of forms in degree 0). The source states it without the sign; the sign is -1 for a ≡ 2, 3 mod 4

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.remark_filteredFirstChernClass
declarations.statement:
theorem remark_filteredFirstChernClass (k : ℕ)
    (L : ℕ → Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property) :
    (filteredLogarithmicDifferentialComplexMap B D ≫
        HomologicalComplex.ιStupidTrunc (deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D) (embeddingUpIntGE 1) =
      logarithmicDifferentialComplexMap B D) ∧
    (∀ c : Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj
        (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property,
      deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian B D c =
        (truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap B D 1 2).hom (filteredFirstChernClass B D c)) ∧
    (∀ c : Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj
        (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property,
      ∃ y : (hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D 1 2 : AddCommGrpCat.{u}),
        ((hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D 1 2).arrow).hom y = deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian B D c) ∧
    (∀ c : Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj
        (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property,
      (degreeOneProjectionCohomologyMap B D).hom (filteredFirstChernClass B D c) =
        (sheafCohomologyOneIsoShiftedCohomologyTwo X.carrier
          ((deRhamAbelianComplex B D).X 1)).hom.hom (hodgeFirstChernClassAbelian B D c)) ∧
    ((truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap B D (cupLength k) (cupDegree k)).hom
      (filteredChernProduct B D k L) = deRhamChernProduct B D k L) ∧
    (∃ y : (hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D (cupLength k) (cupDegree k) : AddCommGrpCat.{u}),
      ((hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D (cupLength k) (cupDegree k)).arrow).hom y =
        deRhamChernProduct B D k L) ∧
    ((hodgeGradedIso B D (k + 1) (k + 1) (cupLength k) (cupDegree k) (cast_eq_cupLength k)
        (cast_add_cupLength k)).inv.hom
      ((gradedPieceProjectionCohomologyMap B D (cupLength k) (cupDegree k)).hom
        (filteredChernProduct B D k L)) =
      hodgeChernSign k • hodgeCupChernProduct B D k L)
declarations.comment: Remark 50.9.2 IN FULL: ALL NINE CLAUSES A-I, FOR EVERY a. The conjuncts in order are A (d log as a map into σ^{≥1}Ω^•, pinned down to d log), B (the class γ₁(L), the morphism `filteredFirstChernClass` the conjuncts speak of), C (its image in H²_dR is c₁^dR), D (so c₁^dR ∈ F¹H²_dR), E (its image in H²(Ω¹[-1]) = H¹(Ω¹) is c₁^Hodge), F (the a-fold product ξ, the class `filteredChernProduct` the conjuncts speak of), G (its image in H^{2a}_dR is the a-fold product of the c₁^dR), H (so that product lies in F^a H^{2a}_dR) and I (its image in H^{2a}(Ω^a[-a]) = H^a(Ω^a) is (-1)^{a(a-1)/2} times the a-fold Hodge cup product of Tag 0FM4 of the c₁^Hodge, the sign being the one the identifications force, absent from the source). Every cup product is the one of Cohomology Section 0FKU along the multiplication the source names

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.filteredLogarithmicDifferentialComplexMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FME.** **Logarithmic differentiation as a morphism of complexes into
the first step of the Hodge filtration**, `d log : 𝒪_X^*[-1] ⟶ σ^{≥1}Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A}`.

The source is concentrated in degree one, hence strictly supported in degrees `≥ 1`, so the
morphism `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.logarithmicDifferentialComplexMap` into the de Rham
complex factors uniquely through the brutal truncation.
declarations.statement:
def filteredLogarithmicDifferentialComplexMap :
    unitsComplex X ⟶ (deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D).stupidTrunc (embeddingUpIntGE 1)
declarations.comment: d log as a map to the first step of the Hodge filtration

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.filteredLogarithmicDifferentialComplexMap_ι
declarations.doc:
The factorization of `d log` through the brutal truncation is one: composing it with the
inclusion of the truncation returns the unfiltered logarithmic differential.
declarations.statement:
theorem filteredLogarithmicDifferentialComplexMap_ι :
    filteredLogarithmicDifferentialComplexMap B D ≫
        HomologicalComplex.ιStupidTrunc (deRhamAbelianComplexInt B D)
          (embeddingUpIntGE 1) =
      logarithmicDifferentialComplexMap B D
declarations.comment: Remark 50.9.2, clause A of A-I, the theorem half: the factorization of d log through σ^{≥1}Ω^• IS d log, composing with σ^{≥1}Ω^• ⟶ Ω^• back to the unfiltered one. This is what pins `filteredLogarithmicDifferentialComplexMap` down to the source's map rather than to some morphism into the truncation. The covering set here is the a = 1 case, clauses A-E; the a ≥ 2 clauses F-I are proved for every a in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.DeRham.FirstChernClass.CanonicalChernCupProduct`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.filteredFirstChernClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FME.** **The first Chern class in Hodge-filtered de Rham
cohomology.** Logarithmic differentiation is a morphism of complexes of abelian sheaves
`𝒪_X^*[-1] ⟶ σ^{≥1}Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A}`, and `Pic(X) = H¹(X, 𝒪_X^*) = H²(X, 𝒪_X^*[-1])`; the class
`γ₁(L) ∈ H²(X, σ^{≥1}Ω^•_{𝒪_X/A})` of an invertible module is the image of its Picard class
under the composite.
declarations.comment: the filtered first Chern class

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian_eq
declarations.doc:
**The de Rham first Chern class is the image of the Hodge-filtered one** under the map
`H²(X, σ^{≥1}Ω^•) ⟶ H²_{dR}` induced by the inclusion of the first filtered step. In
particular `c₁^{dR}(L)` lies in the first step of the Hodge filtration,
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeFiltrationAbelian`, that step being by definition the
image of that map.
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian_eq
    (c : Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property) :
    deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian B D c =
      (truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap B D 1 2).hom (filteredFirstChernClass B D c)
declarations.comment: Remark 50.9.2, clause C of A-I: the image of γ₁(L) under σ^{≥1}Ω^• ⟶ Ω^• is the de Rham first Chern class c₁^dR(L). The a = 1 case; the a ≥ 2 analogue, clause G, is `truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelianMap_filteredChernProduct` in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.DeRham.FirstChernClass.CanonicalChernCupProduct`, which this is the base case of

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian_mem_hodgeFiltrationAbelian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FME.** **`c₁^{dR}(L)` lies in `F¹H²_{dR}(X/S)`**, the first step of
the Hodge filtration of Tag 0FM8.

The step `F¹H²_{dR}` is the image of `H²(X, σ^{≥1}Ω^•) ⟶ H²_{dR}`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian_eq` exhibits `c₁^{dR}(L)` as the
image of `γ₁(L)` under exactly that map; the witness is therefore `γ₁(L)` pushed into the
image.
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian_mem_hodgeFiltrationAbelian
    (c : Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property) :
    ∃ y : (hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D 1 2 : AddCommGrpCat.{u}),
      ((hodgeFiltrationAbelian B D 1 2).arrow).hom y =
        deRhamFirstChernClassAbelian B D c
declarations.comment: Remark 50.9.2, clause D of A-I: c₁^dR(L) lies in the first step F¹H²_dR of the Hodge filtration. The a = 1 case; the a ≥ 2 analogue, clause H, that the a-fold product c₁^dR(L₁) ∪ … ∪ c₁^dR(L_a) lies in F^a H^{2a}_dR, is `deRhamChernProduct_mem_hodgeFiltrationAbelian` in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.DeRham.FirstChernClass.CanonicalChernCupProduct`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.hodgeFirstChernClassAbelian_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FME.** **The image of `γ₁(L)` under `σ^{≥1}Ω^• ⟶ Ω¹_{𝒪_X/A}[-1]`
recovers `c₁^{Hodge}(L)`**, read through the identification `H¹(X, Ω¹) ≅ H²(X, Ω¹[-1])` of
`sheafCohomologyOneIsoShiftedCohomologyTwo`.

Both sides are the image of the Picard class under a map on degree-two hypercohomology induced
by `d log : 𝒪_X^*[-1] ⟶ Ω¹[-1]`: on the left because the projection composed with the filtered
`d log` is that map (`filteredLogarithmicDifferentialComplexMapPlus_degreeOneProjectionPlus`), on
the right because the identification is natural in the sheaf
(`sheafCohomologyOneIsoShiftedCohomologyTwo_hom_naturality`).
declarations.statement:
theorem hodgeFirstChernClassAbelian_eq
    (c : Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property) :
    (degreeOneProjectionCohomologyMap B D).hom (filteredFirstChernClass B D c) =
      (sheafCohomologyOneIsoShiftedCohomologyTwo X.carrier
          ((deRhamAbelianComplex B D).X 1)).hom.hom
        (hodgeFirstChernClassAbelian B D c)
declarations.comment: Remark 50.9.2, clause E of A-I: the image of γ₁(L) under σ^{≥1}Ω^• ⟶ Ω¹[-1] is the Hodge first Chern class c₁^Hodge(L) ∈ H¹(X, Ω¹). The a = 1 case; the a ≥ 2 analogue, clause I, is `hodgeGradedIso_inv_gradedPieceProjection_filteredChernProduct` in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.DeRham.FirstChernClass.CanonicalChernCupProduct`, which this is the base case of

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.filteredFirstChernClassOf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FME.** The Hodge-filtered first Chern class of an invertible
module.
declarations.statement:
abbrev filteredFirstChernClassOf (L : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf X.sheaf))
    (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L) :
    truncatedDeRhamCohomologyAbelian B D 1 2
declarations.comment: the filtered first Chern class of an invertible module

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjEulerSequence.exists_shortExact_eulerSequence
declarations.doc:
**There is a short exact sequence `0 ⟶ Ω ⟶ 𝒪(-1)^{⊕ (n+1)} ⟶ 𝒪 ⟶ 0`** on projective
`n`-space over a commutative ring, with `Ω` the sheaf of differentials relative to the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_eulerSequence :
    ∃ (a : projDifferentials R n ⟶ twistMinusOneSum R n)
      (b : twistMinusOneSum R n ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit (projRingSheaf (polyGrading R n)))
      (h : a ≫ b = 0), (CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.mk a b h).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceHodge.exists_basis_chernPow
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FMI], the basis.** For `0 ≤ p ≤ n` the `A`-module `Hᵖ(ℙⁿ_A, Ωᵖ)` is free of
rank one with basis element `c₁^{Hodge}(𝒪(1))ᵖ`, the `p`-th cup power of the Hodge first Chern
class of `𝒪(1)` (`hodgeChernPow`).

The proof is the source's. In degree zero `H⁰(ℙⁿ_A, 𝒪) = A` carries the unit `1` as a basis. The
boundary of `1` along the Euler sequence `0 ⟶ Ω ⟶ 𝒪(-1)^{⊕ (n+1)} ⟶ 𝒪 ⟶ 0` is
`c₁^{Hodge}(𝒪(1))`, computed on Čech cocycles: both are the class of `d log(T_{i₁}/T_{i₀})` on the
standard covering (`boundary_euler_one`). By [Stacks, Tag 07MC] applied to the filtration sequence
`0 ⟶ Ω^{p+1} ⟶ ⋀^{p+1}(𝒪(-1)^{⊕ (n+1)}) ⟶ Ωᵖ ⟶ 0` and the Euler sequence, the boundary of the
filtration sequence is, up to sign, the cup product with `c₁^{Hodge}(𝒪(1))`
(`boundary_wedgeSC`); since the middle term is acyclic it is an isomorphism
`Hᵖ(ℙⁿ_A, Ωᵖ) ≅ H^{p+1}(ℙⁿ_A, Ω^{p+1})` carrying `c₁^{Hodge}(𝒪(1))ᵖ` to
`±c₁^{Hodge}(𝒪(1))^{p+1}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_basis_chernPow (p : ℕ) (hp : p ≤ m + 1) :
    ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin 1) A ↥(hodgeCohomology A m p p), b 0 = hodgeChernPow A m p
declarations.comment:
for 0 ≤ p ≤ n the A-module H^p(ℙⁿ_A, Ω^p) is free of rank one with basis element
c₁^{Hodge}(𝒪(1))^p, the p-th cup power of the Hodge first Chern class of 𝒪(1)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceHodge.isZero_hodgeCohomology_of_ne_or_gt
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FMI], the vanishing.** `H^q(ℙⁿ_A, Ωᵖ) = 0` unless `0 ≤ p = q ≤ n`. The
source quotes this from [Stacks, Tag 0FUK], and so does the proof. The basis assertion of
[Stacks, Tag 0FMI] is `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceHodge.exists_basis_chernPow`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_hodgeCohomology_of_ne_or_gt (p q : ℕ)
    (hpq : p ≠ q ∨ m + 1 < p) : IsZero (hodgeCohomology A m p q)
declarations.comment: H^q(ℙⁿ_A, Ω^p) = 0 unless 0 ≤ p = q ≤ n

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceHodge.isZero_projectiveHodgeCohomology
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FMI], the vanishing, for every `n ≥ 0`.** `H^q(ℙⁿ_A, Ωᵖ) = 0` unless
`0 ≤ p = q ≤ n`. For `n ≥ 1` it is clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0FUK]
(`isZero_hodgeCohomology_of_ne_or_gt`); for `n = 0` it is
`isZero_projectiveHodgeCohomology_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_projectiveHodgeCohomology (p q : ℕ) (hpq : p ≠ q ∨ n < p) :
    IsZero (projectiveHodgeCohomology A n p q)
declarations.comment: H^q(ℙⁿ_A, Ω^p) = 0 unless 0 ≤ p = q ≤ n, for every n ≥ 0

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceHodge.exists_basis_projectiveHodgeChernPow
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FMI], the basis, for every `n ≥ 0`.** For `0 ≤ p ≤ n` the `A`-module
`Hᵖ(ℙⁿ_A, Ωᵖ)` is free of rank one with basis element `c₁^{Hodge}(𝒪(1))ᵖ`, the `p`-th cup power
of the Hodge first Chern class of `𝒪(1)` (`projectiveHodgeChernPow`).

For `n ≥ 1` this is `exists_basis_chernPow`, through `projectiveHodgeChernPow_succ`. For `n = 0`
only `p = 0` occurs, and `c⁰ = 1` is a basis of `H⁰(ℙ⁰_A, 𝒪) = A`
(`exists_basis_projectiveHodgeCohomology_unitForm`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_basis_projectiveHodgeChernPow (p : ℕ) (hp : p ≤ n) :
    ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin 1) A ↥(projectiveHodgeCohomology A n p p),
      b 0 = projectiveHodgeChernPow A n p
declarations.comment:
for 0 ≤ p ≤ n the A-module H^p(ℙⁿ_A, Ω^p) is free of rank one with basis element
c₁^{Hodge}(𝒪(1))^p, for every n ≥ 0

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceDeRham.isZero_deRhamCohomology
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FMJ], the vanishing.** In every degree that is not `2i` for some
`0 ≤ i ≤ n` the de Rham cohomology `H^•_dR(ℙⁿ_A/A)` of projective space vanishes.

By [Stacks, Tag 0FMI] the Hodge cohomology `H^q(ℙⁿ_A, Ωᵖ)` vanishes unless `p = q ≤ n`, so the
hypercohomology `H^k(ℙⁿ_A, Ωᵖ[-p])` of the graded pieces of the brutal filtration vanishes unless
`k = 2p`, and the terms vanish above degree `n`; inductively along the brutal filtration the
de Rham cohomology vanishes outside the degrees `2i`, `0 ≤ i ≤ n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_deRhamCohomology (i : ℤ) (hi : ∀ p : ℕ, p ≤ m + 1 → i ≠ 2 * p) :
    IsZero (deRhamCohomology A m i)
declarations.comment: the vanishing in every degree other than 2i with 0 ≤ i ≤ n

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceDeRham.exists_basis_chernPow
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FMJ], the computation in degree `2i`.** For `0 ≤ i ≤ n` the `A`-module
`H^{2i}_dR(ℙⁿ_A/A)` is free of rank one **with basis element `c₁^{dR}(𝒪(1))^i`**, the `i`-th cup
power of the de Rham first Chern class of `𝒪(1)`.

The Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence degenerates, which identifies `H^{2i}_dR(ℙⁿ_A/A)` with
`Hⁱ(ℙⁿ_A, Ωⁱ)` (`deRhamCohomologyEquiv`); under it `c₁^{dR}(𝒪(1))^i` goes to a unit multiple of
`c₁^{Hodge}(𝒪(1))^i` (`exists_gradedEquiv_gradedChernPow`), which is a basis by
[Stacks, Tag 0FMI].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_basis_chernPow (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ m + 1) :
    ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin 1) A ↥(deRhamCohomology A m (2 * (i : ℤ))), b 0 = chernPow A m i
declarations.comment: free of rank one with basis c₁^dR(𝒪(1))^i for 0 ≤ i ≤ n

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceDeRham.exists_basis_and_isZero_projectiveDeRhamCohomology
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FMJ].** For every `n ≥ 0`: for `0 ≤ i ≤ n` the `A`-module
`H^{2i}_dR(ℙⁿ_A/A)` is free of rank one with basis element `c₁^{dR}(𝒪(1))^i`, and in every
other degree `k` the de Rham cohomology `H^k_dR(ℙⁿ_A/A)` vanishes.

For `n ≥ 1` both parts are `exists_basis_chernPow` and `isZero_deRhamCohomology`. For `n = 0`
they are `exists_basis_projectiveDeRhamChernPow_zero` and
`isZero_projectiveDeRhamCohomology_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_basis_and_isZero_projectiveDeRhamCohomology :
    (∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ n → ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin 1) A ↥(projectiveDeRhamCohomology A n (2 * (i : ℤ))),
      b 0 = projectiveDeRhamChernPow A n i) ∧
    ∀ k : ℤ, (∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ n → k ≠ 2 * i) → IsZero (projectiveDeRhamCohomology A n k)
declarations.comment:
for 0 ≤ i ≤ n the A-module H^{2i}_dR(ℙⁿ_A/A) is free of rank one with basis
c₁^dR(𝒪(1))^i, and every other degree vanishes, for every n ≥ 0

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.deRhamSmoothFiltration_spec
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamSmoothFiltration_spec :
    (deRhamSmoothFiltration f g).X = deRhamCochainComplex (f ≫ g) ∧
      (∀ k : ℤ, (deRhamSmoothFiltration f g).filtration.subobject (op k) =
        AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.wedgeFiltrationStep
          (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras (f ≫ g))
          (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential
            (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras (f ≫ g)))
          (pulledBackDeRhamComplex f g)
          (Stacks.DeRhamPullback.deRhamPullbackChain f g) k) ∧
      Antitone (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.wedgeFiltrationStep
        (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras (f ≫ g))
        (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential
          (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras (f ≫ g)))
        (pulledBackDeRhamComplex f g)
        (Stacks.DeRhamPullback.deRhamPullbackChain f g)) ∧
      ∀ k : ℤ, k ≤ 0 → IsIso ((deRhamSmoothFiltration f g).filtration.ι.app (op k))
declarations.comment: the filtered complex: F^kΩ^•_{X/S} is the image of the wedge map out of Tot(f^{-1}σ_{≥k}Ω^•_{Y/S} ⊗_{p^{-1}O_S} Ω^•_{X/S}), a decreasing filtration of Ω^•_{X/S} by subcomplexes with F^0Ω^•_{X/S} = Ω^•_{X/S}; it holds for every f, smooth or not

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.relativeDifferentialsShortComplex_shortExact_and_locally_split
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0FMK: the locally split short exact sequence.** For `f : X ⟶ Y`
smooth over a base `S`, the sequence `0 ⟶ f^*Ω_{Y/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ 0` is short exact,
and every point of `X` has an open neighbourhood over which it splits.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDifferentialsShortComplex_shortExact_and_locally_split [Smooth f] :
    (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsShortComplex f g).ShortExact ∧
      ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧
        Nonempty (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsShortComplexRestrict f g U).Splitting
declarations.comment: the locally split short exact sequence 0 → f^*Ω_{Y/S} → Ω_{X/S} → Ω_{X/Y} → 0 of a smooth f (Tag 02K4)

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.relativeDifferentialsExteriorFiltration_smooth_spec
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDifferentialsExteriorFiltration_smooth_spec [Smooth f] (p : ℕ) :
    Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsExteriorFiltration f g p 0 = ⊤ ∧
      Antitone (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsExteriorFiltration f g p) ∧
      IsZero (Subobject.underlying.obj
        (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsExteriorFiltration f g p (p + 1))) ∧
      (∀ k m : ℕ, k + 1 + m = p →
        IsIso (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsPullbackGradedComparison f g k m)) ∧
      Nonempty (Subobject.underlying.obj
          (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsExteriorFiltration f g p p) ≅
        (Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.toRingedSpace.sheaf)).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
              (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms g (p : ℤ)),
            AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms f ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ)))
declarations.comment: the filtration Ω^p_{X/S} = F^0 ⊃ F^1 ⊃ … ⊃ F^{p+1} = 0 induced by f^*Ω_{Y/S} ⊆ Ω_{X/S}, with gr^kΩ^p_{X/S} ≅ f^*Ω^k_{Y/S} ⊗_{O_X} Ω^{p-k}_{X/Y} for k = 0, …, p (for k < p the canonical comparison is an isomorphism; for k = p, gr^p = F^p since F^{p+1} = 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.gradedPieceIsoGradedTargetComplexOfSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0FMK: the graded pieces of the filtered complex.** For
`f : X ⟶ Y` smooth over a base `S` and every `k`, the `k`-th graded piece of the filtration of
`Ω^•_{X/S}` by the forms pulled back from `Y` is

`gr^kΩ^•_{X/S}  ≅  f^{-1}Ω^k_{Y/S}[-k] ⊗_{f^{-1}𝒪_Y} Ω^•_{X/Y}`,

an isomorphism of complexes of `(f ∘ g)^{-1}𝒪_S`-modules on `X`. The target is
`Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.gradedTargetComplex`: its degree-`n` term is
`f^{-1}Ω^k_{Y/S} ⊗_{f^{-1}𝒪_Y} Ω^{n-k}_{X/Y}` (`Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.gradedTargetComplex_X`) and
its differential is `(-1)^k(1 ⊗ d_{X/Y})`, the one the shift `[-k]` carries
(`Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.gradedTargetComplex_d`).
declarations.comment: the graded pieces of the filtered complex: gr^kΩ^•_{X/S} ≅ f^{-1}Ω^k_{Y/S}[-k] ⊗_{f^{-1}O_Y} Ω^•_{X/Y} as complexes, for f smooth

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.nonempty_gradedPiece_X_iso_pulledBackTargetFormsTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0FMK: the graded pieces in each degree, over `f^{-1}𝒪_Y`.** For
`f : X ⟶ Y` smooth over a base `S` and `p = k + j`, the degree-`p` term of the `k`-th graded piece
of the filtration of `Ω^•_{X/S}` is `f^{-1}Ω^k_{Y/S} ⊗_{f^{-1}𝒪_Y} Ω^j_{X/Y}`, read over
`(f ∘ g)^{-1}𝒪_S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_gradedPiece_X_iso_pulledBackTargetFormsTensor [Smooth f] (k j p : ℕ)
    (h : k + j = p) :
    Nonempty ((gradedPiece (inverseImageBase (f ≫ g)) (k : ℤ) (deRhamSmoothFiltration f g)).X
        (p : ℤ) ≅
      (coefficientRestriction f g).obj ((pulledBackTargetFormsTensor f g k).obj
        ((pushforward (toInverseImageBase f)).obj
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms f ((j : ℕ) : ℤ)))))
declarations.comment: gr^kΩ^p_{X/S} ≅ f^{-1}Ω^k_{Y/S} ⊗_{f^{-1}O_Y} Ω^{p-k}_{X/Y} in each degree p = k + j, for f smooth

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeComplexPushforward.isIso_projectionFormulaMap_relativeComplex_of_isLocallyBounded_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FML, conclusion (5)**, with no hypothesis beyond the tag's own.  For
`f : X ⟶ S` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `K` an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_S)` and `F` a *locally
bounded* complex of `f^{-1}𝒪_S`-modules, the term in degree `i` being the restriction of scalars
of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `M i`, the projection-formula morphism of [Stacks, Tag 0B53] at
`(X, f^{-1}𝒪_S) ⟶ (S, 𝒪_S)` is an isomorphism.

`isIso_projectionFormulaMap_relativeComplex_of_isLocallyBounded` above with its hypothesis
discharged by `isIso_projectionFormulaMap_single_relativeBase`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_projectionFormulaMap_relativeComplex_of_isLocallyBounded_of_isQuasicoherent
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (K : DerivedCategory (Modules S.toRingedSpace))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf) K)
    (F : CochainComplex (Modules (inverseImageBase f)) ℤ)
    (hF : Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.IsLocallyBounded (inverseImageBase f) F)
    (M : ℤ → X.Modules) (hM : ∀ i, (M i).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hFM : ∀ i, F.X i ≅ (pushforward (toInverseImageBase f)).obj (M i)) :
    IsIso (projectionFormulaMap (inverseImageBaseProjection f)
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) K)
declarations.comment: conclusion (5), with no hypothesis beyond the tag's own: for a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes a : X ⟶ S, a LOCALLY BOUNDED complex F^• of a^{-1}O_S-modules each of whose terms carries a compatible quasi-coherent O_X-module structure, and K in D_QCoh(O_S), the Tag 0B53 map Ra_*F^• ⊗ᴸ_{O_S} K ⟶ Ra_*(F^• ⊗ᴸ_{a^{-1}O_S} L(a')^*K) is invertible. One difference from the source's phrasing, not a weakening: flatness of the terms, which the source assumes, is not needed for this conclusion and is not assumed. The two tensor factors are in the order the Tag 0B53 map produces them, which is the opposite of the source's

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeComplexPushforward.relativeComplexProjectionFormulaIsoOfIsLocallyBoundedOfIsQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FML, conclusion (5)** read as an isomorphism and with no hypothesis
beyond the tag's own,

`Rf_*F^• ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} K ≅ Rf_*(F^• ⊗^𝐋_{f^{-1}𝒪_S} f^{-1}K)`

for `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_S)` and `F` locally bounded, the two tensor products being written in the
order the morphism of [Stacks, Tag 0B53] produces them.
declarations.statement:
def relativeComplexProjectionFormulaIsoOfIsLocallyBoundedOfIsQuasicoherent [QuasiCompact f]
    [QuasiSeparated f] (K : DerivedCategory (Modules S.toRingedSpace))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf) K)
    (F : CochainComplex (Modules (inverseImageBase f)) ℤ)
    (hF : Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.IsLocallyBounded (inverseImageBase f) F)
    (M : ℤ → X.Modules) (hM : ∀ i, (M i).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hFM : ∀ i, F.X i ≅ (pushforward (toInverseImageBase f)).obj (M i)) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor S.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
        ((derivedPushforward (inverseImageBaseProjection f)).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F))).obj K ≅
      (derivedPushforward (inverseImageBaseProjection f)).obj
        (((derivedTensorProductFunctor (inverseImageBase f).sheaf).obj
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F)).obj
          ((derivedPullback (inverseImageBaseProjection f)).obj K))
declarations.comment: conclusion (5) read as an isomorphism, with no hypothesis beyond the tag's own: Ra_*F^• ⊗ᴸ_{O_S} K is Ra_*(F^• ⊗ᴸ_{a^{-1}O_S} a^{-1}K) for K in D_QCoh(O_S) and F^• LOCALLY BOUNDED. The same single difference from the source's phrasing as in the invertibility form, not a weakening: flatness of the terms is not needed for this conclusion and is not assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeComplexPushforward.relativeComplexOrdinaryProjectionFormulaIsoOfIsLocallyBoundedOfIsQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FML, conclusion (4)**, with no hypothesis beyond the tag's own.  For
`f : X ⟶ S` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `G` a *quasi-coherent* `𝒪_S`-module and `F` a
*locally bounded* complex of `f^{-1}𝒪_S`-modules, each term flat over `f^{-1}𝒪_S` and the
restriction of scalars of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module,

`Rf_*F^• ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} G ≅ Rf_*(F^• ⊗_{f^{-1}𝒪_S} f^{-1}G)`,

the tensor product on the right being the *ordinary* one.

`relativeComplexOrdinaryProjectionFormulaIsoOfIsLocallyBounded` above with its hypothesis
discharged by `isIso_projectionFormulaMap_single_relativeBase` at `K = G[0]`, which lies in
`D_QCoh(𝒪_S)` by `derivedCategoryB_isQuasicoherent_single`.
declarations.statement:
def relativeComplexOrdinaryProjectionFormulaIsoOfIsLocallyBoundedOfIsQuasicoherent
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (G : Modules S.toRingedSpace) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherent)
    (F : CochainComplex (Modules (inverseImageBase f)) ℤ)
    (hF : Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.IsLocallyBounded (inverseImageBase f) F)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u}
      (O := (inverseImageBase f).sheaf) (F.X i))
    (M : ℤ → X.Modules) (hM : ∀ i, (M i).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hFM : ∀ i, F.X i ≅ (pushforward (toInverseImageBase f)).obj (M i)) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor S.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
        ((derivedPushforward (inverseImageBaseProjection f)).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F))).obj
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Modules S.toRingedSpace) 0).obj G) ≅
      (derivedPushforward (inverseImageBaseProjection f)).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.tensorComplex (inverseImageBase f).sheaf).obj F).obj
            ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules (inverseImageBase f)) 0).obj
              ((RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback
                (inverseImageBaseProjection f)).obj G))))
declarations.comment: conclusion (4), with no hypothesis beyond the tag's own: for a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes a : X ⟶ S, a LOCALLY BOUNDED complex F^• of a^{-1}O_S-modules each of whose terms is flat over a^{-1}O_S and carries a compatible quasi-coherent O_X-module structure, and an ORDINARY quasi-coherent O_S-module G, Ra_*F^• ⊗ᴸ_{O_S} G is Ra_*(F^• ⊗_{a^{-1}O_S} a^{-1}G) with the ORDINARY tensor product on the right. The two tensor factors are in the order the Tag 0B53 map produces them, which is the opposite of the source's

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeComplexPushforward.relativeDerivedPushforward_locallyBounded_qcoh_torDimension_projectionFormula
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FML.** Let `a : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
morphism of schemes and `F^•` a locally bounded complex of `a⁻¹𝒪_S`-modules, each term `F^n` a
flat `a⁻¹𝒪_S`-module carrying the structure of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `M n` compatible
with its `a⁻¹𝒪_S`-module structure (`F^n ≅ b_*(M n)` for `b : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (X, a⁻¹𝒪_S)`; the
differentials of `F^•` need not be `𝒪_X`-linear). Write `Ra_*F^•` for the derived pushforward
along the morphism of ringed spaces `(X, a⁻¹𝒪_S) ⟶ (S, 𝒪_S)`. Then

1. `Ra_*F^•` is locally bounded: every point of `S` has an open neighbourhood `U` on which
   `(Ra_*F^•)|_U` has only finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves;
2. `Ra_*F^•` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_S)`;
3. `Ra_*F^•` locally has finite Tor dimension;
4. `Ra_*F^• ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} 𝒢 ≅ Ra_*(F^• ⊗_{a⁻¹𝒪_S} a⁻¹𝒢)` for every quasi-coherent `𝒢`;
5. the map of [Stacks, Tag 0B53] `Ra_*F^• ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} K ⟶ Ra_*(F^• ⊗^𝐋_{a⁻¹𝒪_S} a⁻¹K)` is an
   isomorphism for every `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_S)`.

The tensor products in (4) and (5) are written in the order the map of [Stacks, Tag 0B53]
produces them, the opposite of the source's; the two orders agree by symmetry. Conclusions (4)
and (5) are `relativeComplexOrdinaryProjectionFormulaIsoOfIsLocallyBoundedOfIsQuasicoherent` and
`isIso_projectionFormulaMap_relativeComplex_of_isLocallyBounded_of_isQuasicoherent`.
Conclusions (1)–(3) are local on `S`; over an affine open `V` the complex is bounded on the
quasi-compact `a⁻¹V`, and `prop_restrict_derivedPushforward_relativeComplex` reduces each of
them to a single quasi-coherent `M n`, where (1) is [Stacks, Tag 01XJ], (2) is the
quasi-coherence of the higher direct images and (3) is the Mayer–Vietoris bound on Tor amplitude
of a derived direct image of a module flat over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDerivedPushforward_locallyBounded_qcoh_torDimension_projectionFormula
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (F : CochainComplex (Modules (inverseImageBase f)) ℤ)
    (hF : Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.IsLocallyBounded (inverseImageBase f) F)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u}
      (O := (inverseImageBase f).sheaf) (F.X i))
    (M : ℤ → X.Modules) (hM : ∀ i, (M i).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hFM : ∀ i, F.X i ≅ (pushforward (toInverseImageBase f)).obj (M i)) :
    (∀ s : S, ∃ U : S.Opens, s ∈ U ∧ DerivedCategoryB.IsBounded
      ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((derivedPushforward (inverseImageBaseProjection f)).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F)))) ∧
    (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (_root_.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf) :
      ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (Modules S.toRingedSpace)))
      ((derivedPushforward (inverseImageBaseProjection f)).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F)) ∧
    LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension S.toRingedSpace
      ((derivedPushforward (inverseImageBaseProjection f)).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F)) ∧
    (∀ G : Modules S.toRingedSpace, G.IsQuasicoherent →
      Nonempty (((derivedTensorProductFunctor S.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
          ((derivedPushforward (inverseImageBaseProjection f)).obj
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F))).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Modules S.toRingedSpace) 0).obj G) ≅
        (derivedPushforward (inverseImageBaseProjection f)).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.tensorComplex (inverseImageBase f).sheaf).obj F).obj
              ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules (inverseImageBase f)) 0).obj
                ((RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback
                  (inverseImageBaseProjection f)).obj G)))))) ∧
    (∀ K : DerivedCategory (Modules S.toRingedSpace),
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf) K →
      IsIso (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedProjectionFormula.projectionFormulaMap
        (inverseImageBaseProjection f) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) K))
declarations.comment: all five conclusions, under exactly the source's hypotheses: a : X ⟶ S quasi-compact and quasi-separated, F^• a LOCALLY BOUNDED complex of a^{-1}O_S-modules with flat terms each carrying a compatible quasi-coherent O_X-module structure (differentials not O_X-linear); Ra_* is the unbounded derived pushforward along (X, a^{-1}O_S) ⟶ (S, O_S).
