(1) every point of S has an open neighbourhood U with (Ra_*F^•)|_U cohomologically bounded; (2) Ra_*F^• in D_QCoh(O_S); (3) LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension at the derived tensor product of Tag 06YU; (4) an isomorphism Ra_*F^• ⊗ᴸ G ≅ Ra_*(F^• ⊗ a^{-1}G) for G quasi-coherent; (5) invertibility of the Tag 0B53 map for K in D_QCoh(O_S). Tensor factors in (4), (5) are in the order the Tag 0B53 map produces them, the opposite of the source's

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeComplexPushforward.isQuasicoherent_homology_relativeDerivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FML, conclusion (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be quasi-compact and
quasi-separated and let `K` be a complex of `f^{-1}𝒪_S`-modules, strictly bounded below, whose
term in degree `i` is the restriction of scalars of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `M i`. Then
every cohomology sheaf of `Rf_*K` is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_homology_relativeDerivedPushforward [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (n : ℤ) (K : CochainComplex (Modules (inverseImageBase f)) ℤ)
    [CochainComplex.IsStrictlyGE K n] (M : ℤ → X.Modules) (hM : ∀ i, (M i).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hK : ∀ i, K.X i ≅ (pushforward (toInverseImageBase f)).obj (M i)) (i : ℤ) :
    ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor S.Modules i).obj
      (relativeDerivedPushforward f n K)).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: conclusion (2), that Ra_* of the complex lies in D_QCoh, degreewise, for a complex bounded below with an explicit bound rather than merely locally bounded

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeComplexPushforward.derivedCategoryB_relativeDerivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FML, conclusion (2)**, in the membership form: the object property on
`D(𝒪_S)` cutting out the complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology holds of `Rf_*K`. The complex
being bounded below, `Rf_*K` is read in `D⁺(𝒪_S)` and compared with `D(𝒪_S)` along the
inclusion, under which the cohomology functors agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryB_relativeDerivedPushforward [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (n : ℤ) (K : CochainComplex (Modules (inverseImageBase f)) ℤ)
    [CochainComplex.IsStrictlyGE K n] (M : ℤ → X.Modules) (hM : ∀ i, (M i).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hK : ∀ i, K.X i ≅ (pushforward (toInverseImageBase f)).obj (M i)) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (_root_.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf)
      (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj (relativeDerivedPushforward f n K))
declarations.comment: conclusion (2), that Ra_* of the complex lies in D_QCoh, as a membership, for a complex bounded below with an explicit bound rather than merely locally bounded

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.exists_boundedDeRhamSpectralSequence_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated and smooth morphism of schemes over a base
scheme `S`, with `g : Y ⟶ S` the structure morphism of the target. There is a bounded cohomological
spectral sequence of sheaves of `g^{-1}𝒪_S`-modules on `Y`, starting at its first page, with

`E_1^{p,q} = H^q(Ω^p_{Y/S} ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_Y} Rf_*Ω^•_{X/Y})`,

which abuts to `R^{p+q}f_*Ω^•_{X/S}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedDeRhamSpectralSequence_of_smooth
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [Smooth f] :
    ∃ E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing (Stacks.DeRhamDirectImage.inverseImageBase g))) 1,
      _root_.IsBounded E ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty ((E.page 1).X (p, q) ≅ deRhamFirstPage f g p q)) ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo E (fun n => deRhamHigherDirectImage f g n)
declarations.comment: the bounded spectral sequence of a quasi-compact, quasi-separated, smooth morphism, with first page H^q(Ω^p_{Y/S} ⊗ᴸ Rf_*Ω^•_{X/Y}) and abutment R^{p+q}f_*Ω^•_{X/S}

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamRigidity.isLocallyFree_deRhamCohomologySheaf_of_proper_smooth_rat
declarations.doc:
**The de Rham cohomology sheaves of a proper smooth morphism over `ℚ` are finite locally
free** ([Stacks, Tag 0FMN], the sentence the source defers to a future reference). Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be proper and smooth, with `Y` over a scheme `S` over `Spec R` for a `ℚ`-algebra `R`.
Then every `ℋ^q_dR(X/Y)` is a finite locally free `𝒪_Y`-module. The proof reduces to an Artinian
local base (`Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.isLocallyFree_deRhamCohomologySheaf_of_artinian`), where the
de Rham complex is rigid (`nonempty_derivedDeRhamDirectImage_iso_trivialMap`) and the trivial
deformation has free cohomology (`free_moduleSpecΓ_deRhamCohomologySheaf_trivialMap`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyFree_deRhamCohomologySheaf_of_proper_smooth_rat {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    {R : CommRingCat.{u}} [Algebra ℚ R] (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) (σ : S ⟶ Spec R) [IsProper f]
    [Smooth f] (q : ℤ) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (deRhamCohomologySheaf f q)
declarations.comment: if f is proper in addition to being smooth and S is a scheme over Q, then H^q_dR(X/Y) is finite locally free (the sentence the source defers to a future reference)

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.deRhamSmoothSpectralSequence_gaussManin
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FMN.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated, smooth
morphism of schemes over `S`, with `g : Y ⟶ S` the structure morphism of the target, and suppose
the de Rham cohomology sheaves `ℋ^q_dR(X/Y)` are flat `𝒪_Y`-modules. Then the spectral sequence
`E` of [Stacks, Tag 0FMM] (bounded, abutting to `R^{p + q}f_*Ω^•_{X/S}`) has
`E_1^{p, q} = Ω^p_{Y/S} ⊗_{𝒪_Y} ℋ^q_dR(X/Y)` (`deRhamSmoothFirstPageFlatIso`), and for every `q`:

1. its differentials are maps `d_1^{p, q} : Ω^p_{Y/S} ⊗ ℋ^q ⟶ Ω^{p + 1}_{Y/S} ⊗ ℋ^q`, namely
   `deRhamFirstPageFlatDifferential`, and they satisfy the Katz–Oda Leibniz rule
   `d_1(ω ⊗ s) = dω ⊗ s + (-1)^p ω ∧ d_1(1 ⊗ s)`;
2. `d_1^{0, q} : ℋ^q ⟶ Ω^1_{Y/S} ⊗ ℋ^q` is the integrable connection `∇` of
   `gaussManinConnection` (the **Gauss–Manin connection**), read through
   `Ω^1_{Y/S} ⊗ ℋ^q ≅ ℋ^q ⊗ Ω_{Y/S}`;
3. the complex `ℋ^q ⟶ Ω^1_{Y/S} ⊗ ℋ^q ⟶ Ω^2_{Y/S} ⊗ ℋ^q ⟶ ⋯` with differentials `d_1^{•, q}` is
   the de Rham complex of `∇` (`gaussManinTwistedDifferential`, a complex), its differential in
   degree `p` being `d_1^{p, q}` read through `Ω^p_{Y/S} ⊗ ℋ^q ≅ ℋ^q ⊗ Ω^p_{Y/S}`.

The sentence of the remark on finite local freeness for proper `f` over `ℚ` is deferred by the
source to a future reference and is not included.
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamSmoothSpectralSequence_gaussManin (q : ℤ) :
    _root_.IsBounded (deRhamSmoothSpectralSequence f g) ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo (deRhamSmoothSpectralSequence f g)
        (fun n => deRhamHigherDirectImage f g n) ∧
      (∀ p : ℤ, Nonempty (((deRhamSmoothSpectralSequence f g).page 1).X (p, q) ≅
        deRhamFirstPageFlat f g p q)) ∧
      (∀ p : ℤ, ((deRhamSmoothSpectralSequence f g).page 1).d (p, q) (p + 1, q) =
        (deRhamSmoothFirstPageFlatIso f g hflat p q).hom ≫
          deRhamFirstPageFlatDifferential f g hflat p q ≫
            (deRhamSmoothFirstPageFlatIso f g hflat (p + 1) q).inv) ∧
      IsKatzOdaLeibniz g (deRhamCohomologySheaf f q)
        (fun p => deRhamFirstPageFlatDifferential f g hflat p q) ∧
      (∀ (U : (Y.Opens)ᵒᵖ) (s : (deRhamCohomologySheaf f q).val.obj U),
        (gaussManinConnection f g hflat q).d U s =
          (formsTensorConnectionIso g (deRhamCohomologySheaf f q)).hom.val.app U
            ((deRhamFirstPageFlatDifferential f g hflat 0 q).val.app U
              (formsTensorUnitTmul g (deRhamCohomologySheaf f q) U s))) ∧
      (gaussManinConnection f g hflat q).IsIntegrable (gaussManinTwistedDifferential f g hflat q) ∧
      (gaussManinTwistedDifferential f g hflat q).IsComplex ∧
      ∀ p : ℕ, (gaussManinTwistedDifferential f g hflat q).d p =
        (_root_.pushforward (toInverseImageBase g)).map
            (β_ (modulesOnRing (deRhamCohomologySheaf f q)) (formsOnRing g p)).hom ≫
          deRhamFirstPageFlatDifferential f g hflat p q ≫
          (_root_.pushforward (toInverseImageBase g)).map
            ((formsTensorSuccIso g (deRhamCohomologySheaf f q) p).hom ≫
              (β_ (formsOnRing g ((p + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ))
                (modulesOnRing (deRhamCohomologySheaf f q))).hom)
declarations.comment: the first page Ω^p_{Y/S} ⊗ ℋ^q_dR(X/Y) for flat ℋ^q_dR, d_1^{0,q} the integrable Gauss–Manin connection and d_1^{•,q} its de Rham complex; the finite local freeness for proper f over ℚ is deferred by the source and omitted

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.deRhamCohomologySheaf
declarations.doc:
**`ℋ^q_dR(X/Y) = H^q(Rf_*Ω^•_{X/Y})`**, the `q`-th de Rham cohomology sheaf of `X` over `Y`:
the `q`-th cohomology sheaf of the derived direct image along `f` of the relative de Rham complex
of `X` over `Y`, a sheaf of `𝒪_Y`-modules.

The derived direct image is `Stacks.DeRhamDirectImage.derivedDeRhamDirectImage`, an object of
`D⁺(𝒪_Y)`, so the cohomology is read with the cohomology functors of `D⁺`; along the inclusion
of `D⁺(𝒪_Y)` into `D(𝒪_Y)` these agree with the cohomology functors of `D(𝒪_Y)`. By
[Stacks, Tag 0FLX] — `Stacks.DeRhamDirectImage.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedDeRhamDirectImage`
— these sheaves are quasi-coherent whenever `f` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
declarations.statement: def deRhamCohomologySheaf (q : ℤ) : Y.Modules
declarations.comment: the cohomology sheaves ℋ^q_dR(X/Y) = H^q(Rf_*Ω^•_{X/Y})

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.deRhamFirstPageFlat
declarations.doc:
**`Ω^p_{Y/S} ⊗_{𝒪_Y} ℋ^q_dR(X/Y)`**, the module the remark [Stacks, Tag 0FMN] writes the
first page of the spectral sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0FMM] as when the `ℋ^q_dR(X/Y)` are flat:
the ordinary — not derived — tensor product over `𝒪_Y` of the sheaf `Ω^p_{Y/S}` of relative
`p`-forms of `Y` over `S` with the `q`-th de Rham cohomology sheaf of `X` over `Y`, read as a
sheaf of `g^{-1}𝒪_S`-modules by restriction of scalars along `g^{-1}𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_Y`.

The restriction of scalars is the one `Stacks.DeRhamSmooth.deRhamFirstPage` uses, so this module
and `deRhamFirstPage f g p q` are objects of the same category; `deRhamFirstPageIsoFlat` is the
isomorphism between them, granted the hypotheses the source does not discharge.
declarations.statement: def deRhamFirstPageFlat (p q : ℤ) : Modules (inverseImageBase g)
declarations.comment: the module Ω^p_{Y/S} ⊗_{𝒪_Y} ℋ^q_dR(X/Y) of the flat case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeRhamLerayHirsch.isIso_deRhamClassSumMorphism
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FMP], the Leray--Hirsch theorem for de Rham cohomology.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
smooth proper morphism of schemes, let `n_1, …, n_N ≥ 0` be integers and let
`ξ_i ∈ H^{n_i}_{dR}(X/Y)`. If for every point `y ∈ Y` the images of `ξ_1, …, ξ_N` in
`H^*_{dR}(X_y/κ(y))` form a basis over `κ(y)`, then the morphism

`⨁_{i=1}^N 𝒪_Y[-n_i] ⟶ Rf_*Ω^•_{X/Y}`

associated to `ξ_1, …, ξ_N` is an isomorphism in `D(𝒪_Y)`.

The source and the target are perfect, the target by [Stacks, Tag 0FM0], so it suffices that its
derived pullback to every point be an isomorphism; the formation of `Rf_*Ω^•_{X/Y}` commutes with
that base change ([Stacks, Tag 0FM0]), and over `κ(y)` the morphism carries the pullbacks of the
classes of `1` to the images of the `ξ_i` in the de Rham cohomology of the fibre, which form a
basis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_deRhamClassSumMorphism [Smooth f] [IsProper f] {N : ℕ} (n : Fin N → ℕ)
    (ξ : ∀ i : Fin N, ToType (Scheme.Hom.deRhamCohomology f (n i : ℤ)))
    (hb : HasFibrewiseDeRhamBasis f n ξ) :
    IsIso (deRhamClassSumMorphism f n ξ)
declarations.comment: the Leray-Hirsch isomorphism for de Rham cohomology: for f : X -> Y smooth proper, classes xi_i in H^{n_i}_dR(X/Y) whose images in H^*_dR(X_y/kappa(y)) form a kappa(y)-basis at every point y give an isomorphism (+)_i O_Y[-n_i] -> Rf_*Omega^bullet_{X/Y} in D(O_Y); the morphism is constructed from the classes through H^m_dR(X/Y) = Hom(O_Y[-m], Rf_*Omega^bullet_{X/Y}), and perfectness and base change of Rf_*Omega^bullet (Tag 0FM0) are the library's unconditional theorems

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.kFlat_totalCechComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FMQ.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes with `S` affine and
`A = Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`, and let `U : I → X.Opens` be a finite family of opens all of whose
finite intersections are affine. Let `K` be a bounded complex of presheaves of `A`-modules
on `X` whose degree-`n` term is the presheaf of sections of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module
`F n` that is flat over `S`. Then `Tot(Č^•(𝒰, K))` is K-flat as a complex of `A`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem kFlat_totalCechComplex {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S)
    {I : Type u} [Finite I] (U : I → X.Opens)
    (haffine : ∀ (p : ℕ) (s : Fin (p + 1) → I), IsAffineOpen (⨅ k, U (s k)))
    (K : CochainComplex ((X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} ↑Γ(S, ⊤)) ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
    [CochainComplex.IsStrictlyGE K a] [CochainComplex.IsStrictlyLE K b]
    (F : ℤ → X.Modules) (hqc : ∀ n, (F n).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hflat : ∀ n, IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom (F n))
    (hterm : ∀ n, K.X n ≅ sectionsPresheaf f (F n)) :
    CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} ((totalCechComplex U).obj K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeRhamLerayHirsch.isIso_lerayHirschMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Proposition 0FMR, the derived statement.** For a smooth proper morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` over `S` and classes `ξ_i ∈ H^{n_i}_{dR}(X/S)` whose images in `H^*_{dR}(X_y/y)` form a
basis over `κ(y)` for every point `y ∈ Y`, the morphism
`ξ̃ = ⨁ ξ̃_i[-n_i] : ⨁ Ω^•_{Y/S}[-n_i] ⟶ Rf_*Ω^•_{X/S}` is an isomorphism in
`D(Y, (Y ⟶ S)^{-1}𝒪_S)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_lerayHirschMorphism [Smooth f] [IsProper f] {r : ℕ} (n : Fin r → ℕ)
    (ξ : ∀ i, SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomology (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras (f ≫ g))
      (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras (f ≫ g))) (n i : ℤ))
    (hb : ∀ y : Y, ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin r) (Y.residueField y)
        (DirectSum ℤ fun m : ℤ => ↥(fibreDeRhamModule f y m)),
      ∀ i, b i = DirectSum.lof (Y.residueField y) ℤ (fun m : ℤ => ↥(fibreDeRhamModule f y m))
        (n i : ℤ) (fibreClassOverS f g y (n i : ℤ) (ξ i))) :
    IsIso (lerayHirschMorphism f g n ξ)
declarations.comment: first assertion: for f smooth proper over S and classes ξ_i ∈ H^{n_i}_dR(X/S) whose images in H^*_dR(X_y/y) form a κ(y)-basis for all y ∈ Y, the map ξ~ = ⊕ ξ~_i[-n_i] : ⊕ Ω_{Y/S}[-n_i] → Rf_*Ω_{X/S} is an isomorphism in D(Y, (Y → S)^{-1}O_S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeRhamLerayHirsch.bijective_sum_deRhamCohomologyCup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Proposition 0FMR, the statement on de Rham cohomology.** For a smooth proper
morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` over `S` and classes `ξ_i ∈ H^{n_i}_{dR}(X/S)` whose images in
`H^*_{dR}(X_y/y)` form a basis over `κ(y)` for every point `y ∈ Y`, the map
`⨁_i H^*_{dR}(Y/S) ⟶ H^*_{dR}(X/S), (a_i) ↦ ∑ ξ_i ∪ f^*a_i` is an isomorphism: in every degree `k`
the map `⨁_i H^{k - n_i}_{dR}(Y/S) ⟶ H^k_{dR}(X/S)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_sum_deRhamCohomologyCup [Smooth f] [IsProper f] {r : ℕ} (n : Fin r → ℕ)
    (ξ : ∀ i, SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomology (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras (f ≫ g))
      (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras (f ≫ g))) (n i : ℤ))
    (hb : ∀ y : Y, ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin r) (Y.residueField y)
        (DirectSum ℤ fun m : ℤ => ↥(fibreDeRhamModule f y m)),
      ∀ i, b i = DirectSum.lof (Y.residueField y) ℤ (fun m : ℤ => ↥(fibreDeRhamModule f y m))
        (n i : ℤ) (fibreClassOverS f g y (n i : ℤ) (ξ i))) (k : ℤ) :
    Function.Bijective (fun a : ∀ i, SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomology
        (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras g)
        (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras g)) (k - n i) =>
      ∑ i, (eqToHom (congrArg (SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomology
          (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras (f ≫ g))
          (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras (f ≫ g))))
          (add_sub_cancel (n i : ℤ) k))).hom
        (SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomologyCup _ _ (n i) (k - n i) (ξ i)
          (DeRhamKatzOdaCech.deRhamPullbackModule f g (k - n i) (a i))))
declarations.comment: second assertion: under the same hypotheses the map ⊕_i H^*_dR(Y/S) → H^*_dR(X/S), (a_1, ..., a_N) ↦ Σ ξ_i ∪ f^*a_i, is an isomorphism (in every degree k, from ⊕_i H^{k-n_i}_dR(Y/S))

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveBundleDeRham.bijective_sum_cup_projectiveBundle
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FMT], the projective bundle formula for de Rham cohomology.** Let
`g : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, `ℰ` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, locally free of constant
rank `r`, and `p : P = 𝐏(ℰ) ⟶ X` its projective bundle. Then for every `k` the map
`⨁_{i = 0}^{r - 1} H^{k - 2i}_{dR}(X/S) ⟶ H^k_{dR}(P/S)`,
`(a_0, …, a_{r-1}) ↦ ∑_i c₁^{dR}(𝒪_P(1))^i ∪ p^*(a_i)`, is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_sum_cup_projectiveBundle (r : ℕ)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] (k : ℤ) :
    Function.Bijective (fun a : ∀ i : Fin r, SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomology
        (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras g)
        (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras g))
        (k - ((2 * (i : ℕ) : ℕ) : ℤ)) =>
      ∑ i : Fin r, (eqToHom (congrArg (SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomology
          (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras (projectiveBundleToBase X E ≫ g))
          (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential
            (Scheme.Hom.deRhamAlgebras (projectiveBundleToBase X E ≫ g))))
          (add_sub_cancel ((2 * (i : ℕ) : ℕ) : ℤ) k))).hom
        (SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomologyCup _ _ ((2 * (i : ℕ) : ℕ) : ℤ)
          (k - ((2 * (i : ℕ) : ℕ) : ℤ))
          (DeRhamLerayHirsch.classPow (projectiveBundleToBase X E ≫ g) 2
            (DeRhamLerayHirsch.projectiveBundleChernClass g E) i)
          (DeRhamKatzOdaCech.deRhamPullbackModule (projectiveBundleToBase X E) g
            (k - ((2 * (i : ℕ) : ℕ) : ℤ)) (a i))))
declarations.comment: the projective bundle formula: for E locally free of constant rank r on X over S and p : P = P(E) -> X, the map (+)_{i = 0, ..., r - 1} H^*_dR(X/S) -> H^*_dR(P/S), (a_i) |-> sum c_1^dR(O_P(1))^i cup p^*(a_i), is an isomorphism, i.e. bijective in every degree k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.HasLogPolesDeRhamComplex
declarations.doc:
The *de Rham complex of log poles is defined* for an effective Cartier divisor `Y ⊆ X`,
recorded by its ideal sheaf `I`, over a base `S` if for every point `y` of `Y` and every local
equation `t ∈ 𝒪_{X, y}` of `Y` the map `𝒪_{X, y} → Ω_{X/S, y}`, `g ↦ g · dt`, is a split injection
and `Ω^p_{X/S, y}` is `t`-torsion free for all `p`.
declarations.statement: def HasLogPolesDeRhamComplex (f : X ⟶ S) (I : X.IdealSheafData) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.shortExact_logShortComplex_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FMW.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and let `Y ⊆ X` be an
effective Cartier divisor, recorded by its ideal sheaf `I`, with the de Rham complex of log poles
defined for `Y ⊆ X` over `S` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 0FMV]. Then at every point `y` of `Y`
and for every local equation `t` of `Y` at `y` the residue sequence of complexes

`0 → Ω^•_{X/S} → Ω^•_{X/S}(log Y) → Ω^•_{Y/S}[-1] → 0`

of `𝒪_{S, f y}`-modules, built from the germ of `t` over `R = 𝒪_{X, y}`, is short exact. The
three terms are the de Rham complex of `R`, the complex of log poles
`Stacks.LogPoles.logComplex` of the germ of `t`, and the shift of the de Rham complex of
`R ⧸ (germ t)`, which `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.quotientSpanGermEquivStalk` identifies with
`𝒪_{Y, y}`.

The divisor is only locally principal, and the equation `t` is a local one: both conditions the
affine case of Tag 0FMW asks on the ring are supplied at the local ring by Tag 0FMV, so nothing
is assumed about `g ↦ g · dt` on an open of `X`. Local equations exist at every point of an
effective Cartier divisor by `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_germ_span_eq_ker_stalkMap`.

The source states a short exact sequence of complexes of sheaves on `X`; the module docstring
records what would be needed to read this one as its stalkwise verification. Of the two pieces
only the first is genuinely absent: `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.logPolesForms` carries no
differential, so there is no sheaf-level complex. The identification of its stalk with
`Stacks.LogPoles.logFormsX` is unassembled rather than missing — its sheaf-side and ring-side
halves are `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.logPolesFormsStalkEquiv`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.logPolesFormsStalkKerEquiv`,
`Stacks.LogPoles.homIdealEquivLogFormsR` and `Stacks.LogPoles.logFormsXKerEquiv`, and what is
owed is their composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_logShortComplex_stalk (h : f.HasLogPolesDeRhamComplex I) (y : I.subscheme)
    (U : X.Opens) (hy : I.subschemeι y ∈ U) (t : Γ(X, U))
    (ht : RingHom.ker (I.subschemeι.stalkMap y).hom =
      Ideal.span {(X.presheaf.germ U (I.subschemeι y) hy).hom t}) :
    letI : Algebra (ToType (S.presheaf.stalk (f (I.subschemeι y))))
        (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk (I.subschemeι y))) := algebraStalkMap f (I.subschemeι y)
    (Stacks.LogPoles.logShortComplex
        (A := ToType (S.presheaf.stalk (f (I.subschemeι y))))
        (R := ToType (X.presheaf.stalk (I.subschemeι y)))
        (HasLogPolesDeRhamComplex.isSMulRegular_exteriorPower h y U hy t ht)
        (HasLogPolesDeRhamComplex.exists_retraction_D h y U hy t ht)).ShortExact
declarations.comment: for an arbitrary morphism of schemes and an effective Cartier divisor whose log poles complex is defined in the sense of 0FMV, the short exactness of the residue sequence of complexes at each point of the divisor and each local equation there

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.logResidueShortComplex_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FMW.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and `Y ⊆ X` an
effective Cartier divisor, cut out by `I`, for which the de Rham complex of log poles is defined
([Stacks, Tag 0FMV]). Then the sequence of complexes

`0 → Ω^•_{X/S} → Ω^•_{X/S}(log Y) → i_*Ω^•_{Y/S}[-1] → 0`

formed by the inclusion of forms with no pole and the residue is short exact. Here
`Ω^p_{X/S}(log Y)` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.logPolesForms`, its differential is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.logD`, characterised by the Leibniz rule
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.logD_eq`, and the residue is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.logRes`,
`α + dlog t ∧ β ↦ β|_Y` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.logRes_map_eq`).
declarations.statement: theorem logResidueShortComplex_shortExact : (logResidueShortComplex f I hI hlog).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.LogPoles.shortExact_logShortComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FMW**, in its affine local form.  Let `A → R` be a ring map and let
`t ∈ R` cut out the effective Cartier divisor `Y = Spec (R ⧸ (t))` in `X = Spec R`.  Assume the
de Rham complex of log poles is defined for `Y ⊆ X` over `S = Spec A`, that is: `g ↦ g · dt` is a
split injection `R → Ω[R⁄A]` and `Ω^p_{R/A}` is `t`-torsion free for every `p`.  Then there is a
canonical short exact sequence of complexes
`0 → Ω^•_{X/S} → Ω^•_{X/S}(log Y) → Ω^•_{Y/S}[-1] → 0`,
given by the inclusion of the forms with no pole and by the residue.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_logShortComplex {t : R}
    (ht : ∀ p : ℕ, IsSMulRegular (↥(⋀[R]^p (Ω[R⁄A]))) t)
    (hsplit : ∃ r : Ω[R⁄A] →ₗ[R] R,
      r ∘ₗ LinearMap.toSpanSingleton R Ω[R⁄A] (KaehlerDifferential.D A R t) = LinearMap.id) :
    (logShortComplex ht hsplit).ShortExact
declarations.comment: the affine local case: the residue short exact sequence of complexes for a principal effective Cartier divisor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.deRhamCohomologyCup_firstChernClass_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FMX.** Let `p : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and let `Y ⊆ X` be an
effective Cartier divisor for which the de Rham complex of log poles is defined over `S`. If a
class `b ∈ H^m_{dR}(X/S)` restricts to zero on `Y`, then

`c₁^{dR}(𝒪_X(Y)) ∪ b = 0`

in `H^{2 + m}_{dR}(X/S)`. The restriction of `b` is its image under the pullback map
`H^m_{dR}(X/S) ⟶ H^m_{dR}(Y/S)` of the closed immersion `Y ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamCohomologyCup_firstChernClass_eq_zero (hlog : p.HasLogPolesDeRhamComplex Y)
    (m : ℤ)
    (b : SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomology (deRhamAlgebras p)
      (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (deRhamAlgebras p)) m)
    (hb : (deRhamCohomologyPullback Y.subschemeι p (Y.subschemeι ≫ p) (𝟙 S)
      (Category.comp_id _).symm m).hom
        ((SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomologyAbelianIsoDeRhamCohomology (deRhamAlgebras p)
          (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (deRhamAlgebras p)) m).inv.hom b) = 0) :
    SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomologyCup (deRhamAlgebras p)
        (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (deRhamAlgebras p)) 2 m
        (SheafOfModules.deRhamCohomologyFirstChernClass (X := X.toRingedSpace) (deRhamAlgebras p)
          (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (deRhamAlgebras p))
          (Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' Y) inferInstance) b = 0
declarations.comment: b|_Y is the pullback along the closed immersion Y ⟶ X; 𝒪_X(Y) is the dual of ℐ_Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.hasLogPolesDeRhamComplex_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FMY.** Let `X ⟶ T ⟶ S` be morphisms of schemes and let `Y ⊆ X` be an
effective Cartier divisor, recorded by its ideal sheaf `I`.  If both `X ⟶ T` and `Y ⟶ T` are
smooth, then the de Rham complex of log poles is defined for `Y ⊆ X` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLogPolesDeRhamComplex_of_smooth {X T S : Scheme.{u}} (h : X ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ S)
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I)
    [Smooth h] [Smooth (I.subschemeι ≫ h)] :
    (h ≫ g).HasLogPolesDeRhamComplex I

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.nonempty_sheafPushforwardContinuousCompCocontinuousIso_and_leftAdjointCompPullbackIso_of_final
declarations.doc:
Let `(C', J')`, `(C, J)`, `(D', K')`, `(D, K)` be sites and consider a square
of functors
```
  C' --v'--> C
  |          |
  u'         u
  v          v
  D' --v---> D
```
with `u' ⋙ v = v' ⋙ u`, where `u` and `u'` are cocontinuous — giving rise to morphisms of topoi `f`
and `f'` with `f_* = {}_su`, `f'_* = {}_su'` (Stacks 00XO) — and `v` and `v'` are continuous, so
that `g⁻¹ = v^p` and `(g')⁻¹ = (v')^p` are restriction (Stacks 00XR). Assume that for every object
`V'` of `D'` the comparison functor
```
  {}^{u'}_{V'} I ⥤ {}^u_{v(V')} I,   (U', ψ) ↦ (v'(U'), v(ψ) : u(v'(U')) = v(u'(U')) ⟶ v(V')),
```
on the categories of Section 00XF is cofinal, i.e. final. Then `f'_* ∘ (g')⁻¹ ≅ g⁻¹ ∘ f_*`, and
moreover `g'_! ∘ (f')⁻¹ ≅ f⁻¹ ∘ g_!` whenever the two restrictions have left adjoints `g_!`, `g'_!`
and the two pushforwards have left adjoints `f⁻¹`, `(f')⁻¹`. This holds for sheaves with values
in an arbitrary category `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
  nonempty_sheafPushforwardContinuousCompCocontinuousIso_and_leftAdjointCompPullbackIso_of_final
    {C' : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C'] {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} C] {D' : Type u₃}
    [Category.{v₃} D'] {D : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} D] (A : Type u₅) [Category.{v₅} A]
    (J' : GrothendieckTopology C') (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K' : GrothendieckTopology D')
    (K : GrothendieckTopology D) (u' : C' ⥤ D') (u : C ⥤ D) (v' : C' ⥤ C) (v : D' ⥤ D)
    [u.IsCocontinuous J K] [u'.IsCocontinuous J' K'] [v.IsContinuous K' K] [v'.IsContinuous J' J]
    [∀ F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A, u.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F]
    [∀ F : C'ᵒᵖ ⥤ A, u'.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F] (hsq : u' ⋙ v = v' ⋙ u)
    (hfinal :
      ∀ V' : D',
        (CostructuredArrow.map₂ (S := u') (T := V') (U := u) (V := v.obj V') (F := v') (G := v)
            (eqToHom hsq.symm) (𝟙 (v.obj V'))).Final) :
    Nonempty
        (v'.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J' J ⋙ u'.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous A J' K' ≅
          u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous A J K ⋙ v.sheafPushforwardContinuous A K' K) ∧
      ∀ [(u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous A J K).IsRightAdjoint]
        [(u'.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous A J' K').IsRightAdjoint]
        [(v'.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J' J).IsRightAdjoint]
        [(v.sheafPushforwardContinuous A K' K).IsRightAdjoint],
        Nonempty
          ((u'.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous A J' K').leftAdjoint ⋙ v'.sheafPullback A J' J ≅
            v.sheafPullback A K' K ⋙ (u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous A J K).leftAdjoint)
declarations.comment:
Beck–Chevalley for a commutative square of sites whose vertical functors are
  cocontinuous and whose horizontal functors are continuous: if the comparison functors
  `{}^{u'}_{V'} I ⥤ {}^u_{v(V')} I` are all cofinal then `f'_* (g')⁻¹ = g⁻¹ f_*`, and
  `g'_! (f')⁻¹ = f⁻¹ g_!` whenever the relevant left adjoints exist — a hypothesis of the second
  conjunct only, the first equality being the cofinality content and using no adjoint. For
  coefficients in an arbitrary category, the source's sheaves of sets being the case `A = Type u`;
  cocontinuity of the horizontal functors is not needed once their inverse images are read as
  restriction (Stacks 00XR).

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous_comp_eq_and_nonempty_sheafPullbackCompIso
declarations.doc:
Let `(C', J')`, `(C, J)`, `(D', K')`, `(D, K)` be sites and consider a square
of functors
```
  C' --v'--> C
  ↑          ↑
  u'         u
  D' --v---> D
```
with `v ⋙ u = u' ⋙ v'`, where `u` and `u'` are continuous — giving rise to morphisms of sites `f`
and `f'` with `f_* = u^s`, `f'_* = (u')^s` and `f⁻¹ = u_s`, `(f')⁻¹ = (u')_s` (Stacks 00X0) — and
`v` and `v'` are continuous, so that `g⁻¹ = v^p` and `(g')⁻¹ = (v')^p` are restriction and `g_!`,
`g'_!` are their left adjoints (Stacks 00XR, for `v`, `v'` also cocontinuous). Then
`f'_* ∘ (g')⁻¹ = g⁻¹ ∘ f_*` and `g'_! ∘ (f')⁻¹ ≅ f⁻¹ ∘ g_!`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem sheafPushforwardContinuous_comp_eq_and_nonempty_sheafPullbackCompIso {C' : Type u₁}
    [Category.{v₁} C'] {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} C] {D' : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} D']
    {D : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} D] (A : Type u₅) [Category.{v₅} A] (J' : GrothendieckTopology C')
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K' : GrothendieckTopology D') (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    (u : D ⥤ C) (u' : D' ⥤ C') (v : D' ⥤ D) (v' : C' ⥤ C) [u.IsContinuous K J]
    [u'.IsContinuous K' J'] [v.IsContinuous K' K] [v'.IsContinuous J' J]
    [(u.sheafPushforwardContinuous A K J).IsRightAdjoint]
    [(u'.sheafPushforwardContinuous A K' J').IsRightAdjoint]
    [(v.sheafPushforwardContinuous A K' K).IsRightAdjoint]
    [(v'.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J' J).IsRightAdjoint] (hsq : v ⋙ u = u' ⋙ v') :
    v'.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J' J ⋙ u'.sheafPushforwardContinuous A K' J' =
        u.sheafPushforwardContinuous A K J ⋙ v.sheafPushforwardContinuous A K' K ∧
      Nonempty
        (u'.sheafPullback A K' J' ⋙ v'.sheafPullback A J' J ≅
          v.sheafPullback A K' K ⋙ u.sheafPullback A K J)
declarations.comment:
Exchange for a commutative square of sites whose horizontal functors `u`, `u'` are
  continuous and whose vertical functors `v`, `v'` are continuous (in the source, continuous and
  cocontinuous): `f'_* (g')⁻¹ = g⁻¹ f_*` on the nose, and `g'_! (f')⁻¹ ≅ f⁻¹ g_!`. For coefficients
  in an arbitrary category; cocontinuity of `v`, `v'` is not needed once their inverse images are
  read as restriction (Stacks 00XR).

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageCompCocontinuousPushforwardOfIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FN3**, first conclusion, for the canonical direct images. For a commutative square
of ringed topoi as in the module docstring — all four functors cocontinuous giving `f`, `f'`,
`g`, `g'`, the functors `v`, `v'` continuous as well as cocontinuous, `u' ⋙ v = v' ⋙ u`, the
comparison functors `{}^{u'}_{V'} I ⥤ {}^u_{v(V')} I` all cofinal, and `g^{-1} O_D = O_{D'}`,
`(g')^{-1} O_C = O_{C'}` — we have `f'_* ∘ (g')^* ≅ g^* ∘ f_*` on sheaves of modules.

The direct images of sheaves of modules are the canonical ones: `f_*` is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.pushforwardCocontinuous` for the given structure map
`f^♯ : O_D ⟶ {}_su O_C`, and `f'_*` is the same construction for the structure map
`(f')^♯ : O_{D'} ⟶ {}_su' O_{C'}` that `f^♯` induces by restriction along `v` and base change.
For these the linearity hypothesis of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonempty_inverseImage_comp_cocontinuousPushforward_iso` is a theorem,
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.ranSMul_squareComparison`, so no hypothesis beyond the square, the
cofinality and the structure map remains, and the isomorphism itself is available: it is the
inverse of `Stacks.SheafOfModules.squareComparison`.
declarations.statement:
def inverseImageCompCocontinuousPushforwardOfIso
    (fSharp : OD ⟶ (u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous RingCat.{r} J K).obj OC)
    (hsq : u' ⋙ v = v' ⋙ u)
    (hfinal : ∀ V' : D',
      (CostructuredArrow.map₂ (S := u') (T := V') (U := u) (V := v.obj V') (F := v') (G := v)
        (eqToHom hsq.symm) (𝟙 (v.obj V'))).Final) :
    inverseImage.{v} J' J v' OC ⋙
        (CocontinuousPushforward.of.{v} J' K' u'
          (structureMapSquare (J' := J') (K' := K') fSharp hsq)).functor ≅
      (CocontinuousPushforward.of.{v} J K u fSharp).functor ⋙ inverseImage.{v} K' K v OD
declarations.comment:
first conclusion: `f'_* ∘ (g')^* ≅ g^* ∘ f_*` on sheaves of modules, for a
  commutative square of ringed topoi whose four functors `u`, `u'`, `v`, `v'` are cocontinuous,
  with `v`, `v'` continuous as well, with the comparison functors of the index categories of
  Section 00XF cofinal, and with `g^{-1} O_D = O_{D'}`, `(g')^{-1} O_C = O_{C'}`. An isomorphism
  rather than an equality, the sheaf-level comparison of Stacks 0FN1 being a base change of
  right Kan extensions. The direct images of sheaves of modules along the cocontinuous `u` and
  `u'` are the canonical ones attached to the structure map `f^♯ : O_D → {}_su O_C` of the
  morphism of ringed topoi, whose underlying sheaves of abelian groups are `{}_su`, `{}_su'`.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriekCompLeftAdjointOfIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FN3**, second conclusion, for the canonical direct images. In the situation of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageCompCocontinuousPushforwardOfIso` we have
`g'_! ∘ (f')^{-1} ≅ f^{-1} ∘ g_!`. The composite
`g'_! ∘ (f')^{-1}` is left adjoint to `f'_* ∘ (g')^*` and `f^{-1} ∘ g_!` is left adjoint to
`g^* ∘ f_*`; by the first conclusion those two right adjoints are isomorphic, so uniqueness of
left adjoints identifies the two composites. The left adjoints `g_!` and `g'_!` of `g^*` and
`(g')^*` are the concrete lower shriek of Stacks 0797, and the inverse images `f^{-1}` and
`(f')^{-1}` of the two canonical direct images along the cocontinuous `u` and `u'` — which is
condition (1) — are `Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageCocontinuous`, constructed by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageCocontinuousAdjunction`. All four exist by the `UnivLE`,
`HasWeakSheafify` and `WEqualsLocallyBijective` hypotheses of this section.
declarations.statement:
def lowerShriekCompLeftAdjointOfIso
    (fSharp : OD ⟶ (u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous RingCat.{r} J K).obj OC)
    (hsq : u' ⋙ v = v' ⋙ u)
    (hfinal : ∀ V' : D',
      (CostructuredArrow.map₂ (S := u') (T := V') (U := u) (V := v.obj V') (F := v') (G := v)
        (eqToHom hsq.symm) (𝟙 (v.obj V'))).Final) :
    (CocontinuousPushforward.of.{v} J' K' u'
          (structureMapSquare (J' := J') (K' := K') fSharp hsq)).functor.leftAdjoint ⋙
        lowerShriek.{v} J' J v' OC ≅
      lowerShriek.{v} K' K v OD ⋙
        (CocontinuousPushforward.of.{v} J K u fSharp).functor.leftAdjoint
declarations.comment:
second conclusion: `g'_! ∘ (f')⁻¹ ≅ f⁻¹ ∘ g_!` on sheaves of modules, for a
  commutative square of ringed topoi whose four functors `u`, `u'`, `v`, `v'` are cocontinuous,
  with `v`, `v'` continuous as well, with the comparison functors of the index categories of
  Section 00XF cofinal, and with `g^{-1} O_D = O_{D'}`, `(g')^{-1} O_C = O_{C'}`. Deduced from
  the first conclusion by uniqueness of left adjoints, so an isomorphism and not an equality.
  `g_!` and `g'_!` are the lower shriek of Stacks 0797, and `f^{-1}`, `(f')^{-1}` the inverse
  image `f^* G = O_C ⊗_{f^{-1}O_D} f^{-1}G` of
  `Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageCocontinuous`: all four are constructed, none assumed, so
  the source's condition (1) — a cocontinuous functor giving rise to a morphism of ringed topoi
  — is a theorem here. The direct images along `u` and `u'` are the canonical ones attached to
  the structure map `f^♯ : O_D → {}_su O_C`.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImage_comp_pushforward_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FN4**, first conclusion. For a commutative square of ringed topoi as in the module
docstring — `u`, `u'` continuous giving `f`, `f'`, the functors `v`, `v'` continuous as well as
cocontinuous giving `g`, `g'`, `v ⋙ u = u' ⋙ v'`, and `g^{-1} O_D = O_{D'}`,
`(g')^{-1} O_C = O_{C'}` — we have `f'_* ∘ (g')^* = g^* ∘ f_*` on sheaves of modules. Both sides
are restriction along one of the two sides of the square together with restriction of scalars
along the corresponding composite structure map, and the square says those agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem inverseImage_comp_pushforward_eq (hsq : v ⋙ u = u' ⋙ v')
    (hcomm : f'Sharp = restrictStructureMap J' J K' K u u' v v' OC OD fSharp hsq) :
    inverseImage.{v} J' J v' OC ⋙ _root_.SheafOfModules.pushforward.{v} f'Sharp =
      _root_.SheafOfModules.pushforward.{v} fSharp ⋙ inverseImage.{v} K' K v OD
declarations.comment:
first conclusion: `f'_* ∘ (g')^* = g^* ∘ f_*` on sheaves of modules, for a
  commutative square of ringed topoi whose horizontal functors `u`, `u'` are continuous and whose
  vertical functors `v`, `v'` are continuous as well as cocontinuous, with
  `g^{-1} O_D = O_{D'}` and `(g')^{-1} O_C = O_{C'}`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.pullbackCompLowerShriekIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FN4**, second conclusion. In the situation of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImage_comp_pushforward_eq` we have
`g'_! ∘ (f')^{-1} ≅ f^{-1} ∘ g_!`, where `g_!` and `g'_!` are the lower shriek
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriek` of Stacks 0797 and `f^{-1}`, `(f')^{-1}` are the pullbacks
`SheafOfModules.pullback` of Stacks 03D7. The composite `g'_! ∘ (f')^{-1}` is left adjoint to
`f'_* ∘ (g')^*` and `f^{-1} ∘ g_!` is left adjoint to `g^* ∘ f_*`; by the first conclusion those
two right adjoints are the same functor, so uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the two
composites.

Nothing beyond the square is assumed: the four adjunctions are
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriekAdjunction` of Stacks 0797 and
`SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction` of Stacks 03D7, which the `UnivLE`,
`HasWeakSheafify` and `WEqualsLocallyBijective` hypotheses of this section make available.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackCompLowerShriekIso (hsq : v ⋙ u = u' ⋙ v')
    (hcomm : f'Sharp = restrictStructureMap J' J K' K u u' v v' OC OD fSharp hsq) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.pullback.{v} f'Sharp ⋙ lowerShriek.{v} J' J v' OC ≅
      lowerShriek.{v} K' K v OD ⋙ _root_.SheafOfModules.pullback.{v} fSharp
declarations.comment:
second conclusion: `g'_! ∘ (f')⁻¹ ≅ f⁻¹ ∘ g_!` on sheaves of modules, for a
  commutative square of ringed topoi whose horizontal functors `u`, `u'` are continuous and whose
  vertical functors `v`, `v'` are continuous as well as cocontinuous, with
  `g^{-1} O_D = O_{D'}` and `(g')^{-1} O_C = O_{C'}`; a canonical isomorphism rather than an
  equality, uniqueness of left adjoints giving no more. `g_!` and `g'_!` are the lower shriek of
  Stacks 0797 and `f⁻¹`, `(f')⁻¹` the pullback of Stacks 03D7; the existence of all four is
  proved, not assumed.

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.derivedModulesPushforwardBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FN5.** For a cartesian square
```
  X' --a--> X
  |b        |c
  V         V
  Y' --d--> Y
```
of a ringed site `(C, O)`, the inverse image of sheaves of modules along the relocalization at `d`
after the derived direct image along the relocalization at `c` is naturally isomorphic to the
derived direct image along the relocalization at `b` after the inverse image along the
relocalization at `a`.

All four derived functors are arbitrary choices with their canonical transformations from the
corresponding functors on homotopy categories.
declarations.statement:
def derivedModulesPushforwardBaseChangeIso
    (a : X' ⟶ X) (b : X' ⟶ Y') (c : X ⟶ Y) (d : Y' ⟶ Y) (hsq : IsPullback a b c d)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over X))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over Y))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wU} (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over X'))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wV} (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over Y'))]
    (Rc : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over Y)))
    (Rb : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over X')) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over Y')))
    (Ra : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over X')))
    (Rd : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over Y)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over Y')))
    (αc : homotopyToDerived (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Relocalization.pushforward J O c) ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rc)
    (αb : homotopyToDerived (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Relocalization.pushforward J O b) ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rb)
    (αa : homotopyToDerived (_root_.SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} O a) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Ra)
    (αd : homotopyToDerived (_root_.SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} O d) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rd)
    [Rc.IsRightDerivedFunctor αc
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over X)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Rb.IsRightDerivedFunctor αb
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over X')) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Ra.IsRightDerivedFunctor αa
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over X)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Rd.IsRightDerivedFunctor αd
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (O.over Y)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    Rc ⋙ Rd ≅ Ra ⋙ Rb

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.nonempty_inverseImage_comp_totalDerivedPushforwardOf_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FN6.** For a commutative square of ringed topoi whose four functors `u : C ⥤ D`,
`u' : C' ⥤ D'`, `v : D' ⥤ D`, `v' : C' ⥤ C` are cocontinuous — giving `f`, `f'`, `g`, `g'` with
`f_* = {}_su`, `f'_* = {}_su'` — with `u' ⋙ v = v' ⋙ u`, with `v` and `v'` continuous as well as
cocontinuous so that `g^{-1}`, `(g')^{-1}` are restriction, with the comparison functors
`{}^{u'}_{V'} I ⥤ {}^u_{v(V')} I` of the index categories of Section 00XF all cofinal, with
`g^{-1} O_D = O_{D'}` and `(g')^{-1} O_C = O_{C'}`, and with `g'_! : Ab(C') ⥤ Ab(C)` exact, we
have `Rf'_* ∘ (g')^* = g^* ∘ Rf_*` as functors `D(O_C) ⥤ D(O_{D'})`.

Condition (5) is built into the statement by taking the restrictions along `v` and `v'` as *the*
sheaves of rings on `D'` and `C'`, so that `g^* = g^{-1}` and `(g')^* = (g')^{-1}` are
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImage` and are exact; `(f')^♯` is the structure map the square
forces, as in Stacks 0FN3. Condition (6) is the hypothesis
`PreservesFiniteLimits (v'.sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat J' J)`: `v'.sheafPullback` is the left
adjoint `g'_! = (v')_s` of the inverse image `(g')^{-1} = (v')^p` of abelian sheaves, which
Stacks 00XR produces for a continuous and cocontinuous `v'`, and right exactness of a left
adjoint is automatic, so left exactness is the whole of the condition.

Both `Rf_*` and `Rf'_*` are the total right derived functors of the degreewise direct images of
sheaves of modules; nothing about them is assumed. The source's proof is followed exactly: the
underived identity is Stacks 0FN3, which is what the cofinality hypothesis `hfinal` — condition
(4) — feeds; condition (6) and Stacks 08BJ make `(g')^{-1}` preserve K-injectivity *of abelian
sheaves*, Stacks 0FN1 gives the underived identity there, and Stacks 0D6J carries the resulting
statement — that the inverse image of a K-injective complex of `O_C`-modules computes `Rf'_*` —
back to modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_inverseImage_comp_totalDerivedPushforwardOf_iso
    [PreservesFiniteLimits (v'.sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat.{u} J' J)]
    (fSharp : OD ⟶ (u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj OC)
    (hsq : u' ⋙ v = v' ⋙ u)
    (hcomm : f'Sharp = structureMapSquare (J' := J') (K' := K') fSharp hsq)
    (hfinal : ∀ V' : D',
      (CostructuredArrow.map₂ (S := u') (T := V') (U := u) (V := v.obj V') (F := v') (G := v)
        (eqToHom hsq.symm) (𝟙 (v.obj V'))).Final) :
    Nonempty ((inverseImage.{u} J' J v' OC).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        UnboundedComplexes.totalRightDerivedOfAdditive
          (pushforwardCocontinuous.{u} u' f'Sharp) ≅
      UnboundedComplexes.totalRightDerivedOfAdditive (pushforwardCocontinuous.{u} u fSharp) ⋙
        (inverseImage.{u} K' K v OD).mapDerivedCategory)
declarations.comment:
`Rf'_* ∘ (g')^* ≅ g^* ∘ Rf_*` on the unbounded derived categories
  `D(O_C) → D(O_{D'})`, for a commutative square of ringed topoi whose four functors `u`, `u'`,
  `v`, `v'` are cocontinuous, with `u' ⋙ v = v' ⋙ u`, with `v`, `v'` continuous as well, with
  the comparison functors `{}^{u'}_{V'} I → {}^u_{v(V')} I` of the index categories of Section
  00XF cofinal, with `g^{-1} O_D = O_{D'}` and `(g')^{-1} O_C = O_{C'}`, and with the tag's
  condition (6) in the source's own form: exactness of `g'_! : Ab(C') → Ab(C)`, written
  `PreservesFiniteLimits (v'.sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat J' J)`, right exactness of a left
  adjoint being automatic. `Rf_*` and `Rf'_*` are *constructed*, as the total right derived
  functors of the degreewise direct images of sheaves of modules, and nothing about them is
  required. The price of the source's condition (6) is that the four sites lie in one universe,
  which is where Stacks 0D6J, the transport from abelian sheaves to modules that the source's
  proof opens with, is available. An isomorphism rather than an equality, and asserted through
  `Nonempty` as its underived input Stacks 0FN3 is, a right derived functor being determined only
  up to a canonical isomorphism and the sheaf-level comparison of Stacks 0FN1 being a base change
  of right Kan extensions.

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.inverseImageCompDerivedPushforwardPlusIsoOfRingedSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FN7, first conclusion, with the acyclicity step discharged.** The same statement
as `inverseImageCompDerivedPushforwardPlusIso`, in the universes at which Stacks 0D6X and
Stacks 072W are available: `C'` is a small site and `C` is the site of a ringed site `Y` whose
structure sheaf, module sections and `Ext`-groups lie in the universe of its objects, while `D`
and `D'` keep arbitrary universes.

The source's condition (6) is not a hypothesis, and neither is the acyclicity it would be used
for: it is proved here from Stacks 0D6X and Stacks 072W by
`rightAcyclic_pushforward_inverseImage_of_injective`.
declarations.statement:
def inverseImageCompDerivedPushforwardPlusIsoOfRingedSite (hsq : v ⋙ u = u' ⋙ v')
    (hcomm : f'Sharp =
      restrictStructureMap J' Y.J K' K u u' v v' (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O) OD
        fSharp hsq) :
    (inverseImage.{w} J' Y.J v'
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)).mapDerivedCategoryPlus ⋙
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.pushforward.{w} f'Sharp).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ≅
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.pushforward.{w} fSharp).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        (inverseImage.{w} K' K v OD).mapDerivedCategoryPlus
declarations.comment:
first conclusion: `Rf'_* ∘ (g')^* ≅ g^* ∘ Rf_*` on the *bounded below* derived
  categories `D⁺(O_C) → D⁺(O_{D'})`, for a commutative square of ringed topoi whose horizontal
  functors `u`, `u'` are continuous and whose vertical functors `v`, `v'` are continuous as well
  as cocontinuous, with `v ⋙ u = u' ⋙ v'`, `g^{-1} O_D = O_{D'}` and `(g')^{-1} O_C = O_{C'}`,
  and WITHOUT the tag's condition (6), exactness of `g'_!` — which is what the second
  conclusion, on the unbounded derived categories, needs; that conclusion, under the source's
  own condition (6), is
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.inverseImageCompTotalDerivedPushforwardIsoOfExactLowerShriek`.
  Proved as in the source, through the vanishing of Stacks 0D6X, the sheafified cohomology
  presheaf of Stacks 072W, and Leray's acyclicity lemma Stacks 015E. An isomorphism rather than an
  equality, a right derived functor being determined only up to a canonical isomorphism. The sites
  `C` and `C'` are at the single universe at which Stacks 0D6X and the Ext-to-derived-sections
  comparison of Stacks 03FD are available in this library — `C'` small and `C` the site of a ringed
  site — and `v'` is continuous in the sense of Sites, Definition 00WV, which is the hypothesis
  Stacks 0D6X uses and which Mathlib's `IsContinuous` does not supply; that is not an extra
  assumption relative to the source, where `v'` is continuous in exactly that sense, and
  `Stacks.Sites.preservesCoveringPullbacks_of_isContinuous` derives it from the project's
  formalization of Definition 00WV.

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.inverseImageCompTotalDerivedPushforwardIsoOfExactLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FN7**, second conclusion, under the source's own condition (6). For a commutative
square of ringed topoi whose horizontal functors `u : D ⥤ C`, `u' : D' ⥤ C'` are continuous —
giving `f`, `f'` with `f_* = u^s`, `f'_* = (u')^s` — whose vertical functors `v : D' ⥤ D`,
`v' : C' ⥤ C` are continuous as well as cocontinuous — giving `g`, `g'` with `g^{-1}`,
`(g')^{-1}` restriction — with `v ⋙ u = u' ⋙ v'`, with `g^{-1} O_D = O_{D'}` and
`(g')^{-1} O_C = O_{C'}`, and with `g'_! : Ab(C') ⥤ Ab(C)` exact, we have
`Rf'_* ∘ (g')^* = g^* ∘ Rf_*` as functors `D(O_C) ⥤ D(O_{D'})`.

Condition (6) is the hypothesis `PreservesFiniteLimits (v'.sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat J' J)`:
`v'.sheafPullback` is the left adjoint `g'_! = (v')_s` of the inverse image `(g')^{-1} = (v')^p`
of abelian sheaves, which Stacks 00XR produces for a continuous and cocontinuous `v'`, and
right exactness of a left adjoint is automatic, so left exactness is the whole of the condition.

Both `Rf_*` and `Rf'_*` are the total right derived functors of the degreewise direct images;
nothing about them is assumed. The source's proof is followed exactly: condition (6) and
Stacks 08BJ make `(g')^{-1}` preserve K-injectivity *of abelian sheaves*, Stacks 0FN2 gives the
underived identity there, and Stacks 0D6J carries the resulting statement — that the inverse
image of a K-injective complex of `O_C`-modules computes `Rf'_*` — back to modules.
declarations.statement:
def inverseImageCompTotalDerivedPushforwardIsoOfExactLowerShriek
    [PreservesFiniteLimits (v'.sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat.{u} J' J)]
    (fSharp : OD ⟶ (u.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} K J).obj OC)
    (hsq : v ⋙ u = u' ⋙ v')
    (hcomm : f'Sharp = restrictStructureMap J' J K' K u u' v v' OC OD fSharp hsq) :
    (inverseImage.{u} J' J v' OC).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        UnboundedComplexes.totalRightDerivedOfAdditive
          (_root_.SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u} f'Sharp) ≅
      UnboundedComplexes.totalRightDerivedOfAdditive
          (_root_.SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u} fSharp) ⋙
        (inverseImage.{u} K' K v OD).mapDerivedCategory
declarations.comment:
the second conclusion, at the source's full statement of it:
  `Rf'_* ∘ (g')^* ≅ g^* ∘ Rf_*` on the *unbounded* derived categories `D(O_C) → D(O_{D'})`, for
  a commutative square of ringed topoi whose horizontal functors `u`, `u'` are continuous and
  whose vertical functors `v`, `v'` are continuous as well as cocontinuous, with
  `v ⋙ u = u' ⋙ v'`, `g^{-1} O_D = O_{D'}` and `(g')^{-1} O_C = O_{C'}`, and with the tag's
  condition (6) as the source states it — exactness of `g'_! : Ab(C') → Ab(C)`, written
  `PreservesFiniteLimits (v'.sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat J' J)`, right exactness of a left
  adjoint being automatic. Nothing else is assumed: in particular NOT the module-level
  substitution for condition (6) that
  `Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.inverseImageCompDerivedPushforwardIso` and
  `Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.inverseImageCompTotalDerivedPushforwardIso` grant in its
  place, those two adding four independent universes instead. The price here is that the four
  sites lie in one universe, which is where Stacks 0D6J, the transport from abelian sheaves to
  modules that the source's proof opens with, is available. `Rf_*` and `Rf'_*` are
  *constructed*, as the total right derived functors of the degreewise direct images, and
  nothing about them is assumed. An isomorphism rather than an equality, a right derived functor
  being determined only up to a canonical isomorphism. The first conclusion of the tag, the same
  identity on `D^+` without condition (6), is
  `Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.inverseImageCompDerivedPushforwardPlusIsoOfRingedSite`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.existsUnique_homEquiv_of_isRightDerivedValueAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FND**: deriving adjoints. Let `F : 𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟'` be right adjoint to `G : 𝒟' ⥤ 𝒟`, let
`S`, `S'` be classes of morphisms of `𝒟`, `𝒟'` admitting left, resp. right fractions, and let
`Q : 𝒟 ⥤ S⁻¹𝒟` and `Q' : 𝒟' ⥤ (S')⁻¹𝒟'` be localization functors. Let `K` be an object of `𝒟`
at which the right derived functor `RF` of `Q' ∘ F` is defined, with value `RF(K) = c.pt`, and
let `M` be an object of `𝒟'` at which the left derived functor `LG` of `Q ∘ G` is defined, with
value `LG(M) = d.pt.unop` (the left derived value is the right derived value of the opposite
functors, as in Stacks 05S9). Then there is a unique bijection
`Hom_{(S')⁻¹𝒟'}(M, RF(K)) ≃ Hom_{S⁻¹𝒟}(LG(M), K)` compatible with the fractions computing the
two sides: for every index `s : K ⟶ I` of the ind-object defining `RF(K)`, every index
`t : P ⟶ M` of the pro-object defining `LG(M)` and every `f : P ⟶ F(I)`, a morphism
`ψ : M ⟶ RF(K)` satisfies `Q'(t) ≫ ψ = Q'(f) ≫ (coprojection at s)` if and only if its image
satisfies `φ(ψ) ≫ Q(s) = (projection at t) ≫ Q(f^♯)`, where `f^♯ : G(P) ⟶ I` is adjoint
to `f`.

The source's further assertion that this bijection is functorial in both variables is proved in
`StacksFrontier.CategoryTheory.Localization.DerivingAdjointsNaturality`, where the bijection is named
`CategoryTheory.Adjunction.derivedHomEquiv`: `derivedHomEquiv_naturality` for morphisms of `𝒟`
and `𝒟'`, and `derivedHomEquiv_comp_eq_comp`, `derivedHomEquiv_comp_eq_comp_left` for morphisms
of `S⁻¹𝒟` and `(S')⁻¹𝒟'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_homEquiv_of_isRightDerivedValueAt
    {D : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} D] {D' : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D']
    {SD : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} SD] {SD' : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} SD']
    {F : D ⥤ D'} {G : D' ⥤ D} (adj : G ⊣ F)
    (S : MorphismProperty D) (S' : MorphismProperty D')
    [S.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions] [S'.HasRightCalculusOfFractions]
    (Q : D ⥤ SD) [Q.IsLocalization S] (Q' : D' ⥤ SD') [Q'.IsLocalization S']
    (K : D) (M : D')
    (c : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget S ⊤ K ⋙ Under.forget K ⋙ F ⋙ Q'))
    (hc : (F ⋙ Q').IsRightDerivedValueAt S K c)
    (d : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget S'.op ⊤ (Opposite.op M) ⋙
      Under.forget (Opposite.op M) ⋙ (G ⋙ Q).op))
    (hd : (G ⋙ Q).op.IsRightDerivedValueAt S'.op (Opposite.op M) d) :
    ∃! φ : (Q'.obj M ⟶ c.pt) ≃ (d.pt.unop ⟶ Q.obj K),
      ∀ (s : S.Under ⊤ K) (t : S'.op.Under ⊤ (Opposite.op M))
        (f : t.right.unop ⟶ F.obj s.right) (ψ : Q'.obj M ⟶ c.pt),
        Q'.map t.hom.unop ≫ ψ = Q'.map f ≫ c.ι.app s ↔
          φ ψ ≫ Q.map s.hom = (d.ι.app t).unop ≫ Q.map ((adj.homEquiv _ _).symm f)
declarations.comment:
the canonical bijection and its characterisation by fractions; its functoriality
in both variables is `derivedHomEquiv_naturality`, `derivedHomEquiv_comp_eq_comp` and
`derivedHomEquiv_comp_eq_comp_left`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.derivedHomEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FND**, functoriality of the canonical bijection in both variables, with respect to
morphisms of `𝒟` and `𝒟'`. Let `κ : K ⟶ K'` be a morphism of `𝒟` with `RF` defined at `K` and
`K'`, and `γ : M' ⟶ M` a morphism of `𝒟'` with `LG` defined at `M'` and `M`, with induced
morphisms `RF(κ) : RF(K) ⟶ RF(K')` and `LG(γ) : LG(M') ⟶ LG(M)` between the values
(Stacks 05SA). Then for every `ψ : M ⟶ RF(K)`,
`φ_{K',M'}(Q'(γ) ≫ ψ ≫ RF(κ)) = LG(γ) ≫ φ_{K,M}(ψ) ≫ Q(κ)`. Morphisms of the localized categories
are `derivedHomEquiv_comp_eq_comp` and `derivedHomEquiv_comp_eq_comp_left`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedHomEquiv_naturality
    (hc : (F ⋙ Q').IsRightDerivedValueAt S K c) (hc' : (F ⋙ Q').IsRightDerivedValueAt S K' c')
    (hd : (G ⋙ Q).op.IsRightDerivedValueAt S'.op (op M) d)
    (hd' : (G ⋙ Q).op.IsRightDerivedValueAt S'.op (op M') d')
    (κ : K ⟶ K') (γ : M' ⟶ M) (ψ : Q'.obj M ⟶ c.pt) :
    adj.derivedHomEquiv hc' hd' (Q'.map γ ≫ ψ ≫ rightDerivedMap S (F ⋙ Q') hc hc' κ) =
      (rightDerivedMap S'.op (G ⋙ Q).op hd hd' γ.op).unop ≫
        adj.derivedHomEquiv hc hd ψ ≫ Q.map κ
declarations.comment: functoriality of the bijection in both variables, for morphisms of `𝒟` and `𝒟'`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.derivedHomEquiv_comp_eq_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FND**, functoriality of the canonical bijection in `K` with respect to a morphism
`g : Q(K) ⟶ Q(K')` of `S⁻¹𝒟`. Such a morphism is a left fraction `g = Q(κ) ≫ Q(σ)⁻¹` with
`κ : K ⟶ L` and `σ : K' ⟶ L` in `S`, that is `g ≫ Q(σ) = Q(κ)`; then `RF` is defined at `L`
(Stacks 05SB) and `RF(g) = RF(κ) ≫ RF(σ)⁻¹` is the morphism `ρ : RF(K) ⟶ RF(K')` with
`ρ ≫ RF(σ) = RF(κ)`. For every `ψ : M ⟶ RF(K)`, `φ_{K',M}(ψ ≫ ρ) = φ_{K,M}(ψ) ≫ g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedHomEquiv_comp_eq_comp
    (hc : (F ⋙ Q').IsRightDerivedValueAt S K c) (hc' : (F ⋙ Q').IsRightDerivedValueAt S K' c')
    (hL : (F ⋙ Q').IsRightDerivedValueAt S L cL)
    (hd : (G ⋙ Q).op.IsRightDerivedValueAt S'.op (op M) d)
    (κ : K ⟶ L) (σ : K' ⟶ L) (hσ : S σ) (g : Q.obj K ⟶ Q.obj K')
    (hg : g ≫ Q.map σ = Q.map κ) (ρ : c.pt ⟶ c'.pt)
    (hρ : ρ ≫ rightDerivedMap S (F ⋙ Q') hc' hL σ = rightDerivedMap S (F ⋙ Q') hc hL κ)
    (ψ : Q'.obj M ⟶ c.pt) :
    adj.derivedHomEquiv hc' hd (ψ ≫ ρ) = adj.derivedHomEquiv hc hd ψ ≫ g
declarations.comment: functoriality of the bijection in `K`, for morphisms of `S⁻¹𝒟`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.derivedHomEquiv_comp_eq_comp_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FND**, functoriality of the canonical bijection in `M` with respect to a morphism
`γ : Q'(M') ⟶ Q'(M)` of `(S')⁻¹𝒟'`. Such a morphism is a right fraction
`γ = Q'(τ)⁻¹ ≫ Q'(ν)` with `τ : N ⟶ M'` in `S'` and `ν : N ⟶ M`, that is `Q'(τ) ≫ γ = Q'(ν)`;
then `LG` is defined at `N` (Stacks 05SB) and `LG(γ) = LG(τ)⁻¹ ≫ LG(ν)` is the morphism
`μ : LG(M') ⟶ LG(M)` with `LG(τ) ≫ μ = LG(ν)`. For every `ψ : M ⟶ RF(K)`,
`φ_{K,M'}(γ ≫ ψ) = μ ≫ φ_{K,M}(ψ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedHomEquiv_comp_eq_comp_left
    (hc : (F ⋙ Q').IsRightDerivedValueAt S K c)
    (hd : (G ⋙ Q).op.IsRightDerivedValueAt S'.op (op M) d)
    (hd' : (G ⋙ Q).op.IsRightDerivedValueAt S'.op (op M') d')
    (hN : (G ⋙ Q).op.IsRightDerivedValueAt S'.op (op N) dN)
    (ν : N ⟶ M) (τ : N ⟶ M') (hτ : S' τ) (γ : Q'.obj M' ⟶ Q'.obj M)
    (hγ : Q'.map τ ≫ γ = Q'.map ν) (μ : d'.pt.unop ⟶ d.pt.unop)
    (hμ : (rightDerivedMap S'.op (G ⋙ Q).op hd' hN τ.op).unop ≫ μ =
      (rightDerivedMap S'.op (G ⋙ Q).op hd hN ν.op).unop)
    (ψ : Q'.obj M ⟶ c.pt) :
    adj.derivedHomEquiv hc hd' (γ ≫ ψ) = μ ≫ adj.derivedHomEquiv hc hd ψ
declarations.comment: functoriality of the bijection in `M`, for morphisms of `(S')⁻¹𝒟'`

declarations.name: CochainComplex.HomComplex.iteratedHomComplex_differential_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNE.** The differential of a degree-`n` cochain in `Hom^•(Hom^•(K, L), M)`,
evaluated on `f ∈ Hom^{-s-1}(K, L)`, is the sum of the target, middle and source differential
terms, with respective signs `1`, `-(-1)^n` and `(-1)^(p+1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem iteratedHomComplex_differential_apply
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (K L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ)
    (n p s : ℤ) (hps : p + s = n)
    (β : Cochain (HomComplexR R K L) M n)
    (f : Cochain K L (-s - 1)) :
    ((δ n (n + 1) β).v (-s - 1) p (by omega)).hom f =
      (M.d (p - 1) p).hom ((β.v (-s - 1) (p - 1) (by omega)).hom f) -
        n.negOnePow •
          ((β.v (-s) p (by omega)).hom
            (f.comp (Cochain.diff L) (by omega))) +
        (p + 1).negOnePow •
          ((β.v (-s) p (by omega)).hom
            ((Cochain.diff K).comp f (by omega)))

declarations.name: CochainComplex.HomComplex.tensorHomComplex_differential_component
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNF.** On the `(p, q, r)`-component of `Tot(Hom^•(L, M) ⊗ K)`, the total
differential is the Hom-complex differential plus `(-1)^(p+q)` times the differential of `K`;
the Hom-complex differential itself is postcomposition by `d_M` minus `(-1)^(p+q)` times
precomposition by `d_L`. Thus the total differential is the three-term expression
`d_M - (-1)^(p+q) d_L + (-1)^(p+q) d_K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorHomComplex_differential_component
    (L M K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (p q r : ℤ) :
    let H := HomComplexR R L M
    let T := HomologicalComplex.tensorObj H K
    ((homComponent R L M p q ▷ K.X r) ≫
          HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj H K (p + q) r (p + q + r) rfl ≫
          T.d (p + q + r) (p + q + r + 1) =
        (postcomposeDifferential R L M p q ▷ K.X r) ≫
            (homComponent R L M (p + 1) q ▷ K.X r) ≫
            HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj H K (p + 1 + q) r
              (p + q + r + 1) (by omega) +
          -(p + q).negOnePow •
            ((precomposeDifferential R L M p q ▷ K.X r) ≫
              (homComponent R L M p (q + 1) ▷ K.X r) ≫
              HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj H K (p + (q + 1)) r
                (p + q + r + 1) (by omega)) +
          (p + q).negOnePow •
            ((homComponent R L M p q ⊗ₘ K.d r (r + 1)) ≫
              HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj H K (p + q) (r + 1)
                (p + q + r + 1) (by omega)))

declarations.name: CochainComplex.HomComplex.tensorShiftIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNH.** The canonical isomorphism from the shift by `a + b` of the tensor product
`M ⊗ N` to the tensor product `M[a] ⊗ N[b]` of the shifts.

It is the inverse of the composite that removes the shift from the first factor, then from the
second factor, and finally recombines the two shifts; see
`CochainComplex.HomComplex.tensorShiftIso_hom_ι_and_naturality` for the homogeneous formula that
pins it down.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorShiftIso (M N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (a b : ℤ) :
    (M ⊗ N)⟦a + b⟧ ≅ M⟦a⟧ ⊗ N⟦b⟧
declarations.comment: canonical isomorphism

declarations.name: CochainComplex.HomComplex.tensorShiftHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNH.** The morphism corresponding to
`CochainComplex.HomComplex.tensorShiftIso`: its source is the unshifted tensor product and its
target is the tensor product of the shifts, shifted back by `-a - b`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorShiftHom (M N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (a b : ℤ) :
    M ⊗ N ⟶ (M⟦a⟧ ⊗ N⟦b⟧)⟦-a - b⟧
declarations.comment: corresponding shifted map

declarations.name: CochainComplex.HomComplex.tensorShiftIso_hom_ι_and_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNH.** On the summand `M^p ⊗ N^q`, the simultaneous-shift isomorphism
`CochainComplex.HomComplex.tensorShiftIso` is multiplication by the Koszul sign `(-1)^(p*b)`
followed by the canonical inclusion of `M[a]^{p-a} ⊗ N[b]^{q-b}` into the shifted total complex.
Since the homogeneous summands generate, this determines the isomorphism. It is moreover natural
in both complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorShiftIso_hom_ι_and_naturality
    (M N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (a b : ℤ) :
    (∀ (p q : ℤ),
      HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj M N p q (p + q) rfl ≫
          (CochainComplex.shiftFunctorObjXIso (M ⊗ N) (a + b)
            (p + q - a - b) (p + q) (by omega)).inv ≫
          (tensorShiftIso M N a b).hom.f (p + q - a - b) =
        ((p * b).negOnePow : ℤˣ) •
          ((CochainComplex.shiftFunctorObjXIso M a (p - a) p (by omega)).inv ⊗ₘ
              (CochainComplex.shiftFunctorObjXIso N b (q - b) q (by omega)).inv) ≫
            HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj (M⟦a⟧) (N⟦b⟧)
              (p - a) (q - b) (p + q - a - b) (by omega)) ∧
      (∀ (M' N' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (f : M ⟶ M') (g : N ⟶ N'),
        (HomologicalComplex.tensorHom f g)⟦a + b⟧' ≫
            (tensorShiftIso M' N' a b).hom =
          (tensorShiftIso M N a b).hom ≫
            HomologicalComplex.tensorHom (f⟦a⟧') (g⟦b⟧'))
declarations.comment: homogeneous sign formula and naturality

declarations.name: TotalTensorComplex.cochainComplex_symmetricMonoidalCategory
declarations.doc:
The category of cochain complexes of modules over a commutative ring, with tensor product
given by the total complex of the degreewise tensor product, is symmetric monoidal. On the
summand of bidegree `(p, q)`, its braiding is the ordinary symmetry of tensor products multiplied
by the Koszul sign `(-1)^(p*q)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cochainComplex_symmetricMonoidalCategory (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    ∃ s : SymmetricCategory (CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ),
      ∀ (K L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (p q n : ℤ) (h : p + q = n),
        HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj K L p q n h ≫
            (s.toBraidedCategory.braiding K L).hom.f n =
          ((p * q).negOnePow : ℤˣ) •
            ((β_ (K.X p) (L.X q)).hom ≫
              HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj L K q p n (by simpa [add_comm] using h))

declarations.name: ModuleCat.LeftDual.finite_projective_and_linearDual_equiv_of_exactPairing
declarations.doc:
If `N` is a left dual of `M` in the monoidal category of `R`-modules, then `M` and `N` are
finite projective. Moreover, contraction with the coevaluation identifies `M⁺` with `N`, and
under this identification the given evaluation map sends `n ⊗ m` to the value at `m` of the
functional corresponding to `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_projective_and_linearDual_equiv_of_exactPairing :
    Module.Finite R M ∧ Module.Projective R M ∧
      Module.Finite R N ∧ Module.Projective R N ∧
        ∃ e : Module.Dual R M ≃ₗ[R] N,
          e.toLinearMap = linearDualToLeftDual R M N ∧
            ∀ (n : N) (m : M),
              (ε_ (ModuleCat.of R M) (ModuleCat.of R N)).hom (n ⊗ₜ[R] m) = e.symm n m

declarations.name: CochainComplex.LeftDual.exactPairing_iff_bounded_finiteProjective
declarations.doc:
A complex of modules and a chosen left dual are bounded complexes of finite projective
modules, and the pairing is the termwise linear-dual pairing with signed transpose differential.
Conversely, every bounded complex of finite projective modules admits exactly this construction
as a left dual.
declarations.statement:
theorem exactPairing_iff_bounded_finiteProjective (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    (∀ (M N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (p : ExactPairing M N),
      (∃ a b : ℤ, M.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧
        (∃ a b : ℤ, N.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ N.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite R (M.X n) ∧ Module.Projective R (M.X n)) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite R (N.X n) ∧ Module.Projective R (N.X n)) ∧
        IsLinearDualPairing R M N p) ∧
      (∀ M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ,
        (∃ a b : ℤ, M.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M.IsStrictlyLE b) →
        (∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite R (M.X n) ∧ Module.Projective R (M.X n)) →
        ∃ (N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (p : ExactPairing M N),
          (∃ a b : ℤ, N.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ N.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧
            IsLinearDualPairing R M N p)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.LeftDual.tensorLeftDualIsoHomComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNL.** For a complex `M` with left dual `N`, the canonical sign-free tensor–Hom
morphism is a natural isomorphism `K ⊗ N ≅ Hom^•(M, K)`. On the summand `K^p ⊗ N^q`, its
component in `Hom(M^{-q}, K^p)` sends `x ⊗ y` to the map `m ↦ ε(y ⊗ m) • x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorLeftDualIsoHomComplex
    (M N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (pairing : ExactPairing M N) :
    letI := pairing
    ∃ e : ∀ K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ,
        K ⊗ N ≅ HomComplexR R M K,
      (∀ (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (n p q : ℤ) (hpq : p + q = n)
          (x : K.X p) (y : N.X q) (m : M.X (-q)),
        (((((e K).hom.f n).hom
            ((ιTensorObj K N p q n hpq).hom (x ⊗ₜ[R] y))) : Cochain M K n).v
              (-q) p (by omega)).hom m =
          ((ιTensorObj N M q (-q) 0 (by omega) ≫ (ε_ M N).f 0 ≫
              (singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 (𝟙_ (ModuleCat R))).hom).hom
            (y ⊗ₜ[R] m)) • x) ∧
        ∀ (K L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (f : K ⟶ L),
          (e K).hom ≫ Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomComparison.HomCxMap M M K L (𝟙 M) f =
            (f ▷ N) ≫ (e L).hom

declarations.name: CochainComplex.HomComplex.evaluationToDoubleHom_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNM.** The canonical evaluation into the double Hom complex sends homogeneous
`x ∈ K^n` and `f ∈ Hom^m(K, M)` to `(-1)^(nm) f(x)`. It is natural in `K` and dinatural in the
coefficient complex `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem evaluationToDoubleHom_apply :
    (∀ (K M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (n m : ℤ)
        (x : K.X n) (f : Cochain K M m),
      ((((evaluationToDoubleHom K M).f n).hom x).v m (m + n) (by omega)).hom f =
        (n * m).negOnePow • (f.v n (m + n) (by omega)).hom x) ∧
    (∀ (K K' M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (g : K ⟶ K'),
      evaluationToDoubleHom K M ≫
          Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R (HomComplexR R K' M) (HomComplexR R K M) M
            (Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R K K' M g) =
        g ≫ evaluationToDoubleHom K' M) ∧
    (∀ (K M M' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (g : M ⟶ M'),
      evaluationToDoubleHom K M ≫
          Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.postcomp R (HomComplexR R K M) M M' g =
        evaluationToDoubleHom K M' ≫
          Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R (HomComplexR R K M) (HomComplexR R K M') M'
            (Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.postcomp R K M M' g))

declarations.name: CochainComplex.HomComplex.homComplexShiftIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNN.** The canonical identification
`Hom^•(M, K)[a - b] ≅ Hom^•(M[b], K[a])`.

After shifting the identification back to a map `Hom^•(M, K) ⟶ Hom^•(M[b], K[a])[b - a]`, its
degree-`n` component is the sign `(-1)^(n b)` times the evident reindexing. The final conjunct is
the homogeneous differential calculation: before inserting this degree-dependent sign, the
target differential is `(-1)^b` times the reindexed source differential.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homComplexShiftIso (R : Type*) [CommRing R]
    (M K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (a b : ℤ) :
    { e : (CochainComplex.HomComplexR R M K)⟦a - b⟧ ≅
        CochainComplex.HomComplexR R (M⟦b⟧) (K⟦a⟧) //
      let H := CochainComplex.HomComplexR R M K
      let T := CochainComplex.HomComplexR R (M⟦b⟧) (K⟦a⟧)
      let reindex : ∀ n : ℤ, Cochain M K n → Cochain (M⟦b⟧) (K⟦a⟧) (n + (b - a)) :=
        fun n z ↦ Cochain.mk fun p q _ ↦
          (M.shiftFunctorObjXIso b p (p + b) rfl).hom ≫
            z.v (p + b) (q + a) (by omega) ≫
            (K.shiftFunctorObjXIso a q (q + a) rfl).inv
      let g : H ⟶ T⟦b - a⟧ :=
        (shiftFunctorCompIsoId _ (a - b) (b - a) (by omega)).inv.app H ≫ e.hom⟦b - a⟧'
      (∀ (n : ℤ) (z : Cochain M K n),
        (T.shiftFunctorObjXIso (b - a) n (n + (b - a)) rfl).hom.hom ((g.f n).hom z) =
          (n * b).negOnePow • reindex n z) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℤ) (z : Cochain M K n),
        (T.shiftFunctorObjXIso (b - a) (n + 1) (n + 1 + (b - a)) rfl).hom.hom
            (((T⟦b - a⟧).d n (n + 1)).hom
              ((T.shiftFunctorObjXIso (b - a) n (n + (b - a)) rfl).inv.hom
                (reindex n z))) =
          b.negOnePow • reindex (n + 1) (δ n (n + 1) z)) }

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.Invertible.derivedCategory_symmetricMonoidalCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNQ.** The derived category of modules over a commutative ring is symmetric
monoidal under derived tensor product. Under the canonical comparison with tensor products of
K-flat representatives, its associator is induced by the ordinary associator of complexes, and
its braiding is the canonical Koszul symmetry.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedCategory_symmetricMonoidalCategory (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    let D := DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)
    let C := CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ
    let Q := DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{u} R)
    let T := CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalSymmetricDerivedTensorProduct R
    ∃ m : MonoidalCategory D,
      letI := m
      ∃ s : SymmetricCategory D,
        letI := s
        ∃ e : curriedTensor D ≅ T.tensorProduct.tensor,
          (∀ K L : D,
              (β_ K L).hom ≫ ((e.app L).app K).hom =
                ((e.app K).app L).hom ≫ ((T.braiding.iso.app K).app L).hom) ∧
            ∀ (K L M : C) (hK : K.KFlat) (hL : L.KFlat) (hM : M.KFlat)
                (hKL : (K ⊗ L).KFlat) (hLM : (L ⊗ M).KFlat),
              let comparison : ∀ (A B : C), A.KFlat → B.KFlat →
                  (Q.obj A ⊗ Q.obj B ⟶ Q.obj (A ⊗ B)) :=
                fun A B hA hB =>
                  ((e.app (Q.obj A)).app (Q.obj B)).hom ≫
                    (T.tensorProduct.comparison A B hA hB).hom
              (α_ (Q.obj K) (Q.obj L) (Q.obj M)).hom ≫
                    (Q.obj K ◁ comparison L M hL hM) ≫
                    comparison K (L ⊗ M) hK hLM =
                ((comparison K L hK hL :
                    Q.obj K ⊗ Q.obj L ⟶ Q.obj (K ⊗ L)) ▷ Q.obj M) ≫
                  comparison (K ⊗ L) M hKL hM ≫
                  Q.map (HomologicalComplex.associator K L M).hom

declarations.name: exists_subcomplex_bounded_finiteFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0FNR (Lemma 15.128.2).**
Let `R` be a ring and let `F` be a bounded above complex of free `R`-modules. Given a finite
family of pairs `(n i, f i)` (indexed by `i : Fin N`), with `n i ∈ ℤ` and `f i ∈ F^{n i}`,
there exists a subcomplex `G ⊆ F` such that:
1. `f i ∈ G^{n i}` for every `i` (i.e. `G` contains all the `f i`);
2. `G` is bounded; and
3. `G` consists of finite free `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_subcomplex_bounded_finiteFree (F : ZComplex R) (hFa : F.BoundedAbove) (hFfree :
  F.IsFree)
    {N : ℕ} (n : Fin N → ℤ) (f : ∀ i, F.obj (n i)) :
    ∃ G : F.Subcomplex,
      (∀ i, f i ∈ G.carrier (n i)) ∧ G.Bounded ∧ G.FiniteFree

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.Invertible.isPerfect_iff_exists_leftDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNS.** An object of the derived category has a left dual exactly when it is perfect.
For a perfect object the derived dual `RHom(M, R)` is a left dual, and every other left dual is
isomorphic to it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPerfect_iff_exists_leftDual
    (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} (ULift.{v} R))) :
    ((∃ N : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} (ULift.{v} R)),
        Nonempty (DerivedLeftDualPairing M N)) ↔
        IsPerfect M) ∧
      (IsPerfect M →
        Nonempty (DerivedLeftDualPairing M (derivedDual M))) ∧
      (∀ (N : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} (ULift.{v} R))),
        DerivedLeftDualPairing M N →
        Nonempty (N ≅ derivedDual M))

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.Invertible.isInvertible_iff_locallyShiftedUnit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNT.** A derived object is invertible if and only if it is locally a shift of the
ring. In that case it is perfect, is the direct sum of its cohomology modules, every cohomology
module is finite projective, and those modules are invertible on the factors of a finite product
decomposition of the ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isInvertible_iff_locallyShiftedUnit
    (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) :
    let derivedMonoidal := (derivedCategory_symmetricMonoidalCategory R).choose
    letI := derivedMonoidal
    (MonoidalCategory.IsInvertible M ↔ IsLocallyShiftedUnit M) ∧
      (MonoidalCategory.IsInvertible M →
        StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect M ∧
          SplitsAsCohomology M ∧
          (∀ n : ℤ,
            Module.Finite R
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj M) ∧
              Module.Projective R
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj M)) ∧
          HasInvertibleCohomologyDecomposition M)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exactPairingDualSheafOfRetract
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FNV.** Let `𝒪` be a sheaf of commutative rings on a site `(C, J)` and
let `F` be a sheaf of `𝒪`-modules which is locally a direct summand of a finite free sheaf of
modules: on the members of a family covering the final object, `F` restricts to a retract of
`SheafOfModules.free (I k)` with `I k` finite. Then the dual
`F^∨ = SheafHom(F, 𝒪)`, with the canonical coevaluation `𝒪 ⟶ F ⊗ F^∨` and the canonical
evaluation `F^∨ ⊗ F ⟶ 𝒪`, is a **left dual** of `F` in the monoidal category of sheaves of
`𝒪`-modules of Tag 01CA.

The retracts are converted into the dual bases that the canonical coevaluation is built from by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.FiniteDualBasis.ofRetract`, and the two snake identities are
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.coevaluation_evaluation_dualSheaf` and
`evaluation_coevaluation_dualSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def exactPairingDualSheafOfRetract
    (h : ∀ k, Retract (F.over (X k))
      (free (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪).over (X k)) (I
        k))) :
    ExactPairing F (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 F)
declarations.comment: the LEFT-DUAL assertion itself: the canonical coevaluation `𝒪 ⟶ ℱ ⊗ ℱ^∨` and evaluation `ℱ^∨ ⊗ ℱ ⟶ 𝒪` satisfy the two snake identities, so `ℱ^∨` is a left dual of `ℱ` in the monoidal category of Tag 01CA, for `ℱ` locally a retract of a finite free sheaf of modules. This is the clause none of `dual_sheaf`, `evaluation`, `coevaluation` or the rank-one isomorphism `ℱ ⊗ ℱ^∨ ≅ 𝓗om(ℱ,ℱ)` asserts: those construct the four objects and compute them on sections, this one is the duality

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.coevaluation
declarations.doc:
**The coevaluation `O_X ⟶ F ⊗ F^∨`** of Stacks 0FNV: the inverse image of the identity
endomorphism under the rank-one isomorphism `F ⊗ F^∨ ≅ SheafHom(F, F)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coevaluation
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (hF : IsLocallyFiniteFreeSummand X F) :
    SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X) ⟶
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨((X)).presheaf, ((X)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (F)).obj
        ((dualSheaf X F)))
declarations.comment: coevaluation

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.coevaluation_comp_tensorDualToEndomorphism
declarations.doc: Under the rank-one isomorphism, the coevaluation is the identity endomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem coevaluation_comp_tensorDualToEndomorphism
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (hF : IsLocallyFiniteFreeSummand X F) :
    coevaluation X F hF ≫ tensorDualToEndomorphism X F = identityEndomorphism X F
declarations.comment: coevaluation

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.coevaluation_apply_eq_sum_of_retract
declarations.doc:
