**Stacks 0FNV.** On an open `U` carrying a splitting `i ≫ p = 𝟙` of `F|_U` through a
finite free module, the value of the coevaluation at `1` is `∑ j, p(e j) ⊗ (e j)^* ∘ i`. The
left-hand side does not mention the splitting, so the displayed sum is independent of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem coevaluation_apply_eq_sum_of_retract
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (hF : IsLocallyFiniteFreeSummand X F) (U : Opens X.carrier) (n : ℕ)
    (i : F.over U ⟶
      SheafOfModules.free (R := (structureSheafRing X).over U) (ULift.{u} (Fin n)))
    (p : SheafOfModules.free (R := (structureSheafRing X).over U)
      (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) ⟶ F.over U) (hip : i ≫ p = 𝟙 _) :
    ((coevaluation X F hF).val.app (op U)).hom (1 : X.presheaf.obj (op U)) =
      ∑ j : Fin n, toTensorSheafSection X F (dualSheaf X F) (op U)
        (splittingBasisSection X F U n p j ⊗ₜ[X.presheaf.obj (op U)]
          splittingDualSection X F U n i j)
declarations.comment: coevaluation

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.dualSheaf_isLeftDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FNV.** For a sheaf of modules which is locally a direct summand of
a finite free module, its internal-Hom dual, with the canonical coevaluation and evaluation, is
a left dual.

The monoidal structure is exhibited together with the equations identifying its unit, its
tensor product on objects and on morphisms, and its pairing morphisms, with the canonical
sheaf constructions.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualSheaf_isLeftDual
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (hF : IsLocallyFiniteFreeSummand X F) :
    ∃ (M : MonoidalCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))),
      letI := M
      ∃ (hunit : 𝟙_ (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) =
          SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X))
        (htensor : ∀ A B : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X),
          A ⊗ B = (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
            ⟨((X)).presheaf, ((X)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (A)).obj (B)))
        (_htensorMap : ∀ {A A' B B' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)}
          (f : A ⟶ A') (g : B ⟶ B'),
          eqToHom (htensor A B).symm ≫ (f ⊗ₘ g) ≫ eqToHom (htensor A' B') =
            ((Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
              ⟨((X)).presheaf, ((X)).IsSheaf⟩)).map
              ((f, g) : (_, _) ⟶ (_, _))))
        (p : ExactPairing F (dualSheaf X F)),
        @ExactPairing.coevaluation _ _ _ _ _ p =
          eqToHom hunit ≫ coevaluation X F hF ≫
            eqToHom (htensor F (dualSheaf X F)).symm ∧
        @ExactPairing.evaluation _ _ _ _ _ p =
          eqToHom (htensor (dualSheaf X F) F) ≫ evaluation X F ≫ eqToHom hunit.symm
declarations.comment: sheaf_module_left_dual

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.tensorDualToEndomorphism_tmul_apply
declarations.doc:
On a local pure tensor of a section `f` and a local functional `lam`, the canonical
morphism is the rank-one endomorphism `g ↦ lam(g) • f`. The formula is recorded on every
object `V` of the slice site over `U`, so it determines the resulting section of the
internal hom.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorDualToEndomorphism_tmul_apply
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X.carrier)
    (f : F.val.obj (op U)) (lam : (dualSheaf X F).val.obj (op U))
    (V : (Over U)ᵒᵖ) (g : F.val.obj (op V.unop.left)) :
    ((((tensorDualToEndomorphism X F).val.app (op U)).hom
      (toTensorSheafSection X F (dualSheaf X F) (op U)
        (f ⊗ₜ[X.presheaf.obj (op U)] lam))).app V).hom g =
      dualValue X F lam V g • (F.val.map V.unop.hom.op).hom f
declarations.comment: tensor_dual_endomorphism_iso

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.tensorDualToEndomorphism_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNV.** If `F` is locally a direct summand of a finite free module, the
canonical rank-one-operator morphism `F ⊗ F^∨ ⟶ SheafHom(F, F)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorDualToEndomorphism_isIso
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (hF : IsLocallyFiniteFreeSummand X F) :
    IsIso (tensorDualToEndomorphism X F)
declarations.comment: tensor_dual_endomorphism_iso

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.dualSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The dual of a sheaf of modules**, `F^∨ = SheafHom(F, 𝒪)`: the sheaf-hom into the
structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualSheaf
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
      :
    SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪)
declarations.comment: dual_sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.evaluation
declarations.doc:
**The evaluation pairing of sheaves of modules**, `F^∨ ⊗_𝒪 F ⟶ 𝒪`. The tensor product of
sheaves of modules is the sheafification of the pointwise one (Tag 05NA), so this is the
morphism which `evaluationPresheaf` induces through the sheafification adjunction.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def evaluation
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
      :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, max u v, max u v, max u v}
      ⟨𝒪, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp J 𝒪
        (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) h𝒪⟩).obj (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 F)).obj F ⟶
      SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪)
declarations.comment: evaluation

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorDualToEndomorphism_toTensorSheafSection
declarations.doc:
**The canonical morphism on a local pure tensor is the rank-one operator.** This pins the
morphism down: its value on the image of `f ⊗ lam` is the endomorphism `g ↦ lam(g) • f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorDualToEndomorphism_toTensorSheafSection
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
      (U : Cᵒᵖ)
    (f : F.val.obj U) (lam : (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 F).val.obj U) :
    ((tensorDualToEndomorphism 𝒪 h𝒪 F).val.app U).hom
        (toTensorSheafSection 𝒪 h𝒪 F (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 F) U
          (f ⊗ₜ[(Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureRingPresheaf 𝒪).obj U] lam)) =
      rankOneSection 𝒪 h𝒪 (U := U.unop) f lam
declarations.comment: the rank-one map `ℱ ⊗ ℱ^∨ ⟶ 𝓗om(ℱ,ℱ)` read on sections: a local pure tensor `f ⊗ λ` goes to the endomorphism `g ↦ λ(g) • f`. This pins the morphism down; the companion clause `isIso_tensorDualToEndomorphism` says it is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_tensorDualToEndomorphism
declarations.doc:
**`F ⊗ F^∨ ⟶ SheafHom(F, F)` is an isomorphism** when `F` has finite dual bases on a family
covering the final object — that is, when `F` is locally a direct summand of a finite free sheaf
of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_tensorDualToEndomorphism {K : Type*} {X : K → C} (hX : J.CoversTop X)
    {I : K → Type*} [∀ k, Fintype (I k)]
    (b : ∀ k, FiniteDualBasis 𝒪 h𝒪 F (X k) (I k)) :
    IsIso (tensorDualToEndomorphism 𝒪 h𝒪 F)
declarations.comment: the rank-one map `ℱ ⊗ ℱ^∨ ⟶ 𝓗om(ℱ,ℱ)` is an ISOMORPHISM when `ℱ` admits a finite dual basis on a covering family. A different assertion from the section formula that pins the map down, which is carried by `tensorDualToEndomorphism_toTensorSheafSection`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.coevaluation
declarations.doc:
**The canonical coevaluation `𝒪 ⟶ F ⊗ F^∨`** of a sheaf of modules which is locally a
direct summand of a finite free sheaf of modules: the inverse image of the identity
endomorphism under the rank-one isomorphism `F ⊗ F^∨ ≅ SheafHom(F, F)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coevaluation
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
    {K : Type*} {X : K → C} (hX : J.CoversTop X) {I : K → Type*} [∀ k, Fintype (I k)]
    (b : ∀ k, FiniteDualBasis 𝒪 h𝒪 F (X k) (I k)) :
    SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪) ⟶
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, max u v, max u v, max u v}
        ⟨𝒪, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ 𝒪 (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) h𝒪⟩).obj F).obj
          (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 F)
declarations.comment: EXISTENCE of the canonical coevaluation `𝒪 ⟶ ℱ ⊗ ℱ^∨`, as a named morphism.  Its value on local sections is a separate assertion, carried by `coevaluation_app_one_eq_sum_of_dualBasis`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.coevaluation_app_one_eq_sum_of_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
**The local formula for the canonical coevaluation.** On an object `U` over which `F` has a
finite dual basis `(e i, lam i)`, the value of the coevaluation at the unit section is
`∑ i, e i ⊗ lam i`.

Because the left-hand side does not mention the dual basis, this also says that the displayed
sum is **independent of the chosen dual basis** — equivalently, of the chosen finite-free
retract, since a retract `i ≫ p = 𝟙` of `F|_U` onto a finite free sheaf of modules yields the
dual basis `e j = p(e_j)`, `lam j = e_j^* ∘ i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coevaluation_app_one_eq_sum_of_dualBasis
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
    {K : Type*} {X : K → C} (hX : J.CoversTop X) {I : K → Type*} [∀ k, Fintype (I k)]
    (b : ∀ k, FiniteDualBasis 𝒪 h𝒪 F (X k) (I k))
    (U : C) {I' : Type*} [Fintype I'] (c : FiniteDualBasis 𝒪 h𝒪 F U I') :
    ((coevaluation 𝒪 h𝒪 F hX b).val.app (op U)).hom
        (1 : (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪).obj.obj (op U)) =
      ∑ i : I', toTensorSheafSection 𝒪 h𝒪 F (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 F) (op U)
        (c.e i ⊗ₜ[(Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureRingPresheaf 𝒪).obj (op U)]
          c.lam i)
declarations.comment: the canonical coevaluation READ ON SECTIONS: over an object of the covering family it sends `1` to `∑ i, eᵢ ⊗ λᵢ` for a finite dual basis. This is what makes the coevaluation canonical rather than `some morphism exists`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.dualSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FNW (2).** A left dual `G` of `F` is canonically isomorphic to the
dual sheaf `F^∨ = SheafHom(F, O_X)`. The isomorphism sends a local functional `lam` over `U` to
`∑ i, lam (f i) • g i` for any expansion `η(1) = ∑ i, f i ⊗ g i` of the coevaluation over `U`;
in particular that expression does not depend on the chosen expansion.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualSheafIso
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (η : SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X) ⟶
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩).obj F).obj G)
    (ε : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩).obj G).obj F ⟶
      SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X))
    (h : IsLeftDual X F G η ε) :
    { e : dualSheaf X F ≅ G //
      ∀ (U : Opens X.carrier) (lam : (dualSheaf X F).val.obj (op U))
        (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → F.val.obj (op U)) (g : Fin n → G.val.obj (op U)),
        (η.val.app (op U)).hom (1 : X.presheaf.obj (op U)) =
          toTensorSheafSection X F G (op U)
            (∑ i, f i ⊗ₜ[X.presheaf.obj (op U)] g i) →
        (e.hom.val.app (op U)).hom lam =
          ∑ i, dualEval X F lam (f i) • g i }
declarations.comment: dual_sheaf_isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.evaluation_eq_dualSheafIso_inv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FNW (3).** Pairing a local section of a left dual `G` with a local
section of `F` under the evaluation `ε` is ordinary evaluation of the corresponding local
functional on `F`, the correspondence being the inverse of the isomorphism of Stacks 0FNW (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem evaluation_eq_dualSheafIso_inv
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (η : SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X) ⟶
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩).obj F).obj G)
    (ε : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩).obj G).obj F ⟶
      SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X))
    (h : IsLeftDual X F G η ε)
    (U : Opens X.carrier)
    (g : G.val.obj (op U)) (f : F.val.obj (op U)) :
    (ε.val.app (op U)).hom
        (toTensorSheafSection X G F (op U) (g ⊗ₜ[X.presheaf.obj (op U)] f)) =
      (((((dualSheafIso X F G η ε h).val.inv.val.app (op U)).hom g).app
        (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U)))).hom f)
declarations.comment: evaluation_formula

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.isLocallyFiniteFreeSummand_of_exactPairing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FNW (1)**, with no coherence hypotheses: a sheaf of modules with a
left dual in the monoidal category of `O_X`-modules is locally a direct summand of a finite
free module.

The three coherence hypotheses of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isLocallyFiniteFreeSummand_of_exactPairing` — which constrain the
supplied monoidal instance on local pure tensors — are discharged here against the constructed
monoidal structure by `associator_tmul`, `leftUnitor_tmul` and `rightUnitor_tmul`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyFiniteFreeSummand_of_exactPairing
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (p : ExactPairing F G) :
    IsLocallyFiniteFreeSummand X F
declarations.comment: local_finite_free_summand

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_tensorDualToEndomorphism_of_localSummand
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FNY, first assertion.** For a sheaf of modules which is locally a
direct summand of a finite free sheaf of modules, the canonical map
`F ⊗_𝒪 SheafHom(F, 𝒪) ⟶ SheafHom(F, F)` is an isomorphism.

The map is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorDualToEndomorphism`, pinned down on local sections by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorDualToEndomorphism_toTensorSheafSection`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_tensorDualToEndomorphism_of_localSummand
    (hF : IsLocallyDirectSummandOfFiniteFree 𝒪 h𝒪 F) :
    IsIso (tensorDualToEndomorphism 𝒪 h𝒪 F)
declarations.comment: the map `ℱ ⊗ 𝓗om(ℱ,𝒪) ⟶ 𝓗om(ℱ,ℱ)` is an ISOMORPHISM, with the local hypothesis in the per-object form the tag states it in

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exactPairingDualSheafOfLocalSummand
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FNY, second assertion.** For a sheaf of modules `F` which is locally a
direct summand of a finite free sheaf of modules, the dual `F^∨ = SheafHom(F, 𝒪)`, with the
canonical coevaluation `η : 𝒪 ⟶ F ⊗ F^∨` and the canonical evaluation `ε : F^∨ ⊗ F ⟶ 𝒪`, is a
**left dual** of `F` in the monoidal category of sheaves of `𝒪`-modules of Tag 01CA. That is, the
two triangle identities hold.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def exactPairingDualSheafOfLocalSummand
    (hF : IsLocallyDirectSummandOfFiniteFree 𝒪 h𝒪 F) :
    ExactPairing F (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 F)
declarations.comment: the LEFT-DUAL assertion: `𝓗om(ℱ,𝒪)` with the canonical coevaluation and evaluation satisfies the two triangle identities, with the local hypothesis in the per-object form the tag states it in

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.dualSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The dual of a sheaf of modules**, `F^∨ = SheafHom(F, 𝒪)`: the sheaf-hom into the
structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualSheaf
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
      :
    SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪)
declarations.comment: the dual `SheafHom(ℱ, 𝒪)` whose left-dual property is the content of the tag; the construction is for an arbitrary site, so the ringed-space and the ringed-site tags name the same object

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.evaluation
declarations.doc:
**The evaluation pairing of sheaves of modules**, `F^∨ ⊗_𝒪 F ⟶ 𝒪`. The tensor product of
sheaves of modules is the sheafification of the pointwise one (Tag 05NA), so this is the
morphism which `evaluationPresheaf` induces through the sheafification adjunction.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def evaluation
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
      :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, max u v, max u v, max u v}
      ⟨𝒪, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp J 𝒪
        (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) h𝒪⟩).obj (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 F)).obj F ⟶
      SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪)
declarations.comment: the evaluation map `ε : ℱ^∨ ⊗ ℱ ⟶ 𝒪`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorDualToEndomorphism_toTensorSheafSection
declarations.doc:
**The canonical morphism on a local pure tensor is the rank-one operator.** This pins the
morphism down: its value on the image of `f ⊗ lam` is the endomorphism `g ↦ lam(g) • f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorDualToEndomorphism_toTensorSheafSection
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
      (U : Cᵒᵖ)
    (f : F.val.obj U) (lam : (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 F).val.obj U) :
    ((tensorDualToEndomorphism 𝒪 h𝒪 F).val.app U).hom
        (toTensorSheafSection 𝒪 h𝒪 F (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 F) U
          (f ⊗ₜ[(Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureRingPresheaf 𝒪).obj U] lam)) =
      rankOneSection 𝒪 h𝒪 (U := U.unop) f lam
declarations.comment: the map `ℱ ⊗ 𝓗om(ℱ,𝒪) ⟶ 𝓗om(ℱ,ℱ)` read on sections, which pins it down

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.dualSheafIsoOfLeftDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FNZ (2).** A left dual `G` of a sheaf of `𝒪`-modules `F` on a ringed
site is isomorphic to `SheafHom(F, 𝒪)`.

Both `SheafHom(F, 𝒪)` and `G` are left duals of `F` — the first by
`exactPairingDualSheafOfLeftDual` — and two left duals of one object are isomorphic through the
adjoint mate of the identity. That this isomorphism is the map Tag 0FNZ (2) names, namely
`λ ↦ (λ ⊗ 1)(η)`, is `dualSheafIsoOfLeftDual_hom_val_app`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def dualSheafIsoOfLeftDual : dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 F ≅ G
declarations.comment: (2), the isomorphism `𝓗om(ℱ,𝒪) ≅ 𝒢`; that it is the map `λ ↦ (λ ⊗ 1)(η)` of the tag is `dualSheafIsoOfLeftDual_hom_val_app`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.dualSheafIsoOfLeftDual_hom_val_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FNZ (2), the formula for the isomorphism.** On an object `U` over
which the coevaluation expands as `η(1) = ∑ fᵢ ⊗ gᵢ`, the isomorphism
`SheafHom(F, 𝒪) ≅ G` of Tag 0FNZ (2) sends a local section `λ` to `∑ λ(fᵢ) • gᵢ`, which is
`(λ ⊗ 1)(η)`. In particular that expression does not depend on the chosen expansion.

Such an expansion exists on a covering of every object of the site, by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_cover_localDualBasis_tensorSheaf`, so these formulas determine the
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualSheafIsoOfLeftDual_hom_val_app (U : C) {n : ℕ}
    (f : Fin n → F.val.obj (op U)) (g : Fin n → G.val.obj (op U))
    (hη : (η_ F G).val.app (op U)
        (1 : (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪).obj.obj (op U)) =
      ∑ i, tensorPt 𝒪 h𝒪 F G (op U) (f i) (g i))
    (lam : (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 F).val.obj (op U)) :
    (dualSheafIsoOfLeftDual 𝒪 h𝒪 F G).hom.val.app (op U) lam =
      ∑ i, dualEval lam (f i) • g i
declarations.comment: (2), that the isomorphism is the map `λ ↦ (λ ⊗ 1)(η)` the tag describes

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.evaluation_eq_dualEval_dualSheafIsoOfLeftDual_inv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FNZ (3).** Pairing a local section `g` of a left dual `G` of `F`
against a local section `f` of `F` under the given evaluation `ε` is the value at `f` of the
local homomorphism `e⁻¹(g) : F ⟶ 𝒪`, where `e` is the isomorphism of Tag 0FNZ (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem evaluation_eq_dualEval_dualSheafIsoOfLeftDual_inv (U : C)
    (y : G.val.obj (op U)) (x : F.val.obj (op U)) :
    (ε_ F G).val.app (op U) (tensorPt 𝒪 h𝒪 G F (op U) y x) =
      dualEval ((dualSheafIsoOfLeftDual 𝒪 h𝒪 F G).inv.val.app (op U) y) x
declarations.comment: (3), the evaluation formula `ε(f, g) = e⁻¹(g)(f)`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_cover_retract_finiteFree_of_exactPairing_tensorSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `F` be a sheaf of `O`-modules with a left dual `G` for
the monoidal structure given by the tensor product sheaf. Then every object `U` of the site has
a covering on whose members `F` restricts to a direct summand of a finite free module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cover_retract_finiteFree_of_exactPairing_tensorSheaf
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [∀ V : C, HasWeakSheafify (J.over V) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [∀ V : C, (J.over V).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (p : ExactPairing F G) (U : C) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ J U ∧
      ∀ (V : C) (i : V ⟶ U), S i →
        ∃ I : Type w, Finite I ∧
          Nonempty (Retract (F.over V)
            (SheafOfModules.free (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O
              hO).over V) I))
declarations.comment: local_finite_free_summand

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_cover_retract_finiteFree_of_exactPairing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FNZ (1) for the `𝒪_F`-modules of an algebraic space.**  If an `𝒪_F`-module `M` has
a left dual `N` in the monoidal category of `𝒪_F`-modules, then every object `U` of the small
étale site of `F` has a covering on whose members `M` restricts to a direct summand of a free
module on a finite index type.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cover_retract_finiteFree_of_exactPairing
    (M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) (p : ExactPairing M N)
    (U : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).C) :
    ∃ T : Sieve U, T ∈ (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).J U ∧
      ∀ (V : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).C) (i : V ⟶ U), T i →
        ∃ I : Type u, Finite I ∧
          Nonempty (Retract (M.over V)
            (SheafOfModules.free (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
              (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O).over V) I))
declarations.comment: (1), for the modules of an algebraic space

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackTensor.derivedPullbackTensorIso_toTensor_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FP0.**  Let `f : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y, 𝒪_Y)` be a morphism of ringed spaces and let
`K, M` be complexes of `𝒪_Y`-modules.  The diagram

```
Lf^*(K ⊗^L_{𝒪_Y} M)  ⟶  Lf^*Tot(K ⊗_{𝒪_Y} M)
        |                           |
        v                           v
Lf^*K ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} Lf^*M        f^*Tot(K ⊗_{𝒪_Y} M)
        |                           |
        v                           v
 f^*K ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} f^*M    ⟶   Tot(f^*K ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*M)
```

commutes: the left hand column — Stacks 079U, then the comparison `Lf^*(QN) ⟶ Q(f^*N)` in each
tensor factor — followed by the canonical map to the ordinary total tensor complex on `X`
equals the top row — the derived pullback of the canonical map to the ordinary total tensor
complex on `Y` — followed by the right hand column, the comparison `Lf^*(QN) ⟶ Q(f^*N)` at
`Tot(K ⊗_{𝒪_Y} M)` and then the comparison of total complexes of Stacks 01CD.

This is
`derivedPullbackTensorIso_hom_app_comp_rightComparison_of_complexes` with the right comparison
written out: postcomposing with the comparison of total complexes cancels the inverse that the
right comparison ends with, leaving the six arrows of the source's diagram.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPullbackTensorIso_toTensor_comm
    (K L : CochainComplex (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules Y) ℤ) :
    (derivedPullbackTensorIso f).hom.app
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K, DerivedCategory.Q.obj L) ≫
        (Functor.uncurry.obj
              (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf)).map
            ((derivedPullbackNatTrans f).app K ×ₘ (derivedPullbackNatTrans f).app L) ≫
          (derivedToTensorNatTrans X).app
            ((pullbackComplex f).obj K, (pullbackComplex f).obj L) =
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback f).map
          ((derivedToTensorNatTrans Y).app (K, L)) ≫
        (derivedPullbackNatTrans f).app
            ((totalComplexPair (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor Y.sheaf)).obj (K, L)) ≫
          DerivedCategory.Q.map ((pullbackTensorComplexNatIso f).hom.app (K, L))

registrations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedAdjunction_counit_fac
registrations.comment: the square of the ordinary and the derived counit commutes

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedRelativeCupProduct.homEquiv_symm_relativeCupProduct
declarations.doc:
The two constructions of the cup product agree: the adjunct of the tensor product `ξ ⊗ η` of
two cohomology classes followed by the relative cup product of Stacks 0B68 is the derived
pullback-tensor comparison of Stacks 079U followed by the tensor product `ξ̃ ⊗ η̃` of their
adjuncts.
declarations.statement:
theorem homEquiv_symm_relativeCupProduct
    {U V : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))}
    {K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))}
    (ξ : U ⟶ (derivedPushforward f).obj K) (η : V ⟶ (derivedPushforward f).obj M) :
    ((derivedAdjunction f).homEquiv _ _).symm
        (((derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf).map ξ).app V ≫
          ((derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf).obj
              ((derivedPushforward f).obj K)).map η ≫
            relativeCupProduct f K M) =
      (pullbackTensorComparison f).app (U, V) ≫
        ((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).map
              (((derivedAdjunction f).homEquiv U K).symm ξ)).app
            ((derivedPullback f).obj V) ≫
          ((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).map
            (((derivedAdjunction f).homEquiv V M).symm η)
declarations.comment: the identification-free core, at arbitrary objects of `D(𝒪_Y)` in place of the source's shifted structure sheaves, and for an arbitrary morphism of ringed spaces

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedRelativeCupProduct.homEquiv_symm_comp_relativeCupProduct
declarations.doc:
Let `χ : W ⟶ U ⊗^L_{𝒪_Y} V`. The adjunct of `χ` followed by `ξ ⊗ η` and the relative cup
product of Stacks 0B68 is `Lf^*χ` followed by the derived pullback-tensor comparison of
Stacks 079U and by the tensor product `ξ̃ ⊗ η̃` of the adjuncts.
declarations.statement:
theorem homEquiv_symm_comp_relativeCupProduct
    {W U V : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))}
    {K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))}
    (χ : W ⟶ ((derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf).obj U).obj V)
    (ξ : U ⟶ (derivedPushforward f).obj K) (η : V ⟶ (derivedPushforward f).obj M) :
    ((derivedAdjunction f).homEquiv _ _).symm
        (χ ≫ ((derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf).map ξ).app V ≫
          ((derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf).obj
              ((derivedPushforward f).obj K)).map η ≫
            relativeCupProduct f K M) =
      (derivedPullback f).map χ ≫ (pullbackTensorComparison f).app (U, V) ≫
        ((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).map
              (((derivedAdjunction f).homEquiv U K).symm ξ)).app
            ((derivedPullback f).obj V) ≫
          ((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).map
            (((derivedAdjunction f).homEquiv V M).symm η)
declarations.comment: stated for an arbitrary morphism of ringed spaces, with the source's identification `𝒪_Y[-i-j] = 𝒪_Y[-i] ⊗ᴸ 𝒪_Y[-j]` carried as an arbitrary morphism `χ`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CupProductAndDerivedPushforwardOnRingedSpaces.naiveCupProduct_relativeCupProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FP3.**  For a morphism of ringed spaces `f : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y, 𝒪_Y)` and complexes
`𝒦^•`, `ℳ^•` of `𝒪_X`-modules, the hexagon

```
f_*𝒦^• ⊗^L_{𝒪_Y} f_*ℳ^• ─────→ Rf_*𝒦^• ⊗^L_{𝒪_Y} Rf_*ℳ^•
          │                                │
          ↓                                ↓
Tot(f_*𝒦^• ⊗_{𝒪_Y} f_*ℳ^•)        Rf_*(𝒦^• ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} ℳ^•)
          │                                │
          ↓                                ↓
f_*Tot(𝒦^• ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℳ^•) ─────→ Rf_*Tot(𝒦^• ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℳ^•)
```

commutes in `D(𝒪_Y)`.  Its horizontal edges and its top right edge are the comparison
`f_* ⟶ Rf_*`; the top left and bottom right edges are the canonical map from the derived
tensor product to the ordinary total tensor complex of Stacks 06YU; the middle left edge is
the naive cup product and the middle right edge is the relative cup product of Stacks 0B68.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCupProduct_relativeCupProduct :
    (derivedToTensorNatTrans Y).app
          ((pushforwardComplex f).obj K, (pushforwardComplex f).obj M) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (naiveCupProduct f K M) ≫
        pushforwardComparisonQ f ((totalComplexPair (sheafTensor X.sheaf)).obj (K, M)) =
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf)).map
          (pushforwardComparisonQ f K ×ₘ pushforwardComparisonQ f M) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) ≫
        (derivedPushforward f).map ((derivedToTensorNatTrans X).app (K, M))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedRelativeCupProduct.relativeCupProduct_assoc
declarations.doc:
**The relative cup product is associative.**  For a morphism of ringed spaces
`f : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y, 𝒪_Y)` and arbitrary `K, L, M ∈ D(𝒪_X)` the square

```
(Rf_*K ⊗^L Rf_*L) ⊗^L Rf_*M ⟶ Rf_*(K ⊗^L L) ⊗^L Rf_*M ⟶ Rf_*((K ⊗^L L) ⊗^L M)
            |                                                      |
            | a                                                    | Rf_*a
            v                                                      v
Rf_*K ⊗^L (Rf_*L ⊗^L Rf_*M) ⟶ Rf_*K ⊗^L Rf_*(L ⊗^L M) ⟶ Rf_*(K ⊗^L (L ⊗^L M))
```

commutes in `D(𝒪_Y)`, where the four unlabelled arrows are relative cup products of Stacks 0B68
in one or the other tensor factor and `a` is the associativity constraint of Stacks 0FPB.  The
compatibility of the comparison of Stacks 079U with those constraints is
`pullbackTensorComparisonAssociative`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_assoc
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (Mod X.sheaf)) :
    (Functor.uncurry.obj
            (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf)).map
        (relativeCupProduct f K L ×ₘ 𝟙 ((derivedPushforward f).obj M)) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f
            ((Functor.uncurry.obj
              (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf)).obj (K, L))
            M ≫
          (derivedPushforward f).map (derivedAssociator X K L M) =
      derivedAssociator Y ((derivedPushforward f).obj K) ((derivedPushforward f).obj L)
          ((derivedPushforward f).obj M) ≫
        (Functor.uncurry.obj
              (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf)).map
            (𝟙 ((derivedPushforward f).obj K) ×ₘ relativeCupProduct f L M) ≫
          relativeCupProduct f K
            ((Functor.uncurry.obj
              (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf)).obj (L, M))
declarations.comment: associativity of the relative cup product, for a morphism of ringed spaces and arbitrary K, L, M in D(O_X): the associativity constraints are those of Tag 0FPB (derivedAssociator), and their compatibility with the comparison of Tag 079U is pullbackTensorComparisonAssociative

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedRelativeCupProduct.relativeCupProduct_braiding
declarations.doc:
**The relative cup product is commutative.**  For a morphism of ringed spaces
`f : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y, 𝒪_Y)` and arbitrary `K, L ∈ D(𝒪_X)` the square

```
Rf_*K ⊗^L Rf_*L ⟶ Rf_*(K ⊗^L L)
      |                  |
      ψ                 Rf_*ψ
      v                  v
Rf_*L ⊗^L Rf_*K ⟶ Rf_*(L ⊗^L K)
```

commutes in `D(𝒪_Y)`, where the horizontal arrows are the relative cup product of Stacks 0B68
and `ψ` is the commutativity constraint of Stacks 0FPB.  The compatibility of the comparison of
Stacks 079U with those constraints is `pullbackTensorComparisonBraided`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_braiding (K L : DerivedCategory (Mod X.sheaf)) :
    derivedBraiding Y ((derivedPushforward f).obj K) ((derivedPushforward f).obj L) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f L K =
      relativeCupProduct f K L ≫ (derivedPushforward f).map (derivedBraiding X K L)
declarations.comment: the whole tag: for a morphism of ringed spaces and arbitrary K, L in D(𝒪_X), the commutativity square of the relative cup product commutes. The commutativity constraints are derivedBraiding of Stacks 0FPB, and their compatibility with the Stacks 079U comparison is pullbackTensorComparisonBraided

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedRelativeCupProduct.relativeCupProduct_comp
declarations.doc:
**The relative cup product is compatible with composition.**  For the composite adjunction
`Lg^*Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*Rg_*` and the composite derived pullback-tensor comparison, the relative cup
product of Stacks 0B68 is the relative cup product for `g` at the pair `(Rf_*K, Rf_*L)` followed
by `Rg_*` of the relative cup product for `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_comp
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    adjunctionBitensorMap
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedAdjunction g).comp
          (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedAdjunction f))
        (Functor.uncurry.obj
          (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor Z.sheaf))
        (Functor.uncurry.obj
          (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf))
        (pullbackTensorComparisonComp f g) K L =
      relativeCupProduct g
          ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj K)
          ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj L) ≫
        (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward g).map
          (relativeCupProduct f K L)
declarations.comment: for the composite adjunction and the composite pullback-tensor comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedRelativeCupProduct.relativeCupProduct_comp'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FP6: the relative cup product is compatible with composition.**  For composable
morphisms of ringed spaces `f : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y, 𝒪_Y)` and `g : (Y, 𝒪_Y) ⟶ (Z, 𝒪_Z)` and
arbitrary `K, L ∈ D(𝒪_X)` the square

```
Rg_*Rf_*K ⊗^L Rg_*Rf_*L ⟶ R(g ∘ f)_*K ⊗^L R(g ∘ f)_*L
          |                            |
          |                            | relative cup product for f ≫ g
          v                            v
   Rg_*Rf_*(K ⊗^L L)     ⟶      R(g ∘ f)_*(K ⊗^L L)
```

commutes in `D(𝒪_Z)`, where the horizontal arrows are the composition isomorphism
`Rf_* ⋙ Rg_* ≅ R(g ∘ f)_*` of Stacks 0D5T — in each tensor factor on top and at the tensor
product on the bottom — and the left vertical arrow is the relative cup product for `g` at
`(Rf_*K, Rf_*L)` followed by `Rg_*` of the relative cup product for `f`.

This is the statement of the source, the two identifications being the composition isomorphism.
It is
`relativeCupProduct_comp` transported by `adjunctionBitensorMap_transport`, whose two inputs are
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedAdjunction_comp` and
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackTensor.derivedPullbackTensorIso_comp`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_comp'
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    (Functor.uncurry.obj
            (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor Z.sheaf)).map
          ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforwardCompIso f
              g).hom.app K ×ₘ
            (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforwardCompIso f
              g).hom.app L) ≫
        relativeCupProduct (f ≫ g) K L =
      relativeCupProduct g
          ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj K)
          ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj L) ≫
        (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward g).map
            (relativeCupProduct f K L) ≫
          (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforwardCompIso f
              g).hom.app
            (((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).obj
              L)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MonoidalComplexes.symmetricMonoidalComplexes
declarations.doc:
Complexes of modules on a ringed space form a symmetric monoidal category; its tensor
bifunctor is the total complex of the sheafified degreewise tensor product and its unit is the
structure sheaf in degree zero.  This is Tag 0FPQ at the ringed site of opens of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public def symmetricMonoidalComplexes :
    Stacks.Cohomology.MonoidalComplexesOfModules.SymmetricMonoidalComplexes X.sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.exists_exactPairing_ihomUnit_of_isLocallyBounded
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FP9].**  Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space and `ℱ^•` a locally bounded
complex of `𝒪_X`-modules each of whose terms `ℱ^n` is locally a direct summand of a finite free
`𝒪_X`-module, and let `𝒢^• = Hom^•(ℱ^•, 𝒪_X)`.  Let `ηₙ : 𝒪_X ⟶ ℱ^n ⊗ 𝒢^{-n}` and
`εₙ : 𝒢^{-n} ⊗ ℱ^n ⟶ 𝒪_X` be the coevaluation and evaluation of the duality between `ℱ^n` and
`𝒢^{-n}`.  Then there is a left dual structure on `𝒢^•` over `ℱ^•` in the monoidal category of
complexes of `𝒪_X`-modules whose coevaluation is `η = ∑ ηₙ` and whose evaluation is
`ε = ∑ εₙ`: in degree zero, read through the identification of the degree zero term of the unit
complex with `𝒪_X`, the component of `η` on the summand `ℱ^n ⊗ 𝒢^{-n}` of
`Tot(ℱ^• ⊗ 𝒢^•)^0` is `ηₙ`, and the component of `ε` on the summand `𝒢^{-n} ⊗ ℱ^n` of
`Tot(𝒢^• ⊗ ℱ^•)^0` is `εₙ`.  The structure is `exactPairingIhomUnitComplexOfIsLocallyBounded`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_exactPairing_ihomUnit_of_isLocallyBounded
    (F : CochainComplex (Strict.Mod X.sheaf) ℤ)
    (hb : IsLocallyBounded X F) (hF : ∀ n : ℤ, IsLocallyFiniteFreeSummand X (F.X n)) :
    letI : MonoidalCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.sheaf)) :=
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.Strict.monoidalCategory X.sheaf.obj
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.sheaf).property
    letI : MonoidalPreadditive (Strict.Mod X.sheaf) :=
      Strict.monoidalPreadditiveRingSheaf X.sheaf
    letI : ∀ X₁ X₂ : GradedObject ℤ (Strict.Mod X.sheaf), GradedObject.HasTensor X₁ X₂ :=
      fun _ _ => inferInstance
    letI := Strict.monoidalCategoryCochainComplex X.sheaf
    letI := Strict.monoidalClosedCochainComplex X.sheaf
    ∃ P : ExactPairing F ((ihom F).obj (𝟙_ (CochainComplex (Strict.Mod X.sheaf) ℤ))),
      (∀ n : ℤ, P.coevaluation'.f 0 ≫
          GradedObject.Monoidal.πTensorObj F.X
            ((ihom F).obj (𝟙_ (CochainComplex (Strict.Mod X.sheaf) ℤ))).X n (-n) 0
            (add_neg_cancel n) =
        ((HomologicalComplex.tensorUnitIso (Strict.Mod X.sheaf) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).inv 0 ≫
            GradedObject.Monoidal.tensorUnit₀.hom) ≫
          (Strict.exactPairingIhomComplexX X.sheaf F n
            (isLocallyDirectSummandOfFiniteFree_of_isLocallyFiniteFreeSummand X (F.X n)
              (hF n))).coevaluation') ∧
      ∀ n : ℤ, HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj
          ((ihom F).obj (𝟙_ (CochainComplex (Strict.Mod X.sheaf) ℤ))) F (-n) n 0
          (neg_add_cancel n) ≫ P.evaluation'.f 0 =
        (Strict.exactPairingIhomComplexX X.sheaf F n
            (isLocallyDirectSummandOfFiniteFree_of_isLocallyFiniteFreeSummand X (F.X n)
              (hF n))).evaluation' ≫
          GradedObject.Monoidal.tensorUnit₀.inv ≫
            (HomologicalComplex.tensorUnitIso (Strict.Mod X.sheaf) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).hom 0

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Strict.isLocallyBounded_and_isLocallyDirectSummand_and_isoDualComplex_of_exactPairing
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FPA].** Let `(C, 𝒪)` be a ringed site and let `ℱ^•` be a complex of
`𝒪`-modules. If `ℱ^•` has a left dual `𝒢^•` in the monoidal category of complexes of
`𝒪`-modules, then all three of the following hold.

1. `ℱ^•` is locally bounded: every object of the site has a covering sieve on whose members all
   but finitely many terms of `ℱ^•` restrict to zero, the finite set of surviving degrees
   depending on the member.
2. Every term `ℱ^n` is locally a direct summand of a finite free `𝒪`-module.
3. The left dual is the one constructed in [Stacks, Tag 0FP9]: `𝒢^•` is isomorphic to the complex
   `SheafHom^•(ℱ^•, 𝒪)` of [Stacks, Tag 0FPR] by an isomorphism carrying the coevaluation and the
   evaluation of the given pairing to `η = ∑ ηₙ` and `ε = ∑ εₙ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyBounded_and_isLocallyDirectSummand_and_isoDualComplex_of_exactPairing
    (p : @ExactPairing _ _ (monoidalCategoryCochainComplex R) K L) :
    letI := monoidalCategoryCochainComplex R
    letI := p
    letI := exactPairingDualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect
      (isLocallyStrictlyPerfect_of_exactPairing R K L p)
    (∀ U : C, ∃ T : Sieve U, T ∈ J U ∧ ∀ ⦃V : C⦄ (g : V ⟶ U), T g →
        ∃ S : Finset ℤ, ∀ n ∉ S, IsZero ((K.X n).over V)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, IsLocallyDirectSummandOfFiniteFree R.obj (isSheaf_ringSheaf R) (K.X n)) ∧
      ∃ e : L ≅ dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect R K
          (isLocallyStrictlyPerfect_of_exactPairing R K L p),
        η_ K L ≫ K ◁ e.hom =
            η_ K (dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect R K
              (isLocallyStrictlyPerfect_of_exactPairing R K L p)) ∧
          e.hom ▷ K ≫ ε_ K (dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect R K
              (isLocallyStrictlyPerfect_of_exactPairing R K L p)) = ε_ K L
declarations.comment: the WHOLE statement of the tag under the tag's OWN hypothesis, for a ringed site — of which the ringed space of the tag is a case — and over the monoidal structure on complexes of 𝒪-modules whose tensor product is the one of Tag 01CA: a complex `ℱ^•` with a left dual `𝒢^•` is (1) locally bounded, (2) has every term a local direct summand of a finite free module, and (3) has `𝒢^•` the complex of Example 0FP9, namely `SheafHom^•(ℱ^•, 𝒪)` — `Stacks.SheafOfModules.Strict.dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect`, the dual sheaves of Tag 0FNY in the opposite degrees with the signed-transpose differential — together WITH its pairings: the isomorphism carries η and ε to the η = ∑ ηₙ and ε = ∑ εₙ that Tag 0FPR puts on that complex, so the triple `(𝒢^•, η, ε)` is identified with Example 0FP9's triple and not merely the underlying complexes. (3) is uniqueness of left duals (Tag 0FFR, `CategoryTheory.rightDualIso`) applied to the left dual Tag 0FPR builds from the local strict perfectness of Tag 0FPS, which (1) and (2) supply. The site-level analogue of the whole tag is Tag 0FPS, `Stacks.SheafOfModules.Strict.exists_cover_isStrictlyPerfect_of_exactPairing` for its first assertion

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MonoidalDerived.symmetricMonoidalDerivedCategory
declarations.doc:
**The derived category of modules on a ringed space is a symmetric monoidal category**, with
tensor product the derived tensor product, unit the structure sheaf in degree zero, and the
usual associativity and commutativity constraints.  This is the ringed site statement at the
site of opens of `X`, exactly as Tag 0FP8 is Tag 0FPQ there.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedDual_isLeftDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPC.**  Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and let `K` be a perfect object of
`D(O_X)` (Tag 08CM), with `K^∨ = RSheafHom(K, O_X)`.  Then

* the map `c : K ⊗^L_{O_X} K^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(K, K)` of Stacks 08I1 is an isomorphism;
* the coevaluation `η : O_X ⟶ K ⊗^L_{O_X} K^∨` is the map sending `1` to the section
  corresponding to `id_K` under `c`: `η ≫ c` is that section;
* with `ε : K^∨ ⊗^L_{O_X} K ⟶ O_X` the evaluation map, `K^∨, η, ε` is a left dual of `K`
  (Categories, Definition 0FFP): `(1 ⊗ ε) ∘ (η ⊗ 1) = id_K` and `(ε ⊗ 1) ∘ (1 ⊗ η) = id_{K^∨}`,
  read through the associativity and unit constraints of the monoidal structure of Stacks 0FPT on
  `D(O_X)`.

The evaluation is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedDualEvaluation`, the application morphism of
Stacks 08J8 at target `O_X`
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomCounit_structureSheaf_eq_derivedDualEvaluation`), and
the coevaluation is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedDualCoevaluation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedDual_isLeftDual (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X) K) :
    letI := derivedMonoidalStructure X.sheaf
    letI : MonoidalCategory (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
        (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.sheaf))) := derivedMonoidalStructure X.sheaf
    IsIso (derivedTensorDualToSheafHom X.sheaf K K) ∧
      derivedDualCoevaluation X.sheaf K
          (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.isPerfect_ringedSite_of_isPerfect X K hK) ≫
          derivedTensorDualToSheafHom X.sheaf K K =
        RingedSite.derivedIdentitySection (ringedSite X.sheaf) K ∧
      derivedDualCoevaluation X.sheaf K
          (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.isPerfect_ringedSite_of_isPerfect X K hK) ▷ K ≫
          (α_ K (derivedDual X.sheaf K) K).hom ≫ K ◁ derivedDualEvaluation X.sheaf K =
        (λ_ K).hom ≫ (ρ_ K).inv ∧
      derivedDual X.sheaf K ◁ derivedDualCoevaluation X.sheaf K
          (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.isPerfect_ringedSite_of_isPerfect X K hK) ≫
          (α_ (derivedDual X.sheaf K) K (derivedDual X.sheaf K)).inv ≫
          derivedDualEvaluation X.sheaf K ▷ derivedDual X.sheaf K =
        (ρ_ (derivedDual X.sheaf K)).hom ≫ (λ_ (derivedDual X.sheaf K)).inv

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_derivedDualToLeftDualMonoidal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPD, second assertion: a left dual of `M` in `D(O_X)` is the dual object of
Example 0FPC.** The morphism `M^∨ = RSheafHom(M, O_X) ⟶ N` which the exact pairing matches with
the evaluation of Example 0FPC is an isomorphism; its inverse is the morphism which the
tensor–internal-Hom bijection of Stacks 08DK matches with the evaluation of the pairing.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedDualToLeftDualMonoidal
    (pair : letI : MonoidalCategory (DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :=
        RingedSite.derivedMonoidalStructure (ringedSite Rc)
      ExactPairing M N) :
    letI : @ExactPairing
        (DerivedCategory
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (ringedSite Rc).O)))
        inferInstance (RingedSite.derivedMonoidalStructure (ringedSite Rc)) M N := pair
    IsIso (RingedSite.derivedDualToLeftDual (X := ringedSite Rc) M N)
declarations.comment: conclusion (b) only: that the left dual of M is the object constructed in Example 0FPC, namely the derived dual RSheafHom(M, O_X), the identification being the morphism matched with the evaluation of Example 0FPC by the pairing — see `Stacks.SheafOfModules.whiskerRight_derivedDualToLeftDualMonoidal` for the compatibility of the two evaluations and `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedDualEvaluation_eq_ringedSite` for the identification of that evaluation with the one Example 0FPC constructs. The monoidal structure on D(O_X) is the one of Tag 0FPB and a left dual is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.ExactPairing`, which is Definition 0FFP. Conclusion (a) of the tag — that M is PERFECT — is NOT proved here and NOT assumed here: it needs the pairing to restrict to the slices D(O_X|_U), for which the derived restriction functor would have to be monoidal, and nothing in this library makes it so. The naturality of the bijection of Tag 08DK/08JA in its source variable, which the argument uses, is the theorem `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCurryHomEquiv_naturality_source`, so the exact pairing itself is the one remaining input

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.LeftDualPerfect.isPerfect_and_isIso_derivedDualToLeftDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPD.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and let `M` be an object of `D(O_X)` with a
left dual `N` in the symmetric monoidal category `D(O_X)` of Stacks 0FPB (an exact pairing,
Categories, Definition 0FFP). Then

* (a) `M` is perfect (Tag 08CM), and
* (b) the left dual is the one constructed in Example 0FPC: the morphism
  `M^∨ = RSheafHom(M, O_X) ⟶ N` which the pairing matches with the evaluation of Example 0FPC is
  an isomorphism.

The monoidal structure is written in its ringed-site spelling, which is the structure of
Stacks 0FPB on the nose (`derivedCategoryMonoidalCategory_eq_ringedSite`, by `rfl`). Conclusion
(a) is `isPerfect_of_exactPairing`; conclusion (b) is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_derivedDualToLeftDualMonoidal`, whose morphism carries the evaluation
of the pairing to the evaluation of Example 0FPC
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.whiskerRight_derivedDualToLeftDualMonoidal`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_and_isIso_derivedDualToLeftDual (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (M N : DerivedModules X.sheaf)
    (pair : letI := derivedMonoidalSpace X; ExactPairing M N) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect M ∧
      (letI := derivedMonoidalSpace X
       let _ := pair
       IsIso (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedDualToLeftDual
        (X := Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite X.sheaf) M N))
declarations.comment: both conclusions, for one pairing: M is perfect, and the left dual is the derived dual of Example 0FPC

declarations.name: Stacks.Modules.globalSections_equivalence_finiteFreeSummand_finiteProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FPF.** Global sections induce an equivalence from
direct summands of finite free `𝒪`-modules to finite projective modules over
the ring of global sections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem globalSections_equivalence_finiteFreeSummand_finiteProjective :
    ∃ (e : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsDirectSummandOfFiniteFree 𝒪) ≌
        ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
          (fun M : ModuleCat.{u} (𝒪.obj.obj (op (⊤ : Opens X))) =>
            Module.Finite (𝒪.obj.obj (op (⊤ : Opens X))) M ∧
              Module.Projective (𝒪.obj.obj (op (⊤ : Opens X))) M)),
      Nonempty
        (e.functor ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _ ≅
          ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙ globalSectionsFunctor 𝒪)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InvertibleDerived.hasInvertibleModuleDecomposition_of_isInvertibleObject
declarations.doc:
**The implication `(1) ⟹ (2)` of Stacks 0FPG.** If `M` is an invertible object of `D(𝒪_X)`,
there is a locally finite direct product decomposition `𝒪_X = ∏ 𝒪_n` and invertible
`𝒪_n`-modules `ℋ^n` with `M = ⨁ ℋ^n[-n]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasInvertibleModuleDecomposition_of_isInvertibleObject
    [inst : HasDerivedCategory.{d} (Mod X.sheaf)] (M : DerivedModules X.sheaf)
    (hM : IsInvertibleObject M) : HasInvertibleModuleDecomposition X M
declarations.comment: clause (1) implies clause (2): an invertible object of D(𝒪_X) has a locally finite invertible module decomposition

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InvertibleDerived.isInvertibleObject_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPG.** Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space and `M` an object of `D(𝒪_X)`. The following
are equivalent:
1. `M` is invertible in `D(𝒪_X)` for the derived tensor product;
2. there is a locally finite direct product decomposition `𝒪_X = ∏ 𝒪_n` and for each `n` an
   invertible `𝒪_n`-module `ℋ^n` with `M = ⨁ ℋ^n[-n]` in `D(𝒪_X)`.

If they hold, `M` is perfect. If every stalk `𝒪_{X,x}` is a local ring, they are also equivalent
to
3. there is an open covering `X = ⋃ U_i` and for each `i` an integer `n_i` such that `M|_{U_i}` is
   represented by an invertible `𝒪_{U_i}`-module placed in degree `n_i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isInvertibleObject_tfae [inst : HasDerivedCategory.{d} (Mod X.sheaf)]
    (M : DerivedModules X.sheaf) :
    [IsInvertibleObject M, HasInvertibleModuleDecomposition X M].TFAE ∧
      (IsInvertibleObject M → @Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect.{u, u, d} X inst M) ∧
      ((∀ x : X.carrier, IsLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)) →
        [IsInvertibleObject M, HasInvertibleModuleDecomposition X M,
          HasLocalInvertibleDegree M].TFAE)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InvertibleDerived.hasInvertibleModuleDecomposition_iff_hasLocalInvertibleDegree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPG, the equivalence of clauses (2) and (3).** Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space all
of whose stalks `𝒪_{X,x}` are local rings, and let `M` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)`. Then `M` admits a
locally finite direct product decomposition `𝒪_X = ∏ 𝒪_n` with invertible `𝒪_n`-modules `ℋ^n` and
`M = ⨁ ℋ^n[-n]` — clause (2) — if and only if there is an open covering `X = ⋃ U_i` and integers
`n_i` such that `M|_{U_i}` is represented by an invertible `𝒪_{U_i}`-module placed in degree
`n_i` — clause (3).
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasInvertibleModuleDecomposition_iff_hasLocalInvertibleDegree
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (Mod X.sheaf)] (M : DerivedModules X.sheaf)
    (hloc : ∀ x : X.carrier, IsLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    HasInvertibleModuleDecomposition X M ↔ HasLocalInvertibleDegree M
declarations.comment: if every stalk of 𝒪_X is a local ring, clauses (2) and (3) are equivalent

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InvertibleDerived.isInvertibleObject_of_hasInvertibleModuleDecomposition_unconditional
declarations.doc:
If `M` admits a locally finite invertible module decomposition, then `M` is an invertible
object of `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isInvertibleObject_of_hasInvertibleModuleDecomposition_unconditional
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (Mod X.sheaf)] (M : DerivedModules X.sheaf)
    (hM : HasInvertibleModuleDecomposition X M) :
    IsInvertibleObject M
declarations.comment: clause (2) implies clause (1): a locally finite invertible module decomposition of M makes M an invertible object of D(𝒪_X) for the derived tensor product of Stacks 0FPB

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InvertibleDerived.HasInvertibleModuleDecomposition
declarations.doc:
**Clause (2) of Stacks 0FPG.** There is a locally finite direct product decomposition
`𝒪_X = ∏_{n ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_n` of the structure sheaf and for each `n` an invertible `𝒪_n`-module
`ℋ^n` such that `M = ⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} ℋ^n[-n]` in `D(𝒪_X)`, the `n`-th summand being `ℋ^n` viewed
as an `𝒪_X`-module and placed in degree `n`.
declarations.statement: public def HasInvertibleModuleDecomposition (M : DerivedModules X.sheaf) : Prop
declarations.comment: clause (2) as a condition on M: that there is a locally finite direct product decomposition 𝒪_X = ∏_{n ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_n and for each n an invertible 𝒪_n-module ℋ^n, in the sense of Stacks 01CS, with M = ⨁ ℋ^n[-n] in D(𝒪_X). This is the clause, not an implication between clauses; the decomposition itself is `ProductDecomposition`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InvertibleDerived.isPerfect_of_hasInvertibleModuleDecomposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPG, the perfectness conclusion.** Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space and let `M`
be an object of `D(𝒪_X)`. If there is a locally finite direct product decomposition
`𝒪_X = ∏_{n ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_n` and for each `n` an invertible `𝒪_n`-module `ℋ^n` with
`M = ⨁ ℋ^n[-n]` in `D(𝒪_X)`, then `M` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`.

Near a point only finitely many factors survive, each `ℋ^n` is locally a direct summand of a
finite free `𝒪_n`-module and `𝒪_n` is a direct summand of `𝒪_X`, so the complex with `ℋ^n` in
degree `n` and zero differentials — which represents `⨁ ℋ^n[-n]` — is locally strictly
perfect.
declarations.comment: clause (2) implies that M is a perfect object of D(𝒪_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InvertibleDerived.IsInvertibleObject
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of Stacks 0FPG.** `M` is an invertible object of `D(𝒪_X)`: there is an object
`N` of `D(𝒪_X)` with `M ⊗^L N ≅ 𝒪_X` and `N ⊗^L M ≅ 𝒪_X`, the tensor product being the derived
tensor product and `𝒪_X` the structure sheaf in degree zero.
declarations.statement: public def IsInvertibleObject (M : DerivedModules X.sheaf) : Prop
declarations.comment: clause (1) as a condition on M: that M is invertible in D(𝒪_X) in the sense of Stacks 0FFN, for the derived tensor product of Stacks 0FPB. This is the clause, not an implication between clauses

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InvertibleDerived.HasLocalInvertibleDegree
declarations.doc:
**Clause (3) of Stacks 0FPG.** `M` is represented by a complex which, on each member of
some open covering of `X`, is quasi-isomorphic to an invertible module placed in a single
degree — the degree being allowed to vary with the member of the covering.
declarations.statement: public def HasLocalInvertibleDegree (M : DerivedModules X.sheaf) : Prop
declarations.comment: clause (3) as a condition on M: that there is an open covering X = ⋃ U_i and for each i an integer n_i with M|_{U_i} represented by an invertible 𝒪_{U_i}-module placed in degree n_i. The source's condition that every stalk 𝒪_{X,x} is a local ring belongs to the equivalence of (3) with the other clauses, which is hasInvertibleModuleDecomposition_iff_hasLocalInvertibleDegree

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.OfToposHom.derivedPullback_toTensor_square
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPH, for a morphism of ringed topoi.**  For a morphism of ringed topoi
`f : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` — a morphism of the underlying topoi together with the
structure map — and cochain complexes `K`, `M` of `O_D`-modules, the square formed by the
canonical maps from the derived tensor product to the ordinary total tensor complex, the
comparison `Lf^*(K ⊗^L_{O_D} M) ≅ Lf^*K ⊗^L_{O_C} Lf^*M` of Stacks 07A4 followed by the
comparison `Lf^* ⟶ f^*` in each tensor factor, and that same comparison at `Tot(K ⊗ M)`
followed by the identification `f^*Tot(K ⊗_{O_D} M) ≅ Tot(f^*K ⊗_{O_C} f^*M)` of Stacks 03EL,
commutes.

The statement has no hypothesis and no class argument of its own: instance search supplies
every class argument of `derivedPullback_toTensor_square_of_instances`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPullback_toTensor_square {X Y : RingedTopos.{u, u, u}}
    (f : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom X Y)
    (K M : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) ℤ) :
    (derivedPullback f).map
          ((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct Y.O).toTensor K M) ≫
        pullbackComparisonQ f
            (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.tensorComplex Y.O).obj K).obj M) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (pullbackTensorComplexIso f K M).hom =
      (derivedPullbackTensorIso f).hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K, DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) ≫
        bifunctorMap (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X.O).tensor
            (pullbackComparisonQ f K) (pullbackComparisonQ f M) ≫
        (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X.O).toTensor
          ((pullbackComplex f).obj K) ((pullbackComplex f).obj M)
declarations.comment: for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi in the two-field sense of Tag 01D3, part (2) (a morphism of the underlying topoi with its structure map, no functor between the underlying sites and no morphism-of-sites hypothesis), at RingedTopos.{u, u, u}, for all complexes K, M; the statement carries no hypothesis or class argument

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.derivedPullback_toTensor_square_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPH.** For a morphism of ringed topoi `f : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` and cochain
complexes `K`, `M` of `O_D`-modules, the square formed by the canonical maps from the derived
tensor product to the ordinary total tensor complex, the comparison
`Lf^*(K ⊗^L_{O_D} M) ⟶ Lf^*K ⊗^L_{O_C} Lf^*M` of Stacks 07A4 followed by the derived-to-degreewise
pullback comparison in each tensor factor, and that same comparison followed by the
identification `f^*Tot(K ⊗_{O_D} M) ≅ Tot(f^*K ⊗_{O_C} f^*M)`, commutes.

The complexes are arbitrary and the only inputs are `f` and `hmos`. `hmos` is not a hypothesis
beyond the source's: it is this development's encoding of "`f` is a morphism of ringed topoi".
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom` presents the geometric morphism by a functor `f.u` between
the underlying sites and asks only that it be *continuous*; exactness of `f^{-1}` is not a field
of it, and along a merely continuous functor the inverse image need not be exact, so such an `f`
need not present a morphism of topoi at all. `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMorphismOfSites` is
continuity together with that exactness — it is Stacks 00X1 — and it is exactly what
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom.toToposHom` consumes to produce the underlying morphism of
topoi.

The existence of `Lf^*` is not assumed: it is `hasLeftDerivedFunctor_pullbackOnHomotopy`, the
existence assertion of Stacks 06YY, which holds along every morphism of ringed topoi.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPullback_toTensor_square_unconditional
    (K M : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) ℤ) :
    haveI := hasLeftDerivedFunctor_pullbackOnHomotopy f hmos
    (derivedPullback f).map
          ((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct Y.O).toTensor K M) ≫
        pullbackComparisonQ f
            (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.tensorComplex Y.O).obj K).obj M) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (pullbackTensorComplexIso f hmos K M).hom =
      derivedPullbackTensorComparison f hmos (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) ≫
        bifunctorMap (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X.O).tensor
            (pullbackComparisonQ f K) (pullbackComparisonQ f M) ≫
        (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X.O).toTensor
          ((pullbackComplex f).obj K) ((pullbackComplex f).obj M)
declarations.comment:
for a morphism of ringed topoi presented by a morphism of the underlying sites,
at RingedTopos.{u, u, u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedAdjunction_counit_fac
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPI for a morphism of ringed topoi.**  For a complex `𝒦` of `𝒪`-modules the square

```
Lf^* f_* 𝒦 ⟶ f^* f_* 𝒦
    ↓               ↓
Lf^* Rf_* 𝒦 ⟶       𝒦
```

commutes in `D(𝒪)`: its upper edge is the comparison `Lf^* ⟶ f^*` of Stacks 06YY at `f_*𝒦`, its
left edge is `Lf^*` applied to the comparison `f_* ⟶ Rf_*`, its lower edge is the counit of the
derived adjunction `Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` of Stacks 07A6 at `Rf_*𝒦`, and its right edge is the ordinary
counit `f^*f_*𝒦 ⟶ 𝒦` of Stacks 03D7.

The derived counit is by construction the one induced by the ordinary one, which is exactly this
commutativity, so the proof is
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforward.derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunction_counit_fac` at the
datum `kFlatLeftDerivedPullback`.

The square is stated for an object of the unbounded homotopy category rather than for a cochain
complex, which is the form the comparison maps of the two derived functors take and is more
general: a complex gives such an object through `HomotopyCategory.quotient`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedAdjunction_counit_fac (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (K : HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) :
    (derivedPullback f).map
        (((pushforwardOnHomotopy (X := X) (Y := Y) f).totalRightDerivedUnit DerivedCategory.Qh
          (sourceQuasiIso X)).app K) ≫
        (derivedAdjunction f).counit.app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj K) =
      (derivedPullbackComparison f).app ((pushforwardMapHomotopy f).obj K) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Qh.map ((pullbackAdjPushforwardMapHomotopy f).counit.app K)
declarations.comment:
for a morphism of ringed topoi in the two-field sense of Tag 01D3, part (2) --
a morphism of the underlying topoi together with the structure map, with no continuous functor
between the underlying sites -- and with no hypothesis beyond those making the two categories of
modules exist; stated at an object of the unbounded homotopy category, which a complex gives
through `HomotopyCategory.quotient`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOnRingedTopoi.derivedAdjunction_counit_fac
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPI.**  For a complex `K` of `𝒪_C`-modules the square

```
Lf^* f_* K ⟶ f^* f_* K
    ↓              ↓
Lf^* Rf_* K ⟶      K
```

commutes in `D(𝒪_C)`: its upper edge is the comparison `Lf^* ⟶ f^*`, its left edge is `Lf^*`
applied to the comparison `f_* ⟶ Rf_*`, its lower edge is the counit of the derived adjunction
`Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*`, and its right edge is the ordinary counit `f^* f_* ⟶ id`.

The derived counit is the one induced by the ordinary counit, which is exactly this
commutativity, so the proof is `derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfKFlat_counit_fac`.

The source's hypothesis is just that `f` be a morphism of ringed topoi, and `hmos` is how that is
spelled here, not an extra condition: `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom` records only the
continuity of `f.u`, while `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMorphismOfSites` is the library's encoding
of Stacks 00X1 — continuity together with exactness of `f^{-1}` — and by Stacks 00XC
(`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMorphismOfSites.morphismOfTopoi`) it is exactly `hmos` that makes the
geometric datum of `f` a morphism of topoi.  See the implementation notes above for the
presentation restriction, which is the repository's convention for ringed topoi and is separate
from `hmos`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedAdjunction_counit_fac
    (K : HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) :
    (derivedPullback f).map ((derivedPushforwardUnit f).app K) ≫
        (derivedAdjunction f hmos).counit.app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj K) =
      (derivedPullbackComparison f).app
          ((f.pushforwardTopos.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Qh.map
          ((homotopyPullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CupProductAndDerivedPushforward.naiveCupProduct_relativeCupProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPK, site-presented.**  For a morphism of ringed topoi
`f : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` presented by a morphism of sites and
unbounded cochain complexes `K`, `M` of `O_C`-modules, the hexagon

```
f_*K ⊗^L_{O_D} f_*M ───────────→ Rf_*K ⊗^L_{O_D} Rf_*M
        │                                 │
        ↓                                 ↓
Tot(f_*K ⊗_{O_D} f_*M)            Rf_*(K ⊗^L_{O_C} M)
        │                                 │
        ↓                                 ↓
f_*Tot(K ⊗_{O_C} M) ───────────→ Rf_*Tot(K ⊗_{O_C} M)
```

commutes in `D(O_D)`.  Its horizontal edges and its top right edge are the comparison
`f_* ⟶ Rf_*`; the top left and bottom right edges are the canonical map from the derived tensor
product to the ordinary total tensor complex of Stacks 06YU; the middle left edge is the naive
cup product and the middle right edge is the relative cup product of Stacks 0B6C.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCupProduct_relativeCupProduct
    (K M : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ) :
    (canonicalDerivedTensorProduct Y.O).toTensor ((pushforwardComplex f).obj K)
          ((pushforwardComplex f).obj M) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (naiveCupProduct f hmos K M) ≫
        pushforwardComparisonQ f (HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor K M
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.O) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) =
      bifunctorMap (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.O) (pushforwardComparisonQ f K)
            (pushforwardComparisonQ f M) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f hmos (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) ≫
        (derivedPushforward f).map ((canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X.O).toTensor K M)
declarations.comment:
variant: the special case of a morphism of ringed topoi presented by a morphism of
sites; the tag for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi is
Stacks.Cohomology.CupProductAndDerivedPushforwardOfToposHom.naiveCupProduct_relativeCupProduct

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CupProductAndDerivedPushforwardOfToposHom.naiveCupProduct_relativeCupProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPK.**  For a morphism of ringed topoi `f : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` — a
morphism of the underlying topoi together with the structure map, with no functor between the
underlying sites — and unbounded cochain complexes `K`, `M` of `O_C`-modules, the hexagon

```
f_*K ⊗^L_{O_D} f_*M ───────────→ Rf_*K ⊗^L_{O_D} Rf_*M
        │                                 │
        ↓                                 ↓
Tot(f_*K ⊗_{O_D} f_*M)            Rf_*(K ⊗^L_{O_C} M)
        │                                 │
        ↓                                 ↓
f_*Tot(K ⊗_{O_C} M) ───────────→ Rf_*Tot(K ⊗_{O_C} M)
```

commutes in `D(O_D)`.  Its horizontal edges and its top right edge are the comparison
`f_* ⟶ Rf_*`; the top left and bottom right edges are the canonical map from the derived tensor
product to the ordinary total tensor complex of Stacks 06YU; the middle left edge is the naive
cup product and the middle right edge is the relative cup product of Stacks 0B6C.

The statement has no hypothesis and no class argument of its own: instance search supplies
every class argument of `naiveCupProduct_relativeCupProduct_of_instances`.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCupProduct_relativeCupProduct {X Y : RingedTopos.{u, u, u}} (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (K M : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ) :
    (canonicalDerivedTensorProduct Y.O).toTensor ((pushforwardComplex f).obj K)
          ((pushforwardComplex f).obj M) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (naiveCupProduct f K M) ≫
        pushforwardComparisonQ f (HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor K M
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} X.O) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) =
      bifunctorMap (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.O) (pushforwardComparisonQ f K)
            (pushforwardComparisonQ f M) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) ≫
        (derivedPushforward f).map ((canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X.O).toTensor K M)
declarations.comment: the whole tag, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi in the two-field sense of Tag 01D3, part (2) (a morphism of the underlying topoi with its structure map, no functor between the underlying sites and no morphism-of-sites hypothesis), at RingedTopos.{u, u, u}, for all unbounded complexes K, M; the statement carries no hypothesis or class argument

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeCupProductOfToposHom.relativeCupProduct_assoc
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FPL].**  The relative cup product of [Stacks, Tag 0B6C] is associative.  Let
`f : (Sh(C), 𝒪) ⟶ (Sh(C'), 𝒪')` be a morphism of ringed topoi: a morphism of the underlying
topoi together with the structure map.  Then for **all** `K`, `L`, `M` in `D(𝒪)` the square

```
(Rf_*K ⊗' Rf_*L) ⊗' Rf_*M --→ Rf_*(K ⊗ L) ⊗' Rf_*M --→ Rf_*((K ⊗ L) ⊗ M)
          |                                                     |
          | a                                                   | Rf_*a
          ↓                                                     ↓
Rf_*K ⊗' (Rf_*L ⊗' Rf_*M) --→ Rf_*K ⊗' Rf_*(L ⊗ M) --→ Rf_*(K ⊗ (L ⊗ M))
```

commutes in `D(𝒪')`.  The four unlabelled arrows are relative cup products in one or the other
tensor factor; the two edges `a` are the associativity constraints `derivedAssociator` of
`⊗^L_{𝒪'}` and `⊗^L_𝒪`, the associators of the monoidal structures of [Stacks, Tag 0FPT] whose
tensor product is the derived tensor product of [Stacks, Tag 06YU] on the nose; they appear
because the source draws its square with `⊗^L` strictly associative.

The statement has no hypothesis and no class argument of its own.  The associativity law of the
comparison of [Stacks, Tag 07A4] that the source's proof uses silently is
`pullbackTensorComparisonAssociative`, proved above.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_assoc {X Y : RingedTopos.{u, u, u}} (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (K L M : DerivedModules X.O) :
    (uncurriedDerivedTensor Y).map
          (relativeCupProduct f K L ×ₘ 𝟙 ((derivedPushforward f).obj M)) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f ((uncurriedDerivedTensor X).obj (K, L)) M ≫
          (derivedPushforward f).map (derivedAssociator X K L M).hom =
      (derivedAssociator Y ((derivedPushforward f).obj K) ((derivedPushforward f).obj L)
            ((derivedPushforward f).obj M)).hom ≫
        (uncurriedDerivedTensor Y).map
            (𝟙 ((derivedPushforward f).obj K) ×ₘ relativeCupProduct f L M) ≫
          relativeCupProduct f K ((uncurriedDerivedTensor X).obj (L, M))
declarations.comment: the whole tag, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi in the two-field sense of Tag 01D3, part (2) (a morphism of the underlying topoi with its structure map, no functor between the underlying sites and no morphism-of-sites hypothesis), at RingedTopos.{u, u, u}, for all K, L, M in D(𝒪); the edges a are the associativity constraints derivedAssociator of Tag 0FPT and the statement has no hypothesis or class argument; the associativity law of the comparison of Tag 07A4, which the source's proof uses silently, is pullbackTensorComparisonAssociative

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeCupProductOfToposHom.relativeCupProduct_braiding
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FPM].** The relative cup product of [Stacks, Tag 0B6C] is commutative. Let
`f : (Sh(C), 𝒪) ⟶ (Sh(C'), 𝒪')` be a morphism of ringed topoi: a morphism of the underlying
topoi together with the structure map. Then for **all** `K, L` in `D(𝒪)` the square

```
Rf_*K ⊗^L_{𝒪'} Rf_*L --cup--→ Rf_*(K ⊗^L_𝒪 L)
        | ψ                          | Rf_*ψ
        ↓                            ↓
Rf_*L ⊗^L_{𝒪'} Rf_*K --cup--→ Rf_*(L ⊗^L_𝒪 K)
```

commutes in `D(𝒪')`. The horizontal arrows are the relative cup product. The left edge is `ψ` at
`(Rf_*K, Rf_*L)` and the right edge is `Rf_*` applied to `ψ` at `(K, L)`, as the source draws
them. `ψ` is the commutativity constraint of [Stacks, Tag 0FPT] on each of the two derived
categories.

The statement has no hypothesis and no class argument of its own.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_braiding {X Y : RingedTopos.{u, u, u}} (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    relativeCupProduct f K L ≫ (derivedPushforward f).map (canonicalBraidingHom X.O K L) =
      canonicalBraidingHom Y.O ((derivedPushforward f).obj K) ((derivedPushforward f).obj L) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f L K
declarations.comment: the whole tag, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi in the two-field sense of Tag 01D3, part (2) (a morphism of the underlying topoi with its structure map, no functor between the underlying sites and no morphism-of-sites hypothesis), at RingedTopos.{u, u, u}, for all K, L in D(𝒪); ψ on both edges is the commutativity constraint of Tag 0FPT and the statement carries no hypothesis or class argument

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeCupProductOfToposHom.relativeCupProduct_comp_pushforwardCompIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FPN].**  Let `f : (Sh(C), 𝒪) ⟶ (Sh(C'), 𝒪')` and
`f' : (Sh(C'), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(C''), 𝒪'')` be morphisms of ringed topoi.  The relative cup product of
[Stacks, Tag 0B6C] is compatible with composition: for all `K`, `L` in `D(𝒪)` the diagram

```
R(f'f)_*K ⊗'' R(f'f)_*L --c⊗c--→ Rf'_*Rf_*K ⊗'' Rf'_*Rf_*L
        |                                   |
        ↓ cup for f'∘f                      ↓ cup for f'
R(f'f)_*(K ⊗ L) --c--→ Rf'_*Rf_*(K ⊗ L) ←--Rf'_*(cup for f)-- Rf'_*(Rf_*K ⊗' Rf_*L)
```

commutes in `D(𝒪'')`.  The left edge is the relative cup product of the composite `f' ∘ f`; the
two edges `c` the source draws as equalities `R(f' ∘ f)_* = Rf'_*Rf_*` are the components of the
composition isomorphism `derivedPushforwardCompIsoOfAdjoints`, the conjugate of the isomorphism of
[Stacks, Tag 0D6D] (`conjugateEquiv_derivedPullbackCompIso_hom`).

There is no hypothesis beyond the two morphisms of ringed topoi and the ambient instances making
the derived categories and derived tensor products exist.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_comp_pushforwardCompIso (K L : DerivedModules X.O) :
    relativeCupProduct (RingedToposHom.comp (X := X) f' f) K L ≫
        (derivedPushforwardCompIsoOfAdjoints f f').inv.app
          ((uncurriedDerivedTensor X).obj (K, L)) =
      (uncurriedDerivedTensor Z).map
          ((derivedPushforwardCompIsoOfAdjoints f f').inv.app K ×ₘ
            (derivedPushforwardCompIsoOfAdjoints f f').inv.app L) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f' ((derivedPushforward f).obj K) ((derivedPushforward f).obj L) ≫
          (derivedPushforward f').map (relativeCupProduct f K L)
declarations.comment: for morphisms of ringed topoi in the two-field sense of Tag 01D3, part (2) -- morphisms of the underlying topoi together with the structure maps, with no continuous functor between the underlying sites and no morphism-of-sites hypothesis; the left edge is the relative cup product of Tag 0B6C for f' ∘ f and the two equality edges of the source are the components of the composition isomorphism of derived pushforward, the conjugate of the Tag 0D6D isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeCupProductOnRingedTopoi.relativeCupProduct_comp_pushforwardCompIso
declarations.doc:
For
`f : (Sh(C), 𝒪) ⟶ (Sh(C'), 𝒪')`, `f' : (Sh(C'), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(C''), 𝒪'')` and `K`, `L` in `D(𝒪)`
the diagram

```
R(f'f)_*K ⊗'' R(f'f)_*L --c⊗c--→ Rf'_*Rf_*K ⊗'' Rf'_*Rf_*L
        |                                   |
        ↓ cup for f'∘f                      ↓ cup for f'
R(f'f)_*(K ⊗ L) --c--→ Rf'_*Rf_*(K ⊗ L) ←--Rf'_*(cup for f)-- Rf'_*(Rf_*K ⊗' Rf_*L)
```

commutes in `D(𝒪'')`. The left-hand vertical arrow is the relative cup product for the composite
morphism `f' ∘ f` itself, and the two horizontal edges `c` are the components of the composition
isomorphism `derivedPushforwardCompIso`.

The proof transports `relativeCupProduct_comp`, the same square for the composite adjunction
`Rf_* ⋙ Rf'_*` with the composite of the two comparisons of [Stacks, Tag 07A4], along the
composition isomorphism, using the compatibility of the comparison of [Stacks, Tag 07A4] with
composition, `Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.derivedPullbackTensorIso_hom_app_comp`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_comp_pushforwardCompIso (K L : DerivedModules X.O) :
    relativeCupProduct (f'.comp f)
          (RingedToposSiteHom.isMorphismOfSites_comp_u f f' hmosf hmosf') K L ≫
        (derivedPushforwardCompIso f f' hmosf hmosf').inv.app
          ((uncurriedDerivedTensor X).obj (K, L)) =
      (uncurriedDerivedTensor Z).map
          ((derivedPushforwardCompIso f f' hmosf hmosf').inv.app K ×ₘ
            (derivedPushforwardCompIso f f' hmosf hmosf').inv.app L) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f' hmosf' ((derivedPushforward f).obj K)
              ((derivedPushforward f).obj L) ≫
          (derivedPushforward f').map (relativeCupProduct f hmosf K L)
declarations.comment: the square at the composite morphism itself, with no carried input: the left edge is the relative cup product of Tag 0B6C for f' ∘ f and the two equality edges of the source are the components of the composition isomorphism of derived pushforward, the conjugate of the Tag 0D6D isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MonoidalComplexesOfModules.symmetricMonoidalComplexes
declarations.doc:
Complexes of modules on any ringed site form a symmetric monoidal category; its tensor
bifunctor is totalized sheaf tensor.
declarations.statement: public def symmetricMonoidalComplexes : SymmetricMonoidalComplexes R

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Strict.isLeftDual_dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect
declarations.doc:
