**[Stacks, Tag 0FPR].** Let `(C, 𝒪)` be a ringed site and let `ℱ^•` be a complex of
`𝒪`-modules such that for every object `U` of `C` there exists a covering `{U_i → U}` with
`ℱ^•|_{U_i}` strictly perfect. Let `𝒢^• = SheafHom^•(ℱ^•, 𝒪)`, with degree-`j` term
`SheafHom(ℱ^{-j}, 𝒪)`. Then there is a left dual structure `(𝒢^•, η, ε)` on `ℱ^•` in the
monoidal category of complexes of `𝒪`-modules of [Stacks, Tag 0FPQ] — both triangle identities
of [Stacks, Tag 0FFP] hold — whose coevaluation is `η = ∑ ηₙ` and whose evaluation is
`ε = ∑ εₙ`: the degree-zero component of `η` on the summand `ℱ^n ⊗ 𝒢^{-n}` is the coevaluation
`ηₙ`, and the degree-zero component of `ε` on the summand `𝒢^{-n} ⊗ ℱ^n` is the evaluation `εₙ`,
of [Stacks, Tag 0FNY] at the term `ℱ^n`. Both `η` and `ε` are concentrated in degree zero, and
the degree-zero parts of `ℱ^• ⊗ 𝒢^•` and `𝒢^• ⊗ ℱ^•` are the coproducts of these summands, so
these components determine them.

The structure is `exactPairingDualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeftDual_dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect (hK : IsLocallyStrictlyPerfect R K) :
    letI : MonoidalCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R)) :=
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.Strict.monoidalCategory R.obj
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R).property
    letI : MonoidalPreadditive (Mod R) := monoidalPreadditiveRingSheaf R
    letI : ∀ X₁ : Mod R, PreservesColimit (Functor.empty.{0} (Mod R))
        ((curriedTensor (Mod R)).obj X₁) := fun X₁ => preservesColimit_tensorLeft R _ X₁
    letI : ∀ X₂ : Mod R, PreservesColimit (Functor.empty.{0} (Mod R))
        ((curriedTensor (Mod R)).flip.obj X₂) := fun X₂ => preservesColimit_tensorRight R _ X₂
    letI : ∀ X₁ X₂ X₃ : GradedObject ℤ (Mod R),
        GradedObject.HasGoodTensor₁₂Tensor X₁ X₂ X₃ := hasGoodTensor₁₂Tensor R
    letI : ∀ X₁ X₂ X₃ : GradedObject ℤ (Mod R),
        GradedObject.HasGoodTensorTensor₂₃ X₁ X₂ X₃ := hasGoodTensorTensor₂₃ R
    letI : ∀ X₁ X₂ X₃ X₄ : GradedObject ℤ (Mod R),
        GradedObject.HasTensor₄ObjExt X₁ X₂ X₃ X₄ := hasTensor₄ObjExt R
    ∃ P : @ExactPairing _ _ (monoidalCategoryCochainComplex R) K
        (dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect R K hK),
      (∀ n : ℤ, (@ExactPairing.coevaluation' _ _ inferInstance K
          (dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect R K hK) P).f 0 ≫
          GradedObject.Monoidal.πTensorObj K.X (dualComplexX R K) n (-n) 0 (add_neg_cancel n) =
        ((HomologicalComplex.tensorUnitIso (Mod R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).inv 0 ≫
          GradedObject.Monoidal.tensorUnit₀.hom) ≫
          (dualComplexPairing R K
            (isLocallyDirectSummandOfFiniteFree_X_of_isLocallyStrictlyPerfect hK) n (-n)
            (add_neg_cancel n)).coevaluation') ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj (dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect R K hK) K
          (-n) n 0 (neg_add_cancel n) ≫
          (@ExactPairing.evaluation' _ _ inferInstance K
            (dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect R K hK) P).f 0 =
        (dualComplexPairing R K
            (isLocallyDirectSummandOfFiniteFree_X_of_isLocallyStrictlyPerfect hK) n (-n)
            (add_neg_cancel n)).evaluation' ≫ GradedObject.Monoidal.tensorUnit₀.inv ≫
          (HomologicalComplex.tensorUnitIso (Mod R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).hom 0)
declarations.comment: for a complex `ℱ^•` of 𝒪-modules such that every object of the site has a covering sieve on whose members `ℱ^•` is strictly perfect (Tag 08FL), the complex `𝒢^• = SheafHom^•(ℱ^•, 𝒪)` with η = ∑ ηₙ and ε = ∑ εₙ is a left dual of `ℱ^•` (Tag 0FFP) in the monoidal category of complexes of Tag 0FPQ. The left dual is an `ExactPairing`, so both triangle identities hold; η and ε are pinned down by their degree-zero components on the summands `ℱ^n ⊗ 𝒢^{-n}` and `𝒢^{-n} ⊗ ℱ^n`, which are the coevaluation ηₙ and the evaluation εₙ of Tag 0FNY at `ℱ^n`. The complex is `dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect`, with terms `SheafHom(ℱ^{-j}, 𝒪)` (`dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect_X`) and the signed-transpose differential of Tag 0FNK (`dualComplex_d`); the pairing itself is `exactPairingDualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect`. The converse is Tag 0FPS

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Strict.isLocallyStrictlyPerfect_and_isoDualComplex_of_exactPairing
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FPS]**. Let `(C, 𝒪)` be a ringed site and `ℱ^•` a complex of `𝒪`-modules with a
left dual `𝒢^•` in the monoidal category of complexes of `𝒪`-modules. Then every object of the site
has a covering on whose members `ℱ^•` is strictly perfect, and the left dual is the complex of
[Stacks, Tag 0FPR] together with its pairings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyStrictlyPerfect_and_isoDualComplex_of_exactPairing
    (p : @ExactPairing _ _ (monoidalCategoryCochainComplex R) K L) :
    letI := monoidalCategoryCochainComplex R
    letI := p
    letI := exactPairingDualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect
      (isLocallyStrictlyPerfect_of_exactPairing R K L p)
    IsLocallyStrictlyPerfect R K ∧
      ∃ e : L ≅ dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect R K
          (isLocallyStrictlyPerfect_of_exactPairing R K L p),
        η_ K L ≫ K ◁ e.hom =
            η_ K (dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect R K
              (isLocallyStrictlyPerfect_of_exactPairing R K L p)) ∧
          e.hom ▷ K ≫ ε_ K (dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect R K
              (isLocallyStrictlyPerfect_of_exactPairing R K L p)) = ε_ K L
declarations.comment: the WHOLE tag, under the tag's OWN hypothesis that `ℱ^•` has a left dual `𝒢^•` in the monoidal category of complexes of 𝒪-modules of Tag 0FPQ, whose tensor product is the one of Tag 01CA. Both conclusions: every object of the site has a covering on whose members `ℱ^•` is strictly perfect in the sense of Tag 08FL — the witness `Stacks.SheafOfModules.Strict.IsLocallyStrictlyPerfect`, unfolding to the covering sieve and `IsStrictlyPerfect` of the restricted complex — and `𝒢^•` is the left dual of Example 0FPR with its pairings: it is isomorphic to `Stacks.SheafOfModules.Strict.dualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect`, the complex `SheafHom^•(ℱ^•, 𝒪)`, by an isomorphism matching the coevaluation and the evaluation of the given pairing with those of `Stacks.SheafOfModules.Strict.exactPairingDualComplexOfLocallyStrictlyPerfect`, the η = ∑ ηₙ and ε = ∑ εₙ of that example — which is uniqueness of left duals (Tag 0FFR)

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.DerivedTensorProduct.braidingIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FPT], the commutativity constraint.** The derived tensor product of two
objects of `D(𝒪)` is symmetric: `A ⊗^L_𝒪 B ≅ B ⊗^L_𝒪 A`.

Both objects are replaced by their chosen K-flat models, on which the derived tensor product is
the ordinary total tensor complex; there the isomorphism is the Koszul symmetry
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.tensorComplexFlipIso`.
declarations.statement:
def braidingIso (A B : DerivedModules X.O) :
    (T.tensor.obj A).obj B ≅ (T.tensor.obj B).obj A
declarations.comment: the commutativity constraint at a pair of objects, as an isomorphism; not the monoidal structure and not its coherence axioms

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.DerivedTensorProduct.rightUnitIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FPT], the unit constraint on the right.** The structure sheaf in degree zero
is a unit for the derived tensor product: `A ⊗^L_𝒪 𝒪 ≅ A`.

The right factor is already K-flat by `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isKFlat_single_unit`, so only the
left factor is replaced by its chosen K-flat model; on representatives the statement is the
ordinary unit law `Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorComplexUnitIso`.
declarations.statement:
def rightUnitIso (A : DerivedModules X.O) :
    (T.tensor.obj A).obj (unitObject X) ≅ A
declarations.comment: the unit constraint on the right at an object, as an isomorphism; not the monoidal structure and not its coherence axioms

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.DerivedTensorProduct.leftUnitIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FPT], the unit constraint on the left.** The structure sheaf in degree zero
is a unit for the derived tensor product on the other side too: `𝒪 ⊗^L_𝒪 A ≅ A`.

It is the right unit constraint read through the commutativity constraint.
declarations.statement:
def leftUnitIso (A : DerivedModules X.O) :
    (T.tensor.obj (unitObject X)).obj A ≅ A
declarations.comment: the unit constraint on the left at an object, as an isomorphism; not the monoidal structure and not its coherence axioms

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedMonoidal.symmetricMonoidalDerivedTensor
declarations.doc:
**The derived category of modules on a ringed site is a symmetric monoidal category with
tensor product the derived tensor product and the usual associativity and commutativity
constraints**, the latter being those of the total tensor product of complexes with the Koszul
sign convention.
declarations.statement: public def symmetricMonoidalDerivedTensor : SymmetricMonoidalDerivedTensor R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_self
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPU: the canonical map `K ⊗^𝐋_O K^∨ ⟶ R𝓗om_O(K, K)` is an isomorphism.**  For a
perfect object `K` of `D(O)` the canonical map of Stacks 08JD at `M = K` is invertible.

This is the assertion Stacks 0FPU cites, from [Stacks, Tag 08JJ], in order to define the
coevaluation; the source states it only at `M = K`, which is the case registered here.  The
general statement, for an arbitrary target and an arbitrary derived tensor product datum, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfect` of
`StacksFrontier.Topology.Sheaves.Cohomology.InternalHom.DerivedCompositionPerfect`, which is where
the mathematics is; nothing is re-proved here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_self
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K) :
    IsIso (derivedTensorDualToSheafHom X
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X) K K)
declarations.comment: tensor_hom_iso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.coevaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPU: the coevaluation of a perfect object.**  For a perfect object `K` of `D(O)`
with dual `K^∨ = R𝓗om_O(K, O)` the coevaluation is the morphism

`η : O ⟶ K ⊗^𝐋_O K^∨`

corresponding to `id_K` under the comparison `K ⊗^𝐋_O K^∨ ≅ R𝓗om_O(K, K)` of Stacks 08JD: the
section corresponding to `id_K` (`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedIdentitySection`, the class
of the identity under the two identifications of Stacks 08JA), followed by the inverse of that
comparison.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedDualCoevaluation`, which takes the invertibility of
the comparison as a hypothesis, with that hypothesis discharged for a perfect `K` by
`isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_self`.
declarations.statement:
def coevaluation
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K) :
    derivedStructureSheaf X ⟶
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).obj (derivedDual X K)
declarations.comment: coevaluation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.evaluation_coevaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPU, the triangle identity on the perfect object.**  For a perfect `K`, with the
coevaluation `η` and the evaluation `ε`,

`(η ▷ K) ≫ α ≫ (K ◁ ε) = λ ≫ ρ⁻¹`.

The chain is `(η ▷ K) ≫ α ≫ (K ◁ ε) ≫ ρ = ((η ≫ Φ) ▷ K) ≫ app = (ι ▷ K) ≫ app = λ`, whose
first step is (E1), whose middle step is `monoidalCoevaluation_comp` and whose last step is the
unit law (UL), `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomCounit_unit_law_monoidal`, at the
section corresponding to `id_K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem evaluation_coevaluation
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K) :
    monoidalCoevaluation X K hK ▷ K ≫ (α_ K (derivedDual X K) K).hom ≫
        K ◁ monoidalEvaluation X K = (λ_ K).hom ≫ (ρ_ K).inv
declarations.comment: left_dual

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedDualExactPairing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPU: the derived dual of a perfect object is a left dual.**  For a perfect object
`K` of `D(O)` the pair `(η, ε)` is an exact pairing — `K^∨ = R𝓗om_O(K, O)` is a left dual of `K`
in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 0FFP] — in the monoidal structure of [Stacks, Tag 0FPT] on `D(O)`.

Only the first triangle identity is checked: the second follows from it by
`CategoryTheory.ExactPairing.ofEvaluationCoevaluation`, because the evaluation detects
endomorphisms of `K^∨` (`eq_id_of_whiskerRight_comp_derivedDualEvaluation`), which is what the
closed structure of `D(O)` supplies.
declarations.statement:
def derivedDualExactPairing
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K) : ExactPairing K (derivedDual X K)
declarations.comment: left_dual

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.coevaluation_evaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPU, the triangle identity on the derived dual.**  For a perfect `K`,

`(K^∨ ◁ η) ≫ α⁻¹ ≫ (ε ▷ K^∨) = ρ ≫ λ⁻¹`.

This is the second clause of `derivedDualExactPairing`, which
`CategoryTheory.ExactPairing.ofEvaluationCoevaluation` derives from the first.
declarations.statement:
theorem coevaluation_evaluation
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K) :
    derivedDual X K ◁ monoidalCoevaluation X K hK ≫
        (α_ (derivedDual X K) K (derivedDual X K)).inv ≫
        monoidalEvaluation X K ▷ derivedDual X K =
      (ρ_ (derivedDual X K)).hom ≫ (λ_ (derivedDual X K)).inv
declarations.comment: left_dual

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_exactPairing_derivedDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPU: the derived dual of a perfect object is a left dual, on an arbitrary ringed
site.**  Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and `K` a perfect object of `D(O)`, with dual
`K^∨ = R𝓗om_O(K, O)`, coevaluation `η` (the section corresponding to `id_K` under
`K ⊗^𝐋_O K^∨ ≅ R𝓗om_O(K, K)`) and evaluation `ε`.  Then `(K^∨, η, ε)` is a left dual of `K`
in the monoidal category `D(O)` of [Stacks, Tag 0FPT], in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 0FFP]: there
is an exact pairing between `K` and `K^∨` whose coevaluation is `η` and whose evaluation is `ε`,
that is, both triangle identities hold for `η` and `ε`.

The only hypothesis is the perfectness of `K`.  The additivity of `⊗_O` in each variable, the
existence of the total tensor complexes, and sheafification of abelian sheaves on the site and
on its slices hold for every ringed site, and are discharged here; the pairing is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedDualExactPairing`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_exactPairing_derivedDual
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)))
    (hK : Y.IsPerfect K) :
    ∃ P : ExactPairing K (derivedDual Y K),
      P.coevaluation' = monoidalCoevaluation Y K hK ∧
        P.evaluation' = monoidalEvaluation Y K
declarations.comment: left_dual

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedDualEvaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPU: the evaluation map.** For an object `K` of `D(O)` with dual
`K^∨ = RSheafHom(K, O)` the evaluation is the morphism

`ε : K^∨ ⊗^L_O K ⟶ O`

matched with the identity of `K^∨` by the tensor–internal-Hom bijection of Stacks 08J8, under
which morphisms `K^∨ ⊗^L_O K ⟶ O` are morphisms `K^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(K, O) = K^∨`. No perfectness
hypothesis is needed: evaluation exists for every object of `D(O)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedDualEvaluation
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj (derivedDual X K)).obj K ⟶
      derivedStructureSheaf X
declarations.comment: evaluation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPerfect_and_isIso_derivedDualToLeftDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPV.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `M` be an object of `D(O)` with a left
dual `N` in the symmetric monoidal category `D(O)` of Stacks 0FPT. Then `M` is perfect, and the
left dual is the object `M^∨ = RSheafHom(M, O)` of Example 0FPU: the morphism `M^∨ ⟶ N` which the
pairing matches with the evaluation of Example 0FPU is an isomorphism, and it carries the
evaluation `ε` of the pairing to the evaluation `ε'` of Example 0FPU.

The first assertion is `isPerfect_of_exactPairing`, the second `isIso_derivedDualToLeftDual`
together with `whiskerRight_derivedDualToLeftDual`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_and_isIso_derivedDualToLeftDual
    (M N : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (pair : letI := derivedMonoidal X.O; ExactPairing M N) :
    X.IsPerfect M ∧
      (letI := derivedMonoidal X.O; letI := pair;
        IsIso (derivedDualToLeftDual M N) ∧
          derivedDualToLeftDual M N ▷ M ≫ ε_ M N = derivedDualEvaluationMonoidal M)
declarations.comment: both assertions: `M` is perfect, and the left dual `N` is the object `RSheafHom(M, O)` of Example 0FPU, by the morphism `derivedDualToLeftDual` which the pairing matches with the evaluation of Example 0FPU and which carries the evaluation of the pairing to that of Example 0FPU. The monoidal structure on `D(O)` is the one of Tag 0FPT, `Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedMonoidal.derivedMonoidal`, a left dual is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.ExactPairing` (Definition 0FFP), and perfect is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsPerfect` (Definition 08G5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedDualToLeftDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPV, second assertion: a left dual of `M` is the dual object of Example 0FPU.**
The morphism `M^∨ = RSheafHom(M, O) ⟶ N` which the exact pairing matches with the evaluation of
Example 0FPU is an isomorphism; its inverse is the morphism which the tensor–internal-Hom
bijection of Stacks 08J8 matches with the evaluation of the pairing.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_derivedDualToLeftDual : IsIso (derivedDualToLeftDual M N)
declarations.comment: the left dual is the object constructed in Example 0FPU, namely the derived dual `RSheafHom(M, O)` of Tag 08JD, and the identification is the morphism matched with the evaluation of Example 0FPU by the pairing; see `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.whiskerRight_derivedDualToLeftDual` for the compatibility of the two evaluations. The monoidal structure on `D(O)` is the one of Tag 0FPT, `Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedMonoidal.derivedMonoidal`, and a left dual is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.ExactPairing`, which is Definition 0FFP

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.finiteFreeSummandEquivalenceFiniteProjective
declarations.doc:
On a ringed site `(C, O)` with `R = Γ(C, O)`, the category of `O`-modules which are summands
of finite free modules is equivalent to the category of finite projective `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def finiteFreeSummandEquivalenceFiniteProjective :
    ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory X.IsDirectSummandOfFiniteFree ≌
      ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
        (fun M : ModuleCat.{max u w}
            (Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.GlobalSectionRing
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) =>
          Module.Finite
              (Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.GlobalSectionRing
                (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) M ∧
            Module.Projective
              (Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.GlobalSectionRing
                (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) M)
declarations.comment: the equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.finiteFreeSummandEquivalenceFiniteProjective_iso_globalSections
declarations.doc:
The equivalence `finiteFreeSummandEquivalenceFiniteProjective` is given by taking global
sections.
declarations.statement:
def finiteFreeSummandEquivalenceFiniteProjective_iso_globalSections :
    X.finiteFreeSummandEquivalenceFiniteProjective.functor ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _ ≅
      ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙
        Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.globalSectionsFunctor
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
declarations.comment: identification with global sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.InvertibleDerived.isPerfect_of_hasInvertibleModuleDecomposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPY, the perfectness conclusion.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `M` be an
object of `D(O)`. If there is a locally finite direct product decomposition
`O = ∏_{n ∈ ℤ} O_n` of the structure sheaf and for each `n` an invertible `O_n`-module `ℋ^n`
with `M = ⨁ ℋ^n[-n]` in `D(O)`, then `M` is a perfect object of `D(O)`.

On a covering of every object only finitely many factors survive, each `ℋ^n` is there a direct
summand of a finite free `O_n`-module and `O_n` is a direct summand of `O`, so the complex with
`ℋ^n` in degree `n` and zero differentials — which represents `⨁ ℋ^n[-n]` — is locally
strictly perfect.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_hasInvertibleModuleDecomposition (M : DerivedModules X.O)
    (hM : HasInvertibleModuleDecomposition X M) : X.IsPerfect M
declarations.comment: clause (2) implies that M is a perfect object of D(O)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.InvertibleDerived.IsInvertibleObject
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of Stacks 0FPY.** `M` is an invertible object of `D(O)`: there is an object `N`
of `D(O)` with `M ⊗^L N ≅ O` and `N ⊗^L M ≅ O`, the tensor product being the derived tensor
product of Stacks 0FPT and `O` the structure sheaf in degree zero.
declarations.statement: def IsInvertibleObject (M : DerivedModules X.O) : Prop
declarations.comment: clause (1) as a condition on M: that M is invertible in D(O) in the sense of Stacks 0FFN, for the symmetric monoidal structure of Stacks 0FPT. This is the clause, not an implication between clauses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.InvertibleDerived.HasLocalInvertibleDegree
declarations.doc:
**Clause (3) of Stacks 0FPY.** Every object `U` of the site has a covering `{U_i → U}` and
for each `i` an integer `n_i` such that `M|_{U_i}` is represented by an invertible
`O_{U_i}`-module placed in degree `n_i`: there are an invertible `O_{U_i}`-module `L` and an
isomorphism `M|_{U_i} ≅ L[-n_i]` in `D(O_{U_i})`.

`M|_{U_i}` is the image of `M` under the functor `D(O) ⥤ D(O_{U_i})` induced by the exact
restriction functor `Mod(O) ⥤ Mod(O_{U_i})`, and `L[-n_i]` is `L` placed in degree `n_i`. The
derived category `D(O_{U_i})` is read in its standard model `HasDerivedCategory.standard`; any
two models are equivalent compatibly with their localization functors, so the condition does not
depend on that reading.
declarations.statement: def HasLocalInvertibleDegree (M : DerivedModules X.O) : Prop
declarations.comment: clause (3) as a condition on M: that every object U of the site has a covering {U_i → U} and for each i an integer n_i with M|_{U_i} isomorphic in D(O_{U_i}) to an invertible O_{U_i}-module placed in degree n_i. This is the clause, not an implication between clauses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.InvertibleDerived.isInvertibleObject_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FPY.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `M` be an object of `D(O)`. The
following are equivalent:

1. `M` is invertible in `D(O)` (`IsInvertibleObject`: Stacks 0FFN for the derived tensor product
   of Stacks 0FPT);
2. there is a locally finite direct product decomposition `O = ∏_{n ∈ ℤ} O_n` and for each `n` an
   invertible `O_n`-module `ℋ^n` (Stacks 0409) with `M = ⨁ ℋ^n[-n]` in `D(O)`
   (`HasInvertibleModuleDecomposition`).

If they hold, `M` is a perfect object of `D(O)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsPerfect`,
Stacks 08G5). If `(C, O)` is a locally ringed site (Stacks 04EU) they are also equivalent to

3. for every object `U` of `C` there are a covering `{U_i → U}` and integers `n_i` such that
   `M|_{U_i}` is isomorphic in `D(O_{U_i})` to an invertible `O_{U_i}`-module placed in degree
   `n_i` (`HasLocalInvertibleDegree`).

`D(O)` is any model of the derived category. The ringed site has its objects, its morphisms and
its rings of sections in one universe; see the note of the `stacks` attribute.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertibleObject_tfae (M : DerivedCategory (Mod X.O)) :
    [IsInvertibleObject X M, HasInvertibleModuleDecomposition X M].TFAE ∧
      (IsInvertibleObject X M → X.IsPerfect M) ∧
      (IsLocallyRinged X →
        [IsInvertibleObject X M, HasInvertibleModuleDecomposition X M,
          HasLocalInvertibleDegree X M].TFAE)
declarations.comment: All of the tag: (1) ⟺ (2) on every ringed site; (1) implies that M is perfect; and (1) ⟺ (2) ⟺ (3) on a locally ringed site. The ringed site is RingedSite.{u, u, u} -- objects, morphisms and sections of O in one universe u. This is the library's one-universe convention for D(O) as a symmetric monoidal category: the derived tensor product of Stacks 0FPT on a ringed site (Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedMonoidal.derivedMonoidal) is built from the K-flat resolutions of Stacks 06YS, which the library constructs at that universe pattern only, so clause (1) has no meaning off it. The four HasSheafify / WEqualsLocallyBijective instance arguments are the library's standard ones, and Mathlib synthesizes all four for every RingedSite.{u, u, u}

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.leftRightEquivalence
declarations.doc:
Graded opposition is an equivalence from left differential graded `A`-modules to
right differential graded modules over the graded opposite algebra.
declarations.statement:

    (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, v} R) : OppositeEquivalence R A

declarations.name: ExternallyGradedRightModule.shift
declarations.doc: The shift `M[k]` of a graded right module, with `M[k]ⁿ = Mⁿ⁺ᵏ`.
declarations.statement:

    ExternallyGradedRightModule A
declarations.comment: right graded modules

declarations.name: ExternallyGradedLeftModule.shift
declarations.doc:
The shift `M[k]` of a graded left module.  A homogeneous element of degree `i`
acts with the Koszul factor `(-1)^(i*k)`.

declarations.name: CochainComplex.endomorphismDGA
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism differential graded algebra of a cochain complex of `R`-modules, with its
canonical identification of homogeneous pieces with cochains.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def endomorphismDGA (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) :
    EndomorphismDGA M
declarations.comment: endomorphism algebra

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.toEndomorphismHom_spec_surjective_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FQ3.** Giving a left differential graded `A`-module structure on a complex `M` is the
same thing as giving a homomorphism of differential graded `R`-algebras from `A` into the
endomorphism algebra `E = Hom^•(M, M)`. A structure is a left differential graded `A`-module `L`
with an identification `i` of its underlying complex with `M`; it corresponds to
`toEndomorphismHom A L M i`, and:

* this homomorphism sends a homogeneous `a ∈ A^n` to the cochain `M^p → M^{p + n}` which is
  multiplication by `a` transported through `i`, with no sign;
* every homomorphism `A ⟶ E` arises from some structure;
* two structures `(L, i)` and `(L', i')` give the same homomorphism if and only if they put the
  same multiplication `A^n × M^p → M^{p + n}` on `M`.

So the correspondence is a bijection between multiplications on `M` making it a left differential
graded `A`-module and homomorphisms `A ⟶ E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toEndomorphismHom_spec_surjective_eq_iff (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) :
    (∀ (L : LeftModule A) (i : toCochainComplex A L ≅ M) (n p : ℤ) (a : A.grading n)
        (x : L.grading p),
        ((endomorphismDGA M).cochainEquiv n
            ⟨(toEndomorphismHom A L M i).toAlgebraHom a,
              (toEndomorphismHom A L M i).map_grading n a a.property⟩).v p (p + n) rfl
            (i.hom.f p x) =
          i.hom.f (p + n)
            (⟨(a : A.A) • (x : L.M), by
              simpa only [add_comm] using
                L.smul_mem n p (a : A.A) (x : L.M) a.property x.property⟩ :
              L.grading (p + n))) ∧
    (∀ φ : A.Hom (endomorphismDGA M).algebra,
      ∃ (L : LeftModule A) (i : toCochainComplex A L ≅ M), toEndomorphismHom A L M i = φ) ∧
    (∀ (L : LeftModule A) (i : toCochainComplex A L ≅ M)
        (L' : LeftModule A) (i' : toCochainComplex A L' ≅ M),
      toEndomorphismHom A L M i = toEndomorphismHom A L' M i' ↔
        ∀ (n p : ℤ) (a : A.grading n) (y : M.X p),
          i.hom.f (p + n)
              (⟨(a : A.A) • (show L.grading p from i.inv.f p y).1, by
                simpa only [add_comm] using
                  L.smul_mem n p (a : A.A) _ a.property (show L.grading p from i.inv.f p y).2⟩ :
                L.grading (p + n)) =
            i'.hom.f (p + n)
              (⟨(a : A.A) • (show L'.grading p from i'.inv.f p y).1, by
                simpa only [add_comm] using
                  L'.smul_mem n p (a : A.A) _ a.property (show L'.grading p from i'.inv.f p y).2⟩ :
                L'.grading (p + n)))
declarations.comment: left module structures on a complex and algebra homomorphisms

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.rightTensorHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
For a right differential graded `A`-module `M'`, a left differential graded `A`-module `M` and
a complex `N` of `R`-modules, homomorphisms of right differential graded `A`-modules
`M' → Hom(M, N)` are the maps of complexes of `R`-modules `M' ⊗_A M → N`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def rightTensorHomEquiv :
    DifferentialGradedModule.Hom M' P ≃ (tensorComplex M' M ⟶ N)
declarations.comment: the identification

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.rightTensorHomEquiv_apply
declarations.doc: `rightTensorHomEquiv` sends `g` to the map of complexes taking `x ⊗ y` to `(g x)(y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rightTensorHomEquiv_apply (g : DifferentialGradedModule.Hom M' P)
    (p q n : ℤ) (h : p + q = n) (x : M'.grading p) (y : M.grading q) :
    ((rightTensorHomEquiv M' M N P iso hact g).f n).hom ((tensorTmul M' M).map p q n h x y) =
      (((iso.hom.f p) ⟨g.toFun x, g.map_grading p x x.property⟩).v q n (by omega)).hom y
declarations.comment: the identification on pure tensors

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.exists_rightTensorHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
There is a right differential graded `A`-module `P` with underlying complex `Hom(M, N)` such
that homomorphisms `M' → P` are in bijection with maps of complexes `M' ⊗_A M → N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_rightTensorHomEquiv :
    ∃ (P : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, u} A)
      (_ : P.toCochainComplex ≅ HomComplexR R (LeftModule.toCochainComplex A M) N),
      Nonempty (DifferentialGradedModule.Hom M' P ≃ (tensorComplex M' M ⟶ N))
declarations.comment: existence of the identification

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.existsUnique_isSignedAction
declarations.doc:
A right differential graded `A`-module whose underlying complex is identified with `M`
determines a unique homomorphism of differential graded algebras from `A` into the graded opposite
of the endomorphism algebra of `M`, namely the one satisfying the signed-action equation.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isSignedAction (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R)
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (L : DifferentialGradedModule A)
    (i : L.toCochainComplex ≅ M) :
    ∃! τ : A.Hom (oppEndAlgebra M), IsSignedAction A M L i τ
declarations.comment: module to homomorphism

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_rightModule_isSignedAction
declarations.doc:
Every homomorphism of differential graded algebras from `A` into the graded opposite of the
endomorphism algebra of `M` arises from a right differential graded `A`-module whose underlying
complex is `M`, with the action given by the signed-action equation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_rightModule_isSignedAction (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R)
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (τ : A.Hom (oppEndAlgebra M)) :
    ∃ (L : DifferentialGradedModule A) (i : L.toCochainComplex ≅ M), IsSignedAction A M L i τ
declarations.comment: homomorphism to module

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.leftTensorHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
For a right differential graded `A`-module `M`, a left differential graded `A`-module `M'` and
a complex `N` of `R`-modules, homomorphisms of left differential graded `A`-modules
`M' → Hom(M, N)` are the maps of complexes of `R`-modules `M ⊗_A M' → N`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def leftTensorHomEquiv :
    LeftModule.Hom M' H ≃ (tensorComplex M M' ⟶ N)
declarations.comment: the identification

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.leftTensorHomEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
`leftTensorHomEquiv` sends `g` to the map of complexes taking `x ⊗ y` to
`(-1)^{pq} (g y)(x)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem leftTensorHomEquiv_apply (g : LeftModule.Hom M' H)
    (p q n : ℤ) (h : p + q = n) (x : M.grading p) (y : M'.grading q) :
    ((leftTensorHomEquiv M M' N H iso hact g).f n).hom ((tensorTmul M M').map p q n h x y) =
      ((p * q).negOnePow : ℤ) •
        (((iso.hom.f q) ⟨g.toFun y, g.map_grading q y y.property⟩).v p n (by omega)).hom x
declarations.comment: the identification on pure tensors

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.exists_leftTensorHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
There is a left differential graded `A`-module `H` with underlying complex `Hom(M, N)` such
that homomorphisms `M' → H` are in bijection with maps of complexes `M ⊗_A M' → N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_leftTensorHomEquiv :
    ∃ (H : LeftModule A)
      (_ : LeftModule.toCochainComplex A H ≅ HomComplexR R M.toCochainComplex N),
      Nonempty (LeftModule.Hom M' H ≃ (tensorComplex M M' ⟶ N))
declarations.comment: existence of the identification

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.exists_homEvaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FQ7.** Let `A` be a differential graded `R`-algebra, `L` a left differential graded
`A`-module and `N` a complex of `R`-modules. Then there are a right differential graded
`A`-module `rightHom` with underlying complex `Hom^•(L, N)`, acting by precomposition with the
left action of `L`; a left differential graded `A`-module `doubleHom` with underlying complex
`Hom^•(Hom^•(L, N), N)`, acting by signed precomposition with the right action of `rightHom`; and
an evaluation map

`ev : L ⟶ doubleHom`

in the category of left differential graded `A`-modules, so in particular `ev (a • x) = a • ev x`
for every `a ∈ A`; on underlying complexes of `R`-modules `ev` is the evaluation map of
Tag 0FNM, read through the two identifications.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homEvaluation (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, v} R)
    (L : DifferentialGraded.LeftModule A) (N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) :
    ∃ (rightHom : DifferentialGradedModule A)
      (rightHomIso : rightHom.toCochainComplex ≅ HomComplexR R (toCochainComplex A L) N)
      (doubleHom : DifferentialGraded.LeftModule A)
      (doubleHomIso : toCochainComplex A doubleHom ≅ HomComplexR R rightHom.toCochainComplex N)
      (ev : DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.Hom L doubleHom),
      (∀ (p q : ℤ) (a : A.grading p) (f : rightHom.grading q),
        (rightHomIso.hom.f (q + p))
            (⟨MulOpposite.op (a : A.A) • (f : rightHom.M),
              rightHom.smul_mem q p (f : rightHom.M) (a : A.A) f.property a.property⟩ :
              rightHom.grading (q + p)) =
          ((leftAction A L (toCochainComplex A L) (Iso.refl _)).action p a).comp
            ((rightHomIso.hom.f q) f) (by omega)) ∧
      (∀ (p q r : ℤ) (a : A.grading p) (g : doubleHom.grading r) (f : rightHom.grading q),
        HEq
          ((((doubleHomIso.hom.f (p + r))
              (⟨(a : A.A) • (g : doubleHom.M),
                doubleHom.smul_mem p r (a : A.A) (g : doubleHom.M) a.property g.property⟩ :
                doubleHom.grading (p + r))).v q (q + (p + r)) (by omega)).hom f)
          ((p * (q + r)).negOnePow •
            (((doubleHomIso.hom.f r) g).v (q + p) (q + p + r) (by omega)).hom
              (⟨MulOpposite.op (a : A.A) • (f : rightHom.M),
                rightHom.smul_mem q p (f : rightHom.M) (a : A.A) f.property a.property⟩ :
                rightHom.grading (q + p)))) ∧
      (∀ (a : A.A) (x : L.M), ev.toFun (a • x) = a • ev.toFun x) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : L.grading n),
        (doubleHomIso.hom.f n)
            (⟨ev.toFun x, ev.map_grading n x x.property⟩ : doubleHom.grading n) =
          ((CochainComplex.HomComplex.evaluationToDoubleHom (toCochainComplex A L) N ≫
              Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R rightHom.toCochainComplex
                (HomComplexR R (toCochainComplex A L) N) N rightHomIso.hom).f n) x)
declarations.comment:
the LEFT-handed remark: `M` is a LEFT differential graded `A`-module (called `L`
here), `Hom(M, N)` is a RIGHT one (`rightHom`), `Hom(Hom(M, N), N)` is a LEFT one (`doubleHom`),
and `ev` is a map of LEFT differential graded `A`-modules — its type is
`DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.Hom L doubleHom`, whose `A`-linearity the third conjunct spells
out. The modules are asserted to exist rather than named, having no canonical presentation, so
each comes with an isomorphism of its underlying complex with the relevant Hom complex and with
the formula for its action; the last conjunct identifies `ev` on underlying complexes with
`CochainComplex.HomComplex.evaluationToDoubleHom`, which is 0FNM.

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.nonempty_homEvaluationData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FQ8.** For a right differential graded `A`-module `M` and a complex `N` of
`R`-modules, the Hom complex `Hom^•(M, N)` carries a left differential graded `A`-module structure,
its Hom complex into `N` carries a right one, and the canonical evaluation map of Tag 0FNM is a
homomorphism of right differential graded `A`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_homEvaluationData (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, v} R)
    (M : DifferentialGradedModule A) (N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) :
    Nonempty (HomEvaluationData A M N)
declarations.comment:
the RIGHT-handed remark: `M` is a RIGHT differential graded `A`-module,
`Hom(M, N)` is a LEFT one (`leftHom`), `Hom(Hom(M, N), N)` is a RIGHT one (`doubleHom`), and
`ev` is a map of RIGHT differential graded `A`-modules — its type is
`DifferentialGradedModule.Hom M doubleHom`. The data are asserted to exist rather than named,
the Hom modules having no canonical presentation; `evaluation_apply` pins `ev` to 0FNM.

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedAlgebra.LeftAction.shiftHomCochain_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FQ9**, left modules. If `M` is a left differential graded `A`-module then the
identification `Hom^•(M, N)[a - b] ≅ Hom^•(M[b], N[a])` of Tag 0FNN is a map of right differential
graded `A`-modules: both actions are precomposition, on the source with the given action — shifting
a right module introduces no sign — and on the target with the Koszul-signed shifted action
`DifferentialGradedAlgebra.LeftAction.shift`. Remark 22.26.9 is the case `a = 0`, `b = k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem LeftAction.shiftHomCochain_comp (act : A.LeftAction M) (a b p q : ℤ) (α : A.grading p)
    (z : Cochain M N q) :
    shiftHomCochain M N a b (p + q) ((act.action p α).comp z rfl) =
      ((act.shift b).action p α).comp (shiftHomCochain M N a b q z) (by omega)
declarations.comment: left modules

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedAlgebra.RightAction.shiftHomCochain_homAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FQ9**, right modules. If `M` is a right differential graded `A`-module then the
identification `Hom^•(M, N)[a - b] ≅ Hom^•(M[b], N[a])` of Tag 0FNN is a map of left differential
graded `A`-modules: the target carries the left action induced by the shifted right action on
`M[b]`, and the source carries the left action induced on `Hom^•(M, N)`, multiplied by the Koszul
factor `(-1)^(p (a - b))` of the shift by `a - b`. Remark 22.26.9 is the case `a = 0`, `b = k`,
where that factor is `(-1)^(p k)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem RightAction.shiftHomCochain_homAction (t : A.RightAction M) (a b p q : ℤ)
    (α : A.grading p) (z : Cochain M N q) :
    shiftHomCochain M N a b (p + q)
        ((p * (a - b)).negOnePow • (t.homLeftAction N).homAction p q (p + q) (by omega) α z) =
      ((t.shift b).homLeftAction (N⟦a⟧)).homAction p (q + (b - a)) (p + q + (b - a)) (by omega) α
        (shiftHomCochain M N a b q z)
declarations.comment: right modules

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.property_of_coproducts_of_two_out_of_three_of_shifts
declarations.doc:
*"Let `R` be a ring. Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded `R`-algebra.
Using P-resolutions we can sometimes reduce statements about general objects of `D(A, d)` to
statements about `A[k]`. Namely, let `T` be a property of objects of `D(A, d)` and assume that*

1. *if `Kᵢ`, `i ∈ I` is a family of objects of `D(A, d)` and `T(Kᵢ)` holds for all `i ∈ I`, then
   `T(⨁ Kᵢ)`,*
2. *if `K → L → M → K[1]` is a distinguished triangle of `D(A, d)` and `T` holds for two, then
   `T` holds for the third object, and*
3. *`T(A[k])` holds for all `k ∈ ℤ`.*

*Then `T` holds for all objects of `D(A, d)`."*

The object denoted `A` in the source is the image of the regular module `A` in `D(A, d)`, so
hypothesis (3) is `T` on each shift of that image. Hypothesis (2) is stated as the conjunction of
its three implications, one for each position of the triangle. Isomorphism invariance of `T` is
not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem property_of_coproducts_of_two_out_of_three_of_shifts
    (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R) (T : derivedCategory' A → Prop)
    (hsum : ∀ {ι : Type u} (K : ι → derivedCategory' A), (∀ i, T (K i)) → T (∐ K))
    (htriangle : ∀ Δ : Pretriangulated.Triangle (derivedCategory' A),
      Δ ∈ Pretriangulated.distinguishedTriangles →
      (T Δ.obj₁ → T Δ.obj₂ → T Δ.obj₃) ∧ (T Δ.obj₁ → T Δ.obj₃ → T Δ.obj₂) ∧
      (T Δ.obj₂ → T Δ.obj₃ → T Δ.obj₁))
    (hshift : ∀ k : ℤ, T (((toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj
      (regularModule A))⟦k⟧)) :
    ∀ K : derivedCategory' A, T K

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.General.property_of_coproducts_of_two_out_of_three_of_shifts
declarations.doc:
The dévissage with the carrier of the algebra in a universe of its own. *"Let `R` be
a ring. Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded `R`-algebra. Using P-resolutions we can sometimes
reduce statements about general objects of `D(A, d)` to statements about `A[k]`. Namely, let `T`
be a property of objects of `D(A, d)` and assume that*

1. *if `Kᵢ`, `i ∈ I` is a family of objects of `D(A, d)` and `T(Kᵢ)` holds for all `i ∈ I`, then
   `T(⨁ Kᵢ)`,*
2. *if `K → L → M → K[1]` is a distinguished triangle of `D(A, d)` and `T` holds for two, then
   `T` holds for the third object, and*
3. *`T(A[k])` holds for all `k ∈ ℤ`.*

*Then `T` holds for all objects of `D(A, d)`."*

This is `DifferentialGradedModule.property_of_coproducts_of_two_out_of_three_of_shifts` with the
universe of the base ring `R` and the universe of the carrier of `A` independent of one another.

The object denoted `A` in the source is the image of the regular module `A` in `D(A, d)`, so
hypothesis (3) is `T` on each shift of that image. Hypothesis (2) is stated as the conjunction of
its three implications, one for each position of the triangle. Isomorphism invariance of `T` is
not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem property_of_coproducts_of_two_out_of_three_of_shifts
    (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, v} R) (T : derivedCategory.{u, v, v} A → Prop)
    (hsum : ∀ {ι : Type v} (K : ι → derivedCategory.{u, v, v} A), (∀ i, T (K i)) → T (∐ K))
    (htriangle : ∀ Δ : Pretriangulated.Triangle (derivedCategory.{u, v, v} A),
      Δ ∈ Pretriangulated.distinguishedTriangles →
      (T Δ.obj₁ → T Δ.obj₂ → T Δ.obj₃) ∧ (T Δ.obj₁ → T Δ.obj₃ → T Δ.obj₂) ∧
      (T Δ.obj₂ → T Δ.obj₃ → T Δ.obj₁))
    (hshift : ∀ k : ℤ, T (((toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms A).Q).obj
      (regularModule A))⟦k⟧)) :
    ∀ K : derivedCategory.{u, v, v} A, T K
declarations.comment: algebra carrier universe independent of the base ring; cone-triangle structure

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.isTriangulated_onK
declarations.doc:
**A differential graded functor across two ringed sites commuting with the shift is exact on
the homotopy categories**, which is [Stacks, Tag 0FQF] in the generality the derived pullback
and the derived pushforward of a sheaf of differential graded modules need. The triangulated
structures are the ones of [Stacks, Tag 0FS7]: restriction of scalars to `ℤ` changes neither the
homotopy categories, nor their cones, nor their admissible short exact sequences, so the cone
situation here is the one that puts the triangulated structure on `K(Mod(A, d))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated_onK
    {F : DGCategory.DGFunctor (dgCategoryOverInt.{u, v, w} A) (dgCategoryOverInt.{u, v, w} B)}
    (hF : F.CommShiftB (coneSituationOverInt.{u, v, w} A).shift
      (coneSituationOverInt.{u, v, w} B).shift) :
    letI : Preadditive (dgCategoryOverInt.{u, v, w} A).K :=
      DGCategory.homotopyPreadditive _
    letI : HasZeroObject (dgCategoryOverInt.{u, v, w} A).K :=
      DGCategory.homotopyHasZeroObject _ (coneSituationOverInt.{u, v, w} A)
    letI : HasShift (dgCategoryOverInt.{u, v, w} A).K ℤ :=
      (coneSituationOverInt.{u, v, w} A).shift.kShift
    letI : ∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor (dgCategoryOverInt.{u, v, w} A).K n).Additive := fun n =>
      DGCategory.homotopyShiftAdditive _ (coneSituationOverInt.{u, v, w} A) n
    letI : Pretriangulated (dgCategoryOverInt.{u, v, w} A).K :=
      DGCategory.homotopyPretriangulated _ (coneSituationOverInt.{u, v, w} A)
    letI : Preadditive (dgCategoryOverInt.{u, v, w} B).K :=
      DGCategory.homotopyPreadditive _
    letI : HasZeroObject (dgCategoryOverInt.{u, v, w} B).K :=
      DGCategory.homotopyHasZeroObject _ (coneSituationOverInt.{u, v, w} B)
    letI : HasShift (dgCategoryOverInt.{u, v, w} B).K ℤ :=
      (coneSituationOverInt.{u, v, w} B).shift.kShift
    letI : ∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor (dgCategoryOverInt.{u, v, w} B).K n).Additive := fun n =>
      DGCategory.homotopyShiftAdditive _ (coneSituationOverInt.{u, v, w} B) n
    letI : Pretriangulated (dgCategoryOverInt.{u, v, w} B).K :=
      DGCategory.homotopyPretriangulated _ (coneSituationOverInt.{u, v, w} B)
    letI : F.onK.CommShift ℤ := commShift_onK A B hF
    F.onK.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the induced functor on homotopy categories is exact, across two ringed sites

declarations.name: DGCategory.DGFunctor.CommShiftB.isDistinguishedTriangle_mapTriangleK
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FQF.** The functor induced by `F` on homotopy categories carries the distinguished
triangles of `K(A)` to the distinguished triangles of `K(B)`, the third arrow of the image
triangle being formed with the comparison isomorphism `F(x[1]) = F(x)[1]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDistinguishedTriangle_mapTriangleK (CA : ConeSituation A) (CB : ConeSituation B)
    (hF : F.CommShiftB CA.shift CB.shift) :
    letI : HasShift A.K ℤ := CA.shift.kShift
    letI : HasShift B.K ℤ := CB.shift.kShift
    ∀ T : Pretriangulated.Triangle A.K, IsDistinguishedTriangle A CA T →
      IsDistinguishedTriangle B CB (hF.mapTriangleK.obj T)
declarations.comment: distinguished triangles are carried to distinguished triangles

declarations.name: DGCategory.DGFunctor.CommShiftK.commShift
declarations.doc: **Tag 0FQF.** The induced functor `K(A) ⥤ K(B)` commutes with the translation functors.
declarations.statement:
def commShift (hF : F.CommShiftK SA SB) :
    letI : HasShift A.K ℤ := SA.kShift
    letI : HasShift B.K ℤ := SB.kShift
    F.onK.CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment: the induced functor commutes with the translations

declarations.name: DGCategory.DGFunctor.CommShiftK.isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FQF.** A functor `F : A ⥤ B` of differential graded categories over `R` between
categories satisfying axioms (A), (B) and (C), which commutes with the shift, induces an exact
functor `K(A) ⥤ K(B)` of triangulated categories.

The commutation is asked for here as a `CommShiftK`, that is, together with the two coherences of
the comparison isomorphisms with the `ℤ`-action data of the translations. Under the source's
hypothesis `F(x[1]) = F(x)[1]` alone those two are
`DGCategory.DGFunctor.CommShiftK.ofCommShiftB` away, as soon as the translations of the homotopy
categories are strict; `DGCategory.DGFunctor.CommShiftB.isTriangulated` is that form.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated (CA : ConeSituation A) (CB : ConeSituation B)
    (hF : F.CommShiftK CA.shift CB.shift) :
    letI : Preadditive A.K := homotopyPreadditive A
    letI : HasZeroObject A.K := homotopyHasZeroObject A CA
    letI : HasShift A.K ℤ := CA.shift.kShift
    letI : ∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor A.K n).Additive := fun n => homotopyShiftAdditive A CA n
    letI : Pretriangulated A.K := homotopyPretriangulated A CA
    letI : Preadditive B.K := homotopyPreadditive B
    letI : HasZeroObject B.K := homotopyHasZeroObject B CB
    letI : HasShift B.K ℤ := CB.shift.kShift
    letI : ∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor B.K n).Additive := fun n => homotopyShiftAdditive B CB n
    letI : Pretriangulated B.K := homotopyPretriangulated B CB
    letI : F.onK.CommShift ℤ := hF.commShift
    F.onK.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the induced functor on homotopy categories is exact, from the translation coherences as data

declarations.name: DGCategory.DGFunctor.CommShiftB.isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FQF.** A functor `F : A ⥤ B` of differential graded categories over `R` between
categories satisfying axioms (A), (B) and (C) and such that `F(x[1]) = F(x)[1]` induces an exact
functor `K(A) ⥤ K(B)` of triangulated categories.

The hypothesis on `F` is exactly the source's, namely `CommShiftB`; what is assumed besides is
not about `F` but about the two axiom (B) data, namely that the translations they put on the
homotopy categories are the strict ones of the source
(`DGCategory.ShiftAxiomB.IsStrictKShift`). That is what makes the two coherences of
`DGCategory.DGFunctor.CommShiftK` — the agreement of the comparison isomorphisms with
`shiftFunctorZero` and `shiftFunctorAdd`, which Mathlib's `Functor.CommShift` demands and which
`F(x[1]) = F(x)[1]` does not imply for an arbitrary translation — available, by
`DGCategory.DGFunctor.CommShiftK.ofCommShiftB`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated (CA : ConeSituation A) (CB : ConeSituation B)
    (hA : CA.shift.IsStrictKShift) (hB : CB.shift.IsStrictKShift)
    (hF : F.CommShiftB CA.shift CB.shift) :
    letI : Preadditive A.K := homotopyPreadditive A
    letI : HasZeroObject A.K := homotopyHasZeroObject A CA
    letI : HasShift A.K ℤ := CA.shift.kShift
    letI : ∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor A.K n).Additive := fun n => homotopyShiftAdditive A CA n
    letI : Pretriangulated A.K := homotopyPretriangulated A CA
    letI : Preadditive B.K := homotopyPreadditive B
    letI : HasZeroObject B.K := homotopyHasZeroObject B CB
    letI : HasShift B.K ℤ := CB.shift.kShift
    letI : ∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor B.K n).Additive := fun n => homotopyShiftAdditive B CB n
    letI : Pretriangulated B.K := homotopyPretriangulated B CB
    letI : F.onK.CommShift ℤ := (CommShiftK.ofCommShiftB hF hA hB).commShift
    F.onK.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the induced functor on homotopy categories is exact, from F(x[1]) = F(x)[1]

declarations.name: DGCategory.DGFunctor.CommShiftB.isTriangulated_strictify
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FQF, with nothing assumed but the source's hypothesis.** A functor `F : A ⥤ B` of
differential graded categories over `R` between categories satisfying axioms (A), (B) and (C) and
such that `F(x[1]) = F(x)[1]` induces an exact functor `K(A) ⥤ K(B)` of triangulated categories,
for the triangulated structures attached to the strictifications of the two axiom bundles.

Passing to the strictifications changes nothing about the differential graded categories, their
shifts, their cones or the distinguished triangles of Tag 09QW: it only replaces the `HasShift`
field of axiom (B), whose functors `kShift_functor` already pins down, by the one whose coherence
isomorphisms are the canonical ones. So this is Tag 0FQF with no hypothesis beyond the source's
`F(x[1]) = F(x)[1]`, and `DGCategory.DGFunctor.CommShiftB.isTriangulated` is the form in which
the strictness is left as a hypothesis, for a caller who already knows it of the translations
in hand.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated_strictify (CA : ConeSituation A) (CB : ConeSituation B)
    (hF : F.CommShiftB CA.shift CB.shift) :
    letI : Preadditive A.K := homotopyPreadditive A
    letI : HasZeroObject A.K := homotopyHasZeroObject A CA.strictify
    letI : HasShift A.K ℤ := CA.strictify.shift.kShift
    letI : ∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor A.K n).Additive := fun n =>
      homotopyShiftAdditive A CA.strictify n
    letI : Pretriangulated A.K := homotopyPretriangulated A CA.strictify
    letI : Preadditive B.K := homotopyPreadditive B
    letI : HasZeroObject B.K := homotopyHasZeroObject B CB.strictify
    letI : HasShift B.K ℤ := CB.strictify.shift.kShift
    letI : ∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor B.K n).Additive := fun n =>
      homotopyShiftAdditive B CB.strictify n
    letI : Pretriangulated B.K := homotopyPretriangulated B CB.strictify
    letI : F.onK.CommShift ℤ := (CommShiftK.ofCommShiftB hF.strictify
      CA.isStrictKShift_strictify CB.isStrictKShift_strictify).commShift
    F.onK.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the induced functor on homotopy categories is exact, from F(x[1]) = F(x)[1] alone

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule
declarations.doc:
A differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule, presented as a right differential graded `B`-module
with a compatible left differential graded `A`-action.
declarations.statement: structure Bimodule
declarations.comment: (3): a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule, presented as in Tag 0FQI by a right differential graded `B`-module together with a left differential graded `A`-action on its underlying complex whose homogeneous multiplications are right `B`-linear; the grading, the differential and the two Leibniz rules are those of the right module and of the left action. Its underlying graded bimodule, part (2), is `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.toGradedBimodule`

declarations.name: AlgebraBimodule
declarations.doc:
An `(A, B)`-bimodule over a commutative ring `R`, for `R`-algebras `A` and `B`: an `R`-module
`M` with an `R`-bilinear left `A`-action and an `R`-bilinear right `B`-action which commute.

All of the source's clauses are discharged by the Mathlib classes listed as fields, so the only
data is the carrier: `mul_smul` of the two module structures is clause (a), `SMulCommClass` is
clause (b), `one_smul` is clause (c), and the two `IsScalarTower` fields together with the
`R`-module structure are the `R`-bilinearity of the two actions.
declarations.statement:
structure AlgebraBimodule (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (A : Type u) [Ring A] [Algebra R A]
    (B : Type u) [Ring B] [Algebra R B]
declarations.comment: (1): an `(A, B)`-bimodule, bundled as a carrier together with the Mathlib classes that discharge the source's clauses — `Module A M` and `Module Bᵐᵒᵖ M` (clause (a) by `mul_smul`, clause (c) by `one_smul`), `SMulCommClass A Bᵐᵒᵖ M` (clause (b)), and `Module R M` with the two `IsScalarTower`s (`R`-bilinearity of the two actions)

declarations.name: GradedBimodule
declarations.doc:
A graded `(A, B)`-bimodule over a commutative ring `R`, for `ℤ`-graded `R`-algebras `𝒜` and
`ℬ`: an `(A, B)`-bimodule `M` with a grading `M = ⨁ Mⁿ` such that `Aⁿ Mᵐ ⊆ Mⁿ⁺ᵐ` and
`Mⁿ Bᵐ ⊆ Mⁿ⁺ᵐ`.

The underlying `(A, B)`-bimodule of part (1) is the parent projection
`GradedBimodule.toAlgebraBimodule`.
declarations.statement:
structure GradedBimodule {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {A : Type u} [Ring A] [Algebra R A]
    (𝒜 : ℤ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] {B : Type u} [Ring B] [Algebra R B]
    (ℬ : ℤ → Submodule R B) [GradedAlgebra ℬ] extends AlgebraBimodule R A B
declarations.comment: (2): a graded `(A, B)`-bimodule, an `AlgebraBimodule` (part (1), the parent projection `toAlgebraBimodule`) together with a grading by `R`-submodules which decomposes the module and satisfies `Aⁿ Mᵐ ⊆ Mⁿ⁺ᵐ` and `Mⁿ Bᵐ ⊆ Mⁿ⁺ᵐ`

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.toGradedBimodule
declarations.doc:
The graded `(A, B)`-bimodule underlying a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule: the right
differential graded `B`-module with its grading, the left `A`-action totalized from the left
differential graded action, and the differential forgotten.

This is what makes the three parts of [Stacks, Tag 0FQH] one definition rather than three
unrelated ones: part (3), `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule`, refines part (2), `GradedBimodule`,
which in turn extends part (1), `AlgebraBimodule`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Bimodule.toGradedBimodule (M : Bimodule.{u, u} A B) :
    GradedBimodule A.grading B.grading
declarations.comment: the graded (A, B)-bimodule underlying a differential graded one, which is what makes part (3) a refinement of part (2); the three parts themselves are tagged with stacks_fixed, which plain @[stacks] cannot carry on a structure

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.bimoduleStructureEquivRightLinearEndomorphismHom
declarations.doc:
Compatible left differential graded actions on a fixed right differential graded `B`-module
correspond bijectively to homomorphisms into its right `B`-linear endomorphism differential graded
algebra. The specified equation makes the correspondence canonical on every homogeneous element.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bimoduleStructureEquivRightLinearEndomorphismHom :
    { e : BimoduleStructure A B M ≃ RightLinearEndomorphismHom A B M //
      ∀ (L : BimoduleStructure A B M) (n : ℤ) (a : A.grading n),
        (endomorphismDGA M.toCochainComplex).cochainEquiv n
          ⟨(e L).1.toAlgebraHom a, (e L).1.map_grading n a a.property⟩ = L.1.action n a }

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorEquivalence
declarations.doc:
A differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule is canonically a right differential graded module over
the graded tensor product of the graded opposite of `A` with `B`, and this is an equivalence of
categories.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def tensorEquivalence : TensorEquivalence A B

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.exists_propertyP_resolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FQK.** *"Let `R` be a ring. Let `(A, d)` and `(B, d)` be differential graded
`R`-algebras. Let `M` be a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule. There exists a homomorphism
`P → M` of differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodules which is a quasi-isomorphism such that `P`
has property (P)."*

Property (P) of the resolving bimodule is recorded as a property-(P) filtration of the right
differential graded `Aᵒᵖ ⊗_R B`-module it is by Tag 0FQJ, and being a quasi-isomorphism is
Mathlib's `QuasiIso` on the cochain complex underlying the homomorphism of right `B`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_propertyP_resolution (A B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R)
    (M : Bimodule A B) :
    ∃ (P : Bimodule A B) (f : P ⟶ M),
      QuasiIso ((DifferentialGradedModule.forgetToCochainComplex B).map f.rightHom) ∧
        Nonempty (DifferentialGradedModule.PropertyPFiltration (toTensorModule A B P))

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.exists_admissible_telescope
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FQL.** *"Let `R` be a ring. Let `(A, d)` and `(B, d)` be differential graded
`R`-algebras. Let `P` be a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule having property (P) with
corresponding filtration `F_•`, then we obtain a short exact sequence
`0 → ⨁ F_iP → ⨁ F_iP → P → 0` of differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodules which is split as a
sequence of graded `(A, B)`-bimodules."*

Property (P) is read on the right differential graded `Aᵒᵖ ⊗_R B`-module of Tag 0FQJ, and the
stages of the filtration are brought back to bimodules through the same construction. The direct
sum is recorded by its universal property, the second map is the sum of the inclusions
`F_iP → P`, and the first map is, on the summand `F_iP`, the identity minus the inclusion
`F_iP → F_{i+1}P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_admissible_telescope (P : Bimodule A B)
    (F : DifferentialGradedModule.PropertyPFiltration (toTensorModule A B P)) :
    ∃ (S : Bimodule A B) (ι : ∀ i : ℕ, ofTensorModule A B (F.F i) ⟶ S) (α : S ⟶ S) (β : S ⟶ P),
      (∀ (T : Bimodule A B) (g : ∀ i : ℕ, ofTensorModule A B (F.F i) ⟶ T),
          ∃! h : S ⟶ T, ∀ i : ℕ, ι i ≫ h = g i) ∧
        (∀ (i : ℕ) (x : (F.F i).M),
          β.rightHom.toFun ((ι i).rightHom.toFun x) = (F.ι i).toFun x) ∧
        (∀ (i : ℕ) (x : (F.F i).M), α.rightHom.toFun ((ι i).rightHom.toFun x) =
          (ι i).rightHom.toFun x - (ι (i + 1)).rightHom.toFun ((F.incl i).toFun x)) ∧
        IsAdmissibleShortExact A B α β

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorShiftIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FQN.** The canonical, sign-free identification `(M ⊗_A N)[k] ≅ M[k] ⊗_A N`: it
sends each pure tensor to the same pure tensor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorShiftIso (N : Bimodule A B) (M : DifferentialGradedModule A) (k : ℤ) :
    { e : shift ((tensorDGFunctor N).functor.obj M) k ≅
        (tensorDGFunctor N).functor.obj (shift M k) //
      ∀ (x : M.M) (y : N.rightModule.M),
        e.hom.toFun (((tensorDGFunctor N).pure M).toLinearMap x y) =
          ((tensorDGFunctor N).pure (shift M k)).toLinearMap x y }

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homHomotopyDescent
declarations.doc:
The internal hom functor on homotopy categories is the descent of the internal hom functor on
differential graded modules: both send `P` to the chosen presentation of `Hom^•_B(N, P)` and a
homotopy class to the class of the postcomposition.
declarations.comment: descent of the functor on DG modules

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homDGFunctorData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FQQ.** The internal hom functor of a differential graded bimodule, as a functor of
differential graded categories.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def homDGFunctorData : HomDGFunctorData A B N L
declarations.comment: the DG functor

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homModuleFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FQQ.** The internal hom functor on the categories of differential graded
modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homModuleFunctor :
    DifferentialGradedModule B ⥤ DifferentialGradedModule A
declarations.comment: the functor on DG modules

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homHomotopyCategoryFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FQQ.** The internal hom functor on the homotopy categories of differential graded
modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homHomotopyCategoryFunctor :
    HomotopyCategory B ⥤ HomotopyCategory A
declarations.comment: the functor on homotopy categories

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.shiftHomIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical, sign-free isomorphism
`Hom_B^gr(N,P)[k] ≅ Hom_B^gr(N,P[k])` of right DG `A`-modules.
The equality says that the associated homogeneous maps have the same value
on each homogeneous element of `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem shiftHomIso (k : ℤ) :
    ∃ (H : HomDGModulePresentation A B N P L)
      (Hk : HomDGModulePresentation A B N (DifferentialGradedModule.shift P k) L)
      (e : DifferentialGradedModule.shift H.module k ≅ Hk.module),
      ∀ (n p : ℤ) (f : (DifferentialGradedModule.shift H.module k).grading n)
        (x : N.grading p),
        ((Hk.homogeneousEquiv n (e.hom.gradedMap n f)).1 x : P.M) =
          (H.homogeneousEquiv (n + k)
            ⟨(f.1 : H.module.M), by
              simpa only [DifferentialGradedModule.shift_grading] using f.property⟩).1 x

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.shiftHomModuleIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FQR.** The canonical, sign-free isomorphism `Hom^•_B(N, P)[k] ≅ Hom^•_B(N, P[k])`
of right differential graded `A`-modules. The displayed equation says that the homogeneous maps
associated with corresponding elements take the same value on every homogeneous element of `N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem shiftHomModuleIso (k : ℤ) :
    ∃ (H : HomModuleData A B N P L)
      (Hk : HomModuleData A B N (shift P k) L)
      (e : shift H.module k ≅ Hk.module),
      ∀ (n p : ℤ) (f : (shift H.module k).grading n) (x : N.grading p),
        ((Hk.homogeneousEquiv n (e.hom.gradedMap n f)).1 x : P.M) =
          (H.homogeneousEquiv (n + k)
            ⟨(f.1 : H.module.M), by
              simpa only [shift_grading] using f.property⟩).1 x

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.UnitalHom
declarations.doc: A unital homomorphism of sheaves of graded algebras.
declarations.statement: structure UnitalHom (A B : GradedAlgebra.{t, a} R)
declarations.comment: unital homomorphisms of sheaves of graded algebras

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.Hom
declarations.doc:
A homomorphism of sheaves of graded algebras: a morphism of sheaves of modules in each
degree, preserving products of homogeneous local sections. The distinguished degree-zero unit
need not be preserved; the homomorphisms that preserve it are `UnitalHom`.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (A B : GradedAlgebra.{t, a} R)
declarations.comment: homomorphisms of sheaves of graded algebras, and the category they form

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra
declarations.doc: A sheaf of `ℤ`-graded algebras over a sheaf of rings.
declarations.statement: structure GradedAlgebra (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{t})
declarations.comment: sheaves of graded algebras, over a sheaf of rings on an arbitrary site

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.reesGradedAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**The sheaf of graded algebras `⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝓘ⁿ` of a sheaf of ideals.**  Its degree-`n`
homogeneous piece is the `n`-th power of `𝓘` for `n ≥ 0` and the zero sheaf of ideals otherwise,
and its multiplication is the multiplication of sections of the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def reesGradedAlgebra : GradedAlgebra.{t, t} R
declarations.comment: the graded algebra of the powers of a sheaf of ideals

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.GradedAlgebraEssentiallySmall.gradedAlgebraPullbackPushforwardAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Part (3) of Stacks 0FQX**: pullback of sheaves of graded algebras along a morphism of
ringed topoi is left adjoint to the direct image, and the right adjoint has the direct-image
graded algebras as its values on objects.

The unit and the counit are `unitApp` and `counitApp`, whose degreewise components are those of
the Stacks 03D7 adjunction for sheaves of modules; everything else is
`adjunctionOfGradedUnitCounit`.
declarations.comment: part (3): adjunction for graded algebras

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.transport
declarations.doc:
**The transport of a sheaf of graded algebras along a lax monoidal functor between
categories of sheaves of modules**, with homogeneous pieces the images `F(A_n)` of those of
`A`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def transport : GradedAlgebra.{w, w} (toRingCat K Psharp)
declarations.comment: graded_algebra_pushforward, graded_algebra_pullback

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.transportFunctor
declarations.doc:
**A lax monoidal functor between categories of sheaves of modules induces a functor between
the categories of sheaves of graded algebras.**
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def transportFunctor :
    GradedAlgebra.{w, w} (toRingCat J Osharp) ⥤ GradedAlgebra.{w, w} (toRingCat K Psharp)
declarations.comment: graded_algebra_pushforward, graded_algebra_pullback: functoriality

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.transportAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**The transport of sheaves of graded algebras along the left adjoint of a monoidal
adjunction is left adjoint to the transport along the right adjoint.** For a morphism of ringed
topoi this is part (3) of the functoriality of sheaves of graded algebras: the pullback of
graded algebras is left adjoint to the pushforward, so homomorphisms `f^*B ⟶ A` correspond to
homomorphisms `B ⟶ f_*A`, naturally in both arguments.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def transportAdjunction :
    transportFunctor L hP hO ⊣ transportFunctor G hO hP
declarations.comment: part (3): adjunction for graded algebras

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.GradedAlgebraPullback.gradedAlgebraPullbackSpecification
declarations.doc:
The degreewise module pullbacks assemble into a functor of sheaves of graded algebras, with
the induced multiplication and unit.

This is the pullback half of Stacks 0FQX.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def gradedAlgebraPullbackSpecification :
    GradedAlgebraPullbackSpecification f
declarations.comment: graded_algebra_pullback

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.GradedAlgebraPullback.nonempty_gradedAlgebraPullbackSpecification
declarations.doc:
A pullback of sheaves of graded algebras exists.

This is the pullback half of Stacks 0FQX; see `gradedAlgebraPullbackSpecification`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_gradedAlgebraPullbackSpecification :
    Nonempty (GradedAlgebraPullbackSpecification f)
declarations.comment: graded_algebra_pullback

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.GradedAlgebraPushforward.exists_pushforwardGradedAlgebra
declarations.doc:
A graded algebra whose pieces and operations are the canonical direct images
of those of the source exists.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pushforwardGradedAlgebra
    {X : RingedTopos.{u, u, u}}
    {Y : RingedTopos.{u', u', u'}}
    (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (A : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (RingedTopos.ringedSite X).O)) :
    ∃ B : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (RingedTopos.ringedSite Y).O),
      IsPushforwardGradedAlgebra f A B
declarations.comment: graded_algebra_pushforward

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.GradedAlgebraPushforward.pushforwardGradedAlgebraData
declarations.doc: A graded algebra together with its direct-image specification.
declarations.comment: graded_algebra_pushforward

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule
declarations.doc: A right graded module over a sheaf of graded algebras.
declarations.statement: structure GradedModule (A : GradedAlgebra.{t, a} R)
declarations.comment: right graded modules, over a sheaf of rings on an arbitrary site

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule.Hom
declarations.doc: A homomorphism of right graded modules over a sheaf of graded algebras.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (M N : GradedModule.{t, a, m} A)
declarations.comment: homomorphisms of right graded modules

declarations.doc: The category of right graded modules over a fixed sheaf of graded algebras.
declarations.statement: instance : Category (GradedModule.{t, a, m} A)
declarations.comment: the category of right graded modules

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule.regularModule
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of graded algebras, acting on itself on the right. This is the graded counterpart of
`SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.regularModule`.
declarations.statement: def regularModule (A : GradedAlgebra.{t, m} R) : GradedModule.{t, m, m} A
declarations.comment: a sheaf of graded algebras as a right graded module over itself

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.LeftGradedModule
declarations.doc: A left graded module over a sheaf of graded algebras.
declarations.statement: structure LeftGradedModule (A : GradedAlgebra.{t, a} R)
declarations.comment: left graded modules, over a sheaf of rings on an arbitrary site

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.LeftGradedModule.Hom
declarations.doc: A homomorphism of left graded modules over a sheaf of graded algebras.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (M N : LeftGradedModule.{t, a, m} A)
declarations.comment: homomorphisms of left graded modules

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.LeftGradedModule.instCategory
declarations.doc: The category of left graded modules over a fixed sheaf of graded algebras.
declarations.statement: instance instCategory : Category (LeftGradedModule.{t, a, m} A)
declarations.comment: the category of left graded modules

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule.hasCoproducts
declarations.doc:
**Graded modules over a sheaf of graded algebras have arbitrary direct sums**, formed
degreewise.
declarations.statement: instance hasCoproducts : HasColimitsOfShape (Discrete ι) (GradedModule.{t, a, m} A)
declarations.comment: direct_sums

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule.pieceFunctor_preservesCoproducts
declarations.doc: **Taking a fixed homogeneous component commutes with set-indexed direct sums.**
declarations.statement:
instance pieceFunctor_preservesCoproducts (n : ℤ) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete ι) (pieceFunctor.{t, a, m} A n)
declarations.comment: direct_sums

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule.abelian
declarations.doc:
**The category of right graded modules over a sheaf of graded algebras is abelian.**

Kernels and cokernels are formed degreewise, and the coimage-image comparison of a homomorphism
is an isomorphism because it is one in each homogeneous degree.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance abelian : Abelian (GradedModule.{t, a, m} A)
declarations.comment: abelian

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule.pieceFunctor_preservesColimits
declarations.doc:
**Taking a fixed homogeneous component of a graded module commutes with all colimits.**

The module universe is `max u m'` for a site `C : Type u`, because that is the hom universe of
`SheafOfModules.{max u m'} R` and `PreservesColimits` quantifies over diagrams of that size;
`pieceFunctor_preservesColimitsOfSize'` is the same content with the size universe free.
declarations.statement:
instance pieceFunctor_preservesColimits (n : ℤ) :
    PreservesColimits (pieceFunctor.{t, a, max u m'} A n)
declarations.comment: degree_preserves_colimits

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule.pieceFunctor_preservesLimitsOfSize
declarations.doc:
**Taking a fixed homogeneous component of a graded module commutes with all limits.**

A limit of any shape of the size of the module universe is built from products and equalizers,
and the degree-`n` component preserves both: products and kernels of graded modules are formed
degreewise.
declarations.statement:
instance pieceFunctor_preservesLimitsOfSize (n : ℤ) :
    PreservesLimitsOfSize.{m, m} (pieceFunctor.{t, a, m} A n)
declarations.comment: degree_preserves_limits

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule.filteredColimits_exact
declarations.doc:
**Filtered colimits of right graded modules over a sheaf of graded algebras are exact**, at
every size at which those colimits exist.
declarations.statement:
instance filteredColimits_exact (A : GradedAlgebra.{t, a} R)
    [HasFilteredColimitsOfSize.{s, s'} (GradedModule.{t, a, max u m'} A)] :
    AB5OfSize.{s, s'} (GradedModule.{t, a, max u m'} A)
declarations.comment: filtered_colimits_exact

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule.ab5OfSize
declarations.doc:
**Filtered colimits of right graded modules are exact**, unconditionally, at the module
universe `max u m'` of a site `C : Type u`.

The graded modules have all colimits of that size, so the size hypothesis of
`filteredColimits_exact` is discharged rather than assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem ab5OfSize (A : GradedAlgebra.{t, a} R) :
    AB5OfSize.{max u m', max u m'} (GradedModule.{t, a, max u m'} A)
declarations.comment: filtered_colimits_exact

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule.hasLimitsOfSize
declarations.doc:
**Graded modules over a sheaf of graded algebras admit all small limits.**

A limit of any shape of the size of the module universe is built from degreewise products and
from equalizers, the latter being the kernel of a difference.
declarations.statement: instance hasLimitsOfSize : HasLimitsOfSize.{m, m} (GradedModule.{t, a, m} A)
declarations.comment: limits

registrations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule.hasProducts
registrations.comment: products

registrations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedModule.hasColimitsOfSize
registrations.comment: colimits

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedHomOfDegree
declarations.doc:
A homomorphism of right graded `A`-modules homogeneous of degree `n`: a family of morphisms
`M^i ⟶ L^{i + n}` of sheaves of modules compatible with the right action. These are the
elements of `Hom^n` in the graded category of right graded `A`-modules.
declarations.statement: structure GradedHomOfDegree (M L : GradedModule.{t, a, w} A) (n : ℤ)
declarations.comment: homogeneous homomorphisms of degree n of right graded modules

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedHomOfDegree.comp
declarations.doc:
**Composition in the graded category `Mod^gr(A)` of Stacks 0FR1**: the composite
`g ∘ f : K → M`, homogeneous of degree `n + m`, of homogeneous homomorphisms `f : K → L` of
degree `n` and `g : L → M` of degree `m`.
declarations.statement:
def comp (g : GradedHomOfDegree L M m) (f : GradedHomOfDegree K L n) :
    GradedHomOfDegree K M (n + m)
declarations.comment: composition `Hom^m(L, M) × Hom^n(K, L) → Hom^{n + m}(K, M)` in `Mod^gr(A)`

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedHomOfDegree.id
declarations.doc:
**The identity in `Mod^gr(A)`**: the identity of a right graded `A`-module, homogeneous of
degree zero.
declarations.statement: def id (M : GradedModule.{t, a, w} A) : GradedHomOfDegree M M 0
declarations.comment: the identity of `Mod^gr(A)`, in `Hom^0(M, M)`

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedHomOfDegree.add_comp
declarations.doc: Composition in `Mod^gr(A)` is additive in the first variable.
declarations.statement:
theorem add_comp (g g' : GradedHomOfDegree L M m) (f : GradedHomOfDegree K L n) :
    (g + g').comp f = g.comp f + g'.comp f
declarations.comment: composition is additive in `g`

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedHomOfDegree.comp_add
declarations.doc: Composition in `Mod^gr(A)` is additive in the second variable.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_add (g : GradedHomOfDegree L M m) (f f' : GradedHomOfDegree K L n) :
    g.comp (f + f') = g.comp f + g.comp f'
declarations.comment: composition is additive in `f`

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedHomOfDegree.smul_comp
declarations.doc: Composition in `Mod^gr(A)` is `Γ(C, O)`-linear in the first variable.
declarations.statement:
theorem smul_comp (c : Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.GlobalSectionRing R)
    (g : GradedHomOfDegree L M m) (f : GradedHomOfDegree K L n) :
    (c • g).comp f = c • g.comp f
declarations.comment: composition is `R`-linear in `g`

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedHomOfDegree.comp_smul
declarations.doc: Composition in `Mod^gr(A)` is `Γ(C, O)`-linear in the second variable.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_smul (c : Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.GlobalSectionRing R)
    (g : GradedHomOfDegree L M m) (f : GradedHomOfDegree K L n) :
    g.comp (c • f) = c • g.comp f
declarations.comment: composition is `R`-linear in `f`

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedHomOfDegree.components
declarations.doc:
**The components of a homogeneous map** (Stacks 0FR1): a map `f` homogeneous of degree `n`
as the family `f_{p, q} : L^{-q} → M^p`, `p + q = n`, of its components; the reversal of indices
is that of the source.
declarations.statement:
def components (f : GradedHomOfDegree L M n) (p q : ℤ) (h : p + q = n) :
    L.piece (-q) ⟶ M.piece p
declarations.comment: the components `f_{p, q} : L^{-q} → M^p`, `p + q = n`, of `f ∈ Hom^n(L, M)`

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.GradedHomOfDegree.componentsEquiv
