`(A, B)`-bimodule** through a unital homomorphism `φ : A ⟶ B`, with `a` acting on the left as
`φ a` and `B` acting on the right by its own multiplication.
declarations.statement: def asBimodule (φ : A ⟶ B) (hφ : φ.IsUnital) : DifferentialGradedBimodule.{t, a, a} A B
declarations.comment: B as a differential graded (A,B)-bimodule through a homomorphism φ : A ⟶ B

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.restrictScalars
declarations.doc:
**The restriction functor `res_φ : Mod(B, d) ⥤ Mod(A, d)`** attached to a unital
homomorphism `φ : A ⟶ B` of sheaves of differential graded algebras.
declarations.statement:
def restrictScalars (φ : A ⟶ B) (hφ : φ.IsUnital) :
    DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} B ⥤ DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} A
declarations.comment: restriction res_φ along a homomorphism of sheaves of differential graded algebras

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.RelativeTensor.dgTensorRightFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The tensor product functor `- ⊗_A N`** from right differential graded `A`-modules to
right differential graded `B`-modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dgTensorRightFunctor
    (N : DifferentialGradedBimodule.{t, max u v, max u v} A B) :
    DifferentialGradedModule.{t, max u v, max u v} A ⥤
      DifferentialGradedModule.{t, max u v, max u v} B
declarations.comment: the functor - ⊗_A N : Mod(A, d) ⥤ Mod(B, d) for a dg (A, B)-bimodule N

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.sheafHomModule
declarations.doc:
**The internal hom `SheafHom^dg_{A'}(N, M)` of a differential graded `(A, A')`-bimodule `N`
and a right differential graded `A'`-module `M`**, as a right differential graded `A`-module: the
complex of sheaves of local homomorphisms `N|_U → M|_U`, with `(q a)(x) = q (a x)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev sheafHomModule (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, s} A') :
    DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, max u v z s} A
declarations.comment: SheafHom^dg_B(N, L) is a right differential graded A-module

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.sheafHomFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The functor `SheafHom^dg_{A'}(N, -) : Mod(A', d) ⥤ Mod(A, d)`** of a differential
graded `(A, A')`-bimodule `N`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomFunctor :
    DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, s} A' ⥤ DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, max u v z s} A
declarations.comment: the functor SheafHom^dg_B(N, -) : Mod(B, d) ⥤ Mod(A, d), constructed

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.sheafHomConcreteDGFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The internal hom `SheafHom^dg_{𝒜'}(𝒩, -)`, extended to homogeneous maps** by
postcomposition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomConcreteDGFunctor (N : DifferentialGradedBimodule.{u, a, z} A A') :
    ConcreteDGFunctor.{u, a, a, s, max u z s} A' A
declarations.comment: SheafHom^dg_B(N, -) as a functor of differential graded categories

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedAlgebra.Hom.toBimodule
declarations.doc:
The target of a unit-preserving homomorphism `φ : A ⟶ B` of sheaves of differential graded
algebras, read as a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `{}_A B_B`: the underlying complex is
that of `B`, the right action is the multiplication of `B`, and a homogeneous local section `a`
of `A` acts on the left through `φ(a)`.

This is `SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedAlgebra.asBimodule`.
declarations.statement:
def Hom.toBimodule (φ : A ⟶ B) (hφ : φ.PreservesOne) :
    DifferentialGradedBimodule.{t, a, a} A B
declarations.comment: the bimodule _A B_B attached to a homomorphism of differential graded algebras

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.restrictionObj
declarations.doc:
Restriction of scalars of a right differential graded `B`-module along a unit-preserving
homomorphism `φ : A ⟶ B` of sheaves of differential graded algebras: the underlying cochain
complex of sheaves of modules is unchanged and a homogeneous local section `a` of `A` acts
through `φ(a)`.

This is `SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.restrictScalarsObj`.
declarations.statement:
def restrictionObj (φ : A ⟶ B) (hφ : φ.PreservesOne)
    (N : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} B) : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} A
declarations.comment: the restriction functor res_φ on objects

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.restrictionMap
declarations.doc:
Restriction of scalars of a homomorphism of right differential graded `B`-modules: the same
morphism of underlying cochain complexes.
declarations.comment: the restriction functor res_φ on homomorphisms

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.restriction
declarations.doc:
**Restriction of scalars** `res_φ : Mod(B, d) ⥤ Mod(A, d)` along a unit-preserving
homomorphism `φ : A ⟶ B` of sheaves of differential graded algebras.

This is `SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.restrictScalars`.
declarations.statement:
def restriction (φ : A ⟶ B) (hφ : φ.PreservesOne) :
    DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} B ⥤ DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} A
declarations.comment: the restriction functor res_φ

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.isSheafHomRestrictionObj
declarations.doc:
**`SheafHom^dg_B({}_A B_B, L) = res_φ(L)` as right differential graded `A`-modules**
([Stacks, Tag 0FRP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FRP)): the restriction `res_φ L` is
the internal hom out of the bimodule `{}_A B_B`, with its right `A`-module structure by
precomposition with the left action of `A` on `{}_A B_B`.
declarations.statement:
def isSheafHomRestrictionObj :
    IsSheafHom (φ.toBimodule hφ) L (restrictionObj φ hφ L)
declarations.comment: SheafHom^dg_B(_A B_B, L) = res_φ(L) as right differential graded A-modules

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.isInternalHomRestrictionObjOfTensor
declarations.doc:
**`SheafHom^dg_B(M ⊗_A B, L) = SheafHom^dg_A(M, res_φ L)`**
([Stacks, Tag 0FRP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FRP)): for a right differential
graded `A`-module `M`, a tensor product `T = M ⊗_{A, φ} B` with the bimodule `{}_A B_B` and a
complex `G` which is the internal hom `SheafHom^dg_B(T, L)`, the complex `G` is also the
internal hom `SheafHom^dg_A(M, res_φ L)`, differentials included.
declarations.statement:
def isInternalHomRestrictionObjOfTensor {M : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} A}
    {T : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} B} (hT : IsTensorProduct M (φ.toBimodule hφ) T)
    {G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{s} R) ℤ} (hG : IsInternalHom T L G) :
    IsInternalHom M (restrictionObj φ hφ L) G
declarations.comment: SheafHom^dg_B(M ⊗_A B, L) = SheafHom^dg_A(M, res_φ L)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.restrictionConcreteDGFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Restriction of scalars, extended to homogeneous maps**: a cochain between right
differential graded `B`-modules which commutes with the action of `B` is the same cochain between
their restrictions, and commutes with the action of `A` through `φ`.
declarations.statement: def restrictionConcreteDGFunctor : ConcreteDGFunctor.{u, v, v, w, w} B A
declarations.comment: res_φ as a functor of differential graded categories Mod^dg(B, d) ⥤ Mod^dg(A, d)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedBimodule.sectionBimodule
declarations.doc:
**The sections `N(U) = ⨁ n, N^n(U)` of a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N` over `U`
form a differential graded `(A(U), B(U))`-bimodule**: the right `B(U)`-module of sections of the
underlying right module, with the left action of `A(U)` read on sections, which is by right
`B(U)`-linear maps.
declarations.statement: def sectionBimodule : DifferentialGraded.Bimodule (A.sectionAlgebra U) (B.sectionAlgebra U)
declarations.comment: N(U) = ⊕ N^n(U) is a differential graded (A(U), B(U))-bimodule

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgTensorRightConcreteDGFunctor
declarations.doc:
**`- ⊗_A N` as a functor of differential graded categories**: the functor
`Mod(A, d) ⥤ Mod(B, d)` of the tensor product with a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N`,
sending a homogeneous map `c` of degree `n` to the induced map `c ⊗ 1` of degree `n`,
additively and compatibly with the differentials of the hom complexes, composition and
identities.
declarations.statement:
def dgTensorRightConcreteDGFunctor (N : DifferentialGradedBimodule.{u, u, u} A B) :
    ConcreteDGFunctor.{u, u, u, u, u} (X := X) (Y := X) A B
declarations.comment: - ⊗_A N as a functor of differential graded categories Mod^dg(A, d) ⥤ Mod^dg(B, d)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.baseChangeConcreteDGFunctor
declarations.doc:
**`- ⊗_{A, φ} B` as a functor of differential graded categories**, for a homomorphism
`φ : A ⟶ B` of sheaves of differential graded algebras: base change, sending a homogeneous map
`c` of degree `n` to `c ⊗ 1`.
declarations.statement:
def baseChangeConcreteDGFunctor (φ : A ⟶ B) (hφ : φ.PreservesOne) :
    ConcreteDGFunctor.{u, u, u, u, u} (X := X) (Y := X) A B
declarations.comment: - ⊗_{A,φ} B as a functor of differential graded categories

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedBimodule
declarations.doc:
A differential graded bimodule between two sheaves of differential graded algebras: a
cochain complex of sheaves of modules with commuting unital left and right actions, each
obeying the signed Leibniz rule.
declarations.statement: structure DifferentialGradedBimodule (A B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{t, a} R)
declarations.comment: differential graded bimodules

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedBimodule.Hom
declarations.doc:
A homomorphism of differential graded bimodules: a morphism of the underlying complexes
compatible with both actions.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (M N : DifferentialGradedBimodule.{t, a, m} A B)
declarations.comment: homomorphisms of differential graded bimodules

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.isEndomorphismAlgebra_endomorphismAlgebraOfIsInternalHom
declarations.doc:
The sheafified differential graded endomorphisms of a right differential graded `B`-module
`N` carry a differential graded `R`-algebra structure, with composition of local endomorphisms
as multiplication and the identity as unit.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isEndomorphismAlgebra_endomorphismAlgebraOfIsInternalHom
    (hH : IsInternalHom N N H) :
    IsEndomorphismAlgebra N (endomorphismAlgebraOfIsInternalHom hH)
declarations.comment: the differential graded endomorphism algebra

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.bimoduleStructureEquiv
declarations.doc:
Compatible `(A, B)`-bimodule structures on a right differential graded `B`-module `N` are in
one-to-one correspondence with identity-preserving homomorphisms of sheaves of differential
graded `R`-algebras `A ⟶ SheafHom^dg_B(N, N)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bimoduleStructureEquiv (hE : IsEndomorphismAlgebra N E) :
    BimoduleStructure A N ≃ UnitalHom A E
declarations.comment: bimodule structures correspond to maps into the endomorphism algebra

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.bimoduleStructureEquiv_app
declarations.doc:
The correspondence between compatible bimodule structures and identity-preserving
homomorphisms into the endomorphism algebra is pinned down by the requirement that the
homomorphism attached to a structure act on local sections of `N` by left multiplication for
that structure.
declarations.statement:
theorem bimoduleStructureEquiv_app (hE : IsEndomorphismAlgebra N E) (s : BimoduleStructure A N)
    (n i j : ℤ) (hij : i + n = j) (U : C) (V : Over U)
    (a : (A.complex.X n).val.obj (Opposite.op U))
    (x : (N.complex.X i).val.obj (Opposite.op V.left)) :
    HEq ((hE.isInternalHom.sectionsEquiv n U
        (((bimoduleStructureEquiv hE s).toHom.toHomologicalComplex.f n).val.app
          (Opposite.op U) a)).app i j hij V x)
      ((s.leftMul n i).app (Opposite.op V.left) ((A.complex.X n).val.map V.hom.op a) x)
declarations.comment: bimodule structures correspond to maps into the endomorphism algebra

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.isInternalHom_tensor
declarations.doc:
**Tensor-hom adjunction for sheaves of differential graded modules**, second identity: a
complex of sheaves of `R`-modules which is the internal hom `SheafHom^dg_B(M ⊗_A N, L)` is also
the internal hom `SheafHom^dg_A(M, SheafHom^dg_B(N, L))`, differentials included.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isInternalHom_tensor (hT : IsTensorProduct M N T)
    (hH : IsSheafHom N L H) (hG : IsInternalHom T L G) :
    IsInternalHom M H G
declarations.comment: SheafHom^dg_B(M ⊗_A N, L) = SheafHom^dg_A(M, SheafHom^dg_B(N, L))

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.tensorSectionsEquiv_naturality_left
declarations.doc:
**Tensor-hom adjunction for sheaves of differential graded modules**, second identity,
functoriality in `M`: a morphism `u : M' ⟶ M` of right differential graded `A`-modules induces
`t : M' ⊗_A N ⟶ M ⊗_A N` and hence `α : SheafHom^dg_B(M ⊗_A N, L) ⟶ SheafHom^dg_B(M' ⊗_A N, L)`,
and `α` is also the map that the second identity attaches to `u`, namely precomposition with
`u` on `SheafHom^dg_A(M, SheafHom^dg_B(N, L))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorSectionsEquiv_naturality_left (hT : IsTensorProduct M N T)
    (hT' : IsTensorProduct M' N T') (hH : IsSheafHom N L H) (hG : IsInternalHom T L G)
    (hG' : IsInternalHom T' L G') (u : M' ⟶ M) (t : T' ⟶ T) (α : G ⟶ G')
    (ht : ∀ (i j : ℤ) (U : Cᵒᵖ) (x : (M'.complex.X i).val.obj U)
      (y : (N.complex.X j).val.obj U),
      (t.toHomologicalComplex.f (i + j)).val.app U (hT'.tmul i j U x y) =
        hT.tmul i j U ((u.toHomologicalComplex.f i).val.app U x) y)
    (hα : ∀ (n : ℤ) (U : C) (p : (G.X n).val.obj (Opposite.op U)) (i j : ℤ) (hij : i + n = j)
      (V : Over U) (x : (T'.complex.X i).val.obj (Opposite.op V.left)),
      (hG'.sectionsEquiv n U ((α.f n).val.app (Opposite.op U) p)).app i j hij V x =
        (hG.sectionsEquiv n U p).app i j hij V
          ((t.toHomologicalComplex.f i).val.app (Opposite.op V.left) x))
    (n : ℤ) (U : C) (p : (G.X n).val.obj (Opposite.op U)) (i j : ℤ) (hij : i + n = j)
    (V : Over U) (x : (M'.complex.X i).val.obj (Opposite.op V.left)) :
    (tensorSectionsEquiv hT' hH hG' n U ((α.f n).val.app (Opposite.op U) p)).app i j hij V x =
      (tensorSectionsEquiv hT hH hG n U p).app i j hij V
        ((u.toHomologicalComplex.f i).val.app (Opposite.op V.left) x)
declarations.comment: functoriality of the internal-hom identity in M, on local sections

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.tensorSectionsEquiv_naturality_right
declarations.doc:
**Tensor-hom adjunction for sheaves of differential graded modules**, second identity,
functoriality in `L`: a morphism `k : L ⟶ L'` of right differential graded `B`-modules induces
`α : SheafHom^dg_B(M ⊗_A N, L) ⟶ SheafHom^dg_B(M ⊗_A N, L')` and
`g : SheafHom^dg_B(N, L) ⟶ SheafHom^dg_B(N, L')`, and under the second identity `α` is
postcomposition with `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorSectionsEquiv_naturality_right (hT : IsTensorProduct M N T)
    (hH : IsSheafHom N L H) (hH' : IsSheafHom N L' H') (hG : IsInternalHom T L G)
    (hG' : IsInternalHom T L' G') (k : L ⟶ L') (g : H ⟶ H') (α : G ⟶ G')
    (hg : ∀ (m : ℤ) (U : C) (q : (H.complex.X m).val.obj (Opposite.op U)) (i j : ℤ)
      (hij : i + m = j) (V : Over U)
      (y : (N.complex.X i).val.obj (Opposite.op V.left)),
      (hH'.isInternalHom.sectionsEquiv m U
          ((g.toHomologicalComplex.f m).val.app (Opposite.op U) q)).app i j hij V y =
        (k.toHomologicalComplex.f j).val.app (Opposite.op V.left)
          ((hH.isInternalHom.sectionsEquiv m U q).app i j hij V y))
    (hα : ∀ (n : ℤ) (U : C) (p : (G.X n).val.obj (Opposite.op U)) (i j : ℤ) (hij : i + n = j)
      (V : Over U) (x : (T.complex.X i).val.obj (Opposite.op V.left)),
      (hG'.sectionsEquiv n U ((α.f n).val.app (Opposite.op U) p)).app i j hij V x =
        (k.toHomologicalComplex.f j).val.app (Opposite.op V.left)
          ((hG.sectionsEquiv n U p).app i j hij V x))
    (n : ℤ) (U : C) (p : (G.X n).val.obj (Opposite.op U)) (i j : ℤ) (hij : i + n = j)
    (V : Over U) (x : (M.complex.X i).val.obj (Opposite.op V.left)) :
    (tensorSectionsEquiv hT hH' hG' n U ((α.f n).val.app (Opposite.op U) p)).app i j hij V x =
      (g.toHomologicalComplex.f j).val.app (Opposite.op V.left)
        ((tensorSectionsEquiv hT hH hG n U p).app i j hij V x)
declarations.comment: functoriality of the internal-hom identity in L, on local sections

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.tensorSectionsEquiv_naturality_bimodule
declarations.doc:
**Tensor-hom adjunction for sheaves of differential graded modules**, second identity,
functoriality in `N`: a morphism `σ : N ⟶ N'` of differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodules induces
`t : M ⊗_A N ⟶ M ⊗_A N'`, hence `α : SheafHom^dg_B(M ⊗_A N', L) ⟶ SheafHom^dg_B(M ⊗_A N, L)`,
and `g : SheafHom^dg_B(N', L) ⟶ SheafHom^dg_B(N, L)`; under the second identity `α` is
postcomposition with `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorSectionsEquiv_naturality_bimodule (hT : IsTensorProduct M N T)
    (hT' : IsTensorProduct M N' T') (hH : IsSheafHom N L H) (hH' : IsSheafHom N' L H')
    (hG : IsInternalHom T L G) (hG' : IsInternalHom T' L G')
    (σ : N ⟶ N') (t : T ⟶ T') (g : H' ⟶ H) (α : G' ⟶ G)
    (ht : ∀ (i j : ℤ) (U : Cᵒᵖ) (x : (M.complex.X i).val.obj U)
      (y : (N.complex.X j).val.obj U),
      (t.toHomologicalComplex.f (i + j)).val.app U (hT.tmul i j U x y) =
        hT'.tmul i j U x ((σ.toHomologicalComplex.f j).val.app U y))
    (hg : ∀ (m : ℤ) (U : C) (q : (H'.complex.X m).val.obj (Opposite.op U)) (i j : ℤ)
      (hij : i + m = j) (V : Over U)
      (y : (N.complex.X i).val.obj (Opposite.op V.left)),
      (hH.isInternalHom.sectionsEquiv m U
          ((g.toHomologicalComplex.f m).val.app (Opposite.op U) q)).app i j hij V y =
        (hH'.isInternalHom.sectionsEquiv m U q).app i j hij V
          ((σ.toHomologicalComplex.f i).val.app (Opposite.op V.left) y))
    (hα : ∀ (n : ℤ) (U : C) (p : (G'.X n).val.obj (Opposite.op U)) (i j : ℤ) (hij : i + n = j)
      (V : Over U) (x : (T.complex.X i).val.obj (Opposite.op V.left)),
      (hG.sectionsEquiv n U ((α.f n).val.app (Opposite.op U) p)).app i j hij V x =
        (hG'.sectionsEquiv n U p).app i j hij V
          ((t.toHomologicalComplex.f i).val.app (Opposite.op V.left) x))
    (n : ℤ) (U : C) (p : (G'.X n).val.obj (Opposite.op U)) (i j : ℤ) (hij : i + n = j)
    (V : Over U) (x : (M.complex.X i).val.obj (Opposite.op V.left)) :
    (tensorSectionsEquiv hT hH hG n U ((α.f n).val.app (Opposite.op U) p)).app i j hij V x =
      (g.toHomologicalComplex.f j).val.app (Opposite.op V.left)
        ((tensorSectionsEquiv hT' hH' hG' n U p).app i j hij V x)
declarations.comment: functoriality of the internal-hom identity in N, on local sections

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Tensor-hom adjunction for sheaves of differential graded modules**, first identity, in a
fixed degree: the degree-`n` homogeneous right-linear maps `M ⊗_A N → L` of right differential
graded `B`-modules are the degree-`n` homogeneous right-linear maps
`M → SheafHom^dg_B(N, L)` of right differential graded `A`-modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv (hT : IsTensorProduct M N T) (hH : IsSheafHom N L H)
    (n : ℤ) : HomogeneousMap B T L n ≃ HomogeneousMap A M H n
declarations.comment:
Hom_{Mod^dg(B, d)}(M ⊗_A N, L) = Hom_{Mod^dg(A, d)}(M, SheafHom^dg_B(N, L))
as hom-complexes: degreewise, additively, and compatibly with the differentials

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.homogeneousEquiv_add
declarations.doc:
**Tensor-hom adjunction for sheaves of differential graded modules**, first identity, on
the additions: the identification of the homogeneous morphisms is additive, so each degree of
the two hom-complexes is identified as an abelian group.
declarations.statement:
theorem homogeneousEquiv_add (hT : IsTensorProduct M N T) (hH : IsSheafHom N L H) (n : ℤ)
    (φ φ' χ : HomogeneousMap B T L n) (hχ : χ.val = φ.val + φ'.val) :
    (tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv hT hH n χ).val =
      (tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv hT hH n φ).val + (tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv hT hH n φ').val
declarations.comment:
Hom_{Mod^dg(B, d)}(M ⊗_A N, L) = Hom_{Mod^dg(A, d)}(M, SheafHom^dg_B(N, L))
as hom-complexes: degreewise, additively, and compatibly with the differentials

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.homogeneousEquiv_delta
declarations.doc:
**Tensor-hom adjunction for sheaves of differential graded modules**, first identity, on
the differentials: the identification of the homogeneous morphisms commutes with the commutator
differential of the two hom-complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem homogeneousEquiv_delta (hT : IsTensorProduct M N T) (hH : IsSheafHom N L H) (n : ℤ)
    (φ : HomogeneousMap B T L n) (ψ : HomogeneousMap B T L (n + 1))
    (hψ : ψ.val = δ n (n + 1) φ.val) :
    (tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv hT hH (n + 1) ψ).val =
      δ n (n + 1) (tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv hT hH n φ).val
declarations.comment:
Hom_{Mod^dg(B, d)}(M ⊗_A N, L) = Hom_{Mod^dg(A, d)}(M, SheafHom^dg_B(N, L))
as hom-complexes: degreewise, additively, and compatibly with the differentials

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Tensor-hom adjunction for sheaves of differential graded modules**, first identity: the
degree-`n` homogeneous morphisms `M ⊗_A N → L` of the differential graded category
`Mod^dg(B, d)` are the degree-`n` homogeneous morphisms `M → SheafHom^dg_B(N, L)` of the
differential graded category `Mod^dg(A, d)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dgHomEquiv (hT : IsTensorProduct M N T) (hH : IsSheafHom N L H) (n : ℤ) :
    (dgCategoryData B).category.Hom (moduleObject B (dgCategoryData B) T)
        (moduleObject B (dgCategoryData B) L) n ≃
      (dgCategoryData A).category.Hom (moduleObject A (dgCategoryData A) M)
        (moduleObject A (dgCategoryData A) H) n
declarations.comment:
Hom_{Mod^dg(B, d)}(M ⊗_A N, L) = Hom_{Mod^dg(A, d)}(M, SheafHom^dg_B(N, L))
as hom-complexes: degreewise, additively, and compatibly with the differentials

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgHomEquiv_d
declarations.doc:
**Tensor-hom adjunction for sheaves of differential graded modules**, first identity: the
identification of the two hom-complexes commutes with their differentials, so it is an equality
of complexes and not only of their degreewise components.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgHomEquiv_d (hT : IsTensorProduct M N T) (hH : IsSheafHom N L H) (n : ℤ)
    (f : (dgCategoryData B).category.Hom (moduleObject B (dgCategoryData B) T)
      (moduleObject B (dgCategoryData B) L) n) :
    (dgCategoryData A).category.d (dgHomEquiv hT hH n f) =
      dgHomEquiv hT hH (n + 1) ((dgCategoryData B).category.d f)
declarations.comment:
Hom_{Mod^dg(B, d)}(M ⊗_A N, L) = Hom_{Mod^dg(A, d)}(M, SheafHom^dg_B(N, L))
as hom-complexes: degreewise, additively, and compatibly with the differentials

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.homogeneousEquiv_naturality_left
declarations.doc:
**Tensor-hom adjunction for sheaves of differential graded modules**, first identity,
functoriality in `M`: a morphism `u : M' ⟶ M` of right differential graded `A`-modules induces
`t : M' ⊗_A N ⟶ M ⊗_A N`, and the identification of the hom-complexes carries precomposition
with `t` to precomposition with `u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homogeneousEquiv_naturality_left (hT : IsTensorProduct M N T)
    (hT' : IsTensorProduct M' N T') (hH : IsSheafHom N L H) (u : M' ⟶ M) (t : T' ⟶ T)
    (ht : ∀ (i j : ℤ) (U : X.Cᵒᵖ) (x : (M'.complex.X i).val.obj U)
      (y : (N.complex.X j).val.obj U),
      (t.toHomologicalComplex.f (i + j)).val.app U (hT'.tmul i j U x y) =
        hT.tmul i j U ((u.toHomologicalComplex.f i).val.app U x) y)
    (n : ℤ) (φ : HomogeneousMap B T L n) (φ' : HomogeneousMap B T' L n)
    (hφ' : φ'.val = (Cochain.ofHom t.toHomologicalComplex).comp φ.val (zero_add n)) :
    (tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv hT' hH n φ').val =
      (Cochain.ofHom u.toHomologicalComplex).comp
        (tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv hT hH n φ).val (zero_add n)
declarations.comment: functoriality of the hom-complex identity in M: a morphism M' ⟶ M compatible with the tensor products carries the identification at M to the one at M'

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.homogeneousEquiv_naturality_right
declarations.doc:
**Tensor-hom adjunction for sheaves of differential graded modules**, first identity,
functoriality in `L`: a morphism `k : L ⟶ L'` of right differential graded `B`-modules induces
`g : SheafHom^dg_B(N, L) ⟶ SheafHom^dg_B(N, L')`, and the identification of the hom-complexes
carries postcomposition with `k` to postcomposition with `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homogeneousEquiv_naturality_right (hT : IsTensorProduct M N T)
    (hH : IsSheafHom N L H) (hH' : IsSheafHom N L' H') (k : L ⟶ L') (g : H ⟶ H')
    (hg : ∀ (m : ℤ) (U : X.C) (p : (H.complex.X m).val.obj (Opposite.op U)) (i j : ℤ)
      (hij : i + m = j) (V : Over U) (y : (N.complex.X i).val.obj (Opposite.op V.left)),
      (hH'.isInternalHom.sectionsEquiv m U
          ((g.toHomologicalComplex.f m).val.app (Opposite.op U) p)).app i j hij V y =
        (k.toHomologicalComplex.f j).val.app (Opposite.op V.left)
          ((hH.isInternalHom.sectionsEquiv m U p).app i j hij V y))
    (n : ℤ) (φ : HomogeneousMap B T L n) (φ' : HomogeneousMap B T L' n)
    (hφ' : φ'.val = φ.val.comp (Cochain.ofHom k.toHomologicalComplex) (add_zero n)) :
    (tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv hT hH' n φ').val =
      (tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv hT hH n φ).val.comp
        (Cochain.ofHom g.toHomologicalComplex) (add_zero n)
declarations.comment: functoriality of the hom-complex identity in L: a morphism L ⟶ L', with the induced map of internal homs, commutes with the identification

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.homogeneousEquiv_naturality_bimodule
declarations.doc:
**Tensor-hom adjunction for sheaves of differential graded modules**, first identity,
functoriality in `N`: a morphism `σ : N ⟶ N'` of differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodules induces
`t : M ⊗_A N ⟶ M ⊗_A N'` and `g : SheafHom^dg_B(N', L) ⟶ SheafHom^dg_B(N, L)`, and the
identification of the hom-complexes carries precomposition with `t` to postcomposition with
`g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homogeneousEquiv_naturality_bimodule (hT : IsTensorProduct M N T)
    (hT' : IsTensorProduct M N' T') (hH : IsSheafHom N L H) (hH' : IsSheafHom N' L H')
    (σ : N ⟶ N') (t : T ⟶ T') (g : H' ⟶ H)
    (ht : ∀ (i j : ℤ) (U : X.Cᵒᵖ) (x : (M.complex.X i).val.obj U)
      (y : (N.complex.X j).val.obj U),
      (t.toHomologicalComplex.f (i + j)).val.app U (hT.tmul i j U x y) =
        hT'.tmul i j U x ((σ.toHomologicalComplex.f j).val.app U y))
    (hg : ∀ (m : ℤ) (U : X.C) (p : (H'.complex.X m).val.obj (Opposite.op U)) (i j : ℤ)
      (hij : i + m = j) (V : Over U) (y : (N.complex.X i).val.obj (Opposite.op V.left)),
      (hH.isInternalHom.sectionsEquiv m U
          ((g.toHomologicalComplex.f m).val.app (Opposite.op U) p)).app i j hij V y =
        (hH'.isInternalHom.sectionsEquiv m U p).app i j hij V
          ((σ.toHomologicalComplex.f i).val.app (Opposite.op V.left) y))
    (n : ℤ) (φ : HomogeneousMap B T L n) (φ' : HomogeneousMap B T' L n)
    (hφ : φ.val = (Cochain.ofHom t.toHomologicalComplex).comp φ'.val (zero_add n)) :
    (tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv hT hH n φ).val =
      (tensorHomHomogeneousEquiv hT' hH' n φ').val.comp
        (Cochain.ofHom g.toHomologicalComplex) (add_zero n)
declarations.comment: functoriality of the hom-complex identity in N: a morphism N ⟶ N' of bimodules, compatible with the tensor products and the internal homs, commutes with the identification

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgTensorRightSheafHomAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**The tensor-hom adjunction `- ⊗_A N ⊣ SheafHom^dg_B(N, -)`**, with both functors
constructed: for a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N`, the tensor product functor
`- ⊗_A N : Mod(A, d) ⥤ Mod(B, d)` is left adjoint to the internal hom functor
`SheafHom^dg_B(N, -) : Mod(B, d) ⥤ Mod(A, d)`, that is
`Hom_{Mod(B, d)}(M ⊗_A N, L) = Hom_{Mod(A, d)}(M, SheafHom^dg_B(N, L))` functorially in `M` and
`L`, by `ψ ↦ (x ↦ (y ↦ ψ (x ⊗ y)))`.
declarations.statement:
def dgTensorRightSheafHomAdjunction (N : DifferentialGradedBimodule.{u, u, u} A B) :
    (dgTensorRightData N).functor ⊣ sheafHomFunctor N
declarations.comment:
Hom(M ⊗_A N, L) = Hom(M, SheafHom^dg_B(N, L)) as an adjunction of the constructed
functors - ⊗_A N and SheafHom^dg_B(N, -)

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedPullbackConstruction.exists_pullbackPushforwardHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Pull and push for sheaves of differential graded modules**: for the direct image `f_*` and
the pullback `f^*M = f⁻¹M ⊗_{f⁻¹A'} A` along a morphism of small ringed sites, together with a
unital homomorphism `φ₀ : f⁻¹A' ⟶ A`,
`Hom_{Mod^dg(A', d)}(M, f_*N) = Hom_{Mod^dg(A, d)}(f^*M, N)`.

The identification `e` of the two differential graded Hom objects is given in every degree `n`,
it is precomposition with the unit `M ⟶ f^*M` of the pullback — so in particular it is additive
and natural — and it carries the differential of the one Hom complex to the differential of the
other. Its degree-zero closed part is the bijection `e₀` of hom-sets of the adjunction
`f^* ⊣ f_*`, which sends a morphism `g : f^*M ⟶ N` to the unit followed by `g`, read as a
morphism `M ⟶ f_*N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pullbackPushforwardHomEquiv (φ₀ : inverseImageAlgebra α hO hP A' ⟶ A)
    (hφ₀ : φ₀.IsUnital) :
    ∃ (e : ∀ (M : SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A')
          (N : SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A) (n : ℤ),
          HomogeneousMap (X := ⟨D, K, Psharp⟩) A (pullbackObj α hO hP φ₀ hφ₀ M) N n ≃
            HomogeneousMap (X := ⟨C, J, Osharp⟩) A' M
              (pushforwardObj (semilinearHom α hO hP φ₀ hφ₀) N) n)
        (e₀ : ∀ (M : SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A')
          (N : SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A),
          (pullbackObj α hO hP φ₀ hφ₀ M ⟶ N) ≃
            (M ⟶ pushforwardObj (semilinearHom α hO hP φ₀ hφ₀) N)),
      (∀ M N n w, (e M N n w).val =
          precompCochain (pullbackUnit α hO hP φ₀ hφ₀ M) w.val) ∧
      (∀ M N n w w' w'', w''.val = w.val + w'.val →
          (e M N n w'').val = (e M N n w).val + (e M N n w').val) ∧
      (∀ M N n w w', w'.val = δ n (n + 1) w.val →
          (e M N (n + 1) w').val = δ n (n + 1) (e M N n w).val) ∧
      (∀ M N g, e₀ M N g = semilinearHomEquiv (semilinearHom α hO hP φ₀ hφ₀) M N
          ((pullbackUnit α hO hP φ₀ hφ₀ M).postcomp g))
declarations.comment: the case of a morphism of small ringed sites whose functor is continuous, representably flat and final; for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi this is SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.exists_toposPullbackPushforwardHomEquiv

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.exists_toposPullbackPushforwardHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FRU.** Let `(f, f♯) : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` be a morphism of
ringed topoi, let `A` be a differential graded `O_C`-algebra, let `B` be a differential graded
`O_D`-algebra and let `φ : B ⟶ f_*A` be a unital homomorphism of differential graded
`O_D`-algebras (the datum of Tag 0FRT in the form of Remark 0FRG). Then for a right differential
graded `B`-module `N` and a right differential graded `A`-module `M`,
`Hom_{Mod^dg(B, d)}(N, f_*M) = Hom_{Mod^dg(A, d)}(f^*N, M)`.

Here `f^*N = f^*N ⊗_{f^*B} A` is `toposPullbackDg f φ hφ` (that is, `toposBaseChangeFunctor f φ
hφ`) and `f_*` is `toposPushforwardDg f φ hφ` (that is,
`toposPushforward (toposDirectImageModules f) φ hφ`). The identification `e` of the two
differential graded Hom objects is given in every degree `n`; it is `w ↦ η_N ∘ f_*(w)` for `η`
the unit of the adjunction `f^* ⊣ f_*` and `f_*(w)` the direct image of the homogeneous map `w`;
it is additive and carries the differential of the one Hom complex to the differential of the
other, so it is an isomorphism of complexes; it is natural in `N` and in `M`; and on morphisms of
differential graded modules it is the hom-set bijection of the adjunction `f^* ⊣ f_*`
(`toposPullbackPushforwardAdjunction`, that is, `toposBaseChangeAdjunction`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_toposPullbackPushforwardHomEquiv :
    ∃ e : ∀ (N : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} B)
        (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A) (n : ℤ),
        HomogeneousMap (X := X.toRingedSite) A ((toposPullbackDg f φ hφ).obj N) M n ≃
          HomogeneousMap (X := Y.toRingedSite) B N ((toposPushforwardDg f φ hφ).obj M) n,
      (∀ N M n w, toposCochain (e N M n w) =
        (Cochain.ofHom (toposBaseChangeUnit f φ hφ N).toHomologicalComplex).comp
          (toposCochain (toposPushforwardHomogeneous f φ hφ w)) (zero_add n)) ∧
      (∀ N M n w w' w'', toposCochain w'' = toposCochain w + toposCochain w' →
        toposCochain (e N M n w'') = toposCochain (e N M n w) + toposCochain (e N M n w')) ∧
      (∀ N M n w w', toposCochain w' = δ n (n + 1) (toposCochain w) →
        toposCochain (e N M (n + 1) w') = δ n (n + 1) (toposCochain (e N M n w))) ∧
      (∀ (N N' : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} B) M n (v : N' ⟶ N) w w',
        toposCochain w' =
          (Cochain.ofHom ((toposPullbackDg f φ hφ).map v).toHomologicalComplex).comp
            (toposCochain w) (zero_add n) →
        toposCochain (e N' M n w') =
          (Cochain.ofHom v.toHomologicalComplex).comp (toposCochain (e N M n w)) (zero_add n)) ∧
      (∀ N (M M' : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A) n (v : M ⟶ M') w w',
        toposCochain w' = (toposCochain w).comp (Cochain.ofHom v.toHomologicalComplex)
          (add_zero n) →
        toposCochain (e N M' n w') = (toposCochain (e N M n w)).comp
          (Cochain.ofHom ((toposPushforwardDg f φ hφ).map v).toHomologicalComplex) (add_zero n)) ∧
      (∀ (N : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} B) (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A)
          (g : (toposPullbackDg f φ hφ).obj N ⟶ M) w,
        toposCochain w = Cochain.ofHom g.toHomologicalComplex →
        toposCochain (e N M 0 w) = Cochain.ofHom
          ((toposPullbackPushforwardAdjunction f φ hφ).homEquiv N M g).toHomologicalComplex)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.dgExtendHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FRW in degree zero.** The homomorphisms `j_!M ⟶ N` of right differential graded
`A`-modules are the homomorphisms `M ⟶ j^*N` of right differential graded `A_U`-modules. The
bijection is the degreewise adjunction `j_{U!} ⊣ j_U^*` of ordinary sheaves of modules; the
content is that it matches the `A`-linear chain maps with the `A_U`-linear ones. This is the
degree-zero closed part of the hom-complex identification of the source; the identification in
every degree is `SheafOfModules.dgHomOfDegreeExtendEquiv_isHomComplexDifferential`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dgExtendHomEquiv (N : DifferentialGradedModule.{w, max u v m, max u v m} A) :
    (dgExtensionByZero.{m} O U A M ⟶ N) ≃ (M ⟶ N.over U)
declarations.comment: Hom(j_! M, N) = Hom(M, j^* N) in degree zero

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.dgExtensionByZeroAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FRW in degree zero, as an adjunction.** `j_! : Mod^dg(A_U, d) ⥤ Mod^dg(A, d)` is left
adjoint to `j^* : Mod^dg(A, d) ⥤ Mod^dg(A_U, d)`, which is the displayed identification of
Hom-sets of the source together with its naturality in both variables.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dgExtensionByZeroAdjunction :
    dgExtensionByZeroFunctor.{m} O U A ⊣ DifferentialGradedModule.overFunctor A U
declarations.comment: the identification is an adjunction `j_! ⊣ j^*` of differential graded modules

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.dgHomOfDegreeExtendEquiv_isHomComplexDifferential
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FRW.** The identification of Tag 0FRA of the homogeneous homomorphisms of degree `d`
out of `j_!M` with those into `j^*N` matches the differentials of the two hom-complexes. Read in
every degree together with `SheafOfModules.gradedHomOfDegreeExtendEquiv` and its naturality, this
is the displayed identification
`Hom_{Mod^dg(A, d)}(j_!M, N) = Hom_{Mod^dg(A_U, d)}(M, j^*N)`
of complexes of abelian groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgHomOfDegreeExtendEquiv_isHomComplexDifferential
    (N : DifferentialGradedModule.{w, max u v m, max u v m} A) (d : ℤ)
    (f : GradedHomOfDegree (GradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded (dgExtensionByZero.{m} O U A M))
      (GradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded N) d)
    (g : GradedHomOfDegree (GradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded (dgExtensionByZero.{m} O U A M))
      (GradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded N) (d + 1)) :
    IsHomComplexDifferential f g ↔
      IsHomComplexDifferential (A := A.over U) (M := M) (N := N.over U) (d := d)
        (gradedHomOfDegreeExtendEquiv.{m} (M := GradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded M)
          (N := GradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded N) O U A.toGradedAlgebra d f)
        (gradedHomOfDegreeExtendEquiv.{m} (M := GradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded M)
          (N := GradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded N) O U A.toGradedAlgebra (d + 1) g)
declarations.comment: Hom(j_! M, N) = Hom(M, j^* N) as complexes: compatibility with the differentials

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.dgExtendTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FRX.** The relative tensor product of the extension by zero of a right differential
graded `A_U`-module `M` with a left differential graded `A`-module `N` is the extension by zero
of the relative tensor product of `M` with the restriction of `N`:
`j_!M ⊗_A N = j_!(M ⊗_{A_U} N|_U)` as complexes of `O`-modules. In each degree it is the
isomorphism of Tag 0FRB, which sends the local section `j_!x ⊗ y` to `j_!(x ⊗ y)` and is natural
in `M` and in `N`; what is proved here is that it commutes with the differentials.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dgExtendTensorIso :
    dgExtendTensor.{m} O U A M N ≅ dgExtendSliceTensor.{m} O U A M N
declarations.comment: j_! M ⊗_A N = j_!(M ⊗_{A_U} N|_U) as complexes of O-modules

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.dgExtendTensorIso_naturality_left
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FRX, functoriality in the right differential graded module.** In every degree the
identification `j_!M ⊗_A N = j_!(M ⊗_{A_U} N|_U)` commutes with a homomorphism `M ⟶ M'` of right
differential graded `A_U`-modules; its components are the degreewise maps of the relative tensor
products induced by `j_!M ⟶ j_!M'`, respectively by `M ⟶ M'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgExtendTensorIso_naturality_left
    {M' : DifferentialGradedModule.{w, max u v m, max u v m} (A.over U)} (h : M ⟶ M') (n : ℤ) :
    RelativeTensor.gradedTensorMapRight (gradedExtensionByZeroMap.{m} O U A.toGradedAlgebra
          (GradedModule.ofDifferentialGradedMap h))
          (LeftGradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded N) n ≫
        (dgExtendTensorIso.{m} O U A M' N).hom.f n =
      (dgExtendTensorIso.{m} O U A M N).hom.f n ≫ (extendSheaf.{m} O U).map
        (RelativeTensor.gradedTensorMapRight (J := J.over U) (Osharp := O.over U)
          (GradedModule.ofDifferentialGradedMap h)
          ((LeftGradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded N).over U) n)
declarations.comment: functoriality of j_! M ⊗_A N = j_!(M ⊗_{A_U} N|_U) in M, in each degree

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.dgExtendTensorIso_naturality_right
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FRX, functoriality in the left differential graded module.** In every degree the
identification `j_!M ⊗_A N = j_!(M ⊗_{A_U} N|_U)` commutes with a homomorphism `N ⟶ N'` of left
differential graded `A`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgExtendTensorIso_naturality_right
    {N' : LeftDifferentialGradedModule.{w, max u v m, max u v m} A} (f : N ⟶ N') (n : ℤ) :
    RelativeTensor.gradedTensorMap (gradedExtensionByZero.{m} O U A.toGradedAlgebra
          (GradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded M))
          (LeftGradedModule.ofDifferentialGradedMap f) n ≫
        (dgExtendTensorIso.{m} O U A M N').hom.f n =
      (dgExtendTensorIso.{m} O U A M N).hom.f n ≫ (extendSheaf.{m} O U).map
        (RelativeTensor.gradedTensorMap (J := J.over U) (Osharp := O.over U)
          (GradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded M)
          (LeftGradedModule.overMap (LeftGradedModule.ofDifferentialGradedMap f) U) n)
declarations.comment: functoriality of j_! M ⊗_A N = j_!(M ⊗_{A_U} N|_U) in N, in each degree

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgShiftFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FRY.** The `k`-th shift functor `[k]` on the differential graded
category `Mod^dg(A, d)` of right differential graded `A`-modules: a functor of differential
graded categories, so additive and linear on `Hom` modules and compatible with the differential,
the composition and the identities.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dgShiftFunctor (k : ℤ) :
    DGCategory.DGFunctor (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category
      (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category
declarations.comment: the shift functor [k] on Mod^dg(A, d)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgShiftFunctor_complex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FRY, clauses (1) and (2).** The complex of sheaves of modules
underlying `M[k]` is the `k`-th shift of the complex underlying `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgShiftFunctor_complex (k : ℤ) (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A) :
    (asModule A ((dgShiftFunctor.{u, v, w} A k).obj (asObject A M))).complex =
      (CochainComplex.shiftFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) k).obj M.complex
declarations.comment: clauses (1) and (2): the underlying complex of M[k]

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgShiftFunctor_map_v
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FRY.** The components of the shift `f[k]` of a homogeneous morphism
`f` of degree `n` are those of `f`, multiplied by `(-1)^{k n}`. See the implementation notes:
the sign is forced by the requirement that `[k]` be a functor of differential graded
categories, and it is `+1` in the degree the source's clause is about.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgShiftFunctor_map_v (k n : ℤ) (M N : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A)
    (f : (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.Hom (asObject A M) (asObject A N) n)
    (p q : ℤ) (h : p + n = q) :
    HEq ((asCochain A ((dgShiftFunctor.{u, v, w} A k).map f)).v p q h)
      ((Int.negOnePow (k * n) : ℤ) • (asCochain A f).v (p + k) (q + k) (by omega))
declarations.comment: the components of f[k]

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgShiftFunctor_map_v_of_degree_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FRY.** On a homogeneous morphism of degree zero — in particular on a
morphism of `Mod(A, d)` — the shift `f[k]` has literally the same component maps as `f`, which
is the source's formulation.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgShiftFunctor_map_v_of_degree_zero (k : ℤ)
    (M N : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A)
    (f : (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.Hom (asObject A M) (asObject A N) 0)
    (p q : ℤ) (h : p + 0 = q) :
    HEq ((asCochain A ((dgShiftFunctor.{u, v, w} A k).map f)).v p q h)
      ((asCochain A f).v (p + k) (q + k) (by omega))
declarations.comment: f[k] has the same component maps as f in degree zero

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgShiftFunctor_zero_obj
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0FRY.** The zeroth shift is the identity on objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgShiftFunctor_zero_obj (M : (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.Obj) :
    (dgShiftFunctor.{u, v, w} A 0).obj M = M
declarations.comment: [0] is the identity

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgShiftFunctor_add_obj
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0FRY.** `[k + l] = [k] ∘ [l]` on objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgShiftFunctor_add_obj (k l : ℤ) (M : (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.Obj) :
    (dgShiftFunctor.{u, v, w} A (k + l)).obj M =
      (dgShiftFunctor.{u, v, w} A k).obj ((dgShiftFunctor.{u, v, w} A l).obj M)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgShiftFunctor_add_map
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0FRY.** `[k + l] = [k] ∘ [l]` on homogeneous morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgShiftFunctor_add_map (k l : ℤ) {M N : (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.Obj}
    {n : ℤ} (f : (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.Hom M N n) :
    HEq ((dgShiftFunctor.{u, v, w} A (k + l)).map f)
      ((dgShiftFunctor.{u, v, w} A k).map ((dgShiftFunctor.{u, v, w} A l).map f))
declarations.comment: [k + l] = [k] ∘ [l] on morphisms

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgShiftHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FRY.** The identification `Hom(L, M[k])^n = Hom(L, M)^{n + k}`, as
modules over the global sections of the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dgShiftHomEquiv (k : ℤ) (L M : (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.Obj)
    (n : ℤ) :
    (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.Hom L M (n + k) ≃ₗ[(limit X.O.obj : CommRingCat.{u})]
      (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.Hom L ((dgShiftFunctor.{u, v, w} A k).obj M) n
declarations.comment: Hom(L, M[k]) = Hom(L, M)[k]

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.dgShiftHomEquiv_d
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FRY.** The identification `Hom(L, M[k]) = Hom(L, M)[k]` is compatible
with the differentials: on the right hand side the differential of a shifted complex carries the
sign `(-1)^k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgShiftHomEquiv_d (k : ℤ) (L M : (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.Obj) (n : ℤ)
    (f : (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.Hom L M (n + k)) :
    dgShiftHomEquiv.{u, v, w} A k L M (n + 1)
        ((dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.d' (by omega : (n + k) + 1 = (n + 1) + k) f) =
      (-1 : (limit X.O.obj : CommRingCat.{u})) ^ k.natAbs •
        (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.d (dgShiftHomEquiv.{u, v, w} A k L M n f)
declarations.comment: Hom(L, M[k]) = Hom(L, M)[k] is compatible with the differentials

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.homotopyCategoryEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The homotopy category of right differential graded modules over a sheaf of differential
graded algebras is the homotopy category of their differential graded category.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homotopyCategoryEquivalence :
    HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A ≌ (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.K

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.homotopyCategoryEquivalence_obj
declarations.doc:
The identification of the two homotopy categories sends a differential graded module to
itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem homotopyCategoryEquivalence_obj (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A) :
    (homotopyCategoryEquivalence A).functor.obj ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A).obj M) =
      asObject A M

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.homotopyCategoryEquivalence_map
declarations.doc:
The identification of the two homotopy categories sends the homotopy class of a morphism
to the homotopy class of the closed degree-zero homogeneous map with the same underlying
cochain.
declarations.statement:
theorem homotopyCategoryEquivalence_map {M N : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A}
    (f : M ⟶ N) :
    ∃ c : (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category.Cocycle (asObject A M) (asObject A N),
      HEq (asCochain A c.val) (Cochain.ofHom f.toHomologicalComplex) ∧
        HEq ((homotopyCategoryEquivalence A).functor.map
            ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A).map f))
          (Quotient.mk ((dgCategoryData A).category.homotopySetoid _ _) c)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.Homotopy
declarations.doc:
A homotopy between two morphisms of right differential graded modules: a map of graded
modules of degree `-1` whose commutator with the differentials is the difference of the two
morphisms.
declarations.statement: structure Homotopy {M N : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} A} (f g : M ⟶ N)
declarations.comment: homotopies

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.Homotopic
declarations.doc:
Two morphisms of right differential graded modules are homotopic if there is a homotopy
between them.
declarations.statement: abbrev Homotopic {M N : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} A} (f g : M ⟶ N) : Prop
declarations.comment: homotopic morphisms

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory
declarations.doc:
The homotopy category of right differential graded modules over a sheaf of differential
graded algebras: the quotient of the category of right differential graded modules by the
homotopy relation.
declarations.statement: abbrev HomotopyCategory (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{t, a} R) : Type _
declarations.comment: the homotopy category

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.homotopic_congruence
declarations.doc: Being homotopic is an equivalence relation compatible with composition on either side.
declarations.statement:
theorem homotopic_congruence (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{t, a} R) :
    CategoryTheory.Congruence
      (fun {M N : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} A} (f g : M ⟶ N) => Homotopic f g)
declarations.comment: homotopy classes form a congruence

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory.hasProducts
declarations.doc: The homotopy category of right differential graded modules admits arbitrary products.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance hasProducts (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{t, a} R) :
    HasProducts.{m} (HomotopyCategory.{t, a, m} A)
declarations.comment: homotopy_products

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory.hasCoproducts_ringedSite
declarations.doc:
The homotopy category of right differential graded modules over a sheaf of differential
graded algebras on a ringed site admits arbitrary direct sums.

No side condition is carried: the two sheafification conditions of
`SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory.hasCoproducts` are discharged here
from the essential smallness of the site.
declarations.comment: homotopy_direct_sums

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.hasZeroObject
declarations.doc:
The zero differential graded module has unique homogeneous maps to and from every object in
every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasZeroObject :
    ∃ Z : (dgCategoryData A).category.Obj,
      (∀ (M : (dgCategoryData A).category.Obj) (n : ℤ),
        Nonempty ((dgCategoryData A).category.Hom Z M n) ∧
          Subsingleton ((dgCategoryData A).category.Hom Z M n)) ∧
      (∀ (M : (dgCategoryData A).category.Obj) (n : ℤ),
        Nonempty ((dgCategoryData A).category.Hom M Z n) ∧
          Subsingleton ((dgCategoryData A).category.Hom M Z n))
declarations.comment: axiom_a

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.hasBinaryBiproducts
declarations.doc:
Any two right differential graded modules admit a differential graded direct sum with closed
degree-zero structure maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasBinaryBiproducts
    (M N : (dgCategoryData A).category.Obj) :
    Nonempty (DGCategory.BinaryBiproductData (dgCategoryData A).category M N)
declarations.comment: axiom_a

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.shiftAxiomB
declarations.doc: The canonical DG shifts and Hom-complex shift isomorphisms for sheaf DG modules.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def shiftAxiomB : CanonicalShiftAxiomB.{u, v, w} A
declarations.comment: axiom_b

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.shiftPackage_nonempty
declarations.doc:
The degree-one shift of a right differential graded module exists with
the unchanged right action.
declarations.statement:
theorem shiftPackage_nonempty {A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{t, a} R}
    (K : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} A) : Nonempty (ShiftPackage K)
declarations.comment: fixed shifted module for the canonical cone projection

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.conePackage_nonempty
declarations.doc:
The mapping-cone construction exists with its componentwise action and
canonical inclusion and projection.
declarations.statement:
theorem conePackage_nonempty {A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{t, a} R}
    {K L : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} A} (f : K ⟶ L) : Nonempty (ConePackage f)
declarations.comment: existence of the cone with its canonical maps

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.conePackage
declarations.doc:
The cone and its canonical maps, characterized by the
mapping-cone complex and the direct-sum action.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conePackage {A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{t, a} R}
    {K L : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, m} A} (f : K ⟶ L) : ConePackage f
declarations.comment: the cone construction

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.coneSituation
declarations.doc:
The differential graded category of right sheaf modules admits cones whose connecting
arrows are the shifts of the original morphisms, using the fixed axiom (B) shift.
declarations.statement:
theorem coneSituation {X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.{u, u, u}}
    (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :
    ∃ S : DGCategory.ConeSituation
        (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category,
      S.shift = (shiftAxiomB A).axiomB

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory.instHasShift
declarations.doc:
The translation functors of the homotopy category of right differential graded modules,
lifted from the differential graded shifts along the identification of the two homotopy
categories.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance instHasShift : HasShift (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A) ℤ
declarations.comment: part (1): the shift functors

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory.instPretriangulated
declarations.doc: The homotopy category of right differential graded modules is pretriangulated.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance instPretriangulated :
    Pretriangulated (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)
declarations.comment: the pre-triangulated structure

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory.instIsTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FS7.** The homotopy category of right differential graded modules over a sheaf of
differential graded algebras on a ringed site is a triangulated category.
declarations.statement: instance instIsTriangulated : IsTriangulated (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory.distinguished_iff
declarations.doc:
A triangle of the homotopy category of right differential graded modules is distinguished
exactly when it is isomorphic to the triangle built from an admissible short exact sequence of
right differential graded modules, the connecting arrow being the class of `π d s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem distinguished_iff (T : Pretriangulated.Triangle (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)) :
    T ∈ Pretriangulated.distinguishedTriangles (C := HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A) ↔
      ∃ (M N P : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A) (f : M ⟶ N) (g : N ⟶ P)
        (δ : (quotient A).obj P ⟶
          (shiftFunctor (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A) (1 : ℤ)).obj ((quotient A).obj M))
        (E : DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact (A := (dgCategoryData.{u, v, w} A).category)
          (asObject A M) (asObject A N) (asObject A P)),
        cocycleOfHom A (dgCategoryData A) f = E.a ∧
          cocycleOfHom A (dgCategoryData A) g = E.b ∧
          Nonempty (T ≅ Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk ((quotient A).map f)
            ((quotient A).map g) δ) ∧
          Nonempty ((homotopyCategoryToDG A).mapTriangle.obj
              (Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk ((quotient A).map f) ((quotient A).map g) δ) ≅
            DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.associatedKTriangle
              (dgConeSituation A).shift E)
declarations.comment: part (2): the distinguished triangles

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory.shiftFunctor_obj
declarations.doc:
The degree-one translation of the homotopy category is the shift of differential graded
modules of Stacks 0FS5.
declarations.statement:
theorem shiftFunctor_obj (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A) :
    (shiftFunctor (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A) (1 : ℤ)).obj ((quotient A).obj M) =
      (quotient A).obj (shift M)
declarations.comment: part (1): the shift functors are those of Section 24.20

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.coneIdentity_hom_equiv_sections
declarations.doc:
A morphism from the identity cone is uniquely specified by a pair of global
sections `(x,y)` with `x = d y`; the equivalence evaluates at the canonical
unit elements in degrees zero and minus one.
declarations.statement:
theorem coneIdentity_hom_equiv_sections (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{t, a} R)
    (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, a} A) :
    ∃ e : (identityCone A ⟶ M) ≃
        { p : (M.complex.X 0).sections × (M.complex.X (-1)).sections //
          ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ,
            p.1.eval U =
              (M.complex.d (-1) 0).val.app U (p.2.eval U) },
      ∀ (f : identityCone A ⟶ M) (U : Cᵒᵖ),
        (e f).1.1.eval U =
          (f.toHomologicalComplex.f 0).val.app U
            (((conePackage (𝟙 (regularModule A))).componentIso 0).inv.val.app U
              ((biprod.inr : (regularModule A).complex.X 0 ⟶
                  (regularModule A).complex.X 1 ⊞ (regularModule A).complex.X 0).val.app U
                (A.one.eval U))) ∧
        (e f).1.2.eval U =
          (f.toHomologicalComplex.f (-1)).val.app U
            (((conePackage (𝟙 (regularModule A))).componentIso (-1)).inv.val.app U
              ((biprod.inl : (regularModule A).complex.X 0 ⟶
                  (regularModule A).complex.X 0 ⊞ (regularModule A).complex.X (-1)).val.app U
                (A.one.eval U)))

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.isGrothendieckAbelian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FS9.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `(A, d)` be a
differential graded `O`-algebra. The category `Mod(A, d)` of right differential graded
`A`-modules is a Grothendieck abelian category.

It is abelian and has filtered colimits by Tag 0FRJ, those colimits are exact by
`filteredColimits_exact`, it is locally small, and it has the separator
`⨁_{k, U} j_{U!} C_U[k]`, the direct sum of the shifts of the cones on the identities of the
restrictions of `A` to the objects of the site.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance isGrothendieckAbelian (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{t, a} R) :
    IsGrothendieckAbelian.{max u v a w} (DifferentialGradedModule.{t, a, max u v a w} A)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.IsGoodToposBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**A good right differential graded module**, with condition (3) read over the source's own
base changes. A right differential graded `A`-module is good when it is flat as a graded
module, K-flat, and for **every** base
change along a morphism of ringed topoi — a second ringed topos `X`, a morphism of ringed topoi
`f : X ⟶ Y`, a sheaf of differential graded algebras `B` on `X` and a **unital** homomorphism
`ψ : A ⟶ f_*B`, which is the adjoint form of the source's `φ : f⁻¹A ⟶ B` — a pullback of `P`
**exists**, as an object corepresenting `Q ↦ Hom_A(P, f_{*,ψ}Q)`, and every such object is flat
as a graded module and K-flat.

This is the quantification of Tag 0FSA's condition (3), binder for binder: a morphism of ringed
topoi, a differential graded algebra on its source, a homomorphism over it, and conditions (1)
and (2) required of the base-changed module. Nothing weaker and nothing stronger is quantified;
in particular condition (3) is **not** vacuous and **not** an assumption of the sought-for
isomorphism, the existential conjunct being part of the conclusion, and the second conjunct then
transports to every chosen pullback by `Functor.CorepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`.

The direct image of sheaves of modules is `toposDirectImageModules f`, whose lax monoidal
structure is `toposDirectImageModules_laxMonoidal` — unconditional, the coherence of Tag 03EL
being proved in `RingedToposPullbackCoherence.lean` — so the target `f_*B` of `ψ` is formed from
`f` alone and no monoidal datum is quantified beside it.

This is **not** `SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.IsGood` with its binders rewritten, and
the two are **incomparable**, which is why no implication between them is proved here in either
direction. `IsGood` quantifies bare functors of the two underlying categories: such a functor
induces no morphism of topoi and yet can carry a `PullbackData` — the identity functor of a site
at the trivial topology does, every presheaf being a sheaf there — so `IsGood` has clauses this
definition has none at. In the other direction a morphism of topoi need not be induced by any
functor of the two given sites, only by one of a site equivalent to the target (Tag 03CR, the
first step of the source's own proof of Tag 0FSB), so `IsGood` has no clause at such a base
change. What the two do share is conditions (1) and (2), verbatim; `isGradedFlat` and `isKFlat`
below are the comparison that exists.

`IsGoodCocontinuousBaseChange` and `IsGoodSiteBaseChange` restrict `IsGood`'s condition (3) to
fewer base changes, so each is implied by `IsGood` and each is incomparable with this definition
for the second of the two reasons above: a morphism of topoi induced by no functor of the two
given sites is a clause of this definition and of neither of theirs.

**Two restrictions on condition (3), stated rather than hidden.** First, the second ringed topos
carries `HasSheafify X.J (Type w)` and `HasSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{w}`, together with the
three `GrothendieckTopology.HasSheafCompose` instances a morphism of ringed topoi and its direct
image need. The sheafification of abelian groups is what the relative tensor product of the
conclusion needs; the sheafification of types is what lets a sheaf of graded sets and its degree
fibres be formed there, and it is the instance the proof for `A[S]` consumes. Mathlib supplies
both at `Type (max u v)` for a site `C : Type u` with `[Category.{v} C]`, so they hold wherever
the source's sites live, but a reading of condition (3) *without* them would be strictly stronger
and this is not it. Second, the coefficient universe `w` is common to the two ringed topoi, where
`Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.RingedToposHom` allows them independent; that boundary comes
from the differential graded transport and is recorded in
`DifferentialGradedToposDirectImage.lean`. Neither restriction is a hypothesis on a functor
between the two underlying categories — there is none — and neither is a smallness assumption.
declarations.statement: def IsGoodToposBaseChange (P : DifferentialGradedModule.{w, w, w} A) : Prop

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.dgExtensionByZeroRegular_isGoodToposBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FSB: the extension by zero `j_!A_U` of the restriction of `A` to the slice site at `U`
is a good right differential graded `A`-module.** It is flat as a graded module, it is K-flat,
and after every base change along a morphism of ringed topoi a pullback of it exists and every
pullback of it is again flat as a graded module and K-flat.

Conditions (1) and (2) are the two theorems of
`StacksFrontier/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf/GoodExtensionByZero.lean`, which run the source's
argument from Tags 0FRB, 0FRX and 0FSB. Condition (3) is Tag 0FSG's, read through the
identification of `j_!A_U` with the free differential graded module on the sheaf represented by
`U` in degree zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgExtensionByZeroRegular_isGoodToposBaseChange :
    IsGoodToposBaseChange.{u, v₁, u₁} (dgExtensionByZeroRegular.{u} Y.O U A)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.IsAdmissibleShortExact.isGoodToposBaseChange_right
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FSC, the third term.** If the first and the middle term of an admissible short exact
sequence of right differential graded modules are good in the sense of Tag 0FSA, so is the third.

Conditions (1) and (2) are two out of three for flatness and K-flatness. For condition (3) at a
base change `(f, B, ψ)`: the third term is the cokernel of the first map, so a pullback of it is
the cokernel of the pullbacks of the first two, a pullback being a value of a partial left adjoint
of the direct image; and every pullback of it sits in the pullback of the sequence, which is an
admissible short exact sequence whose first two terms are flat and K-flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGoodToposBaseChange_right (h : IsAdmissibleShortExact f g)
    (hK : IsGoodToposBaseChange.{w, v₁, u₁} K) (hL : IsGoodToposBaseChange.{w, v₁, u₁} L) :
    IsGoodToposBaseChange.{w, v₁, u₁} M
declarations.comment: the third term: if the first and the middle term of an admissible short exact sequence are good in the sense of 0FSA (`SheafOfModules.IsGoodToposBaseChange`, condition (3) over every morphism of ringed topoi), so is the third

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.IsAdmissibleShortExact.isGoodToposBaseChange_left
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FSC, the first term.** If the middle and the third term of an admissible short exact
sequence of right differential graded modules are good in the sense of Tag 0FSA, so is the first.

The shift `K[1]` is the third term of the admissible short exact sequence
`0 → C(1_M) → C(g) → K[1] → 0`, whose first two terms are cones of morphisms between good
modules and hence good; so `K[1]` is good by the third-term case, and `K` is good with it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGoodToposBaseChange_left (h : IsAdmissibleShortExact f g)
    (hL : IsGoodToposBaseChange.{w, v₁, u₁} L) (hM : IsGoodToposBaseChange.{w, v₁, u₁} M) :
    IsGoodToposBaseChange.{w, v₁, u₁} K
declarations.comment: the first term: if the middle and the third term of an admissible short exact sequence are good in the sense of 0FSA (`SheafOfModules.IsGoodToposBaseChange`, condition (3) over every morphism of ringed topoi), so is the first

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.IsAdmissibleShortExact.isGoodToposBaseChange_middle
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FSC, the middle term.** If the two outer terms of an admissible short exact sequence of
right differential graded modules are good in the sense of Tag 0FSA, so is the middle one.

The shift `L[1]` is the cone of the connecting morphism `δ : M ⟶ K[1]`, a morphism between good
modules, so it is good, and `L` is good with it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGoodToposBaseChange_middle (h : IsAdmissibleShortExact f g)
    (hK : IsGoodToposBaseChange.{w, v₁, u₁} K) (hM : IsGoodToposBaseChange.{w, v₁, u₁} M) :
    IsGoodToposBaseChange.{w, v₁, u₁} L
declarations.comment: the middle term: if the two outer terms of an admissible short exact sequence are good in the sense of 0FSA (`SheafOfModules.IsGoodToposBaseChange`, condition (3) over every morphism of ringed topoi), so is the middle one

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.PullbackData.preservesColimitsOfSize_functor
declarations.doc:
**The pullback of sheaves of differential graded modules along a morphism of ringed sites
preserves colimits of every shape.** The pullback is a left adjoint, the direct image along the
morphism being its right adjoint, and a left adjoint preserves colimits.
declarations.statement: theorem preservesColimitsOfSize_functor : PreservesColimitsOfSize.{w, w'} P.functor
declarations.comment: colimits commute with pullback: the pullback along a morphism of ringed sites preserves every colimit, being the left adjoint of the direct image

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.RelativeTensor.isColimit_dgTensorFunctor_mapCocone
declarations.doc:
**The relative tensor product `- ⊗_A N` carries a colimit cocone of right differential
graded modules to a colimit cocone of complexes of `O`-modules.** A cocone of complexes is
colimiting as soon as it is in every degree, and in degree `n` the functor is the composite of
forgetting the differential, a left adjoint, with degree `n` of the relative tensor product of
graded modules.
declarations.comment: the relative tensor product with a fixed left differential graded module commutes, as a functor to complexes, with the colimits of right differential graded modules

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.isGradedFlat_and_isKFlat_of_isColimit
declarations.doc:

differential graded modules, along any shape whose colimits of sheaves of modules are exact.
This is the conjunction that appears both as conditions (1) and (2) of
`IsGoodCocontinuousBaseChange` and as its condition (3) after a base change.

theorem isGradedFlat_and_isKFlat_of_isColimit {D : Type m} [Category.{m} D]

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.exists_flat_surjection
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FSE.** Every right differential graded `A`-module `M` receives a homomorphism from a
right differential graded `A`-module which is surjective, which is surjective on the sheaves of
cocycles, and whose source is flat as a graded module and K-flat.

The source is the first stage of the tower of the first proof of Tag 0FSH: the twisted extension
of the free differential graded module on the sheaf of graded sets of closed sections of `M` by
the free module on the sheaf of graded sets of boundary pairs of its homomorphism to `M`. It is
built from `M` alone.

Clause (2) is available on sections as well, as
`SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.exists_closed_preimage_towerStepMap`: every local
section of `M^n` killed by the differential is the image of a local section of the source killed
by the differential. Clause (3) is read here as conditions (1) and (2) of the definition of good
in Section 0FSA, flatness of the underlying graded module and K-flatness, over a ringed site and
with the ring universe and the module universe independent;
`SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.exists_good_surjection` concludes the same three clauses
for the same module with the third at the whole of goodness, over a ringed topos.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_flat_surjection (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, m, m} A) :
    ∃ (Q : DifferentialGradedModule.{t, m, m} A) (π : Q ⟶ M),
      (∀ n : ℤ, Epi (π.toHomologicalComplex.f n)) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ, Epi (HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap π.toHomologicalComplex n)) ∧
          RelativeTensor.IsGradedFlat (GradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded Q) ∧
            RelativeTensor.IsKFlat Q
declarations.comment: the resolution is built from M alone: the first stage of the tower of Tag 0FSH, the twisted extension of the free module on the closed sections of M by the free module on the boundary pairs of its homomorphism to M. Clause (2) is concluded as surjectivity on the sections killed by the differential, which is stronger than surjectivity of Ker(d_P) to Ker(d_M), and also as an epimorphism on the sheaves of cocycles. Clause (3) is concluded here as conditions (1) and (2) of the definition of good in Section 0FSA, flatness of the underlying graded module and K-flatness, over a ringed site and with the ring universe and the module universe independent, and the whole of condition (3) for this same module is concluded over a ringed topos by exists_good_surjection

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.exists_good_surjection
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FSE.** Every right differential graded `A`-module `M` receives a homomorphism from a
right differential graded `A`-module which is surjective, which is surjective on the sheaves of
cocycles, and whose source is good — `SheafOfModules.IsGoodToposBaseChange`, which is flat as a
graded module, K-flat, and such that along every morphism of ringed topoi out of the base, every
sheaf of differential graded algebras on its source and every unital homomorphism over it a
pullback exists and is again flat and K-flat.

The source is the first stage of the tower of the first proof of Tag 0FSH: the twisted extension
of the free differential graded module on the sheaf of graded sets of closed sections of `M` by
the free module on the sheaf of graded sets of boundary pairs of its homomorphism to `M`. It is
built from `M` alone.

Clause (2) is available on sections as well, as
`SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.exists_closed_preimage_towerStepMap`: every local
section of `M^n` killed by the differential is the image of a local section of the source killed
by the differential.

`SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.exists_flat_surjection` is the same three clauses with
the third read as conditions (1) and (2) of Section 0FSA alone, over a ringed site and with the
ring universe and the module universe independent.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_good_surjection [HasWeakSheafify Y.J (Type w)]
    (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{w, w, w} A) :
    ∃ (Q : DifferentialGradedModule.{w, w, w} A) (π : Q ⟶ M),
      (∀ n : ℤ, Epi (π.toHomologicalComplex.f n)) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ, Epi (HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap π.toHomologicalComplex n)) ∧
          IsGoodToposBaseChange.{w, v₁, u₁} Q

declarations.doc:
A sheaf of graded sets on a site: a sheaf of sets together with a degree morphism to the
constant sheaf of integers.
declarations.statement: structure SheafOfGradedSets (J : GrothendieckTopology C) [HasWeakSheafify J (Type w)]
declarations.comment: sheaf_of_graded_sets

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.freeGradedModuleData
declarations.doc:
**The free graded `A`-module on a sheaf of graded sets**, with its presentation, its
generators, its universal property and — whenever `A` is the graded algebra underlying a
differential graded algebra — its closed-generator differential.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def freeGradedModuleData : FreeGradedModuleData A S
declarations.comment: free_graded_mathcal_a_module_mathcal_a_mathcal_s

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.freeDGModule_isGoodToposBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FSG: the free differential graded module `A[S]` on a sheaf of graded sets is good**, at
the source's own quantification. Conditions (1) and (2) are the two unconditional theorems of
`FreeGradedModuleFlat.lean`; condition (3) is the corepresentability of `B[f⁻¹S]` together with
the flatness of every object corepresenting the same functor, which is
`SheafOfModules.nonempty_corepresentableBy_and_flat` at the geometric direct image. There is no
hypothesis beyond those under which `A[S]` exists.
declarations.statement:
theorem freeDGModule_isGoodToposBaseChange [HasWeakSheafify Y.J (Type w)]
    (S : Stacks.SheafOfGradedSets.{w} Y.J) :
    IsGoodToposBaseChange.{w, v₁, u₁} (freeDGModule S A)
declarations.comment: the free differential graded module on a sheaf of graded sets is good, with condition (3) of 0FSA read over morphisms of ringed topoi

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.freeDGModule_isGradedFlat
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FSG, condition (1) of Tag 0FSA.** The graded module underlying the free differential
graded `A`-module `A[S]` on a sheaf of graded sets is flat. The differential plays no part: the
underlying graded module of `A[S]` as a differential graded module **is** the free graded module
on `S` over the graded algebra underlying `A`, so this is
`SheafOfModules.freeGradedModule_isGradedFlat`.
declarations.statement:
theorem freeDGModule_isGradedFlat (D : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{t, m} (toRingCat J Osharp))
    (S : SheafOfGradedSets.{m} J) :
    RelativeTensor.IsGradedFlat (GradedModule.ofDifferentialGraded (freeDGModule S D))
declarations.comment: condition (1) of good (Stacks 0FSA) for the free graded module A[S] on a sheaf of graded sets: the underlying graded module is flat. No hypotheses; the source's own argument. Condition (2) is SheafOfModules.freeDGModule_isKFlat in this file; condition (3) is not proved here, and goodness is concluded at SheafOfModules.freeDGModule_isGoodToposBaseChange, where condition (3) is read over morphisms of ringed topoi as 0FSA states it. At the three site-indexed readings IsGood, IsGoodCocontinuousBaseChange and IsGoodSiteBaseChange condition (3) is still open -- see the implementation notes

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.freeDGModule_isKFlat
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FSG, condition (2) of Tag 0FSA.** The free differential graded `D`-module `D[S]` on a
sheaf of graded sets is K-flat: `D[S] ⊗_D N` is acyclic for every acyclic left differential
graded `D`-module `N`.

The proof is the source's. Degree `n` of `D[S] ⊗_D N` is the free graded module `N[S]` on `S`
with coefficients in `N`, by `SheafOfModules.freeTensorCoeffIso`, and under that identification
the differential is the signed degree-raising map of `N[S]`, by
`SheafOfModules.freeTensorCoeff_dgTensorDiff`. Exactness in degree `n + 1` is then the exactness
of a short complex of pieces of `N[S]` twisted by the sign automorphism, which
`SheafOfModules.coeffPiece_exact_sign` deduces from the exactness of `N` in the three adjacent
degrees; the transports matching the degrees of the three terms are
`SheafOfModules.coeffCastPieceIso`.
declarations.statement: theorem freeDGModule_isKFlat : RelativeTensor.IsKFlat (freeDGModule S D)
declarations.comment: condition (2) of good (Stacks 0FSA) for the free differential graded module D[S] on a sheaf of graded sets: D[S] tensor_D N is acyclic for every acyclic left differential graded D-module N. No hypotheses; the source's own argument. Condition (1) is SheafOfModules.freeDGModule_isGradedFlat in this file; condition (3) is not proved here, and goodness is concluded at SheafOfModules.freeDGModule_isGoodToposBaseChange, where condition (3) is read over morphisms of ringed topoi as 0FSA states it. At the three site-indexed readings IsGood, IsGoodCocontinuousBaseChange and IsGoodSiteBaseChange condition (3) is still open -- see the implementation notes

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.exists_good_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0FSH: every right differential graded `A`-module receives a quasi-isomorphism from a
good one.** Goodness is `SheafOfModules.IsGoodToposBaseChange`: flat as a graded module, K-flat,
and a pullback exists and is again flat and K-flat along every morphism of ringed topoi out of
the base, every sheaf of differential graded algebras on its source and every unital
homomorphism over it.

The source's tower is built here rather than assumed: the first stage is the free differential
graded module on the sheaf of graded sets of closed sections of `M`, good by Tag 0FSG; each
further stage is the twisted extension of the previous one by the free module on the boundary
pairs of its homomorphism to `M`, good by
`SheafOfModules.cone_freeDGModule_isGoodToposBaseChange` since a twisted extension is the cone of
a homomorphism out of a free module; and the resolution is the colimit of the resulting sequence,
good by `SheafOfModules.isGoodToposBaseChange_of_isColimit_nat`, the sequential shape being
filtered.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_good_quasiIso [HasWeakSheafify Y.J (Type w)]
    (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{w, w, w} A) :
    ∃ (Q : DifferentialGradedModule.{w, w, w} A) (f : Q ⟶ M),
      QuasiIso f.toHomologicalComplex ∧ IsGoodToposBaseChange.{w, v₁, u₁} Q

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.exists_flat_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Every right differential graded `A`-module receives a quasi-isomorphism from a right
differential graded `A`-module which is flat as a graded module and K-flat.**

The source's tower is built here rather than assumed: the first stage is the free differential
