declarations.comment: corrected form, clause (1): Ω^a_{X/S} ⟶ b_*Ω^a_{X'/S} is an isomorphism for every a ≥ 0, for f smooth and i a closed immersion of a scheme smooth over S whose image has EMPTY INTERIOR in X. The interior hypothesis is a correction: as stated (any closed immersion of S-smooth schemes) the clause is false when Z contains a nonempty open of X — for S = X = Z = Spec k the blowup is empty and 𝒪_X ⟶ 0 is not an isomorphism (counterexample Stacks.DeRham.exists_smooth_not_isIso_formsDirectImage, untagged). The blowup is AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase i.ker

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.isIso_formsDirectImageComparison_exceptionalDivisorToCentre
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FUU], clause (2), in corrected form.**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be smooth, let
`i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion with `Z` smooth over `S` and with image of empty interior in
`X`, let `E` be the exceptional divisor of the blowing up of `X` along `Z`, and let `p : E ⟶ Z`
be its structure morphism.  Then for every `a ≥ 0` the canonical map
`Ω^a_{Z/S} ⟶ p_*Ω^a_{E/S}` is an isomorphism.

As in clause (1), the hypothesis on the interior corrects the source: for `S = X = Z = Spec k`
the exceptional divisor is empty and `𝒪_Z ⟶ 0` is not an isomorphism
(`Stacks.DeRham.exists_smooth_not_isIso_formsDirectImageComparison_blowUpToBase`).  The proof is
the étale-local reduction of the source to clause (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0FUR], on the exceptional
divisor of the coordinate model.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_formsDirectImageComparison_exceptionalDivisorToCentre [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [Smooth f] [Smooth (i ≫ f)] (hint : interior (Set.range i.base) = ∅) (a : ℕ) :
    IsIso (formsDirectImageComparison (exceptionalDivisorToCentre i) (i ≫ f) (a : ℤ))
declarations.comment: corrected form, clause (2): Ω^a_{Z/S} ⟶ p_*Ω^a_{E/S} is an isomorphism for every a ≥ 0, for f smooth and i a closed immersion of a scheme smooth over S whose image has EMPTY INTERIOR in X; E is the exceptional divisor of AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase i.ker and p is AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalDivisorToCentre i. The interior hypothesis is a correction: as stated the clause is false when Z contains a nonempty open of X — for S = X = Z = Spec k, E is empty and 𝒪_Z ⟶ 0 is not an isomorphism (counterexample Stacks.DeRham.exists_smooth_not_isIso_formsDirectImageComparison_blowUpToBase, untagged)

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.isIso_blowupFormsDirectImage_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FUU], clause (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be smooth and let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed
immersion with `Z` smooth over `S`, of positive codimension at every point, i.e. containing no
nonempty open subset of `X`. Let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowing up of `X` along `Z`. Then for every
`a ≥ 0` the canonical map `Ω^a_{X/S} ⟶ b_*Ω^a_{X'/S}` is an isomorphism.

The positivity of the codimension is not stated in the source, and it is needed: where `Z`
contains an open subset `W` of `X` the ideal of the centre vanishes on `W`, the blowup is empty
over `W` (`AlgebraicGeometry.isEmpty_blowUp_bot`), and `𝒪_W = Ω^0_{W/S} ⟶ b_*Ω^0 = 0` is not an
isomorphism — for instance for `Z = X = S = Spec k`. The source's proof reduces to the
coordinate situation `𝐀^m_S ⊆ 𝐀^{m+n}_S` of Section 50.16, where `n ≥ 1`, and that is exactly
what the hypothesis provides in the charts of [Stacks, Tag 0FUE].
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_blowupFormsDirectImage_of_smooth (hint : interior (Set.range i.base) = ∅) (a : ℕ) :
    IsIso (blowupFormsDirectImage i f (a : ℤ))
declarations.comment: clause (1), corrected: false as written when Z contains a nonempty open of X (counterexample Z = X = S = Spec k: the blowup is empty and O_X → b_*O = 0), so stated for Z containing no nonempty open of X (positive codimension everywhere)

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.isIso_exceptionalFormsDirectImage_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FUU], clause (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be smooth and let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed
immersion with `Z` smooth over `S`, of positive codimension at every point, i.e. containing no
nonempty open subset of `X`. Let `p : E ⟶ Z` be the projection onto the centre of the
exceptional divisor of the blowing up of `X` along `Z`. Then for every `a ≥ 0` the canonical
map `Ω^a_{Z/S} ⟶ p_*Ω^a_{E/S}` is an isomorphism.

As for clause (1), the positivity of the codimension is not stated in the source and is needed:
for `Z = X` the exceptional divisor is empty and `𝒪_Z ⟶ p_*𝒪_E = 0` is not an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_exceptionalFormsDirectImage_of_smooth (hint : interior (Set.range i.base) = ∅)
    (a : ℕ) : IsIso (exceptionalFormsDirectImage i f (a : ℤ))
declarations.comment: clause (2), corrected: false as written when Z contains a nonempty open of X (counterexample Z = X = S = Spec k: E is empty and O_Z → p_*O_E = 0), so stated for Z containing no nonempty open of X (positive codimension everywhere)

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.isIso_formsDirectImage_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FUU], clauses (1) and (2), for a centre which is an effective Cartier
divisor.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion whose ideal sheaf is an effective Cartier
divisor, let `f : X ⟶ S` be any morphism, let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowing up of `X` along `Z`,
let `E` be its exceptional divisor and let `p : E ⟶ Z` be the structure morphism of `E` over the
centre.  Then in every degree the comparison maps

* `Ω^a_{X/S} ⟶ b_*Ω^a_{X'/S}` and
* `Ω^a_{Z/S} ⟶ p_*Ω^a_{E/S}`

are isomorphisms.

This is the degenerate case of the tag, and it is proved for a nearly trivial reason.  Blowing up
an effective Cartier divisor leaves the scheme unchanged ([Stacks, Tag 0807]), so `b` is an
isomorphism; the exceptional divisor is the fibre product of the blowup with the centre, so `p`
is the base change of `b` along `i` and is an isomorphism too.  Each comparison is then the unit
of the inverse image–direct image adjunction along an isomorphism, followed by the direct image
of a map which is an isomorphism by [Stacks, Tag 0FLV].

For a closed immersion of schemes smooth over `S` the ideal of the centre is locally generated by
a regular sequence, by [Stacks, Tag 0FUE], so the hypothesis here holds precisely when that
sequence has length one at every point of the centre — the centre is a divisor, of codimension
one wherever it is non-empty.  The empty centre satisfies it vacuously, its ideal being the unit
ideal.  The source states the tag for a centre of arbitrary codimension, and nothing of its
proof — the étale-local reduction of [Stacks, Tag 0FUE] to the coordinate situation
`𝐀^m_S ⊆ 𝐀^{m+n}_S` and the computation of [Stacks, Tag 0FUR] there — is used.  Smoothness of
`f` and of `i ≫ f` is not needed for this case and is not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_formsDirectImage_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor {S X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hi : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor i.ker) (a : ℤ) :
    IsIso (blowupFormsDirectImage i f a) ∧ IsIso (exceptionalFormsDirectImage i f a)
declarations.comment: clauses (1) and (2) in every integer degree, for a centre whose ideal sheaf is an effective Cartier divisor — a divisorial centre, which for a closed immersion of schemes smooth over S means codimension one at every point of the centre (the empty centre qualifying vacuously). This is the degenerate case of the tag, proved for a nearly trivial reason: blowing up an effective Cartier divisor leaves the scheme unchanged (Stacks 0807), so b : X' ⟶ X is an isomorphism, and the exceptional divisor is the fibre product of the blowup with the centre, so p : E ⟶ Z is the base change of b along i and is an isomorphism too; each comparison is then the unit of the inverse image–direct image adjunction along an isomorphism followed by the direct image of a map which is an isomorphism by Stacks 0FLV. A centre of codimension two or more is NOT proved, in any degree: none of the content of the source's proof — the étale-local reduction of Stacks 0FUE to the coordinate situation 𝐀^m_S ⊆ 𝐀^{m+n}_S, and the computation of Stacks 0FUR there — is used. In the other direction this is more general than the source: the smoothness of f and of i ≫ f is not needed for a divisorial centre and is not assumed, and every integer degree is covered, not only a ≥ 0. Clause (3) is not included: the derived comparison of Rb_* ∘ j_* against i_* ∘ Rp_* has no carrier in this library, so clause (3) has no canonical map to be a statement about

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.isIso_homology_blowupFormsDerivedComparison
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FUU], clause (3).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be smooth and `i : Z ⟶ X` a closed
immersion with `Z` smooth over `S`, let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowing up along `Z`, `E` its
exceptional divisor and `p : E ⟶ Z` the structure morphism. For every `a ≥ 0` and every `q ≥ 1`
the comparison `Rb_*Ω^a_{X'/S} ⟶ i_*Rp_*Ω^a_{E/S}`
(`Stacks.DeRham.blowupFormsDerivedComparison`) is an isomorphism on `H^q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homology_blowupFormsDerivedComparison [IsClosedImmersion i] [Smooth f]
    [Smooth (i ≫ f)] (a : ℕ) {q : ℤ} (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).map
      (blowupFormsDerivedComparison f i (a : ℤ)))
declarations.comment: clause (3): for f smooth and i a closed immersion of an S-smooth scheme, Rb_*Ω^a_{X'/S} ⟶ i_*Rp_*Ω^a_{E/S} is an isomorphism on cohomology sheaves in every degree q ≥ 1. No interior hypothesis is needed for this clause

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.isIso_homology_blowupFormsRestrictionDerivedComparison_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FUU], clause (3).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be smooth and let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed
immersion with `Z` smooth over `S`. Let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowing up of `X` along `Z`, with
exceptional divisor `E` and projection `p : E ⟶ Z`. Then for every `a ≥ 0` the canonical map
`Rb_*Ω^a_{X'/S} ⟶ i_*Rp_*Ω^a_{E/S}` is an isomorphism on cohomology sheaves in every degree
`q ≥ 1`, at any models of the derived categories.

No hypothesis on the codimension is needed: where `Z` contains an open of `X`, the blowup and the
exceptional divisor are empty there. The proof reduces, étale locally by [Stacks, Tag 0FUE], to
the coordinate situation of Section 50.16, where it is clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0FUR].
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homology_blowupFormsRestrictionDerivedComparison_of_smooth (a : ℕ) (q : ℤ)
    (hq : 0 < q) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).map
      (blowupFormsRestrictionDerivedComparison f i (a : ℤ)))
declarations.comment: clause (3): Rb_*Ω^a_{X'/S} ⟶ i_*Rp_*Ω^a_{E/S} is an isomorphism on cohomology sheaves in every degree q ≥ 1, every a ≥ 0, for a closed immersion of schemes smooth over S of any codimension

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.BlowupTriangle.exists_distTriang
declarations.doc:
**The blowup triangle of de Rham complexes.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be smooth and let `i : Z ⟶ X`
be a closed immersion with `Z` smooth over `S`, of any codimension. Let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the
blowing up of `X` along `Z`, with exceptional divisor `j : E ⟶ X'` and projection `p : E ⟶ Z`.
Then there is a distinguished triangle

`Ω^•_{X/S} ⟶ Rb_*Ω^•_{X'/S} ⊕ i_*Ω^•_{Z/S} ⟶ i_*Rp_*Ω^•_{E/S} ⟶ Ω^•_{X/S}[1]`

in `D(X, f^{-1}𝒪_S)` whose first map has components the canonical maps
`Ω^•_{X/S} ⟶ Rb_*Ω^•_{X'/S}` and `Ω^•_{X/S} ⟶ i_*Ω^•_{Z/S}`, and whose second map has components
the canonical map `Rb_*Ω^•_{X'/S} ⟶ i_*Rp_*Ω^•_{E/S}` and the negative of the canonical map
`i_*Ω^•_{Z/S} ⟶ i_*Rp_*Ω^•_{E/S}`, for any models of the derived categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_distTriang :
    ∃ δ : exceptionalDeRham f i ⟶ (deRham f)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk (biprod.lift (toBlowUp f i) (toCentre f i))
        (biprod.desc (blowUpToExceptional f i) (-centreToExceptional f i)) δ ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaves (inverseImageBase f)))
declarations.comment: the distinguished triangle Ω^•_{X/S} → Rb_*Ω^•_{X'/S} ⊕ i_*Ω^•_{Z/S} → i_*Rp_*Ω^•_{E/S} → Ω^•_{X/S}[1] in D(X, f^{-1}O_S) whose four maps are the canonical ones, the sign of i_*Ω^•_{Z/S} → i_*Rp_*Ω^•_{E/S} reversed; Z ⊂ X closed, X and Z smooth over S, any codimension

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.BlowupTriangle.exists_retraction_toBlowUp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FUW]: the de Rham complex splits off along a blowing up with smooth centre.**
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be smooth, `i : Z ⟶ X` a closed immersion with `Z` smooth over `S`, and
`b : X' ⟶ X` the blowing up of `X` along `Z`. If `Z` contains no nonempty open subset of `X` (in
particular, if `Z` has positive codimension in `X` at every point), the canonical map
`Ω^•_{X/S} ⟶ Rb_*Ω^•_{X'/S}` has a retraction in `D(X, (X ⟶ S)⁻¹𝒪_S)`, for any models of the
derived categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_retraction_toBlowUp [Smooth f] [Smooth (i ≫ f)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleSheaves (inverseImageBase f))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleSheaves (inverseImageBase (blowupMap i ≫ f)))]
    (hint : interior (Set.range i.base) = ∅) :
    ∃ r : blowUpDeRham f i ⟶ deRham f, toBlowUp f i ≫ r = 𝟙 _
declarations.comment: f : X -> S smooth, i : Z -> X a closed immersion with Z smooth over S, b : X' -> X the blowing up along Z; if Z has positive codimension in X at every point (used in the weaker form that Z contains no nonempty open subset of X), then Omega_{X/S} -> Rb_*Omega_{X'/S} has a splitting in D(X, (X -> S)^{-1}O_S), for any models

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.naiveCotangent_baseChange_truncGE_comparison_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FUY.** For `R → S → S'`, the canonical comparison from derived to termwise base
change of the naive cotangent complex induces an isomorphism after truncation in degrees at
least `-1`. This holds for the canonical presentation and for every polynomial presentation of
`S` over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem naiveCotangent_baseChange_truncGE_comparison_isIso
    {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} {S' : Type uS'}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra S S'] :
    letI : Functor.IsLeftAdjoint
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uS, uS', max uS' (max uR uS w)} (algebraMap S S')) :=
      ModuleCat.instIsLeftAdjointExtendScalars.{uS, uS', max uR uS w} (algebraMap S S')
    ∀ (derivedBaseChange : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uS' (max uR uS w)} S) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uS' (max uR uS w)} S'))
      (comparison : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ derivedBaseChange ⟶
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uS, uS', max uS' (max uR uS w)}
          (algebraMap S S')).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
      [derivedBaseChange.IsLeftDerivedFunctor comparison
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max uS' (max uR uS w)} S)
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ))],
    let canonicalMapInducesIso
        (L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max uS' (max uR uS w)} S) ℤ) : Prop :=
      ∃ f : ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t
                (C := ModuleCat.{max uS' (max uR uS w)} S')).truncGE (-1)).obj
              (derivedBaseChange.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L)) ⟶
            DerivedCategory.Q.obj
              (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uS, uS', max uS' (max uR uS w)}
                  (algebraMap S S')).mapHomologicalComplex
                (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj L),
        comparison.app L =
          ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t
              (C := ModuleCat.{max uS' (max uR uS w)} S')).truncGEπ (-1)).app
            (derivedBaseChange.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L)) ≫ f ∧
          IsIso f
    canonicalMapInducesIso
        (CochainComplex.mappingCone
          ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max uS' (max uR uS w)} S) 0).map
            (ModuleCat.ofHom
              (ULift.moduleEquiv.{uS, max uR uS,
                  max uS' (max uR uS w)}.symm.toLinearMap.comp
                ((NaiveCotangent.NL (NaiveCotangent.canonicalGenerators R S)).d.comp
                  ULift.moduleEquiv.{uS, max uR uS,
                    max uS' (max uR uS w)}.toLinearMap))))) ∧
      ∀ (ι : Type w) (P : Algebra.Generators R S ι),
        canonicalMapInducesIso
          (CochainComplex.mappingCone
            ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max uS' (max uR uS w)} S) 0).map
              (ModuleCat.ofHom
                (ULift.moduleEquiv.{uS, max (max uR uS) w,
                    max uS' (max uR uS w)}.symm.toLinearMap.comp
                  ((NaiveCotangent.NL P).d.comp
                    ULift.moduleEquiv.{uS, max uR w,
                      max uS' (max uR uS w)}.toLinearMap)))))

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.naiveCotangentComplex_baseChange_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FUZ.** Formation of the naive cotangent complex commutes with arbitrary base change
on `H⁰` and is surjective on `H⁻¹`, both for a chosen polynomial presentation and for the
canonical one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem naiveCotangentComplex_baseChange_homology
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {T : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R T] {ι : Type t} (P : Algebra.Generators R S ι) :
    let S' := T ⊗[R] S
    letI : Algebra S S' := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    let P' := P.baseChange T
    let h := (P.baseChangeFromBaseChange T).comp (P.toExtension.toBaseChange T)
    let d := AlgebraTensorModule.lTensor S' S' P.toExtension.cotangentComplex
    let f₁ := (Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map h).liftBaseChange S'
    let f₀ := (Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map h).liftBaseChange S'
    P'.toExtension.cotangentComplex ∘ₗ f₁ = f₀ ∘ₗ d ∧
      (∀ y, ∃ x, y - f₀ x ∈ LinearMap.range P'.toExtension.cotangentComplex) ∧
      (∀ x, f₀ x ∈ LinearMap.range P'.toExtension.cotangentComplex ↔
        x ∈ LinearMap.range d) ∧
      (∀ y, P'.toExtension.cotangentComplex y = 0 →
        ∃ x, d x = 0 ∧ f₁ x = y) ∧
      let Pc := Algebra.Generators.self R S
      let Pc' := Algebra.Generators.self T S'
      let hc := (Pc.defaultHom Pc').toExtensionHom
      let dc := AlgebraTensorModule.lTensor S' S' Pc.toExtension.cotangentComplex
      let fc₁ := (Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map hc).liftBaseChange S'
      let fc₀ := (Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map hc).liftBaseChange S'
      Pc'.toExtension.cotangentComplex ∘ₗ fc₁ = fc₀ ∘ₗ dc ∧
        (∀ y, ∃ x, y - fc₀ x ∈ LinearMap.range Pc'.toExtension.cotangentComplex) ∧
        (∀ x, fc₀ x ∈ LinearMap.range Pc'.toExtension.cotangentComplex ↔
          x ∈ LinearMap.range dc) ∧
        ∀ y, Pc'.toExtension.cotangentComplex y = 0 →
          ∃ x, dc x = 0 ∧ fc₁ x = y

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.naiveCotangentComplex_isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude
declarations.doc:
The naive cotangent complex of a local complete intersection is perfect and
has Tor-amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem naiveCotangentComplex_isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (h : RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (algebraMap A B))
    (derivedTensor :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} B) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} B) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} B))
    (comparison : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v} B,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} B) 0).obj M) ⟶
        (tensorModuleRight M).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerived : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v} B,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} B) 0).obj M)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison M)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max u v} B) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect (naiveCotangentObject A B) ∧
      HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived
        (naiveCotangentObject A B) (-1) 0

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.finite_projective_ker_naiveCotangent_baseChange_homology_negOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV1.** In a pushout square of rings, if both parallel maps are local complete
intersections, then the kernel of the base-change map on degree `-1` homology of the naive
cotangent complex is a finite projective module over the pushout.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finite_projective_ker_naiveCotangent_baseChange_homology_negOne
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {A' : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing A'] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A A']
    (h : RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (algebraMap A B)) :
    let B' := A' ⊗[A] B
    letI : Algebra B B' := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (algebraMap A' B') →
      let P := Algebra.Generators.self A B
      let P' := Algebra.Generators.self A' B'
      let comparison := (P.defaultHom P').toExtensionHom
      let d := AlgebraTensorModule.lTensor B' B' P.toExtension.cotangentComplex
      let f := (Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map comparison).liftBaseChange B'
      Module.Finite B' (LinearMap.ker (f.domRestrict (LinearMap.ker d))) ∧
        Module.Projective B' (LinearMap.ker (f.domRestrict (LinearMap.ker d)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.Sites.homologyNegOneIsoConormalSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV2, degree `-1` clause.**  For an immersion of schemes `i : Z ⟶ X` the degree
`-1` cohomology sheaf of the naive cotangent complex `NL_{Z/X}` is the conormal sheaf
`𝒞_{Z/X}` of `Z` in `X`.

Three identifications are composed.  `NL_{Z/X}` is the naive cotangent complex of the
*canonical polynomial* presentation of `𝒪_Z` over `i^{-1}𝒪_X`, so its degree `-1` term is the
conormal sheaf of that presentation and not of `i^{-1}𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_Z` itself; Stacks 08TL for the
trivial presentation (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.quasiIso_trivialNaiveCotangentComplexComparison`)
identifies the cohomology of the two complexes.  The complex of the trivial presentation is
`I/I² ⟶ 0`, so its degree `-1` cohomology is `I/I²` on the nose
(`Stacks.Conormal.Sites.trivialHomologyNegOneIso`).  Finally
`Stacks.Conormal.Sites.sitesConormalSheafIsoConormalSheaf` identifies that sites-level `I/I²`
with the geometric conormal sheaf `𝒞_{Z/X}`.
declarations.comment: degree -1 clause: H^{-1}(NL_{Z/X}) is the conormal sheaf C_{Z/X}

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.Sites.quasiIso_conormalShiftComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV2, the shift.**  For an immersion of schemes `i : Z ⟶ X` the canonical chain
map from `𝒞_{Z/X}[1]` — the cochain complex with the conormal sheaf of `Z` in `X` in degree
`-1` and zero in every other degree — to the naive cotangent complex `NL_{Z/X}` is a
quasi-isomorphism.

The source states the conclusion as an isomorphism `NL_{Z/X} ≅ 𝒞_{Z/X}[1]` in `D(𝒪_Z)`.  A
quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes of sheaves of `𝒪_Z`-modules is the scheme-level content
of that statement: it is a map of honest complexes which the localisation functor to the derived
category inverts.  The statement is given in that form, and the clause label says so.
declarations.statement: theorem quasiIso_conormalShiftComparison : QuasiIso (conormalShiftComparison i)
declarations.comment: shift clause as a quasi-isomorphism of complexes C_{Z/X}[1] ⟶ NL_{Z/X}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isZero_homology_zero_naiveCotangentComplex_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV2, degree `0` clause.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be an immersion of schemes.  Then the
degree `0` cohomology sheaf of the naive cotangent complex `NL_{Z/X}` vanishes.

The source states that `NL_{Z/X}` is isomorphic to `C_{Z/X}[1]` in `D(𝒪_Z)`, with `C_{Z/X}` the
conormal sheaf of `Z` in `X`.  Since both sides are complexes concentrated in one degree, that
assertion is the conjunction of the two degreewise statements `H⁻¹(NL_{Z/X}) ≅ C_{Z/X}` and
`H⁰(NL_{Z/X}) = 0`.  The second is what is proved here; the first is not proved, here or
anywhere in this library, and the attribute is scoped accordingly.
declarations.comment: degreewise form of the shift statement, degree 0 clause only: H^0(NL_{Z/X}) = 0; NOT the identification of H^{-1}(NL_{Z/X}) with the conormal sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentCompositionTriangle.coneMap_comp_fst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV3**, the comparison.  The canonical map
`f^*NL_{Y/Z} ⟶ C(NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y})[-1]` of Stacks 0E1Z, composed with the projection of the
mapping cocone onto `NL_{X/Z}`, is the negative of the canonical map `f^*NL_{Y/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Z}`.
This is what makes the comparison a lift of that canonical map; the sign is the one between the
projection out of the mapping cocone and the projection of Stacks 0E1Z.
declarations.statement:
theorem coneMap_comp_fst :
    ringedSpaceNaiveCotangentConeMap f g ≫ mappingCocone.fst (relativeNaiveCotangentMap f g) =
      -pulledNaiveCotangentMap f g
declarations.comment: the canonical map f^*NL_{Y/Z} -> C(NL_{X/Z} -> NL_{X/Y})[-1] of 0E1Z and its compatibility, up to the sign of the cocone projection, with the canonical map f^*NL_{Y/Z} -> NL_{X/Z}; NOT its invertibility, which is where the complete intersection hypothesis enters and which is isIso_Q_map_coneMap_of_lci

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentCompositionTriangle.triangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV3**, the triangle.  The triangle on the canonical map `NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y}`,
with the shift by `-1` of its cone as first vertex, is a distinguished triangle of `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement: theorem triangle_distinguished : triangle f g ∈ distTriang _
declarations.comment: the distinguished triangle C(NL_{X/Z} -> NL_{X/Y})[-1] -> NL_{X/Z} -> NL_{X/Y} -> C(NL_{X/Z} -> NL_{X/Y})[-1][1] of D(O_X), whose second morphism is the canonical map, together with the canonical map of 0E1Z into its first vertex (coneMap_comp_fst); NOT the invertibility of that comparison, which is where the complete intersection hypothesis enters, and NOT the recovery of the six-term exact sequence of 0E44 -- those two are isIso_Q_map_coneMap_of_lci and lciTriangle_recovers_sixTerm, and the triangle with f^*NL_{Y/Z} as its first vertex is lciTriangle_distinguished

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentCompositionTriangle.isIso_Q_map_coneMap_of_lci
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV3, the isomorphism.**  For morphisms of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` with
`f` a local complete intersection morphism, the canonical map

`f^*NL_{Y/Z} ⟶ C(NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y})[-1]`

of Stacks 0E1Z is an isomorphism in `D(𝒪_X)`.

This is the reduction the source makes: the triangle of Stacks 0FV3 is the triangle of the
mapping cocone of `NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y}` with its first vertex replaced by `f^*NL_{Y/Z}` along
this isomorphism.  The map is surjective on `H^{-1}` and an isomorphism on `H⁰` for an arbitrary
pair of composable morphisms of ringed spaces; injectivity on `H^{-1}` is what the complete
intersection hypothesis supplies, through Stacks 07D4 at the stalks.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_Q_map_coneMap_of_lci (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map
      (ringedSpaceNaiveCotangentConeMap f.toLRSHom.toShHom g.toLRSHom.toShHom))
declarations.comment: the canonical map f^*NL_{Y/Z} -> C(NL_{X/Z} -> NL_{X/Y})[-1] of 0E1Z is an ISOMORPHISM in D(O_X) when X -> Y is a complete intersection morphism, which is the reduction the source's proof makes

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentCompositionTriangle.lciTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV3.**  For morphisms of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` with `f` a local
complete intersection morphism, the canonical triangle

`f^*NL_{Y/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y} ⟶ f^*NL_{Y/Z}[1]`

is a distinguished triangle of `D(𝒪_X)`: it is the triangle of the mapping cocone of the
canonical map `NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y}`, which is distinguished, with its first vertex replaced along
the comparison of Stacks 0E1Z, an isomorphism by `isIso_Q_map_coneMap_of_lci`.  Its first two
morphisms are the canonical maps, by `lciTriangle_mor₁` and `lciTriangle_mor₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lciTriangle_distinguished (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    lciTriangle f g hf ∈ distTriang _
declarations.comment: the canonical distinguished triangle f^*NL_{Y/Z} -> NL_{X/Z} -> NL_{X/Y} -> f^*NL_{Y/Z}[1] of D(O_X) for a complete intersection morphism X -> Y, with its first two morphisms the canonical maps (lciTriangle_mor₁, lciTriangle_mor₂)

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentCompositionTriangle.lciTriangle_recovers_sixTerm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV3: the triangle recovers the six-term exact sequence of Stacks 0E44.**  The long
exact sequence of cohomology sheaves of the triangle

`f^*NL_{Y/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y} ⟶ f^*NL_{Y/Z}[1]`

is the six-term exact sequence

`H^{-1}(f^*NL_{Y/Z}) ⟶ H^{-1}(NL_{X/Z}) ⟶ H^{-1}(NL_{X/Y}) --∂--> H⁰(f^*NL_{Y/Z}) ⟶`
`H⁰(NL_{X/Z}) ⟶ H⁰(NL_{X/Y}) ⟶ 0`:

its five assertions are exactness at the four interior terms and the final `⟶ 0`.  The two arrows
are the maps induced by the canonical chain maps, whose images under `DerivedCategory.Q` are the
first two morphisms of the triangle by `lciTriangle_mor₁` and `lciTriangle_mor₂`, and the
connecting morphism is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSpaceJacobiZariskiConnecting`, the connecting
morphism of the long exact sequence of the cone read through the comparison of Stacks 0E1Z.  The
sequence has six terms and no more because all three vertices have vanishing cohomology outside
degrees `-1` and `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lciTriangle_recovers_sixTerm (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    (lciTriangle f g hf).mor₁ =
        DerivedCategory.Q.map
          (pulledNaiveCotangentMap f.toLRSHom.toShHom g.toLRSHom.toShHom) ∧
      (lciTriangle f g hf).mor₂ =
        DerivedCategory.Q.map
          (relativeNaiveCotangentMap f.toLRSHom.toShHom g.toLRSHom.toShHom) ∧
      (ringedSpaceJacobiZariskiHomologySequence f.toLRSHom.toShHom
        g.toLRSHom.toShHom (-1)).Exact ∧
      (ShortComplex.mk
        (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
          (relativeNaiveCotangentMap f.toLRSHom.toShHom g.toLRSHom.toShHom) (-1))
        (ringedSpaceJacobiZariskiConnecting f.toLRSHom.toShHom g.toLRSHom.toShHom)
        (homologyMap_comp_ringedSpaceJacobiZariskiConnecting
          f.toLRSHom.toShHom g.toLRSHom.toShHom)).Exact ∧
      (ShortComplex.mk
        (ringedSpaceJacobiZariskiConnecting f.toLRSHom.toShHom g.toLRSHom.toShHom)
        (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
          (pulledNaiveCotangentMap f.toLRSHom.toShHom g.toLRSHom.toShHom) 0)
        (ringedSpaceJacobiZariskiConnecting_comp_homologyMap
          f.toLRSHom.toShHom g.toLRSHom.toShHom)).Exact ∧
      (ringedSpaceJacobiZariskiHomologySequence f.toLRSHom.toShHom
        g.toLRSHom.toShHom 0).Exact ∧
      Epi (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
        (relativeNaiveCotangentMap f.toLRSHom.toShHom g.toLRSHom.toShHom) 0)
declarations.comment: the recovery of the six-term exact sequence of 0E44 from lciTriangle: its first two morphisms are the images under Q of the canonical chain maps f^*NL_{Y/Z} -> NL_{X/Z} and NL_{X/Z} -> NL_{X/Y}, and the six-term sequence of the maps those induce on cohomology sheaves, with the connecting morphism of the long exact sequence of the cone, is exact at its four interior terms and ends in `-> 0`

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentCompositionTriangle.connecting_comp_homologyMap_eq_homologyδOfTriangle
declarations.doc:
**The connecting map of Stacks 0E44 is a triangle connecting morphism.**  Composed with the
map induced on `H⁰` by the canonical map of Stacks 0E1Z it is the connecting morphism of the long
exact sequence of the triangle

`C(NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y})[-1] ⟶ NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y} ⟶ C(NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y})[-1][1]`

of the mapping cocone, whose image in `D(𝒪_X)` is the triangle of Stacks 0FV3 before its first
vertex is replaced by `f^*NL_{Y/Z}` along that same map.
declarations.statement:
theorem connecting_comp_homologyMap_eq_homologyδOfTriangle :
    jacobiZariskiConnecting f g ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
        (ringedSpaceNaiveCotangentConeMap (ringedSpaceHom f) (ringedSpaceHom g)) 0 =
      CochainComplex.homologyδOfTriangle
        (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.triangle (iteratedRelativeMap f g)) (-1) 0 (by omega)
declarations.comment: the connecting map of the six-term sequence of 0E44, read along H^0 of the canonical map of 0E1Z, is the connecting morphism of the long exact sequence of the triangle of the mapping cocone of NL_{X/Z} -> NL_{X/Y}

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentCompositionTriangle.lciSchemeTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV3.**  For morphisms of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` with `f` a local
complete intersection morphism, the canonical triangle

`f^*NL_{Y/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y} ⟶ f^*NL_{Y/Z}[1]`

is a distinguished triangle of `D(𝒪_X)`, with `NL_{X/Z}` the naive cotangent complex of `f ≫ g`
and its first two morphisms the two canonical chain maps of the six-term exact sequence of
Stacks 0E44.

It is the triangle of `Stacks.NaiveCotangentCompositionTriangle.lciTriangle` with its second
vertex transported along the identification of `NL_{f ≫ g}` with its iterated spelling.
declarations.statement:
theorem lciSchemeTriangle_distinguished (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    lciSchemeTriangle f g hf ∈ distTriang _
declarations.comment: the canonical distinguished triangle f^*NL_{Y/Z} -> NL_{X/Z} -> NL_{X/Y} -> f^*NL_{Y/Z}[1] of D(O_X) for a complete intersection morphism X -> Y, written over the complexes and the two canonical chain maps of the six-term sequence of 0E44 (lciSchemeTriangle_mor₁, lciSchemeTriangle_mor₂)

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentCompositionTriangle.δ_lciSchemeTriangle_comp_map
declarations.doc:
**The connecting morphism of the triangle of Stacks 0FV3.**  Composed with the map induced on
`H⁰` by the canonical map of Stacks 0E1Z it is the negative of the connecting morphism of the
triangle of the mapping cocone of `NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y}`.  The sign is the one between the
projection out of the mapping cocone and the projection through which Stacks 0E1Z characterises
its canonical map; it is the price of the triangle's first morphism being the canonical map
`f^*NL_{Y/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Z}` with no sign.
declarations.statement:
theorem δ_lciSchemeTriangle_comp_map (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ (lciSchemeTriangle f g hf) (-1) 0 (by omega) ≫
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
              (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology (X.toRingedSpace : TopCat))
              X.toRingedSpace.sheaf)) (0 : ℤ)).map (DerivedCategory.Q.map
          (ringedSpaceNaiveCotangentConeMap (ringedSpaceHom f) (ringedSpaceHom g))) =
      -(DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ
        (triangle (ringedSpaceHom f) (ringedSpaceHom g)) (-1) 0 (by omega))
declarations.comment: the connecting morphism of the triangle, read along H^0 of the canonical map of 0E1Z, is the negative of the connecting morphism of the long exact sequence of the triangle of the mapping cocone of NL_{X/Z} -> NL_{X/Y}

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentCompositionTriangle.lciSchemeTriangle_recovers_sixTerm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV3: the triangle recovers the six-term exact sequence of Stacks 0E44.**  For
morphisms of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` with `f` a local complete intersection
morphism, the long exact sequence of cohomology sheaves of the distinguished triangle

`f^*NL_{Y/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Z} ⟶ NL_{X/Y} ⟶ f^*NL_{Y/Z}[1]`

is the six-term exact sequence

`H^{-1}(f^*NL_{Y/Z}) ⟶ H^{-1}(NL_{X/Z}) ⟶ H^{-1}(NL_{X/Y}) --∂--> f^*Ω_{Y/Z} ⟶ Ω_{X/Z} ⟶`
`Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ 0`

of Stacks 0E44.  The nine assertions below are: its first two morphisms are the images under
`DerivedCategory.Q` of the two canonical chain maps `pullbackToTotalMap` and
`totalToRelativeMap` of Stacks 0E44, which induce four of the five arrows; its connecting
morphism and the connecting map `jacobiZariskiConnecting` of Stacks 0E44 both become, along the
map induced on `H⁰` by the canonical map of Stacks 0E1Z, the connecting morphism of the long
exact sequence of the triangle of the mapping cocone — up to the sign of the cocone projection;
and the sequence of those arrows is exact at its four interior terms and ends in `⟶ 0`.  The
last three terms are `f^*Ω_{Y/Z}`, `Ω_{X/Z}` and `Ω_{X/Y}` by
`Stacks.NaiveCotangentSixTermSequence.pullbackHomologyZeroIso` and Stacks 0D0J.
declarations.statement:
theorem lciSchemeTriangle_recovers_sixTerm (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    (lciSchemeTriangle f g hf).mor₁ = DerivedCategory.Q.map (pullbackToTotalMap f g) ∧
      (lciSchemeTriangle f g hf).mor₂ = DerivedCategory.Q.map (totalToRelativeMap f g) ∧
      DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ (lciSchemeTriangle f g hf) (-1) 0 (by omega) ≫
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
              (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology (X.toRingedSpace : TopCat))
              X.toRingedSpace.sheaf)) (0 : ℤ)).map (DerivedCategory.Q.map
            (ringedSpaceNaiveCotangentConeMap (ringedSpaceHom f) (ringedSpaceHom g))) =
        -(DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ
          (triangle (ringedSpaceHom f) (ringedSpaceHom g)) (-1) 0 (by omega)) ∧
      jacobiZariskiConnecting f g ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
          (ringedSpaceNaiveCotangentConeMap (ringedSpaceHom f) (ringedSpaceHom g)) 0 =
        CochainComplex.homologyδOfTriangle
          (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.triangle (iteratedRelativeMap f g)) (-1) 0 (by omega) ∧
      (ShortComplex.mk (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (pullbackToTotalMap f g) (-1))
        (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (totalToRelativeMap f g) (-1))
        (homologyMap_pullbackToTotalMap_comp_totalToRelativeMap f g (-1))).Exact ∧
      (ShortComplex.mk (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (totalToRelativeMap f g) (-1))
        (jacobiZariskiConnecting f g)
        (homologyMap_totalToRelativeMap_comp_connecting f g)).Exact ∧
      (ShortComplex.mk (jacobiZariskiConnecting f g)
        (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (pullbackToTotalMap f g) 0)
        (connecting_comp_homologyMap_pullbackToTotalMap f g)).Exact ∧
      (ShortComplex.mk (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (pullbackToTotalMap f g) 0)
        (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (totalToRelativeMap f g) 0)
        (homologyMap_pullbackToTotalMap_comp_totalToRelativeMap f g 0)).Exact ∧
      Epi (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (totalToRelativeMap f g) 0)
declarations.comment: the recovery of the six-term exact sequence of 0E44 from lciSchemeTriangle: its first two morphisms are the images under Q of the two canonical chain maps of 0E44, its connecting morphism and the connecting map of 0E44 are both the connecting morphism of the long exact sequence of the triangle of the mapping cocone read along H^0 of the canonical map of 0E1Z, and the six-term sequence of those arrows is exact at its four interior terms and ends in `-> 0`

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentFormallySmoothComparison.quasiIso_naiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle
declarations.doc:
**The 0D0L input of [Stacks Project, Tag 0FV4].**  For a formally smooth morphism of schemes
`g : P ⟶ Y` the canonical chain map `NL_{P/Y} ⟶ Ω_{P/Y}[0]` is a quasi-isomorphism: the naive
cotangent complex of `g` is identified with its sheaf of relative differentials placed in degree
`0`.

This is the step the proof of 0FV4 records as `NL_{P/Y} = Ω_{P/Y}`.  Its two ingredients are the
clauses of [Stacks Project, Tag 0D0L] proved for a formally smooth morphism, namely the vanishing
of the cohomology sheaves outside degree `0`
(`Stacks.Smooth.isZero_homology_naiveCotangentComplex_of_formallySmooth`, which rests on
`Stacks.Smooth.isZero_homology_negOne_naiveCotangentComplex_of_formallySmooth`), together with
the degree-zero identification `H⁰(NL_{P/Y}) = Ω_{P/Y}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 0D0J].  Those are
statements about cohomology sheaves; what is added here is the chain map itself, which is what
0FV4 uses.

As in `Stacks.Conormal.Sites.quasiIso_conormalShiftComparison` — the corresponding step of 0FV4
coming from [Stacks Project, Tag 0FV2] — the conclusion is given as a quasi-isomorphism of
complexes of sheaves of `𝒪_P`-modules, which is the chain-level content of the source's
identification in `D(𝒪_P)`: a map of honest complexes that the localisation functor to the
derived category inverts.

The other three steps of 0FV4's proof are not covered; see the `Scope` section of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_naiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle
    (hg : Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme g) :
    QuasiIso (naiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle g)
declarations.comment: the 0D0L input NL_{P/Y} = Omega_{P/Y} as a quasi-isomorphism of complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentFormallySmoothComparison.isIso_Q_map_naiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle
declarations.doc:
**The 0D0L input of [Stacks Project, Tag 0FV4], read in `D(𝒪_P)`.**  For a formally smooth
morphism of schemes `g : P ⟶ Y` the canonical chain map `NL_{P/Y} ⟶ Ω_{P/Y}[0]` becomes an
isomorphism in the derived category of sheaves of `𝒪_P`-modules; that is, `NL_{P/Y}` and
`Ω_{P/Y}[0]` are canonically isomorphic objects of `D(𝒪_P)`.

This is the form `NL_{P/Y} = Ω_{P/Y}` in which the proof of 0FV4 uses the step.  Its content is
that of `quasiIso_naiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle`, the localisation functor to the derived
category inverting exactly the quasi-isomorphisms; what is added is that the two complexes are
compared as objects of `D(𝒪_P)` rather than by their cohomology sheaves.  The derived category is
the one of `HasDerivedCategory.standard`, taken as a local instance.

Only this one step of 0FV4 is covered; see the `Scope` section of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_Q_map_naiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle
    (hg : Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme g) :
    IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map (naiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle g))
declarations.comment: the 0D0L input: NL_{P/Y} -> Omega_{P/Y}[0] is invertible in D(O_P)

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentImmersionFormallySmooth.naiveCotangentIsoConormalDifferentialComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0FV4].**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes which factors as
`f = g ∘ i` with `i : X ⟶ P` an immersion and `g : P ⟶ Y` formally smooth (for example smooth,
by [Stacks Project, Tag 02H6]).  Then there is a canonical isomorphism

`NL_{X/Y} ≅ (𝒞_{X/P} ⟶ i^*Ω_{P/Y})`

in `D(𝒪_X)`, where the conormal sheaf `𝒞_{X/P}` is placed in degree `-1`.

The right-hand side is `Stacks.ConormalSequenceRight.conormalDifferentialComplex i g`: the
two-term complex whose degree `-1` term is the conormal sheaf of [Stacks Project, Tag 01R2],
whose degree `0` term is `i^*Ω_{P/Y}`, and whose only differential is the first arrow of the
conormal sequence of [Stacks Project, Tag 01UZ].

See the `Route` section of this file; the proof does not go through the distinguished triangle of
[Stacks Project, Tag 0FV3] and so has no sign to track.
declarations.statement:
def naiveCotangentIsoConormalDifferentialComplex (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f = i ≫ g)
    (hg : Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme g) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Stacks.ConormalSequenceRight.conormalDifferentialComplex i g)
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism NL_{X/Y} = (C_{X/P} -> i^*Omega_{P/Y}) in D(O_X), with C_{X/P} in degree -1, for f = g . i with i an immersion and g formally smooth

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentPullbackFormallySmooth.isZero_homology_negOne_modulePullbackNaiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**The pullback step of [Stacks Project, Tag 0FV4]: the vanishing `H^{-1}(i^*NL_{P/Y}) = 0`.**
For a formally smooth morphism of schemes `g : P ⟶ Y` and an arbitrary morphism `i : X ⟶ P` the
degree `-1` cohomology sheaf of the termwise pullback along `i` of `NL_{P/Y}` vanishes.

This is the step the source records as a small detail omitted, and obtains from local projectivity
of `Ω_{P/Y}` — the locally projective clause of [Stacks Project, Tag 0D0L] — through
[Stacks Project, Tag 0FUY].  The pullback of sheaves of modules is only right exact, so this does
not follow from the vanishing `H^{-1}(NL_{P/Y}) = 0` before pullback; what makes it true is that
local projectivity splits the one differential of `NL_{P/Y}` at every stalk, and a split
monomorphism stays one under any functor.  See the `Route` section of this file.

Only this step of 0FV4 is covered; see the `Scope` section of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homology_negOne_modulePullbackNaiveCotangentComplex
    (hg : Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme g) :
    IsZero ((modulePullbackNaiveCotangentComplex i g).homology (-1))
declarations.comment: the pullback step: H^{-1}(i^*NL_{P/Y}) = 0, the detail the source omits

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentPullbackFormallySmooth.quasiIso_pullbackNaiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle
declarations.doc:
**The pullback step of [Stacks Project, Tag 0FV4].** For a formally smooth morphism of schemes
`g : P ⟶ Y` and an arbitrary morphism `i : X ⟶ P` the canonical chain map
`i^*NL_{P/Y} ⟶ i^*Ω_{P/Y}[0]` is a quasi-isomorphism: the pullback along `i` of the naive cotangent
complex of `g` is identified with the pullback of its sheaf of relative differentials, placed in
degree `0`.

This is the form `NL_{P/Y} = Ω_{P/Y}` in which the proof of 0FV4 uses the tag *after* pulling back
along `i`, and it is the step that does not follow from
`Stacks.NaiveCotangentFormallySmoothComparison.quasiIso_naiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle`, the
same statement before pullback, the pullback of sheaves of modules not being exact.  Its three
ingredients are the vanishing
`isZero_homology_negOne_modulePullbackNaiveCotangentComplex` proved above, and the two clauses
of [Stacks Project, Tag 0E44] available in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.MoreMorphisms.NaiveCotangentSixTermSequence`: the identification
`H^0(i^*NL_{P/Y}) = i^*Ω_{P/Y}` and the vanishing of the cohomology sheaves outside degrees `-1`
and `0`.

Only this step of 0FV4 is covered; see the `Scope` section of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_pullbackNaiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle
    (hg : Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme g) :
    QuasiIso (pullbackNaiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle i g)
declarations.comment: the pullback step: i^*NL_{P/Y} -> i^*Omega_{P/Y}[0] is a quasi-isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentPullbackFormallySmooth.isIso_Q_map_pullbackNaiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle
declarations.doc:
**The pullback step of [Stacks Project, Tag 0FV4], read in `D(𝒪_X)`.** For a formally smooth
morphism of schemes `g : P ⟶ Y` and an arbitrary morphism `i : X ⟶ P` the canonical chain map
`i^*NL_{P/Y} ⟶ i^*Ω_{P/Y}[0]` becomes an isomorphism in the derived category of sheaves of
`𝒪_X`-modules; that is, `i^*NL_{P/Y}` and `i^*Ω_{P/Y}[0]` are canonically isomorphic objects of
`D(𝒪_X)`.

This is the form in which the proof of 0FV4 uses the step: the first vertex of its distinguished
triangle is `i^*NL_{P/Y}`, and what the proof needs of it is that it is `i^*Ω_{P/Y}` in degree `0`.
Its content is that of
`quasiIso_pullbackNaiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle`, the localisation functor to the derived
category inverting exactly the quasi-isomorphisms.  The
derived category is the one of `HasDerivedCategory.standard`, taken as a local instance.

Only this step of 0FV4 is covered; see the `Scope` section of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_Q_map_pullbackNaiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle
    (hg : Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme g) :
    IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map (pullbackNaiveCotangentToDifferentialsSingle i g))
declarations.comment: the pullback step in D(O_X): i^*NL_{P/Y} = i^*Omega_{P/Y}[0]

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentBaseChange.isIso_homologyMap_zero_baseChangeMapOfComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV5, the degree-zero isomorphism.**  For a cartesian square of schemes the
canonical map `(g')^*NL_{X/Y} ⟶ NL_{X'/Y'}` induces an isomorphism on degree-zero cohomology.

No flatness is assumed anywhere, and the canonical map is constructed and not assumed: it is
`Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.baseChangeMapOfComparison` taken against the canonical
base-ring comparison `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison` of the square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homologyMap_zero_baseChangeMapOfComparison (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g) :
    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
      (baseChangeMapOfComparison f f' g' (baseRingComparison f f' g' g hsq.w)
        (baseRingComparison_comp f f' g' g hsq.w)) 0)
declarations.comment: the degree-zero ISOMORPHISM, for a CARTESIAN square (`hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g`) and NO other hypothesis -- in particular no flatness. The canonical map is CONSTRUCTED, not assumed: `Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.baseChangeMapOfComparison` is the source's own composite of the [Stacks, Tag 08TM] identification of `(g')^*NL_{X/Y}` with a base change (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.pulledNaiveCotangentComparison`), the base-change map `NL_{B/A} (x)_B C -> NL_{C/A}` of [Stacks, Tag 0E1Y] (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.spaceBaseChangeNaiveCotangentMap`) for the tower `(g')^-1 f^-1 O_Y -> (g')^-1 O_X -> O_{X'}`, and the relative map `NL_{C/A} -> NL_{C/B}` (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.spaceRelativeNaiveCotangentComplexMap`) for the tower through `(f')^-1 O_{Y'}`. The base-ring comparison it is taken against is the CANONICAL one of the square, `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison`, with its compatibility `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison_comp`; it is built from the square and is not a `Classical.choose` of a non-unique existence statement. It is the same map the flat statements [Stacks, Tag 0FJZ] and [Stacks, Tag 0FK0] are about. PROVED: the reduction to the stalks ([Stacks, Tag 08TL], through `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isIso_homologyMap_iff_forall_stalk`); the degreewise vanishing outside degrees -1 and 0; and the stalkwise statement `isBijectiveOnCokernel_stalkFunctor_map_baseChangeMapOfComparison`, which is `Stacks.NaiveCotangentTowerStalk.isBijectiveOnCokernel_stalkFunctor_map_towerComposite` read through the stalk identification of the naive cotangent complex ([Stacks, Tag 0D09], the stalk-level form of [Stacks, Tag 0D0I]) and fed with the ring-level ARBITRARY base change [Stacks, Tag 0FUZ] `NaiveCotangent.naiveCotangentComplex_baseChange_homology`, composed with localization of the target [Stacks, Tag 00S7] in `NaiveCotangent.isH₀IsoH₁Surj_nlExtensionBaseChangeMap_of_isLocalization_tensor`. The one geometric input is the identification of `O_{X',x'}` as a localization of `O_{Y',f'(x')} (x)_{O_{Y,y}} O_{X,g'(x')}`, `AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.stalk_isLocalization_of_isPullback_inverseImage_comm` ([Stacks, Tag 01JR]), and that is the one place cartesianness is used. The companion clause, the `H^{-1}` surjection, is `Stacks.NaiveCotangentBaseChange.epi_homologyMap_negOne_baseChangeMapOfComparison`

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentBaseChange.epi_homologyMap_negOne_baseChangeMapOfComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV5, the degree-minus-one surjection.**  For a cartesian square of schemes the
canonical map `(g')^*NL_{X/Y} ⟶ NL_{X'/Y'}` induces a surjection on degree-minus-one
cohomology.

No flatness is assumed anywhere, and nothing is claimed about injectivity in degree `-1`: the
source's `H^{-1}` assertion is a surjection and not an isomorphism, and that is exactly what the
ring-level statement provides.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_homologyMap_negOne_baseChangeMapOfComparison (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g) :
    Epi (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
      (baseChangeMapOfComparison f f' g' (baseRingComparison f f' g' g hsq.w)
        (baseRingComparison_comp f f' g' g hsq.w)) (-1))
declarations.comment: the degree-minus-one SURJECTION, for a CARTESIAN square (`hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g`) and NO other hypothesis -- in particular no flatness. The canonical map is the one described on `Stacks.NaiveCotangentBaseChange.isIso_homologyMap_zero_baseChangeMapOfComparison`, the same constructed map `Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.baseChangeMapOfComparison` taken against the canonical base-ring comparison of the square. PROVED: the reduction of EPIMORPHY to the stalks (`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.epi_homologyMap_iff_forall_stalk`, the epimorphy counterpart of [Stacks, Tag 08TL]); the degreewise vanishing outside degrees -1 and 0; and the stalkwise statement `isSurjectiveOnKernel_stalkFunctor_map_baseChangeMapOfComparison`, which is `Stacks.NaiveCotangentTowerStalk.isSurjectiveOnKernel_stalkFunctor_map_towerComposite` fed with the ring-level ARBITRARY base change [Stacks, Tag 0FUZ]. Only SURJECTIVITY on the degree -1 cycles is assumed and only a surjection is concluded, which is what the source asserts and all that [Stacks, Tag 0FUZ] supplies: injectivity there is the half flatness would buy, and is the content of the stronger [Stacks, Tag 0FJZ] / [Stacks, Tag 0FK0]. The companion clause, the `H^0` isomorphism, is `Stacks.NaiveCotangentBaseChange.isIso_homologyMap_zero_baseChangeMapOfComparison`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIso_baseChangeNaiveCotangentHomologyZeroMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FV5, the degree-zero isomorphism.**  For a cartesian square of
schemes the canonical map `(g')^*H^0(NL_{X/Y}) ⟶ H^0(NL_{X'/Y'})` is an isomorphism.

The map is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.baseChangeNaiveCotangentHomologyZeroMap`, defined for every
commutative square; cartesianness is used only here, through Stacks 01V0.  See the tag clause
for what this statement does and does not cover.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_baseChangeNaiveCotangentHomologyZeroMap (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (hcart : IsPullback g' f' f g) :
    IsIso (baseChangeNaiveCotangentHomologyZeroMap f g f' g' hcart.w)
declarations.comment: the degree-zero ISOMORPHISM, for a CARTESIAN square, with no hypothesis beyond the cartesianness the source itself assumes. The map is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.baseChangeNaiveCotangentHomologyZeroMap`, the canonical map `(g')^*Omega_{X/Y} -> Omega_{X'/Y'}` of [Stacks, Tag 01UV] (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsMap`, characterized there by compatibility with the universal derivations) read through the degree-zero identification `H^0(NL) = Omega` of [Stacks, Tag 0D0J] (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.naiveCotangentComplexHomologyZeroIso`) at both ends. Like the source's own map it is defined from COMMUTATIVITY alone, and cartesianness is used only for invertibility, through [Stacks, Tag 01V0] (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isIso_relativeDifferentialsMap_of_isPullback`, which is itself proved outright from the cartesian-stalk localization and `KaehlerDifferential.tensorKaehlerEquivOfFormallyEtalePushout`). This is a SECOND, independent route to the tag's `H^0` clause, through the sheaf of relative differentials. The tag's two clauses for the canonical map of COMPLEXES are proved outright at `Stacks.NaiveCotangentBaseChange.isIso_homologyMap_zero_baseChangeMapOfComparison` and `Stacks.NaiveCotangentBaseChange.epi_homologyMap_negOne_baseChangeMapOfComparison`, which take the same canonical base-ring comparison of the square that [Stacks, Tag 0FJZ] does. NOT covered here: that the map of this statement is the one induced on `H^0` by that map of complexes. Comparing the two needs the identification of Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullback` -- the functor `Omega` and its canonical maps are stated over -- with the inverse-image-then-extend-scalars model that map of complexes is stated over, which is the open input recorded at `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/EtaleAlgebra/FlatBaseChange/StructureSheaf.lean`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV6.** The naive cotangent complex of a local complete intersection morphism is a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` of Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.

Near a point of the source the morphism restricts to a morphism of affine schemes whose map on
sections is a local complete intersection homomorphism, and there `NL_{X/Y}` is the derived
pullback of the derived sheafification of the naive cotangent complex of that homomorphism; both
conditions hold on it by Stacks 0FV0 and descend to the restriction by Stacks 08E9 and Stacks
08EB. Both conditions are local on the source, so they hold on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude_naiveCotangentComplex {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace)
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
      Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0
declarations.comment: both halves: NL_{X/Y} of a local complete intersection morphism is perfect and has tor-amplitude in [-1,0]

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedVirtualNormalGysinRestriction_eq_of_isTopChernComposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV7.** Let `Z' = Z ×_X X'` be the chosen base change of a closed immersion
`i : Z ⟶ X` along `f : X' ⟶ X`, both locally of finite type over the base, let `𝒩` be a virtual
normal sheaf for `Z ⊂ X` and `𝒩'` one for `Z' ⟶ X'`, of arbitrary ranks, and let
`0 ⟶ 𝒩' ⟶ g^*𝒩 ⟶ ℰ ⟶ 0` be a short exact sequence of finite locally free `𝒪_{Z'}`-modules such
that the square of `hcomm` commutes. Then

  `res(c(Z ⟶ X, 𝒩)) = c_top(ℰ) ∘ c(Z' ⟶ X', 𝒩')`

in `A^*(Z' ⟶ X')^∧`, for the classes of Stacks 0FBK, the top Chern class of Stacks 0FA4 and the
composition on completions (a class for `𝟙 ≫ (Z' ⟶ X')`).
declarations.statement:
theorem completedVirtualNormalGysinRestriction_eq_of_isTopChernComposition
    (w : inc ≫ pr = 0) (hseq : (ShortComplex.mk inc pr w).ShortExact)
    (hcomm : pullbackDualMap (pullback.fst i f) N.bundle ≫
        dualMap inc ≫ 𝒩'.surjection =
      (modulePullback (pullback.fst i f).toLRSHom.toShHom).map N.surjection ≫
        Stacks.Immersion.immersionConormalSheafMap (pullback.snd i f) i (pullback.fst i f) f
          (Stacks.Immersion.toShHom_square (isPullback_pullbackSnd i f).w)) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian Z := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sZ
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X' := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (f ≫ sX)
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian (pullback i f) :=
      LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (pullback.fst i f ≫ sZ)
    completedBivariantRestrictionViaSequence C sZ sX i hi f
        (completedVirtualNormalGysinClass C sZ sX i hi N) =
      completedBivariantGroup.copy C (Category.id_comp (pullback.snd i f)) _
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sZ sX i hi f)
        (completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible C (pullback.fst i f ≫ sZ)
          (pullback.fst i f ≫ sZ) (f ≫ sX) (𝟙 _) (pullback.snd i f) (Category.id_comp _)
          (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sZ sX i hi f)
          (topChernClassOfInvertible C (pullback.fst i f ≫ sZ) Eb)
          (completedVirtualNormalGysinClass C (pullback.fst i f ≫ sZ) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.snd i f)
            (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sZ sX i hi f) 𝒩'))
declarations.comment: res(c(Z → X, N)) = c_top(E) ∘ c(Z' → X', N') in A^*(Z' → X')^∧, for a cartesian square of closed immersions (the chosen fibre product Z' = Z ×_X X', where restriction lives), virtual normal sheaves N, N' of arbitrary rank, and a short exact sequence 0 → N' → g^*N → E → 0 of finite locally free modules whose dual square against the conormal sheaves commutes; c the completed classes of Tag 0FBK, c_top(E) of Tag 0FA4, the composite read at Z' → X'; proved as in the source, by the base-change clause of Tag 0FBK and then Tag 0FBL

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VirtualNormalBundle.completedBivariantRestriction_completedClass_eq_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FV7.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of schemes locally of finite type over
the base, `h : X' ⟶ X` locally of finite type, and `Z' = Z ×_X X'` with its closed immersion
`i' : Z' ⟶ X'` and projection `g : Z' ⟶ Z`. Let `𝒩` be a virtual normal sheaf for `Z ⊂ X` and
`𝒩'` one for `Z' ⊂ X'`, and let `0 ⟶ 𝒩' ⟶ g^*𝒩 ⟶ ℰ ⟶ 0` be a short exact sequence of finite
locally free `𝒪_{Z'}`-modules such that the square
`g^*𝒩^∨ ⟶ (𝒩')^∨ ⟶ 𝒞_{Z'/X'}` = `g^*𝒩^∨ ⟶ g^*𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z'/X'}` commutes (`hcomm`). Then

  `res(c(Z ⟶ X, 𝒩)) = c_top(ℰ) ∘ c(Z' ⟶ X', 𝒩')`   in   `A^*(Z' ⟶ X')^∧`,

where `c(-, -)` are the classes of Stacks 0FBK, `res` the restriction of Stacks 0F9Z on the
completed groups, `c_top(ℰ) ∈ A^*(Z')^∧` the top Chern class of Stacks 0FA4 and `∘` the
composition of Stacks 0FE0; the composite, a class for `𝟙 Z' ≫ i'`, is read at `i'`. No rank is
assumed constant.

The proof is the source's: Stacks 0FBK gives `res(c(Z ⟶ X, 𝒩)) = c(Z' ⟶ X', g^*𝒩)`, the
commuting square says that the conormal surjection of `g^*𝒩` factors through `σ'` along the dual
of `𝒩' ⟶ g^*𝒩`, and Stacks 0FBL concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem completedBivariantRestriction_completedClass_eq_comp :
    haveI := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sZ
    haveI := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    haveI := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (h ≫ sX)
    haveI := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (pullback.fst i h ≫ sZ)
    completedBivariantRestrictionOfInvertible C sZ sX i hZ h (𝒩.completedClass C sX sZ hZ) =
      completedBivariantGroupCongr C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.fst i h ≫ sZ)
        (h ≫ sX) (Category.id_comp (pullback.snd i h))
        (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq (Category.id_comp _)
          (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sZ sX i hZ h))
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sZ sX i hZ h)
        (completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible C (pullback.fst i h ≫ sZ)
          (pullback.fst i h ≫ sZ) (h ≫ sX) (𝟙 _) (pullback.snd i h) (Category.id_comp _)
          (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sZ sX i hZ h)
          (topChernClassCompleted C (pullback.fst i h ≫ sZ) E).1
          (𝒩'.completedClass C (h ≫ sX) (pullback.fst i h ≫ sZ)
            (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sZ sX i hZ h)))
declarations.comment: res(c(Z → X, 𝒩)) = c_top(ℰ) ∘ c(Z' → X', 𝒩') in A^*(Z' → X')^∧ for the cartesian square Z' = Z ×_X X' of a closed immersion i along X' → X locally of finite type, virtual normal sheaves 𝒩 for Z ⊂ X and 𝒩' for Z' ⊂ X', and a short exact sequence 0 → 𝒩' → g^*𝒩 → ℰ → 0 of finite locally free O_{Z'}-modules whose dual square against the conormal sheaves commutes; ranks arbitrary, c the completed classes of Tag 0FBK, res on completed groups, c_top(ℰ) of Tag 0FA4, ∘ the composition of Tag 0FE0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundleKZero.exists_minusOneAdamsOperator
declarations.doc:
**The minus-one Adams operation.** There is a ring endomorphism `ψ^{-1}` of `K₀(Vect(X))`
which sends the class of a finite locally free module to the class of its dual, and which
commutes with duality along any ring map `p : K₀(Vect(X)) → K₀(Vect(Y))` sending the class of a
finite locally free module `ℰ` to the class of `f^*ℰ`, for a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_minusOneAdamsOperator (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃ ψ : VectorBundleKZero X →+* VectorBundleKZero X,
      (∀ M : X.Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) M →
          ψ (classOf X M) = classOf X (dualSheaf X.toRingedSpace M)) ∧
        ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ X) (p : VectorBundleKZero X →+* VectorBundleKZero Y),
          (∀ M : X.Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) M →
              p (classOf X M) = classOf Y ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj M)) →
            ∀ a : VectorBundleKZero X,
              dualAddHom (dualPreservesFiniteLocallyFree Y) (dualShortExact Y) (p a) = p (ψ a)
declarations.comment: the ring map, its values on finite locally free modules and its compatibility with pullback

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantTransport_completedBivariantRestriction_lciGysinMap
declarations.doc:
Let `g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g` be a cartesian square of schemes locally of finite type over the base,
with `f` and `f'` local complete intersection morphisms and the Gysin map of Stacks 0FF3 existing
for `f`. Then the sheaf

  `𝒞 = Ker(H^{-1}((g')^*NL_{X/Y}) ⟶ H^{-1}(NL_{X'/Y'}))`,

for the base change map of Stacks 0FV5, is a finite locally free `𝒪_{X'}`-module, the Gysin map
exists for `f'`, and

  `res(f^!) = c_top(𝒞^∨) ∘ (f')^!`   in `A^*(X' ⟶ Y')^∧`,

for the Gysin maps of Stacks 0FF3, the restriction of Stacks 0F9Z (carried from the chosen fibre
product `X ×_Y Y'` to `X'` along the canonical isomorphism), the top Chern class of Stacks 0FA4
and the composition of Stacks 0FE0 (a class for `𝟙 ≫ f'`).
declarations.statement:
theorem completedBivariantTransport_completedBivariantRestriction_lciGysinMap
    (hlf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) (hlf' : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f')
    (hG : GysinMapExists f) :
    ∃ hC : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
        (kernel (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
          (Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.baseChangeMapOfComparison f f' g'
            (AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison f f' g' g hsq.w)
            (AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison_comp f f' g' g hsq.w)) (-1))),
      ∃ hG' : GysinMapExists f',
        haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
        haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sY
        haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X' := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX'
        haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y' := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (g ≫ sY)
        haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian (pullback f g) :=
          LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX)
        haveI : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (dualSheaf (kernel
            (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
              (Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.baseChangeMapOfComparison f f' g'
                (AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison f f' g' g hsq.w)
                (AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison_comp f f' g' g hsq.w))
              (-1)))) :=
          isFiniteLocallyFree_dualSheaf_of_schemeOpens _ hC
        completedBivariantTransport C (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX) sX' (g ≫ sY) (pullback.snd f g)
            (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf g) f' hf' hsq.isoPullback.symm
            hsq.isoPullback_inv_snd
            (completedBivariantRestrictionViaSequence C sX sY f hf g
              (lciGysinMap C sX sY hf hlf hG)) =
          completedBivariantGroup.copy C (Category.id_comp f') _ hf'
            (completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible C sX' sX' (g ≫ sY) (𝟙 X') f'
              (Category.id_comp sX') hf'
              (topChernClassOfInvertible C sX' (dualSheaf (kernel (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
                (Stacks.NaiveCotangentFlatBaseChange.baseChangeMapOfComparison f f' g'
                  (AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison f f' g' g hsq.w)
                  (AlgebraicGeometry.BaseChangeStalk.baseRingComparison_comp f f' g' g hsq.w))
                (-1)))))
              (lciGysinMap C sX' (g ≫ sY) hf' hlf' hG'))
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: for a cartesian square of schemes locally of finite type over S with f, f' local complete intersection morphisms and the Gysin map existing for f, the kernel C of H^{-1}((g')^*NL_{X/Y}) → H^{-1}(NL_{X'/Y'}) is finite locally free, the Gysin map exists for f', and res(f^!) = c_top(C^∨) ∘ (f')^! in A^*(X' → Y')^∧

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.completedBivariantRestriction_lciGysinMap_blowUpToBase
declarations.doc:
**The blow up formula.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a regular closed immersion of schemes locally of
finite type over the base, `b : X' ⟶ X` the blowing up of `X` with centre `Z`, and `E = X' ×_X Z`
with `j : E ⟶ X'` and `π : E ⟶ Z`. Assume that the Gysin map of Stacks 0FF3 exists for `b` (a local
complete intersection morphism, Stacks 0BIQ). Then

  `res(b^!) = c_top(𝓕^∨) ∘ π^*`   in `A^*(E ⟶ Z)^∧`,

where `𝓕` is the kernel of the canonical map `π^*𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{E/X'}` (finite locally free,
`Stacks.Chow.isFiniteLocallyFree_blowupExcessConormal`), `res` is the restriction of Stacks 0F9Z
along `i`, `c_top` the top Chern class of Stacks 0FA4, `π^*` the flat pullback of the smooth
morphism `π` and the composition that of Stacks 0FE0 (a class for `𝟙 ≫ π`).
declarations.statement:
theorem completedBivariantRestriction_lciGysinMap_blowUpToBase (hi : IsRegularImmersion i)
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (hG : GysinMapExists (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker)) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    haveI := Stacks.Blowup.smooth_pullbackSnd_blowUpToBase i hi
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian Z := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (i ≫ sX)
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian (Stacks.Blowup.blowUp i.ker) :=
      LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker ≫ sX)
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian (pullback (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker) i) :=
      LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (pullback.fst (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker) i ≫
        Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker ≫ sX)
    haveI : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (blowupExcessConormal i) :=
      isFiniteLocallyFree_blowupExcessConormal i hi hG
    haveI : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (dualSheaf (blowupExcessConormal i)) :=
      isFiniteLocallyFree_dualSheaf_of_schemeOpens _ inferInstance
    completedBivariantRestrictionViaSequence C (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker ≫ sX) sX
        (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker) rfl i
        (lciGysinMap C (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker ≫ sX) sX rfl
          (Stacks.Blowup.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_blowUpToBase i hi) hG) =
      completedBivariantGroup.copy C (Category.id_comp (pullback.snd _ i)) _
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C _ sX _ rfl i)
        (completedBivariantCompositeOfInvertible C
          (pullback.fst (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker) i ≫
            Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker ≫ sX)
          (pullback.fst (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker) i ≫
            Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker ≫ sX)
          (i ≫ sX) (𝟙 _) (pullback.snd (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker) i) (Category.id_comp _)
          (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C _ sX _ rfl i)
          (topChernClassOfInvertible C _ (dualSheaf (blowupExcessConormal i)))
          (completedFlatPullbackOfSmooth C _ (i ≫ sX)
            (pullback.snd (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpToBase i.ker) i)
            (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C _ sX _ rfl i)))
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: for a regular closed immersion i : Z → X of schemes locally of finite type over S, the blowing up b : X' → X with centre Z, E = X' ×_X Z with π : E → Z, and the Gysin map existing for b, res(b^!) = c_top(F^∨) ∘ π^* in A^*(E → Z)^∧, F the kernel of π^*C_{Z/X} → C_{E/X'}

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedDualPairingSquare_cup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FVB.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space
and let `K` and `E` be objects of `D(O_X)` with `E` perfect (Tag 08CM). The diagram

`H⁰(X, K ⊗^L E^∨) × H⁰(X, E) ⟶ H⁰(X, (K ⊗^L E^∨) ⊗^L E)`
`        ↓                               ↓`
`Hom_X(E, K) × H⁰(X, E)        ⟶       H⁰(X, K)`

commutes: the cup product `ξ ∪ η` (Section 0FKU, the relative cup product of Stacks 0B68 for
`(X, O_X) ⟶ (pt, Γ(X, O_X))`, `Stacks.SheafOfModules.globalCupProductZero`) followed by the map
induced on `H⁰` by `1_K ⊗ ε` and the unit constraint (`ε : E^∨ ⊗^L E ⟶ O_X` of Example 0FPC)
is the morphism `E ⟶ K` attached to `ξ` by the identification
`H⁰(X, K ⊗^L E^∨) = Hom_{D(O_X)}(E, K)` of Lemma 08DQ
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap`), evaluated on `η`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedDualPairingSquare_cup (K E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (hE : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X) E)
    (ξ : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
        (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj K).obj (derivedDual X.sheaf E))) : Type u))
    (η : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
      ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj E) : Type u)) :
    (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).map
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).map
          (derivedDualContraction X.sheaf K E))
        (globalCupProductZero X (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj K).obj (derivedDual X.sheaf E)) E
          ξ η) =
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).map
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).map
          (derivedTensorDualGlobalSectionsMap X.sheaf E K ξ)) η

declarations.name: Stacks.VeryAmpleFixedTwist.eventuallyVeryAmpleFixedTwist_of_isRelativelyAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0FVC.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and `N`, `L` invertible
`𝒪_X`-modules. If `S` is quasi-compact, `f` is of finite type and `L` is `f`-relatively ample,
then `N ⊗ L^{⊗ d}` is `f`-relatively very ample for every sufficiently large `d`.

The proof is the source's. The affine open covering `S.affineCover.finiteSubcover` of `S` is
finite because `S` is quasi-compact, and
`Stacks.VeryAmpleFixedTwist.eventually_familyImmersion_tensor` at the restriction of `f`, whose
ampleness hypothesis is the defining clause of relative ampleness, gives over each member a bound
past which `N ⊗ L^{⊗ d}` restricted to the member carries a generating family pinning an
immersion into projective space over the member — the source's reduction to an affine base, Tag
02NQ, performed by hand so that the engine runs with absolute ampleness. The largest of the
finitely many bounds serves every member, and
`Stacks.VeryAmpleGlue.isRelativelyVeryAmple_of_cover` (Stacks Tag 01VT's (5) ⟹ (3) and Stacks Tag
01VR's (2) ⟹ (1) together) turns the families into relative very ampleness over `S`; the
restriction of `N ⊗ L^{⊗ d}` is matched with the module the families live on by
`Stacks.VeryAmpleFixedTwist.pullbackTensorTwistIso`. Quasi-compactness of `f` is taken from
relative ampleness.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventuallyVeryAmpleFixedTwist_of_isRelativelyAmple {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (N L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X N] [IsInvertibleModule X L]
    [CompactSpace S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hL : Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L) :
    EventuallyVeryAmpleFixedTwist f N L

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_splittingMorphism_isBundleTower
declarations.doc:
The morphism `π : P ⟶ X` of Stacks 02UL is a finite composition of projective space bundles
associated to locally free modules of finite constant rank.

Let `(S, δ)` be the situation of Stacks 02QL, let `X` be locally of finite type over `S` and let
`ℰ_i`, `i ∈ I` finite, be finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules of ranks `r_i`. Then there is a
splitting morphism `T`, flat and proper of relative dimension `d = ∑_i binom(r_i, 2)`, with
injective flat pullback on Chow groups in every degree, splitting every `ℰ_i`, and satisfying
`Stacks.Chow.IsBundleTower`: it is the identity of `X` or the projection of one layer `𝐏(ℰ)` with
`ℰ` finite locally free of constant rank, composed with such a tower over `𝐏(ℰ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_splittingMorphism_isBundleTower (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (step : ∀ {Y : Scheme.{u}} (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (F : Y.Modules) (m : ℕ),
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} F (m + 1) →
        BundleStep C sY F m)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (I : Type) [Fintype I]
    (E : I → X.Modules) (r : I → ℕ)
    (hE : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} (E i) (r i)) :
    ∃ T : SplittingMorphism C sX (∑ i, (r i).choose 2),
      IsBundleTower C sX (∑ i, (r i).choose 2) T ∧
        ∀ i, Stacks.WeilCohomology.HasInvertibleFiltration T.P
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.π).obj (E i)) (r i)
declarations.comment: clause (1) only: the 02UL morphism is a constant-rank projective bundle tower

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_splittingMorphism_isProjectiveBundleTower_recoversByCaps
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FVE.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL, `X` locally of finite type over `S`
and `ℰ_i` (`i ∈ I`, finite) finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules of ranks `r_i`. The morphism
`π : P ⟶ X` built in the proof of Stacks 02UL — flat and proper of relative dimension
`d = ∑_i binom(r_i, 2)`, with injective flat pullback on Chow groups, such that each `π^*ℰ_i` has
a filtration with invertible successive quotients — has the further properties

1. `π` is a finite composition of projective space bundles associated to finite locally free
   modules of constant rank (`Stacks.Chow.IsProjectiveBundleTower`, whose layers are the actual
   projective bundles `Stacks.Chow.bundle`), and
2. there are invertible `𝒪_P`-modules `L_1, …, L_d` such that, with `ξ_j = c₁(L_j)`, every
   `α ∈ CH_k(X)` satisfies `α = π_*(ξ_1 ∩ ⋯ ∩ ξ_d ∩ π^*α)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_splittingMorphism_isProjectiveBundleTower_recoversByCaps (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (I : Type) [Fintype I]
    (E : I → X.Modules) (r : I → ℕ)
    (hE : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} (E i) (r i)) :
    ∃ T : SplittingMorphism C sX (∑ i, (r i).choose 2),
      (∀ i, Stacks.WeilCohomology.HasInvertibleFiltration T.P
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.π).obj (E i)) (r i)) ∧
      IsProjectiveBundleTower C sX (∑ i, (r i).choose 2) T ∧
      ∃ (Ls : List (InvertibleModule T.P)) (hLs : Ls.length = ∑ i, (r i).choose 2),
        ∀ (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C sX k),
          properChowPushforward C T.sP sX T.π T.hsP k
              (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper C T.sP sX T.π
                T.hsP k)
              (iteratedChernCapOnChow C T.sP (invCapList C T.sP Ls) k
                (chowGroupCast C T.sP (by rw [length_invCapList, hLs])
                  (T.pullbackChow k α))) = α

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.FlatBaseChangeSituation
declarations.doc:
A flat morphism between two bases for Chow homology whose dimension functions differ by a
fixed integer on the generic points of the irreducible components of every fibre.
declarations.statement: structure FlatBaseChangeSituation

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.deltaDimension_component_baseChange
declarations.doc:
In the flat base-change situation of Stacks 0FVG, if `X` is integral and locally of finite
type over `S` with `dim_δ(X) = k`, then every irreducible component of the base change
`X ×_S S'` has delta-dimension `k + c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem deltaDimension_component_baseChange (B : FlatBaseChangeSituation.{u})
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ B.base.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsIntegral X]
    (k : ℤ) (hk : schemeDeltaDimension B.base f = (k : EInt))
    (Z : irreducibleComponents (pullback f B.g : Scheme.{u})) :
    deltaDimension B.baseChange (pullback.snd f B.g)
        ⟨Z, Z.2.1,
