          isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents
            (Z : Set (pullback f B.g : Scheme.{u})) Z.2⟩ =
      k + B.c

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_baseChange_closedSubscheme_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FVI, part (1), dimension bound.** In the flat base-change situation of Stacks
0FVG, the base change `Z' = Z ×_X X'` of a closed subscheme `Z ⊆ X` of delta-dimension at most
`k` is a closed subscheme of `X' = X ×_S S'` of delta-dimension at most `k + c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeDeltaDimension_baseChange_closedSubscheme_le (B : FlatBaseChangeSituation.{u})
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ B.base.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] {k : ℤ}
    (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension B.base (i ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    schemeDeltaDimension B.baseChange
        (pullback.snd i (pullback.fst f B.g) ≫ pullback.snd f B.g) ≤ ((k + B.c : ℤ) : EInt)
declarations.comment: part (1): dimension bound

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension_baseChange_support_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FVI, part (2), dimension bound.** In the flat base-change situation of Stacks
0FVG, if a coherent sheaf on `X` has support of delta-dimension at most `k`, then the support of
its base change to `X' = X ×_S S'` has delta-dimension at most `k + c`.

Every point of the support of the base change lies over the support of the sheaf, so part (1)
for the reduced support bounds the relative dimension there.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeDeltaDimension_baseChange_support_le (B : FlatBaseChangeSituation.{u})
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ B.base.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsCoherent] {k : ℤ}
    (hFk : schemeDeltaDimension B.base ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (pullback f B.g : Scheme.{u}) :=
      LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (pullback.snd f B.g)
    letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f B.g)).obj F).IsCoherent :=
      AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback (pullback.fst f B.g) F
    schemeDeltaDimension B.baseChange
        ((reducedSupport ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f B.g)).obj F)).subschemeι ≫
          pullback.snd f B.g) ≤ ((k + B.c : ℤ) : EInt)
declarations.comment: part (2): support dimension bound

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.baseChangeCyclePullback_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FVI, part (2), cycle identity.** In the flat base-change situation of Stacks 0FVG,
the base change of the cycle of a coherent sheaf `F` on `X` whose support has delta-dimension at
most `k` is the cycle of the base change of `F`:

`g^*[F]_k = [F']_{k + c}`.

The two sides are compared at one point `x'` of `X'` at a time. If `x'` has relative dimension
other than `k + c` both vanish, the left one because the base-change multiplicity is formed only
in that degree. If `x'` lies off the support of `F'` then its image lies off the support of `F`,
since the support of a pullback is the inverse image of the support, so the coefficient of
`[F]_k` already vanishes there. In the remaining case the relative dimension of the image is
forced to be exactly `k`, because it is at most `k` on the support of `F` while the relative
dimension of `x'` exceeds it by at most `c`; the two multiplicities are then
`length_A M * length_B (B / 𝔪_A B)` and `length_B (B ⊗_A M)` for `A = 𝒪_{X, x}`, `B = 𝒪_{X', x'}`
and `M = F_x`, equal by Stacks 02M1.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangeCyclePullback_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf (B : FlatBaseChangeSituation.{u})
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ B.base.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (k : ℤ) (hFk : schemeDeltaDimension B.base ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (pullback f B.g : Scheme.{u}) :=
      LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (pullback.snd f B.g)
    letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f B.g)).obj F).IsCoherent :=
      AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback (pullback.fst f B.g) F
    baseChangeCyclePullback B f k (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf B.base f F k hFk) =
      cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf B.baseChange (pullback.snd f B.g)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f B.g)).obj F) (k + B.c)
        (schemeDeltaDimension_baseChange_support_le B f F hFk)
declarations.comment: part (2): cycle identity

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.baseChangeCyclePullback_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FVI, part (1), cycle identity.** In the flat base-change situation of Stacks 0FVG,
the base change of the cycle of a closed subscheme `Z ⊆ X` of delta-dimension at most `k` is the
cycle of the base change `Z' = Z ×_X X'`:

`g^*[Z]_k = [Z']_{k + c}`.

By Stacks 02QY both cycles are cycles of coherent sheaves, namely of `i_* 𝒪_Z` and of
`i'_* 𝒪_{Z'}`, so part (2) reduces the claim to the flat base change of `i_* 𝒪_Z` being
`i'_* 𝒪_{Z'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangeCyclePullback_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (B : FlatBaseChangeSituation.{u})
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ B.base.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (k : ℤ)
    (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension B.base (i ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    baseChangeCyclePullback B f k (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme B.base f i k) =
      cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme B.baseChange (pullback.snd f B.g)
        (pullback.snd i (pullback.fst f B.g)) (k + B.c)
declarations.comment: part (1): cycle identity

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback
registrations.comment: part (2): coherence of the base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.baseChangeCyclePullback_maps_rationalEquivalences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVJ, preservation of rational equivalence.** In a flat base-change
situation with dimension shift `c`, the base-change homomorphism on cycle groups carries
`k`-cycles rationally equivalent to zero on `X` to `(k + c)`-cycles rationally equivalent to
zero on `X' = X ×_S S'`.

By Stacks 02S4 part (4) such a cycle is the total fibre difference of a locally finite family of
integral closed subschemes of `X ×_S 𝐏¹_S`, each of relative dimension `k + 1` at its generic
points and contained in neither distinguished section. Its base change is the total fibre
difference of the base-changed family, which is again locally finite, and each member of the
base-changed family satisfies the hypotheses of Stacks 02S5 over the new base: the dimension
bounds are those of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.ChangeBaseScheme.FamilyDimension`, and the condition on
associated points holds because the projection to the original member is flat. The individual
equivalences are summed by `Stacks.Chow.rationallyEquivalentToZero_finsum`, the carriers of the
members forming a locally finite family.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangeCyclePullback_maps_rationalEquivalences (k : ℤ) :
    rationalEquivalences B.base f k ≤
      (rationalEquivalences B.baseChange (pullback.snd f B.g) (k + B.c)).comap
        (baseChangeCyclePullback B f k)
declarations.comment: preservation of rational equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.baseChangeChowPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVJ, the map on Chow groups.** The homomorphism
`g^* : CH_k(X) ⟶ CH_{k+c}(X ×_S S')` induced on Chow groups by the base-change homomorphism
on cycle groups, which preserves rational equivalence by
`Stacks.Chow.baseChangeCyclePullback_maps_rationalEquivalences`.
declarations.statement:
def baseChangeChowPullback (k : ℤ) :
    chowGroup B.base f k →+ chowGroup B.baseChange (pullback.snd f B.g) (k + B.c)
declarations.comment: induced map on Chow groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flat_relativeDimension_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FVK.** In a flat base-change situation, the base change of a morphism locally of
finite type and flat of relative dimension `r` is again locally of finite type and flat of
relative dimension `r`.

Flatness and local finite type are stable under base change, and the relative dimension is
Stacks 02NK.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_relativeDimension_baseChange (B : FlatBaseChangeSituation.{u}) {Y X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sY : Y ⟶ B.base.S) (sX : X ⟶ B.base.S) (f : Y ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f]
    (f' : (pullback sY B.g : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pullback sX B.g : Scheme.{u}))
    (hsq : IsPullback (pullback.fst sY B.g) f' f (pullback.fst sX B.g))
    (r : ℕ) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f' :=
      MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) inferInstance
    Flat f' ∧ AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f' r
declarations.comment: flatness and relative dimension of the base-changed morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.baseChange_flatPullback_cycles
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FVK.** The square of cycle groups commutes: base change after flat pullback is
flat pullback after base change, as homomorphisms `Z_k(X) ⟶ Z_{k+c+r}(Y')`.

The two composites land in cycle groups of degree `(k + r) + c` and `(k + c) + r`, so the
statement is heterogeneous; its content is the coefficient identity
`Stacks.Chow.baseChangeCyclePullback_flatPullback_apply`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChange_flatPullback_cycles
    (B : FlatBaseChangeSituation.{u}) {Y X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sY : Y ⟶ B.base.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (sX : X ⟶ B.base.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (f : Y ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] (hbase : f ≫ sX = sY)
    (f' : (pullback sY B.g : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pullback sX B.g : Scheme.{u}))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f'] [Flat f']
    (hbase' : f' ≫ pullback.snd sX B.g = pullback.snd sY B.g)
    (hcomm : pullback.fst sY B.g ≫ f = f' ≫ pullback.fst sX B.g)
    (r : ℕ) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r)
    (hf' : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f' r) (k : ℤ) :
    HEq ((baseChangeCyclePullback B sY (k + (r : ℤ))).comp
          (flatPullback B.base sY sX f hbase r hf k))
      ((flatPullback B.baseChange (pullback.snd sY B.g) (pullback.snd sX B.g) f' hbase' r hf'
          (k + B.c)).comp (baseChangeCyclePullback B sX k))
declarations.comment: commuting diagram of cycle groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.baseChange_flatPullback_chow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FVK.** The square of Chow groups commutes: base change after flat pullback is flat
pullback after base change, as homomorphisms `A_k(X) ⟶ A_{k+c+r}(Y')`.

This is the image of `Stacks.Chow.baseChange_flatPullback_cycles` under the quotient maps, which
is why the source says it suffices to prove the square of cycle groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChange_flatPullback_chow
    (B : FlatBaseChangeSituation.{u}) {Y X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sY : Y ⟶ B.base.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (sX : X ⟶ B.base.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (f : Y ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] (hbase : f ≫ sX = sY)
    (f' : (pullback sY B.g : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pullback sX B.g : Scheme.{u}))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f'] [Flat f']
    (hbase' : f' ≫ pullback.snd sX B.g = pullback.snd sY B.g)
    (hcomm : pullback.fst sY B.g ≫ f = f' ≫ pullback.fst sX B.g)
    (r : ℕ) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r)
    (hf' : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f' r) (k : ℤ) :
    HEq ((flatBaseChangeChowPullback B sY (k + (r : ℤ))
            (baseChangeFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence B sY (k + (r : ℤ)))).comp
          (flatPullbackChow B.base sY sX f hbase r hf k
            (flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_general B.base sY sX f hbase r hf k)))
      ((flatPullbackChow B.baseChange (pullback.snd sY B.g) (pullback.snd sX B.g) f' hbase' r hf'
          (k + B.c)
          (flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_general B.baseChange
            (pullback.snd sY B.g) (pullback.snd sX B.g) f' hbase' r hf' (k + B.c))).comp
        (flatBaseChangeChowPullback B sX k
          (baseChangeFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence B sX k)))
declarations.comment: commuting diagram of Chow groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isProper_baseChangeMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVL, properness of the base change.** In a flat base change of Chow
situations, the morphism `f' : Y ×_S S' ⟶ X ×_S S'` induced by a proper morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` is
proper, because it is a base change of `f` and properness is stable under base change.
declarations.statement: theorem isProper_baseChangeMorphism [IsProper f] : IsProper (baseChangeMorphism B sX f)
declarations.comment: properness of the base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_baseChangeCyclePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVL, the cycle square.** In a flat base change of Chow situations,
proper pushforward commutes with the base-change map on cycle groups: for `f : Y ⟶ X` proper
over the base `S`, the square whose horizontal maps are `g^* : Z_k(Y) ⟶ Z_{k+c}(Y')` and
`g^* : Z_k(X) ⟶ Z_{k+c}(X')` and whose vertical maps are `f_*` and `f'_*` commutes.

Both routes are additive, and a cycle agrees, on the part of its support lying over a single
point `x` of `X'`, with a finite sum of prime cycles: that part is the intersection of the
support with the fibre of the proper morphism `f` over the image of `x`, hence finite, and both
routes read the coefficient at `x` only off that part. So it suffices to treat a prime cycle,
which is the fundamental cycle of the reduced closure of a point and so is covered by the case
of a closed subscheme.

Coherence of the direct image of a coherent module under a proper morphism to a locally
Noetherian scheme is `Stacks.Chow.forall_properDirectImageIsCoherent`, the first assertion of
Stacks 02O5.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_baseChangeCyclePullback
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] [IsProper f] (k : ℤ)
    (z : CycleGroup B.base (f ≫ sX) k) :
    letI : IsProper (baseChangeMorphism B sX f) := isProper_baseChangeMorphism B sX f
    properPushforward B.baseChange (pullback.snd (f ≫ sX) B.g) (pullback.snd sX B.g)
        (baseChangeMorphism B sX f) (baseChangeMorphism_comp_snd B sX f) (k + B.c)
        (baseChangeCyclePullback B (f ≫ sX) k z) =
      baseChangeCyclePullback B sX k (properPushforward B.base (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k z)
declarations.comment: the cycle square

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properChowPushforward_baseChangeChowPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVL, the Chow square.** In a flat base change of Chow situations,
proper pushforward commutes with the base-change map on Chow groups: for `f : Y ⟶ X` proper over
the base `S`, the square whose horizontal maps are `g^* : CH_k(Y) ⟶ CH_{k+c}(Y')` and
`g^* : CH_k(X) ⟶ CH_{k+c}(X')` and whose vertical maps are `f_*` and `f'_*` commutes.

Every class is the class of a cycle, and on classes of cycles both routes are the class of the
corresponding route on cycles, so this follows from the cycle square.

The base-change map on Chow groups is a parameter `gChow` of this statement rather than a fixed
map, constrained by `hgChow` to be induced by the base-change map on cycle groups. This is a
generality, not an assumption: quantifying over every such map is stronger than the source's
statement, and the map itself exists, so
`Stacks.Chow.properChowPushforward_baseChangeChowPullback_of_baseChangeChowPullback` below
instantiates this at the base-change map of Stacks 0FVJ and is unconditional. Coherence of the
direct image of a
coherent module under a proper morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme is
`Stacks.Chow.forall_properDirectImageIsCoherent`, the first assertion of Stacks 02O5.
declarations.statement:
theorem properChowPushforward_baseChangeChowPullback
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] [IsProper f] (k : ℤ)
    (gChow : ∀ {W : Scheme.{u}} (sW : W ⟶ B.base.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sW] (j : ℤ),
      chowGroup B.base sW j →+ chowGroup B.baseChange (pullback.snd sW B.g) (j + B.c))
    (hgChow : ∀ {W : Scheme.{u}} (sW : W ⟶ B.base.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sW] (j : ℤ)
      (a : CycleGroup B.base sW j),
      gChow sW j (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences B.base sW j) a) =
        QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences B.baseChange (pullback.snd sW B.g) (j + B.c))
          (baseChangeCyclePullback B sW j a))
    (w : chowGroup B.base (f ≫ sX) k) :
    letI : IsProper (baseChangeMorphism B sX f) := isProper_baseChangeMorphism B sX f
    properChowPushforward B.baseChange (pullback.snd (f ≫ sX) B.g) (pullback.snd sX B.g)
        (baseChangeMorphism B sX f) (baseChangeMorphism_comp_snd B sX f) (k + B.c)
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper B.baseChange
          (pullback.snd (f ≫ sX) B.g) (pullback.snd sX B.g) (baseChangeMorphism B sX f)
          (baseChangeMorphism_comp_snd B sX f) (k + B.c))
        (gChow (f ≫ sX) k w) =
      gChow sX k (properChowPushforward B.base (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper B.base (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl
          k) w)
declarations.comment: the Chow square, in the generality of every Chow base-change map induced by the cycle-level one of Tag 0FVJ; instantiated at that map, with nothing left to supply, by properChowPushforward_baseChangeChowPullback_of_baseChangeChowPullback below

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properChowPushforward_baseChangeChowPullback_of_baseChangeChowPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVL, the Chow square for the base-change map of Stacks 0FVJ.** In a
flat base change of Chow situations, proper pushforward commutes with the base-change map
`g^* : CH_k(X) ⟶ CH_{k+c}(X ×_S S')` of Stacks 0FVJ: for `f : Y ⟶ X` proper over the base `S`,
the square whose horizontal maps are those base-change maps for `Y` and for `X` and whose
vertical maps are `f_*` and `f'_*` commutes.

This is the Chow square with its Chow base-change map supplied rather than assumed: the map is
`Stacks.Chow.baseChangeChowPullback`, and it meets the characterization of the general statement
because `Stacks.Chow.baseChangeChowPullback_mk` says it sends the class of a cycle to the class
of the base change of that cycle. Coherence of the direct image of a coherent module under a
proper morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme is
`Stacks.Chow.forall_properDirectImageIsCoherent`, the first assertion of Stacks 02O5.
declarations.statement:
theorem properChowPushforward_baseChangeChowPullback_of_baseChangeChowPullback
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] [IsProper f] (k : ℤ)
    (w : chowGroup B.base (f ≫ sX) k) :
    letI : IsProper (baseChangeMorphism B sX f) := isProper_baseChangeMorphism B sX f
    properChowPushforward B.baseChange (pullback.snd (f ≫ sX) B.g) (pullback.snd sX B.g)
        (baseChangeMorphism B sX f) (baseChangeMorphism_comp_snd B sX f) (k + B.c)
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper B.baseChange
          (pullback.snd (f ≫ sX) B.g) (pullback.snd sX B.g) (baseChangeMorphism B sX f)
          (baseChangeMorphism_comp_snd B sX f) (k + B.c))
        (baseChangeChowPullback B (f ≫ sX) k w) =
      baseChangeChowPullback B sX k (properChowPushforward B.base (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper B.base (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl
          k) w)
declarations.comment: the Chow square for the base-change map of Tag 0FVJ

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.baseChange_firstChernClassCapChow
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVM].** In the flat base-change situation of [Stacks, Tag 0FVG] let `X` be
locally of finite type over `S`, let `X' = X ×_S S'` be the base change by `S' ⟶ S`, and let `ℒ`
be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module with base change `ℒ'` on `X'`. Then the square

  `CH_{k+1}(X) --g^*--> CH_{k+1+c}(X')`
  `      |c₁(ℒ) ∩ -             |c₁(ℒ') ∩ -`
  `CH_k(X)     --g^*--> CH_{k+c}(X')`

of Chow groups commutes, `g^*` being the base-change map of [Stacks, Tag 0FVJ].

The cap product of [Stacks, Tag 02TI] is indexed by the degree of its value, so the top row is
written at `k + 1`; the source states the square for every `k ∈ ℤ`, so nothing is lost. The
transport between the two spellings `(k + 1) + c` and `(k + c) + 1` of the degree of the base
change of the top-left corner is `Stacks.Chow.chowGroupCast`. The module `ℒ'` is
`(D.baseChange g).L`, which is the pullback `g^*ℒ` by
`Stacks.LineBundle.Situation.baseChange_L`.

**Proof.** Let `p : Tot(ℒ) ⟶ X` be the line bundle attached to `ℒ` with zero section `o`. By
clause (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0F96], `o_*α = -p^*(c₁(ℒ) ∩ α)`. Applying `g^*` and using
[Stacks, Tag 0FVL] on `o` and [Stacks, Tag 0FVK] on `p` turns this into

  `õ_*(g^*α) = -p̃^*(g^*(c₁(ℒ) ∩ α))`

on the fibre product `Tot(ℒ) ×_S S'`, where `õ` and `p̃` are the base changes of `o` and `p`. On
the other hand `Stacks.Chow.zeroSectionBaseChange_chowPushforward_eq_neg` — clause (5) for `ℒ'`,
transported along `Tot(ℒ') ≅ Tot(ℒ) ×_S S'` — gives

  `õ_*(g^*α) = -p̃^*(c₁(ℒ') ∩ g^*α)`.

So `p̃^*` takes the same value on the two classes to be identified, and `p̃^*` is injective by
`Stacks.Chow.injective_flatPullbackChow_totalSpaceBaseChangeMorphism`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChange_firstChernClassCapChow (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup B.base sX (k + 1)) :
    firstChernClassCapChow B.baseChange (k + B.c) (pullback.snd sX B.g)
        (baseChangeSituation B D sX).L
        (chowGroupCast B.baseChange (pullback.snd sX B.g)
          (show k + 1 + B.c = k + B.c + 1 from by omega)
          (baseChangeChowPullback B sX (k + 1) α)) =
      baseChangeChowPullback B sX k (firstChernClassCapChow B.base k sX D.L α)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.baseChange_chowCohomologyCap_chernClassOfLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVN].** Let `g : S' ⟶ S` be a flat base change of Chow situations with
dimension shift `c` ([Stacks, Tag 0FVG]), let `X` be locally of finite type over `S` with base
change `X' = X ×_S S'`, and let `ℰ` be a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module of rank `r` with base
change `ℰ'` on `X'`. Then for every `i` the square

  `CH_k(X)     --g^*--> CH_{k+c}(X')`
  `    |c_i(ℰ) ∩ -              |c_i(ℰ') ∩ -`
  `CH_{k-i}(X) --g^*--> CH_{k+c-i}(X')`

commutes, where `c_i ∈ A^i` is the Chern class of [Stacks, Tag 0ESW], built from the classes of
[Stacks, Tag 0B7H] (zero for `i > r`), and `g^*` is the map of [Stacks, Tag 0FVJ]. For `i ≤ r`
the cap products are those of [Stacks, Tag 02U6] (`Stacks.Chow.baseChange_chernCap`).
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChange_chowCohomologyCap_chernClassOfLocallyFree (i : ℕ) (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup B.base sX k) :
    letI := AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.isFiniteLocallyFree E r
    haveI := AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback (pullback.fst sX B.g) E r
    letI := AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.isFiniteLocallyFree
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst sX B.g)).obj E) r
    chowCohomologyCap B.baseChange (gysinSystemOfInvertible B.baseChange) (pullback.snd sX B.g)
        (i : ℤ)
        (SectionZeroScheme.chernClassOfLocallyFree
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst sX B.g)).obj E) B.baseChange
          (pullback.snd sX B.g) i) (k + B.c) (baseChangeChowPullback B sX k α) =
      chowGroupCast B.baseChange (pullback.snd sX B.g)
        (show k - (i : ℤ) + B.c = k + B.c - (i : ℤ) from by omega)
        (baseChangeChowPullback B sX (k - (i : ℤ))
          (chowCohomologyCap B.base (gysinSystemOfInvertible B.base) sX (i : ℤ)
            (SectionZeroScheme.chernClassOfLocallyFree E B.base sX i) k α))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.composed_dimensionFunction_eq_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVP, part (1).** For composable flat base changes of Chow situations
with dimension shifts `B.c` and `c'`, every generic point `s''` of the fibre of `g' ≫ B.g` over
`s` satisfies `δ''(s'') = δ(s) + (B.c + c')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem composed_dimensionFunction_eq_add (s : B.base.S)
    (s'' : genericPoints ((g' ≫ B.g) ⁻¹' {s} : Set C.S)) :
    C.dimensionFunction s''.1.1 = B.base.dimensionFunction s + (B.c + c')
declarations.comment: part (1): the composite dimension shift is the sum of the two shifts

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.baseChangeCyclePullbackSquare_comp_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVP, part (2).** The pullbacks on cycle groups of two composable flat
base changes compose to the pullback of the composite, read coefficientwise.

Both composites send a cycle `z` to a multiple of the coefficient of `z` at the image point `x`
of the given point, the factor depending only on the point. If `x` does not have relative
dimension `k` then every `k`-cycle vanishes there and both sides are zero. Otherwise the
fundamental cycle of the reduced closure of `x` is a `k`-cycle with coefficient one at `x`, so
the two factors agree by
`Stacks.Chow.comp_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme_coeff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangeCyclePullbackSquare_comp_apply (k : ℤ) (z : CycleGroup B.base f k) (y : Y'') :
    (baseChangeCyclePullbackSquare (FlatBaseChangeSituation.second B C g' c' hg') q sq' (k + B.c)
        (baseChangeCyclePullbackSquare B f sq k z)).1 y =
      (baseChangeCyclePullbackSquare (FlatBaseChangeSituation.comp B C g' c' hg') f
        (sq'.paste_horiz sq) k z).1 y
declarations.comment: part (2): pullback on cycle groups respects composition, coefficientwise

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.baseChangeCyclePullbackSquare_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVP, part (2).** The pullbacks on cycle groups of two composable flat
base changes compose to the pullback of the composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangeCyclePullbackSquare_comp (k : ℤ) :
    (baseChangeCyclePullbackSquare (FlatBaseChangeSituation.second B C g' c' hg') q sq'
          (k + B.c)).comp (baseChangeCyclePullbackSquare B f sq k) =
      ((cycleGroupCongrDegree C q'
          (show k + (B.c + c') = k + B.c + c' from (add_assoc k B.c c').symm)).toAddMonoidHom).comp
        (baseChangeCyclePullbackSquare (FlatBaseChangeSituation.comp B C g' c' hg') f
          (sq'.paste_horiz sq) k)
declarations.comment: part (2): pullback on cycle groups respects composition

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.baseChangeChowPullbackSquare_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVP, part (3).** The pullbacks on Chow groups of two composable flat
base changes compose to the pullback of the composite: both are induced by the corresponding
pullbacks on cycle groups, which compose by
`Stacks.Chow.baseChangeCyclePullbackSquare_comp`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangeChowPullbackSquare_comp (k : ℤ) :
    (baseChangeChowPullbackSquare (FlatBaseChangeSituation.second B C g' c' hg') q sq'
          (k + B.c)).comp (baseChangeChowPullbackSquare B f sq k) =
      ((chowGroupCongrDegree C q'
          (show k + (B.c + c') = k + B.c + c' from (add_assoc k B.c c').symm)).toAddMonoidHom).comp
        (baseChangeChowPullbackSquare (FlatBaseChangeSituation.comp B C g' c' hg') f
          (sq'.paste_horiz sq) k)
declarations.comment: part (3): pullback on Chow groups respects composition

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.FilteredBaseChangeSystem.exists_stageChowPullback_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVQ, surjectivity for Chow groups.** Every `k`-cycle class on `X'` is
the image of a `k`-cycle class on `X_i` for some finite stage `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_stageChowPullback_eq (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup s.limitBaseChange.baseChange
      (pullback.snd s.X.hom s.limitBaseChange.g) k) :
    ∃ (i : I) (β : chowGroup (s.stageSituation i)
      (pullback.snd s.X.hom (s.stageToBase i)) k),
      s.stageChowPullback i k β = α
declarations.comment: Chow groups, surjectivity: every k-cycle class on X' comes from some X_i

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.FilteredBaseChangeSystem.exists_transitionChowPullback_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVQ, eventual injectivity for Chow groups.** A `k`-cycle class on
`X_j` whose image in `CH_k(X')` vanishes is annihilated by the comparison homomorphism along
some transition `X_i ⟶ X_j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_transitionChowPullback_eq_zero (j : I) (k : ℤ)
    (β : chowGroup (s.stageSituation j) (pullback.snd s.X.hom (s.stageToBase j)) k)
    (hβ : s.stageChowPullback j k β = 0) :
    ∃ (i : I) (f : i ⟶ j), s.transitionChowPullback f k β = 0
declarations.comment:
Chow groups, eventual injectivity: a k-cycle class on X_j killed by base change
to X' is killed by some transition X_i -> X_j

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.FilteredBaseChangeSystem.exists_stageCyclePullback_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVQ, surjectivity for cycle groups.** Every `k`-cycle on `X'` is the
image of a `k`-cycle on `X_i` for some finite stage `i`.

Since `X'` is quasi-compact the cycle has finite support, so it is a finite integral combination
of fundamental cycles of integral closed subschemes of `X'`. Each of those descends to a finite
stage by `Stacks.Chow.FilteredBaseChangeSystem.exists_stage_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme`,
and the index category being cofiltered, one stage serves for all of them at once.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_stageCyclePullback_eq (k : ℤ)
    (z : CycleGroup s.limitBaseChange.baseChange (pullback.snd s.X.hom s.limitBaseChange.g) k) :
    ∃ (i : I) (w : CycleGroup (s.stageSituation i) (pullback.snd s.X.hom (s.stageToBase i)) k),
      s.stageCyclePullback i k w = z
declarations.comment: cycle groups, surjectivity: every k-cycle on X' is the image of a k-cycle on X_i

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.FilteredBaseChangeSystem.exists_transitionCyclePullback_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVQ, eventual injectivity for cycle groups.** A `k`-cycle on `X_j`
whose image in `Z_k(X')` vanishes is annihilated by the transition to some finite stage
`X_i ⟶ X_j`.

A point of `X_j` carrying a nonzero coefficient cannot lie in the image of `X'`: otherwise the
base-changed cycle would have a nonzero coefficient at a generic point of the inverse image of
the reduced closure of that point, by
`Stacks.Chow.eq_zero_of_baseChangeCyclePullback_eq_zero_of_mem_range`. The cycle has finite
support because `X_j` is quasi-compact, and `X'` is the limit of the `X_i` along affine
transition morphisms, so finitely many points outside the image of `X'` are already outside the
image of a single `X_i`; every coefficient of the transition of the cycle to that stage is a
coefficient of the cycle at a point of that image, hence vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_transitionCyclePullback_eq_zero (j : I) (k : ℤ)
    (z : CycleGroup (s.stageSituation j) (pullback.snd s.X.hom (s.stageToBase j)) k)
    (hz : s.stageCyclePullback j k z = 0) :
    ∃ (i : I) (f : i ⟶ j), s.transitionCyclePullback f k z = 0
declarations.comment:
cycle groups, eventual injectivity: a k-cycle on X_j killed by base change to X'
is killed by some transition X_i -> X_j

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.FilteredBaseChangeSystem.exists_projectiveLineStageCyclePullback_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVQ, surjectivity for the projective-line family.** Every `k`-cycle on
`X' ×_{S'} 𝐏¹_{S'}` is the image of a `k`-cycle on `X_i ×_{S_i} 𝐏¹_{S_i}` for some finite stage
`i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_projectiveLineStageCyclePullback_eq (k : ℤ)
    (z : CycleGroup s.limitBaseChange.baseChange
      (pullback.fst (pullback.snd s.X.hom s.limitBaseChange.g)
        (relativeProjectiveLine s.limitBaseChange.baseChange.S ↘
          s.limitBaseChange.baseChange.S) ≫ pullback.snd s.X.hom s.limitBaseChange.g) k) :
    ∃ (i : I) (c : CycleGroup (s.stageSituation i)
      (pullback.fst (pullback.snd s.X.hom (s.stageToBase i))
        (relativeProjectiveLine (s.diagram.obj i) ↘ s.diagram.obj i) ≫
          pullback.snd s.X.hom (s.stageToBase i)) k),
      s.projectiveLineStageCyclePullback i k c = z
declarations.comment: cycle groups, surjectivity for the projective line family

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.WeilChernData.untwistTrace_one_spec_galois
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FVR.** Assume given data (D0), (D1), (D2') satisfying axioms
(A1)–(A7), and let `k'/k` be a finite Galois extension. Then `∫_{Spec(k')} 1 = [k' : k]`: every
`F`-linear map `λ : H^0(Spec(k'))(0) ⟶ F` with `(id ⊗ λ) γ([Δ]) = 1` (axiom (A6), `γ` the cycle
class map of Tag 0FIF; such a `λ` is unique by Remark 0FIK and is `∫_{Spec(k')}`) takes the unit
class to `[k' : k]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem untwistTrace_one_spec_galois
    (lam : tateTwist F 𝔚.tate (𝔚.grade (spec k k') (2 * ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))) (0 : ℕ) →ₗ[F] F)
    (hlam : 𝔚.traceContract 𝔚.kunneth (spec k k') 0 lam
      (𝔚.γ (prod (spec k k') (spec k k')) 0 (diagonalClass (spec k k') 0)) = 1) :
    𝔚.untwistTrace (spec k k') 0 lam 1 = (Module.finrank k k' : F)
declarations.comment: the source's statement on the actual data (D0), (D1), (D2') satisfying (A1)-(A7) (WeilChernData, with γ of 0FIF): every λ normalised as in (A6) at Spec(k'), i.e. ∫_{Spec(k')} (unique by 0FIK), takes the unit class to [k' : k]; the nonvanishing of H^*(Spec(k')) needed to cancel the unit is derived from (A3), (A4), (A5)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.WeilChernData.toWeilData_trace_one_spec_galois
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FVR for the trace map `∫_X` of the data of Section 0FHA defined by `𝔚`**:
`∫_{Spec(k')} 1 = [k' : k]`, where `∫_{Spec(k')}` is the trace map of `𝔚.toWeilData`, the `λ`
of the axiom (A6) at `Spec(k')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toWeilData_trace_one_spec_galois :
    𝔚.untwistTrace (spec k k') 0 (𝔚.toWeilData.trace (spec k k') 0
      (isNonemptyEquidimensional_of_dimension_zero
        (FirstChernClassData.topologicalKrullDim_spec_field (k := k) (K' := k')))) 1 =
      (Module.finrank k k' : F)
declarations.comment: the source's statement for the trace map ∫_{Spec(k')} of 𝔚.toWeilData, the λ of (A6) at Spec(k'), on the data (D0), (D1), (D2') satisfying (A1)-(A7): ∫_{Spec(k')} 1 = [k' : k]

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.FirstChernClassData.injective_pull_specMap_of_nontrivial
declarations.doc:
For finite separable field extensions `k''/k'/k` and a finite normal separable extension `K/k`
containing `k''` (for instance a normal closure of `k''/k`) with `H^*(Spec(K)) ≠ 0`, pullback
`H^*(Spec(k')) ⟶ H^*(Spec(k''))` is injective, under axioms (A1) and (A5) (the source assumes
(A1)–(A7)); in particular it is injective on `H^0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_pull_specMap_of_nontrivial (hA1 : 𝔇.CoproductAxiom) (hA5 : 𝔇.KunnethAxiom)
    {k' : Type u} [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [FiniteDimensional k k'] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k']
    {k'' : Type u} [Field k''] [Algebra k k''] [FiniteDimensional k k''] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'']
    (incl : k' →ₐ[k] k'') {E : Type u} [Field E] [Algebra k E] [FiniteDimensional k E]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable k E] [Normal k E] (ι : k'' →ₐ[k] E) (hE : Nontrivial (𝔇.H (spec k E))) :
    Function.Injective (𝔇.pull (specMap incl))
declarations.comment: the source's statement, on the actual data (D0), (D1), (D2') over smooth projective k-schemes: with H^*(Spec K) ≠ 0 for a finite normal separable K ⊇ k'' (a normal closure), H^*(Spec k') ⟶ H^*(Spec k'') is injective, from (A1) and (A5)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.FirstChernClassData.injective_pull_specMap_of_axioms
declarations.doc:
For finite separable field extensions `k''/k'/k`, pullback `H^*(Spec(k')) ⟶ H^*(Spec(k''))` is
injective under axioms (A1), (A3), (A4) and (A5), `F` having characteristic zero: the hypothesis
`H^0(Spec(K)) ≠ 0` of the source is a consequence of the axioms
(`Stacks.WeilCohomology.FirstChernClassData.nontrivial_H_spec`). This is the form in which the
proof of Stacks 0FIS uses 0FVS.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_pull_specMap_of_axioms [CharZero F] (hA1 : 𝔇.CoproductAxiom)
    (hA3 : 𝔇.ProjectiveBundleAxiom) (hA4 : 𝔇.DivisorAxiom) (hA5 : 𝔇.KunnethAxiom)
    {k' : Type u} [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [FiniteDimensional k k'] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k']
    {k'' : Type u} [Field k''] [Algebra k k''] [FiniteDimensional k k''] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'']
    (incl : k' →ₐ[k] k'') : Function.Injective (𝔇.pull (specMap incl))
declarations.comment: unconditional form: the nonvanishing hypothesis is derived from (A3), (A4), (A5)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.injective_pullback_of_separable
declarations.doc:
Let `k''/k'/k` be finite separable field extensions. Then pullback
`H^0(Spec(k')) → H^0(Spec(k''))` is injective.

Here `H` is the cohomology functor of `(D1)`, read on the spectra of finite étale `k`-algebras;
since these schemes are zero dimensional, `H^0` is the total cohomology `H^*`. The hypothesis
`kunneth` is axiom `(A5)` and `disjointUnion` is axiom `(A1)`; `traceMap` is the trace map
`∫_{Spec(L)}` of axiom `(A6)` for the zero-dimensional scheme `Spec(L)`, `cycleClass` is the
cycle class map `γ` of `(D2')` on the zero cycles of `Spec(L)`, free of rank one on `[Spec(L)]`,
and `traceMap_cycleClass` is axiom `(C)(b)` for the structure morphism of `Spec(L)`, which
evaluates that trace on `γ(n · [Spec(L)])` as its degree `n · [L : k]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_pullback_of_separable
    (k k' k'' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Field k'']
    [Algebra k k'] [Algebra k k''] [Algebra k' k''] [IsScalarTower k k' k'']
    [FiniteDimensional k k'] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k']
    [FiniteDimensional k' k''] [Algebra.IsSeparable k' k'']
    (F : Type v) [Field F] [CharZero F] (H : FinEtaleAlg k ⥤ CommAlgCat.{w} F)
    (kunneth : ∀ X Y : FinEtaleAlg k, Function.Bijective (finEtaleKunnethMap H X Y))
    (disjointUnion : ∀ (ι : Type u) [Fintype ι] (X : ι → FinEtaleAlg k),
      Function.Bijective (componentRestriction H X))
    (cycleClass : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] (hfin : Module.Finite k L)
      (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparable k L), ℤ →+ H.obj (ofField k L hfin hsep))
    (traceMap : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] (hfin : Module.Finite k L)
      (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparable k L), H.obj (ofField k L hfin hsep) →ₗ[F] F)
    (traceMap_cycleClass : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
      (hfin : Module.Finite k L) (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparable k L) (n : ℤ),
      traceMap L hfin hsep (cycleClass L hfin hsep n) =
        (n : F) * (Module.finrank k L : F)) :
    Function.Injective (H.map (algHomMk (X := ofField k k' inferInstance inferInstance)
      (Y := ofField k k'' (Module.Finite.trans k' k'') (Algebra.IsSeparable.trans k k' k''))
      (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k k' k'')))
declarations.comment: injectivity on cohomology for a tower of finite separable field extensions; the Künneth decomposition of Spec(k') x Spec(K) as a product over the embeddings, the functoriality relations, and the nonvanishing of the cohomology of Spec(K) are derived from the functor of (D1) together with axioms (A1), (A5), (A6) and (C)(b), which are explicit arguments here, as elsewhere in Section 45.14

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.exists_axioms_of_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0FVT.** Let `k'/k` be an extension of fields and `F'/F` an extension of fields
of characteristic zero. Let `𝔇 = (F(1), H^*, c₁^H)` be data (D0), (D1), (D2') for `k` and `F`
and `𝔚' = (F'(1), (H')^*, c₁^{H'})` data (D0), (D1), (D2') for `k'` and `F'`, given with an
isomorphism `F(1) ⊗_F F' ≅ F'(1)` and isomorphisms `H^*(X) ⊗_F F' ≅ (H')^*(X_{k'})` of graded
`F'`-algebras, functorial in the smooth projective scheme `X` over `k`, under which `c₁^H` and
`c₁^{H'}` correspond (`Φ`, a `Stacks.WeilCohomology.FieldExtensionComparison`). If
`F'(1), (H')^*, c₁^{H'}` satisfy (A1)–(A9) — (A1)–(A7) being the fields of
`Stacks.WeilCohomology.WeilChernData`, (A8) `GlobalSections`, (A9) `DivisorTrace` — then
`F(1), H^*, c₁^H` satisfy (A1)–(A9): (A1)–(A5), (A6) for the cycle class map `γ` of Tag 0FIF of
the data `𝔇` (which (A1)–(A4) determine), (A7), (A8), and (A9) for that `γ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_axioms_of_fieldExtension [CharZero F] [CharZero F'] (𝔇 : FirstChernClassData k F)
    (𝔚' : WeilChernData k' F') (Φ : FieldExtensionComparison 𝔇 𝔚'.toFirstChernClassData)
    (h8 : 𝔚'.GlobalSections) (h9 : 𝔚'.DivisorTrace) :
    ∃ (hA1 : 𝔇.CoproductAxiom) (hA2 : 𝔇.PullbackAxiom) (hA3 : 𝔇.ProjectiveBundleAxiom)
      (hA4 : 𝔇.DivisorAxiom) (hA5 : 𝔇.KunnethAxiom),
      𝔇.TraceAxiomFor hA5 (𝔇.cycleClassOf hA1 hA2 hA3 hA4) ∧ 𝔇.BlowupAxiom ∧
        𝔇.GlobalSectionsAxiom ∧ 𝔇.DivisorTraceAxiomFor hA5 (𝔇.cycleClassOf hA1 hA2 hA3 hA4)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The duality isomorphisms.** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k` and
`ω_X^• = a(𝒪_{Spec k})` its relative dualizing complex. For `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and every `i`
there is a `k`-linear isomorphism `Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•) ≅ Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k)`, sending `α` to
`t ∘ H^{-i}(X, α)` with `t : H⁰(X, ω_X^•) ⟶ k` the trace (`Stacks.Duality.traceOverField`); it is
natural in `K` (`Stacks.Duality.dualityEquiv_comp`) and compatible with shifts and distinguished
triangles (`Stacks.Duality.dualityEquiv_shiftedHomComp`,
`Stacks.Duality.dualityEquiv_triangle`).
declarations.statement:
def dualityEquiv (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i : ℤ) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    DerivedCategory.Ext K.obj (ωX).obj i ≃ₗ[k]
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj K.obj) →ₗ[k] k)
declarations.comment: part (5): the isomorphisms Ext^i_X(K, ω_X) = Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityEquiv_comp
declarations.doc:
**Part (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0FVV], functoriality.** The duality isomorphisms are natural in
`K`: for `g : K ⟶ L` in `D(𝒪_X)` and `α ∈ Ext^i_X(L, ω_X^•)`, the linear form attached to
`g ≫ α` is the one attached to `α` precomposed with `H^{-i}(X, g)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualityEquiv_comp (K L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i : ℤ) (g : K.obj ⟶ L.obj)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Ext L.obj (ωX).obj i)
    (x : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).obj
      ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj K.obj)) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualityEquiv f K i (g ≫ α) x =
      dualityEquiv f L i α
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).map
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map g) x)
declarations.comment: part (5): the isomorphisms are functorial in K

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityEquiv_shiftedHomComp
declarations.doc:
**Part (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0FVV], compatibility with shifted morphisms.** For
`β ∈ Ext^j_X(L, K)` and `α ∈ Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•)`, the linear form on `H^{-(i+j)}(X, L)` attached to
the product `β.comp α ∈ Ext^{i+j}_X(L, ω_X^•)` is the one attached to `α` precomposed with the map
`H^{-(i+j)}(X, L) ⟶ H^{-i}(X, K)` induced by `β`. Taking for `β` the identity of `K⟦n⟧` gives
compatibility with shifts (`Stacks.Duality.dualityLinearMap_shift`), and taking for `β` the third
morphism of a distinguished triangle gives compatibility with its connecting maps
(`Stacks.Duality.dualityLinearMap_triangle`).
declarations.statement:
theorem dualityEquiv_shiftedHomComp (K L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) {i j c : ℤ}
    (β : DerivedCategory.Ext L.obj K.obj j) (α : DerivedCategory.Ext K.obj (ωX).obj i)
    (h : i + j = c)
    (x : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-c)).obj
      ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj L.obj)) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualityEquiv f L c (β.comp α h) x =
      dualityEquiv f K i α ((HX).shiftMap β (-c) (-i) (by omega) x)
declarations.comment: part (5): compatibility with shifts and distinguished triangles

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityLinearMap_shift
declarations.doc:
**Compatibility of the duality map with shifts.** Under `Ext^{i+n}_X(K⟦n⟧, ω_X^•) =
Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•)` (composition with the identity of `K⟦n⟧`, an element of `Ext^n_X(K⟦n⟧, K)`) and
the canonical isomorphism `H^{-(i+n)}(X, K⟦n⟧) ≅ H^{-i}(X, K)`, the duality maps of `K⟦n⟧` and
of `K` agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualityLinearMap_shift (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (i n : ℤ)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Ext K (ωX).obj i)
    (x : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-(i + n))).obj
      ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj (K⟦n⟧))) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualityLinearMap f (K⟦n⟧) (i + n)
        (ShiftedHom.comp (𝟙 (K⟦n⟧)) α rfl) x =
      dualityLinearMap f K i α
        (((HX).shiftIso n (-(i + n)) (-i) (by omega)).hom.app K x)
declarations.comment: part (5): compatibility with shifts

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityLinearMap_triangle
declarations.doc:
**Compatibility of the duality map with distinguished triangles.** For a triangle
`K ⟶ L ⟶ M ⟶ K⟦1⟧` of `D(𝒪_X)`, the duality maps intertwine composition with its third morphism,
`Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•) ⟶ Ext^{i+1}_X(M, ω_X^•)`, and the connecting morphism
`H^{-(i+1)}(X, M) ⟶ H^{-i}(X, K)` of the long exact cohomology sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualityLinearMap_triangle (T : Pretriangulated.Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules))
    (i : ℤ) (α : DerivedCategory.Ext T.obj₁ (ωX).obj i)
    (x : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-(i + 1))).obj
      ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj T.obj₃)) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualityLinearMap f T.obj₃ (i + 1)
        (ShiftedHom.comp (T.mor₃ : DerivedCategory.Ext T.obj₃ T.obj₁ 1) α rfl) x =
      dualityLinearMap f T.obj₁ i α
        ((HX).homologySequenceδ T (-(i + 1)) (-i) (by omega) x)
declarations.comment: part (5): compatibility with distinguished triangles

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isDualizingComplex_relativeDualizingComplex_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVV], existence.** For `X` proper over a field `k`, the complex
`ω_X^• = a(𝒪_{Spec k})` is a dualizing complex on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingComplex_relativeDualizingComplex_of_isProper :
    letI := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    IsDualizingComplex (relativeDualizingComplex f
      (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
      (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))).obj
declarations.comment: existence: ω_X^• = a(O_{Spec k}) is a dualizing complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.le_zero_and_le_dim_of_not_isZero_homology_of_isProper
declarations.doc: **[Stacks, Tag 0FVV], part (1).** `H^i(ω_X^•)` is nonzero only for `i ∈ [-dim X, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_zero_and_le_dim_of_not_isZero_homology_of_isProper (i : ℤ)
    (hi : ¬ Limits.IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj
      (relativeDualizingComplex f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))).obj)) :
    i ≤ 0 ∧ (((-i).toNat : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim X
declarations.comment: part (1): H^i(ω_X^•) is nonzero only for i ∈ [-dim X, 0]

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.relativeDualizingModule_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVV], part (2).** `ω_X = H^{-dim X}(ω_X^•)` is a coherent module with property
`(S₂)` whose support is the union of the irreducible components of dimension `dim X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDualizingModule_of_isProper :
    (relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))).IsCoherent ∧
    SheafHasPropertySk X (relativeDualizingModule f
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))) 2 ∧
    _root_.SheafOfModules.supp (relativeDualizingModule f
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))) =
      ⋃₀ {C ∈ irreducibleComponents X | topologicalKrullDim C = topologicalKrullDim X}
declarations.comment: part (2): ω_X is a coherent (S₂)-module supported on the components of dimension dim X

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.topologicalKrullDim_supp_homology_le_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVV], part (3).** The support of `H^i(ω_X^•)` has dimension at most `-i`
(and is empty for `i > 0`).
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_supp_homology_le_of_isProper (i : ℤ) :
    topologicalKrullDim (_root_.SheafOfModules.supp
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj
          (relativeDualizingComplex f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
            (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))).obj)) ≤
      if i ≤ 0 then (((-i).toNat : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) else ⊥
declarations.comment: part (3): dim Supp H^i(ω_X^•) ≤ -i

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_nontrivial_stalk_homology_iff_depth_le_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVV], part (4).** For `x ∈ X` closed, one of `H^i(ω_{X,x}^•)`, …,
`H^0(ω_{X,x}^•)` is nonzero if and only if `depth(𝒪_{X,x}) ≤ -i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nontrivial_stalk_homology_iff_depth_le_of_isProper {x : X}
    (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) (i : ℤ) :
    (∃ j : ℤ, i ≤ j ∧ j ≤ 0 ∧ Nontrivial (moduleStalkAtPoint
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj
          (relativeDualizingComplex f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
            (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))).obj) x)) ↔
      i ≤ 0 ∧ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
        (X.presheaf.stalk x) ≤ ((-i).toNat : ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: part (4): H^i(ω_{X,x}^•) ⊕ … ⊕ H^0(ω_{X,x}^•) ≠ 0 iff depth(O_{X,x}) ≤ -i, at closed points

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualizingModuleHomEquivOfIsProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVV], part (6).** For `F` quasi-coherent on `X` there is a `k`-linear
isomorphism `Hom_X(F, ω_X) ≅ Hom_k(H^{dim X}(X, F), k)`, natural in `F`
(`Stacks.Duality.dualizingModuleHomEquivOfIsProper_comp`).
declarations.statement:
def dualizingModuleHomEquivOfIsProper (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    (F ⟶ relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))) ≃ₗ[k]
      (cohomologyOverField k f F (ENat.toNat ((topologicalKrullDim X).getD 0)) →ₗ[k] k)
declarations.comment: part (6): Hom(F, ω_X) = Hom_k(H^{dim X}(X, F), k) for F quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualizingModuleHomEquivOfIsProper_comp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVV], part (6), functoriality.** The isomorphisms of part (6) are natural in
the quasi-coherent module `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModuleHomEquivOfIsProper_comp {F G : X.Modules} [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    [G.IsQuasicoherent] (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (v : G ⟶ relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))))
    (x : cohomologyOverField k f F (ENat.toNat ((topologicalKrullDim X).getD 0))) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualizingModuleHomEquivOfIsProper f F (φ ≫ v) x =
      dualizingModuleHomEquivOfIsProper f G v
        ((cohomologyOverFieldFunctor k f (ENat.toNat ((topologicalKrullDim X).getD 0))).map
          φ x)
declarations.comment: part (6): the isomorphisms are functorial in F

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.boundedCoherent_relativeDualizingComplex_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVV], footnote to part (5): `ω_X^•` lies in `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`.** Its cohomology
sheaves are coherent ([Stacks, Tag 0A89]) and vanish outside `[-dim X, 0]` (part (1)).
declarations.statement:
theorem boundedCoherent_relativeDualizingComplex_of_isProper :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded (A := X.Modules) (isCoherentSheaf X)
      (relativeDualizingComplex f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))).obj
declarations.comment: footnote to part (5): ω_X^• is in D^b_Coh(O_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.existsUnique_iso_relativeDualizingComplex_of_quasiCoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVV], footnote to part (5): the duality isomorphisms characterize `ω_X^•` in
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` up to unique isomorphism.** If `ω ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` has bijections
`Hom(K, ω) ≃ Hom_k(H⁰(X, K), k)` natural in `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, then exactly one isomorphism
`ω ≅ ω_X^•` carries them to the duality isomorphisms of `ω_X^•` (degree zero of part (5)).
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_relativeDualizingComplex_of_quasiCoherent
    (ω : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
    (φ : ∀ K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X, (K.obj ⟶ ω.obj) ≃
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) 0).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj K.obj) ⟶ ModuleCat.of k k))
    (hφ : ∀ {K L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X} (g : K.obj ⟶ L.obj) (α : L.obj ⟶ ω.obj),
      φ K (g ≫ α) =
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) 0).map
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map g) ≫ φ L α) :
    ∃! e : ω.obj ≅ (relativeDualizingComplex f
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))).obj,
      ∀ (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (α : K.obj ⟶ ω.obj),
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) 0).map
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map (α ≫ e.hom)) ≫ traceOverField f = φ K α
declarations.comment: footnote to part (5): the isomorphisms characterize ω_X^• in D_QCoh(O_X) up to unique isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.existsUnique_iso_relativeDualizingComplex_of_boundedCoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVV], footnote to part (5): it suffices to consider `K ∈ D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`.** If
`ω ∈ D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)` has bijections `Hom(K, ω) ≃ Hom_k(H⁰(X, K), k)` natural in
`K ∈ D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`, then exactly one isomorphism `ω ≅ ω_X^•` carries them to the duality
isomorphisms of `ω_X^•`; this uses that `ω_X^•` lies in `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`
(`Stacks.Duality.boundedCoherent_relativeDualizingComplex_of_isProper`).
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_relativeDualizingComplex_of_boundedCoherent
    (ω : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hω : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded (A := X.Modules) (isCoherentSheaf X) ω)
    (φ : ∀ K : DerivedCategory X.Modules,
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded (A := X.Modules) (isCoherentSheaf X) K →
      ((K ⟶ ω) ≃ ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) 0).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj K) ⟶ ModuleCat.of k k)))
    (hφ : ∀ {K L : DerivedCategory X.Modules}
      (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded (A := X.Modules) (isCoherentSheaf X) K)
      (hL : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded (A := X.Modules) (isCoherentSheaf X) L)
      (g : K ⟶ L) (α : L ⟶ ω),
      φ K hK (g ≫ α) =
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) 0).map
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map g) ≫ φ L hL α) :
    ∃! e : ω ≅ (relativeDualizingComplex f
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))).obj,
      ∀ (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
        (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded (A := X.Modules) (isCoherentSheaf X) K)
        (α : K ⟶ ω),
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) 0).map
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map (α ≫ e.hom)) ≫ traceOverField f = φ K hK α
declarations.comment: footnote to part (5): ω_X^• is characterized by the isomorphisms for K in D^b_Coh(O_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_relativeDualizingComplex_iso_and_relativeDualizingModule_iso_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVV], part (7).** Let `X` be proper over a field `k`, with
`ω_X^• = a(𝒪_{Spec k})`. If `X ⟶ Spec k` is smooth of relative dimension `d`, then
`ω_X^• ≅ ∧^d Ω_{X/k}[d]` and `ω_X ≅ ∧^d Ω_{X/k}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_relativeDualizingComplex_iso_and_relativeDualizingModule_iso_of_smooth
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] (d : ℕ)
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] :
    haveI : CompactSpace X := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f
    haveI : QuasiSeparatedSpace X := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated f
    Nonempty ((relativeDualizingComplex f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))).obj ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules (-d)).obj
        (Scheme.Modules.exteriorPower (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f) d)) ∧
    Nonempty (relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k))) ≅
      Scheme.Modules.exteriorPower (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f) d)
declarations.comment: part (7): for X smooth of relative dimension d over k, ω_X^• ≅ ∧^d Ω_{X/k}[d] and ω_X ≅ ∧^d Ω_{X/k}

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityEquiv_id_eq_traceOverField
declarations.doc:
**The identity of `ω_X^•` corresponds to the trace.** Under the isomorphism of part (5) of
[Stacks, Tag 0FVV] in degree zero, `Hom(ω_X^•, ω_X^•) ≅ Hom_k(H⁰(X, ω_X^•), k)`, the identity
of `ω_X^•` is sent to the trace `t : H⁰(X, ω_X^•) ⟶ k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualityEquiv_id_eq_traceOverField :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualityEquiv f ωX 0 (ShiftedHom.mk₀ (0 : ℤ) rfl (𝟙 (ωX).obj)) = (traceOverField f).hom
declarations.comment: the identity of ω_X^• corresponds via 0FVV (5) to the trace t : H^0(X, ω_X^•) → k

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityEquiv_mk₀_apply
declarations.doc:
**The degree-zero pairing.** For `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, the identification
`Hom(K, ω_X^•) ≅ H⁰(X, K)^∨` of part (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0FVV] is the pairing
`(α, β) ↦ t(α(β))`, where `α(β)` is the image of `β ∈ H⁰(X, K)` under the map
`H⁰(X, K) ⟶ H⁰(X, ω_X^•)` induced by `α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualityEquiv_mk₀_apply (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (α : K.obj ⟶ (ωX).obj)
    (β : (H⁰).obj ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj K.obj)) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualityEquiv f K 0 (ShiftedHom.mk₀ (0 : ℤ) rfl α) β =
      (traceOverField f).hom (((H⁰).map ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map α)).hom β)
declarations.comment: the degree-zero pairing Hom_X(K, ω_X^•) × H^0(X, K) → k, (α, β) ↦ t(α(β))

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityEquiv_apply_eq_traceOverField
declarations.doc:
**The pairing in degree `i`.** For `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `i ∈ ℤ`, the identification
`Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•) ≅ H^{-i}(X, K)^∨` of part (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0FVV] is the pairing
`(α, β) ↦ t(α(β))`: here `α` is regarded as a morphism `K⟦-i⟧ ⟶ ω_X^•` (`extShiftHom`), `β` as an
element of `H⁰(X, K⟦-i⟧) ≅ H^{-i}(X, K)`, and `α(β) ∈ H⁰(X, ω_X^•)` is the image of `β` under
the map that `α` induces on `H⁰(X, -)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualityEquiv_apply_eq_traceOverField (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i : ℤ)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Ext K.obj (ωX).obj i)
    (β : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).obj
      ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj K.obj)) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualityEquiv f K i α β =
      (traceOverField f).hom (((H⁰).map ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map (extShiftHom α))).hom
        ((((HX).shiftIso (-i) 0 (-i) (add_zero _)).inv.app K.obj).hom β))
declarations.comment: the pairing Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•) × H^{-i}(X, K) → k, (α, β) ↦ t(α(β)), with α a morphism K[-i] → ω_X^• and β in H^0(X, K[-i])

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.bijective_dualityLinearMap
declarations.doc:
**The pairing is nondegenerate on one side.** For `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and every `i`, the
pairing `(α, β) ↦ t(α(β))` of `Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•)` with `H^{-i}(X, K)` identifies
`Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•)` with the `k`-linear dual of `H^{-i}(X, K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_dualityLinearMap (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i : ℤ) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    Function.Bijective (dualityLinearMap f K.obj i)
declarations.comment: the pairing identifies Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•) with the k-linear dual of H^{-i}(X, K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_not_bijective_dualityLinearMap_flip
declarations.doc:
**The pairing is in general not nondegenerate on the other side** (the clause "but in general
not vice versa" of [Stacks, Tag 0FVW]). For every field `k`, on the proper scheme `X = Spec k`
there is an object `K` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` for which the other-side map
`H⁰(X, K) ⟶ Hom_X(K, ω_X^•)^∨`, `β ↦ (α ↦ t(α(β)))`, is not bijective: take for `K` the object
with `RΓ(X, K) = k^{(ℕ)}[0]` ([Stacks, Tag 06Z0]), whose `H⁰(X, K) = k^{(ℕ)}` is infinite
dimensional, so that the evaluation map into its double dual is not surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_bijective_dualityLinearMap_flip (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    ∃ K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory (Spec (.of k)),
      letI := Scheme.linearOver (𝟙 (Spec (.of k)))
      ¬ Function.Bijective (dualityLinearMap (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) K.obj 0).flip
declarations.comment: the 'not vice versa' clause: on X = Spec k some K in D_QCoh has H^0(X, K) → Hom_X(K, ω_X^•)^∨ not bijective

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.finiteDimensional_and_isPerfPair_of_coherent
declarations.doc:
**The coherent case.** For `K` in `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`, the `k`-vector spaces
`Hom_X(K, ω_X^•)`, `Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•)` and `H^n(X, K)` are finite dimensional, and for every `i`
the pairing `Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•) × H^{-i}(X, K) ⟶ k`, `(α, β) ↦ t(α(β))`, is perfect.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_and_isPerfPair_of_coherent (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded (fun M : X.Modules => M.IsCoherent) K) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    FiniteDimensional k (K ⟶ (ωX).obj) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, FiniteDimensional k (DerivedCategory.Ext K (ωX).obj i)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, FiniteDimensional k ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) n).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj K))) ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ, (dualityLinearMap f K i).IsPerfPair
declarations.comment: K in D^b_Coh: Hom_X(K, ω_X^•), Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•), H^i(X, K) are finite dimensional and the pairings are perfect

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.coherentTracePairing_isPerfPair_and_dualMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVX].** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k`, `ω_X^•` and
`t : H⁰(X, ω_X^•) ⟶ k` as in [Stacks, Tag 0FVW], and `i ∈ ℤ`.
1. For a coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`, `Ext^i_X(ℱ, ω_X^•)` and `H^{-i}(X, ℱ)` are finite dimensional
   and the pairing `⟨α, β⟩ = t(α(β))` between them (`α` regarded as a morphism
   `ℱ[-i] ⟶ ω_X^•`, `β` as an element of `H⁰(X, ℱ[-i])`) is perfect.
2. For a homomorphism `φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, `⟨α ∘ φ, β⟩ = ⟨α, φ(β)⟩` for
   `α ∈ Ext^i_X(𝒢, ω_X^•)` and `β ∈ H^{-i}(X, ℱ)`.
3. For a homomorphism `φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, the map
   `Ext^i_X(𝒢, ω_X^•) ⟶ Ext^i_X(ℱ, ω_X^•)` induced by `φ` is, via the identifications of
   `Ext^i_X(-, ω_X^•)` with `H^{-i}(X, -)^∨` given by the pairings, the `k`-linear dual of the map
   `H^{-i}(X, ℱ) ⟶ H^{-i}(X, 𝒢)` induced by `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentTracePairing_isPerfPair_and_dualMap (i : ℤ) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    (∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsCoherent →
      FiniteDimensional k (DerivedCategory.Ext ((single₀).obj F) (ωX).obj i) ∧
      FiniteDimensional k ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj ((single₀).obj F))) ∧
      (dualityLinearMap f ((single₀).obj F) i).IsPerfPair ∧
      ∀ (α : DerivedCategory.Ext ((single₀).obj F) (ωX).obj i)
        (β : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).obj
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj ((single₀).obj F))),
        dualityLinearMap f ((single₀).obj F) i α β =
          (traceOverField f).hom
            (((H⁰).map ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map (extShiftHom α))).hom
              ((((HX).shiftIso (-i) 0 (-i) (add_zero _)).inv.app ((single₀).obj F)).hom β))) ∧
    (∀ (F G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), F.IsCoherent → G.IsCoherent →
      ∀ (α : DerivedCategory.Ext ((single₀).obj G) (ωX).obj i)
        (β : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).obj
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj ((single₀).obj F))),
        dualityLinearMap f ((single₀).obj F) i ((single₀).map φ ≫ α) β =
          dualityLinearMap f ((single₀).obj G) i α
            (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).map
              ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map ((single₀).map φ))).hom β)) ∧
    ∀ (F G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherent),
      (dualityEquiv f (singleQuasiCoherent F hF 0) i).toLinearMap ∘ₗ
          extPrecompLinearMap f ((single₀).map φ) i =
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).map
            ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map ((single₀).map φ))).hom.dualMap ∘ₗ
          (dualityEquiv f (singleQuasiCoherent G hG 0) i).toLinearMap

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isPerfPair_dualityCupPairing
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVY].** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k`, with structure morphism
`f : X ⟶ Spec k`, let `ω_X^•` be its dualizing complex of [Stacks, Tag 0FVV] and
`t : H⁰(X, ω_X^•) ⟶ k` the trace of [Stacks, Tag 0FVW]. Let `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` be perfect. Then for
every `i` the pairing

`Hⁱ(X, ω_X^• ⊗^𝐋 E^∨) × H⁻ⁱ(X, E) ⟶ k`, `(ξ, η) ↦ t((1 ⊗ ε)(ξ ∪ η))`

is perfect: both spaces are finite-dimensional `k`-vector spaces and the pairing is a perfect
pairing (`LinearMap.IsPerfPair`: each side is identified with the `k`-linear dual of the other).
Here `∪` is the cup product of Cohomology, Section 0FKU (`cupPairing` at the canonical global cup
product), `E^∨ = R𝓗om(E, 𝒪_X)` and `ε : E^∨ ⊗^𝐋 E ⟶ 𝒪_X` is the evaluation of Cohomology,
Example 0FPC, and `1 ⊗ ε : (ω_X^• ⊗^𝐋 E^∨) ⊗^𝐋 E ⟶ ω_X^•` is followed by the unit constraint
(`dualityCupPairing`). The cohomology groups are the `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`-modules of hypercohomology with
the scalars restricted along `k ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`, and `t` is `Stacks.Duality.traceOverField` read on
them (`traceStd`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfPair_dualityCupPairing
    (hE : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) (i : ℤ) :
    FiniteDimensional k ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u} (globalRingHom f)).obj
        (cohomologyModule (tensorDual X.toRingedSpace (dualizingComplexStd f) E) i)) ∧
      FiniteDimensional k
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u} (globalRingHom f)).obj (cohomologyModule E (-i))) ∧
      (dualityCupPairing f E i).IsPerfPair

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isDualizingModuleOf_relativeDualizingModule_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVZ], part (1).** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k` which is
Cohen--Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension `d`. The module `ω_X` of [Stacks, Tag 0FVV] is a
dualizing module on `X` in the sense of [Stacks, Section 0AWH]: `ω_X^•` is a dualizing complex,
`-d` is the least degree in which it has nonzero cohomology, and `ω_X = H^{-d}(ω_X^•)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingModuleOf_relativeDualizingModule_of_isProper
    (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X)
    (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d) :
    letI := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    IsDualizingModuleOf ωM (ωX).obj (-(d : ℤ))
declarations.comment: part (1): ω_X is a dualizing module on X (Section 0AWH)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.relativeDualizingModule_isCoherent_cohenMacaulay_supp_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVZ], part (2).** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k` which is
Cohen--Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension `d`. The module `ω_X` of [Stacks, Tag 0FVV] is a
coherent Cohen--Macaulay `𝒪_X`-module whose support is `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDualizingModule_isCoherent_cohenMacaulay_supp_of_isProper
    (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X) :
    (ωM).IsCoherent ∧ AlgebraicGeometry.SheafIsCohenMacaulay X ωM ∧
      _root_.SheafOfModules.supp ωM = Set.univ
declarations.comment: part (2): ω_X is a coherent Cohen-Macaulay module whose support is X

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVZ], part (3), the isomorphisms.** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k`
which is Cohen--Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension `d`. For `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and every
`i` there is a `k`-linear isomorphism `Ext^i_X(K, ω_X[d]) ≅ Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k)`. It is part (5)
of [Stacks, Tag 0FVV] (`Stacks.Duality.dualityEquiv`) read through `ω_X^• ≅ ω_X[d]`
(`Stacks.Duality.relativeDualizingComplexIsoShiftOfIsProper`); it is natural in `K`
(`Stacks.Duality.dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_comp`) and compatible with shifts and distinguished
triangles (`Stacks.Duality.dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_shiftedHomComp`,
`Stacks.Duality.dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_shift`,
`Stacks.Duality.dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_triangle`).
declarations.statement:
def dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X)
    (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X) (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d)
    (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i : ℤ) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    DerivedCategory.Ext K.obj (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj ωM)⟦(d : ℤ)⟧) i
      ≃ₗ[k] ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj K.obj) →ₗ[k] k)
declarations.comment: part (3): the isomorphisms Ext^i_X(K, ω_X[d]) = Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_comp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVZ], part (3), functoriality.** The isomorphisms of part (3) are natural in
`K`: for `g : K ⟶ L` and `α ∈ Ext^i_X(L, ω_X[d])`, the linear form attached to `g ≫ α` is the one
attached to `α` precomposed with `H^{-i}(X, g)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_comp (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X)
    (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X) (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d)
    (K L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i : ℤ) (g : K.obj ⟶ L.obj)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Ext L.obj
      (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj ωM)⟦(d : ℤ)⟧) i)
    (x : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).obj
      ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj K.obj)) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper f hCM hequi d hd K i (g ≫ α) x =
      dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper f hCM hequi d hd L i α
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).map
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map g) x)
declarations.comment: part (3): the isomorphisms are functorial in K

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_shiftedHomComp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVZ], part (3), compatibility with shifted morphisms.** For
`β ∈ Ext^j_X(L, K)` and `α ∈ Ext^i_X(K, ω_X[d])`, the linear form on `H^{-(i+j)}(X, L)` attached to
`β.comp α ∈ Ext^{i+j}_X(L, ω_X[d])` is the one attached to `α` precomposed with the map
`H^{-(i+j)}(X, L) ⟶ H^{-i}(X, K)` induced by `β`. This contains the compatibility with shifts
(`Stacks.Duality.dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_shift`) and with distinguished triangles
(`Stacks.Duality.dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_triangle`).
declarations.statement:
theorem dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_shiftedHomComp (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X)
    (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X) (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d)
    (K L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) {i j c : ℤ}
    (β : DerivedCategory.Ext L.obj K.obj j)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Ext K.obj
      (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj ωM)⟦(d : ℤ)⟧) i)
    (h : i + j = c)
    (x : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-c)).obj
      ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj L.obj)) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper f hCM hequi d hd L c (β.comp α h) x =
      dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper f hCM hequi d hd K i α
        ((HX).shiftMap β (-c) (-i) (by omega) x)
declarations.comment: part (3): compatibility with shifts and distinguished triangles

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_shift
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVZ], part (3), compatibility with shifts.** Under
`Ext^{i+n}_X(K⟦n⟧, ω_X[d]) = Ext^i_X(K, ω_X[d])` (composition with the identity of `K⟦n⟧`) and
`H^{-(i+n)}(X, K⟦n⟧) ≅ H^{-i}(X, K)`, the isomorphisms of `K⟦n⟧` and of `K` agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_shift (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X)
    (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X) (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d)
    (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i n : ℤ)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Ext K.obj
      (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj ωM)⟦(d : ℤ)⟧) i)
    (x : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-(i + n))).obj
      ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj (K.obj⟦n⟧))) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper f hCM hequi d hd
        ⟨K.obj⟦n⟧, ObjectProperty.le_shift _ n K.obj K.property⟩ (i + n)
        (ShiftedHom.comp (𝟙 (K.obj⟦n⟧)) α rfl) x =
      dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper f hCM hequi d hd K i α
        (((HX).shiftIso n (-(i + n)) (-i) (by omega)).hom.app K.obj x)
declarations.comment: part (3): compatibility with shifts

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_triangle
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVZ], part (3), compatibility with distinguished triangles.** For a triangle
`K ⟶ L ⟶ M ⟶ K⟦1⟧` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, the isomorphisms intertwine composition with its third
morphism, `Ext^i_X(K, ω_X[d]) ⟶ Ext^{i+1}_X(M, ω_X[d])`, and the connecting morphism
`H^{-(i+1)}(X, M) ⟶ H^{-i}(X, K)` of the long exact cohomology sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper_triangle (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X)
    (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X) (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d)
    (T : Pretriangulated.Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules))
    (h₁ : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := X.Modules)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf) T.obj₁)
    (h₃ : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := X.Modules)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf) T.obj₃)
    (i : ℤ)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Ext T.obj₁
      (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj ωM)⟦(d : ℤ)⟧) i)
    (x : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-(i + 1))).obj
      ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj T.obj₃)) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper f hCM hequi d hd ⟨T.obj₃, h₃⟩ (i + 1)
        (ShiftedHom.comp (T.mor₃ : DerivedCategory.Ext T.obj₃ T.obj₁ 1) α rfl) x =
      dualityEquivShiftOfIsProper f hCM hequi d hd ⟨T.obj₁, h₁⟩ i α
        ((HX).homologySequenceδ T (-(i + 1)) (-i) (by omega) x)
declarations.comment: part (3): compatibility with distinguished triangles

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualizingModuleExtEquivOfIsProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVZ], part (4).** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k` which is
Cohen--Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension `d`. For `F` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module there
are `k`-linear isomorphisms `Ext^{d-i}_X(F, ω_X) ≅ Hom_k(H^i(X, F), k)`, natural in `F`
(`Stacks.Duality.dualizingModuleExtEquivOfIsProper_comp`). It is part (3) for `K = F[0]` in degree
`-i`, through `Ext^{d-i}(F[0], ω_X[0]) = Ext^{-i}(F[0], ω_X[d])` and
`H^{-(-i)}(X, F[0]) = H^i(X, F)`.
declarations.statement:
def dualizingModuleExtEquivOfIsProper (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X)
    (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X) (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (i : ℕ) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    Abelian.zExt F ωM ((d : ℤ) - i) ≃ₗ[k] (cohomologyOverField k f F i →ₗ[k] k)
declarations.comment: part (4): Ext^{d-i}(F, ω_X) = Hom_k(H^i(X, F), k) for F quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualizingModuleExtEquivOfIsProper_comp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FVZ], part (4), functoriality.** The isomorphisms of part (4) are natural in
the quasi-coherent module `F`: for `φ : F ⟶ G` and `α ∈ Ext^{d-i}_X(G, ω_X)`, the linear form
attached to `φ ≫ α` is the one attached to `α` precomposed with `H^i(X, φ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModuleExtEquivOfIsProper_comp (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X)
    (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X) (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d)
    {F G : X.Modules} [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] (φ : F ⟶ G) (i : ℕ)
    (α : Abelian.zExt G ωM ((d : ℤ) - i)) (x : cohomologyOverField k f F i) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    dualizingModuleExtEquivOfIsProper f hCM hequi d hd F i
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map φ ≫ α) x =
      dualizingModuleExtEquivOfIsProper f hCM hequi d hd G i α
        ((cohomologyOverFieldFunctor k f i).map φ x)
declarations.comment: part (4): the isomorphisms are functorial in F

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.serrePairing_isPerfPair
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FW0].** Let `X` be a proper Cohen--Macaulay scheme over a field `k` which is
equidimensional of dimension `d`, let `ω_X^•` and `ω_X` be as in [Stacks, Tag 0FVV], so that
`ω_X^• = ω_X[d]` by [Stacks, Tag 0FVZ], and let `t : Hᵈ(X, ω_X) ⟶ k` be the trace of
[Stacks, Tag 0FVW] (`Stacks.Duality.topTrace`). Let `ℰ` be a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module with
dual `ℰ^∨`. Then for all `i + j = d` the pairing

`Hⁱ(X, ω_X ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℰ^∨) × Hʲ(X, ℰ) ⟶ k,  (ξ, η) ↦ t((1 ⊗ ε)(ξ ∪ η))`

(`Stacks.Duality.serrePairing`) is perfect, where `∪` is the cup product of Cohomology,
Section 0FKU and `ε : ℰ^∨ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℰ ⟶ 𝒪_X` is the evaluation map.
declarations.statement:
theorem serrePairing_isPerfPair (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X)
    (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X) (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d)
    (E : X.Modules) (hE : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E)
    (i j : ℤ) (hij : i + j = d) :
    (serrePairing f hCM hequi d hd E i j hij).IsPerfPair

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_iso_relativeDualizing_of_factorization
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be proper over a field `k` with structure morphism `f`, and suppose `f` factors as
`f' ≫ g` with `f' : X ⟶ Spec k'` for a field `k'`. Then `ω_X^•` and `ω_X` of [Stacks, Tag 0FVV]
for `f` are isomorphic to those constructed for `f'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_relativeDualizing_of_factorization {k' : Type u} [Field k']
    (f' : X ⟶ Spec (.of k')) (g : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (h : f' ≫ g = f) :
    haveI : IsProper f' := haveI : IsProper (f' ≫ g) := h ▸ ‹IsProper f›; IsProper.of_comp f' g
    Nonempty (relativeDualizingComplex f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k))) ≅
      relativeDualizingComplex f' (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f')
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k')))) ∧
    Nonempty (relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k))) ≅
      relativeDualizingModule f' (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f')
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k'))))
declarations.comment: (1): ω_X^• and ω_X are as in 0FVV for a factorization X → Spec k' → Spec k

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_iso_relativeDualizing_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be proper over a field `k` with structure morphism `f`, let `K/k` be a field extension
and `X_K = X ×_{Spec k} Spec K`, with projections `g' : X_K ⟶ X` and `f_K : X_K ⟶ Spec K`. Then
the pullbacks `L(g')^* ω_X^•` and `(g')^* ω_X` are isomorphic to the dualizing complex and module
of [Stacks, Tag 0FVV] constructed for `f_K`.
declarations.statement:
