theorem nonempty_iso_relativeDualizing_baseChange (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    Nonempty ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback'
        (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))).obj
          (relativeDualizingComplex f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
            (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))) ≅
      relativeDualizingComplex (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs _)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of K)))) ∧
    Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
        (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))).obj
          (relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
            (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))) ≅
      relativeDualizingModule (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs _)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of K))))
declarations.comment: (2): the pullbacks of ω_X^• and ω_X to X_K are as in 0FVV for X_K → Spec K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeFrobenius_relativeFormsTrace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks, Lemma 0FW2.** Let `p` be a prime number and let `X → S` be a smooth morphism of
relative dimension `d` of schemes in characteristic `p`. Then:

* the relative Frobenius `F = F_{X/S} : X → X^{(p)}` (Varieties, Definition 0CC9) is finite and
  syntomic; it is a morphism over `S`, `F ≫ (X^{(p)} → S) = (X → S)`, so `F_*Ω^•_{F ≫ g}` is
  `F_{X/S,*}Ω^•_{X/S}`;
* the corresponding map `Θ_{X/X^{(p)}} : F_{X/S,*}Ω^•_{X/S} → Ω^•_{X^{(p)}/S}` of Proposition
  0FLC (3) (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.relativeFormsTrace`, a map of complexes by
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.relativeFormsTrace_deRhamComplex_d`) is zero in every degree
  `k ≠ d`;
* in degree `d` it is a surjection (an epimorphism of sheaves of modules on `X^{(p)}`).
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeFrobenius_relativeFormsTrace :
    haveI := isFinite_relativeFrobenius S p hS X d
    IsFinite (relativeFrobenius S p hS X).left ∧ Syntomic (relativeFrobenius S p hS X).left ∧
      (relativeFrobenius S p hS X).left ≫ ((frobeniusTwist S p hS).obj X).hom = X.hom ∧
      (∀ k ≠ d, (relativeFrobenius S p hS X).left.relativeFormsTrace
          ((frobeniusTwist S p hS).obj X).hom (syntomic_relativeFrobenius S p hS X d) k = 0) ∧
      Epi ((relativeFrobenius S p hS X).left.relativeFormsTrace
          ((frobeniusTwist S p hS).obj X).hom (syntomic_relativeFrobenius S p hS X d) d)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.hodgeDuality
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FW4].** Let `k` be a field and `X` a nonempty smooth proper scheme over `k`,
equidimensional of dimension `d`. There is a `k`-linear map `t : Hᵈ(X, Ω^d_{X/k}) ⟶ k` such
that for all `p, q` the pairing `H^q(X, Ω^p_{X/k}) × H^{d-q}(X, Ω^{d-p}_{X/k}) ⟶ k`,
`(ξ, ξ') ↦ t(ξ ∪ ξ')` is perfect, and `t` is unique up to precomposing with multiplication by a
unit of `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)`: a linear map `t'` has the same property if and only if
`t' = t ∘ (u · -)` for a unit `u` of `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)`, and that unit is unique. The map `t` is the
trace read through `ω_X ≅ Ω^d_{X/k}` ([Stacks, Tag 0FVV], part (7)).
declarations.statement:
theorem hodgeDuality [Smooth f] [Nonempty X] (d : ℕ)
    (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d) :
    ∃ t : sheafCohomology f (relativeDifferentialForms f d) d →ₗ[k] k,
      (∀ p q : ℤ, (hodgePairing f d t p q).IsPerfPair) ∧
      ∀ t' : sheafCohomology f (relativeDifferentialForms f d) d →ₗ[k] k,
        (∀ p q : ℤ, (hodgePairing f d t' p q).IsPerfPair) ↔
          ∃! u : (Γ(X, ⊤))ˣ, t' = t ∘ₗ cohomologySMul f (relativeDifferentialForms f d) d u
declarations.comment: for X nonempty smooth proper over a field k, equidimensional of dimension d: there is t : H^d(X, Omega^d) -> k, unique up to precomposition with multiplication by a unit of H^0(X, O_X), such that every pairing H^q(X, Omega^p) x H^{d-q}(X, Omega^{d-p}) -> k, (xi, xi') |-> t(xi cup xi') is perfect

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.deRhamComplex_d_zero_app_top_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The degree-zero de Rham differential of a smooth proper scheme over a field vanishes on
global sections.**
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamComplex_d_zero_app_top_eq_zero (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [Smooth f] [IsProper f]
    (B : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
      (SheafOfModules.moduleOfDifferentials.{u, u, u} (inverseImageStructureMap f)))
    (D : SheafOfModules.DeRhamDifferential B) :
    ((SheafOfModules.deRhamComplex B D).d 0 1).val.app (op ⊤) = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeDifferential.rightDerived_map_deRham_d_eq_zero_of_isProper_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0FW6].** Let `k` be a field and `X` a smooth proper scheme over `k`,
equidimensional of dimension `d`. Then the map `d : Hᵈ(X, Ω^{d-1}_{X/k}) ⟶ Hᵈ(X, Ω^d_{X/k})`
induced by the de Rham differential is zero. The dualizing module of a smooth proper scheme over
a field is its sheaf of top forms by [Stacks, Tag 0FVV], part (7).
declarations.statement:
theorem rightDerived_map_deRham_d_eq_zero_of_isProper_of_smooth {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] [Smooth f]
    (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ((sectionsFunctor X.carrier ⊤).rightDerived d).map
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).map (f.deRhamComplex.d (d - 1) d)) = 0
declarations.comment: for X smooth proper over a field k, equidimensional of dimension d, the map d : H^d(X, Omega^{d-1}_{X/k}) -> H^d(X, Omega^d_{X/k}) is zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.deRhamPoincareDuality
declarations.doc:
**Poincaré duality for de Rham cohomology ([Stacks, Tag 0FW7]).** Let `k` be a field and
`X` a nonempty smooth proper scheme over `k`, equidimensional of dimension `d`. There is a
`k`-linear map `t : H^{2d}_{dR}(X/k) ⟶ k` such that for every `i` the pairing
`Hⁱ_{dR}(X/k) × H^{2d-i}_{dR}(X/k) ⟶ k`, `(ξ, ξ') ↦ t(ξ ∪ ξ')` is perfect, and `t` is unique up
to precomposing with multiplication by a unit of `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)`: a linear map `t'` has the same
property if and only if `t' = t(ξ ∪ -)` for the class `ξ ∈ H⁰_{dR}(X/k)` of a unit `u` of
`H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` — `H⁰_{dR}(X/k) = H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` through `Ω^•_{X/k} ⟶ 𝒪_X[0]`
(`bijective_deRhamCohomologyZeroToSections`) — and that unit is unique.

The cup product is that of Section 0FM3 (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.deRhamCup`, see
`deRhamCupBilinear_apply`), defined for `X` with affine diagonal; a scheme proper over a field
is separated, so it has affine diagonal.
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamPoincareDuality [IsProper f] [Smooth f] [Nonempty X] (d : ℕ)
    (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = d) :
    letI := AlgebraicGeometry.DeRhamTypeComplex.isAffineHom_diagonal_of_isProper f
    ∃ t : deRhamCohomologyOverField f ((d : ℤ) + d) →ₗ[k] k,
      (∀ i : ℤ, ((deRhamCupBilinear f i ((d : ℤ) + d - i) ((d : ℤ) + d) (by ring)).compr₂
        t).IsPerfPair) ∧
      ∀ t' : deRhamCohomologyOverField f ((d : ℤ) + d) →ₗ[k] k,
        (∀ i : ℤ, ((deRhamCupBilinear f i ((d : ℤ) + d - i) ((d : ℤ) + d) (by ring)).compr₂
          t').IsPerfPair) ↔
          ∃! u : (Γ(X, ⊤))ˣ, ∃ ξ : deRhamCohomologyOverField f 0,
            deRhamCohomologyZeroToSections f ξ = u ∧
              t' = t ∘ₗ deRhamCupBilinear f 0 ((d : ℤ) + d) ((d : ℤ) + d) (zero_add _) ξ
declarations.comment: for X nonempty smooth proper over a field k, equidimensional of dimension d: there is t : H^{2d}_dR(X/k) -> k, unique up to precomposition with multiplication by a unit of H^0(X, O_X), such that for all i the pairing H^i_dR(X/k) x H^{2d-i}_dR(X/k) -> k, (xi, xi') |-> t(xi cup xi') is perfect

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamChern.existsUnique_deRhamTotalChernClass
declarations.doc:
There is a unique rule which assigns to every quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme `X` a
total Chern class `c^{dR} : K₀(Vect(X)) ⟶ ∏_{i ≥ 0} H^{2i}_{dR}(X/𝐙)`, read by components
`c X α i ∈ H^{2i}_{dR}(X/𝐙)` in the even-degree ring, such that `c(α + β) = c(α) c(β)` (and
`c(0) = 1`), `c(f^*α) = f^*c(α)` and `c([ℒ]) = 1 + c₁^{dR}(ℒ)`
(`Stacks.DeRhamChern.IsDeRhamTotalChernClass`).
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_deRhamTotalChernClass :
    ∃! c : ∀ X : (QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).FullSubcategory,
        VectorBundleKZero ((QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι.obj X).left → ℕ →
          evenDeRhamRing ((QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι.obj X).hom,
      IsDeRhamTotalChernClass (QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι c
declarations.comment: there is a unique rule assigning to every quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme X a total Chern class c^dR : K_0(Vect(X)) -> prod_{i >= 0} H^{2i}_dR(X/Z) with (1) c^dR(alpha + beta) = c^dR(alpha) c^dR(beta), (2) c^dR(f^*alpha) = f^*c^dR(alpha) for every morphism f : X -> X' of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, (3) c^dR([L]) = 1 + c_1^dR(L) for L in Pic(X)

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamChern.exists_injective_pull_hasInvertibleFiltration
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FWA: the splitting principle for de Rham cohomology.** Let `X` be a
quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let `ℰ_i` be a finite collection of locally free
`𝒪_X`-modules of ranks `r_i`. There is a morphism `p : P ⟶ X` of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes such that

1. `p^* : ⨁_i H^{2i}_{dR}(X/𝐙) ⟶ ⨁_i H^{2i}_{dR}(P/𝐙)` is injective,
2. each `p^*ℰ_i` has a filtration whose successive quotients `ℒ_{i,1}, …, ℒ_{i,r_i}` are
   invertible `𝒪_P`-modules.

The projection is moreover flat. This is Tag 0FI7 in the de Rham situation of the proof of
Tag 0FW9.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_injective_pull_hasInvertibleFiltration
    (X : (QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).FullSubcategory) (I : Type*) [Finite I]
    (E : I → ((QCQSScheme.toScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).obj X).Modules) (r : I → ℕ)
    (hE : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{0, 0, 0} (E i) (r i)) :
    ∃ (P : (QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).FullSubcategory) (p : P ⟶ X),
      Flat ((QCQSScheme.toScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).map p) ∧
      Function.Injective (pull (QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι p) ∧
      ∀ i, HasInvertibleFiltration ((QCQSScheme.toScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).obj P)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((QCQSScheme.toScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).map p)).obj
          (E i)) (r i)
declarations.comment: the analogue of Weil Cohomology Theories, Lemma 0FI7 (splitting principle) holds for de Rham Chern classes on quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes: for a finite collection of locally free O_X-modules E_i of ranks r_i there is p : P -> X with p^* injective on (+)_i H^{2i}_dR(-/Z) and each p^*E_i filtered with invertible successive quotients

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamChern.IsDeRhamTotalChernClass.apply_classOf_tensorObj_invertible_of_any
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FWA: the Chern classes of a twist for de Rham Chern classes.** Let
`c^{dR}` be the de Rham total Chern class of Tag 0FW9 (by that lemma there is exactly one rule with
its three properties), let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, `ℰ` a finite locally
free `𝒪_X`-module of constant rank `r` and `ℒ` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. Then for every `i`

`c^{dR}_i(ℰ ⊗ ℒ) = ∑_{j=0}^{i} binom(r - i + j, j) c^{dR}_{i-j}(ℰ) ∪ c₁^{dR}(ℒ)^j`

in `H^{2i}_{dR}(X/𝐙)`, the binomial coefficient written `(r + j - i).choose j`: it equals
`binom(r - i + j, j)` whenever `r - i + j ≥ 0`, and otherwise `i - j > r` and the factor
`c^{dR}_{i-j}(ℰ)` vanishes. This is Tag 0FI8 in the de Rham situation of the proof of Tag 0FW9;
the splitting principle half of Tag 0FWA is
`Stacks.DeRhamChern.exists_injective_pull_hasInvertibleFiltration`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsDeRhamTotalChernClass.apply_classOf_tensorObj_invertible_of_any
    {c : ∀ X : (QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).FullSubcategory,
      VectorBundleKZero ((QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι.obj X).left → ℕ →
        evenDeRhamRing ((QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι.obj X).hom}
    (hc : IsDeRhamTotalChernClass (QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι c)
    (X : (QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).FullSubcategory)
    (E L : ((QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι.obj X).left.Modules) (r : ℕ)
    (hE : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{0, 0, 0} E r)
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
      ((QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι.obj X).left.presheaf
      ((QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι.obj X).left.ringCatSheaf.2 L)
    (i : ℕ) :
    c X (VectorBundleKZero.classOf _
        (Scheme.Modules.tensorObjRingedSpace
          ((QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι.obj X).left E L)) i =
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (i + 1), (r + j - i).choose j •
        (c X (VectorBundleKZero.classOf _ E) (i - j) *
          c₁ (QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι X
            (picardClassOf ((QCQSScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℤ))).ι.obj X).left L hL) ^ j)
declarations.comment: the analogue of Weil Cohomology Theories, Lemma 0FI8 (chern classes of tensor products) holds for de Rham Chern classes on quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes: for the de Rham total Chern class c^dR of Tag 0FW9, E finite locally free of constant rank r, L invertible and every i, c^dR_i(E (x) L) = sum_{j=0}^i binom(r-i+j, j) c^dR_{i-j}(E) cup c_1^dR(L)^j, binom(r-i+j, j) written (r + j - i).choose j in N, which agrees with it wherever c^dR_{i-j}(E) is nonzero. The analogue of Lemma 0FI7 is exists_injective_pull_hasInvertibleFiltration

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamChern.existsUnique_deRhamChernCharacter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FWB.** There is a unique rule which assigns to every quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme `X` over `𝐐` a Chern character
`ch^{dR} : K₀(Vect(X)) ⟶ ∏_{i ≥ 0} H^{2i}_{dR}(X/𝐐)` such that (1) `ch^{dR}` is a ring map,
(2) `f^* ∘ ch^{dR} = ch^{dR} ∘ f^*` for every morphism `f : X' ⟶ X` of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes over `𝐐`, and (3) `ch^{dR}([ℒ]) = exp(c₁^{dR}(ℒ))` for `ℒ ∈ Pic(X)`.

An element of `∏_{i ≥ 0} H^{2i}_{dR}(X/𝐐)` is the sequence of its components, the `i`-th read in
`⨁_j H^{2j}_{dR}(X/𝐐)` and lying in `H^{2i}_{dR}(X/𝐐)`; the properties are
`Stacks.DeRhamChern.IsDeRhamChernCharacter`. The proof is the source's: the category of
quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes over `𝐐` with `A(X) = ⨁_i H^{2i}_{dR}(X/𝐐)` satisfies
the axioms of Section 45.12, and `A(X)` is a `𝐐`-algebra, so Proposition 0FI9 applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_deRhamChernCharacter :
    ∃! ch : ∀ X : (QCQSScheme specRat).FullSubcategory,
        VectorBundleKZero X.obj.left → ℕ → evenDeRhamRing X.obj.hom,
      IsDeRhamChernCharacter (QCQSScheme specRat).ι ch
declarations.comment: the unique rule ch^dR : K_0(Vect(X)) -> prod_i H^{2i}_dR(X/Q) on quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes X over Q, with (1) ch^dR a ring map, (2) f^* ch^dR = ch^dR f^* on all of K_0 for every morphism f : X' -> X of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes over Q, (3) ch^dR([L]) = exp(c_1^dR(L)) for L in Pic(X); prod H^{2i} read as sequences of components in ⨁ H^{2j} with the i-th in H^{2i}. Proved from Tag 0FI9 at the standing situation sourceChernSetupRat, whose axioms are all proved: (1) Tag 0FM3, (2) the clopen splitting, (3) Tag 0FMD, (4) Proposition 0FMT, (5) Lemmas 0FMX and 0FMY, clauses (1)-(3)(c) of the category

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilDeRham.exists_weilCohomologyTheory_deRham
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Proposition 0FWD**: for a field `k` of characteristic zero, the functor
`X ↦ H^*_{dR}(X/k)` on smooth projective schemes over `k` is a Weil cohomology theory over `k`
with coefficients in `k` (Definition 0FI2).

Formulation: there is a Weil cohomology theory `W : WeilCohomologyTheory k k` (Definition 0FI2:
data (D0) – (D3) satisfying (A), (B), (C) and condition (2) of Lemma 0FI0) whose data (D0) – (D3)
are those of de Rham cohomology. These are `h.toWeilData …` for `h` a cohomological Chern
character (Tag 0FIE) of the de Rham data `deRhamFirstChernClassData k` of Section 0FWC, so that
* (D0) `F(1)` is `k`;
* (D1) `H^*(X)` is `H^*_{dR}(X/k)`, with its grading, cup product and pullbacks
  (`W.H`, `W.grade`, the ring structure and `W.pull` are those of `deRhamFirstChernClassData k`);
* (D2) the cycle class map `γ` is the one of Lemma 0FIF built from the de Rham first Chern class
  `c₁^{dR}` (the Chern character `ch` is determined by `c₁^{dR}`,
  `FirstChernClassData.existsUnique_isCohomologicalChernCharacter`);
* (D3) `∫_X` is the trace map `λ_X` of axiom (A6), normalised by `(1 ⊗ λ_X)γ([Δ]) = 1`.

The proof assembles axioms (A1) – (A8) for de Rham cohomology and applies Proposition 0FIU.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_weilCohomologyTheory_deRham [CharZero k] :
    ∃ W : WeilCohomologyTheory k k, ∃ ch,
      ∃ h : (deRhamFirstChernClassData k).IsCohomologicalChernCharacter ch,
        W.toWeilData = h.toWeilData coproductAxiom deRham_projectiveBundleAxiom
          (deRham_kunnethAxiom k) (deRham_traceAxiom h)
declarations.comment: de Rham cohomology over a field of characteristic zero is a Weil cohomology theory (Definition 0FI2, coefficients k), with data (D0)-(D3) those of de Rham cohomology: F(1) = k, H^* = H^*_dR(-/k) with cup product and pullbacks, gamma from c_1^dR (0FIF), trace lambda of (A6)

declarations.name: Stacks.HodgeWeil.exists_weilCohomologyTheory_hodge
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Remark 0FWE, part 1**: for a field `k` of characteristic zero, Hodge
cohomology `X ↦ H^*_{Hodge}(X/k) = ⨁_{p, q} H^q(X, Ω^p_{X/k})` on smooth projective schemes over
`k`, equipped with `c₁^{Hodge}`, determines a Weil cohomology theory over `k` with coefficients in
`k` (Definition 0FI2).

Formulation, as for de Rham cohomology (Proposition 0FWD,
`Stacks.WeilDeRham.exists_weilCohomologyTheory_deRham`): there is a Weil cohomology theory
`W : WeilCohomologyTheory k k` (data (D0) – (D3) satisfying (A), (B), (C) and condition (2) of
Lemma 0FI0) whose data are `h.toWeilData …` for a cohomological Chern character `h` (Tag 0FIE) of
the Hodge data `hodgeFirstChernClassData k`, so that
* (D0) `F(1)` is `k`;
* (D1) `H^*(X)` is `H^*_{Hodge}(X/k)` graded by total degree, with its cup product and pullbacks;
* (D2) the cycle class map `γ` is the one of Lemma 0FIF built from `c₁^{Hodge}` (the Chern
  character is determined by `c₁^{Hodge}`,
  `FirstChernClassData.existsUnique_isCohomologicalChernCharacter`);
* (D3) `∫_X` is the trace map `λ_X` of axiom (A6), normalised by `(1 ⊗ λ_X)γ([Δ]) = 1`.

The proof is the one of Proposition 0FWD: (A1) – (A8) for the Hodge data and Proposition 0FIU.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_weilCohomologyTheory_hodge [CharZero k] :
    ∃ W : WeilCohomologyTheory k k, ∃ ch,
      ∃ h : (hodgeFirstChernClassData k).IsCohomologicalChernCharacter ch,
        W.toWeilData = h.toWeilData (hodge_coproductAxiom k) (hodge_projectiveBundleAxiom k)
          (hodge_kunnethAxiom k) (hodge_traceAxiom k h)
declarations.comment: part 1 (the first sentence): for k of characteristic zero, Hodge cohomology H^*_Hodge(-/k) with c_1^Hodge is a Weil cohomology theory (Definition 0FI2, coefficients k), with data (D0)-(D3) those of Hodge cohomology: F(1) = k, H^* = H^*_Hodge(-/k) with cup product and pullbacks, gamma from c_1^Hodge (0FIF), trace lambda of (A6). Part 2 (the consequence) is degeneratesAt_one_of_finrank_grade_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.HodgeWeil.degeneratesAt_one_of_finrank_grade_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Remark 0FWE, part 2** (the "amusing consequence"): let `k` be a field of
characteristic zero. If the betti numbers of a Weil cohomology theory over `k` are independent of
the chosen Weil cohomology theory, then the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence degenerates at
`E_1`.

Formulation: the hypothesis `hbetti` says that for any two Weil cohomology theories `W`, `W'` over
`k` (Definition 0FI2), with coefficients in fields `F`, `F'` of characteristic zero,
`dim_F H^n_W(X) = dim_{F'} H^n_{W'}(X)` for every smooth projective `X` over `k` and every `n`.
The conclusion is that for every smooth projective `X` over `k`, every Hodge-to-de Rham spectral
sequence `E_1^{p, q} = H^q(X, Ω^p_{X/k}) ⟹ H^{p + q}_{dR}(X/k)` of `X` (a brutal-truncation
spectral sequence of `Ω^•_{X/k}` abutting to `H^*_{dR}(X/k)`, which exists by Tag 0FM7)
degenerates at `E_1`.

The proof: by part 1 (`exists_weilCohomologyTheory_hodge`) and Proposition 0FWD
(`Stacks.WeilDeRham.exists_weilCohomologyTheory_deRham`), Hodge and de Rham cohomology are Weil
cohomology theories with coefficients in `k`, so `hbetti` gives
`dim_k H^n_{Hodge}(X/k) = dim_k H^n_{dR}(X/k)`; as the Hodge groups are finite dimensional this
is `E_1`-degeneration (`degeneratesAt_one_of_finrank_hodgeGradeOf_eq`).
declarations.statement:
theorem degeneratesAt_one_of_finrank_grade_eq [CharZero k]
    (hbetti : ∀ (F F' : Type u) [Field F] [CharZero F] [Field F'] [CharZero F']
      (W : WeilCohomologyTheory k F) (W' : WeilCohomologyTheory k F')
      (X : (SmoothProjectiveScheme k).FullSubcategory) (n : ℤ),
      Module.finrank F (W.grade X n) = Module.finrank F' (W'.grade X n))
    (X : (SmoothProjectiveScheme k).FullSubcategory)
    (S : StupidTruncationSpectralSequence (baseRingedSpace _)
      (deRhamComplexInt (X := X.obj.left.toRingedSpace) (formsAlgebras X.obj.hom)
        (deRhamDifferential (formsAlgebras X.obj.hom))))
    (hS : SpectralSequence.AbutsTo S.spectralSequence
      (deRhamCohomology (X := X.obj.left.toRingedSpace) (formsAlgebras X.obj.hom)
        (deRhamDifferential (formsAlgebras X.obj.hom)))) :
    S.spectralSequence.DegeneratesAt 1
declarations.comment: part 2 (the amusing consequence): over k of characteristic zero, if the betti numbers dim_F H^n(X) of Weil cohomology theories (any coefficient fields F of characteristic zero) do not depend on the theory, then for every smooth projective X over k the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence (every brutal-truncation spectral sequence of the de Rham complex abutting to H^*_dR(X/k), 0FM7) degenerates at E_1. Part 1 is exists_weilCohomologyTheory_hodge

declarations.name: Algebra.isGeometricallyIntegral_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FWF.** Let `k` be a field and let `S` be a `k`-algebra. The following are
equivalent: (1) `S` is geometrically integral over `k`; (2) `S ⊗[k] k'` is a domain for every
field extension `k'/k`; (3) `S ⊗[k] k'` is a domain for every finite extension `k'/k`;
(4) `S ⊗[k] AlgebraicClosure k` is a domain.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isGeometricallyIntegral_tfae (k S : Type u) [Field k] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] :
    List.TFAE
      [ Algebra.IsGeometricallyIntegral k S,
        ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'], IsDomain (S ⊗[k] k'),
        ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [Module.Finite k k'], IsDomain (S ⊗[k] k'),
        IsDomain (S ⊗[k] AlgebraicClosure k) ]

declarations.name: Module.projective_iff_isLocallyConstant_finrank_fiber
declarations.doc:
**A finite module over a reduced ring is projective iff its fibre dimension is locally
constant.** For `R` a reduced commutative ring and `M` a finite `R`-module, `M` is projective
(equivalently, by `Module.finite_projective_tfae`, finite locally free) if and only if the
function `ρ_M : Spec(R) → ℕ`, `𝔭 ↦ dim_{κ(𝔭)} M ⊗_R κ(𝔭)`, is locally constant. This is item (9)
in the list of characterizations of finite projective modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.projective_iff_isLocallyConstant_finrank_fiber (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [IsReduced R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    Module.Projective R M ↔
      IsLocallyConstant fun p : PrimeSpectrum R ↦
        Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.Fiber M)

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.Reduced.isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_isFiniteType_and_isLocallyConstant_fiberRank
declarations.doc:
On a reduced scheme, a quasi-coherent sheaf is finite locally free exactly
when it is of finite type and has locally constant fibre rank.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_isFiniteType_and_isLocallyConstant_fiberRank
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree F ↔
      (F.IsFiniteType ∧ IsLocallyConstant (fiberRank F))

étale morphism of `FTS S`. Then `f^! ≅ f^*` as functors on `D^+_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, for `f^!` computed
at any compactification `j`. The isomorphism at `K` is
`Lf^*K ≅ Lf^*K ⊗ᴸ 𝒪_X ≅ Lf^*K ⊗ᴸ f^!𝒪_Y ≅ f^!K`, the last map being `μ_{f,K}` of

declarations.name: padicInt_tensorProduct_not_henselian
declarations.doc:
For an odd prime `p`, the coproduct over `ℤ` of two copies of the Henselian pair
`(ℤ_[p], (p))` is not Henselian. Its residue ring is `ZMod p`, and an explicit nontrivial
idempotent, built from a square root of an integer which is not a rational square, witnesses that
its spectrum is disconnected.
declarations.statement:
theorem padicInt_tensorProduct_not_henselian (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : Odd p) :
    let R := ℤ_[p]
    let A := R ⊗[ℤ] R
    let I : Ideal A := Ideal.span {algebraMap ℤ A (p : ℤ)}
    HenselianRing R (Ideal.span {(p : R)}) ∧
      Ideal.map (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft : R →ₐ[ℤ] A).toRingHom
        (Ideal.span {(p : R)}) = I ∧
      Ideal.map (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : R →ₐ[ℤ] A).toRingHom
        (Ideal.span {(p : R)}) = I ∧
      Nonempty ((A ⧸ I) ≃+* ZMod p) ∧
      (HenselianRing A I → IsLocalRing A) ∧
      ¬ IsLocalRing A ∧
      ¬ HenselianRing A I ∧
      ¬ ConnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum A) ∧
      ∃ t u v w : R,
        t = algebraMap ℤ R (if p = 3 then 7 else 1 + (p : ℤ)) ∧
        ¬ IsSquare ((if p = 3 then (7 : ℤ) else 1 + (p : ℤ)) : ℚ) ∧
        u ^ 2 = t ∧ 2 * v = 1 ∧ t * w = 1 ∧
        let e : A := (v ⊗ₜ[ℤ] (1 : R)) *
          ((1 : R) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] (1 : R) - (w * u) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] u)
        IsIdempotentElem e ∧ e ≠ 0 ∧ e ≠ 1

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.exists_extension_of_preservesFilteredColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FWY** (existence).
Let `C` and `D` have `w`-filtered colimits, let `P` be a property of objects of `C` cutting out
an essentially `w`-small full subcategory of categorically compact objects (Stacks 0FWX), and
assume every object of `C` is a `w`-filtered colimit of objects satisfying `P`. Then every
functor `F'` out of that subcategory extends to a functor `C ⥤ D` commuting with filtered
colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_extension_of_preservesFilteredColimits
    [HasFilteredColimitsOfSize.{w, w} C] [HasFilteredColimitsOfSize.{w, w} D]
    [EssentiallySmall.{w} P.FullSubcategory]
    (hP : P ≤ isFinitelyPresentable.{w} C) (hgen : ∀ X : C, P.ind.{w} X)
    (F' : P.FullSubcategory ⥤ D) :
    ∃ F : C ⥤ D, PreservesFilteredColimitsOfSize.{w, w} F ∧ Nonempty (P.ι ⋙ F ≅ F')

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.existsUnique_iso_of_preservesFilteredColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FWY** (uniqueness).
Under the hypotheses of `exists_extension_of_preservesFilteredColimits`, an extension of `F'`
commuting with filtered colimits is unique up to a unique natural isomorphism compatible with
the identifications of the restrictions with `F'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_of_preservesFilteredColimits
    [HasFilteredColimitsOfSize.{w, w} C] [EssentiallySmall.{w} P.FullSubcategory]
    (hP : P ≤ isFinitelyPresentable.{w} C) (hgen : ∀ X : C, P.ind.{w} X)
    {F' : P.FullSubcategory ⥤ D} (F₁ F₂ : C ⥤ D)
    [PreservesFilteredColimitsOfSize.{w, w} F₁] [PreservesFilteredColimitsOfSize.{w, w} F₂]
    (e₁ : P.ι ⋙ F₁ ≅ F') (e₂ : P.ι ⋙ F₂ ≅ F') :
    ∃! φ : F₁ ≅ F₂, Functor.whiskerLeft P.ι φ.hom = (e₁ ≪≫ e₂.symm).hom

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.Triangle.hom_ext_of_hom₁_eq_of_hom₃_eq
declarations.doc:
A morphism of distinguished triangles is determined by its outer two components, as
soon as one of the following five vanishing conditions holds:
`Hom(Y, X') = 0`, or `Hom(Z, Y') = 0`, or `Hom(X, X') = Hom(Z, X') = 0`, or
`Hom(Z, X') = Hom(Z, Z') = 0`, or `Hom(X[1], Z') = Hom(Z, X') = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Triangle.hom_ext_of_hom₁_eq_of_hom₃_eq {T T' : Triangle C}
    (hT : T ∈ distTriang C) (hT' : T' ∈ distTriang C) (φ ψ : T ⟶ T')
    (h₁ : φ.hom₁ = ψ.hom₁) (h₃ : φ.hom₃ = ψ.hom₃)
    (H : (∀ u : T.obj₂ ⟶ T'.obj₁, u = 0) ∨
      (∀ u : T.obj₃ ⟶ T'.obj₂, u = 0) ∨
      ((∀ u : T.obj₁ ⟶ T'.obj₁, u = 0) ∧ ∀ u : T.obj₃ ⟶ T'.obj₁, u = 0) ∨
      ((∀ u : T.obj₃ ⟶ T'.obj₁, u = 0) ∧ ∀ u : T.obj₃ ⟶ T'.obj₃, u = 0) ∨
      ((∀ u : T.obj₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧ ⟶ T'.obj₃, u = 0) ∧ ∀ u : T.obj₃ ⟶ T'.obj₁, u = 0)) :
    φ = ψ

declarations.name: closedUnderDirectSums_add_star_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FX3 (1).** `add 𝒜 ⋆ add ℬ` is closed under direct sums:
for all `X, X' ∈ add 𝒜 ⋆ add ℬ` we have `X ⊞ X' ∈ add 𝒜 ⋆ add ℬ`.

Proof (as in the source): pick distinguished triangles `T : A → X → B → A[1]`
and `T' : A' → X' → B' → A'[1]` with `A, A' ∈ add 𝒜`, `B, B' ∈ add ℬ`. The product
triangle `productTriangle ![T, T']` is distinguished (`productTriangle_distinguished`),
its legs are the `Fin 2`-products of the legs of `T, T'`, which via `finProd2` are the
binary biproducts `A ⊞ A'`, `X ⊞ X'`, `B ⊞ B'`. Since `add` is closed under `⊞`
(`add_closedUnderDirectSums`) and under iso (`add_iso`), `A ⊞ A' ∈ add 𝒜`,
`B ⊞ B' ∈ add ℬ`, and the middle object is iso to `X ⊞ X'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedUnderDirectSums_add_star_add (𝒜 ℬ : Set C) :
    ClosedUnderDirectSums (add 𝒜 ⋆ add ℬ)

declarations.name: closedUnderDirectSums_smd_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FX3 (2).** `smd (add 𝒜)` is closed under direct sums:
for all `X, X' ∈ smd (add 𝒜)` we have `X ⊞ X' ∈ smd (add 𝒜)`.

Proof (as in the source): write `A ≅ X ⊞ Y`, `A' ≅ X' ⊞ Y'` with
`A, A' ∈ add 𝒜`. Then `A ⊞ A' ∈ add 𝒜` (`add_closedUnderDirectSums`) and
`A ⊞ A' ≅ (X ⊞ Y) ⊞ (X' ⊞ Y') ≅ (X ⊞ X') ⊞ (Y ⊞ Y')` (`biprodRearrange`),
exhibiting `X ⊞ X'` as a direct summand of `A ⊞ A' ∈ add 𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedUnderDirectSums_smd_add (𝒜 : Set C) :
    ClosedUnderDirectSums (smd (add 𝒜))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.retractClosure_extensionProductIter_isClosedUnderBinaryProducts_and_add
declarations.doc:
For a full subcategory `P` of a triangulated category which is closed under direct sums,
the subcategory `smd(P^{⋆ (n + 1)})` of direct summands of `n`-fold extensions of objects of
`P` is strictly full, closed under direct sums and closed under direct summands, and these
subcategories are additive in the number of factors:
`smd(P^{⋆ (n + m + 1)}) = smd(smd(P^{⋆ (n + 1)}) ⋆ smd(P^{⋆ (m + 1)}))`. Taking
`P = add(A)` this is the Stacks project's `Cₙ = smd(add(A)^{⋆ n})`, strictly full, closed under
direct sums and direct summands, with `C_{n + m} = smd(Cₙ ⋆ C_m)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem retractClosure_extensionProductIter_isClosedUnderBinaryProducts_and_add
    (P : ObjectProperty C) [P.IsClosedUnderBinaryProducts] [IsTriangulated C] (n m : ℕ) :
    (P.extensionProductIter n).retractClosure.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
      (P.extensionProductIter n).retractClosure.IsClosedUnderBinaryProducts ∧
      (P.extensionProductIter n).retractClosure.IsStableUnderRetracts ∧
      (P.extensionProductIter (n + m + 1)).retractClosure =
        (extensionProduct (P.extensionProductIter n).retractClosure
          (P.extensionProductIter m).retractClosure).retractClosure

declarations.name: Stacks.TriangulatedGenerators.isoClosure_strictMap_biSup_shift_eq_and_strictMap_operations_le
declarations.statement:
theorem isoClosure_strictMap_biSup_shift_eq_and_strictMap_operations_le
    (A B : ObjectProperty C) (S : Set ℤ) (n : ℕ) :
    ((⨆ i ∈ S, A.isoClosure.shift i).strictMap F).isoClosure =
        ⨆ i ∈ S, (A.strictMap F).isoClosure.shift i ∧
      A.retractClosure.strictMap F ≤ (A.strictMap F).retractClosure ∧
      A.binaryProductsClosure.strictMap F ≤ (A.strictMap F).binaryProductsClosure ∧
      (extensionProduct A B).strictMap F ≤ extensionProduct (A.strictMap F) (B.strictMap F) ∧
      (A.extensionProductIter n).strictMap F ≤ (A.strictMap F).extensionProductIter n
declarations.comment: Each of `F(𝒜[a, b]) = F(𝒜)[a, b]` (for any set of shifts, up to isomorphism), `F(smd(𝒜)) ⊂ smd(F(𝒜))`, `F(add(𝒜)) ⊂ add(F(𝒜))`, `F(𝒜 ⋆ ℬ) ⊂ F(𝒜) ⋆ F(ℬ)` and `F(𝒜^{⋆ n}) ⊂ F(𝒜)^{⋆ n}`, with `F(𝒜) = 𝒜.strictMap F`.

declarations.name: Stacks.TriangulatedGenerators.retractClosure_extensionProductIter_biSup_shift_inverseImage_of_le
declarations.doc:
**The bounded-shift form of `smd(add(P[c, d])^{⋆ n})` is functorial along an exact functor.**
Let `F : C ⥤ D` be an exact functor of pretriangulated categories, let `P` be a property of
objects of `C` and `Q` one of `D`, and suppose `F` carries every object satisfying `P` to one
satisfying `Q`. Then `F` carries `smd(add(P[c, d])^{⋆ n})` into `smd(add(Q[c, d])^{⋆ n})`: the
shift interval `[c, d]` and the number `n` of extensions are the same on both sides.

This composes the compatibilities of Derived Categories, Remark 13.35.5 ([Stacks, Tag 0FX5])
for the explicit subcategories `Cₙ = smd(add(E[c, d])^{⋆ n})` built from a bounded range of
shifts as in [Stacks, Tag 0FX9]. Tracking the interval is the content: the
unbounded-shift form `Stacks.TriangulatedGenerators.triangEnvelopeIter_inverseImage_of_le`,
stated with `ObjectProperty.triangEnvelopeIter`, gives no control on which shifts of `Q` the
image uses.
declarations.statement:
theorem retractClosure_extensionProductIter_biSup_shift_inverseImage_of_le
    {P : ObjectProperty C} {Q : ObjectProperty D} (h : ∀ ⦃X : C⦄, P X → Q (F.obj X))
    (c d : ℤ) (n : ℕ) :
    ((⨆ i ∈ Set.Icc c d, P.isoClosure.shift i).binaryProductsClosure.extensionProductIter n
      ).retractClosure ≤
      ((((⨆ i ∈ Set.Icc c d, Q.isoClosure.shift i).binaryProductsClosure.extensionProductIter n
        ).retractClosure).inverseImage F)
declarations.comment: The composite `F(smd(add(𝒜[c, d])^{⋆ n})) ⊂ smd(add(F(𝒜)[c, d])^{⋆ n})`.

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.prop_retractClosure_extensionProductIter_of_prop_homology_and_of_prop_X
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be an abelian category and `E` a class of objects of `C`, viewed inside the derived
category `D(C)`. Let `a ≤ b`. (1) If the cohomology of `K : D(C)` vanishes outside `[a, b]` and
each `H^i(K)` with `i ∈ [a, b]` is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of objects of `E`, then
`K` is a direct summand of a `(b - a)`-fold extension of finite direct sums of objects of `E`
placed in degrees `[a, b]`, that is, `K ∈ smd(add(E[a, b])^{⋆ (b - a + 1)})`. (2) The same
conclusion holds for `K = Q.obj L` when `L` is a cochain complex vanishing outside `[a, b]` whose
terms `L^i` with `i ∈ [a, b]` are direct summands of finite direct sums of objects of `E`. The
special cases where the objects `H^i(K)`, resp. `L^i`, are themselves in `E` are parts (1) and (3)
of [Stacks, Tag 0FX7].
declarations.statement:
theorem prop_retractClosure_extensionProductIter_of_prop_homology_and_of_prop_X
    (E : ObjectProperty C) {a b : ℤ} (hab : a ≤ b) :
    (∀ (K : DerivedCategory C) [K.IsGE a] [K.IsLE b],
        (∀ i ∈ Set.Icc a b,
          E.binaryProductsClosure.retractClosure ((homologyFunctor C i).obj K)) →
        ((⨆ i ∈ Set.Icc a b,
            E.map (singleFunctor C i)).binaryProductsClosure.extensionProductIter
          (b - a).toNat).retractClosure K) ∧
    (∀ (L : CochainComplex C ℤ) [L.IsStrictlyGE a] [L.IsStrictlyLE b],
        (∀ i ∈ Set.Icc a b, E.binaryProductsClosure.retractClosure (L.X i)) →
        ((⨆ i ∈ Set.Icc a b,
            E.map (singleFunctor C i)).binaryProductsClosure.extensionProductIter
          (b - a).toNat).retractClosure (Q.obj L))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isZero_obj_shift_of_retractClosure_extensionProductIter
declarations.doc:
Let `H : C ⥤ A` be a homological functor from a triangulated category to an abelian category,
with `H^i(X) = H(X⟦i⟧)`, and let `E` be a class of objects of `C` such that `H^i(E) = 0` for
`E ∈ E` and `i ∉ [a, b]`. Then every object `X` which is a direct summand of an `n`-fold extension
of finite direct sums of objects `E⟦-j⟧` with `E ∈ E` and `j ∈ [c, d]` satisfies `H^i(X) = 0` for
`i ∉ [a + c, b + d]`. In the notation of [Stacks, Tag 0FX0], for
`X ∈ smd(add(E[c, d])^{⋆ (n + 1)})` we have `H^i(X) = 0` for `i ∉ [a + c, b + d]`; the window does
not depend on the number of extensions, so it is sharper than the window `[-m + na, m + nb]` of
[Stacks, Tag 0FX8], which it implies for `a ≤ 0 ≤ b`, `c = -m`, `d = m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_obj_shift_of_retractClosure_extensionProductIter
    (H : C ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological] (E : ObjectProperty C) {a b : ℤ}
    (hE : ∀ ⦃Y : C⦄, E Y → ∀ i ∉ Set.Icc a b, IsZero (H.obj (Y⟦i⟧)))
    (c d : ℤ) (n : ℕ) {X : C}
    (hX : ((⨆ j ∈ Set.Icc c d,
      E.isoClosure.shift j).binaryProductsClosure.extensionProductIter n).retractClosure X)
    {i : ℤ} (hi : i ∉ Set.Icc (a + c) (b + d)) :
    IsZero (H.obj (X⟦i⟧))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.triangEnvelopeIter_eq_and_triangEnvelopeIter_add
declarations.doc:
The descriptions of the levels of the triangulated envelope, [Stacks, Tag 0FX9]. Write
`⟨P⟩ₙ₊₁ = P.triangEnvelopeIter n` (Mathlib counts extensions, so its index is one less than the
source's). Then

* `⟨P⟩₁ = smd(add(P[-∞, ∞]))` and `⟨P⟩ₙ₊₁ = smd(⟨P⟩₁ ⋆ ⟨P⟩ₙ)`: these are the source's definition
  of the levels, so `P.triangEnvelopeIter` is the source's `⟨E⟩` for `P = {E}`;
* `⟨P⟩ₙ₊₁ = smd(⟨P⟩ₙ ⋆ ⟨P⟩₁)` as well, so the bracketing of `⟨P⟩₁ ⋆ … ⋆ ⟨P⟩₁` is immaterial;
* `⟨P⟩ₙ₊₁ = smd(⟨P⟩₁^{⋆ (n + 1)})`, the left and middle equalities of the source's display;
* `⟨P⟩ₙ₊₁ = ⋃_{m} smd(add(P[-m, m])^{⋆ (n + 1)})`, the right-hand equality of the display,
  with `P[-m, m]` spelled `⨆ i ∈ Set.Icc (-m) m, P.isoClosure.shift i`;
* `⟨P⟩_{(n + 1) + (n' + 1)} = smd(⟨P⟩ₙ₊₁ ⋆ ⟨P⟩ₙ'₊₁)`, the second claim of the source.

The source's ranges `n, n' ≥ 1` and `m ≥ 1` are `n, n', m : ℕ` here, the same unions since the
families are monotone. An arbitrary property of objects `P` replaces the single object `E`; the
source's statement is the case `P = ObjectProperty.singleton E`. `[IsTriangulated C]` is the
source's "triangulated": the octahedron axiom gives the associativity of `⋆`
([Stacks, Tag 0FX1]) used in the second and last conjuncts.
declarations.statement:
public theorem triangEnvelopeIter_eq_and_triangEnvelopeIter_add [IsTriangulated C]
    (P : ObjectProperty C) :
    P.triangEnvelopeIter 0 = (P.shiftClosure ℤ).binaryProductsClosure.retractClosure ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, P.triangEnvelopeIter (n + 1) =
      (extensionProduct (P.triangEnvelopeIter 0) (P.triangEnvelopeIter n)).retractClosure) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, P.triangEnvelopeIter (n + 1) =
      (extensionProduct (P.triangEnvelopeIter n) (P.triangEnvelopeIter 0)).retractClosure) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, P.triangEnvelopeIter n =
      ((P.triangEnvelopeIter 0).extensionProductIter n).retractClosure) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, P.triangEnvelopeIter n =
      ⨆ m : ℕ, ((⨆ i ∈ Set.Icc (-(m : ℤ)) (m : ℤ),
        P.isoClosure.shift i).binaryProductsClosure.extensionProductIter n).retractClosure) ∧
    ∀ n n' : ℕ, P.triangEnvelopeIter (n + n' + 1) =
      (extensionProduct (P.triangEnvelopeIter n) (P.triangEnvelopeIter n')).retractClosure

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsClassicalTriangulatedGenerator.isStrongTriangulatedGenerator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FXA**: in a triangulated category which has a strong generator, every classical
generator is a strong generator. Here the ambient strong generator is a finite family of objects
`X : ι → C` (the source's case is a single object, `ι = Unit`), and the classical generator is an
object property `P` (the source's case is `P = ObjectProperty.singleton E`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsClassicalTriangulatedGenerator.isStrongTriangulatedGenerator [IsTriangulated C]
    {P : ObjectProperty C} (hP : P.IsClassicalTriangulatedGenerator)
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] {X : ι → C} (hX : (ofObj X).IsStrongTriangulatedGenerator) :
    P.IsStrongTriangulatedGenerator

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isSaturated_isTriangulated_rightOrthogonal_and_leftOrthogonal
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a triangulated category and let `A` be a full subcategory of `C` invariant under
all shifts. Then both the right orthogonal `A.rightOrthogonal` and the left orthogonal
`A.leftOrthogonal` of `A` are strictly full (`ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms`),
saturated (`ObjectProperty.IsSaturated`, [Stacks, Tag 05RB]), triangulated subcategories of `C`:
each is a pre-triangulated subcategory (`ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated`) whose full subcategory is
a triangulated category.

Closure under isomorphisms and the triangulated structure are Mathlib's instances on the
orthogonals of a shift-invariant property; saturation follows from the stability of the
orthogonals under retracts, `isStableUnderRetracts_rightOrthogonal_and_leftOrthogonal`, a direct
summand being a retract.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isSaturated_isTriangulated_rightOrthogonal_and_leftOrthogonal
    (A : ObjectProperty C) [A.IsStableUnderShift ℤ] :
    (A.rightOrthogonal.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧ A.rightOrthogonal.IsSaturated ∧
        A.rightOrthogonal.IsTriangulated ∧
        CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated A.rightOrthogonal.FullSubcategory) ∧
      (A.leftOrthogonal.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧ A.leftOrthogonal.IsSaturated ∧
        A.leftOrthogonal.IsTriangulated ∧
        CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated A.leftOrthogonal.FullSubcategory)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsRightAdmissible
declarations.doc:
A property `A` of the objects of a pretriangulated category `C` is *right admissible* if it is
strictly full (closed under isomorphisms) and triangulated, and the inclusion
`A.ι : A.FullSubcategory ⥤ C` has a right adjoint. By [Stacks, Tag 0CQS] the last condition holds
if and only if every object `X` of `C` fits in a distinguished triangle `A' ⟶ X ⟶ B ⟶ A'⟦1⟧` with
`A'` satisfying `A` and `B` in the right orthogonal of `A`, and it then forces `A = ᗮ(Aᗮ)`.
declarations.statement:
public class IsRightAdmissible (A : ObjectProperty C) : Prop extends
  A.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms, A.IsTriangulated, A.ι.IsLeftAdjoint

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsLeftAdmissible
declarations.doc:
A property `A` of the objects of a pretriangulated category `C` is *left admissible* if it is
strictly full (closed under isomorphisms) and triangulated, and the inclusion
`A.ι : A.FullSubcategory ⥤ C` has a left adjoint. By [Stacks, Tag 0CQT] the last condition holds
if and only if every object `X` of `C` fits in a distinguished triangle `A' ⟶ X ⟶ B ⟶ A'⟦1⟧` with
`A'` in the left orthogonal of `A` and `B` satisfying `A`, and it then forces `A = (ᗮA)ᗮ`.
declarations.statement:
public class IsLeftAdmissible (A : ObjectProperty C) : Prop extends
  A.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms, A.IsTriangulated, A.ι.IsRightAdjoint

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsTwoSidedAdmissible
declarations.doc:
A property `A` of the objects of a pretriangulated category `C` is *two-sided admissible* if
it is both right and left admissible, i.e. `A` is a strictly full triangulated subcategory whose
inclusion `A.ι : A.FullSubcategory ⥤ C` has both a right and a left adjoint.
declarations.statement:
public class IsTwoSidedAdmissible (A : ObjectProperty C) : Prop extends
  A.IsRightAdmissible, A.IsLeftAdmissible

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.PostnikovSystem.subsingleton_hom_last
declarations.doc:
Let `Xₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X₀` and `X'ₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X'₀` be complexes in a pretriangulated category, let
`f i : Xᵢ ⟶ X'ᵢ` be a family of morphisms, and let `S`, `S'` be Postnikov systems for the two
complexes, with objects `Yᵢ`, `Y'ᵢ`. If

1. every morphism `Xᵢ⟦i⟧ ⟶ Y'ₙ⟦n⟧` with `i ≥ 1` is zero, or
2. every morphism `Yₙ⟦n⟧ ⟶ X'ⱼ⟦j⟧` with `j < n` is zero, or
3. every morphism `Xᵢ⟦i - j + 1⟧ ⟶ X'ⱼ` and every morphism `Xⱼ ⟶ X'ᵢ⟦i - j⟧` with `i < j` is
   zero,

then any two morphisms of Postnikov systems `S ⟶ S'` over `f` — families `g i : Yᵢ ⟶ Y'ᵢ`
compatible with the morphisms `Yᵢ ⟶ Xᵢ`, `Xᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Yᵢ` and `Yᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ₊₁⟦1⟧` of the two systems —
induce the same morphism `Yₙ ⟶ Y'ₙ` on the totalizations. Under (3) they agree in every
component (`PostnikovSystem.subsingleton_hom_of_hom_shift_eq_zero`); under (1) or (2) the
intermediate components need not agree (`PostnikovSystem.exists_not_subsingleton_hom` in
`StacksFrontier.CategoryTheory.Triangulated.PostnikovSystemsCounterexample`), and the
uniqueness of the totalization component is the corrected form of these two cases.
declarations.statement:
theorem PostnikovSystem.subsingleton_hom_last {n : ℕ}
    {X X' : Fin (n + 1) → D} {d : ∀ i : Fin n, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc}
    {d' : ∀ i : Fin n, X' i.succ ⟶ X' i.castSucc}
    (S : PostnikovSystem X d) (S' : PostnikovSystem X' d') (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ X' i)
    (h : (∀ i : Fin (n + 1), 0 < (i : ℕ) →
            ∀ u : (X i)⟦((i : ℕ) : ℤ)⟧ ⟶ (S'.obj (Fin.last n))⟦(n : ℤ)⟧, u = 0) ∨
         (∀ j : Fin (n + 1), (j : ℕ) < n →
            ∀ u : (S.obj (Fin.last n))⟦(n : ℤ)⟧ ⟶ (X' j)⟦((j : ℕ) : ℤ)⟧, u = 0) ∨
         ((∀ i j : Fin (n + 1), (i : ℕ) < (j : ℕ) →
            ∀ u : (X i)⟦((i : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((j : ℕ) : ℤ) + 1⟧ ⟶ X' j, u = 0) ∧
          (∀ i j : Fin (n + 1), (i : ℕ) < (j : ℕ) →
            ∀ u : X j ⟶ (X' i)⟦((i : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((j : ℕ) : ℤ)⟧, u = 0))) :
    ((fun g : ∀ i, S.obj i ⟶ S'.obj i => g (Fin.last n)) ''
      {g : ∀ i, S.obj i ⟶ S'.obj i |
        (∀ i, g i ≫ S'.π i = S.π i ≫ f i) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin n, S.p i ≫ g i.castSucc = f i.succ ≫ S'.p i) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin n, S.δ i ≫ (g i.succ)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = g i.castSucc ≫ S'.δ i)}).Subsingleton
declarations.comment: (1), (2), (3): uniqueness of the component on the totalizations

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.PostnikovSystem.subsingleton_hom_of_hom_shift_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Let `Xₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X₀` and `X'ₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X'₀` be complexes in a pretriangulated category, let
`f i : Xᵢ ⟶ X'ᵢ` be a family of morphisms, and let `S`, `S'` be Postnikov systems for the two
complexes, with objects `Yᵢ`, `Y'ᵢ`. If every morphism `Xᵢ⟦i - j + 1⟧ ⟶ X'ⱼ` and every morphism
`Xⱼ ⟶ X'ᵢ⟦i - j⟧` with `i < j` is zero (case (3) of the Stacks lemma), then there is at most one
morphism of Postnikov systems `S ⟶ S'` over `f`: any two families `g i : Yᵢ ⟶ Y'ᵢ` compatible
with the morphisms `Yᵢ ⟶ Xᵢ`, `Xᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Yᵢ` and `Yᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ₊₁⟦1⟧` of the two systems agree in every
component.
declarations.statement:
theorem PostnikovSystem.subsingleton_hom_of_hom_shift_eq_zero {n : ℕ}
    {X X' : Fin (n + 1) → D} {d : ∀ i : Fin n, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc}
    {d' : ∀ i : Fin n, X' i.succ ⟶ X' i.castSucc}
    (S : PostnikovSystem X d) (S' : PostnikovSystem X' d') (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ X' i)
    (h : ∀ i j : Fin (n + 1), (i : ℕ) < (j : ℕ) →
      ∀ u : (X i)⟦((i : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((j : ℕ) : ℤ) + 1⟧ ⟶ X' j, u = 0)
    (h' : ∀ i j : Fin (n + 1), (i : ℕ) < (j : ℕ) →
      ∀ u : X j ⟶ (X' i)⟦((i : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((j : ℕ) : ℤ)⟧, u = 0) :
    {g : ∀ i, S.obj i ⟶ S'.obj i |
      (∀ i, g i ≫ S'.π i = S.π i ≫ f i) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, S.p i ≫ g i.castSucc = f i.succ ≫ S'.p i) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, S.δ i ≫ (g i.succ)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = g i.castSucc ≫ S'.δ i)}.Subsingleton
declarations.comment: (3): at most one morphism of Postnikov systems, all components

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.PostnikovSystem.exists_not_subsingleton_hom
declarations.doc:
Cases (1) and (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0FXE] do not give uniqueness of the whole morphism of
Postnikov systems. In any pretriangulated category with a nonzero object `B` there are complexes
`X₃ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X₀` and `X'₃ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X'₀`, Postnikov systems `S`, `S'` for them and a morphism of
complexes `f` such that every morphism `Xᵢ⟦i⟧ ⟶ Y'₃⟦3⟧` with `i ≥ 1` is zero (case (1)) and every
morphism `Y₃⟦3⟧ ⟶ X'ⱼ⟦j⟧` with `j < 3` is zero (case (2)), and yet there are two different
morphisms of Postnikov systems `S ⟶ S'` over `f`. Under (1) or (2) the component `Yₙ ⟶ Y'ₙ` on
the totalizations is unique, which is `PostnikovSystem.subsingleton_hom_last`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PostnikovSystem.exists_not_subsingleton_hom (B : D) (hB : ¬ IsZero B) :
    ∃ (X X' : Fin 4 → D) (d : ∀ i : Fin 3, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc)
      (d' : ∀ i : Fin 3, X' i.succ ⟶ X' i.castSucc) (S : PostnikovSystem X d)
      (S' : PostnikovSystem X' d') (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ X' i),
      (∀ i : Fin 3, d i ≫ f i.castSucc = f i.succ ≫ d' i) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin 4, 0 < (i : ℕ) →
        ∀ u : (X i)⟦((i : ℕ) : ℤ)⟧ ⟶ (S'.obj (Fin.last 3))⟦((3 : ℕ) : ℤ)⟧, u = 0) ∧
      (∀ j : Fin 4, (j : ℕ) < 3 →
        ∀ u : (S.obj (Fin.last 3))⟦((3 : ℕ) : ℤ)⟧ ⟶ (X' j)⟦((j : ℕ) : ℤ)⟧, u = 0) ∧
      ¬ {g : ∀ i, S.obj i ⟶ S'.obj i |
          (∀ i, g i ≫ S'.π i = S.π i ≫ f i) ∧
          (∀ i : Fin 3, S.p i ≫ g i.castSucc = f i.succ ≫ S'.p i) ∧
          (∀ i : Fin 3, S.δ i ≫ (g i.succ)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = g i.castSucc ≫ S'.δ i)}.Subsingleton
declarations.comment: (1), (2): counterexample to uniqueness of the whole morphism of Postnikov systems

declarations.name: RingTheory.TorIndependence.torIndependent_tensorProduct_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FXF.** Tor independence of two algebras is preserved by extension of scalars along
a flat map of commutative rings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torIndependent_tensorProduct_of_flat
    (R : Type uR) (R' : Type uS) (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra R R']
    (h : TorIndependent R A B)
    (hR' : RingHom.Flat (algebraMap R R')) :
    let _ : Algebra R' (A ⊗[R] R') := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    let _ : Algebra R' (B ⊗[R] R') := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    TorIndependent R' (A ⊗[R] R') (B ⊗[R] R')

declarations.name: StrongGeneration.comp_eq_zero_of_mem_triangEnvelopeIter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FXH**.
If `K` belongs to `⟨R⟩ₙ` in the derived category of a ring and a chain of `n` morphisms beginning
at `K` induces the zero map on cohomology in every degree, then the composite of the chain is
zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_eq_zero_of_mem_triangEnvelopeIter
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (F : ComposableArrows (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) n)
    (hFleft :
      ObjectProperty.triangEnvelopeIter
        (ObjectProperty.singleton
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)))
        (n - 1) F.left)
    (hF : ∀ (i : ℕ) (_ : i < n) (j : ℤ),
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) j).map (F.map' i (i + 1)) = 0) :
    F.hom = 0

declarations.name: StrongGeneration.isRegularRing_and_ringKrullDim_ne_top_of_isStrongGenerator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FXI**.
A Noetherian ring for which `R` strongly generates its perfect derived category — that is, for
which a single stage `⟨R⟩ₙ` already exhausts `⟨R⟩` — is regular and has finite Krull dimension.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularRing_and_ringKrullDim_ne_top_of_isStrongGenerator
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (h : ∃ n : ℕ,
      ObjectProperty.triangEnvelopeIter
        (ObjectProperty.singleton
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R))) n =
      ObjectProperty.triangEnvelope
        (ObjectProperty.singleton
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)))) :
    IsRegularRing R ∧ ringKrullDim R ≠ ⊤

declarations.name: StrongGeneration.subsingleton_hom_of_isGE_of_isLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FXJ**.
Let `R` be a regular Noetherian ring of finite dimension `d`. If `K` and `L` are bounded-above
derived `R`-modules, the cohomology of `K` vanishes in degrees at most `k`, and the cohomology of
`L` vanishes in degrees at least `k - d + 1`, then every morphism from `K` to `L` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_hom_of_isGE_of_isLE [IsRegularRing R]
    (d : ℕ) (hdim : ringKrullDim R = d)
    (K L : DerivedCategory.Minus (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (k : ℤ)
    (hK : K.obj.IsGE (k + 1)) (hL : L.obj.IsLE (k - d)) :
    Subsingleton (K.obj ⟶ L.obj)

declarations.name: StrongGeneration.iso_biproduct_truncations_of_cohomology_isZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FXK**.
Let `R` be a regular Noetherian ring of finite positive dimension `d`. If a perfect derived
`R`-module `K` has zero cohomology in every degree from `k - d + 2` through `k`, then `K` is
isomorphic to the biproduct of its truncations in degrees at most `k - d + 1` and at least
`k + 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem iso_biproduct_truncations_of_cohomology_isZero [IsRegularRing R]
    (d : ℕ) (hdim : ringKrullDim R = d) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (hKperfect : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K) (k : ℤ)
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, k - d + 2 ≤ i → i ≤ k →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj K)) :
    Nonempty
      (K ≅
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLE (k - d + 1)).obj K ⊞
          (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE (k + 1)).obj K)

declarations.name: StrongGeneration.exists_triangEnvelopeIter_eq_isPerfect_of_isRegularRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FXL**.
Over a regular ring of finite Krull dimension, the regular module placed in degree zero is a strong
generator of the perfect derived category: a single stage `⟨R⟩ₙ` of the triangulated envelope of
`R[0]` already contains every perfect complex. One may take for `n` the global dimension of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_triangEnvelopeIter_eq_isPerfect_of_isRegularRing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsRegularRing R] (hdim : ringKrullDim R ≠ ⊤) :
    ∃ n : ℕ,
      ObjectProperty.triangEnvelopeIter
          (ObjectProperty.singleton
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R))) n =
        (StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect :
          ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)))

declarations.name: StrongGeneration.isRegularRing_and_ringKrullDim_ne_top_iff_hasStrongGenerator_iff_regularModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FXM**.
For a Noetherian ring `R` the following are equivalent: `R` is regular of finite Krull dimension;
the perfect derived category of `R` admits a strong generator; and the regular module placed in
degree zero is such a strong generator. The implication from an arbitrary strong generator to the
regular module uses that any object of the perfect derived category already lies in some finite
stage of the envelope of `R[0]`, so the stages of its own envelope are absorbed into those of
`R[0]`.

declarations.name: Stacks.TorIdealPowerVanishing.torMap_idealPowerInclusion_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0FXN.** If `M` is a finite module over a Noetherian ring and `N`
is annihilated by an ideal `I`, then for some positive power of `I` the inclusion
`IⁿM ⟶ M` induces zero on `Tor_p(-, N)` for every `p ≥ 0`. The index `n` denotes the
positive exponent `n + 1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torMap_idealPowerInclusion_eq_zero
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (M N : ModuleCat.{u} A) [Module.Finite A M]
    (hN : I ≤ Module.annihilator A N) :
    let K := (CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj M
    let N₀ := (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N
    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ,
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (-(p : ℤ))).map
          (((DerivedTensorData.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct A).tensor.flip.obj N₀).map
            (DerivedCategory.Q.map
              (image.ι (Stacks.AdicSystem.IdealPowerTensorComparison.idealPowerMultiplication K I
                n)))) = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomTensorMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0FXP.** For objects `K`, `K'`, `M`, `M'` of `D(O_X)` on a ringed space there is a
canonical morphism

`RSheafHom(K, K') ⊗^L_{O_X} RSheafHom(M, M') ⟶ RSheafHom(K ⊗^L_{O_X} M, K' ⊗^L_{O_X} M')`,

the morphism adjoint under Stacks 08DI to the interchange of the two middle factors of
`RSheafHom(K, K') ⊗^L RSheafHom(M, M') ⊗^L K ⊗^L M` followed by evaluation of each internal
hom.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSheafHomTensorMap (K K' M M' : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
